# Platform Adaptation Notes

Field-tested pitfalls and conclusions per platform; each entry records only the pitfall and the fix. Protocol-interop conclusions all come from real buses and real panels. Linux is organized by distribution → desktop environment, Windows / macOS by version; add new conclusions to the matching section and sync the Chinese version ([docs/zh/adaptation.md](/zh/adaptation.md)) in the same batch.

## Icon data and generator (803 icons, 2026-09-29)

Shape comparison for the icon data (803 iconfont icons, debug build, 2026-09-29): switching from the "code shape" (each icon expanded into match branches of Painter calls) to the "data shape" (per-mille fixed-point path strings interpreted and drawn by `fill_icon_path`, emitted by `scripts/gen_icons.py`) — `icons.mbt` 51k lines / 3.5 MB → 4.3k lines / 0.7 MB; showcase.exe 23.7 MB → 14.9 MB (hello likewise 7.9 → 7.5 MB); library-module incremental compile 6.8s → 0.78s; showcase window map 41ms → 7~9ms. Drawing correctness was verified with full probe-icon grid screenshots compared against the old shape (lines / fills / cut-outs consistent). Visible icons per frame are at most in the hundreds, each costing a few hundred characters of parsing — microseconds, no caching needed. Lesson: a generator emitting "code" versus "data" differs by an order of magnitude — for heavily repeated geometry, always choose the data shape plus a small interpreter.

## Cross-platform (build chain / FFI)

### Build and Linking

- Library packages must not carry a `link` section (moon would generate a main-less exe and the build fails); all link flags come from `scripts/prebuild.py` via the `--moonbit-unstable-prebuild` hook, which emits link_configs auto-propagated to every main package depending on the library module. Never hand-write `cc-link-flags` in any package.
- prebuild script constraints: stdout must carry only the final JSON (progress goes to stderr); all flags go in the single link_flags string with hand-controlled ordering (GNU ld is single-pass); the script's cwd is the consumer's project root, so library paths must be absolute.
- Recent moon deprecates `moon.mod.json` / `moon.pkg.json` (`moon fmt` migrates in one shot); `moon doc` only accepts the new format, and older moon does not understand it.
- MSVC misreads BOM-less UTF-8 source as cp936; Chinese comments produce fake preprocessing errors (the reported line has no such directive): CMake adds `/utf-8` for MSVC.
- Recent moon deprecates implicit trait-method promotion: call sites use the explicit static form `ViewLike::method(obj)`; `impl Trait for X` declaration sites need explicit `pub extend X with Trait::{...}` (generate the method list from `moon check --no-render` output, don't hand-copy); black-box tests must qualify in-package symbols as `@<package>.xxx`. These warnings are missed by incremental builds — a clean full build surfaces them all.
- The mooncakes package-page README renderer only displays images with absolute external URLs (field-tested across the 0.5.3–0.5.5 releases: package-relative image paths render neither as plain Markdown nor as HTML — HTML blocks are dropped entirely — while an external CI badge displays fine); switch hero images to jsdelivr absolute URLs (`cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/<user>/<repo>@master/...`, balanced reachability inside and outside China; `@master` references lag a few hours behind due to CDN caching). GitHub-side rendering via the camo proxy is unaffected.
- The toolchain triple (moon / moonc / core) must ship as one matched set (field-tested during the 0.5.3 release): `moon upgrade` aborted midway in a non-interactive terminal (`IO error: not a terminal`) after swapping the binaries but before touching `~/.moon/lib/core`, leaving moonc 0.10.14 paired with core 0.10.12 — the old core lacks `StringView::exact_view` (four "no method" errors in sysdata), and the mismatch only surfaced when a version bump in moon.mod forced a full re-check; earlier incremental `moon check`/`moon test` greens were false. Nightly version numbers are delisted the same day (the CLI server 403s any named historical version), so pinning via `MOONBIT_INSTALL_VERSION` is not viable — the only repair is rerunning `install/unix.sh` with no version to install the latest full bundle (binaries and core replaced in one pass), matching CI. Verify by checking that `moon version --all` and `~/.moon/lib/core/moon.mod` agree, then bumping the version to force a full re-check: 133 tests green.
- **What the mooncakes builder really does with an old-manifest published dependency (field-tested on the 0.1.0 release, 2026-10-15)**: after `native-gui@0.1.0` was published, its package page showed **Build failed / Documentation failed for this version** (no docs generated, no API reference; the package itself stays installable). The build log (public API: `https://mooncakes.io/api/v0/builds/log?module=<owner>/<name>&version=<ver>`) shows all four targets — native / wasm-gc / wasm / js — failing **with one shared cause**: in the published archive of `NoahLiu/yoga-mbt@0.1.0` the package manifest is still `moon.pkg.json` (`moon.pkg.json ... is no longer supported. Run moon fmt to migrate`), so the builder dies while discovering packages (`Failed to calculate build plan / Failed when discovering packages`) before ever reaching this module's own code. This is the same pitfall the CI "migrate the dependency cache in place" loop works around — **CI migrates the local `.mooncakes` download cache, but a published package in the registry cannot be migrated**, so consumers and the builder are bound to hit it. The fix is to **republish that dependency module (its `moon.pkg` is already in this repo) and only then publish the modules depending on it** — the upstream of the publish chain must be fixed first. How to verify: after republishing yoga-mbt, republish native-gui and watch the package page's `build_status`; the diagnostic entry point is the log API above (the same endpoint behind the signed-in page's button).
- **Pre-publish rehearsal and the republish drill (agreed 2026-10-15)**: run `moon publish` from each **module root** (optionally with `--dry-run` first); before pushing, bake a local `moon package` preview archive (`<module>/_build/publish/<Owner>-<name>-<version>.zip`) and unpack it to confirm zero old `.json` manifests and that `moon.mod` / `moon.pkg` are in place. In a multi-module release chain, publish **upstream first** — a downstream build reads the upstream archive, so it can only turn green after the upstream has been republished. A published version cannot be rewritten in the registry; the fix is always a version bump (0.1.0 → 0.1.1 here, with every in-repo pin bumped in the same batch — `moon.work` matches local members by name + version, so a missed pin breaks even local resolution). Archive-level evidence: `NoahLiu/yoga-mbt@0.1.0`'s published zip has the new-format top-level `moon.mod` but still ships the old `src/moon.pkg.json` (published before the in-repo migration; the registry copy is immutable), and `NoahLiu/native-gui@0.1.0`'s zip is a repo-root-era snapshot (old repo URL, old description). Temp-directory staging is not needed: `moon publish` packs just that module from its own root (dependencies are not vendored), and `moon.work` only affects local resolution, not the archive — an extra copy step only adds two risks (missed files; a publish source that is not the git worktree).
- **Taking in mizchi/markdown@0.8.3 and the transitive-dependency publish chain, settled (MD1, 2026-10)**: the root moon.mod pins `mizchi/markdown@0.8.3`; the standalone console probe `examples/probe-markdown` verifies the parse / render_html / serialize calls (`moon run examples/probe-markdown --target native` prints PROBE-OK: parse yields 11 blocks including one heading / fenced code / table / blockquote / list each; render_html produces h1/strong/em/code/a/ul/li/pre/blockquote/table with link hrefs preserved; serialize round-trips through re-parse and re-render), with `moon check` zero warnings and `moon test` 576 all green. Native support is documented: the registry index shows 0.8.0 as js+wasm only, **native arrives in 0.8.1**, wasm-gc in 0.8.2, so pinning 0.8.3 (supported-targets = js+wasm+wasm-gc+native) is the first safe point in the support matrix; its src/moon.pkg imports the experimental `moonbitlang/core/v128` (an in-package comment says it is only reachable on linear-memory targets) — native is linear-memory, and the probe compiling through is the proof, no extra switches needed. **The dependency closure is nominally 5, actually 21 packages**: direct deps moonbitlang/async@0.20.3 / moonbitlang/parser@0.3.18 / moonbitlang/x@0.5.1 / mizchi/syntree@0.2.4 / mizchi/moomaid@0.4.0; expanding each package's moon.mod one level down installs 21 external packages into .mooncakes (parser→lexer/moon_config/prettyprinter; moomaid→tui/signals/svg/font/css/crater-layout/crater-core and their sub-deps tui-terminal-buffer/brotli/zlib/pixelmatch/layout). x and syntree carry co-existing upstream multi-version declarations (markdown wants x@0.5.1, parser wants 0.4.39, moomaid wants 0.4.47; syntree 0.2.4/0.2.3); mooncakes' single-version space installs the highest, so as upstream drifts moon picks the maximum for the closure — upgrading markdown must watch for cascades. **`moon add` transitivity measured**: a consumer's `moon add mizchi/markdown@0.8.3` writes only the direct-dependency line; the transitive closure never enters moon.mod and is resolved and fetched recursively from the registry index at install time (a scratch module printed e.g. "Using cached mizchi/syntree") — after this repo publishes, a consumer adding this module gets the full closure pulled automatically by the builder; the dependency-surface cost is purely install/compile time. **Settled: accept the transitive dependencies, do not split into a standalone module** (from MD2 the markdown_view bridge to mizchi/markdown travels with the main module). Rationale: the closure is all pure MoonBit source packages — no native stubs, no link surface, untouched by prebuild management, zero ABI / platform-matrix / payload-size risk for consumers — a different nature from ffmpeg-mbt, which was split out for its binary matrix + licensing + size. A downgrade path stays open: if the consumer dependency surface gets too heavy or upstream 0.x APIs churn, sink it into its own module then (the library module reverts to zero markdown deps, mirroring the media three-layer split). Note: an in-module sub-package (the old chain's browser sub-package pattern) cannot solve the dependency surface — mooncakes deps are module-level declarations, so a sub-package's imports enter the publish closure all the same; the browser pattern isolates the link-flags layer, a different mechanism — do not conflate the two.

### CI runner environment vs. the development machine (2026-10-15, first time the Linux and Windows jobs reached the test step)

- **Environment**: GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest / windows-latest. The development machine is Ubuntu 24.04 + X11 + XFCE: session bus present, notification service present, display server present. None of the three is guaranteed on a runner, so tests that were green locally failed on CI — each for its own reason, not one shared cause.
- **Dependency-graph resolution (CI was stuck here for a long stretch, two stacked causes, unrelated to this repo's code)**: out of the last 100 master runs (back to 2026-10-13 15:29) only this one succeeded; every other run died in the very first step, `moon check`, before any compilation started, with `Failed to resolve registry dependency ... module was not found in the registry`. Layer one: a freshly installed runner's registry index has no `prowk/moonsqlitefile` or `mizchi/markdown`, and moon prints the password itself — `you may need to run moon update`; both jobs now open with a `moon update` step. Layer two only shows once the index is refreshed: since 2026-10-12 the toolchain only accepts `moon.mod`/`moon.pkg`, while the published third-party packages still ship `moon.mod.json`/`moon.pkg.json` (`... is no longer supported`). There is no way back on the registry side, so the job migrates the old manifests in place once the dependency cache has landed (running `moon fmt` in every `.mooncakes/**/moon.{mod,pkg}.json` directory) — **touching only the git-ignored download cache, never the repo sources, never the dependency versions**. Each round only resolves the batch of packages that has just been downloaded, so the loop runs until it converges (both jobs passed on **round 9** this time). The workspace member `modules/yoga-mbt/src/moon.pkg.json` was migrated to `moon.pkg` in the same batch (`warn_list` unchanged at `-6`) — the new toolchain rejects its old manifest too.
- **Notifications (a real contract bug, fixed)**: on the runner the session bus answers but no notification service is installed, so `@dbus.notify_caps()` returns `NfFailed(ServiceUnknown)` while `notify_supported()` says there is no backend. The old `core/notify_caps()` forwarded the dbus error directly, which made the two probes disagree. Now `notify_caps()` decides "is there a backend" through `notify_backend()` first, gives `Err(Unsupported)` when there is none, and only asks `GetCapabilities` once the D-Bus backend is confirmed. One-line contract: when `notify_supported()` is false, `notify_caps()` must give `Unsupported`. The `dbus/notify_wbtest` capability case prints a skip for "bus present, service absent", the same treatment as `NfUnsupported`, instead of calling it a code failure.
- **Declarative mount (the assertion encoded a dev-machine accident, fixed)**: `mount_window_render(render, ...)` is `mount_window(render(), ...)`, so render runs **exactly once, regardless of whether the window mounts**. The test also demanded "zero runs when no app comes back", which only holds on a machine where window creation succeeds; on a headless machine creation fails but that one run has already happened, so CI went red. Now asserted as "exactly once".
- **The text/layout family needs real fonts - and the runner's problem was "different fonts", not "no fonts"**: the Linux job's diagnostic step (`fc-list` count, `fc-match`, a small C probe measuring `"AAAA"` in `"Sans 14"`) reports **53 fonts, default DejaVu Sans, 52x23**, while the development machine gives **48x23** (Noto Sans CJK). `fonts-dejavu-core` joined the apt list so at least one family exists, and every assertion frozen to the dev machine's metrics became font-independent:
  1. `text/range` ("the coloured range lands on the first glyph") used to demand "the red block ends before the black ink starts" - adjacent glyph ink touching breaks it; it now compares "red block narrower than the black block" (the left-edge check stays);
  2. `ui/form`'s link hover underline used to sample "the bottom row, one cell" - which row that is depends on the font's descent; it now compares total ink (that is what "was an underline drawn" means);
  3. `ui/textarea`'s up/down keys used lines `ab` and `cd`, so the remembered pixel x mapped differently per font (on DejaVu the second line is narrower and up lands mid-line); both lines are now `ab` - the test checks the rule, not one font's width relation;
  4. `mdview`'s marker/content baseline tolerance went from ±2px to ±6px, with the reason written down: what that check must catch is "the marker cell never registered a measurement and got centred mid-row", a 10px-class error, not per-font 1px alignment;
  5. `ui/basic`'s "an underline must add ink" now compares ink pixels instead of ink rows (a 1px line landing inside the last row's leading leaves the row count flat) - and it **exposed a real bug**: in `ui/base.mbt`, `draw_underline` computed `y = top + baseline + 1.5` and then hit `if y >= r.h { return }`, so when the backend's line box only reaches the baseline the whole line was dropped - "the style did nothing", which is worse than drawing it one pixel low. The line must stay inside the box (skip only when `r.h <= 0`, otherwise clamp with `min(r.h-1, max(0, y))` against the bottom edge), and the assertion now prints plain/under ink, both row counts and `measure_font`'s w/h/baseline.
- **`/tmp` is not a universal writable path**: `render/image_wbtest`'s "write PNG, read it back" went red on Windows - `/tmp/...` resolves to `C:\tmp` (absent) there, so `write_to_file` returns false. The test now writes to a relative path (the `moon test` process has the module root `gui/` as cwd), the artifact is in `.gitignore`, and the failure prints the path (this one assertion has been broken by two different causes - missing directory, and an encoder that does not know the format - and the failing line alone cannot tell them apart).
- **Windows manifest-migration loop**: PowerShell has no `Select-String -QuietPattern` parameter (the form is `-Pattern … -Quiet`). With the wrong name the loop dies on parameter binding in the **first** round, reporting a PowerShell error, which looks like "migration did not converge" while not one line ran.
- **The Linux workspace resolution needs the ffmpeg dev packages**: the Linux apt list gained `libavformat-dev` and four other `-dev` packages - not because the main path uses them, but because `moon test`/`moon check` inside the workspace also runs `modules/ffmpeg-mbt`'s own prebuild, which exits non-zero when pkg-config cannot find `libav*` (the hint it prints is exactly that apt command).
- **Verification**: CI run 38676488227 (2026-10-15) is green on both jobs - Linux 912/912 (13 packages) plus build plus the xvfb smoke, Windows 666/666 (11 packages; dbus/sys excluded as platform gaps) plus ffmpeg-mbt 24/24, gui-media 6/6 and the hello link; the font-diagnostic readings are as above; manifest migration converged on round 9 on both. The local control experiment `env -u DISPLAY moon test core ui dbus sys` reproduces the runner's "no display service" shape.

### CI runner environment vs. the development machine (2026-10-15, first time the three jobs reached the test step)

- **Environment**: GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest / windows-latest / macos-latest. The development machine is Ubuntu 24.04 + X11 + XFCE: session bus present, notification service present, display server present. None of that is guaranteed on a runner, so tests that were green locally failed on CI - each for its own reason, not one shared cause.
- **Notifications (a real contract bug, fixed)**: on the runner the session bus answers but no notification service is installed, so `@dbus.notify_caps()` returns `NfFailed(ServiceUnknown)` while `notify_supported()` says there is no backend. The old `core/notify_caps()` forwarded the dbus error directly, which made the two probes disagree. Now `notify_caps()` decides "is there a backend" through `notify_backend()` first and only asks `GetCapabilities` once the D-Bus backend is confirmed. One-line contract: when `notify_supported()` is false, `notify_caps()` must give `Unsupported`.
- **Declarative mount (the assertion encoded a dev-machine accident, fixed)**: `mount_window_render(render, ...)` is `mount_window(render(), ...)`, so render runs **exactly once, regardless of whether the window mounts**. The test also demanded "zero runs when no app comes back", which only holds on a machine where mounting succeeds. Now asserted as "exactly once".
- **The text/layout family needs real fonts - and the runner's problem was "different fonts", not "no fonts"**: the Linux diagnostic step (fc-list count, `fc-match`, a small C probe measuring `"AAAA"` in `"Sans 14"`) reported **53 fonts and 52x23**, while the development machine gives **48x23** (Noto Sans CJK vs the runner's DejaVu). So every red in that family was **an assertion frozen to the dev machine's metrics**. Four of them became font-independent:
  1. `text/range` ("the coloured range lands on the first glyph") used to demand "the red block ends before the black ink starts" - adjacent glyph ink touching breaks it; it now compares "red block narrower than the black block" (the left-edge check stays);
  2. `ui/form`'s link hover underline used to sample "the bottom row, one pixel" - which row that is depends on the font's descent; it now compares total ink (that is what "was an underline drawn" means);
  3. `ui/textarea`'s up/down keys used lines `ab` and `cd`, so the remembered pixel x mapped differently per font (on DejaVu the second line is narrower and up lands mid-line); both lines are now `ab` - the test checks the rule, not one font's width relation;
  4. `mdview`'s marker/content baseline tolerance went from ±2px to ±6px, with the reason written down: what that check must catch is "the marker cell never registered a measurement and got centred mid-row" (a measured 10px-scale fault, `rect=(0,111,18,0)`), not per-font 1px alignment.
- **`/tmp` is not a universal writable path**: `render/image_wbtest`'s "write PNG, read it back" went red on Windows - `/tmp/...` resolves to `C:\tmp` (absent) there, so `write_to_file` returns false. The test now writes to a relative path (the `moon test` process has the module root `gui/` as cwd), the artifact is in `.gitignore`, and the failure prints the path (this one assertion has been broken by two different causes across platforms - missing directory, and an encoder that does not know the format - and the failing line alone cannot tell them apart).
- **Windows ran `moon test` for the first time**: 661 of 662 passed; the single failure was that writable-path issue above. All three platforms are now usable as a compile-and-test gate.
- **Verification**: the local control experiment `env -u DISPLAY moon test core ui dbus sys` (551/551) reproduces the runner's "no display service" shape; the font conclusions come from the CI diagnostic readings compared against 48x23 locally.
- **Windows manifest-migration loop**: PowerShell has no `Select-String -QuietPattern` parameter (the form is `-Pattern … -Quiet`). With the wrong name the loop dies on parameter binding in the **first** round, which looks like "migration did not converge" while nothing actually ran.

### MoonBit cfg(platform=)

- **Decision (2026-10-11): platform dispatch drops cfg for good, even if the toolchain later fixes it** — MoonBit-side cross-platform selection is always "runtime probe + pattern matching", probed in the shape of render's existing degradation probe (paint a stroke and verify pixels, non-zero session handle); now a hard rule in AGENTS.md.

### Native render/text matrix and the three-layer text divergence (new-stack decision, 2026-10-11)

- **Platform matrix**: Linux = GTK3 window + cairo raster + Pango text (system libraries, dynamic linking, no LGPL obligations); Windows = pure-MoonBit software rasterizer + DirectWrite text + WIC image decoding (all OS components, zero third-party dependencies); macOS = CoreGraphics + CoreText (stub placeholder, backend not yet developed). **The sys capability family now has real implementations on both platforms (platform batches ①-⑥, 2026-10-14)**: wallpaper/idle/launcher/desktop/powerprofile/sysinfo/windowctl/appfind/recent_files/volume/printer/print/browser/vscode — 17 items in total, each with real-hardware readings; sys 188/188; see the platform status table in system-capabilities.md. vcpkg static linking of cairo/pango was evaluated and dropped: the dependency weight (glib/fontconfig/harfbuzz and friends) plus the LGPL static-linking "must provide a relinking path" obligation contradict this library's "native, lightweight, no-strings" positioning.
- **The three-layer text divergence and countermeasures**: ① **Height** — line height is unified as `max(engine natural line height, ceil(size×K))`, with K a constant measured across the three platforms against the fattest font (Microsoft YaHei); line height becomes a pure function of size, fallback fonts no longer affect it, the surplus is centered with half-leading and the rounding rule is fixed; fonts whose natural height exceeds the floor grow the line in place (graceful degradation, no glyph clipping). ② **Width** — wrapping/truncation/ellipsis are entirely MoonBit component-layer decisions (the platform only supplies measurement); textarea's wrap_units/layout_lines pure functions stay; CJK advance≈em shows no real difference, Latin differs by one word (wrap/ellipsis boundary points), no content loss. ③ **Pixels** — the vector layer (rects/paths/AA/25 blend modes/gradients) is the MoonBit rasterizer's single implementation on all three platforms, bit-for-bit identical, assertions shared cross-platform; text metrics/pixels are inherently per-platform (the old stack already had three engines: Pango/DirectWrite/CoreText), so assertions split into "structural (shared) / numeric (per-platform baseline directory)" tiers, and the default font is encoded per platform into the theme (Windows pins the YaHei family, Linux follows fontconfig).
- **Linux dividend**: cairo and the MoonBit rasterizer can be pixel-diffed against each other — cairo serves as the reference answer for accepting the self-built engine (the acceptance method of rasterizer batch W4).
- **Platform C stub organization**: a single multi-branch `stub.c` + prebuild macros (see the win/stub.c precedent in the "Windows window foundation W2" section); the render/text stub merges follow the same pattern, with the Windows side pulling in no C render/text libraries (only WIC counts as an OS component).

### MoonBit native GUI stack · pure-MoonBit rasterizer (W4, Windows/mac render backend)

- **Architecture**: `render` gains four pure-MoonBit files — `raster_path.mbt` (path commands / affine matrix / adaptive Bézier flattening / arc→Bézier with kappa), `raster_fill.mbt` (4×4 supersampled nonzero-winding scanline fill + polyline-offset stroking with miter limit 10 / butt caps), `raster_blend.mbt` (25 blend modes: nine Porter-Duff closed forms in premultiplied space + 16 W3C formulas in non-premultiplied space + gradient evaluation), and `raster.mbt` (the `Raster` session, method-for-method mirroring `Cairo`); the `Painter` facade becomes a two-backend enum with **runtime probing** (`Cairo::over` failing to open a session ⇒ pure path), no compile directives (AGENTS rule 11). The stubs merge into `render/stub.c`: the real cairo implementation hangs off the `WM_STUB_CAIRO` macro compiled only by prebuild (Linux), non-Linux keeps placeholders to satisfy the linker, and the probe falls to the pure path when it sees the placeholder. The text layer probes via `Painter::cairo_id()`: with cairo it paints into the session context; the pure backend returns None (W5's DirectWrite shape paints straight into the Bitmap), and `Painter::raster()` fetches the pure session.
- **Coverage quantization**: 4×4 supersampling, 16 samples per pixel, coverage 0..256 (16 per sample) — the per-pixel difference from cairo's analytic coverage is absorbed by the "parity tolerance band ≤16 (one sample step)"; full-coverage and zero-coverage pixels are exact. Crossing tests use the half-open `(ay<=ys)!=(by2<=ys)` to avoid double-counting vertices; the nonzero sweep collects spans where winding ≠ 0, and open polylines auto-close for fill (**the closing edge IS the wrap edge, so the edge count is n, not n+1 — writing n+1 indexes pts[n] out of bounds; unit tests with all-closed paths never see it, the real window crashed within 45 frames. Lesson: open paths need dedicated cases**).
- **Premultiply rounding must be two steps, never merged**: source premultiply lives in the 255 domain (`(v·a+127)/255`), coverage scaling in the 256 domain (`·cov/256`); merging into one 65536-domain step swallows the 255/256 ratio (opaque full coverage measured 254 instead of 255, off-by-one across the board). The Normal composite `s+(d·inv+127)/255` matches Bitmap::paint, so rect paths stay bit-for-bit identical.
- **Known divergences from cairo (inside the tolerance band)**: ① 16-level quantized AA coverage vs cairo's analytic coverage; ② nearest-neighbor blit vs cairo bilinear (1:1 and opaque pixels are bit-exact; scaled sampling differs — the sample-domain clamping semantic is mirrored: sampling never leaves the source sub-rect, so colors do not bleed); ③ gradient stops interpolated non-premultiplied (CSS/W3C) vs cairo's premultiplied space (semi-transparent stop midpoints differ, opaque stops identical); ④ stroke device width = user width × sqrt(|det|), an approximation for non-uniform scaling; ⑤ skewed-clip degrades to the bounding box. The 25 W3C blend values pass the same exact assertions on both platforms (cairo's operators and the hand formulas agree in the 8-bit domain).
- **MoonBit pitfalls hit this batch**: sin/cos live in `moonbitlang/core/math` (`@math.sin`; Double has no such methods); uppercase `let` is illegal — use `const`; scientific notation `1e-9` fails to parse, spell it `0.000000001` (repeated an old pitfall; suggest grepping `1e-`); trailing commas on match arms are illegal, including after tuple arms `(a,b,c)`. Test-side: tests that used `Cairo::over` directly became "backend probe + structural assertions" shared cross-platform; decode-dependent tests gained a `decode_available()` probe guard (missing environment skips instead of hard-failing).
- **Verification** (2026-10-11, Windows machine): render 43/43 (including the new "path/stroke/arc two-backend parity (AA tolerance)" test), icons 4/4 (**all 803 icon paths produce pixels** through the pure rasterizer), core 62 / input 10 / mdview 26 still green, theme 7/8 (the remaining font-measurement case belongs to W5); native-window smoke 45 frames with clean exit (every real-window frame goes through the pure rasterizer); whole-repo check 287/68 unchanged. The Linux cairo path is untouched bit-for-bit (stub content moved verbatim); on Linux the parity test IS the "cairo vs pure" acceptance — pending a user-side rerun.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Windows branches of the system-capability stub (W14: files / env / subprocess / file dialog)

- **The third-party `chensuiyi/subproc` had to go — and master had already dropped it**: the package describes itself as "Synchronous **Linux** process management" and relies on Linux-only machinery (pidfd, procfs, poll). Locally, `.mooncakes/chensuiyi/subproc/src/native.c:7` dies under MSVC with `fatal error C1083: cannot open include file 'poll.h'`, which blocked the whole `sys` chain (and downstream chart/ui/examples/native-app) from even compiling on Windows. The other registry candidate, `trkbt10/subprocess`, covers subprocesses on Unix/macOS only (Windows side is IPC sockets), so it does not fit either. **Fix: port master's already-proven three-platform implementation** (master's implementation calls its own C stubs `proc_spawn/proc_wait/proc_getpid`, zero third-party deps) into `sys/sys_stub.c` as C, symbols `yue_sys_proc_*`, semantics aligned bit-for-bit: POSIX branch shared by Linux/macOS (`fork` → `setsid`/`setpgid` on macOS → `dup2` temp files → `execvpe` on Linux / `execvp` + `*_NSGetEnviron` on macOS, `_exit(127)` on exec failure, `_exit(126)` on `chdir` failure); Windows uses `CreateProcessW` + `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, `STARTF_USESTDHANDLES` with inheritable handles, environment block sorted by name and terminated with a double wide NUL, empty block = inherit parent environment. **Key design difference: only the pid is returned, never a handle** — Windows `wait` reopens it via `OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE|TERMINATE|QUERY_LIMITED)` and closes the handle immediately, which removes an entire cross-call handle table and its leak surface (the original plan of "return hProcess + `proc_drop`" was scrapped).
- **`__uuidof` does not exist in MSVC's C mode**: in `CoCreateInstance(&CLSID_FileOpenDialog, ...)`, writing `__uuidof(FileOpenDialog)` fails with `error C4233: nonstandard extension used: keyword only supported in C++` (the coclass declarations in the SDK headers are C++-only). In C, take the `extern const GUID` constants from the headers (`CLSID_FileOpenDialog` / `IID_IFileDialog` / `IID_IShellItem`), which come from **uuid.lib** — hence `scripts/prebuild.py`'s Windows branch now issues `ole32.lib shell32.lib uuid.lib` for `sys` (MSVC takes them as positional arguments; `-l` triggers D9002).
- **UCRT has no `_getwcwd`**: the name looks like the wide getcwd but is declared nowhere in the SDK — MSVC only emits `warning C4013: undefined, default external return int`, truncating the returned `wchar_t*` to int and then dereferencing it: compiles, crashes. Use the Win32 `GetCurrentDirectoryW` instead (two passes: size 0 to query, then fetch).
- **Environment variables must go wide, and Windows has no "exists but empty" state**: `getenv`/`_putenv_s` are the ANSI versions and round-trip values through the process ANSI code page (936 here), so a UTF-8 Chinese value comes back as mojibake (鍊糀) — caught live by `sys/envx_wbtest.mbt`. Switched to `GetEnvironmentVariableW`/`_wputenv_s` (query size with 0 first). Related semantic difference: on Windows `_wputenv_s(name, L"")` **is the delete operation**, so `envx_get(name)` reads back an empty-value write as `None`, not `Some("")`; the test now asserts per platform. Files follow the same rule: UTF-8 in, wide API out (`FindFirstFileW`/`_wfopen`/`_wremove`) — the A versions misfire on Chinese user-directory names.
- **`ShellExecuteW` succeeds when the return value is > 32**: it returns the legacy HINSTANCE-style status (≤32 are `SE_ERR_*`), so `>32 ? 0 : -1` is the correct judgement. Its `open` verb carries the system associations (URL → default browser, document → associated app), which is exactly the role `xdg-open` plays in the POSIX branch.
- **In the placeholder branch, disk I/O that has nothing to do with graphics must still be real**: `render/stub.c`'s non-Linux branch had `fsw_write_file` as `return 0` (placeholder to keep linking), while the PNG encoder itself lives in pure MoonBit (`png.mbt`) and only needs one write — so chart export (`ci_save`) failed with `WriteFailed` on Windows every time. Rule of thumb: a placeholder should only cover "the backend capability this platform hasn't implemented yet", not backend-free standard I/O.
- **Three platform splits in the tests**: ① in the Windows CRT, `/tmp` means "tmp under the current drive root", so if that directory does not exist the write fails — temp paths must come from `%TEMP%`/`$TMPDIR` per platform (separator too); ② cmd emits `\r\n`, so assertions on `echo` output cannot hard-code `\n`; ③ **when tests run from Git Bash, PATH contains `/usr/bin/*.exe` (`echo`/`cat`/`sleep`/`true`), so POSIX command names "appear to work" and mask the real differences** — from cmd they all fail; hence every round-trip goes through a platform dispatcher (POSIX `sh -c`, Windows `cmd /c`). Unix-convention-specific assertions (exit 127 for a missing command, self-inflicted SIGTERM, forced `LC_ALL=C`, `/etc/hostname`) run on the POSIX side only; Windows gets the equivalent (`CreateProcessW` failure surfaces as `SpawnFailed`) or prints a skip.
- **Without a text layer, self-drawn widgets collapse to size 0**: on the pure-rasterizer platform `@text.measure` returns `None` and `attach_text_measure`'s fallback is `(0.0, 0.0)`, so width-from-text buttons/labels/links neither measure nor get hit — 20 assertions in `ui` are of this kind. Handling: add **runtime probes** at the test layer (`ui_text_guard()` measures `"Ag"`, `ui_decode_guard()` decodes one GIF); when the probe fails, print a skip and keep running the rest. They turn green again with W5 (DirectWrite) / W9 (WIC). Same treatment for theme's "control height baseline". No estimated widths were smuggled into the library: that would be silent fake data, contrary to the settled "probe + degrade with an explicit `Unsupported`" stance.
- **Verification** (Windows 10 19045 + MSVC 14.44 + SDK 10.0.26100, moon 0.1.20260920): `moon test -p sys` **163/163** (first time this package compiles and runs on Windows after dropping subproc), chart 189/189, ui 110/110 (20 probe-skipped), theme 8/8, core 70, render 43, input 10, mdview 26, icons 4 all green; per-package `moon check --deny-warn` zero warnings; `moon check ./examples/native-app --deny-warn` passes (previously blocked at the dependency stage); whole-repo red dots stay at 287 errors/68 warnings. `text` remains red on Windows — that is W5's scope (splitting assertions into "shared structural / per-platform numeric baseline"). The look of the real IFileDialog (filters / multi-select / initial folder) is left for the user to confirm.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · batch-A multi-window host on Windows (W15: slot reuse + idempotent wm_init)

- **Batch A only fixed the GTK branch; the same defect remained on Windows**: d1fb1e8 changed `wm_window_new` in the GTK branch of `win/stub.c` to reuse slots by scanning `area == NULL`, while the `_WIN32` branch of the same function still did `wm_next_id++` — repeatedly opening/closing secondary windows exhausts the 32 slots and `open_window` silently returns `None`. Fixed identically to the GTK branch, with the marker changed to `hwnd == NULL` (set on a successful create, cleared by the memset in `wm_close`, so a torn-down slot and a never-used one are equally reusable).
- **What actually blocked multi-window was a non-idempotent `wm_init`**: `app_window()` calls `@win.init_backend()` once per window, and Win32's `RegisterClassExW` **returns 0 when the class name is already registered** (`ERROR_CLASS_ALREADY_EXISTS`) — so the first call succeeds and every later one reports "backend unavailable", making `App::open_window` always return `None` on Windows (the main window was fine because it is the first call, which is why every single-window smoke passed). Now the whole body returns 1 directly when the waker window already exists, and `ERROR_CLASS_ALREADY_EXISTS` counts as success. The GTK branch uses `gtk_init_check`, already idempotent, so this only surfaces on Windows — **"the same path called twice" is a shape batch A introduced, invisible to all single-window smokes**.
- **Evidence (probe package `experiment/multiwin_probe`)**: ① 40 create/destroy rounds, more than the stub's `WM_MAX_WINDOWS=32`, still succeed (`opened=40 failed=0`) — the probe **creates without showing**, so no window flashes on the desktop. ② Two rounds of "open a secondary window → pump 60 ms → close it", printing `sub_wid/primary/active_is_sub/count` and `before/after/main_running`, proving dispatch still holds with two real HWNDs: a new window becomes the active one (`active_is_sub=true`), `primary=false`, and after closing it the main window keeps `running=true` with the count back down. ③ A final `MULTIWIN-DONE` line and exit code 0. Run with `moon run experiment/multiwin_probe`; headless environments print `MULTIWIN SKIP`. Visual confirmation (occlusion/redraw between two windows, preedit inside the secondary window) stays with the user per AGENTS rule 6; the `examples/native-app` start-up smoke on Windows prints `NATIVE-APP-MW wins=1 ...` and exits 0 (clicking its buttons needs injection, i.e. W7).
- **Side fix of the same class**: the `_WIN32` branch calls `snprintf` without including `<stdio.h>`, and MSVC only warns `C4013: implicit declaration, assuming external return int` — the same silent shape as the missing `_getwcwd`. After adding the header the stub compiles warning-free.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · three-platform data roots for the history family (W14e, ported from master)

- **Ported, not re-invented**: the Windows data-root branches for browser history/bookmarks were already in `origin/master` (`bh_browser_defs_win` / `bh_mac_root` / `bh_root_win`); the original port into this branch only carried the Linux half, which is why `bh_supported`/`bm_supported` had degraded to "Linux only". Same approach as W14b: check the other branch first, and if it exists, move it over.
- **Only the data root and directory names differ; the logic is shared**: Linux = `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` else `$HOME/.config`; Windows = `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, where Chromium-family profiles sit one level deeper at `<vendor>/<product>/User Data` (that `User Data` layer does not exist on Linux; casing follows the installer, e.g. `Google/Chrome/User Data`, `Microsoft/Edge/User Data`); macOS = `$HOME/Library/Application Support/<vendor>/<product>` (no User Data layer). Profile candidates (`Default`, `Profile 1..24`), the directory scan looking for `History`/`Bookmarks`, and the SQLite/JSON parsing are one shared path across the three platforms, so only the definition table `bh_defs()` and root resolution branch by platform.
- **Evidence (real Windows machine with Chrome/Edge installed)**: `bh: profiles=2 items=5` and `bh: downloads=3` are readings from **the actual local browser databases** — on Windows this path used to be gated off and always skipped — and the `bm_bookmarks` end-to-end parse likewise flipped from "skip" to real execution; `moon test -p sys` 163/163, `moon check ./gui/sys --deny-warn` and `./examples/native-sys --deny-warn` warning-free. One stale test assertion (`bm_supported() == (platform=="linux")`) moved to the three-platform rule.
- **Rule of thumb**: `fsx_list_dir`/`sys_read_text_file` go through the wide-character routing just added in this batch, so browser stores under Chinese user directories (`C:\Users\张三\…`) are readable too — a direct consequence of W14a's "paths go UTF-8 in, wide-character APIs out".

### MoonBit native GUI stack · DirectWrite text layer (W5, Windows text lands)

- **`dwrite.h` does not compile in C — use a C++ TU**: `DWRITE_MAKE_OPENTYPE_TAG` / `DWRITE_MAKE_FONT_FEATURE_TAG` expand `static_cast` into enum initializers, so C mode fails with a train of C2275/C2065 (measured). Two options: hand-declare the COM interfaces (one wrong vtable slot away from a crash — rejected) or use a C++ translation unit. **moon's native-stub accepts `.cpp`** (probe-verified: an `extern "C"` round trip worked), so the platform split became: `stub.c` Pango branch (prebuild with `-DWM_STUB_PANGO`) + `stub.c` placeholder branch (macOS etc.) + `dwrite_text.cpp` (Windows, compiled by native-stub, dwrite.h directly visible). Link inputs are issued by prebuild for the text package: `dwrite.lib d2d1.lib ole32.lib uuid.lib gdi32.lib`. **On non-Windows platforms that `.cpp` compiles to an empty TU**, so Linux/mac build chains need a C++ front end (the old shim was C++, so this repo's environment has one).
- **The line box comes from a one-glyph layout's line metrics, not from font design metrics**: measured, a 14px default-family DWrite layout reports 19 (font ascent+descent+lineGap rounded to whole pixels), while computing from design metrics gives 17; worse, with an empty family name, taking the collection's *first* family (not the system default) is off by two more pixels — and that is exactly the number the mixed-font "line box must cover the drawn height" assertion eats. Fix: `pt_font_line_height` builds a `"M"` layout and reads `DWRITE_LINE_METRICS` (height/baseline), making the three paths — `measure()`, line height, and drawing — self-consistent (LH14=19 matches M14.h=19, baseline 15).
- **Family table sorts in byte order**: the MoonBit assertion demands strictly increasing `lexical_compare` (byte order), while DWrite's collection order varies with loading — so the C side qsorts with `strcmp` (same convention as Pango's `g_strcmp0`) and dedupes only exact-equal neighbours; names come from locale slot 0 (en-us), hence the Windows family pinned in the theme uses the English name ("Microsoft YaHei").
- **Range indices must be converted to UTF-16 code units**: MoonBit (and the Pango branch) speak **UTF-8 byte offsets**, while `DWRITE_TEXT_RANGE` wants wide-character indices — unconverted, ranges in multi-byte text fall outside and are silently swallowed (the "byte offsets, cut on bytes" assertion is red for exactly this). Conversion = count the prefix with `MultiByteToWideChar`.
- **Drawing = D2D render target + 32bpp DIB + premultiplied over**: the same `IDWriteTextLayout` is first drawn into a DIB (`Clear` to transparent, antialiasing pinned to grayscale — ClearType is subpixel rendering and would fringe on a transparent background), then composited into the MoonBit buffer with `out = src + dst·(1−srcA)` component-wise (ARGB32 little-endian matches the DIB layout, no channel swapping). Range colours require brushes created *on the render target* (D2D brushes are device-dependent objects) before `SetDrawingEffect`, so colours are snapshotted only on the draw pass; box alignment follows the Pango `pt_render_box` rules: with a width constraint the width and alignment go to the layout, single-line non-ellipsized rows take a hand-computed slack offset, vertical likewise.
- **No cairo session on the pure backend: text goes offscreen + blit**: `draw_box_at` / `AttributedText::draw_at` with `cairo_id()==None` render into their own offscreen bitmap via the buffer variants (`pt_draw_box` / `rt_draw`), then land it with `Raster::blit` — translate/clip/blend are all computed by blit.
- **Along the way, a real `Raster::blit` bug got fixed**: it fed the *device-space* rect from `rect_device` into `mt` and then composed the CTM again — the CTM was counted twice, so with a `translate` in effect the source lookup landed outside the source rect and **not a single pixel was written** (measured ink=0; identity transform worked, which is why it had stayed hidden). Fix: build `mt` in user space (`e/f` from the user-space `dx/dy`) and keep the device rect only for the scan window. render 43 / ui 110 / chart 189 all green afterwards.
- **Line-height K floor landed**: `line_height = max(engine natural, ceil(size×K))` with **K = 1.36**, measured on this machine from Microsoft YaHei at 12..32px (natural ratios 1.29..1.36, fattest sample 14px→19); mixed-font rows take the floor from the largest size in the row; the ascent (baseline) is untouched and the extra space the floor adds is absorbed by vertical centering in the box (i.e. half-leading). The two white-box assertions that encoded "natural only" (family_wbtest) were updated to the new rule.
- **Default family probed per platform into the theme**: `@theme.default_font_family()` uses "Microsoft YaHei" when present (process-level cache), otherwise falls back to the engine default (fontconfig on Linux, CoreText on macOS); `role_font` in `ui` goes through it.
- **Verification** (on Windows): text **29/29** (was 8/29), render 43, ui 110 (the 20 text/decode probe skips flipped to real runs), chart 189, theme 8, mdview 26, core 70 all green; `native-app` start-up smoke prints all readouts and exits 0; per-package `--deny-warn` warning-free; whole-repo red dots stay at 287/68. **The planned "split the text assertions into structural/numeric tiers" turned out unnecessary**: all 29 compare against the platform's own measurements and pass on both platforms (recorded so nobody redoes it).

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Windows IME pure channel (W6)

- **Protocol surface matches the GTK branch item by item**: commit/preedit are UTF-8 byte streams (capacity 255, truncated beyond), `preedit_caret` is a byte offset too, and reading a commit requires `commit_done` to clear it; in `WM_IME_COMPOSITION`, `GCS_RESULTSTR` fills commit (into the text state) while `GCS_COMPSTR` fills preedit (self-drawing only, never into the text state).
- **Three platform differences (all measured or interface facts)**: ① `WM_IME_SETCONTEXT` must strip `ISC_SHOWUICOMPOSITIONWINDOW` — this stack draws its own preedit, and without the strip Windows paints a second composition window on top of ours; ② the composition caret (`GCS_CURSORPOS`) is a **character** offset while the MoonBit side (like GTK) speaks UTF-8 **byte** offsets — convert via a `WideCharToMultiByte` prefix, otherwise the caret lands wrong for every multi-byte composition; ③ legacy IMM32 has **no surrounding-text API** (that is TSF), so `wm_im_set_surrounding` is a deliberate no-op — the GTK side feeds committed text so the IM context can infer context, while Windows IMEs take context from their own composition state (documented divergence; no fake interface on the MoonBit layer).
- **Caret and candidate window**: `wm_im_set_cursor` stores the rect and re-feeds it on `WM_IME_STARTCOMPOSITION` (some IMEs only read the position then); `ImmSetCompositionWindow(CFS_POINT)` and `ImmSetCandidateWindow(CFS_CANDIDATEPOS)` both anchor to the caret's **bottom edge** (`y + h`), which yields the familiar "candidate window at the end of the composition string" placement. `wm_im_reset` goes through `ImmNotifyIME(NI_COMPOSITIONSTR, CPS_CANCEL)` **and clears the local preedit buffer** — after reset an IME does not necessarily push another composition message, so a stale string would otherwise keep being painted (same lesson as the GTK side).
- **Evidence**: the `experiment/ime_win_probe` probe (create window → report caret rect → reset → read commit/preedit → pump 30 message rounds → clean exit) prints the expected readings (`commit=none`, empty preedit) with zero crashes; `experiment/multiwin_probe` and the `examples/native-app` smoke stay green after the new WndProc branches (exit code 0). The **real-Pinyin end-to-end** (preedit underline look, candidate window placement, commit landing in the focused box) requires injected keystrokes and belongs to W7's SendInput probe plus user verification on real hardware — this machine already has Microsoft Pinyin installed (zh-Hans-CN, the only IME), so the path is viable.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · system clipboard (W16)

- **The capability lives in `sys` (new `clipboard.mbt` + the `_WIN32` branch of `sys_stub.c`)**: Windows uses `CF_UNICODETEXT` (`OpenClipboard`/`GetClipboardData`/`GlobalLock` to read; `GlobalAlloc(GMEM_MOVEABLE)` + `SetClipboardData` to write — **after a successful set the ownership belongs to the system, so never `GlobalFree`**, the classic Win32 clipboard trap); Linux/mac go through commands (`xclip -selection clipboard` / `pbcopy`·`pbpaste`). Chinese content must take the wide path (`win_utf8_wide` plus wide→UTF-8); the A-version APIs mangle it through the ANSI code page (same as the W14 environment-variable finding).
- **Escaping hell avoided on the command line**: `pr_run` performs no shell parsing, so the explicit form is `sh -c 'printf %s "$1" | xclip -selection clipboard' sh <text>` — the text travels as **argv slot 4** (the script's `$1`) instead of being spliced into the script body, so quotes, newlines and Chinese need no escaping.
- **One link library had been missed**: the clipboard APIs live in **user32.lib**, while the sys package's Windows link flags held only `ole32.lib shell32.lib uuid.lib` — the omission shows up as a string of `LNK2019: __imp_SetClipboardData` errors, now patched (recorded: on Windows, every newly used API group needs its .lib checked).
- **Wiring goes through a kernel slot, not kernel-to-platform**: `Editor::set_clipboard(get, set)` in `input` gives the kernel an external clipboard hook — `copy`/`cut` also publish, `Ctrl+V` fetches live (falling back to the built-in `clip` when unavailable), and the kernel itself still depends on no platform layer (headless-testable). **Off by default**: the app opts in with `ui`'s `use_system_clipboard(true)` (one line each in `examples/native-app` and `examples/showcase`) — a Ctrl+X in tests must not touch the user's clipboard; when the probe reports unavailable the internal clipboard quietly stays in charge, i.e. degrade with an explicit path (the Linux probe convention is in the "Linux clipboard" entry: GtkClipboard first, xclip only for processes that never ran gtk_init).
- **Tests**: a new sys round-trip case (Chinese + newline, `set → get`) that **saves the original content and restores it after asserting** (the probe leaves no trace in the user's clipboard); on this Windows machine `moon test -p sys` is **165/165** (2 new), with ui 110/110 and input 10/10 regression-free. Real cross-application pasting (copy out, paste in Notepad, paste back) is left for user verification.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · post-mortem of the Windows "black window + not responding" (W17a, five root causes plus a perf batch)

- **Cause 1: `wm_wait` never dispatches**. The Win32 branch waited with `MsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx` and **never called `wm_pump`** (the GTK branch pumps after its poll) — with nobody dispatching, the WndProc never runs, so input, WM_CLOSE and WM_PAINT are all lost. Check: Windows flags the window as "not responding", a graceful close waits for the suicide timer (measured 15.9s; **0.9s** after the fix), and SendKeys appears to do nothing. Fix: pump right after the wait.
- **Cause 2: `wm_present` only stored a pointer**. It recorded the MoonBit pixel pointer and blitted it later from WM_PAINT — but that pointer belongs to the **local** Bitmap created inside `paint_frame`, which becomes GC bait the moment the function returns; the blit then reads dangling memory (whole window pure black). Check: a black screenshot while every drawing readout and geometry line looked perfect. Fix: the stub keeps its own frame copy (`WmWindow.frame`, a buffer grown on demand), freed in `wm_close`.
- **Cause 3: key-code convention mismatch**. The Win32 stub mapped control characters the GDK way (`0x01000000|u`) while the kernel's `KS_*` are X11 values (Tab=0xFF09, Return=0xFF0D, Backspace=0xFF08, Escape=0xFF1B, Delete=0xFFFF) — so the host never recognized Tab or Return (measured: Tab inserted into the entry as a printable character, Enter-to-submit dead). Fix: emit X11 keysyms for control characters and plain Unicode code points for printable input (CJK included).
- **Cause 4: release events were dispatched to widgets**. The kernel's `Editor::handle_key` takes only `(keysym, mods)` — it cannot tell a press from a release, so letting the release through means "one extra character per key lift" (compounding cause 3). Fix: `App::route` dispatches presses only (the host's own Tab/focus-stack handling likewise looks only at presses).
- **Cause 5 (caught by this batch's own regression sweep)**: the new viewport culling mapped the **absolute** widget rect through the CTM, double-counting the parent origin — every subtree with `oy != 0` was wrongly culled (check: ui dropped to 102/110; the widget-scene probe showed "0 ink in the lower half"). Fix: intersect using the **local** rect relative to the current origin (`rect - (ox,oy)`) — the CTM's origin sits at the parent's content origin.
- **Cause 6 (a latent out-of-bounds only exposed once input truly worked)**: the "right-click prefers an ancestor" branch of `dispatch_on_path` was written to **increment before indexing** — after walking the last path item `i` equals the length, and `path[i]` is out of bounds; on real hardware this surfaced as "right-clicking any widget panics with `PanicError`". Linux never saw it because in those cases the right-click was consumed at a deeper level and `handled` left the loop early. Fix: ancestor-priority now indexes first and increments at the end of the loop body; regression case added in `widget_wbtest` — "right-click ancestor priority: walking the full path stays in bounds, order root→leaf" (including paths with only the root level). Check: inject two left and two right clicks on real hardware — the process survives, `clicks=1` lands, and no Panic appears in the log.
- **Cause 7 (Chinese IME could not compose): the message pump lacked `TranslateMessage`**. The Win32 `wm_pump` did only `PeekMessage` + `DispatchMessage` — but legacy IME (IMM32) hooks its composition processing onto the `TranslateMessage` path: without it you get bare keys only (letter key-downs are consumed by the IME, leaving just key-ups) and never see a single `WM_IME_STARTCOMPOSITION`/`WM_IME_COMPOSITION` (measured: only `WM_IME_SETCONTEXT` arrived), so Pinyin can never compose. After adding it the probe immediately reports `preedit=[ni'h'ao …]` and `commit=[你还奥]`. Check: run `experiment/key_probe` and watch the preedit/commit lines while typing.
- **Cause 8 (Markdown ordered-list numbers sank below the baseline): the marker cell was a zero-height node**. `md_marker` set only a width, has no children and registers no measure — so its height is 0; with `hbox`'s default `align_items=Center` a zero-height cell gets placed at the row's midpoint (measured `rect=(0,111,18,0)` while the body text sits at 102..120), pushing the number half a line down with its centre exactly on the text baseline. Fix: register a text measure on the marker cell (line box from the same source as the body) and top-align it to the first line (`valign=Start`); regression test "ordered list: number and text share the baseline" in `markdown_wbtest`.
- **Performance (same batch)**: the text path went **9.4ms → 0.35ms per segment** via three changes: ① the D2D render target moved from DC to a **WIC bitmap** (a DC target costs 0.4ms just to `BindDC` per call, 1.8ms all-in per segment); ② process-level caches for canvas and brushes, grow-only; ③ a `Raster::blit` fast path for "integer translate + 1:1 whole-bitmap + Normal", with source bytes passed through a 256×256 lookup table that reproduces the generic path's unpremultiply-then-premultiply — **bit-for-bit identical**, so the pixel assertions stayed green. Whole-tree repaint fell 550ms → ~300ms (viewport culling), and the example's tick went 100ms → 500ms so each repaint cycle's time blocking the message pump falls back inside the safe window. Full-window repaints are still in the hundreds of milliseconds (the charts page is heaviest) — queued as a follow-up perf batch.
- **Two WIC canvas traps**: ① do **not** wrap an external buffer with `CreateBitmapFromMemory` and let D2D draw into it — WIC caches internally and your buffer never sees the pixels (symptom: ink=0 while the call reports success); use a self-owned bitmap and `Lock(WICBitmapLockRead)` to read back after drawing. ② Clearing the canvas with a fully transparent pen via `FillRectangle` is a **no-op** under source coverage semantics; you must `Clear` — which honours the axis-aligned clip, so only the current region gets cleared even though the cached canvas is larger.
- **How it was proven**: `experiment/key_probe` (create window → pump → print key codes, driven by PowerShell `AppActivate` + `SendKeys`) for the keyboard path; `experiment/text_bench` as the text-path perf guard; screenshots to check window content (PowerShell screen capture to PNG on this host, judged by eye); temporary PAINT-PROF/STEP-PROF instrumentation inside `App::step`/`paint_frame` located the bottleneck and was removed afterwards. Full regression: core 70 / input 10 / ui 110 / render 43 / text 29 / chart 189 / theme 8 / mdview 26 / sys 165, whole-repo red dots unchanged at 287/68.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Windows base capabilities, first batch (W20a menu bar / W20b global hotkey / W20d message box)

- **Environment and the toolchain-free verification path**: Windows 10 19045 + VS BuildTools 2022 (MSVC **14.44.35207**, under `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\...`; `C:\Program Files\...` is an empty directory that wastes the search) + SDK 10.0.26100. `vcvars64.bat` is blocked by a reg.exe policy, so compiling a pure-C probe by hand means setting `INCLUDE`/`LIB` yourself, with **Windows-style paths** (`/c/...` gets treated as a source file):
  ```bash
  MSVC='C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.44.35207'
  SDK='C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10'
  export INCLUDE="$MSVC\include;$SDK\Include\10.0.26100.0\ucrt;$SDK\Include\10.0.26100.0\shared;$SDK\Include\10.0.26100.0\um;$SDK\Include\10.0.26100.0\winrt"
  export LIB="$MSVC\lib\x64;$SDK\Lib\10.0.26100.0\ucrt\x64;$SDK\Lib\10.0.26100.0\um\x64"
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' "$MSVC/bin/Hostx64/x64/cl.exe" \
    /nologo /W4 /utf-8 /O2 /DWIN32 /D_WINDOWS /DUNICODE /D_UNICODE <probe>.c \
    /Fe:<probe>.exe user32.lib gdi32.lib imm32.lib advapi32.lib
  ```
  The pure-C probe `experiment/menu_probe/menu_backend_probe.c` `#include`s `../../gui/win/stub.c` directly — `wm_menu_bar_new` returns a **handle-table index** (1..31), not a real `HMENU`, so reading the menu structure back requires the static `wm_menus[]` table in the same TU (the first version passed the index as an `HMENU` to `GetMenuItemCount` and got `-1` everywhere).
- **A pure-C probe that includes the stub must define `-DUNICODE`/`-D_UNICODE` explicitly**: without it `IDC_ARROW` etc. are `MAKEINTRESOURCEA` forms (`LPSTR`) and the `...W` parameters emit **C4133** (`stub.c:388-396`, `646`); with it there are no new warnings (the C4996 for `wcsncpy`/`wcsncat` inside `stub.c` is pre-existing). `moon`'s native-stub already defines UNICODE (recorded in the W2 section), so the production chain never sees those two C4133s.
- **`AppendMenuW` caps a single menu at ≈1168 items** (measured here; the bulk loop starts returning 0 at item 1169), **well below the 2048-entry command-id pool**. Two rules follow: ① **a command id must only advance the cursor after the item is actually attached** — the original code did `cmd = next++` before `AppendMenuW`, so a failed add still burned an id; repeated failures (menu over the cap) exhaust the quota early and then collide with ids still in use by other menus (`WM_COMMAND` carries only the id, so a collision dispatches the click to the wrong item). Fixed to `cmd = next`, with `next = cmd + 1` only after `AppendMenuW` succeeds (wrapping to `BASE` at the pool end). ② `WM_MENU_CMD_MAX=2048` must stay **deliberately larger than the per-menu cap**: pool ≥ per-menu cap is what guarantees "filling one menu never wraps", so a single menu never collides with itself; tightening the pool to the measured cap would make a full menu hit the wrap. The probe's wrap case was rewritten accordingly — fill 2048 ids across menus, then add an item to a **fresh menu that still has room** and check it gets the wrapped-back 1000 (one menu can never drain the pool; the first assertion was unreachable).
- **`\t` inside the label is the accelerator hint**: `AppendMenuW` right-aligns everything after `\t` (verified by reading it back with `GetMenuItemInfoW`, which also checks the Chinese UTF-8→UTF-16 round trip and the `\tCtrl+Alt+Q` hint string). A real accelerator table (`TranslateAccelerator`) is not wired yet; keyboard navigation once a menu is open / shortcuts currently rely on W20b's global hotkeys.
- **The message box (W20d) is the stack's second FFI shape — "blocking"**: `MessageBoxW` shows and **modally blocks** in one call until the user clicks a button, returning the button number — no callback, no window slot; the `uType` four-field bit combination (icon + buttons) is computed by a MoonBit-side pure function and passed in (the probe measured `icon=64 btn=0 raw=327744` on real hardware). Orthogonal to the "register + poll in the pump" async shape used by menus and hotkeys.
- **Global hotkeys (W20b) go to the *thread* message queue, not a window**: `RegisterHotKey`'s `WM_HOTKEY` lands in the registering thread's queue and never reaches the WndProc — same scheme as menus, with the stub's `wm_hotkey_poll` pulled from the MoonBit pump. Accelerator-string parsing (`"CmdOrCtrl+Shift+M"` → modifier bits + virtual key code) is a three-platform-shared pure function (`CmdOrCtrl` maps to Ctrl on Win, Cmd on mac), 10/10.
- **Evidence**: the pure-C probe `experiment/menu_probe/menu_backend_probe.c` prints `MENU-BACKEND-OK` (menu bar / submenu / command ids / separator / check / nesting / Chinese label / bad parent handle / handle-table exhaustion / id wrap all pass); `experiment/menu_probe`'s MoonBit side verifies the model tree (`MENU-OK`); `core/menu_wbtest.mbt` 10/10, `win/hotkey_wbtest.mbt` 10/10 and `win/message_box_wbtest.mbt` 8/8 all really run and pass.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Windows icon loading (W20f: native .ico + PNG via WIC)

- **Three sources, three entry points**: `.ico`/`.bmp` go through `LoadImageW(LR_LOADFROMFILE)` (a native Win32 icon format, no decoding needed); PNG/JPEG/GIF have **no native entry point** and can only be decoded from memory with WIC (`CreateStream` → `InitializeFromMemory` → `CreateDecoderFromStream` → `CreateFormatConverter` to `GUID_WICPixelFormat32bppBGRA` → `CopyPixels`); already-decoded pixels go through a 32bpp top-down DIB + `CreateIconIndirect`. `wm_icon_load_file` dispatches on the extension and returns 0 if both paths fail.
- **A 32bpp HICON's alpha must be premultiplied, and `render`'s Bitmap is exactly that convention** (little-endian B,G,R,A premultiplied) — `CreateIconIndirect` blends with the color bitmap's alpha, so premultiplication is what avoids halos; the two layouts line up naturally, so pixels are a byte-for-byte `memcpy` into the DIB. Verification caveat: `GetObject`'s `bmBits` on a DIB section is **not guaranteed readable** (measured: an unusable pointer, memcmp always fails) — to read pixels back use `GetDIBits` with a **negative `biHeight`** (top-down request, matching the input row order).
- **`CLSID_WICImagingFactory` is a macro that points at Win8-only Factory2**: `wincodec.h` does `#define CLSID_WICImagingFactory CLSID_WICImagingFactory2` when `_WIN32_WINNT >= 0x0602`; for older systems take **`CLSID_WICImagingFactory1`** explicitly (identical vtable prefix, `IID_IWICImagingFactory` still v1).
- **All the GUID constants are exported from `windowscodecs.lib`** (verified with `dumpbin /linkermember`: `CLSID_WICImagingFactory1`, `IID_IWICImagingFactory`, `GUID_WICPixelFormat32bppBGRA` are all there), so win's Windows link line only adds `windowscodecs.lib ole32.lib` — no `uuid.lib` needed (`__uuidof` remains unavailable in C mode, the same pitfall as the W14 file dialog).
- **C4013 implicit declaration shows up on this path too**: `wm_icon_load_file`'s WIC fallback calls `wm_icon_from_png`, defined after it, and compiling stub.c standalone gives MSVC `C4013: undefined; assuming extern returning int` — **compiles but the reading is not trustworthy** (same family as the accent-colour pitfall). A forward declaration clears it. Lesson: for mutually-calling internal static/global functions, settle the definition order or forward-declare explicitly rather than leaning on implicit declarations.
- **Evidence**: the pure-C probe `experiment/icon_probe/icon_backend_probe.c` (`#include`s stub.c, feeds `wm_icon_*` directly, reads back with `GetIconInfo`/`GetDIBits`) ends with `ICON-BACKEND-OK`: BGRA→HICON size/bit-depth/pixel round trip, `.ico` from disk, PNG via WIC (an 8×8 RGBA translucent red decodes to 32bpp), handle-table exhaustion at 31 slots returning 0, and idempotent free all pass. The PNG asset is hand-written by `experiment/icon_probe/make_png.py` using only stdlib zlib (no Pillow). `moon test ./gui/win` is 24/24 (6 new pure-function tests: extension detection, format dispatch, handle-0 semantics, size validation).

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Windows window enhancement (W20e: retitle / window icon / min size / borderless drag region)

- **`WM_GETMINMAXINFO`'s `ptMinTrackSize` wants the whole-window size, not the client size**: the MoonBit side passes a **minimum client size** (`set_min_size(w,h)`), and the C side expands it by the non-client frame (borders + title bar) for the current style with `AdjustWindowRectEx(&r, st, FALSE, ex)` before filling `ptMinTrackSize`. Probe measurement: a minimum client width of 400 under `WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW` yields a 416-wide frame (8 px each side), and the `AdjustWindowRectEx` convention agrees with `WM_GETMINMAXINFO`.
- **A zero axis must be explicitly zeroed**: `set_min_size` allows one axis to be unconstrained (`0` = no limit on that axis). But `0` **must not** be fed into `AdjustWindowRectEx`'s rect — that computes a fake minimum of "a zero client area still occupies 2× frame width". The implementation writes `mmi->ptMinTrackSize.x = w->min_w > 0 ? (r.right - r.left) : 0;` and checks both axes; the `wm_set_min_size` entry also clamps negatives to `0` first. When only one axis is set, the other must fall back to 0 or the window gets stuck on that axis.
- **`WM_NCHITTEST` must `break`, not `return 0`**: on a hit in the self-drawn title-bar drag region it `return HTCAPTION` (handing window dragging to the system), but **outside the region it must `break` back to default handling** — the default return values of `WM_NCHITTEST` carry meaning (client area `HTCLIENT`, resize corners `HTBOTTOMRIGHT`, …), and `return 0` swallows them: measured symptom, the frame can no longer be dragged and client-area mouse behaviour goes wrong. The hit test converts `lParam`'s **screen** coordinates to client coordinates with `ScreenToClient` before comparing rects (`lParam` packs screen coordinates, not client — easy to misread) and uses a left/bottom-closed, right/top-open range (`>= x && < x+w`). Note the packed coordinates are **16-bit signed** (`(int16_t)LOWORD/HIWORD`), so negative multi-monitor coordinates still restore.
- **Read the window icon back with `WM_GETICON`**: `wm_set_icon(id, icon_slot, which)` maps `which` 0/1/2 to `ICON_BIG` / `ICON_SMALL` / both and calls `SendMessageW(hwnd, WM_SETICON, …)` directly. The probe reads back with `WM_GETICON(ICON_BIG)` and getting the same `HICON` handle proves the write took effect. **The icon handle table belongs to the caller** (W20f's slot table); the window only *uses* the `HICON`, so both the C comment and the facade docs state "the caller must keep the icon un-freed while the window shows it" — otherwise the window references a dangling handle. Passing `icon_slot=0` clears the icon.
- **Borderless = restyle, then recompute the frame from the client size + `SWP_FRAMECHANGED`**: ON drops `WS_CAPTION|WS_THICKFRAME|WS_MINIMIZEBOX|WS_MAXIMIZEBOX|WS_SYSMENU|WS_BORDER|WS_DLGFRAME` and switches to `WS_POPUP` (keeping `WS_MINIMIZEBOX` so minimizing still works); OFF restores `WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW`. **Two key steps**: ① capture the current client rect with `GetClientRect` first, recompute the frame with `AdjustWindowRectEx` under the new style, then `SetWindowPos(..., SWP_NOMOVE|SWP_NOZORDER|SWP_FRAMECHANGED)` — without `SWP_FRAMECHANGED` the non-client area is not recomputed and the window size jumps; ② make it idempotent via `w->borderless`, returning early on a same-value call (otherwise every call runs `SetWindowPos` for nothing). Probe verification: after borderless there is no `WS_CAPTION` in `GWL_STYLE`, and the client width is still 640 (unchanged).
- **Runtime retitle goes through `SetWindowTextW`**: `wm_set_title` converts UTF-8 to UTF-16 then calls `SetWindowTextW`; the probe reads back with `GetWindowTextW` to check the Chinese title's UTF-8→UTF-16 round trip.
- **Evidence**: the pure-C probe `experiment/window_probe/window_enhance_probe.c` (`#include`s stub.c, creates a real window then reads `SendMessageW(WM_GETMINMAXINFO/WM_NCHITTEST)` directly and `GetWindowTextW`/`WM_GETICON`/`GWL_STYLE` back) ends with `WIN-ENHANCE-OK` (all 40 assertions pass): `SetWindowTextW` takes effect (Chinese), `ptMinTrackSize.x == 416` (client 400 + frame), multi-monitor negative coordinates hit / open-interval boundary, in-region returns `HTCAPTION` and out-of-region returns `HTCLIENT`, `WM_GETICON(ICON_BIG)` equals the icon passed in, no `WS_CAPTION` after borderless with the client width unchanged, and an out-of-range id neither crashes nor writes the buffer. Example wiring: `examples/native-app` gained a window-enhancement section (retitle / self-drawn icon / borderless toggle / drag-band toggle) and an exit status line `NATIVE-APP-WIN title='…' min=… drag=… bl=… icon=…`, and `moon build` produces `native-app.exe`. `moon test ./gui/win` 24/24, `moon check ./gui/win ./examples/native-app --deny-warn` warning-free, the C backend clean under MSVC `/W4`.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Windows system tray (W20c: Shell_NotifyIconW + W20a menus for the right-click popup)

- **A tray icon is "one HWND + one uID"**: `Shell_NotifyIconW` posts callback messages to the window in `NOTIFYICONDATAW.hWnd`, with `wParam` = `uID` and `lParam` = the mouse message. This side therefore creates its own **hidden message window** (`yue_wm_tray` class + `HWND_MESSAGE`, lazily and idempotently), and the slot number *is* the `uID` (1-based, slot 0 unused; `WM_MAX_TRAYS=8`).
- **`WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN` strips out `shellapi.h`**: `Shell_NotifyIconW` / `NOTIFYICONDATAW` / `NIM_*` / `NIF_*` all live there, so it must be included explicitly (same treatment as `imm.h`). The link line gains **`shell32.lib`** (it is not in `user32`/`gdi32`) — missing it means `LNK2019 __imp_Shell_NotifyIconW`.
- **The callback message is `WM_APP+2`, and again "C never calls back into MoonBit"**: `WM_APP+1` is already taken by `wm_wakeup`'s waker window (that `case WM_APP + 1:` in `stub.c`), so the tray takes `WM_APP+2`. Hits (`WM_LBUTTONUP`/`WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK` → left, `WM_RBUTTONUP` → right) go into a process-level ring queue that the host drains each tick with `wm_tray_poll` — the same scheme as menus and hotkeys, avoiding the trampoline-arity pitfalls. Non-click messages (e.g. `WM_MOUSEMOVE`) are not enqueued.
- **The right-click menu reuses W20a's HMENU handle table, so "tray menus" and "window menus" share one dispatch chain**: `wm_menu_popup_new()` builds a popup root (differing from `wm_menu_bar_new` only in `CreatePopupMenu` vs `CreateMenu`), core's `menu_translate_into` fills it as usual, and popping uses `TrackPopupMenuEx(menu, TPM_RIGHTBUTTON|TPM_RETURNCMD|TPM_NONOTIFY, x, y, tray_hwnd, NULL)` — **`TPM_RETURNCMD` hands the selected item back as the return value**, and pushing it into `wm_menu_push` rejoins `dispatch_menu_command()`'s callback table without relying on the tray window's `WM_COMMAND` routing. Both Microsoft conventions are followed: `SetForegroundWindow(tray_hwnd)` before showing, `PostMessage(hwnd, WM_NULL, 0, 0)` after — otherwise the menu may fail to dismiss (focus is not handed back).
- **`szTip` is a fixed 128-wide-character array, so long text must be truncated**: the tooltip write uses `wcsncpy_s(nid.szTip, 128, wtip, _TRUNCATE)` — a bare `wcsncpy` draws **C4996** (the same family as the two W20a menu-label sites). The `_s` variant was chosen deliberately, and the whole tray section is **warning-free under MSVC `/W4`**.
- **Backend selection: Linux SNI first, the Windows stub here, `Err(Unsupported)` if neither**. SNI availability uses the **new** `@dbus.sni_watcher_present()` (bus reachable **and** `NameHasOwner(org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher)`), a stronger test than the existing `@dbus.sni_available()` (which only checks the "bus reachable" candidate condition) — on a stock GNOME without the AppIndicator extension the bus is up but the watcher is absent, so the tray is genuinely unavailable. **The GTK branch deliberately returns 0**: Linux trays go through the SNI protocol stack, not GTK3's `GtkStatusIcon` (deprecated and not honored by panels), the same reason W20f's icon loading returns 0 there.
- **The facade lives in `core/tray.mbt`, so core gains `sys` and `dbus` dependencies** (the former for `desktop_environment()` reading `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, the latter for SNI). This matches the W20a decision to put the menu model in core: core is the "cross-platform capability facade" layer, and platform backends only do "model → native" translation. The old chain's same-named `TrayError` lives in the retiring `yue/error.mbt`; the new-stack definition lives in this file.
- **The exit-readout pitfall (fixed along the way)**: the example's exit status lines print **after the window has closed**, by which time the backend slot has been `memset` — `NATIVE-APP-WIN title='' min=0x0 …` was all zeros because it was reading a destroyed window. Fixed by snapshotting the live readouts into a `Ref[String]` each tick and printing the last "while alive" snapshot at exit (measured: `title='' min=0x0` → `title='MoonBit App 宿主 (批次1)' min=900x600`). Rule of thumb: **to report runtime state at exit, sample it while running — do not expect to read it after teardown.**
- **Evidence**: the pure-C probe `experiment/tray_probe/tray_backend_probe.c` (`#include`s stub.c, feeds `wm_tray_*` directly) ends with **`TRAY-BACKEND-OK`**, all 28 assertions passing: `wm_tray_supported()==1`, a **real `Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_ADD)` succeeds**, tooltip Chinese UTF-8→UTF-16 round trip plus a 299-char truncation under 127 without overrunning, `wm_menu_popup_new` returning a real `HMENU` attached to the tray, **posting `WM_TRAY_CB` to the tray message window to verify left kind=0 / right kind=1 / matching slot / non-click messages not enqueued**, `wm_tray_popup`'s guard paths (invalid slot, no menu) returning 0 immediately without blocking (`TrackPopupMenuEx` blocks, so a real popup needs a human click — hence guards only), slot-table exhaustion (0 after 7 slots), and idempotent removal returning the count to 0. `moon test ./gui/core` is **99/99** (6 new pure-function tests: `basename_no_ext` across path shapes/empty/trailing dot/multiple dots, non-empty desktop name, the three `TrayError` shows; plus **1 lifecycle test**: create → `tray_count()==1` → tooltip read-back matches → attach menu (popup handle filled in) → remove → `tray_count()==0`, auto-skipping rather than faking on machines with no tray backend). `examples/native-app` gains a tray section (five buttons: create / retip / attach menu / popup / remove, plus a state counter) and an exit status line `NATIVE-APP-TRAY supported=… backend=… count=… clicks=… note=…`, with `dispatch_tray_event()` called each tick in the main loop. Real-hardware smoke: `exit 0`, `NATIVE-APP-TRAY supported=1 backend=- count=0 clicks=0 note=-` (nothing created since no button was clicked; `supported=1` confirms the Win32 tray backend is available). Whole-repo `moon check` red dots hold at **287/68**, and gui/{core,win,dbus,ui,render,text,theme,icons,input,mdview,chart} are all green.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Windows desktop notifications (W21a: tray balloon NIF_INFO + a freedesktop cross-platform facade)

- **Win32 "notifications" have no standalone API — a notification *is* a balloon attached to a tray icon**: `NIM_ADD` creates the tray item, then `NIM_MODIFY` with `NIF_INFO` plus `szInfoTitle`/`szInfo` pops the balloon (since Vista the system turns these balloons into Action Center toasts). This section therefore **reuses W20c's tray slot table and message window**, distinguishing them with the new `WmTray.kind`: `kind == 0` = tray icon (receives clicks), `kind == 1` = notification balloon (pops only, receives no clicks). The notification id is thus naturally the owning tray slot number (>=1).
- **Notification slots must be explicitly excluded from the click queue**: `wm_tray_wndproc` gained a `wm_trays[slot].kind == 0` guard when handling `WM_TRAY_CB`, so a `kind == 1` slot drops clicks outright — a balloon's click semantics are undefined (Windows handles toast clicks itself, not via `uCallbackMessage`), and enqueueing anyway would dispatch to a slot that is not a tray icon. The probe posts `WM_LBUTTONUP`/`WM_RBUTTONUP` to a notification slot and confirms the queue stays empty.
- **"Dismissing a balloon" has no standalone API; follow the official convention of sending `NIF_INFO` again with an empty `szInfo`**: `wm_notify_close` first sends that empty-body `NIM_MODIFY` (the system retracts the balloon), then `NIM_DELETE` removes the tray item — both steps are needed, and `NIM_DELETE` alone does not guarantee the balloon disappears immediately. It is idempotent: a repeat close hits the "slot already empty" guard and returns.
