- **Two platform differences degrade explicitly rather than pretending to align** (documented in the `core/notify.mbt` header and here): ① **`uTimeout` is ignored by the system since Vista**, so a balloon's dwell time is set by the system's accessibility settings and `timeout_ms` exists only for signature parity with the Linux side — it has no effect here; ② **a Win32 balloon has no "progress hint"**, whereas Linux's freedesktop `value` hint lets the desktop draw a progress bar, so the facade pastes the percentage into the body (`notify_body_with_progress`, a visible degradation rather than a silent drop).
- **`kind`'s three states map to `NIIF_*`**: 0 info / 1 warning / 2 error → `NIIF_ERROR` / `NIIF_WARNING` / `NIIF_INFO` (the system status icon at the balloon's left). This is a hard-coded one-line ternary, and **Win32 has no interface to read `dwInfoFlags` back**, so the probe can only verify that all three kinds dispatch successfully; the mapping itself is covered by code review (stated honestly in the probe's header comment).
- **`szInfoTitle` is a fixed 64-wide-character array and `szInfo` a 256-wide-character one**: writes always use `wcsncpy_s(..., _TRUNCATE)` (a bare `wcsncpy` draws C4996, same family as W20a/W20c). `WmTray.ntitle[64]` keeps a copy of the title for read-back (`wm_notify_title`, UTF-8 output).
- **Tray-icon slots and notification slots share one `WM_MAX_TRAYS=8` table, but their counts are fully decoupled**: `wm_tray_count()` counts only `kind == 0` and `wm_notify_count()` only `kind == 1`. The probe verifies "1 tray + 3 notifications = 4 slots used", "only 3 more succeed once the table is full", and "removing the tray icon does not affect the notification count". Allocation goes through the unified `wm_tray_alloc(kind, icon_slot, tip)`, with `wm_tray_new` delegating at `kind=0`.
- **Facade layering**: `win/notify.mbt` is the thin Windows-side wrapper (`notify_supported`/`notify_send`/`notify_update`/`notify_close`/`notify_count`/`notify_title` plus the `NOTIFY_INFO/WARNING/ERROR` constants); `core/notify.mbt` is the **cross-platform facade** — backend selection is Linux freedesktop D-Bus (`dbus/notify.mbt`) first → Win32 tray balloon → `Err(NotifyError::Unsupported)` if neither. The cross-platform API is `notify_send(app_name, summary, body, icon?, timeout_ms?, replaces_id?, progress?, kind?, icon_handle?)`, where `icon` is a Linux theme icon name and `icon_handle` a Win32 W20f icon handle (0 = use the system status icon). When `replaces_id > 0`, the Win32 side tries `notify_update` first (re-sending on the same slot replaces it).
- **Evidence**: the pure-C probe `experiment/notify_probe/notify_backend_probe.c` (`#include`s stub.c, feeds `wm_notify_*` directly) ends with **`NOTIFY-BACKEND-OK`**, all **37 assertions passing**: `wm_notify_supported()==1`, a **real `Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_MODIFY)` balloon**, Chinese title UTF-8→UTF-16 round trip plus a 399-char truncation under 63 without overrunning, **notification-slot clicks not entering the tray queue**, all three kinds dispatching successfully, **1 tray + 3 notifications sharing the table with decoupled counts**, a new send returning 0 once the table is full (7 slots), closing decrementing by one and idempotent, and invalid/tray slots returning 0 or no-op for the notification APIs. `moon test ./gui/core` is **108/108** (9 new: `notify_clamp_kind` clamped to 0..2, `notify_clamp_pct` clamped to 0..100, `notify_body_with_progress` leaving negative progress alone / appending to the body / clamping the percentage, the two `NotifyError` shows, backend name matching the enum, and `notify_caps` in both the with/without-backend states; plus **1 lifecycle test**: send → update progress → close → idempotent re-close, auto-skipping on machines with no notification backend). `examples/native-app` gains a notification section (five buttons: info / warning / error / 60% progress / close, plus a state counter) and an exit status line `NATIVE-APP-NOTIFY supported=… backend=… sends=… id=… count=… note=…` (the `count=` is snapshotted each tick for the same reason as W20c's exit-readout pitfall). Real-hardware smoke: `exit 0`, `NATIVE-APP-NOTIFY supported=1 backend=win-balloon sends=0 id=0 count=0 note=-` (nothing sent since no button was clicked; `backend=win-balloon` confirms the backend selection). Whole-repo `moon check` red dots hold at **287/68**, and gui/{core,win,dbus,ui,render,text,theme,icons,input,mdview,chart} are all green.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · self-drawn message box (W21b: `@ui.message_box_t`, coexisting with the W20d native tier)

- **The self-drawn and native tiers are two roads that complement rather than replace each other**: `@win.show_message_box` (W20d) goes through `MessageBoxW` — system look, system modality, a **blocking** return code, but **Win32 only** (a stub on macOS); `@ui.message_box_t` (this batch) is fully self-drawn, honours the theme, is **non-blocking** (each button calls back with its code), and is one code path across all three platforms. Callers pick per need, and the semantic surfaces line up (title / text / informative sub-line / multiple buttons / response callback).
- **Response codes are supplied by the caller, not borrowed from Win32's 1..7**: `buttons` is a list of `(label, response code)` and the component passes the code straight back. The native tier's `Ok(1)/Cancel(2)/…/No(7)` is `MessageBoxW`'s return-value convention, and the self-drawn tier must not be tied to it — the **two numbering schemes are deliberately not interoperable**, which is why the status output splits into `NATIVE-APP-MSGBOX` (native) and `NATIVE-APP-MSGBOX2` (self-drawn).
- **✕ / Esc / clicking the mask = dismiss without a code** (via `on_dismiss`): `MessageBoxW`'s ✕ maps to `IDCANCEL`, but the self-drawn tier does not borrow that (see above); if "cancel counts as a result", the caller adds its own cancel button. `close_on_mask` defaults to **false** — a message box usually demands an explicit answer, and closing on a stray click into empty space invites mistakes.
- **Enter = the first button** (same meaning as the native tier's `default_index=0`). For Esc/Enter to arrive at all, the box must **take over focus**: on open it allocates an id from 700000 upward via `msgbox_alloc_focus_id()` and calls `focus.register` + `focus.focus` on `@core.host_active()`, with the panel itself as the focus widget (it sits deeper than the scrim, so keys reach it first); on teardown it `unregister`s and **hands the pre-open focus back**. Starting at 700000 avoids the low ids callers commonly use (the example uses 1..25) — **focus ids are a global namespace, so a component allocating its own must leave room**. After the focus stack became "realigned from the widget tree every round" (see 《Keyboard focus was dead everywhere》 at the end of this file) this `register` still holds: in the layer tier the panel is in this window's tree anyway, so realignment only keeps it.
- **An enum variant must not be called `None` (a compile-time collateral hit this batch)**: `MsgBoxKind` was first written with a `None` variant, and immediately every `Store::new(None)` elsewhere **in the same package** started inferring as `MsgBoxKind::None`, producing 6 type errors in `datetime_wbtest`. The cause: in positions with **no expected type** such as `Store::new(None)`, a same-named constructor gets picked up. Renaming it to `Default` cleared it. Lesson: before adding an enum to a package, **check whether the variant name already has an expected-type-free use in that package** (`None` above all, then names that clash with `SemanticType` such as `Warning`).
- **Relation to `dialog_t`**: both share the same overlay machinery in `core/overlay.mbt` (full-window scrim / centring / close-on-outside-click / relayout on open), differing in semantic surface — `dialog_t` is a *content dialog* (arbitrary content tree + confirm/cancel exits) while `message_box_t` is a *message box* (kind-driven icon + informative sub-line + any number of buttons each carrying a code). Content dialogs still go through `dialog_t`; this batch **did not** merge the two.
- **Evidence**: `ui/message_box_wbtest.mbt` adds **8 tests** (3 pure: the five kinds' icon names / distinct colours / default-button code; 5 runtime: Store-driven open-close + panel centring + the four-region structure + button callback code and close + ✕/Esc taking dismiss while Enter takes the default button + both `close_on_mask` states + an empty informative leaving no sub-line + empty-label buttons skipped), using a headless widget tree with a manually installed overlay host (as in `overlay_wbtest`) — **no real window needed**. `moon test ./gui/ui` is **118/118** (was 110). `examples/native-app` gains a self-drawn message-box section (three buttons: info / warning / error, each driving its own box) and an exit status line `NATIVE-APP-MSGBOX2 shots=… last=… ovl=…` (the `ovl=` is the last snapshot of the live overlay count, for the same reason as W20c's exit-readout pitfall); real-hardware smoke: `exit 0`, `NATIVE-APP-MSGBOX2 shots=0 last=- ovl=0 native_ovl=0` (nothing popped since no button was clicked). `moon check ./gui/ui ./examples/native-app --deny-warn` is warning-free, and whole-repo red dots hold at **287/68**.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · drag-and-drop facade (W21c: `core/drag.mbt` session model + `@ui.drag_source`/`drop_target`)

- **In-app drag and drop is fully self-drawn and one code path across all three platforms**: the old chain's drag source / drop target were **platform callbacks** (GTK `gtk_drag_*` / Win32 `IDropTarget`) requiring three separate handlers for enter/update/leave; in-app drag and drop in this stack touches no platform interface — the session model lives in `core/drag.mbt` (process-level) and the two declarative hooks in `ui/drag.mbt`. **Cross-application** system-level drag (dragging out of the window / accepting OS files) still ships with the platform batch; the facade's interface shape is settled, so the UI side will not change once a backend lands.
- **The payload is our own type, not a platform image type**: `DragData{Text,Html,Paths,Img}`; `Img` holds **raw PNG bytes** rather than a platform image handle — the model layer carries no platform types, which is what lets payloads travel across backends/processes. `DataKind{Text,Html,Image,FilePaths}` each get a stable id (1/2/3/4), and `drag_encode`/`drag_decode` pack `[kind:i32 LE][payload]` (`Paths` joined with `\n`) — the stable ABI for future cross-process/cross-backend payloads.
- **The session is a process-level singleton and drop targets are resolved in window coordinates**: only one drag runs at a time (`drag_current`). The landing point is found by `Widget::drop_target_at`, scanning back-to-front for the **deepest** visible widget carrying `on_drop`; the hover highlight is drawn by the painter reading `@core.drag_hover()` — which **removes the enter/update/leave trio** and with it the "missed leave callback" state-sync problem (the old chain's chronic issue).
- **Press-capture semantics differ from the wrapper's identity (a trap hit this batch, do not conflate them)**: on `Down`, `route_pointer` records the captured id as the **deepest** widget on the hit path (same meaning as a Web `pointerdown` target); the drag source wrapper's `on_pointer` receives the event by **bubbling** (the content widget does not handle the pointer itself, so it travels up). Hence `@core.drag_source()` records the **wrapper** id while the captured id is the **content widget** id — test assertions must distinguish the two (one was first written asserting equality with the wrapper id).
- **Do not put buttons inside a drag source**: pointer events go **deepest-first**, so an interactive child swallows the press first and the drag never starts. A drag source should contain display items only (text / icons / thumbnails). **This is a usage constraint, not a bug.**
- **`payload()` is lazy**: it is only called once the **threshold** is crossed (4px by default); below the threshold the press is released as an ordinary click, so selection/clicks inside the content are unaffected. When `payload()` returns `None` the drag does not materialise, again falling back to an ordinary press.
- **`derive(Eq)` on a value type trips the `implicit_impl_as_method` warning** (this batch's compile-time trap): the correct form is a hand-written `pub impl Eq for DataKind with fn equal(self, other) -> Bool` plus `pub extend DataKind with Eq::{not_equal, equal}`. Note the implementation function is **`fn equal`** (writing `op_equal` first makes the compiler report `no method op_equal in trait Eq`). `DragData` does not go through `Eq` (it holds `Bytes`/`Array`) nor implement `Debug`, so tests observe it via strings/ids.
- Another implementation trap (recorded): `Bytes` has no `op_set` and `raw[4:...]` yields a `BytesView` that cannot be sliced directly — assemble bytes with `FixedArray::make` + `Bytes::from_array`; `split("\n")` yields an `Iter[StringView]` and needs `.map(fn(s){ s.to_owned() })` to become an `Array[String]`.
- **Evidence**: `core/drag_wbtest.mbt` has **6 tests** (id round trip, `DragData::kind`/`as_text`, encode/decode round trip and bad input, `drop_target_at` deepest hit, session `begin→move→drop`, no-target/reject/`cancel`, and a constant no-target result when there is no root); `ui/drag_wbtest.mbt` has **4 tests** (press → cross threshold → drag → move onto target → release delivers, below-threshold press behaving as an ordinary click / release over blank not delivering, `accept` rejecting so the callback does not run, and `payload` returning `None` producing no session), all driven through the host's `@core.route_pointer` (including press capture) — **no real window needed**. `moon test ./gui/core` is **115/115** and `moon test ./gui/ui` is **122/122**. `examples/native-app` gains a drag-and-drop section (two sources "text payload / paths payload" plus two targets "accept all / paths only") and an exit status line `NATIVE-APP-DRAG drags=… drops=… active=… last=…`; real-hardware smoke: `exit 0`, `NATIVE-APP-DRAG drags=0 drops=0 active=0 last=-` (nothing dragged, so the counters are 0). `moon check ./gui/core ./gui/ui ./examples/native-app --deny-warn` is warning-free, and whole-repo red dots hold at **287/68**.
- **Not done this batch, not pretending otherwise**: cross-application system-level drag (dragging out / accepting OS files, deferred to the platform batch), drag-time visual feedback (a ghost thumbnail following the pointer — currently only the target highlight is drawn), the macOS backend, and the real-hardware feel of dragging (tracked in `_人工测试清单.md`).

### MoonBit native GUI stack · autostart at login (W21d: `sys/autostart.mbt`, facade in MoonBit, C only for Windows)

- **Division of labour**: the **cross-platform surface lives in MoonBit** — Linux (and other XDG desktops) assembles `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autostart/<app_id>.desktop` and writes it to disk (pure string assembly plus the existing text-file read/write entries in `fsx.mbt`, so no platform interface at all); **only Windows needs C** — HKCU's Run key is reachable only through the registry API (`RegOpenKeyExW` / `RegQueryValueExW` / `RegSetValueExW` / `RegDeleteValueW`), see the autostart section of `sys/sys_stub.c`. macOS is explicitly `Unsupported` this batch (it needs a LaunchAgents plist; deferred to real hardware).
- **The value's shape is a platform convention, not an arbitrary string**: a Linux `.desktop` Exec must be **wrapped in double quotes** as a whole (with `\` and `"` backslash-escaped inside and `%` written `%%`); a Windows REG_SZ value likewise needs the **whole string quoted** — a path with spaces and no quotes gets truncated at the first word when launched at login (i.e. it autostarts a program that does not exist). The quotes are assembled on the MoonBit side (`autostart_escape_exec` / `autostart_run_value`) and the C stub **writes and reads them verbatim**, with no second pass of processing.
- **Idempotency is part of the contract**: a repeated `enable` is an overwrite (the `.desktop` on Linux, the same-named Run value on Windows), and `disable` also succeeds when the entry was never there (Linux relies on `yue_sys_remove_file`'s probe-then-delete; Windows treats both `RegDeleteValueW`'s `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` and "the key itself is missing" as success).
- **app_id validation is a shared precondition of both landing points**: the app_id doubles as the `.desktop` filename and the Windows Run value name, so the DBus well-known-name character set is reused (≥2 dot-separated elements, each starting with a letter/underscore, only `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, total length ≤255). **`sys` does not depend on `dbus` in reverse**, so the rule is implemented locally in `sys/autostart.mbt` (`autostart_valid_app_id`). **A misconception worth recording**: an element **must not start** with `-` or a digit, but **may contain** them — `com.example.my-app2` is valid while `com.2app` and `com.-app` are not. A test first treated "contains `-`" as invalid (asserting `com.ap-p` to be false, though it is in fact valid); the run corrected it.
- **Link surface**: the `Reg*` family lives in **advapi32.lib**, while `sys`'s Windows link line previously carried only `ole32/shell32/uuid/user32` (those serve the file dialog's COM). This batch adds `advapi32.lib` to the sys entry (`scripts/prebuild.py`-managed; no link parameters inside the package).
- **Two things the pure-C probe provides itself** (`experiment/autostart_probe/autostart_backend_probe.c`): ① **the probe ships its own `moonbit_make_bytes`** — a pure-C probe does not link the moon runtime, yet `yue_sys_*` returns moon byte strings; a self-consistent layout suffices (the length sits in the **4 bytes before** the data pointer, matching the real `moonbit_object` header), with the real ABI interaction covered by the whitebox tests. ② **The `stub.c` include order defeats `_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS`** — the probe includes `<windows.h>` first (which already pulls in `string.h`), and UCRT decides at that instant whether to warn about deprecated names, so the stub's two `wcscpy`/`wcscat` sites produce 2 C4996 warnings in the probe build. That is **an artifact of the probe's include order, not a code problem**: the real build has moon's native-stub include `sys_stub.c` first, so the macro takes effect and no such warning appears.
- **Evidence**: the pure-C probe ends with **`AUTOSTART-BACKEND-OK`**, all **36 assertions passing**: `yue_sys_exe_path` matching an independent `GetModuleFileNameW` call character for character (including the `.exe` suffix and backslashes), ok=0 when unwritten, a write followed by the **probe's own** `RegQueryValueExW` read confirming it landed under `Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run` with type `REG_SZ` and a byte-identical value, overwrite / Chinese-path round trip / empty value (length 0 yet present) / a 1207-character long value, `NULL` arguments returning -1 from all three entry points, an independent read after removal showing `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`, and a second idempotent removal still succeeding. **The probe really writes the user's registry** (that is its point); it deletes its own exclusive value `com.moonbit.native-gui.autostart_cprobe` both on entry and on exit, cleaning up regardless of outcome (checked afterwards with `reg query`; no residue). `sys/autostart_wbtest.mbt` has **8 tests**: 6 pure (directory resolution in three states / Exec escaping / `.desktop` content and parsing in both states / Run value shape and its inverse / app_id validation / the error `Show`) + 1 "an invalid app_id is rejected first on every platform" + **1 real lifecycle** (cleanup → not enabled → enable → enabled → the landing point reads back (the `.desktop` body on Linux, the Run value on Windows, inverted and compared against the exe) → repeated enable is idempotent → disable → not enabled → idempotent disable again), skipping rather than faking when `autostart_supported()` is false. `moon test ./gui/sys` runs **174, 173 pass, 1 red** — that one is the **pre-existing** `fsx_wbtest.mbt:109` (the `sys_make_dirs` case was already red on Windows: `pr_available()` is true there, yet the case used the POSIX `/tmp` plus `pr_run("rm"/"mkdir")`; re-checked with `git stash` on a pristine tree, same single red, unrelated to this batch). **Since fixed** — `sys_make_dirs` is now the C thin FFI `yue_sys_make_dirs` and the case itself is platform-portable; `sys` is 178/178. `examples/native-sys` gains "enable autostart / disable autostart" buttons and a status line, plus the exit readout `NATIVE-SYS-AUTOSTART supported=1 enabled=0 id=… exe=… on_hits=0 note=…` (`is_enabled` reads the disk/registry live, so it still works after the window closes, unlike window readouts); real-hardware smoke: `exit 0` (no button clicked, so `enabled=0` and no registry residue). `moon check ./gui/sys ./examples/native-sys --deny-warn` is warning-free; the C side under MSVC `/W4` keeps only the 2 C4996 warnings explained above; whole-repo red dots hold at **287/68**.
- **Not done this batch, not pretending otherwise**: macOS (a LaunchAgents plist, left as Unsupported), launch arguments and delayed start (Windows could use the `**` prefix or `schtasks` with a delay, Linux could add `X-GNOME-Autostart-Delay` — not written here), capability probing beyond `is_supported`, and the real-hardware feel of autostart (tracked in `_人工测试清单.md`).

### MoonBit native GUI stack · user idle detection (W21e: `sys/idle.mbt`, read-only seconds, no binary state)

- **The interface reports seconds only, with no active/idle binary**: `idle_seconds() -> Result[Double, IdleError]` returns the **seconds since the last input**, and threshold decisions are left to the caller — screen-awake, lock-screen and power-saving each want very different thresholds, and a number picked for the caller in the library would just be worked around. Conversion and clamping (negatives to zero) live in the pure MoonBit functions `idle_clamp_ms` / `idle_ms_to_seconds`; the stub returns only the raw milliseconds.
- **Platform data sources come in three tiers (all in the idle section of `sys/sys_stub.c`)**: Windows uses `GetLastInputInfo` + `GetTickCount`; Linux uses the X11 **XScreenSaver extension (XSS)**; macOS is not implemented this batch (always false / `Unsupported`).
- **Windows: the difference must be an unsigned modular subtraction, not an int64 subtraction** (this batch's key rule). `GetTickCount()` is 32-bit and wraps about every **49.7 days**. The correct form is `DWORD elapsed = GetTickCount() - li.dwTime;` — unsigned subtraction is inherently modulo 2³², so it stays correct across the wrap point; converting each side to int64 first yields a huge negative number at the wrap (a negative idle time once converted to seconds). The pure-C probe pins this semantic down with synthetic values (`0x10 - 0xFFFFFFF0 == 0x20`).
- **Linux: runtime dlopen, with no X link dependency**. `sys`'s Linux link line carries only pthread/dl/m/stdc++ — **a headless consumer should not be tied to X libraries** — so XSS goes entirely through `dlopen("libX11.so.6"/".so")` + `dlopen("libXss.so.1"/".so")` and `dlsym` for `XOpenDisplay` / `XDefaultRootWindow` / `XScreenSaverAllocInfo` / `XScreenSaverQueryInfo` / `XFree` / `XCloseDisplay`. The `XScreenSaverInfo` struct is **declared locally in the stub** (rather than including `X11/extensions/scrnsaver.h`, which would drag in X headers); symbols are fetched through a `void*` hop (`memcpy`) to dodge `-Wcast-function-type`. The result is cached in a static `g_idle_x11` (a `tried` flag guards against repeated probing).
- **A Wayland session gets "unsupported" rather than a wrong number**: with no X server (`DISPLAY` empty) `idle_supported()` is false outright. Under XWayland, input events do not reach the X server, so XSS readings only ever **overstate** — better to report nothing than a value that would mislead the caller (exactly why "seconds only" pairs with `Result`: treating failure as 0 seconds reads as "just moved").
- **Supportability and this call's outcome are two separate tiers**: `idle_supported()` is a runtime capability probe (Windows always true; Linux needs `DISPLAY` non-empty and both libraries dlopened; macOS false). Inside `idle_seconds()`, `ok=1` gives `Ok`; otherwise it **consults `idle_supported()`** — true means `Err(Failed("空闲查询失败"))` (idle query failed, e.g. an X connection dropping mid-flight), false means `Err(Unsupported)`. Keeping them apart is what lets the caller distinguish "this machine has no such capability" from "this particular query failed".
- **Evidence**: the pure-C probe `experiment/idle_probe/idle_backend_probe.c` ends with **`IDLE-BACKEND-OK`**, all **13 assertions passing**: supportability always 1, the reading non-negative and within int32 (no truncation), matching an **independently recomputed** `GetTickCount() - li.dwTime` (within ±2000ms, tolerating the call gap and GetTickCount granularity), consecutive reads non-decreasing, the modular-subtraction semantic on synthetic values (wrap included), five consecutive reads all succeeding, and the `ok` out-parameter written every call. The probe only reads system state and writes nothing (one fewer self-provided artifact than W21d: the idle interface returns no moon byte string, so it needs no bundled `moonbit_make_bytes`). Build recipe in the probe header (add `user32.lib` — `GetLastInputInfo` lives in user32; and because `#include sys_stub.c` pulls in the registry functions, link `advapi32.lib` along with it). `sys/idle_wbtest.mbt` has **4 tests**: 3 pure (millisecond clamping / milliseconds-to-seconds / error `Show`) + 1 "supportability probe" (asserts true on Windows, merely prints elsewhere) + 1 "reading non-negative and two consecutive reads monotonic (a decrease can only mean an input zeroed it in between, and then the new value is necessarily <0.05s)". `moon test ./gui/sys` runs **178, 177 pass, 1 red** — that one is the **pre-existing** `fsx_wbtest.mbt:109` (unrelated to this batch; re-checked on a pristine tree in the previous batch). **Since fixed** — see the revisit of the "C stub on demand and minimal" entry above. `examples/native-sys` gains a "read idle" button and status line, and the exit readout `NATIVE-SYS-IDLE supported=1 seconds=2486.141 hits=0 note=…`; real-hardware smoke: `exit 0`, and `NATIVE-SYS-GEO` includes `idle=1786,368,110x32` (the button laid out). `moon check ./examples/native-sys` is warning-free; the repo-wide red count stays at **287/68**.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · cross-platform global-hotkey facade (W22: `core/hotkey.mbt`, the last of the three service facades)

- **W22's scope, tightened**: under "unify the tray / notification / hotkey facades", the tray (`core/tray.mbt`) and notifications (`core/notify.mbt`) facades already landed in W20c/W21a, and this batch **does not refactor their existing APIs** (changing error types and probe names would be a purely breaking change with zero caller benefit). What was genuinely missing was that **hotkeys had no cross-platform facade at all** — W20b landed only in the win package (free functions such as `register_global_shortcut` plus the `parse_accelerator` pure function), leaving Linux/macOS callers with no way to write isomorphic code. So W22 = add `core/hotkey.mbt`, shaped like the other two facades: **probe `hotkey_supported()` + structured error `HotkeyError{Unsupported, Failed(String)}` + pump hook `hotkey_poll()`**.
- **Current backends and the degradation contract**: Windows is a real implementation (`RegisterHotKey` + a thread queue, already verified in W20b); Linux's X11 `XGrabKey` and macOS's Carbon/AppKit hotkeys are **not wired**, and always return `Err(Unsupported)` — "not built" and "failed" are two separate tiers, so callers can hide UI accordingly, the same contract as the tray's absent SNI watcher and notifications' absent backend.
- **Accelerator strings in, id lookup in the facade**: registration takes a string (`"Ctrl+Alt+F9"` / `"CmdOrCtrl+Shift+M"`, where `CmdOrCtrl` maps to Ctrl/Cmd per platform — parsing delegates to win's pure function rather than reimplementing it in core); `hotkey_poll()` returns `Hotkey{id, spec}` on a hit — Win32's `poll` only returns an id, so **the accelerator-string lookup table is held by the facade itself** (process-level, same lifetime as win's registry; an id outside the table gets an empty `spec`, meaning it was not registered through this facade).
- **Platform probing goes through the runtime `@sys.sys_platform()`** (the C stub `ffi_sys_platform` returns 1/2/3 → "windows"/"macos"/"linux"), consistent with AGENTS rule 11 "runtime probe + match, no `#cfg`"; the `is_mac` criterion comes from the same source (it decides the `CmdOrCtrl` mapping).
- **Two small toolchain pitfalls (both already hit in the code)**: ① `Array` **has no `find`** — the lookup table's linear scan is a hand-written loop (`for h in arr { if … return Some(h) }`); appending uses `arr.push(x)`, **never `arr + [x]`** (the parser treats `+` as infix and reports `unexpected token infix 1`, an error message far from the root cause). ② `inspect(value, content="…")`'s `content` is a string **compared against the value's stringified form** — a boolean must be given `"true"`/`"false"`; passing a descriptive word like "supported" always fails (hit once in this batch and once in the taskbar batch, recorded here once).
- **Evidence**: `gui/core/hotkey_wbtest.mbt` has 2 tests (an unregistered id's lookup returns an empty string; "assert only when connected" — when the backend is available, an empty accelerator string must go through `Err(Failed)` rather than crashing or silently succeeding, other platforms only print skip); `moon test ./gui/core` **118/118** (the original 116 plus 2 new). `examples/native-app`'s hotkey section switched from calling `@win.*` directly to `@core.hotkey_*` (two sites: registration and polling; a poll hit now takes the spec straight for display), `--deny-warn` warning-free, and the smoke run survived 100 seconds with no panic and no CRITICAL.
- **Not done this batch, and not claimed as done**: the macOS hotkey backend (the facade is ready; landing the backends will not change callers); the unification refactor of the tray/notification APIs (explicitly out of scope, reason in the first bullet).

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Linux global-hotkey backend (W22's Linux tier: X11 `XGrabKey`, 2026-10-16)

- **Scope**: in `win/stub.c` the GTK branch's `wm_hotkey_*` trio moves from placeholder stubs to a real implementation, and `wm_hotkey_supported` is added; the facade (`core/hotkey.mbt`) and the parsing (`win/hotkey.mbt`) see zero semantic change. The "two code spaces" convention takes effect this batch: the C ABI register gains a third parameter, both `vk` and `keysym` are passed and each platform stub picks its own (Windows takes vk, X11 takes keysym); the MoonBit-side `register_global_shortcut` now takes the whole `Hotkey`.
- **A self-opened X connection instead of hooking the GTK pump**: one process-level `XOpenDisplay` connection; `XGrabKey` lands on its root window, grabbed KeyPress events enter only this connection's queue, and `wm_hotkey_poll` drains them non-blockingly with `XPending` — neither the `gdk_window_add_filter` nor the periodic `XCheckIfEvent` originally envisioned in the TODO is needed; the pump never enters the GTK main loop.
- **Variant grabs are a requirement, not defensive coding**: registration calls `XGrabKey` for four variants — `base`, `base|Lock`, `base|Mod2`, `base|Lock|Mod2`. The TODO's original "mask with `& ~(Mod2|Lock)` at grab time" does not work (clearing mask bits only loosens modifier matching — with NumLock on the event state contains Mod2, and a mismatch loses the whole key); an injected event on real hardware arrived with `state=28` (Control|Mod1|**Mod2**), direct proof — this machine keeps NumLock on, so without variant grabs the hotkey would never fire. ScrollLock (Mod5) gets no grab variants and is masked out when matching.
- **BadAccess is asynchronous**: when the chord is owned by another client, `XGrabKey` reports no error in place — only a temporary `XSetErrorHandler` trap plus `XSync` reveals it; failure of any variant rolls the whole thing back with `XUngrabKey` and reports registration failure (the facade gives `Err(Failed)`, never silence). Bare keys (no modifiers) are refused, matching Windows' `RegisterHotKey` convention.
- **The VT-switch reserved-space pitfall (symptom → root cause)**: the probe reused W20b's `Ctrl+Alt+F9` — registration succeeded yet injected events never fired; a minimal C repro (bare `XGrabKey` + XTEST injection) did not fire either; switching to `Ctrl+Alt+H` hit on the first try — **`Ctrl+Alt+Fn` is the VT-switch chord, and the server consumes the event before passive grabs see it**; the grab registers but never receives. The Linux tier's default/demo chords avoid the Fn family (Windows has no such constraint); this also explains why W20b's F9/F10 chords were harmless on Windows.
- **Wayland stance**: with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` non-empty `wm_hotkey_supported` is permanently 0 — an XWayland grab only fires while an X11 window holds focus and never achieves true globality, so it reports "not built" instead of pretending success; the way out is the roadmap's "session axis" (portal / desktop-daemon protocols).
- **Verification** (Ubuntu 24.04 + X11 + XFCE): `moon run experiment/hotkey_probe` — ① seven parsing comparisons; ② register / idempotent unregister / slot reuse (`Some(1)`/`Some(2)`/re-register yields `Some(1)`); ③ the new facade polling stage: `xdotool key ctrl+alt+h` (XTEST, the real delivery path) → `HOTKEY-CORE-FIRE id=1 spec=Ctrl+Alt+H`, the full chain = inject → X server → passive grab → pump drain → facade lookup. `moon check` warning-free, library tests 982/982. Along the way: `HotkeyError` gained `Show`/`extend` (isomorphic with the other two families' error types, so the probe can interpolate `\{e}`).

### MoonBit native GUI stack · taskbar progress (W20g: `win/taskbar.mbt`, the Windows half of the §6.3 seam item "taskbar progress / dock badge")

- **Write-only, no read-back**: Win32's `ITaskbarList3` has **no getter** — `TBPF_*` progress state cannot be read back (the same "mapping is not reversible; code review is the backstop" situation as W21a's kind→`NIIF_*` mapping). So the surface only has writers (`set_taskbar_progress` / `set_taskbar_state` / `clear_taskbar_progress`), and the probe (`taskbar_supported`) only reports whether the COM instance came up — it never returns a current progress value. Callers that need to display progress keep their own number (deliberately a different tier from `notify_title`, which *can* read back because `NIF_INFO`'s `szInfoTitle` is readable).
- **The COM instance is a process-level singleton; the target window is distinguished by hwnd**: the `ITaskbarList3` interface itself is window-agnostic (the `hwnd` argument of `SetProgressValue` is the target), so the stub keeps one static singleton (`wm_taskbar` plus a `wm_taskbar_tried` guard against repeated probing) and takes the window handle from the window slot (an out-of-range `id` or a NULL `hwnd` returns 0, the same contract as every other `wm_*` entry). Initialization details: `CoInitializeEx(COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED)` falls back to `CoInitialize` on `RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE`; `S_FALSE` (this thread already initialized) counts as success; a failed `HrInit` must `Release` before reporting unavailable; there is no `CoUninitialize` at exit — the COM object is reclaimed with the process, and other COM users remain on the app exit path (W14 file dialogs, W20f WIC).
- **GUID symbols come from `uuid.lib`, not ole32**: C mode has no `__uuidof`, so the two constants `CLSID_TaskbarList` / `IID_ITaskbarList3` must be resolved at link time — **ole32.lib only exports the basic COM GUIDs; these two live in uuid.lib** (the same pitfall as W20f's `CLSID_WICImagingFactory` family living in windowscodecs.lib: which library a GUID constant lands in has to be confirmed one by one). Hence `gui/scripts/prebuild.py`'s Windows branch adds `uuid.lib` to the win entry (the probe's manual build line does the same).
- **Progress values go through `Int64`**: byte-count-style progress values overflow 32 bits, so the MoonBit side uses `Int64` for `value`/`total` and the C side passes them through as `ULONGLONG`; when `total <= 0` the `SetProgressValue` semantics are meaningless, and the documented convention is "use the `Indeterminate` state for indeterminate progress".
- **Evidence**: the pure-C probe `experiment/taskbar_probe/taskbar_backend_probe.c` ends with **`TASKBAR-BACKEND-OK`** and **all 20 assertions passing**: `wm_init` succeeds, `supported == 1` and the singleton is non-NULL (these two together verify both the uuid.lib GUID symbol resolution and the `CoCreateInstance` + `HrInit` steps), a real window is created (`wm_window_new` + `wm_show`, closed with `wm_close` at the end), all five state ids and the `value`/`total` write paths succeed, a `4GB-1 / 8GB` large value succeeds, the guard paths (out-of-range `id=0` / `id=9999`, an unbuilt window whose slot exists but whose `hwnd` is NULL, illegal `state=5` / `state=-1`) all return 0 without crashing or writing, the teardown clears back to `NoProgress` before closing, and the same id returns 0 after the window closes (`hwnd` already NULL). `gui/win/taskbar_wbtest.mbt` has **4 tests**: ids aligned with `TBPF_*`, id round-trip, unknown ids falling to `NoProgress` (matching the C-side default branch), and "assert only when connected" — when the backend is available, a nonexistent window handle must return `false` rather than silently succeeding (other platforms only print skip). `moon test ./gui/win` **28/28** (the original 24 plus 4 new).
- **Example wiring**: `examples/native-app` gains a "taskbar progress (§6.3)" section — seven writer buttons (10% / 50% / 100% / error / paused / indeterminate / clear) plus a `live_counter` that reads the most recent operation's result label live each frame (a failed write lands in the label rather than staying silent); the exit status line is `NATIVE-APP-TASKBAR supported=… last=…`. `moon check ./examples/native-app --deny-warn` is warning-free; the smoke run survives (110 seconds with no panic and no CRITICAL — note that native-app's self-destruct point is **10 minutes**, so unattended runs always need a timeout, see the `_人工测试清单.md` header).
- **Not done this batch, and not claimed as done**: Linux's taskbar progress has its own Unity LauncherEntry (DBus `com.canonical.Unity.LauncherEntry`) path and macOS's is the dock badge (`NSDockTile`), both deferred to a later cross-platform facade batch — the GTK branch and the placeholder branch only provide compilable failing stubs with `supported` always 0; the **real look** of the taskbar button (green / red / yellow bar, indeterminate marquee) can only be judged by a human and belongs to section O of `_人工测试清单.md`.
- **The probe's two C4996 warnings are a pre-existing artifact**: `wcsncpy` / `wcsncat` in the `wm_im_*` section — the probe's own `#include <windows.h>` disables the stub's `_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS` (the same note as W21d); the real build (moon's native-stub) has no such warning.

### Choosing where examples write temp files: the world beyond TEMP (2026-10-16, browser-example redo batch)

- **Symptom**: `examples/browser`'s `scheme_root()` only honored the `TEMP` env var and fell back to a **relative path** `libyue-browser-scheme/` when it was missing. Linux desktops have no `TEMP` (a Windows convention), so every run of the example dropped a temp directory into the **current working directory** — i.e. the repo root when launched from there, leaving a dirty un-committed directory behind (the leftover `libyue-browser-scheme/` in the repo root was exactly that).
- **Root cause**: the temp-dir choice was hardcoded for a single platform. "Fall back to the current directory when unset" is nearly harmless on Windows (`TEMP` is essentially always present) but on Linux it makes the *worst* place to write the default.
- **Fix** (`scheme_root` in `examples/browser/main.mbt`): per-platform split — Windows reads `TEMP`, then `TMP`, then `C:/Windows/Temp` (never a relative path); Linux/macOS read `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (per-user runtime dir, cleaned at logout), falling back to `/tmp`. The directory was renamed `native-gui-browser-scheme` along with the repo rename; the old leftover directory is simply deleted.
- **Verification**: after a smoke run on Ubuntu 24.04, `/run/user/<uid>/native-gui-browser-scheme/` holds the three protocol-page files (index.html / page2.html / style.css); nothing new appears in the repo root; `git status` clean.
- **Rule**: when an example must write intermediate files to disk, the landing point must be one of the system temp areas (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` → `/tmp` on Linux; `TEMP` → `TMP` on Windows). **Never fall back to the current directory** — `moon run`'s working directory belongs to the user, not the example.

- **How it came up**: the `TODO.md` line "retire the old chain's `modules/gui-media`" was read as "ffmpeg is going away". Checking the tree confirmed ffmpeg is not going anywhere (the new-stack `yue/media` still imports `NoahLiu/ffmpeg-mbt/src` — it is the **decode backend**), but it surfaced a real problem: `yue/media` lived *inside the main module*, and for its import of ffmpeg-mbt to resolve the root `moon.mod` had to declare `NoahLiu/ffmpeg-mbt@0.1.0` — so **every consumer of the main module pulled ffmpeg into its dependency closure**, cancelling the original "media as a separate module = optional dependency" design.
- **The mechanism (a hard moon constraint)**: an import in `moon.pkg` requires the module dependency to be declared in `moon.mod` first (otherwise: `containing module is not imported`). Therefore "the media package lives in the main module" and "module-level optionality" are **mutually exclusive**: optionality can only be had by moving media wholly out of the main module. **Keep the two layers apart** — **package-level optionality** (a `moon.pkg` import is the compile/link boundary) was never lost: not importing `yue/media` means `-lav*` never reaches the link line. What was lost is the **dependency-closure / build-time** layer; they are not the same thing.
- **One measurement correction**: this repo is a moon workspace (`moon.work` lists `modules/ffmpeg-mbt`), so **building any in-repo package runs ffmpeg-mbt's prebuild** — measured: `moon build ./gui/core` and `moon build ./modules/yoga-mbt/src` both print the `ffmpeg(prebuild):` line, and neither has anything to do with media. That is **not** caused by the root `moon.mod`; workspace membership alone triggers it (it runs whether or not `moon.work` changes; `.mooncakes` holds no `NoahLiu/`, so every `NoahLiu/*` resolves from a local workspace member). **This batch's payoff is therefore confined to external consumers**: they sit outside this workspace and resolve only `moon.mod`, so once that line is gone ffmpeg-mbt never enters their closure. In-repo/CI still runs it (CI installs the ffmpeg dev packages anyway; no added burden).
- **What was done**: ①`git mv yue/media modules/gui-media/media` — the media package moves into the existing standalone module `NoahLiu/gui-media` (which was split out for optional media in the first place); ②the miniaudio system-library link flags the media package needs (`-lpthread -ldl -lm -lstdc++ -latomic`) move out of the main repo's `scripts/prebuild.py` into the **new module's own** `modules/gui-media/prebuild.py`, issued by package name `NoahLiu/gui-media/media` (graceful empty link_configs off Linux, same stance as ffmpeg-mbt / the main prebuild); ③`modules/gui-media/moon.mod` gains `NoahLiu/yoga-mbt@0.1.0` (the media package takes layout nodes via `@yoga`) plus the prebuild option; ④the root `moon.mod` drops `NoahLiu/ffmpeg-mbt@0.1.0`.
- **The example has to move with it (the `b01d1dd` lesson)**: `examples/native-web` was the **only** package in the main module importing `yue/media`. Left there, the main module would have to depend back on the media module — recreating the "main ↔ media" publish cycle that once left both unpublishable and forced the examples into `modules/gui-examples`. So the whole example moves to `modules/gui-examples/native-web` (the module documented as "the standalone example module that needs media"); its `moon.pkg` changes `NoahLiu/native-gui/yue/media` to `NoahLiu/gui-media/media` (the alias still derives as `@media`, so **zero source changes**), and `modules/gui-examples/moon.mod` gains `NoahLiu/yoga-mbt@0.1.0`. **No new page**: `native-web`'s header states it is "the accumulating verification example for webview and media — no new page for the same family", and splitting it out would violate that rule.
- **The consolidation policy follows**: the "verification example consolidation" notes in `TODO.md` now point the webview + media landing point at `modules/gui-examples/native-web` instead of `examples/native-web` (the historical evidence lines keep their original wording — that is what happened then).
- **Evidence**: ①`moon tree` for the root module **no longer lists `NoahLiu/ffmpeg-mbt`** (it was explicitly listed before; after the change the first level is just the three yoga-mbt / subproc / markdown branches); ②repo-wide `moon check` red count stays at **287/68** with every error still in the old-chain packages (`events.mbt`/`splitter.mbt`/`types.mbt`/`props.mbt`/`video_view.mbt`…), showing the move did not touch them; ③both moved packages re-check green after a forced re-check (touching sources then `moon check`); ④the new module's prebuild run directly — `echo '{}' | python modules/gui-media/prebuild.py` → `{"link_configs": []}` (non-Linux degradation); ⑤`grep` shows no package in the main module referencing `yue/media` and no `MEDIA_PACKAGE` residue in the main prebuild. **One Windows-side gain (it was already broken)**: on Windows the root module could not build at all — the `native-web` → `yue/media` C stub needs `libavformat/avformat.h` and `audio_stub.c` uses `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`; measured: `moon build ./examples/native-web` fails outright. After the move the root module contains no package that cannot build on Windows.
- **Not done this batch, not pretending otherwise**: `miniaudio.h` is **still two copies** (`modules/gui-media/src/miniaudio.h` and `modules/gui-media/media/miniaudio.h`, same md5 `8d5bf2a0b46efa835bde4d0eac5a0cd8`) — folding them awaits retiring the old chain's `modules/gui-media/src`, blocked on migrating `systemprobe`'s media page; the media package is still unusable on Windows/macOS (POSIX clock + ffmpeg backend unwired); and media's real behaviour on Linux (does audio actually come out, how seek feels) cannot be evidenced on this host — it stays with the manual checklist.
- **Not done this batch, not pretending otherwise**: macOS (would need `CGEventSourceSecondsSinceLastEventType` / IOKit HID, left as Unsupported), idle on a native Wayland session (would need `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver` or `ext-idle-notify-v1`; this batch reports "unsupported" only), the **setter** side of "keep the screen awake" (`XScreenSaverSuspend` / `SetThreadExecutionState` — this batch only **reads** idle, it does not inhibit sleep), any notification mechanism for idle-threshold changes, and the real-hardware feel (tracked in `_人工测试清单.md`).

### Media audio backend goes cross-platform: a three-way monotonic clock (2026-10-12)

- **How it came up**: the previous batch moved the media package into its own module and filed "media cannot build on Windows" under "POSIX clock + ffmpeg unwired". This batch takes care of the half that is **ours** — `audio_stub.c` is media's audio backend (the miniaudio device layer plus a PCM queue) with **zero ffmpeg dependency**, so whether it compiles and runs can be pinned down on its own, without waiting for the ffmpeg line.
- **Symptom (measured under MSVC)**: `audio_stub.c` reports `error C2065: "CLOCK_MONOTONIC": undeclared identifier`, plus `warning C4013: "clock_gettime" undefined`. `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` is a POSIX-only constant that MSVC's `<time.h>` does not provide (and `clock_gettime` itself only lands in some UCRT versions).
- **Fix (one stub.c, multiple branches, platform macros — precedent `win/stub.c`; AGENTS rule 11)**: `mbt_now_ms` now branches three ways — `_WIN32` uses `QueryPerformanceCounter` / `QueryPerformanceFrequency` (QPC is Windows' monotonic high-resolution counter; **not `GetTickCount`**, whose granularity is ~15.6 ms and which is nudged by system-time changes); `__APPLE__` uses `mach_absolute_time` + `mach_timebase_info` (not `clock_gettime`: `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` needs macOS 10.12+, and mach is both more conservative and equally monotonic); everything else POSIX keeps `clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)` **byte-for-byte unchanged**. All three return "milliseconds since some arbitrary fixed epoch", used only for differences (`elapsed = now - wall0`) where the absolute value is meaningless — so a platform-dependent epoch does not affect the playback clock.
- **Two overflow guards**: ①the Windows branch splits into `(ticks / freq) * 1000 + ((ticks % freq) * 1000) / freq` so `ticks * 1000` cannot overflow 64 bits (QPC counts from boot; at 10 MHz a year is ≈ 3.15e14, so ×1000 still has order-of-magnitude headroom, but the split is strictly safer); ②the macOS branch uses `__uint128_t` to bridge `t * numer / denom`, guarding the intermediate product when numer/denom is not 1:1 (as on Apple Silicon).
- **Both copies changed together**: `media/audio_stub.c` and `src/audio_stub.c` were byte-identical (md5 `2b807752…`). At one point the change left one extra comment line in the `src/` copy — which made them **no longer** byte-identical; that line was reverted on the spot and the two are identical again (both md5 `856a4c98e3879e77aa5108f7bb4dcfd8`). Reason: the "fold to one copy" step promised when the old chain retires must stay mechanically decidable, and silent drift between the two breaks that.
- **Evidence (pure C probe `experiment/media_probe/audio_backend_probe.c`, which directly `#include`s the platform backend)**: last line **`AUDIO-BACKEND-OK`**, **48 assertions pass**, 0 failures — ①**clock**: consecutive / five-in-a-row reads are non-decreasing and positive, and `Sleep(60)` advances it by 61 ms (within [40,400]); ②**device-open arguments**: accepted only when `channels ∈ [1,8]` and `rate > 0`; `0`/`9`/`-1`/`rate=0`/negative rate all return NULL; ③**queue and volume semantics** (independent of whether a device exists): `push` appends, `queued_bytes` accumulates 400→600, an invalid push leaves the queue untouched, `clear` zeroes it and is idempotent on the second call, `played_bytes` is non-negative, volume clamps into [0,1] (0.5/1/0.25 read back exactly, -1→0, 2→1); ④**both device-lifecycle branches run** (no environment assumed): with a real device on this host → `start=0`/`is_started=1`/second start = -1/`played_bytes` really advances (measured 35280 bytes)/pause=0/second pause = -1; with no device (CI/headless) → start = -1 and the state stays 0; ⑤**NULL-argument defence across the board** (failure codes where they are due, no crashes where none should be). The probe also **reads `QueryPerformanceFrequency` directly and prints 10000000 Hz**, proving the QPC high-resolution branch is the one taken, not a coarse-grained fallback. Build recipe in the probe header (`-I <moon>/include` for `moonbit.h`; add `ole32.lib uuid.lib` for miniaudio's WASAPI backend; `#pragma warning(disable:4244)` silences only miniaudio's own single assignment narrowing, not our warnings — the probe body is warning-free under /W4).
- **A first-hand measurement**: `miniaudio.h` (a 4.2 MB single header) **does compile under MSVC** — apart from one `ma_uint64 → ma_uint32` (C4244) on its own line 80532 it produces no warnings. The audio backend therefore has a real landing path on Windows; the clock was the only missing piece.
- **A boundary that must be stated**: after the change `audio_stub.c` **compiles and runs** on Windows (the probe is the proof), but `moon test ./modules/gui-media/media` **still cannot run** — the test executable links `ffmpeg_stub.c` as well, and that needs `libavformat/avformat.h` (the `ffmpeg-mbt` line is unwired off Linux). So this batch's Windows payoff is **a compilable, runnable audio backend**, not "the media package now works on Windows". The Linux branch is byte-for-byte untouched, so behaviour is unchanged (this host cannot run Linux — that is a code-level claim, not a measurement).
- **Not done this batch, not pretending otherwise**: `ffmpeg-mbt`'s Windows/macOS backends (wiring a system decoder or shipping DLLs — a separate line); the media package therefore still cannot be built or tested as a whole off Linux; the macOS branch (`mach_absolute_time`) cannot be evidenced on this host and rests on a code-level argument only; audible output and seek feel still belong to `_人工测试清单.md`.
- **One measured conclusion along the way (so nobody "fixes" the wrong place)**: the media prebuild's "non-Linux → empty link_configs" is **correct** — do not add `ole32.lib`/`uuid.lib` to it, nor macOS frameworks. ①**Windows**: taking `audio_stub.c` (which `#include`s miniaudio) and **linking with no extra libraries at all** succeeds (measured: `/Fe:probe_nolibs.exe` links with zero libraries and still passes all 48 assertions at runtime), because miniaudio defaults to **runtime `LoadLibrary`** (`MA_NO_RUNTIME_LINKING` undefined) and emits no link-time symbols — the earlier probes carrying `ole32.lib uuid.lib` proved that pair **unnecessary**, not required. ②**macOS**: miniaudio's own wording is "the macOS build should compile cleanly without the need to download any dependencies nor link to any libraries or frameworks" — the default is runtime framework linking too (only an explicit `-DMA_NO_RUNTIME_LINKING` demands `-framework CoreFoundation -framework CoreAudio -framework AudioToolbox`, and that macro's automatic definition lives in the **DOS** branch, not the Apple one); the command line needs only `-lpthread -lm`, both of which macOS pulls in from libSystem by default. So of the three platforms, **only Linux needs explicit system libraries** (`-lpthread -ldl -lm -lstdc++ -latomic`).

### First example-migration batch: showcase skeleton + basic/feedback pages (G7, 2026-10-12)

- **Scope**: `examples/showcase` moves off the old chain (the `@yue` root package + `@declarative` + `@components`) onto the new stack (the `Node` layer in `core` + `ui` + `theme`); this batch lands the **skeleton + the basic-components page + the feedback-components page**. The other 13 of the old chain's 15 pages (icon library / form / events & layout / navigation / data display / charts / code & docs / Store comparison / system integration / window / browser / canvas & rich text) were **removed from the working tree** (`git rm`; the sources are recoverable from history before `91204ca` at any time) and will come in batch by batch, **basics first, heavy controls later** — the browser page carries a WebKit heavyweight control and the icon-wall page builds 803 icon widgets, so neither is a good place to start.
- **Four mechanical differences (old chain → this stack; recorded once so no page has to rediscover them)**:
  ① **`style=[...]` does not exist**. New-stack components take explicit parameters only (`padding`/`row_gap`/`width`…); spacing is a property of the **layout container**, not of the control. The old walls of `style=[("marginTop", 8.0)]` lines all go away and are expressed by the parent's `row_gap`.
  ② **Visibility and lazy mounting moved a layer**: `View::set_visible` → `Widget::set_visible` (internally the safe `display:none` yoga path) and `Node::mount_into(View)` → `Node::mount_into(Widget)`; `Node.mount`'s closure also returns a `Widget` instead of a `View`. Semantics unchanged.
  ③ **"Fill the remaining height" cannot be written on the control**: the old chain wrote `style=[("flexgrow", 1.0)]`; the new scroll container (`scroll_v`) takes **no** `grow` parameter, so the viewport widget is grown inside the `handle` callback (`node.set_flex_grow(1.0)` — `handle` receives the viewport itself).
  ④ **The nav page is ours to write**: `nav_page` was always an example-local helper (`examples/showcase/ui/section.mbt`) and this stack has no equivalent either, so it was reimplemented on the same mechanism in `shared/section.mbt` — `set_visible` for switching, **mount only on first selection** (mounting all 15 pages up front is not affordable at startup; that mechanism has to stay).
- **Pitfall 1: the local shared layer must not be called `ui/`**. On the old chain the component library was `@components` and the example's own shared layer was `@ui`, so there was no clash; on the new stack the component library **is** `ui`, and two packages both deriving to `@ui` is an outright ambiguity. Fix: `examples/showcase/ui/` → `examples/showcase/shared/` (deriving to `@shared`), with the `@ui.App`/`@ui.page`/`@ui.section` call sites updated along the way. **Do not** paper over it with an explicit alias for the component library in `moon.pkg` — the example would then read wrong for the long run.
- **Pitfall 2: `popover_t`'s width/height are named parameters**. The old call was positional — `popover_t(trigger, content, 180.0, 60.0)`; the new signature is `popover_t(trigger, content, width?, height?, handle?)`, so two positional `Double`s fail to compile with **4080** (`which requires 2 positional arguments, but is given 4`). Whenever a new-stack signature has extra optional parameters, check whether they are named ones — copying old call sites is exactly how this bites.
- **Pitfall 3: the old chain's `@yue.VERSION` is unusable**. It lives in the **root package** (the old-chain root package, i.e. exactly where the repo's 287 red dots are), and importing it drags that whole red package into the dependency closure. The example keeps a local `SHOWCASE_VERSION` constant instead, noting that the authoritative value stays `moon.mod` + `yue/version.mbt` (whose build-time consistency check is `scripts/prebuild.py`'s job).
- **Two component-layer consolidations (write the new shape; do not hunt for the old function)**: `alert_closeable` folded into `alert(closable=true, on_close=)`, and `result` takes only `(title, subtitle, semantic type)` — it **no longer** takes an actions array; the caller lays the actions out alongside ("components give shape, content belongs to the caller" is the general stance of this component layer).
- **One API clarification worth carrying forward**: `toast_layer` on this stack **returns the push function only** — no "layer node + push function" pair. The toast strip opens on the **overlay layer** (created on the first push, taken down with the last), so a page no longer keeps an empty tree resident and toasts always sit above dialogs and other overlays. Migrating code should **delete** the `toast_node` that the old `@components.toast_layer()` destructured rather than mounting it.
- **Verification**: `moon check ./examples/showcase ./examples/showcase/shared ./examples/showcase/pages --deny-warn` is **warning-free**; repo-wide `moon check` red dots hold at **287/68** (the 14 deleted old pages were already counted there); the real-hardware smoke exits `0` with `SHOWCASE-READY title=组件库演示板 pages=2 follow=1` and `SHOWCASE-DONE page=基础组件`, the window title is right, it responds, and `CloseMainWindow` exits cleanly. The `libpng warning: iCCP: cHRM chunk does not match sRGB` line on exit is **pre-existing** (`examples/native-app` prints it too) and unrelated to this batch.
- **Not done this batch, not pretending otherwise**: the remaining 13 pages; the menubar / tray / single-instance wiring (both `dialog_t`s are mounted in the window root and openable from the feedback page, while menubar, tray and single instance are handled "as the system-integration / window pages come in"; `examples/native-app` already demonstrates them); and the real-hardware feel (sidebar hover, scroll position surviving section switches, follow-vs-manual theme switching) which belongs to `_人工测试清单.md`.

### Declarative Layer and Self-Drawn Components

- Never call `set_background_color` inside mouse callbacks: runtime CSS rewrites swallow the immediately following press ("works on the second click"). Interactive states (hover / pressed) are expressed in on_draw; set_background_color is allowed only at mount time and in theme-subscription callbacks.
- A flex container's attach order is also its layout order and z-order: interleave widgets (handles / dividers) must attach in exact layout position and stay permanently visible — users find them by looking, not by hovering.
- **markdown_view style-range accounting and mdast measured semantics (MD2, 2026-10)**: the old hand-written parsers (md_parse_inline / md_parse_blocks) are deleted; `yue/markdown.mbt` now consumes mizchi/markdown (mdast). ①**Rich-text range endpoints must be accumulated per rendered-text segment in UTF-16 code units (`md_utf16_len`) — never counted in code points, never derived from mdast Spans.** MoonBit's `for ch in str` iterates code points while `str.length()` counts UTF-16 code units (measured: "a👍b" iterates 3 times, length 4); AttributedText ranges are UTF-16-semantic, so styling after an emoji (non-BMP, 1 code point = 2 code units) shifts wholesale when accumulated in code points. Span-based locating is not viable at all: rendered text ≠ source text (markers stripped, soft breaks turned into spaces, link URLs dropped) — ranges can only be measured over the rendered text. Flattening recurses the inline-nesting tree with an explicit style-carrying stack (`md_flatten_inline`), merging adjacent same-style segments to cut range count; rendering and tests share one accounting function `md_span_ranges` (wbtest asserts the bold range after an emoji is [4,6), not the code-point-misaligned [3,5)). ②Three mizchi/markdown 0.8.3 parsing semantics: `FencedCode.code` carries a trailing `\n` (line splitting must drop the trailing empty line); `parse_code_block_info` only understands the `lang:file {meta}` form and **does not split space-separated info strings** ("rust title=x" lands whole in lang), so the language must be taken as the first word; blank lines between paragraphs produce `BlankLines` blocks, so AST traversal cannot assume "block index = document order intuition" (a test tripped on children[2] actually being a blank block). Rendering-surface decisions: HtmlBlock / footnotes not rendered by default, tables degrade to row lines (cells joined by two spaces, bold header), task lists consume `ListItem.checked` (☑/☐), Blockquote sub-blocks recurse wholly into the accent bar, ordered lists honor `start`. Verification: `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test` 595 all green (19 new wbtests covering conversion / flattening / ranges / info / line splitting, plus the five-item CommonMark-deviation acceptance set before/after: setext headings / ~~~ fences / info strings / indented code blocks / nested lists).
- **markdown_view GFM rendering surface completed (MD3, 2026-10)**: ①**Strikethrough does not ride on a native attribute — the MoonBit layer draws it itself.** The upstream AttributedText offers only SetFontFor / SetColorFor (vendor libyue `attributed_text.h`; the GTK Pango backend has strikethrough but the wrapper never exposes it and the shim has no entry either); a fork patch would require rebuilding the three platforms' prebuilt libraries, outside this batch's boundary. `md_rich_label` switches from Label to self-drawing at mount (themed_container + draw_attributed_text) and **measures each segment independently with the same font (get_bounds_for) to build a segment pixel-coordinate table**; strikethrough segments draw their horizontal line from the table (mid-line height, foreground colour), **and link hit-testing plus the hover cursor use the same table** — the cross-layer contract: "a rich-text line's ranges are UTF-16 endpoints plus pixel-x intervals: style ranges go to AttributedText, hit ranges go to mouse events". In the single-line (wrap=false) case the per-segment width accumulation matches whole-run layout to sub-pixel precision, so click hits naturally tolerate small offsets (under multi-line wrap the table breaks down; this component's rich-text lines never wrap so it is not involved — if wrap arrives later, switch to per-line layout). ②**Link clicks**: MDSpan carries a url (Link takes it directly; RefLink/RefImage look it up in ParseResult.definitions by exact label match, degrading to a URL-less link style when absent); if an on_mouse_down's view_x lies in [xs, xs+ws) it calls open_url (reusing the system capability — xdg-open on Linux); on_mouse_move switches to the hand cursor and add_tooltip_for_rect registers a per-url address hint (registered once at mount; theme switches do not change the geometry, so no re-mount). ③**Footnote two-pass**: a prescan of the body (recursing through nested lists / blockquotes / table cells / definition lists) numbers references in order of appearance, skipping FootnoteDefinition itself (references inside definitions are not numbered, keeping end-of-document content from polluting the order); a FootnoteReference flattens to a superscript "[n]" (smaller-size range; inline mixed font sizes in AttributedText work under Pango / CoreText / DirectWrite), and after the main content markdown_view draws a separator plus only the referenced definitions (unreferenced ones stay unrendered, per GFM semantics). ④**Images**: shown only when a block is "a paragraph that is exactly one image" (inline-mixed images degrade to alt — rich-text lines cannot embed inline images); Image::new_from_file takes local paths / a file:// prefix (stripped); is_empty degrades to alt; there is no network image loading, so any network url degrades to alt; proportional scaling with a 560 width cap (markdown_view's default width; overflow when an outer box is narrower, matching today's single-line text overflow behaviour). ⑤**Evenly divided table grid**: cell widths use the percentage-string channel ("33.33%", measured usable; precedent: the showcase events page's width "50%"), column alignment goes through the cell container's alignItems (center has precedent; flex-end unmeasured — an unrecognized value is ignored by yoga and falls back to left, no crash surface); cell rich text reuses md_rich_label. Not mixed with table_t — table_t is a Store-driven data panel (fixed column widths / plain-text cells), while in-document tables have an unknown column count and rich-text cells; a self-drawn grid fits better. ⑥Task lists: checkbox_t with an empty title (intrinsic width 30 overridden by a fixed width) plus inline content; the checked state is ListItem.checked; clicking toggles visuals only (the document source never changes). ⑦The showcase demo text and copy string share one source: `demo_md_lines()` is the single source; rendering takes join("\n") and the copy string derives MoonBit literals line by line (escaping backslashes / double quotes), so what you copy equals what you see on the page. Verification: `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test` 600 all green (24 markdown_wbtest cases; new assertions for strikethrough flags / links carrying urls / reference links resolving definitions / missing definitions degrading to literal text / footnote numbering and superscripts / block-level ignoring of definitions / image path conversion / table cell and column-alignment mapping); visual items on real hardware (strikethrough line position / link click and hover / table alignment and grid / image display / task toggling / footnote superscripts and end-of-document list) are for the user to verify on the showcase "code & docs" page's Markdown section.
- **Subscriptions must be unsubscribable, or rebuild-style components accumulate dead subscriptions without bound (CORE2)**: Store/Signal subscription closures are held by the signal kernel and theme subscriptions by theme_box.subs, with no removal entry — every component that rebuilds rows or remounts a subtree leaks a whole generation per rebuild: transfer leaks one set per move; table_t leaks "row container + one themed_container per cell + bind_fg" per rows Store set (over a thousand per refresh on a 1000-row table); each snackbar push leaks two; each bind_node remount leaks the old subtree's bind_label Store subscription. Dead subscriptions cost little memory, but every set / theme_apply then runs against destroyed views (set_color / schedule_paint on removed widgets), and the closures keep the captured view subtrees alive forever. Fix on both the kernel and usage sides: ①subscriptions carry ids — `Signal::subscribe` returns a handle and `Signal::remove(id)` removes it; on Store, `subscribe_id(f)` takes a handle and `remove(handle)` removes it (`Store::subscribe` keeps returning Unit: MoonBit forbids implicitly discarding non-Unit values, so changing its return type would touch a hundred-plus call sites repo-wide). ②Theme subscriptions get the same treatment: `on_theme_change` returns a handle, `off_theme_change(handle)` removes it. ③Deep or bulk subscriptions use the **subscription bag** `sub_bag_begin() / sub_bag_end() / sub_bag_discard(closure list)`: open a bag before a rebuild, and every subscription registered during it (Store + theme, including themed_container / bind_fg / bind_label at any depth of the subtree) pushes its unsubscribe closure into the bag; the old generation is discarded wholesale before rebuilding — transfer's render_all, table_t's rebuild, bind_node's rebuild and the snackbar's dismiss timer all go through it. The bag is a stack (nesting-safe), the same "collection-time global context" pattern as the existing sig_collector in signals.mbt. Verification: moon check zero warnings + moon test 657 all green (8 new: Store unsubscribe and idempotence, Signal handle removal, three bag generations and nesting, theme off and bag, empty-stack bag, theme bag on component rebuild, carousel_stop).
- **Timers started at mount need a reclamation channel; the two timer APIs have different contracts (CORE2)**: a timer started when a component mounts has no "view was removed" notification, so without reclamation it keeps ticking against a destroyed subtree. The two libyue timer contracts differ: `set_timeout` returns an id that `clear_timeout(id)` cancels immediately (self-rescheduling carousel chains use this); `set_timer` is a periodic callback with **no cancellable id — the only way to stop it is returning false from the callback** (the shim yue_mbt.cpp's SetTimer does not hand back an id). Hence carousel_t gains a `rotation? : CarouselHandle` handle plus `carousel_stop(handle)` (stops auto-advance and cancels the pending timeout; manual arrows / dots are unaffected), while video_view_t's frame-advance timer follows the documented contract — `vid_stop(handle)` sets running=false so the next tick returns false and stops, and **must be called before unmounting** (at most one extra tick). Both "must stop before unmounting" contracts are written into the usage docs (components-ui / system-capabilities, zh and en in sync).

### Self-drawn canvas and chart rendering

- 8-digit hex colors have the alpha **first** (`#AARRGGBB` — a libyue `ParseHexColor` source-level convention, the opposite of CSS `#RRGGBBAA`; `yue/color.mbt`'s `parse_hex` agrees). Appending a tail neither errors nor changes opacity — the two hex digits land in the **blue channel**, showing up as color drift. Instance one: the floating scrollbar fade changed the alpha string from "d9" to "73", which actually moved blue 0xd9→0x73 with red/green untouched, so the fading thumb turned yellow. Instance two: chart area fill `color + "26"` — accent `#009688` becomes `#00968826`, parsed as AARRGGBB = alpha 0x00 (fully transparent) + RGB(150,136,38), so **the area fill had never rendered at all**. Fixed by routing everything through `with_alpha(hex, aa)` (prepends the alpha); any set_fill_color/set_stroke_color needing opacity must use it — no hand-appended suffixes.
- An offscreen `Canvas::new + get_painter` supports all geometry drawing (fill / stroke / arc / clip) without `initialize()`, so drawing benchmarks run on headless CI too; but the text paths (`draw_text` / `AttributedText::get_bounds_for`) segfault outright — the GTK text stack needs initialize first. Benchmarks therefore come in two tiers: "pure-function pipeline + geometry-call mirror" without a display, and a real full-frame run including text annotations only after `initialize` when DISPLAY is present; both tiers record into `charts_wbtest.mbt`'s output.
- `stroke()` under the painter's default stroke color is a no-op (draws nothing): a benchmark that forgets `set_stroke_color` shows stroke cost as ~0 and passes bogusly. Always set an explicit color before timing strokes.
- Under software rasterization (GTK/X11, no GPU path) a path stroke costs ~1.8µs per segment, ~13µs for near-vertical segments (slope >30); `fill_rect` ~1µs each (axis-aligned fast path), `draw_text` ~0.11ms per call, `line_to` itself ~12ns (path building only). A 1000-point × 4-series line chart drawn entirely with path strokes costs 45–60ms per frame — far over the 5ms acceptance line.
- Fix (shared by the whole chart family, see `yue/charts.mbt`): in dense mode (more points than the plot's pixel columns) decimate per column (min/max preserving extremes) and switch to rect paths — area mode fills one rect per column down to the anchor line (the fill's top edge *is* the line), line mode draws a min..max vertical bar per column; only sparse mode (points <= columns) uses a true polyline plus polygon area. Per-frame cost is decoupled from window size and grows only with plot width.
- libyue's Arc cannot express a counterclockwise arc: on GTK `PainterGtk::Arc` is a plain `cairo_arc`, and cairo normalizes `ea < sa` into a "plus 2π clockwise long arc"; the Win public API is hardwired clockwise too (the underlying ArcPixel has an anticlockwise parameter that is never exposed). The shim's "ccw as negative span" conversion therefore never takes effect on either backend — using ccw for a ring's inner arc wraps the hole into the long arc and fills a solid pie (verified by real-machine screenshot: donut and gauge centers were not hollow, with "总计"/percentage painted on the solid face). Fix: approximate the inner return arc with a polyline (32 segments per full circle, chord error <0.4px, identical on all three platforms); for pure strokes (icon arcs) simply swap the start/end angles, which is equivalent. Changing `PainterGtk::Arc` to `cairo_arc_negative` in the fork would be the root fix, but that needs a vendor-* release, so it is deferred.
- Chart acceptance benchmarks (release, Ubuntu 24.04 XFCE X11, offscreen canvas + initialize, real full frame incl. text): line 1000 points × 4 series (adversarial steep sawtooth) 3.08ms / smooth data 1.81ms; bar 200 categories 0.38ms; donut 50 sectors 0.70ms; gauge 0.15ms; scatter 10000 points 3.03ms. Pure-function pipeline (range / ticks / decimation / coordinate mapping) for the line chart: 0.028ms. Long-run push: 4800 pushes (10 min at 2Hz × 4 series) total 2.89ms with the window length pinned at 1000 and never growing — live data is bounded at 4 × 1000 × 8B = 32KB; the increment is GC-reclaimed window-swap garbage, which does not accumulate across continuous pushes.
- Line area anchor: the zero line when 0 is inside the range, the plot bottom for all-positive data, the plot top for all-negative (a straddling column emits two rects, above and below).
- `Painter::DrawText` (canvas draw_text) defaults to `wrap=true`: long text in a fixed-height row or narrow box gets wrapped by the platform layout engine and overflows the row bounds. Three measured symptom classes: process-table command lines (often 100+ chars) wrapped and bled into the next row; chart y-axis large values ("21414.7") stacked vertically as multi-line garbage overlapping each other; end-value labels of multiple line series overlapping when their last values were close. Fix: the shim gained `yue_mbt_painter_draw_text_ex` exposing TextAttributes' wrap/ellipsis (pure ABI translation), MoonBit's draw_text gained optional parameters, and table cells now draw uniformly with `wrap=false + ellipsis=true` single-line truncation (done by the platform layout, so no per-cell measurement); `fmt_axis` switches to k/M/G units from |v| >= 1e4 (one decimal, trailing zeros trimmed) so labels stay within 5 characters and never trigger wrapping; end labels are now collected, spread by y (14px minimum gap, clamped back into the canvas as a whole), then drawn.
- Chart / virtual-table responsiveness (the fill switch): no fixed width — the column container's default stretch spreads horizontally and follows window resizes. In the table's fill mode, column geometry is re-laid-out on every paint from the actual width: fixed columns keep their (possibly drag-resized) widths while elastic columns share the remainder (dragging swaps width between the two conservatively, so it never conflicts with the elastic re-layout). Self-drawn row containers that anchor to `w - offset` already follow their parent's width.
- Table header decorations (sort arrows, column-boundary lines, hover highlights) must be painted in the header container's (head) `on_draw`, not in a per-cell container (head_cell): on GTK, libyue Painter path fills (`begin_path` + `fill`) do not render at all inside a single header cell (about one column wide × 32px, with a Label child widget) — the code runs, nothing errors, but no pixels appear; the identical code renders fine on the whole-row header container or the table's big canvas container. `fill_rect` and path `stroke` render at every container size, so the symptom is easily misread as "wrong coordinates". Reproduce by painting fill_rect / path fill / path stroke side by side in one window. Fix: both table_t and table_v_t keep all header decoration in a single `on_draw` on the head container, leaving cells with interaction only. Root cause pending fork-level investigation (suspected to relate to the GTK draw region / clipping of small containers).
- Mouse events at header column boundaries: the pixels just right of a boundary line belong to the next cell, so pressing exactly on a visible boundary lands on the next cell's left edge (triggering a sort instead of a drag). Fix: the drag hot zone recognizes both edges (right 4px → boundary (j, j+1); left 4px → boundary (j-1, j)), with no handle on the last column's right edge.
- The Painter has no dash API: dashed lines (markLine and the like) are always hand-drawn segment simulations (ci_dash_line, 6px on 4px off), identical on all three platforms and independent of platform dash support.
- The chart hover overlay is self-drawn rather than reusing base components (the selection rationale): Popover is click-triggered, positioned relative to a view, and a standalone bare window — hover-following would flicker; the native tooltip is a single-line system style, insufficient for multi-line + theming. So the overlay is painted inside the chart container's own on_draw (painted after the chart puts it on top, no z-order issue); ci_tooltip_pos clamps its position inside the canvas; mouse reachability is verified through the same path as bar_chart_t/donut_chart_t.
- Projection choice for the map and flight lines (geo_map_t, selection and implementation rules): **equirectangular** — lon [-180,180] maps linearly across the plot width and lat [-90,90] maps linearly vertically (north up); inputs are clamped before projecting and outputs never leave the plot area (geo_project).
