Mercator and Lambert were not chosen: Mercator's 85° clamp and latitude stretching hurt China's latitude band and extrapolating past latitudes diverges; Lambert's two standard parallels need per-dataset tuning; equirectangular lets every geometry be pinned by single probe-point assertions (all three typical datasets — North America / China / world — verify). The projection rect is the **merged bounding box** of the region rings and flight-line endpoints, inscaled by its own aspect ratio and centred (geo_fit_rect, shape-preserving) — not a fixed rect: local maps then do not shrink into a corner, and flight ends outside the region stay fully visible; degenerate axes (same lon / same lat) get a 1° minimum span, and non-positive w/h degrade to size 0. Centroids use shoelace signed area (|A| as the axis) plus area-weighted in-ring point averaging (geo_ring_centroid / geo_region_centroid): a ring may be a MultiPolygon of several rings, so the ring with the largest |signed area| is the main ring; concave shapes (Shandong Peninsula / Liaoning) come out steadier than the bbox centre or the first point; the angle-free implementation keeps elliptic-integral approximations from drifting on thin rings. Region fill colours take the theme's primary and nudge lightness ±0.06 by an **FNV-1a hash of the region name** (geo_name_hash, modulo 13 / 12 normalized) — same name same colour, invariant under theme or zoom changes; table indices are not used, since they move with data order and the light/dark contrast would flicker. Flight-line arc control points are computed **in projected canvas coordinates** (geo_flight_ctrl takes the from/to midpoint plus a perpendicular offset of bend × endpoint distance), which makes the arcs' visual bulge uniform; computing control points in lon/lat directly distorts high-latitude arcs because a degree of longitude is shorter at high latitudes. Bézier sampling geo_flight_points defaults to 48 segments, first point = from and last = to (inclusive endpoints keep the arrow direction right). Map data is not built in: geojson_parse reuses the hand-written JSON parser from vscode_history (vsc_json, pure MoonBit), accepting only FeatureCollection / Feature / bare Polygon / MultiPolygon; nonconforming geometry (missing coordinates, rings under 3 points, non-numeric coordinates) gives GeoError::BadGeometry; a Feature with null geometry is legitimately skipped.

### Layout Geometry (Yoga flexbox)

- Layout assertions pass 16/16 (±1px); composition rules: content area = container − 2×padding; gap does not stack with margin; percentages resolve against the parent content width.
- Composite widgets (Tab / Scroll / Group) are measure-less leaf nodes in the yoga tree: their outer size must be given explicitly (e.g. `flex:1`) or they collapse (Tab freezes its minimum size at construction, driving the page area to zero).
- tabs_t once hard-coded the outer width to 360px and gave content pages no flex: any Scroll / Table placed inside collapsed to zero (measured: the sysmonitor overview page rendered completely blank except the tab strip). Fix: outer drops the fixed width in favor of `flex:1` (stretch gets the width in a column parent; fills when the parent has a definite height) and content pages get `flex:1` too. When the parent has no definite height flex does not grow, so embedded usage (the showcase section demo) is unchanged.
- After changing styles at runtime (set_style), calling `update_layout` on the **root container** does not refresh the subtree on GTK at all (yoga state has changed, bounds stay put), and calling it on a single node only re-lays-out that node and its siblings under the same parent — other subtrees (e.g. table body rows) are unaffected. A four-group controlled probe (immediately after mount / 500ms later, update root / leaf, width / flexbasis) pinned the only reliable form: call it on every container whose style changed. table_t column dragging used to call it on the root — the handle moved (bounds follow col_w) while column widths never changed (the style took no effect); the splitter happened to have only one wrapper container to restyle, so calling it on outer looked general but sat in the same unexploded pit. Fix: apply_col_widths calls update_layout on both header cells and both cells of every row individually.
- GUI automation: prefer the keyboard (Tab focus + Space activate); `xdotool key --window` sends XSendEvent events that GTK drops — use XTEST (no --window); coordinate clicks are unreliable due to WM decoration offsets.
- **The Linux/macOS tabs_t page-switch collapse is cured (native ≥ v0.15.6-mbt.19)**: the lesion sits in yoga itself interacting with display:none, a three-layer mechanism — ① the `flex` shorthand (flex:1) resolves in this yoga vintage to grow=1 with a derived basis of 0 (`resolveFlexBasisPtr`); ② hiding a page goes through display:none, where `YGZeroOutLayoutRecursively` wipes the layout wholesale with `= {}`, knocking `computedFlexBasis` back to undefined; ③ after re-showing, the flex basis computation (Yoga.cpp `YGNodeComputeFlexBasisForChild`) rewrites the derived basis-0 whenever the resolved value is defined and `computedFlexBasis` is undefined — and every later round then takes the "already computed" branch and never content-measures again, so under an auto-height owner chain (the scroll content column) with no free space to distribute, the page container stays at zero height for good (probe measured the re-shown page at 1px, outer 65→36 collapsed to head height). Pages never hidden stay healthy only by the coincidence that a content measure once entered the basis cache — not a stable guarantee. The fix (fork patch lb091188/yue 93078300: set a `zeroedByDisplayNone` flag in the display zero-out pass, and for a flagged node the basis computation takes the content-measure branch that round; explicit flexBasis styles unchanged) heals only the shorthand path; **the collapse of an explicit flexbasis 0 is inherent semantics** (every round rewrites 0 from the resolved value, the content-measure branch never runs), which is why tabs_t splits by platform — Windows keeps the explicit basis 0 (treating its show/hide mid-state compression), Linux/macOS return to the plain flex shorthand. Regression tool: `moon run examples/probe-collapse` (four timed switch samples; shorthand pages must hold a steady 22 height). Pit: the CI clang command line carries `-Wshadow -Werror` (the local `-Wall -Wextra` combo does not include shadow — patch code all-green locally, all-red on CI; check shadow first), and the fork patch lands in `patches/` (the prebuilt workflow runs `git -C third_party/yoga apply` after Bootstrap); yoga is a submodule and stays out of fork commits.
- **The boundary of the mbt.19 patch: showcase re-collapse and the shorthand ban on outer (closed by next-day real-hardware re-verification)**: after mbt.19 shipped, real-hardware re-verification of showcase still collapsed — the patch only heals the node itself zeroed by display:none and re-shown; it cannot heal a flex-shorthand ancestor that was never hidden but gets dirty-recalculated by a sibling's visibility flip: tabs_t's own outer also carries the flex:1 shorthand, and once a page switch dirties it, the content-measure round under its auto-height owner (the scroll content column) resolves the derived basis-0 against the available size into 0 (not undefined), which the owner then takes as a zero-height content contribution — outer collapses to its margin height and the whole subtree goes to zero (gauge measured 1px); everything looks fine initially only because the first natural-measure round sees an owner size of nan, where basis-0 resolves back to undefined and the content measure runs. A minimal pure-yoga repro (one availableHeight=undefined round, then a fixed-300 round plus switches) reproduces both shapes faithfully, and printf tracing added in Yoga.cpp captured the three-step collapse chain: `outer mainOwnerSize 300→10→0` (10 being the margin height). The fix stays out of native: tabs_t's outer switches to **flexgrow + flexshrink written separately** — grow/shrink do not participate in the content measure and the basis takes auto semantics (CSS flex:1 1 auto): content height under an auto owner, fill/compress as usual under a definite owner; the sole difference from the shorthand is basis auto. **Rule: any container that must live both ways — fill under a definite-height owner, content-size under an auto owner — must not use the flex shorthand; write grow/shrink separately. The shorthand only fits where the owner height is always definite, or where the node itself is the visibility-switch target (protected by the mbt.19 patch).** Regression tool extended with `moon run examples/probe-collapse2` (full showcase structure repro: sidebar + sibling page toggling + scroll chain + dual-shape tabs; the gauge group must hold a steady 18). Probe-side note: never use button_t as decorative sidebar furniture — during window teardown the GTK focus-out callback can hit destructed resources and intermittently segfault (gdb stack `OnFocusOut → Store<Responder>::get`), unrelated to the collapse; the probe switched to labels, and the button_t focus-chain lifetime is fixed (yue_mbt_quit disconnects signals uniformly; see the "GTK-related" exit-segfault entry).
- **flexWrap does not fire in an over-wide container: Yoga's default flexShrink is 0 (CSS's is 1)**. A 19-segment segmented control ran 2400px in one row and was cut off by the window; the inner hbox carried flexWrap yet never broke — wrapping presupposes a constrained container width, but as a child of the outer container its shrink defaults to 0, so it took its full content width and the constraint never reached it. Fix: the inner layer gets an explicit `flexShrink 1` + `flexWrap wrap` + `rowGap` (row spacing when wrapped); pages with few segments never wrap and look unchanged. General rule: a container expected to "wrap when too wide" must set shrink explicitly whenever it is itself someone's child.
- **Final decision on aligning with web semantics: keep useWebDefaults off, shrink stays default 0, and contraction is opted in with an explicit 1.** Yoga deviates from CSS in four kernel defaults (flexShrink 0 / implicit flexBasis 0 / flexDirection column / alignContent flex-start); the official switch `YGConfigSetUseWebDefaults` aligns all at once (the fork hook is one line at nu's `State::State()` global config), but it is **a global config: yoga layouts inside native widgets flip too**, and native components have no wrapper to exempt them one by one — dropped. A subsequent "declarative-layer defaulting" trial (container_node uniformly defaults flexshrink 1, affecting only declarative hbox/vbox) still regressed too broadly in real-hardware testing: fixed-50px self-drawn icon canvases got squashed and deformed by row compression, images scrambled across rows — the declarative layer is equally full of "fixed-width self-drawn control + slack space" layouts, and the benefit (wide wraps without explicit shrink) is far outweighed by the cost (every fixed-width control needs a lock). **Reverted; final decision: shrink keeps Yoga's original default 0; containers that must shrink or wrap (segmented and friends) explicitly take 1.** Regression evidence: the probe-collapse family's gauges stay steady, the showcase basic/icon-library/chart page screenshots match pre-change, hello-themed/sysmonitor smokes survive. Spot-checking component defaults (control_height 32, font scale 12-18, semantic colour sets) shows they sit close to AntD/Element and desktop GUI convention; no alignment action needed. Methodology: for default-flipping changes, patrol real pages before deciding — the showcase itself is the best regressor.
- **Lazy mounting × the flex shorthand: a new pathology (tabs start at height 0 and recover only after one switch round)**: after pages/segments moved to "mount on first selection", the Linux branch of tabs_t's content pages (`flex 1.0` shorthand) blew up under the new mounting order — in the full-mount era the first natural measure saw owner=nan so the content measure ran and everything looked fine (derived basis-0 resolution mechanics: see the "mbt.19 patch boundary" entry); lazy mounting attaches the tabs only **after the parent chain's layout is stable**, so the first basis evaluation triggered by the child joining sees a definite owner size, the shorthand's derived basis-0 resolves straight to 0 and enters the "already computed" cache, and the initially visible page was never hidden — outside mbt.19's "zeroed by display and re-shown" protection. Result: the initial page has height 0 until one tab switch (which triggers the re-show protection). Fix: the Linux-branch content pages write grow/shrink separately (basis auto content measure, the same two-mode semantics as outer); the Windows explicit-basis-0 branch is kept. Lesson: **mbt.19's re-show protection covers only the "hidden→shown" path; "mounted visible after the layout is stable" is its blind spot, and the ban on the flex shorthand for two-mode containers holds equally for deferred mounting.** Regression: the showcase tab section has height from the start and switches normally, probe-collapse2 gauges stay steady, sysmonitor (mount-at-launch scenario) overview is complete. Family-wide sweep: of the 19 `flex 1.0` shorthands inside yue, the 4 combining a column main axis with an auto-height parent chain (progress_line, the divider's horizontal branch, the slider's auto-width branch, the carousel panel) must collapse the same way and were uniformly rewritten to grow/shrink; the rest sit on row main axes (definite width) or definite-size mount-at-launch contexts and do not collapse, so they stay. Verification: the progress segment shows its 25% fill on first mount, dividers draw their 1px line, and the carousel panel's height were all screenshot-confirmed. Testing-methodology lesson: when driving verification with xdotool, mind single-instance merging (a new instance wakes the first and exits, so screenshots catch the old-code window) and X window-id reuse — always pair "PID filtered by exe path ↔ wmctrl window", and first-mount-class bugs must be verified on a brand-new instance.

- **yoga-mbt, first batch of the pure-MoonBit flexbox engine (feature/yoga-mbt branch — a separate line from the embedded C++ Yoga)**: a layout layer pre-positioned for MoonBit-izing libyue, a standalone sub-package (modules/yoga-mbt, zero FFI, no prebuild). The positioning difference first: the earlier decisions in this section ("shrink defaults to 0 / useWebDefaults off") govern the C++ Yoga inside the native widget tree and do not transfer; yoga-mbt, per the user's requirement, aligns only to the single CSS Flexbox L1 standard and defaults entirely to web semantics (row / shrink 1 / basis auto / align stretch / min:auto). Reference material: W3C css-flexbox-1 §9 in full (w3.org/TR/css-flexbox-1; the §9 algorithm steps sit in li#algo-* list items) plus the official Yoga source (github facebook/yoga, yoga/algorithm/CalculateLayout.cpp and FlexLine.cpp; raw.githubusercontent timed out, so `git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse git@github.com:...` over SSH was used). Three substantive deviations decided by the spec: ① §9.7's freezing algorithm — the spec starts the target size from the flex base, pre-freezes inflexible items (factor 0 / clamped by min-max), and each loop selectively freezes by the sign of the total violation (positive freezes the min-violators, negative the max-violators, zero freezes all); Yoga's own comment admits its two-pass scheme deviates from the spec — this engine follows the spec; ② shrink weighting uses the inner base size (base − own padding/border, per the spec text) while Yoga uses the border-box base; ③ with a single line and a definite container cross size, the line cross size simply takes the container's inner cross size (§9.6), and align-content has no effect on a single line — the earlier implementation that patched with align-content:stretch would misplace non-stretch align_content on single-line containers. Measured pitfalls (pure MoonBit side, moon 0.1.20260904 + moonc 0.10.x): line-continuation operators must sit at the end of the previous line (a leading `+`/`-` reports unbound `~+`); no `+=`/`-=` compound assignment; bare `0..n` is illegal — `0..<n`; a `1e15` scientific-notation literal fails to parse — spell `1000000000000.0`; `fold` requires the label `fold(init=0.0, ...)`; `guard` is a reserved word; generics are `fn[T] f(...)`, not `fn f[T]`; top-level constants use `const NAME` or lowercase `let`; a `pub priv struct` type is invisible outside (a pub fn signature referencing it reports 4046 "public definition cannot depend on private type"), so the need for private fields actually forces `pub struct`; a mut field "never assigned" is an error (0015), and mutating an inner field through a reference does not count as mutating the outer one; the new moon.pkg DSL does not know warn_list (Unexpected key) — to switch a package-level lint off, keep the old JSON file name `moon.pkg.json` with `{"warn_list": "-6"}` (unused_constructor is a false positive for a library whose constructors exist for consumers; this disables it explicitly); test assertions are `assert_eq(a, b)` without the `!` suffix and usable only in a context with an error type (inside test blocks). Verification: `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test -p NoahLiu/yoga-mbt/src` 19/19 all green (expected values hand-computed from the spec; the first version's 5 wrong assertions were treating stretch-fill and the min:auto floor as bugs — same behaviour as browsers, so the expectations were fixed, not the code).

- **yoga-mbt absolute positioning (YG2a)**: the containing block is the parent container's padding box (width/height = border box − both borders, padding included); inset and margin percentages resolve against the containing block's corresponding axis; sizing rule: explicit width/height > both insets on the same axis (stretched = containing block − both insets − both margins, floored at content box 0) > content measure; positioning rule: an inset on the axis wins (the far side takes containing block − right/bottom − margin − size), both-auto on an axis falls to the static position — lay out a phantom item by the parent's justify-content (main axis) / align-items (cross axis), ignoring siblings (space-distributing justify values resolve to 0). One pitfall: sizes from content measure are **not additionally clamped to available space** (available space reaches the measure function only in AtMost form, same as Yoga) — an initial `min(avail)` clamp crushed the "auto-size parent + fixed-content leaf" case to 0 (worst when the auto parent's padding box is 0); verification: `moon check` zero warnings + repo-wide `moon test` 687/687 (7 new: out-of-flow with left/top, same-axis both-side inset stretch, all-auto static-position centering, right/bottom anchoring, not inflating the container's content size, recursive embedded subtree, percentage inset against the padding box).

- **yoga-mbt baseline alignment (YG2b) + a cross-axis margin placement defect**: the API is `set_baseline(f : (avail_w, avail_h) -> Option[Double])`, and the return value means **baseline distance from the content box top** (symmetric with `set_measure`; the engine adds its own padding/border); containers set no callback — baselines are derived by the engine per spec §8.5: if the first line has a baseline-aligned item, take the line's common baseline (max ascent), otherwise the baseline-carrying in-flow item earliest on the cross axis (nested containers propagate theirs upward). The line cross size gets §9.4's front half: collect items whose "inline axis parallel to the main axis + align-self baseline + both cross margins not auto + real baseline", take max(baseline-to-outer-cross-start) + max(baseline-to-outer-cross-end), and max that with the existing "largest outer cross size"; placement per §9.6 "largest ascent sits at the line's cross start" = maxAscent − margin-start − baseline. Three settled points: ① even with a definite container cross size on a single line, the line cross size still takes the container's inner cross size (the §9.6 short-circuit wins) — baselines move items, not lines; ② no baseline alignment when the main axis is column (the spec's collection requires items whose inline axis parallels the main axis; a column container's cross axis is horizontal), placed at the start = browser behaviour; ③ **items without a baseline are excluded from the baseline group and placed as flex-start** — the spec only says "synthesize from the border box when there is no baseline" without stating which edge (css-align-3 synthesizes the first baseline at the block-start edge; browsers historically used the bottom edge for replaced/empty blocks — a real divergence), so this engine chooses "do not synthesize", matching Yoga's dimbound branch and staying fully compatible with the pre-change "treat Baseline as FlexStart" behaviour; consumers wanting the browser's "image bottom sits on the baseline" can return their own height from the baseline callback. Measured defect (surfaced by this batch's new assertions, same origin as the baseline math): **cross-axis margins never participated in child placement** — `pos_cross` was just "line offset + align offset" while `free_c` had already used margin-inclusive outer sizes, so a `margin_top: 30` item stuck to the line start (measured `0 != 30`) and `align-items: flex-end` + `margin_top: 20` swallowed the margin whole (measured `130 != 150`); the main axis was fine (`pos_main` accumulated `m.start`). Fix: placement is now "line offset + align offset + margin start" (auto margins resolve to 0, so the auto branch is unaffected). One more **open item** surfaced: when a container's auto main size is content-derived, `content_main_sum` sums only children and misses the container's own padding/border, and the multi-line branch hardcodes it to 0 (a wrap container's auto main size collapses to 0) — deferred to the next batch (YG2b′, numeric case and fix in that entry); this batch holds the corresponding assertion out. Verification: `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test -p NoahLiu/yoga-mbt/src` 36/36 + repo-wide `moon test` 697/697 (10 new: cross-axis margin placement and stretch, margin with flex-end, two items baseline-aligned, baselines determine line cross size (indefinite container), stretch items excluded from baseline grouping, baseline-less items placed flex-start, margin-top counted in ascent, multi-line baselines scoped per line, nested-container baseline propagation, column containers skip baseline alignment); reference: W3C css-flexbox-1 §9.4 (algo-cross-line) / §9.6 (algo-cross-align) / §8.5 (Flex Container Baselines).

- **yoga-mbt container auto size missing its own padding/border + multi-line main size collapsing to 0 (YG2b′)**: during YG2b a probe measured (parent `padding-top:10 / padding-left:10` + one 100×50 child, container without width/height) auto size 100×50 in both row and column directions; browsers give 110×60. Root cause: the "own size" step used `content_main_sum` (children's size_main + margin only) and `own_cross_content` (line cross sizes only) directly as the container's border-box size, though width/height semantics are explicitly border-box — its own padding/border was never added; child **placement** was always right (`layout_left = own_border.left + own_pad.left + x`), so the symptom is "size one notch short, children correctly placed", easily misread as a broken measure function. The second hole sits in the same place: the multi-line branch hardcoded `content_main_sum` to `0.0`, so a wrap container without an explicit main size collapses that whole axis to 0. Fix: the main axis takes the max over lines of each line's outer size (size_main + both margins + that line's column/row gap), the cross axis sums the line cross sizes, and both then get `pad_border_main / pad_border_cross` added; the `nlines == 1` branch stays equivalent to the old value (an auto-main container never joins flex resolution, so `size_main` ≡ `hyp_main` and switching to "max per line" changes nothing for single lines). Verification: `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test -p NoahLiu/yoga-mbt/src` 40/40 + repo-wide `moon test` 701/701 (4 new: row-container auto size includes padding, column-container same, border-inclusive 47×23, wrap container "main = widest line + cross = summed line heights" = 90×50 with the two rows' children at top 10/30; and the nested-container `b.height == 35` assertion pulled out during YG2b is reinstated).

- **yoga-mbt aspect-ratio (YG2c) — ratio semantics settled as border-box**: the user's rule is "ratio = border-box width / border-box height", consistent with the engine's existing width/height = border-box and differing from CSS's default content-box ratio (noted in the README; no padding subtraction anywhere in the conversion). Four hook points: ① §9.2 flex base — item with a ratio + content basis + definite cross axis → main basis = cross axis converted through the ratio (a column container divides instead); ② §4.5 auto minimum size — main-axis `min:auto` takes the **smaller** of "content size" and "transferred size suggestion", otherwise the ratio is pushed back by the content floor (measured: content width 200 + height 10 + ratio 2 → should be 20; writing `min:auto = content` yields 200); ③ §9.4 hypothetical cross size — once the main size is settled (including the §9.7 flex-resolution result), cross = main converted through the ratio, then clamped by min/max; ④ the container's own size — when one axis is definite (explicitly or dictated by the parent) and the other auto, the converted axis **counts as a definite size** in all later computation (written into `inner_main` / `inner_cross`), so wrap limits, flex resolution, line cross sizes and stretch all run on it; skipping that step gave the wrong result "a `width:320 + aspect-ratio:2` container collapses to content height 50 and its children stretch to 50 too". One straight-from-spec behaviour worth stating: `align-items: stretch` (this engine's default) overrides the ratio's cross-axis conversion — §9.4 algo-stretch keys on "the computed cross size property is auto" and footnotes "this step does not affect the item's main size, even when it has a preferred aspect ratio", so ratio items in a stretch container take the line cross size; keeping the ratio needs non-stretch alignment or an explicit cross size (same as browsers; covered by unit tests). Absolutely positioned children deliberately skip ratio conversion this batch (that path still sizes only by explicit dimensions / same-axis both-side insets / content), recorded in the README's not-implemented list. Verification: `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test -p NoahLiu/yoga-mbt/src` 47/47 + repo-wide `moon test` 708/708 (7 new: width→height, height→width, column container height→width, container self-sizing by ratio with children filling, stretch overriding ratio (and restoring after changing align_self), ratio feeding the min:auto ceiling, non-positive ratio treated as unset); reference: W3C css-flexbox-1 §9.2 / §4.5 / §9.4 and css-sizing-4's preferred aspect ratio.

- **yoga-mbt RTL (direction, YG2d) + two pre-existing defects in flip placement**: direction semantics are settled as **per-node, without CSS's direction inheritance** — the engine's `layout_into` only receives the parent's available size and has no parent-chain style context, while on the libyue side themes/controls know which container to set rtl on; the inheritance chain is left to the wrapper layer. The implementation touches only the "resolution and mapping" layer: two derived flags, `rev_main = is_reverse(flex_direction) != (rtl && the main axis is a row)` (a row container flips once for direction and once for row-reverse; a column container's main axis is the block axis, unaffected by direction) and `rev_cross = rtl && the main axis is a column` (flip only when the cross axis is the inline axis); `axis_margin` gains a `cross_reverse` parameter deciding whether the cross start reads margin-left or margin-right — **the physical edges are always margin-left/right; only the meaning of "start/end" rotates with direction** — and auto-margin allocation follows the edge it belongs to (Yoga's same semantics). A row container's cross axis is the block axis, so baseline grouping, align-items vertical placement and rtl are fully independent; an rtl column container, with `pos_cross` (including the line offset) flipped whole after wrapping, lands the first column on the right and the next to its left (proven by unit tests). This batch's RTL flip reference surfaced two pre-existing defects: ① **row-reverse / column-reverse computed negative offsets under an auto main container size** — the flip reference used `inner_main_dim.unwrap_or(0.0)`, which is None when the container's main size is content-derived, so a 100-wide item landed at -100 and the second at -200 (measured by probe); fixed to "prefer the container's definite inner main size, else the content-derived maximum line main size (`line_main_max`, incidentally hoisted from the own-size step to before the placement step)"; ② **an all-auto abspos item's static position always landed left/top** — YG2a's static position computed only justify/align offsets and never followed the main-axis flip; in a `column-reverse` container it should hug the bottom but hugged the top; fixed so the static position's start follows its axis's flip flag (margins likewise take the owning start's physical edge). Verification: `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test -p NoahLiu/yoga-mbt/src` 60/60 + repo-wide `moon test` 721/721 (13 new: 3 LTR snapshots locking the flip-reference and static-position behaviour + 10 rtl: row container starts at the right, rtl×row-reverse returns to left, column container cross start on the right, start takes the right margin, justify flex-end landing at the physical left, physical margins participating in the main axis, margin auto absorption, abspos static position hugging right in row/column containers, rtl column-container wrap order); the 47 pre-existing LTR assertions keep every value — the direction layer regressed nothing. Reference: W3C css-flexbox-1's definition that "the main-start is decided jointly by direction and flex-direction" (the flex-direction vs Writing-Modes inline/block-axis relation) + css-position-3's static position.

- **yoga-mbt abspos children consuming aspect-ratio (YG2e, closing YG2's standard surface)**: the abspos sizing priority was "explicit width/height > same-axis both-side inset stretch > content measure"; the ratio conversion inserts one step in between — first resolve "the axis that is known" by the old rules (explicit, or stretched by left/right or top/bottom insets), then, when the other axis stays auto, convert it through the ratio with the item's own padding/border as the floor, and clamp by min/max; when **both** axes are auto it **still content-measures** (same as in-flow items — a ratio conjures no size from nothing). All-auto side placement keeps YG2d's direction-flip flags, untouched by this batch. Verification: `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test -p NoahLiu/yoga-mbt/src` 63/63 + repo-wide `moon test` 724/724 (3 new: width→height, height→width, both-side-inset stretch width then ratio height).

- **yoga-mbt enums not constructible across packages (E4036) + the performance baseline (YG3a, first engineering batch)**: a blocking pit first — in this toolchain (moon 0.1.20260920 / moonc 0.10.14) a `pub enum` exposes only the **type** and match-readability outside the package; **constructing variants is read-only outside**: `@lib.Green` or `@lib.Color::Red` in an external package reports `E4036 Cannot create values of the read-only type`; `pub(readonly) enum` syntax is unsupported and a per-variant `pub` reports "No individual visibility for enum constructor". The correct form is **`pub(all) enum`** (basis: the official E4036/E0006 explanations in `moon check --explain` plus a two-package minimal repro). For yoga-mbt this means: the engine's nine enums — `FlexDirection / AlignItems / AlignContent / JustifyContent / FlexWrap / PositionType / Display / Direction / Value` — are all values consumers feed into setters, and under the old form **an external package could not set a single style**; unit tests never exposed it (tests share the package) — it exploded only when the new **external** bench package ran `moon check`, a guaranteed stumble before YG4 integration. Fix: all nine become `pub(all) enum`; `Value`'s existing `fixed/percent/auto/undefined` helpers stay (both spellings work for consumers). The same batch established the performance baseline, tool `modules/yoga-mbt/bench` (`moon run bench` / `moon run --release bench`; tree = root + 20 groups × (1 group head + 10 rows) × 5 nodes per row = 1121 nodes, rows with `align-items: baseline` + grow + gap + padding, leaves with measure, text with baseline callbacks; set `rounds` to 0 for the "process + tree build" baseline): measured here on Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 — 500 rounds of `calculate_layout`: debug 4.57s / release 2.21s; the 0-round baseline ≈ 0.106s, so **per round debug ≈ 8.9ms (8.0µs/node), release ≈ 4.2ms (3.8µs/node)**. The next optimization target is pointed at by the code structure itself: the same node goes through `layout_into` twice, once in "base measure" and once in "cross re-measure"; Yoga solves it with a 16-slot measurement cache — yoga-mbt's cache shape and invalidation policy are settled in the next entry (YG3b). Verification: `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test -p NoahLiu/yoga-mbt/src` 63/63 + repo-wide `moon test` 724/724, and with the bench package participating in `moon check` as an external consumer, "enums constructible across packages" now has a standing regression.

- **yoga-mbt measurement cache (YG3b)**: `measure_content` runs twice per layout for the same node (§9.2 base measure, §9.4 cross re-measure), and containers repeat further through the parent chain — the main redundancy in the baseline. Shape: **the cache hangs on `Node`** (`measure_cache : Array[((avail_w, avail_h), (w, h, baseline))]`; keys and values use only tuples and base types — a field of `pub struct Node` must not reference a priv type or E4046 "public definition cannot depend on private type" recurs), and a hit **returns the baseline together with the size** (the baseline is the intermediate a container propagates up for §9.4 grouping, same source as the size — omitting it would let rtl/baseline scenarios read a stale value). **Invalidation settled: the cache is valid within a single `calculate_layout`; the entry point clears the whole tree in one pre-order pass** — this engine has no dirty flags and consumers may freely change styles between two layouts (measured: padding-left 10→50, baseline 10→18); Yoga's "version/dirty" scheme would introduce a change-notification surface, while one O(n) pass is negligible next to a single layout, traded for zero invalidation holes. Payoff (same machine, same bench tree, 500 rounds): **debug per round 8.9ms → 5.1ms, release 4.2ms → 2.6ms (1121 nodes)** — about 1.7×; the remaining cost sits mainly in "the final placement round with pinned sizes" — that round must really run (child coordinates land); going further is YG4's dirty-region incremental relayout, not the engineering batch. Verification: `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test -p NoahLiu/yoga-mbt/src` 65/65 + repo-wide `moon test` 726/726 (2 new invalidation regressions: re-layout after a padding change does not take the old cache; re-layout after a baseline change likewise; zero regression across the existing 63 assertions means the cache does not alter layout results).

- **yoga-mbt pixel-grid rounding (YG3c)**: a root-node switch `set_pixel_grid(interval)` (`0.0` / negative disables; effective only when the node is the layout root); `calculate_layout` appends a post-pass that lands `left/top/width/height` on the grid; with the switch off every fractional value is preserved and the 65 existing assertions must not regress. Rounding is settled as **snap by absolute edges, then derive relative coordinates**: when adjacent items share a physical edge, both read the same absolute coordinate, so the snap agrees and a 100/3 split gives `33 / 34 / 33` (the sum equals the total width and no 1px seam is left between neighbours) — snapping "relative coordinate + own size" per item would record 33 thrice and lose 1px. **One pitfall**: when recursing the parent's start down, passing only "the snapped parent start" is **not enough** — you must also pass the parent's **pre-snap absolute start**: a child's `layout_left` is relative to the parent's **raw** coordinates, and reconstructing the child's absolute edges from the snapped parent start charges the parent's own half-grid error to the child — measured: the middle container's absolute start 33.33→33 with two children of raw width 16.67, so the second child's absolute start became `33 + 16.67 = 49.67`, absolute end `66.33`, rounding to 50/66 → width 16 (should be 17; the `16 != 17` assertion exploded it). After the fix the parameters split into `raw_*` (reconstructing the children's true absolute edges) and `snap_*` (deriving the children's relative coordinates); error appears only on each edge itself and is never transferred from the parent. **Not done**: Yoga's parent-end snap-back compensation (`pixelGridSnapError` and friends) — when a container has trailing padding/border, an item snapped to the inner edge's end may finish within one grid unit of the parent's inner edge; recorded in the README as a known limitation, to be added if visible seams appear on real hardware. Verification: `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test -p NoahLiu/yoga-mbt/src` 69/69 + repo-wide `moon test` 730/730 (4 new: whole-pixel split `33/34/33`, half-pixel grid `33.5/33/33.5`, no grid keeps `100.0/3.0`, nested items compensated by absolute coordinates `mid.left 33 / width 34` and `inner 0/17 + 17/17`).

- **yoga-mbt intrinsic sizes min/max/fit-content (YG3d, closing YG3)**: sources first — both Yoga and the spec were checked, nothing from memory. **Spec side**: css-flexbox-1 §9.9 "Intrinsic Sizes" is three sentences and delegates the definitions wholesale to css-sizing-3 (§2.1 auto box sizes gives the four sizes stretch-fit / max-content / min-content / fit-content; §5.2 intrinsic contributions says "a contribution is the content-box size of an auto float containing only that item in a zero-width / infinite-width containing block" and leaves the concrete algorithm to the spec of the corresponding display); **a flex container's own intrinsic-sizing rules are not in L1** (checked both w3.org/TR and drafts — `collected … contribution` appears in L1 only in §9.3 line collection), only in the css-flexbox-2 draft (which even splits ideal / web-compatible at §9.10.1). So this engine implements the css-sizing-3 general rules as a single algorithm, not L2's two (recorded in the README). **Yoga side** (checked against an SSH sparse clone of `facebook/yoga`'s `yoga/algorithm`+`yoga/style`+`yoga/enums`): ① `Unit` has only `MaxContent / FitContent / Stretch` — **no min-content keyword**, and the `SizingMode` comment itself admits "Missing min-content"; ② min-content exists only as a §4.5 internal quantity — `computeMinContentMainSize` calls a leaf's measure function with "requested axis `AtMost 0` + the other axis `Undefined`" (text returns the longest word), and for containers recurses directly, **looking only at the container's own main axis** (children's main summed, cross takes the max), ignoring flex-wrap and ignoring gap; ③ under `MaxContent` sizing mode the measure function's available space is rewritten to `YGUndefined`. This engine takes "Yoga's probing conventions + the spec's composition rules": leaf probing keeps `Some(0.0)` / `None` (compatible with the existing `set_measure` signature, no API change), container composition is wrap-aware (a wrap container's min-content main size = the widest single item, then a greedy line-packing at that width for the cross contribution; nowrap sums the items). **Two semantic corrections**: ① §4.5 `min:auto`'s content size suggestion was approximated by "the measured value at the current available space" → now true min-content; ② §9.2 `flex-basis: auto` with an auto main size used the same approximation → now **max-content** (otherwise a wrapped item's basis drifts with available space and shrink never sees the overflow; measured: a 100-wide container holding a wrap sub-container (items 60/50/40) — before: basis 90, no shrink; after: basis 150, shrinking to the available 100; at 55 available the min:auto=60 floor holds). New values `min_content() / max_content() / fit_content()` can enter width / height / min-* / max-* / flex-basis, and abspos items consume them too (one funnel at `axis_size`). Two stumbles: ① **intrinsic probing must not refresh the node's baseline** — the first version's leaf probe went through `measure_content`, and the unconstrained probe call overwrote the real layout's `Node.baseline`, so baseline grouping read a "single-line baseline"; fixed with a dedicated probe path calling the measure function directly. ② **the hot path pays for cache-key allocation** — `measure_content` built its key tuple before the linear compare, and the new intrinsic recursion raised per-node probes from 2 to 4–6, pushing per-round release from 1.30s (500 rounds) to 2.54s; bled down step by step (measured release 500 rounds: 2.54 → 2.07 by having containers compute only the main axis, skipping cross contributions → 1.93 by comparing entries one by one and building keys only at write time → 1.81 by bypassing `measure_content` for leaf probes plus a short-circuit "skip the corresponding intrinsic probe when an explicit size already decides that axis" — values that would be probed then discarded are no longer probed). Bench conventions (timing the built executable directly, 0-round baseline 0.106s — careful comparing with YG3a/YG3b's `moon run` numbers, not the same method; this batch's A/B is same-machine same-method): per round debug 4.9→7.3ms, release 2.4→3.4ms (1121 nodes) — real intrinsic sizes cost about +40%; further recovery needs "cache persistence across layouts + dirty-region incremental relayout", which belongs to the integration layer (YG4), not this batch. Verification: `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test -p NoahLiu/yoga-mbt/src` 79/79 + repo-wide `moon test` 740/740 (10 new: max-content not squeezed by available space, min-content = longest word, fit-content three-way clamp, min-width: max-content holding shrink, flex-basis: max-content joining grow, column container min/max-content width = widest child + padding, wrap-container basis max-content with the min-content floor, nowrap container min-content summing children, abspos item's max-content, intrinsic cache not reused after a child change; zero regression across the existing 69 assertions). Reference: css-flexbox-1 §9.9 / §4.5, css-sizing-3 §2.1 / §5.2, and `facebook/yoga`'s `yoga/algorithm/CalculateLayout.cpp` (`computeMinContentMainSize` / `measureNodeWithMeasureFunc`) with `yoga/style/StyleSizeLength.h`.

### MoonBit native GUI stack (G0 IME probe)

- **Environment**: Ubuntu 24.04 + X11 (XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11) + XFCE, moon 0.1.20260920; system libraries gtk+-3.0 3.24.41 / pangocairo 1.52.1 / cairo 1.18.0 / x11 1.8.7; the fcitx5 and ibus daemons are both installed, `GTK_IM_MODULE=fcitx`. The probe lives in `experiment/ime_probe`, two modes in one binary: mode B = a pure `GtkIMContext` channel (text state kept once, in MoonBit); mode C = a visible `GtkEntry` + CSS theming. **Four build-chain pitfalls**: ① **moon's `link_configs` carries link-time fields only** — adding `c_flags` to an entry is silently ignored, native-stub compiles without system include paths, and `#include <gtk/gtk.h>` is a fatal error; fix: mirror the shim — `scripts/prebuild.py`'s `build_ime_probe_stub()` compiles the stub with `pkg-config --cflags` into `build/libime_probe_stub.a`, passed only through `link_flags`. ② the archive must follow ld naming as `libime_probe_stub.a`, or `-lime_probe_stub` will not find it. ③ **moon does not relink when a native static library changes**: after editing the stub, `moon run` still launches the old exe (the SIGSEGV scene is identical) — the same "delete the artifacts after changing the shim" pit, reproduced here on the `-l` static-library path; delete `build/libime_probe_stub.a` and the package's exe before rerunning. ④ CI runs `moon build --target native` with **full-package linking** on all three platforms, so a Linux-only probe breaks `ip_*` symbols on Windows/macOS; fix: add `ime_probe_stub_portable.c`, giving every entry an empty implementation under `#if !defined(__linux__)` (`ip_init` returns 0 and the MoonBit side prints "no probe on this platform" then exits); this file goes through moon's own native-stub and is wholly empty on Linux. **Our own bug**: `ip_report_im_module` called `G_OBJECT_TYPE_NAME` on `pr.im == NULL` in mode C → SIGSEGV (exit code 139); mode C has no self-built context at all (the IM module hangs off the GtkEntry) — a smoke run of mode B alone never shows it, confirming again that "a branch counts as verified only once it really fired". **Three measured findings (input for G5)**: ① `g_main_context_iteration(NULL, TRUE)` stepping singly drives GTK windows and signals — **no `gtk_main` needed**, the main loop stays wholly in MoonBit, and both Esc and the 1500ms auto-exit quit cleanly with no teardown crash; ② **GtkEntry's size negotiation does push back** — offered a 22px box, the theme default grows the widget to 32~33px (`requested_h=22 allocated_h=33`); after `min-height: 0px` in CSS it lands at 24px (22 + 1px borders top and bottom), i.e. "can be squeezed, but will not honor the requested value"; ③ the Pango readings are directly usable — 14px measured line height 17px, prefix width 59px, caret rectangle `83,22 1x17` pushed to the IM channel (the input for candidate-window placement). **Pending real-hardware items**: commit / inline preedit / candidate window hugging / shortcut pass-through / whether Chinese can actually be typed — run per the `experiment/ime_probe/README.md` checklist under both fcitx5 and ibus `GTK_IM_MODULE` settings; conclusions land back in this section. Verification: `moon check` zero warnings + repo-wide `moon test` 740/740 + `moon build --target native` 68 tasks all pass + local two-mode smoke processes alive and exiting cleanly.

### MoonBit ↔ C ABI

- Trampolines must match the C function pointer prototype bit-for-bit, including arity: C calls `callback(closure, args...)` and the trampoline's first parameter receives the closure. Misalignment hides itself — row counts look right and some callbacks fire; a callback is verified only once it has actually fired.
- `extern "c"` returning nullable types: older toolchains segfault outright (report success/failure via a `Ref[Int]` out-parameter); on moon 0.1.20260904 + moonc v0.10.12, `-> Bytes?` works — a C-side NULL maps to None correctly, verified in both debug and release against real missing-file and directory (EISDIR) paths (sysmonitor's read_text_file). Other nullable types (handles etc.) are untested; the out-parameter pattern remains the fallback.
- FFI pointer parameters need `#borrow` (compiler-enforced); widget parameters take the handle type `View`, never the MoonBit wrapper struct (otherwise handles are invalid at runtime and silently dropped).
- Closures across the ABI: capture-free top-level function literals compile to real C function pointers; capturing closures use the "function pointer + closure pointer" two-parameter form.
- Callback closures are kept alive process-wide by a registry and not reclaimed per window (negligible leak for single-window tools — settled).
- Toolbar / Vibrant have no Linux static-library symbols (the link would fail) and are not exposed; the Browser empty-cookie-list crash is fixed since fork mbt.7.
- Changing a shim signature requires the same batch in `.cpp` / `yue_mbt.h` / ffi.mbt; both a missed signature sync and an entirely missed declaration manifest as a mangle split (`_Z`-prefixed symbol vs plain-C reference) — locate with nm, and run a ".cpp definitions × header declarations" cross-scan before packaging.
- **A standalone translation unit (e.g. `yue_accent_mac.mm`) that does not include `yue_mbt.h` must mark its function definitions `extern "C"` explicitly**: without it they export C++-mangled (`__Z25yue_mbt_system_accent_macv`) while `yue_mbt.cpp` references the plain-C name from the header — link-time undefined. Only macOS exposes this (Linux/Windows never compile the .mm), and neither does the vendor/CI prepare stage (a static archive never checks undefined) — only a real macOS link (moon test/build) hits it; with no local mac, CI is the only defense line. Actually fixed ahead of the 0.5.0 release (symbol re-verified via strings on the re-vendored archive as `_yue_mbt_system_accent_mac`).
- The XFCE panel prioritizes IconPixmap over IconName: set_icon_name and set_pixmap are mutually exclusive — setting one must clear the other.
- **Custom-protocol reject encoding and C-side payload pre-validation (CORE1, high severity)**: the None reject path of `Browser::register_protocol` used to encode `[1,0,0,0]` — the C side read the first 4 little-endian bytes as `ok=1` (success) and kept reading mime_len/content_len past the end of the 4-byte buffer (native heap over-read), then built `std::string(p+8, mime_len)` from a garbage length: undefined behavior. And the reject never actually took effect (libyue's WebKitGTK side rejects a request only when the handler returns nullptr, via `finish_error` — see OnProtocolRequest in the yue fork's `nativeui/gtk/browser_gtk.cc`). Fix: the MoonBit reject payload is now `[0,0,0,0]` (ok=0, so C returns nullptr without reading further bytes), with the encoding extracted into the in-package pure function `encode_protocol_payload` for white-box tests; the C side pre-validates against the MoonBit Bytes length before decoding segment by segment — ok==0 or a payload shorter than 12 bytes is rejected, as are negative or out-of-payload mime_len/content_len (length comparisons go through int64 to avoid `8+mime_len+4` overflow), and a nullptr payload is also defensively rejected. The Bytes length is the 4 bytes preceding the data pointer (the moonbit_object header's meta, which is the length for VAL_ARRAY; layout follows moonbit.h's `Moonbit_array_length` — moonbit.h itself is not included because its extern "C" memcpy declaration conflicts with glibc), and that assumption was empirically verified with a minimal C probe linking libmoonbitrun.o + the libruntime archive directly (make_bytes(23/4/0) all read back the correct length). Lesson: **for a self-encoded ABI payload with length fields, the C side must be able to obtain the total length itself and pre-validate first** — never trust fields after the peer "claims success"; cross-ABI contract tests must mirror the C decode logic (length pre-check, then segment reads) rather than only asserting the encoder's shape. Verification: `moon check` with zero warnings + `moon test` 636 all green (new yue/browser/browser_wbtest.mbt with 8 cases: None payload byte-exact as `[0,0,0,0]`; Some byte-exact across ok/mime_len/mime/content_len/content; UTF-8 multi-byte lengths counted in bytes; the 12-byte minimal payload for empty mime/content; the legacy `[1,0,0,0]` shape and an 8-byte ok=1 short payload both rejected; out-of-payload mime_len/content_len rejected; round-trip with long content containing quotes and newlines); the shim change went through prebuild's incremental rebuild, and after deleting the showcase exe under `_build`, `moon build examples/showcase` relinks with zero warnings (nm confirms the exe references yue_mbt_browser_register_protocol); showcase gains a demo-deny reject-path button and code snippet — the real-hardware load-failure behavior is for the user to confirm under Linux WebKitGTK (Windows WebView2 silently ignores custom protocols anyway).

### Unified style value model (StyVal trait) and MoonBit trait object limits (0.5.2)

- Unified style value model: the open trait `StyVal` (`yue/style.mbt`) implements `apply_to(Self, View, String)` for the builtins `Double`/`String`; the mixed-typed array `Array[(String, &StyVal)]` takes pixel and string values in one parameter, dispatching internally to the two C channels `ffi_view_set_style_prop_float/_str` (the C ABI has no overloads; the split is absorbed inside yue). Where the expected type is known, array literals auto-box (also propagated inside tuples), so existing numeric-only call sites migrate unchanged.
- **trait-object impl limits for builtin types** (moonc v0.10.12 measured, /tmp probes): ① one impl block may define exactly one method — multi-method `impl T for X with fn a.. fn b..`, across lines or on one line, does not exist; ② an impl block must define every trait method at once — a two-method trait with a type implementing only one reports "does not implement trait, although an impl is defined: method X is missing", and `&Trait` references then report "trait not found"; ③ "declare `= _` + package-level default impl + per-type override block" does not work for builtin types (for struct types it is the documented form — see the J trait example in moonbit-docs); even writing both methods in the override block fails the check; ④ conclusion: implementing your own trait for builtin types needs one impl block per type defining all methods (core's Show/Hash take the same shape); therefore StyVal can only be single-method and "reading the value back from the trait object" (an as_num channel) is not viable.
- **Version-sensitive APIs of the core library**: `StringView::exact_view` does not exist in moon 0.1.20260904's core (no method), while on 0.1.20260920 it exists and `sub` in turn is flagged deprecated — such APIs exist mutually exclusively as nightly core evolves; follow the current nightly's canonical names, and on version switches take `moon check` output as the standard.
- **CI-failure investigation path and nightly traits** (measured): when CI is red across all three platforms, the anonymous API cannot fetch logs (the job logs endpoint 403s), but `GET /repos/:repo/check-runs/:job_id/annotations` is readable; when the annotations are empty and only "Process completed with exit code 1" shows, walk the job's steps list (`.../actions/runs/:id/jobs`) to find the red step. moon nightly rolls extremely fast (0.1.20260918 404s within days; 0.1.20260920 was 403/delisted the same evening), so a version-pinned install-script download gets swept by the rolling delisting — **CI must not pin a nightly version number, only follow the latest alias**.
- **bind_node remount breaks Windows mouse hit-testing at runtime (real hardware, three-version evolution conclusion)**: bind_node removes+adds the subtree when the signal changes; on Windows, once a click chain triggers a remount, **every later click in the whole window is routed to the remounted widget** (probe v3 event flow: clicking row 1 / blank space both fire row 2's callback, and the root container receives nothing at all), and deferring the remount by one tick does not dodge it either — the harmful part is remove+add itself, not synchronous stack timing. Hit-testing goes through ContainerImpl::FindChildFromPoint's GetClippedRect (= size_allocation_ layout rect); after remove, the newly added subtree's value abnormally expands; the libyue-level root cause awaits a fork fix. **Workaround**: scenarios whose click chain remounts its own landing point switch to "prebuild both states + set_visible toggling" — visibility goes through the is_visible_ flag + display:none (the fork's yoga-display-none-flex-basis.patch maintains it specifically), no view destroyed or rebuilt; verified by probe row 5; bind_node's doc gained the warning. Linux's GTK layout sync does not have this problem, and bind_node runs normally there.
- **swap_node: the Windows-safe alternative to bind_node (0.5.2, verified on real hardware)**: for two-state switching (icon button swap / whole-view swap), `swap_node(sig, a, b)` prebuilds two node trees and the signal chooses visibility — no view destroyed or rebuilt, zero hit-test risk; the showcase light/dark switch moved to it and Windows real-hardware multi-round switching plus later operations all behave (with the bind_node version every click in the whole window misfired and even the title bar could not close it). Cost: both subtrees stay resident (negligible for low-frequency scenarios). Once the fork root-fix lands, bind_node returns to all platforms and swap_node stays (zero-rebuild, low overhead).
- **theme_apply's Windows branch must not be deferred (lesson archived)**: following the hypothesis "a synchronous repaint inside a click stack disturbs message state", it was once switched to the Linux-style post_task/post_delayed_task deferral — the black-box test (components_wbtest calling theme_apply) then crashed at process exit when the 60ms delayed task ran EnumWindows/RedrawWindow against a destroyed window, failing Windows CI with exit -1 twice in a row; and the hypothesis itself was already disproved by the probe (the real culprit is bind_node remounting). Windows keeps synchronous ffi_repaint_all; Linux keeps its original two-tick deferral.
- **bind_node remount breaks Windows mouse hit-testing at runtime (real hardware)**: bind_node's signal change goes through remove+add remount; on Windows the yoga root is not recomputed (native v0.15.6-mbt.19 only repairs the zeroed node itself, not tree-shape changes), so the new subtree's bounds stay dirty and hit-testing always lands on it — symptom: "after clicking the light/dark switch, every click in the window triggers the theme switch and all other operations are dead"; the keyboard is unaffected because it follows focus. Fix: bind_node's rebuild tail calls refresh_layout on the mounting container under Windows (whole-window relayout + root repaint, the same fallback as tabs page switching). Linux's GTK size request automatically covers the new subtree, so no such step is needed. Same family: the toast layer dynamically removing entries is pure deletion (within mbt.19's repair surface) — currently fine.
- **After moving the repository wholesale, the CMake cache refuses to configure (real hardware)**: CMakeCache.txt under build/ records the configure-time absolute directory; after the repo is copied from the old path to a new one, cmake reports "current CMakeCache.txt directory is different than..." and refuses to configure, aborting prepare.py. Fix: before cmake_build, prepare detects a CMakeCache-recorded CMAKE_CACHEFILE_DIR/CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY that differs from the current path and clears build/ to reconfigure (shim rebuilt along the way) — no manual directory deletion needed.
- **Windows usernames with apostrophes/spaces cause LNK1104 (real hardware)**: on Windows, moon assembles the cl/link command line with broken quoting for absolute paths containing a single quote — library paths under `C:\Users\noah'liu\...` lose the apostrophe, and the two space-separated paths `yue_mbt.lib` and `yue_prebuilt.lib` fuse into **one** link input, giving LNK1104 "cannot open file …lib …lib"; prepare.py/cmake are unaffected (paths pass through verbatim) — only moon's link_flags concatenation breaks. Fix: the prebuild Windows branch issues library/manifest paths **relative to the module root** (`build/yue_mbt.lib`, `lib/windows-x64/…`); the moon link subprocess's cwd is the module root (running `moon build` from the module root is the premise), and relative paths contain only safe characters, sidestepping the issue naturally; Linux/macOS pass argument arrays without command-line concatenation, so they keep absolute paths.
- **Same family, second case: an apostrophe path silently deletes the whole link_flags line (2026-10-15, Windows 10.0.19044 local machine, reproduced on the new stack)**: moon re-splits the `link_flags` issued by prebuild **by shell word lexing**, so a single quote in a path (`C:\Users\noah'liu\...`) is an **unbalanced quote** — the entry is dropped wholesale with **no error at all**; the symptom is not "cannot find this file" but **every library in that entry is gone**. Both absolute-path entries in this repo got hit: ① `gui/scripts/prebuild.py`'s `web/lib/WebView2LoaderStatic.lib` for the web package (the only path-bearing entry; the other 4 pure system libraries unaffected) was dropped whole ⇒ `shlwapi.lib` and the static Loader vanished together, and linking reported a string of LNK2019 for `CreateCoreWebView2EnvironmentWithOptions`/`GetAvailableCoreWebView2LoaderVersion`; ② `modules/ffmpeg-mbt/prebuild.py`'s five ffmpeg import libraries, same shape same result (`av_*` unresolved). Fix: **wrap each path in link_flags in double quotes** (`f'"{lib}"'`) — balanced quotes make the lexer treat the apostrophe as an ordinary character; `stub-cc-flags` follows the same rule (`-I"${build.FFMPEG_INC}"`, otherwise the apostrophe path splits into two arguments on the cl side). **Acceptance check**: run `echo '{}' | python gui/scripts/prebuild.py` and confirm the web entry is a complete quoted path; grep the built exe for `WebView2` to prove the static Loader really linked (for ffmpeg the check is "the test exe links out"; the runtime 0xc0000135 is the separate "dlls not shipped" issue recorded in the README). **Different root cause from the previous entry**: that one broke at command-line assembly for the link subprocess, failing outright with LNK1104; this one loses the entry during moon's own link_flags parsing, so the build looks green all the way until only symbol errors remain — much harder to attribute. **General rule**: on Windows, quote every path-bearing prebuild argument (link_flags / stub-cc-flags) in double quotes; never assume moon escapes for us. Relativizing is even better where possible, but the web/ffmpeg entries must reference absolute paths across modules, so relativizing is not viable there.
- **Vendored library cascade mis-linking (shallow clone) — the root cause of the whole CI line red (closed by measurement)**: the prebuild's `_native_dir()` cascade prefers `lib/<platform>/` vendored and falls back to `build/`, and its freshness test `_sources_newer` relies on git pathspec commit times; under actions/checkout's default fetch-depth=1 shallow clone the pathspec-limited log degrades to HEAD's time, t_shim==t_lib always holds → the shim is judged no newer than the library → vendored is always taken — and `ensure_native_lib` returns with zero compilation when the vendored is in place. New symbols where the shim leads the vendored packaging (e.g. view_set_bounds/scroll_refresh_content_size) are all undefined at CI link time, while a local full clone's git-time comparison uses build/ and never reproduces it. Fix: `_native_dir()` now gives **top priority to build/ whenever prepare artifacts exist (stamp + library)** — dev/CI-chain artifacts are freshly compiled against the current shim and can never be older than vendored; vendored only serves mooncakes users with no build/; `_sources_newer` conservatively falls back to build/ under shallow-clone equality or mtime races. Lesson: **shim-leading-vendored is the normal state**; when in doubt the cascade must recompile rather than mis-link an old library.
- After the layout parameters were folded in, Windows single-line input vertical centering no longer reads numeric values: switched to a pure layout solution — the Entry control is narrowed to the line height (`entry_ctrl_height`, text centers naturally inside the control) and the shell's `justifyContent=center` centers vertically, adapting automatically to any height value (percentages included); the old entry_vcenter "narrow + equal-distribute margins" path is deleted.
- select_t/dropdown_menu popups take the width live at click time via `get_bounds(field)` (after a user style overrides the field width, the popup follows automatically); the popup root container's width/height must still be given at creation time — a late set_style gets swallowed by the popup's allocation timing (see the GTK section).

### Directory enumeration and in-process environment variables (the shim's POSIX / Win32 branches)

- Directory enumeration (`yue_mbt_list_dir`, serving fsx_list_dir; the shim is compiled under prebuild.py's management): POSIX uses `opendir`/`readdir` (skipping `.` and `..`), Windows uses `FindFirstFileW`. **FindFirstFileA is not usable** — the A version is ANSI-codepage, so non-ASCII paths (Chinese user directories) come out garbled; paths convert with `base::SysUTF8ToWide`, the pattern appends `L"\\*"`, and entries convert back via `SysWideToUTF8`. The return value is flat UTF-8 text with entry names separated by '\n' (matching this package's multi-string return convention, same encoding as browser cookie / clipboard get_data); **an extreme filename whose own name contains '\n' gets split apart** — a known boundary of the flat-text encoding that docs must state. The `ok` out-parameter distinguishes "empty text from failure" from "empty directory" (empty directory: ok=1 with empty text, a legitimate success).
- In-process environment variables (`yue_mbt_setenv` / `yue_mbt_unsetenv`, serving fsx/envx): POSIX calls `setenv`/`unsetenv` directly; Windows uses `_putenv_s`, which **always overwrites** — the `overwrite=0` branch must first probe with `std::getenv`, otherwise the "keep the existing value" semantic is silently broken. Deleting an environment variable on Windows is `_putenv_s(name, "")` (removes the variable, not sets it to empty), aligned with POSIX `unsetenv`; a name that was never there also records ok=1 (idempotent). Scope is **the current process** in both cases (later-spawned children see it), with no touch to persistent system configuration and no effect on the parent process.
- fsx folds these two kinds of thin primitives into one module (shared by appfind / browser_history / envx): the point is "list entry names only, never read content", fixing appfind's old trade-off of "reading whole large executables just to test existence" — appfind used read_binary_file for existence, now it checks directory entries through fsx_list_dir.

### Package split: single yue package → core + six sub-packages (0.5.11)

- Environment: moon 0.1.20260920 / moonc v0.10.14, module NoahLiu/native-gui; prebuilt native libs in place.
- Symptom: before the split the single yue package held ~60k lines — FFI, native widgets, the themed component library, 20+ charts, markdown, the declarative layer and 30 system-capability files in one package. MoonBit compiles per package with no tree shaking inside a package, so webview-based or core-only consumers were forced to compile the whole toolkit into their binary.
- Root cause (mechanism): MoonBit cross-package references must be qualified `@alias.name` — two proofs: the official moonbitlang/async src/fs sub-package references the root package as `@async.xxx`, and this repo's yue/media.mbt references the traybus package as `@traybus.xxx`. The split therefore means: one moon.pkg per sub-package, every in-package core reference qualified with `@yue.` (word-boundary codemod that must skip `.field` accesses, `::method` suffixes and string literals), and external dependency declarations sinking to package level (mizchi/markdown → yue/markdown; subproc and moonsqlitefile → yue/system). No prebuild change was needed: link_configs concatenates flags across the dependency closure, so a new package importing only core automatically gets `-lyue_mbt`; webkit stays confined to the yue/browser entry and on-demand linking is not broken.
- Fix (batch order is the cycle-avoidance plan): ① markdown moves first — it calls components' code_view, so moving it later would cycle core→components→core; ② components — the pre-surgery lifts the `hand()` cursor helper from components.mbt into core as pub (charts_interactive references it cross-package and charts moves later), and ~17 private theme getters plus bind_fg/bind_entry_theme/ctrl_height, referenced by 20+ files, get pub-ified on demand; ③ icons; ④ charts (charts_wbtest.mbt carries its own extern "C", so its moon.pkg needs a native-only targets entry); ⑤ declarative — two pre-surgeries: the Node protocol (struct Node + attach) is extracted from declarative.mbt into core's yue/node.mbt (otherwise four packages' unqualified Node references all break), and signals.mbt's trailing `bind()` (which calls bind_label) moves into the declarative package with it; ⑥ system — the cross-platform `open_url` (system.mbt) and the tray tray.mbt stay in core (markdown's link clicks depend on open_url; procrun goes with the system layer); ⑦ version close-out 0.5.11: moon.mod, yue/version.mbt and the modules/gui-media pin synchronized in three places (prebuild validates consistency at build time; a mismatch makes moon build fail outright).
- Verification and the lesson: each batch ran moon check zero-warning + full moon test + moon build of examples/showcase and sysmonitor; an independent reviewer read-only-audited the git diff (symbol-for-symbol equivalence, moon.pkg hygiene, no strays). **Lesson: the gate missed systemprobe** — after the batched commits, the pushed tree failed systemprobe's build with 15 broken links (its import adaptation stayed uncommitted in the working tree); hello/hello-themed were unaffected, so the two-example gate noticed nothing, and only a `git stash` test on the committed state found it. Gate package-split work against every example, and check each commit's scope with git status (uncommitted files from a parallel work stream are easily swept in by whole-file commits).

### MoonBit native GUI stack G1 (paint contract) · toolchain syntax forms and buffer choice

Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 + X11 + XFCE, moon 0.1.20260920 / moonc v0.10.14. Adds `render` (pure MoonBit, zero FFI).

- **Pitfall**: `pub method name(self : T, ...)` fails to parse — `method` is a reserved keyword (Warning 0035 says so). **Fix**: always write `pub fn T::name(self : T, ...)`.
- **Pitfall**: `match expr with { }` reports `unexpected token with` (`match ... with {` appears 0 times in the existing repo code). **Fix**: write `match expr { }`; note `with` stays legal in **record update** `{ s with tx: 1.0 }` — the two constructs differ.
- **Pitfall**: `Bytes` is **read-only** (no `op_set`), and this version has **no** `ByteArray` type (`The type/trait ByteArray is not found`). **Fix**: mutable byte buffers use `FixedArray[Byte]` (already used by `yue/png_rgba.mbt:12-19`), and in-place writes need no `mut` binding. The pixel bitmap field is therefore `FixedArray[Byte]`; G2/G3 take its data address when handing off to Cairo/X11.
- **Pitfall**: `self.field[i] = v` (index assignment through a field) promotes the whole method to requiring `T &mut`, forcing `mut p` at every call site — unacceptable for a painter meant to serve ~10k lines of existing component call sites. **Fix**: copy the handle before writing pixels (`let d = self.data; d[i] = v`); state rebinding (`self.state = {...}`) likewise requires mut, so the mutable fields move onto the **inner** `PainterState`'s `mut` fields while the outer `state` field is never rebound (same shape as `yue/signals.mbt:247`'s `self.node.dirty = false`), keeping `p.fill_rect(..)` usable on an immutable handle.
- **Pitfall**: structs are reference-semantics, so `save()` pushing `self.state` onto the stack means `restore()` gets the same object back and nothing reverts. **Fix**: push a field-by-field snapshot (`snapshot`) and write field by field on pop (`load_state`); covered by a unit test asserting the two pixel sets separately after translate + restore.
- **Pitfall**: named construction `Color { r: ... }` fails to parse. **Fix**: write bare `{ r: .., g: .. }` with the type from context (see `yue/view.mbt:513-521`).
- **Pitfall**: a test-only dependency across `moon.work` members declared only in `moon.pkg.json`'s `wbtest.import` reports `Package ... not found`, and the entry's `alias` field is silently ignored (the default alias is the last path segment, hence `@src` in bench). **Fix / trade-off**: to let `render`'s tests use yoga-mbt, the module dependency would have to be declared in the root `moon.mod`, changing the published dependency graph; this batch leaves it alone, and the "layout tree → pixels" positioning assertions move to the batches that actually wire yoga (G2/G7).
- **Convention fork (recorded, pending a call)**: 8-digit hex is parsed on this stack as CSS `#RRGGBBAA` (alpha last), while libyue's `Color` convention is `#AARRGGBB` (stated in the parse_hex comment of `yue/color.mbt`; mixing them shows up as colour drift, not an opacity change). The new stack does not follow libyue's convention.
- **Pitfall (toolchain side effect, do not repeat)**: repo-wide `moon fmt` on this version rewrites ~80 files unrelated to this batch (the repo is not fmt-clean) and **migrates** `moon.pkg.json` into `moon.pkg` — where the new DSL does not know `warn_list` (see `modules/yoga-mbt/HANDOFF.md` §6.11), so `yoga-mbt/src`'s `warn_list: -6` gets silently moved out. **Fix**: run `moon fmt` only on this batch's new files, then check `git status` and revert anything else with `git checkout -- <explicit paths>`.

- **Verification**: `moon check` zero warnings + repo-wide `moon test` 748/748 (8 new pixel-level assertions in `render`: half-open interval coverage, source-over blending, translate+restore, clip only tightens, one inner stroke ring, a narrow rect fills whole, the 100/3 split shares edges without seams, illegal hex and a zero-size bitmap leave things unchanged).

### MoonBit native GUI stack G2 (GTK3 window layer) · five measured pitfalls in the loop pump and present path

Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 + X11 + XFCE, moon 0.1.20260920 / moonc v0.10.14, GTK3 3.24.x. Adds `win` (GTK3 backend) and `examples/native-window`.

- **Pitfall ① (window never paints, frames=0)**: after `gtk_widget_show_all` the GDK map request still sits in the output buffer, the X server never sees the map, and poll waits for an event that will never come. **Fix**: `gdk_display_flush(...)` after show plus one round of `gtk_main_iteration_do(FALSE)` (do not use the deprecated `gdk_flush`).
- **Pitfall ② (busy poll saturating CPU, dt=0)**: calling `g_main_context_wakeup` before `poll` makes GLib's internal wakeup pipe readable, poll returns immediately, and the outer loop degrades to spinning. **Fix**: never call wakeup inside the wait; cross-thread wakeup only enters via the external `wm_wakeup()` (whose effect is exactly to make the current poll return early).
- **Pitfall ③ (hardened GLib signatures)**: this machine's `g_main_context_query/check` take an extra `n_fds` argument versus online examples (query's 5th is the buffer capacity; check's 4th is n_fds, not n_ready). **Practice**: verify against `/usr/include/glib-2.0/glib/gmain.h` instead of copying documentation examples.
- **Pitfall ④ (time base for relative delays)**: `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` counts from boot — a large number (21405569ms measured here). If `Loop`'s last_now starts at 0, every timer queued before the first advance **fires immediately** — the skeleton animation ran one tick and the 5-second quit timer stopped the loop on the spot. **Fix**: `Loop::start(now_ms)` establishes the time base explicitly; unstarted loops take base 0 (covered by a unit test).
- **Pitfall ⑤ (known pitfall reproduced: moon does not relink on native static library changes)**: after editing `win/gtk_stub.c`, `moon build` reports "no work to do" and runs the old exe (same as "delete the artifacts after changing the shim"). **Fix**: delete `build/libyue_win_stub.a` and the example's `_build` output first.
- **Also recorded (convention)**: the present path copies the caller's RGBA buffer into the backend's staging before swizzling to BGRx, and **never modifies the caller's buffer in place** — the offscreen snapshot shares the same source, so an in-place swizzle would misalign the channels of the next snapshot and flip back and forth on repeated presents.
- **Verification**: `moon check gui/{core,win,render}` warning-free; `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/core` 9/9; `examples/native-window` local smoke: 52 frames, exit code 0, no teardown crash; yoga-mbt 79/79 unchanged.

### MoonBit native GUI stack G3a (Cairo rasterizer) · bitmap format and parity between the two backends

- **Format decision (key)**: the `render` Bitmap's internal layout now matches `CAIRO_FORMAT_ARGB32` exactly (little-endian B,G,R,A with **premultiplied** alpha). Payoff: Cairo can draw straight into our own buffer (`cairo_image_surface_create_for_data`), the window present is a direct copy, and the whole chain carries one format with zero conversions. Cost and countermeasure: the hand-written `Bitmap::paint` now does source-over in premultiplied space (same arithmetic as Cairo) and `Bitmap::pixel` **unpremultiplies**, so the public semantics (independent RGBA components) and all G1 assertions stay unchanged.
- **Simpler present**: `wm_present` drops the RGBA→BGRx swizzle and the staging copy, building an ARGB32 surface over the caller's buffer directly (held by `#borrow` during the session, so the buffer cannot move).
- **`stroke_rect` has one meaning on both sides**: Cairo's `stroke` is **centered**, which contradicts the layout layer's border-box convention, so the C side reproduces inset semantics with four inner band fills; when the UI needs Cairo's centered stroke, open a separate method — do not change this contract.
- **Invariant (under test)**: the same rect and colour (including alpha) rendered through the pure-MoonBit rect painter and through Cairo are **pixel-for-pixel identical** (including `#00000080` over white = 127,127,127,255); a diagonal fill produces intermediate alpha, proving the anti-aliased path is actually used.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/render` 14/14 (6 new Cairo assertions: pixel parity, triangle fill, antialiased intermediate alpha, clip+translate, inner-stroke semantics on both sides, translucent blend parity); `moon check gui/{core,win,render}` warning-free; `examples/native-window` smoke 52 frames, exit code 0 (the demo now draws a Cairo circle and bezier arc, running the whole chain end to end).

### MoonBit native GUI stack G3b (Pango text layer) · FFI out parameters and cross-package field visibility

- **Pitfall (SIGSEGV, no test output)**: using `Array[Int]` as a C out-array (C writes `out[0..2]` through an `int32_t *out`) segfaults — MoonBit hands C the array **object**, so writing `out[0]` corrupts its length header and everything touching that array afterwards dies. The repo's established form is one `Ref[Int]` per out value (`ok : Ref[Int]`, `yue/ffi.mbt:452`); switching to three `Ref[Int]` params made it 7/7. **Rule**: to return several values from C, use several `Ref[Int]` — never borrow an `Array[Int]` pointer.
- **Pitfall**: constructing or reading struct fields across packages requires `pub(all) struct` (the `RectF` shape in `yue/geometry.mbt:20`); plain `pub struct` reports `Cannot create values of the read-only type`. Same story as `pub(all) enum`.
- **Pitfall**: parameters with default values must be labelled (`family? : String = ""`); `family : String = ""` errors with "Only labelled arguments can have default value".
