- **Conventions**: font size takes absolute size in **logical pixels** (`pango_font_description_set_absolute_size(desc, px * PANGO_SCALE)`, not points); `baseline` is the first baseline measured from the top of the layout box, matching yoga-mbt's `set_baseline` definition so wiring needs no conversion; ellipsize/wrap semantics follow the teacher's `attributed_text_gtk.cc:82/128-132`.
- **Test philosophy**: no exact pixel widths/heights (they follow the machine's font configuration — the G0 probe's "14px line height 17px" is this machine's number); assert monotonicity (longer text wider, bigger font taller), constraint behaviour (`max_width` clamps the width, wrapping grows the height) and "pixels really landed" counts instead, so another machine cannot produce a false red.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/text` 7/7; `moon check gui/{core,win,render,text}` warning-free; `examples/native-window` smoke 52 frames, exit code 0 (mixed CJK/Latin text drawn in the window); repo-wide red unchanged at 290 errors.

### MoonBit native GUI stack G3b addendum · line-height definition settled and "the test executable does not relink"

- **Definition settled**: `line_height` takes the **font metrics' ascent+descent** (`pango_context_get_metrics`), and `line_ascent` takes the ascent (= first baseline). Never derive line height from a sample string's box height — that turns "does the text have a descender" into a line-height difference, and layout box heights would jitter with content.
- **Reconciliation with the G0 probe**: the probe's recorded "14px measured line height 17" was actually the **first baseline** (this layer's `line_ascent(14) = 17` matches it); this layer's `line_height(14) = 22` (ascent+descent). Both numbers are right, the label was wrong; G5 should size text boxes from the 22 path.
- **Pitfall**: `PangoFontMetrics` is not a GObject — it must be released with `pango_font_metrics_unref`; misusing `g_object_unref` SIGSEGVs outright (and crashes inside the test driver with no test output at all, easy to misread as an FFI parameter problem).
- **Pitfall (a new face of a known one)**: after changing a native static library, `moon test` executables are **not relinked either** — previously recorded only for `moon build` exes, reproduced here under `_build/native/debug/test/<pkg>`: after fixing the SIGSEGV the tests still crashed, because they ran the old linked artifact. To diagnose, first reproduce with a plain main target (a fresh target is always newly linked): consistently "main fine, test crashes" points at a stale artifact; the fix deletes `_build/native/debug/test/<pkg>` along with the library.
- **Verification**: after removing the artifacts, `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/text` 7/7; `moon check gui/{core,win,render,text}` warning-free; render 14/14, core 9/9, yoga-mbt 79/79 unchanged.

### MoonBit native GUI stack G4a (editor kernel and key codes) · kernel semantics and toolchain syntax

- **Kernel semantics settled**: the single authority for text state lives in `input`; the input method is just one of its clients (no second copy of the text state as in the "channel holds the text" design). All coordinates are **UTF-8 byte indices**, and caret/anchor only land on code-point boundaries (back off over continuation bytes 0xC0..0xBF), same source as the G0 probe; switching to code-point indices would break Pango width measurement and IME preedit offsets at once. `get_text_in_range` aligns **start backwards, end forwards** — better to include one extra code point than return half a character. The kernel never touches the system clipboard: `cut/copy` return text and `paste_text` accepts text, so the whole logic is testable without a display. `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` return "not consumed" for the upper focus stack; printable keys are landed by `keysym_to_text` (Latin-1 and UCS keysym paths), the remaining functional keys are left to G5's IME channel.
- **Pitfalls (this toolchain's syntax, all measured)**: ① the implicit-method form `fn helper(self : Editor, ..)` is **not recognized** (unbound) — private helpers also need `fn Editor::helper(self : Editor, ..)`; ② top-level `pub name : Int = v` fails to parse, use `pub const NAME : Int = v` (uppercase); ③ `move` is a reserved keyword (Warning 0035) — the method is named `move_caret`; ④ `Int.to_char()` returns **`Char?`**, and interpolating it warns "Option does not have a meaningful string representation" — match out the Char first; ⑤ variants of `pub enum X derive(Eq, Show) { A B }` cannot be constructed elsewhere; payload-less enums need `pub(all) enum`, and this batch went further and replaced the two-case enum (Consumed/NotConsumed) with a plain `Bool` to shed one syntactic layer; ⑥ `} else match ... {` is illegal — a match used as a branch body must be wrapped in `{ }`.
- **Pitfall (out of bounds)**: `floor_boundary` allows k == buffer length (the end is a legal boundary), so the loop must short-circuit on `k < n` before indexing, otherwise `Array::at` panics (SIGABRT observed).
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/input` 10/10 (CJK-mixed round trip, backspace deletes a whole character with no residue, selection replacement, word jumping in three directions, shift extend/collapse, copy leaves state untouched while cut deletes, undo/redo round trip, handle_key routing and Tab's attribution, Ctrl+A/Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Left, range alignment); `moon check gui/{core,input}` warning-free; render 14/14, text 7/7, yoga-mbt 79/79 unchanged.

### MoonBit native GUI stack G4b (key/pointer events and focus wiring) · four GTK-side rules

- **Pitfall**: `gdk_keyval_to_lower(ev->keyval)` erases the shift case — X11 keyvals **already encode shift** ('a' and 'A' are different keysyms), so the kernel's `keysym_to_text` yields the correct character when the raw keyval is kept. Keep the original keyval in the event; do not lowercase.
- **Pitfall**: modifier bits cannot pass through GDK's raw values (Shift=1, Control=4, Mod1=8, Mod2=64, Meta=16); they must be remapped explicitly onto this stack's `MOD_SHIFT=1 / MOD_CTRL=2 / MOD_ALT=4 / MOD_META=8`, otherwise every `Ctrl+Left` / `Shift+Tab` combination misfires.
- **Prerequisites for receiving keys**: `gtk_widget_set_can_focus(area, TRUE)` + `gtk_widget_add_events(area, GDK_KEY_PRESS_MASK | ... | GDK_SCROLL_MASK)`, plus `gtk_widget_grab_focus` after `show_all`; missing any one step leaves a live window that reports **not a single key event** — the same class as G2's "no flush, waiting on an event that never arrives": the symptom is silence, not an error.
- **Conventions**: the event queue is a 64-slot FIFO per window, and when full it **drops the new event rather than overwriting** (losing one event is better than corrupting the order); events are read as "`wm_take_event` returns the code, then `wm_ev_*` reads the last taken one" instead of many out parameters — MoonBit cannot hand C a writable array (see the G3b SIGSEGV entry).
- **The focus stack lives on the MoonBit side**: `core/focus.mbt` owns only order and wrap-around (Tab from last to first, Shift+Tab from first to last, unregistering the focused item hands focus to its successor); the platform exposes one action, `Window::request_focus`. Logical focus mirrors libyue's `FocusManager` (containers hold no system focus).
- **Caret placement rule**: click positioning measures prefix widths code point by code point and takes the right-most boundary at or before the click; `Editor::boundary_after` was promoted from private to public so upper layers advance the same way.
- **Verification**: five packages `moon check` warning-free; tests core 14/14, input 10/10, render 14/14, text 7/7, yoga-mbt 79/79; `examples/native-window` local smoke: 49 frames, exit code 0, both boxes' text state intact. **Real-machine items await the collaborator**: typing letters/digits, backspace and arrows, Tab/Shift+Tab wrapping between the two boxes, click-to-place caret, 500ms caret blink, CJK punctuation and compose keys (IME belongs to G5).

### MoonBit native GUI stack G0 · real-hardware evidence: `im_focus` is the precondition for the pure channel working; the preedit gap was in how the probe hooks it

Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 + X11 + XFCE, `GTK_IM_MODULE=fcitx` (fcitx5). Executed by the collaborator on real hardware (AGENTS rule 6).

- **Symptom**: in probe mode B every keystroke landed as an immediate commit and preedit stayed 0 — the IME looked like it never took over. fcitx5 was fine; `GtkIMMulticontext` falls back to the built-in `GtkIMContextSimple` (Latin-1 only, no compose string or candidates) when the context is **not activated**.
- **Root cause**: the probe only called `gtk_im_context_set_client_window`, which makes the context usable, but **never called `gtk_im_context_focus_in`**, so it stayed inactive and `filter_keypress` consumed nothing.
- **Fix**: `gtk_im_context_focus_in(pr.im)` at realize, and sync in/out on the toplevel's focus-in/out events (losing focus must call `focus_out`, otherwise the IM side keeps an unfinished composition — checklist item 5). With this added, **the Chinese commit path works on real hardware**.
- **Closed out (added the same day)**: inline preedit achieved; the pure channel's **four conditions** are all met — ① `focus_in`/`focus_out` synced with focus; ② key handling installed on the **focused widget** (window-level wiring gets both the ordering and the consumption wrong — exactly the difference from `GtkEntry` behaviour); ③ `gtk_im_context_set_surrounding` every tick (committed text only, cursor in UTF-8 bytes); ④ `use_preedit=TRUE` — its meaning is "use the preedit string for inline feedback", not "the IM draws it itself"; reading it backwards cost two false negatives.
- **Another real-hardware pitfall, unrelated to the IM**: the composition string may be assembled in **exactly one place**. The probe used to splice the preedit into the display string on the MoonBit side and splice it again while drawing in C, so the same text appeared twice; the fix moves splicing and the underline into the draw side (body text unlined, composition underlined, matching `GtkEntry`), with MoonBit pushing committed text only.
- **One misdiagnosis to record**: a "frontend version mismatch" suspicion was refuted by the mode-C control (a real `GtkEntry` previews fine in the same environment) — run a reference implementation against real-hardware symptoms before attributing causes.
- **ibus not installed**: the two ibus rounds of the checklist are marked "no ibus daemon in this environment, untested".
- **Verification method**: `moon build experiment/ime_probe` + both modes smoke to exit code 0 (assistant side); real hardware (fcitx5) evidenced by the collaborator: one inline underlined composition, `[preedit] changed` in the stream, `[commit] 中文` intact, the candidate window hugging the end of the composition string.

### MoonBit native GUI stack G4 · first root cause behind the real-hardware report "cannot type / click, Tab does not switch focus": event code 4 unmapped

- **Symptom** (collaborator's real hardware): the self-drawn box accepted no characters, clicks did not move focus, Tab/Shift+Tab did nothing — while window animation and repaint were normal.
- **Root cause**: the backend's `wm_event` uses return value **4** to mean "an input event is pending", but the MoonBit-side `Window::poll_event` mapping only covered 1/2/3, so 4 fell into the `_ => NoEvent` arm — the main loop therefore believed "no events" and ended the drain immediately, and `take_input` was never called. Rendering runs on timers, so animation kept moving; the symptom was exactly "only input is dead" with **no error anywhere**.
- **Lesson (rule level)**: event codes are an implicit contract between the two ends — a new event type must change both the C return value and the MoonBit mapping, and **the default arm must not swallow unknown codes**; from now on, when adding an event type, print (or assert on) unrecognized codes first instead of letting `_ =>` absorb them silently.
- **Still open at the time**: after fixing the mapping, the example's 5-second auto-exit did not fire (the process sat at 0% CPU blocked in the wait). The hypothesis that `Loop::advance` starves later timers by "breaking on the head alone" was ruled out — a new headless case, "a self-rescheduling short-period tick must not starve a longer-period timer", passes (core 15/15). The next step injects keys and clicks into the example window with `xdotool` for objective verification (this path works on this host and can replace eyes).
- **Verification**: `moon check win` warning-free; the five-package tests core 15/15, input 10/10, render 14/14, text 7/7 all green.

### MoonBit native GUI stack G4 · the two real causes of "not a single character can be typed": key handler on the wrong layer, and NumLock read as Meta

Symptom: after G4 landed, the self-drawn box accepted no characters at all, while Tab seemed to "sort of move" (focus really was switching), window animation and repaint were normal, and nothing logged an error. Objective verification by injecting `xdotool key` into the example window (this host, not relying on eyes), printing `code/keysym/mods/focus/len` per event, pinned two causes:

- **(1) Key handling was hooked to the toplevel window instead of the focused widget**: the original `g_signal_connect(w->window, "key-press-event", ...)`. The G0 probe (`ec2849d`) had already settled the hook shape on real hardware: key handling belongs on the **focused widget**, because window-level wiring gets both the ordering and "can it truly eat the event after consumption" wrong (fatal once an IME is involved). Now connected on `w->area` (the drawing area), the same shape as GtkEntry.
- **(2) `GDK_MOD2_MASK` was being treated as Meta — fatal and very easy to misjudge**. `wm_mods()` set MOD_META whenever `state & (GDK_META_MASK | GDK_MOD2_MASK)` matched, but MOD2 on X11 **is NumLock**, which is on on any normal desktop, so **every** key event arrived with mods=8; the kernel's `handle_key` sees alt/meta nonzero, classifies it as a chord, and inserts nothing, silently dropping every printable key. Fix: Meta comes only from `GDK_META_MASK | GDK_SUPER_MASK`; lock bits like NumLock/CapsLock never enter this stack's modifier set.
- **Localization technique worth reusing**: "did the event reach C" — `fprintf(stderr, "[c] key ...")` in the C callback; "where did it die after MoonBit" — print `code/keysym/mods/focus/editor byte-count` at the dispatch point. This time a single `mods=8` field pinned cause (2); reasoning from behaviour alone kept pointing at "events never arrived".
- **One disproved hypothesis, recorded**: after fixing the mapping the example briefly did not auto-exit, and I first suspected `Loop::advance` starving later timers by "breaking once the head is not due". Written as a headless case it **passes** (core 15/15), so the guess was dropped; the actual stall was the draw-vs-GdkWindow lifetime issue (see the G2/G4 timing entry) compounded with too short a wait in my own test loop — not the scheduler.
- **Objective verification**: injecting `a b c Tab d e f` yields `NATIVE-WINDOW-OK ... a='helloabc' b='第二个框def'` — the first three keys into the first box, Tab moves focus, the last three into the second box, with `mods=0`. Five packages `moon check` warning-free; core 15/15, input 10/10, render 14/14, text 7/7, yoga-mbt 79/79; repo-wide red still 290 errors. **Still needs eyes**: click-to-place caret and the 500ms blink appearance (xdotool can inject a click but cannot see the drawn caret).

### MoonBit native GUI stack G5a (Linux pure-channel IME) · the four probe conditions landing in win

The recipe came from the G0 probe (`ec2849d`, four conditions) and this batch implements it into the new stack's own window layer: `win` creates a `GtkIMMulticontext` (`use_preedit=TRUE`), runs `filter_keypress` first on every key (consumed ⇒ eaten, never forwarded to the kernel), reads the commit text and composition string back to MoonBit as "take one + read field by field", and feeds surrounding text plus the caret rectangle every tick; `input` gains `set_preedit`/`preedit_text` (the composition is display-only, **never merged into the text state** — there is still exactly one copy of the text); the example draws the composition after the committed text with an underline and adds the composition width to the candidate-window rectangle.

- **Pitfall 1 (pinyin goes into the text verbatim, the IM looks dead)**: calling `set_client_window` before `show` — the drawing area is not realized yet, `gtk_widget_get_window` returns NULL, the multicontext attaches to no IM module, and `filter_keypress` never consumes. It **must run in the `realize` signal** (same as the probe), paired with `focus-in/out-event` for `focus_in`/`focus_out`.
- **Pitfall 2 (core dump: `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`)**: the UTF-8 string delivered by the `commit` signal is owned by GTK and freed after the handler returns; calling `g_free(text)` there is a double free. The probe's handler indeed does not free either.
- **Pitfall 3 (CJK never appears)**: calling `gtk_im_context_reset` alongside the per-tick surrounding feed **breaks the composition** — reset means "discard the current composition". Feed only `gtk_im_context_set_surrounding(im, text, len, caret_bytes)` (the four-argument legacy call, same as the probe; do not take the newer SelectionData-based API).
- **Pitfall 4**: the `preedit-changed` signal signature is `(GtkIMContext*, gpointer)`; the string must come from `gtk_im_context_get_preedit_string(ctx, &str, &attrs, &caret)` (connecting as `(ctx, text, data)` hands you a bogus pointer); `caret` is a **byte** offset inside the composition, the same unit as this stack's UTF-8 byte caret.
- **Toolchain addenda**: `FixedArray[Byte]` → `String` goes through `@utf8.decode_lossy(FixedArray::unsafe_reinterpret_as_bytes(buf))` (neither `@utf8.decode_utf8` nor `buf.to_bytes()` exists in this version); `Double → Int` is `x.floor().to_int()` (no `Int.floor_of_double`, no `+.` operator, and a **line-continuation operator must sit at the end of the previous line**).
- **Objective verification** (`xdotool` injection, `GTK_IM_MODULE=fcitx`): typing `nihao` + space yields the exit line `a='hello你哈哦'` — no pinyin-letter residue, and `seen=6` counts only the unconsumed keys, so filtering and "consume-and-eat" both behave as intended; the process exits cleanly. Five packages `moon check` warning-free; core 15/15, input 10/10, render 14/14, text 7/7, yoga-mbt 79/79; repo-wide red still 290 errors.
- **Pending eyes / follow-ups**: the look of the preedit underline and whether the candidate window hugs the end of the composition (this machine can only prove the rectangle was pushed), the ibus set (probe-side conclusion: no inline preview under ibus is suspected to be a libpinyin display-style setting, unrelated to this layer — recorded separately), Windows `ImmAssociateContext` and macOS.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Painter contract completion, first batch (facade + blend modes + gradients)

- **Facade decision**: `Painter` is promoted from a pure-rectangle subset to a **full contract facade**. `new(bitmap)` opens a Cairo session; rectangles, paths, transforms, clipping, blending and gradients all go through Cairo. When Cairo is unavailable — a non-Linux stub implementation, or all 16 session slots exhausted — it falls back to the pure-rectangle implementation, where path calls are no-ops. Rectangle drawing is **bit-for-bit identical on both paths**: a new matrix-equivalence case runs rounding, inner stroke, clip intersection, translation and translucent overpaint once per path and compares.
- **Session discipline**: there are 16 Cairo session slots (`CR_MAX`); one session per frame requires `Painter::end()` to reclaim it. A leak makes later Painters silently degrade to the stub implementation. Added a reclamation case that opens and closes 20 Painters while still holding sessions. Nine existing tests never reclaimed, leaking 14 sessions in total; only after adding `end()` did headroom return to the safe zone.
- **Blend modes**: the 25 `BlendMode` values map **1:1** onto Cairo operators — the first 16 are W3C blending, the last 9 Porter-Duff. A standalone C probe confirmed on this machine, cairo 1.18 with pixman, that **all 25 operators really take effect**, including the pigment and HSL families, so no custom blending algorithm is needed. Translucent sources follow the W3C formula, `(1-α)·dst + α·Blend(dst,src)`; measured 0.5 α multiply equals `0.5·dst + 0.5·dst×src`. On a transparent base, Multiply degrades to the source color. The 25-mode measurement table is committed as assertion lines: blend and HSL rows carry a ±2 tolerance against cross-pixman scaling differences, Porter-Duff rows use exact values.
- **Pitfall — rounding must happen in device space**: with rounding done in **user space**, device coordinates after a CTM translation such as `translate(1.3, 0.6)` land on fractional pixels, so Cairo anti-aliases a grey edge and diverges from the pure implementation. The facade-vs-degrade matrix-equivalence case went red first and green on exactly this fix. The fix: convert with `cairo_user_to_device`, round with `floor(v + 0.5)` in **device space**, then temporarily switch to the identity matrix and fill an integer rectangle. When the matrix contains rotation or shear, that is off-diagonal non-zero, no rounding is applied and anti-aliasing handles it as-is.
- **Pitfall — the clip region is graphics state**: a temporary identity matrix plus `cairo_rectangle` plus `cairo_clip` must **not** be wrapped in `cairo_save`/`cairo_restore`. Clipping belongs to the saved state, so `restore` reverts the clip just set. Restore manually with `cairo_get_matrix`/`cairo_set_matrix`. The final clip is stored in device space, so later CTM changes do not affect it.
- **Pitfall — different default line widths**: a Cairo session defaults to **2.0** while the contract defaults to **1.0**. If `Painter::new` does not sync them, strokes that never call `set_line_width`, such as the inner band of `stroke_rect`, come out one step thicker. The "stroke an inner ring" case located it.
- **Pitfall — a function that does not exist**: `cairo_pattern_get_status` does not exist; the correct name is `cairo_pattern_status`. The typo surfaces at **link time** as undefined reference rather than at compile time.
- **Pitfall — build artifact path capitalization, supplement to the G3b entry**: this repository's test artifacts live under `_build/native/debug/test/NoahLiu` with a **capital first letter**. Deleting the lowercase path silently does nothing and tests keep running the old binary. Earlier in this batch a 20-pixel difference survived the device-space rounding fix; it was a stale artifact. The correct path to delete after changing the native library: `_build/native/debug/test/NoahLiu/native-gui/<pkg>`.
- **Gradients**: `Gradient::linear`/`radial` plus `add_stop`. Offsets clamp to [0,1], invalid hex is ignored, a gradient with no stops is ignored as a whole, and `set_fill_color` overrides a gradient. Implementation is a one-shot pattern: create, add stops one by one, set as source, release the handle. Measured semantics: linear samples at pixel centers, `(x+0.5)/axis_length`; beyond the endpoints, pad reproduces the end color. Radial is concentric and symmetric across the four corners.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/render` 25/25 — 11 new: Porter-Duff exact values, 25-mode measurement table, translucent formula, transparent-base degradation, mode independent of color-setting order, linear gradient sampling and pad, radial symmetry, empty gradient ignored plus solid override, facade path with anti-aliasing, save/restore reverting transform and style together, session slot reclamation. Five packages `moon check` zero warnings, core 15/15, input 10/10, text 7/7, yoga-mbt 80/80. `examples/native-window` smoke: 49 frames, exit code 0 — the example now goes through the facade and uses a gradient glow, a multiply square and a path circle. Repo-wide still 290 errors / 68 warnings, no increase.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Painter second batch (offscreen Canvas and images) · sampling domain and archive rebuild

- **Image decoding**: via **GdkPixbuf**, an existing GTK3 dependency, so no new runtime dependency; `GdkPixbufLoader` sniffs the format from content. Pixels convert to this stack's `Bitmap` layout: ARGB32 premultiplied, little-endian B,G,R,A. Premultiplication rounding matches `Bitmap::paint`, `(c*a+127)/255`, so encode → decode → re-encode is byte-stable; translucent colors such as `#12345680` round-trip exactly. The decoder takes only the **first static frame**. The old chain's `Image` was a `GdkPixbufAnimation`, so GIFs animated; animation is a known gap and is not pretended to be supported.
- **Sizing follows the teacher**: `get_width`/`get_height` return the **logical size**, pixels divided by scale; `get_scale_factor` returns the recorded ratio. This matches libyue `image_gtk.cc:75-77`, `ScaleSize(.., 1.f / scale_factor_)`.
- **Pitfall — the blit sampling domain must stay inside the source sub-rectangle**: building a pattern from the **whole source bitmap** and only writing the source rectangle into the pattern matrix makes bilinear sampling pull colors from **outside** the sub-rectangle, so sprite sheets and icon atlases bleed. In the test, "take the top-left quadrant and tile it at 4x4" failed first: the right edge sampled the neighbouring green block. The fix: create a **sub-surface** with `cairo_surface_create_for_rectangle(s, sx, sy, ssw, ssh)`, so the sampling space moves with the sub-rectangle origin, then add `PAD` extension so edges do not open into transparent seams.
- **Pitfall — `ar rcs` appends renamed members**: after splitting the source into `cairo_stub.c` plus `image_stub.c`, the stale `librender_cairo_stub.o` left in the old archive entered the library **together with** the new object, producing `multiple definition` at link time. prebuild's `compile_stub` now deletes the old archive before `ar rcs`, and the cache acceptance check is "any source updated rebuilds everything" instead of the previous single-source mtime comparison.
- **Asset move fallout**: the PNG encoder moved from the root package `yue/png_rgba.mbt` into `render/png.mbt`. The public entry is renamed `png_encode_rgba`; internal `pngr_*` names stay. Six existing cases moved with it. The root package's private helper `utf8_bytes` does not exist in the new package, so it becomes `@utf8.encode` plus `moonbitlang/core/encoding/utf8` in `moon.pkg`. After the move, errors dropped from 290 to **287** — one fewer file and one fewer test in the root package.
- **File writing**: `Canvas`/`Image` `write_to_file` currently supports only "png". Writing goes through the C-side `fsw_write_file` fallback, a temporary channel before the system layer lands; paths are taken as UTF-8 bytes.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/render` 40/40 — 9 new: PNG round-trip opaque/translucent, empty-image semantics and no pixels landing on an empty image, logical size following scale, `resize` upscaling keeping a solid color, `draw_canvas` 2x across four quadrants, `draw_canvas_from_rect` sub-rectangle without bleeding, blit respecting multiply blend, PNG written then read back pixel by pixel; six PNG encoder cases arrived with the move. Five packages `moon check` zero warnings, core 15/15, input 10/10, text 7/7, yoga-mbt 80/80. `examples/native-window` smoke: 49 frames, exit code 0 — adds an offscreen canvas sprite upscaled 4x. Repo-wide **287 errors / 68 warnings**, down from 290, no increase.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Icon drawing port (803 thousandths-fixed-point paths)

- **Scope and fidelity**: lines 1-4197 of master's `icons/icons.mbt` moved wholesale into the new `icons` package: the 803-variant `IconKind`, the `path_num`/`fill_icon_path` interpreter, `draw_icon`, the `icon_path_data` block, and the `kind_index`/`all_icons`/`icon_name` tables. Only two kinds of change: the type reference `@yue.Painter → @render.Painter` and the header note. The **data block matches the original line for line** — `diff` reports only the 7 header lines and 2 type-reference lines. The declarative wrappers `icon`/`icon_button_t` depend on the declarative layer and are left to the component batch, G7.
- **Semantics copied, not reinvented**: coordinates are fixed-point integers of normalized values ×1000; command set M/L/C/Z; each sub-path closes M…Z; one `fill` for the whole path, iconfont outline style; safe margin 0.88, `v × s × 0.88 / 1000 + center`; a single command is read and dispatched immediately with no caching, parsing takes microseconds.
- **Test coverage**: ① the three tables — inventory, names, path data — correspond one-to-one. A count array with every cell exactly 1 replaces a hash set, avoiding a container dependency; name uniqueness uses squared comparison, sufficient at 803 items. ② **Full scan** of the path-string character set: only M/L/C/Z, digits, `-`, `,`, with a leading M and a trailing Z. ③ `draw_icon` lands pixels, and the center of the painted-pixel bounding box stays within ±2px — this checks centering, not a specific shape. ④ **Full scan** of all 803 icons at 24px with no empty image, parsing plus rasterization, finishing inside 0.7s.
- **Environment note, to avoid misdiagnosis**: the `seen` counter on the example's exit line includes **pointer motion** — motion with code 4 also enters the input queue. During a smoke run with the mouse resting on the window, `seen` is non-zero while the text does not change. That is expected, not stray keystrokes.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/icons` 4/4; `moon check icons` zero warnings; `examples/native-window` smoke: 49 frames, exit code 0 — the example adds a row of five vector icons.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Font and rich-text subsystem (Font / TextFormat / AttributedText)

- **Surface**: `Font` — family name, logical pixel size, 9 weight levels, italic; the weight values are CSS 100..900, passed straight to Pango's `PangoWeight` — plus `TextAlign`/`TextFormat`/`TextAttributes`/`SizeF`/`AttributedText`. This batch covers the **whole-run attribute** surface only: font, color, alignment, wrapping, ellipsis, `get_bounds_for`, `set_text`/`get_text`/`clear`. Range attributes, `set_font_for`/`set_color_for`, need ranges attached to a Pango attribute list and are left to the next batch.
- **Draw entry points sit in `text` at the package boundary**: `draw_in_box`/`draw_font`, not a `Painter::draw_text` method. MoonBit cannot add methods to a foreign type, and render must not depend on text in reverse. When the component layer wires up, call sites change from the old contract's `p.draw_text(..)` to `@text.draw_in_box(p.bitmap, ..)`, a fixed-point rewrite under G7.
- **Pitfall, semantic level, caught by probe**: `wrap=false` previously **had no effect at all**. Pango wraps with the default `WRAP_WORD` as soon as `pango_layout_set_width` is set. Measured: 120px wide without a wrap flag, long text still folded into 4 lines at 88px. The fix: pass the width to Pango only when wrapping or ellipsis is requested; a single line without ellipsis draws at natural width and may overflow the box, and in-box alignment is computed locally, using the same code path as vertical alignment. This also corrects the older documentation claim that "long text in a fixed-height line overflows the line bounds" — it was wrapping.
- **Pitfall — an FFI prototype changes in three places together**: adding weight/italic to `pt_font_line_height` touched only the MoonBit extern and the portable stub; the **real implementation**, in the Pango branch of `text/stub.c`, still took 4 arguments. The extra argument landed in the `out_h` pointer slot under the calling convention. The symptom was not a crash but a line-height assertion going false for no visible reason. Rule: an FFI signature change means moon extern plus real implementation plus stub branch, all three in one batch.
- **Pitfall — derived traits are a deprecated path in this toolchain**: `pub(all) enum X { .. } derive(Eq)` triggers the `implicit_impl_as_method` deprecation warning, because `equal`/`not_equal` are implicitly promoted to ordinary methods. Writing `derive(Eq)` after the enum name is a hard compile error; the correct position is after `}`. To hold the zero-warning gate, this batch derives no traits; tests compare enums through a package-local id mapping, `align_id`/`weight_value`.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/text` 14/14 — 7 new: `wrap=false` single-line natural width against the `wrap=true` height, ellipsis width clamped, bold not narrower than regular, in-box horizontal/vertical alignment landing points and centering, `AttributedText` attribute surface and bounding box, `new_with`/`format` round-trip. `moon check text` zero warnings. `examples/native-window` smoke: 49 frames, exit code 0 — the example adds a centered bold title, exercising Font/TextAlign/AttributedText.

### yoga-mbt · Corpus-derived item closed: child flex-basis shadowed by container properties (Chrome cross-check)

- **Origin**: corpus item `93078300`, an open item — explicit `flex-basis: 0` plus `min-height: 0` under an auto-height column container gave 60 from the engine, where CSS derivation says 0.
- **Chrome cross-check technique, reusable**: local HTML plus the browser MCP's `getBoundingClientRect()` to read real heights; the spec text is extracted from the drafts.csswg.org page DOM via `document.querySelector('#anchor')`, which is more reliable than WebFetch — that only returns the table of contents.
- **Conclusion 1, Blink's reading**: auto main-axis size = **the sum of each item's hypothetical main-axis size**, where the flex base is clamped by min/max; growth does not participate at all. Evidence rows: `basis 100 / content 300 / grow 1` → **100**. The Ideal algorithm in spec §9.9.1 would scale by the flex factor and the Web-compatible path would take the max-content contribution, 300; neither matches, so the implementation follows Blink. `basis 0 + min 0` → 0; `basis 0 + min:auto` → 60, the content floor; `basis auto + max-height 30` → 30; `basis 40%` with an indefinite container main axis and no reference → 60, falling back to content.
- **Conclusion 2, root cause, one typo**: when building a flex item, the basis was read from the **container's** `s.flex_basis` instead of `c.style.flex_basis`. Child flex-basis therefore never took effect anywhere in the layout chain, which is why any basis setting produced the same result. The container's auto main-axis size also ignores child basis; it now uses a new `main_contribution`: resolve the basis first and clamp by the min/max it determines, falling back to intrinsic size for auto or a percentage with no reference. The `min: auto` content floor applies only in §4.5 flex resolution, not again in container sizing — otherwise every container measure would recompute intrinsic size.
- **Verification**: the 7-row Chrome matrix, rows A/C/D/F/G/I/L, matches row by row and is committed as standing cases in `patches_regression_wbtest.mbt`. yoga-mbt 81/81, including the `display:none` corpus case and all existing assertions. Bench unchanged: 1121 nodes × 500 rounds release, 1.93s before the fix and 1.95s after, measured A/B.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Theme system, first batch (palette derivation formulas + change subscription)

- **Surface**: `Theme` with a 20-field palette, the `default_theme`/`dark_theme` presets, `theme_from_accent` using the EP theme workbench formula — accent keeps its hue, saturation floor 0.45, lightness clamped by mode: light 0.34..0.52 / dark 0.55..0.72; hover -0.09 in light and +0.08 in dark; `*_light` mixes 12%/14% white in light mode and 30%/28% panel base in dark mode; semantic colors take fixed wheel hues 142/36/4/210, borrowing the accent's saturation when it is ≥0.4 with lightness following the mode; neutrals do not shift with the accent — plus `theme_current`/`on_theme_change`/`off_theme_change`/`theme_apply`, 20 getters, `control_height` (32) and `entry_ctrl_height`.
- **Three deliberate omissions, differences from the old chain**: ① native control CSS push, the old `apply_native_theme_css` — every control in this stack is self-drawn and the palette is the only source at draw time, so "native look follows the system theme" does not exist here. ② `ffi_repaint_all` as a blanket repaint fallback — repaint responsibility lands on each widget's subscription path with the component batch. ③ `theme_from_system`, following system dark/light and accent, needs system integration reads and is not wired. `sub_bag_begin/end` batch unsubscribe arrives with the relink layer.
- **Color math landing point**: `theme/palette.mbt` — hex parsing, `rgb_to_hsl`, `hsl_to_rgb`, `mix_hex`, `lighten_hex`, `darken_hex`. Hex parsing reuses `@render.Color::parse`, i.e. the CSS reading with 8-digit alpha at the end; the divergence from libyue's `#AARRGGBB` is already recorded under G1. Theme strings use the 6-digit form only, so they are unaffected.
- **One measured pitfall inherited from master**: in `mix_hex(a, b, t)`, `t` is the share taken from **the former**, and the endpoints t=0/1 plus invalid input must **return the input string unchanged** without a `hex6` round-trip. `hex6` outputs lowercase hex, which would rewrite `#2D68C4` into `#2d68c4` and break comparison against the original string. Assertions are written in lowercase: `theme_from_accent("#FF0000").primary == "#ff0000"`.
- **Test orientation**: no assertion on concrete derived color values, since changing the base palette would turn everything red. Only formula invariants are asserted — a gray accent's saturation raised to the floor, a white accent's lightness clamped to the ceiling, dark mode lifting a dark accent to the floor, hover's lightness direction, semantic hues within ±1° on the wheel, the mixing direction of the light-base variants, an invalid accent falling back to the base palette. On the subscription surface: notification uses a snapshot, so a listener registered inside the callback does not join the current round; unsubscribe is idempotent; an unknown handle is a no-op; getters follow after `theme_apply`.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/theme` 7/7; `moon check theme --deny-warn` zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings; other packages and yoga-mbt untouched.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Widget host, first batch (layout tree ↔ widget tree, hit testing and event routing)

- **Landing point**: in `core`, per plan §2's package table — the loop and focus stack live in this package, the platform backend in `win`, the drawing contract in `render` — so this layer knows no platform handle at all. This is also yoga-mbt's first appearance as a dependency of a main package: `moon.mod`'s `import` gained `"NoahLiu/yoga-mbt@0.1.0"`. The module is already in the workspace, but omitting this line reports "containing module is not imported".
- **Coordinate convention, converted in one place only**: yoga's `left/top` are offsets relative to the parent's border box. `relayout`/`relayout_at` fold them into absolute window coordinates in a single post-layout pass, `collect_abs`, and write them back onto the widgets. Hit testing and the draw traversal consume absolute rectangles only; events are translated to widget-local coordinates before a handler sees them, where local (0,0) is the widget's border-box top-left. Drawing translates and clips layer by layer, so a widget's `on_draw` writes local coordinates and never clips itself.
- **Propagation rule**: from the hit widget upward along the ancestor chain, the first handler returning `true` consumes the event — one rule for pointer, wheel and key. The host stores **no parent pointers**; bubbling uses the hit path, `hit_path` or a path found by focus id, so re-mounting a subtree cannot leave a dangling parent reference.
- **Pitfall ① — a widget cannot support `==`**: `Widget` has closure fields, so `Eq` cannot be derived and `Option[Widget] == None` is a compile error reported on the `impl Eq for Option` constraint. Approach: each widget carries an auto-increment `id`; identity comparison and test assertions go through id, with a helper returning -1 when nothing is hit.
- **Pitfall ② — a hidden subtree keeps stale rectangles**: the layout engine stops recursing at `display:none`, so descendants retain their `layout_*` values from the previous round. If `collect_abs` does not skip hidden subtrees, a hidden descendant can still be hit or drawn from a stale rectangle. Fix: when a widget is invisible, zero the rectangles of the **whole subtree** before returning.
- **Pitfall ③ — `local` is a reserved word**: `let local = ...` triggers `Warning [0035] reserved_keyword`; this toolchain reserves `local` for future use, so under the zero-warning gate it must be renamed.
- **Real-window evidence — coordinate alignment is not a paper conclusion**: the example adds a 200×28 demo band of four 50×28 cells; each cell's `on_draw` paints a block and its `on_pointer` counts presses only. `xdotool mousemove --window <id> X 250` plus `click 1`, once each at window x 200/250/300/360, gives the exit line `NATIVE-WINDOW-OK band_h=1/1/1/1` — exactly one press per cell, no wrong cell and no double count — with `frames=49`, `queue=0`, exit code 0 in the same run.
- **Not in this batch, G6 remainder**: dirty-region incremental relayout plus measure/intrinsic caches persisting across layouts; the `App` host, translating `win`'s raw events into this layer's `PointerEvent`/`KeyEvent` and owning the present loop, lands with the declarative layer G7.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/core` 22/22 — 7 new: absolute rectangle folding including parent padding, hit taking the deepest and later-painted first while out-of-bounds, zero-size and hidden are not hit, pointer localization with three-level bubbling and consume-then-stop, local coordinates (12,45)→(12,15) on an offset tree, wheel bubbling to the container and not routed outside bounds, key located by focus id and bubbling with unreachable after hiding, and the draw traversal's translation and clipping — an overflowing child leaves no ink — plus hidden subtrees not drawn. `moon check gui/{core,input,render,text,win}` and the example under `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; yoga-mbt 81/81; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · `sys` package opened (JSON parser port + package-local tests)

- **Landing point**: the new stack's system-capability package is named `sys` per plan §2. The first asset is the zero-dependency JSON parser, moved wholesale from master's `yue/vscjson.mbt`. Public names `VscJson`/`vsc_json_parse`/`vsc_json_get`/`vsc_json_str`/`vsc_json_int64`/`vsc_hex_val`/`vsc_codepoint_at` are unchanged; consumers only swap the package prefix from `@yue.` to `@sys.`. The root package loses one file and the error count is unchanged, since that file was already clean.
- **Coverage added**: in the old chain this parser had **no dedicated tests** — coverage was scattered across the `vscode_history`/`browser_bookmarks` cases. Against the baseline "every new-stack package writes its own wbtest", 7 cases were added: scalars and type gates, Int64 millisecond timestamp precision, chained access on nested structures, string escapes — regular, `\u`, surrogate pairs, lone surrogate → U+FFFD, unterminated, malformed `\u`; all 9 syntax errors rejected with a loose-whitespace control; the GeoJSON point path; hex and codepoint helpers.
- **Two measured conventions found while writing the tests**: ① this toolchain's `String.unsafe_get(i)` returns a **UTF-16 code unit**, not a code point; `vsc_codepoint_at("😀", 0)` gives `(0x1F600, 2)`, which is exactly why this surrogate-merging helper exists. ② The 2^53 gate for converting an integral float to Int64 is tested on the **rounded double value**, and the literal `9007199254740993.0` itself lands on 2^53 in binary, so it passes; asserting "out of range rejected" needs magnitudes such as `1e20`.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/sys` 7/7; `moon check sys --deny-warn` zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Rich-text range attributes (`rt_*` sessions) · three measured Pango attribute facts

- **Implementation shape**: `AttributedText` stores data only — text, format, base font/color, and `Array[TextRange]`. Each measure or draw builds a session in the C-side `rt_*` slot table, `RT_MAX 16`, and calls `rt_free` immediately after use. No long-lived handle, so a MoonBit object can never be collected while C still holds a pointer. Text and font names are copied into owned memory at the entry point, since a MoonBit `Bytes` pointer is valid only for the duration of the call.
- **Range convention**: **UTF-8 byte indices** `[start, end)`, the same source as the editing kernel. libyue uses character ranges, a divergence on record. Out-of-bounds is clamped when the tree is built; a range whose start is not below its end is skipped; invalid hex never enters the table. `set_text` keeps the range table per the old semantics. The public surface adds `range_count()`, which the component layer uses to decide whether to take the rich-text path.
- **Three measured Pango-side facts**: ① `pango_layout_insert_attr` needs Pango 1.52+ and this machine's headers have no declaration for it; the C side compiled it as an implicit declaration returning int and truncated the pointer, so the symptom would have been a segfault from nowhere. Switched to `PangoAttrList` plus `pango_layout_set_attributes`, available since 1.44. ② Foreground color and foreground alpha are **two separate attributes**: `pango_attr_foreground_alpha_new` takes a single `guint16`, not RGBA four arguments, so a translucent range needs `foreground_new` and `foreground_alpha_new` inserted together. ③ `pango_attr_font_desc_new` copies the description itself, so the local one is released with `pango_font_description_free` right after construction.
- **Override order**: attributes of the same type apply in insertion order, later overriding earlier. Verified through the pixel bounding box of "paint the whole run red, then set the first character back to black", not by reading Pango documentation.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/text` 20/20 — 6 new: color range landing on the right glyphs with the rest keeping the base color; multibyte text proving the split is on **bytes** not characters; size range raising the bounding box; later overriding earlier; out-of-bounds, empty and invalid colors landing no pixels and not crashing; empty text and range retention after `set_text`. `moon check text --deny-warn` zero warnings. The example's title recolours the leading 7 bytes `MoonBit`; smoke 49 frames, exit code 0. Repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, yoga-mbt 81/81.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · App host and `TextEditorHost` closed out (`core/app.mbt`)

- **Layering landing point**: the host is in `core`, since plan §2 assigns App/Window and dirty-region repaint to core. It gathers window, `Loop`, widget tree, input-method channel and present in one place, so examples and components stop copying the loop themselves. The editor seam is **five callbacks on the focused widget** — `on_key` / `on_commit` / `on_preedit` / `im_context` / `im_cursor` — rather than a host object, because `input` already depends on `core` and a reverse import would form a cycle. The four signatures recorded under G5b, `process_key`/`commit`/`preedit`/`set_cursor_rect`, map one-to-one; only the host shape changes, from holding a host object to dispatching callbacks by focus.
- **Raw event conventions**, with `win`'s `code` coming from the C-side `WmEv`: `0/1` key press/release, `2/3` button press/release, `4` pointer motion, `5` wheel. Two data slots reach MoonBit named after C's `dx/dy`: the button number via `button` (dx), the wheel's vertical delta via `axis` (dy, positive = scroll up); on wheel events `dx` is horizontal. Translation is isolated in `raw_to_event` so it is testable headless, since the rest of the host needs a real window.
- **Click takes over focus as a widget-tree function**: `Widget::focusable_at(x,y)` walks the hit chain from deepest upward and returns the first widget declaring a `focus_id`; on `Down` the host updates the focus stack accordingly, the same origin as Web where clicking a form control focuses it. Widgets never touch the focus stack themselves. When focus is already on that widget, **no input-method action is taken** — otherwise a click inside the same field would break the composition in progress.
- **Two measured input-method issues, both cross-field leakage, found on real hardware in this batch**: ① a window has one `GtkIMContext`, so when logical focus moves to another widget `gtk_im_context_reset` is required; otherwise the composition accumulated in the previous field commits into the next one. Injecting `a b Tab c` measured `t2='第二个框岸边'`, where 岸 and 边 were clearly typed in the first field. Added `Window::im_reset()` — extern plus real stub plus stub, three places in one batch. It is called only at the instant **focus actually changes**; calling it every beat breaks composition continuously. The G5 rule "never call reset" refers to per-beat calls. ② Reset alone is not enough: committed text lands in the C-side buffer while the key event is being handled, so in a rapid scripted sequence a Tab event queues behind several commits, and draining one beat late routes the old widget's commit to the new widget. The switch point must therefore, keyed on the **old** id, drain commits, clear the old composition, then reset — `App::flush_ime_for_switch(prev)` runs **before** the focus stack changes. After the fix the same injection gives `t1='hello岸边' c1=11 t2='第二个框曾'`, each field keeping its own text.
- **Four toolchain notes**: ① `loop` is a reserved word, so App's scheduling field is `sched`; `local` was recorded in the previous batch. ② `PointerKind` has closure fields and cannot derive `Eq`, so decisions use `match`. ③ `FocusStack::focus(id)` is a **mutating** setter; highlighting in the draw path must use the new read-only `is_focused(id)`. The example originally called `focus(id)` inside `on_draw`, so every repaint gave focus to whichever widget drew it last — the exit line read `focus=3` and the first field never received keys. Query/assignment ambiguity is prevented by naming and read-only helpers. ④ Editing files with a script: `str.replace(...,1)` that matches nothing is a **silent failure**; the 8 `Widget has no field` errors at the start of this batch came from exactly that. Assert the hit count.
- **Injection technique, carried over with two additions**: the keyboard must go through XTEST, i.e. `xdotool key` **without** `--window`; with `--window` it is XSendEvent and GTK discards synthetic events outright, see the "GUI automation" entry of this document. The mouse must be one atomic command, `xdotool mousemove --window <id> X Y click 1`; split into `mousemove --window` followed by a separate `click 1`, this round measured `clicks=0`, the same root cause as the recorded "XFCE click-to-focus blocks synthetic clicks". Also: when testing that letters reach the field verbatim, drop the IM bridge with `env -u GTK_IM_MODULE -u XMODIFIERS`, otherwise local fcitx5 double-pinyin turns `a b` into Chinese. Conversely, when testing IM cross-field leakage, **keeping** the default environment is the valid control.
- **Acceptance coordinates must come from the same frame as the layout being clicked** — this check removed a false defect on 2026-10-12. A recorded defect claiming "hit area misaligned with rendering", where clicking a button's rendered centre triggered its neighbour and drift grew to the right, did not reproduce: measuring box boundaries from the screenshot of the same run and taking centres gave seven centres hitting themselves. The error was in **when the coordinates were taken** — the screenshot came from a different layout round, since the same example shifted its button row by tens of pixels before and after the host provided full-page scrolling. Clicking a new layout with old coordinates therefore "drifts", and because drift is proportional to horizontal position it looks worse to the right. Convention: injected click coordinates must come from the **same run and the same layout** as the evidence screenshot — take the window origin with `xwininfo`, screenshot the same window, measure box boundaries, then click. Hit and draw are same-source in this stack, both reading `Widget::rect`, and scrolling only adds an offset to the yoga layout, so there is no code path where the two fall out of frame; when this symptom appears, suspect the measurement first.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/core` 28/28 — 6 new: the raw event translation table; commit bubbling along the ancestor chain and consume-then-stop; preedit delivered only to the focused widget without bubbling; `im_context`/`im_cursor` reachability and unreachable after hiding; a widget with no `im_context` declaration not joining the input-method round; `focusable_at` returning the nearest focusable on the hit chain and unreachable when hidden. Eight packages — core/input/render/text/win/icons/theme/sys — all zero warnings under `--deny-warn`; yoga-mbt 81/81; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings. New example `examples/native-app`, the accumulation page for this class of GUI test: smoke exit code 0, `frames=49`. Injection evidence: `a b Tab c` → `t1='helloab' c1=7 t2='第二个框c' focus=2`, typing plus Tab cycling; clicking the button centre (116,128) → `clicks=1` with focus taken; Enter while holding focus → `clicks=2`; clicking the field's leftmost point, window x=17 → widget-local x=1 → caret goes to 0, then typing `z` gives `t1='zhelloab' c1=1`. This is the **first objective check of click-to-position**, previously visible-only. Still needs the user's eyes: caret blink, preedit underline, whether the candidate window sits at the end of the composition string.

### yoga-mbt · Dirty-region incremental relayout + caches persisting across layouts (YG3e, closing the 40% cost left by YG3d)

- **Three acceptance checks, none dispensable**: ① **Change-notification surface** — the 39 style setters plus `append_child`/`clear_children`/`set_measure`/`set_baseline`/`set_pixel_grid` all begin with `mark_changed(self)`, which bumps a global clock and records it in the node's `rev`. A missed mark raises no error; it **silently returns stale results**, the hardest class of bug to find. ② **Subtree version** — at the entry of `calculate_layout`, `scan_subtree_rev(root)` writes each node's "largest rev inside its subtree" top-down. This is O(node count) integer comparison with no measurement and no math. With it, "this subtree has not changed since the last layout" means `subtree_rev == laid_rev`, **with no parent pointer**: a parent pointer plus `children` is a reference cycle, which this toolchain's collector cannot break, so in a long-lived GUI it would be a steady leak. ③ **Argument fingerprint** — `layout_into` records the previous `(avail_w, avail_h, pinned_w, pinned_h)`, and skipping requires both version and fingerprint to match. After a parent relayouts, the available space or pinned size handed to a child may change, so the subtree must be recomputed even when it did not change itself.
- **Two implementation pitfalls**: ① The reused value must be `layout_into_impl`'s **return value**, before pixel-grid rounding, never `layout_width/height` — the latter is rewritten by the `round_to_grid` post-pass, so reusing it makes a gridded tree drift a little lower every round. `round_to_grid` still traverses the whole tree unconditionally, since rounding is idempotent. ② Cache invalidation moved from "clear the whole tree at entry" to a version gate: `cache_fresh(node)` clears a node's two caches only when `cache_rev != subtree_rev`. A change deep in a leaf invalidates its ancestors' **intrinsic size** caches, handled through subtree version rather than backtracking cleanup. A `cache_slots = 16` cap was added: while the available width keeps changing this means "lose reuse, keep correctness", otherwise one cache entry per width grows without bound.
- **Bench split into three scenarios** — same program, the pre-change engine taken from `git archive HEAD`, same machine, release, µs/round @1121 nodes: `steady` with repeated arguments **3652 → 4**; `one_leaf` changing one leaf per round **3656 → 78**; `resize` changing the root width every round and forcing a full relayout **3664 → 3602**, so no regression on the full path. The same three in debug: 7622→14 / 7570→176 / 7572→5940. **All three scenarios' check values, the sum of layout results, are bit-for-bit identical before and after** — an independent cross-engine correctness signal, harder than any self-asserted assertion. Timings use `moonbitlang/core/env`'s millisecond clock, kept inside the bench package so the engine itself stays dependency-free.
- **Meaning for the host**: `App::paint_frame` calls `root.relayout(w, h)` every frame, which is the `steady` path at 4µs per thousand nodes on a clean tree, so "relayout every frame" becomes viable in a GUI. Once G7 wires text `set_measure`/`set_baseline`, `one_leaf` — changing one line of text — is the actual shape.
- **Test orientation and four toolchain writings**: incremental layout's only correctness standard is **"equal, node by node, to a from-scratch full layout of the same state"**, and all 10 cases assert exactly that, building the reference tree fresh in the same state and laying it out once, with no comparison of intermediate states. What was hit: ① top-level identifiers must be unique within a package — the test's `snap` collided with the rounding `snap` already in `algorithm.mbt`, reported as `toplevel identifier declared twice` rather than an ordinary duplicate-name note. ② The third clause of a C-style three-part loop accepts only `i = i + 3`; `i += 3` is a syntax error. ③ An empty array `let a = []` reports `unresolved_type_variable` under the zero-warning gate; write it out as `let a : Array[(Double, Double, Double, Double)] = []`. ④ A `UInt64` duration passed through `.to_double()` into a function taking `UInt64` is blocked by the type gate, so the unit conversion goes inside the callee. One more rule from the same batch: the reparent case first asserted `left == 50` from "new parent's left margin 50", while the actual value is **150**, since inline `box_a` is 100 wide plus the 50 margin — the fix was comparing against a reference tree built directly in the final structure instead of guessing numbers.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/yoga-mbt` **91/91** — 81 existing with zero regression plus 10 incremental: same arguments reused without changing the result; a single-point change equal to full layout; sibling subtrees not re-measured; root width change matching the reference; pixel grid plus skipping still snapping to the grid; hide-and-reshow leaving no stale coordinates; a node's own style change invalidating its intrinsic caches; structural changes not being masked; a subtree moved across parents; and exceeding the cache slot cap matching full layout every round. `moon check src --deny-warn` and `moon check bench --deny-warn` zero warnings. The eight main packages are unaffected — core 28/28 and the rest all green under `--deny-warn` — and repo-wide is still 287 errors / 68 warnings.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Font family enumeration and fallback + mixed-font line height (`text` third batch)

- **Enumeration implementation**: the C side builds the family table once into a process-local cache — `pango_font_map_list_families`, then **sort plus adjacent dedup**, joined into a `GString` separated by `\n`, with `g_string_free(out, FALSE)` handing over ownership. MoonBit reads it back as "read length, then read byte by byte", since this toolchain cannot hand a writable buffer to C. Sorting is not fastidiousness: fontconfig's enumeration order follows load order and one family appears several times under different locale names, so without sorting no stable assertion is writable — 682 entries on this machine.
- **Availability testing lives in C**: `pt_family_available` walks the cache line by line with `g_ascii_strncasecmp`. Case-insensitive family name comparison is fontconfig/Pango's convention; reimplementing the same ASCII folding in MoonBit would drift from the backend.
- **Three fallback conventions**: ① the generic families `serif`/`sans-serif`/`monospace` always count as available — they are absent from the enumeration table and Pango resolves them to concrete families. ② `resolve_family(candidates)` takes the first available entry of a CSS `font-family` list and returns `""` when none is available; an empty family name means "follow the system default" and is used for both measure and draw. ③ `Font::resolve` falls back to the empty name only when the family is **unavailable**, keeping available names and generic families verbatim, since keeping the requested name is what makes the measurement reflect that family's metrics.
- **One measurement corrected the expectation**: an unavailable family name does not make measurement fail — Pango falls back to the default family and still returns numbers, so `line_height_multi([base, Font::new("不存在的族", 13.0)]))` matches passing `""`. The value of fallback is therefore **a stable line-height convention plus a diagnosable family name**, not crash prevention. Assuming "it returns None / it crashes" while writing the test would produce a false-green assertion.
- **Mixed line height settled**: the line box is **max ascent + max descent** aggregated per font, where each inline box contributes its own font and the two maxima may come from different fonts — not "the line height of whichever font has the largest size". In implementation, `pt_font_line_height`'s existing ascent/descent are split into `FontMetrics`; `line_height_font`/`line_ascent_font` become projections of it, removing two duplicated C-call assemblies; `line_height_multi(fonts)` aggregates; `AttributedText::line_height()` feeds in the base font plus every range font. Two hard properties are asserted: line height **covers** the drawn height from `get_bounds_for`, and the base font's line height **cannot contain** 28px content in a range — a too-short box clips glyphs, which is exactly the acceptance check the component layer needs.
- **Six toolchain notes, all hit while writing tests**: ① **MoonBit's `String` ordering is shortlex — length first, then code units** — so `<` and `compare` are **not** lexicographic: `"Agency FB" < "Aharoni"` is false and `"b" < "aa"` is true. Use `String::lexical_compare` for lexicographic order and `compare_ignore_ascii_case` to ignore case. The family-table assertion hit exactly this: C had sorted lexicographically, yet `list[i-1] < list[i]` failed across the board. ② `Int::to_char()` returns `Char?`, so `unsafe_to_char` is required; interpolating the optional silently yields `"Some('x')"`, with one deprecated warning at compile time and nothing else. ③ This toolchain's `Buffer` has no usable `push`/`push_char`; writing a character is `write_char_utf8`, and short strings are simpler with `+=`. ④ `Array[Byte]` has no `freeze`/`to_fixed_array` path to `FixedArray[Byte]`; when C needs it as `Bytes`, start from `FixedArray::make(n, b'\x00')` and write by index. ⑤ `@utf8`'s package path is `moonbitlang/core/encoding/utf8`; `moonbitlang/core/utf8` reports `Cannot find import`. ⑥ MoonBit has no single-quoted strings — `''` is a lexer error.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/text` 28/28 — 8 new: family table non-empty, ordered, deduplicated and free of the separator; availability covering case flips, generic families and the empty name; `resolve_family` taking the first available and falling back to empty when none; `Font::resolve` and `resolve_fonts` preserving size, weight and style; `font_metrics` same-source as the two existing conventions with 28px ascent greater than 13px; `line_height_multi`'s aggregation order-independent and idempotent; in `AttributedText::line_height` color ranges not participating while size ranges do; line height covering drawn height. `moon check text --deny-warn` zero warnings and eight packages zero warnings; core 28 / input 10 / render 40 / icons 4 / theme 7 / sys 7 / yoga-mbt 91 all green; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings. `examples/native-app` gains a font row — the same text in two boxes, with box heights taken from the base and the mixed `line_height()` respectively, the right box visibly taller: smoke exit code 0, status line `fam=682 use='monospace' lhm=42`; the same round's xdotool injection is field-for-field identical to the previous batch, `clicks=2 t1='zhelloab' c1=1 t2='第二个框c' focus=1`. **Needs the user's eyes**: whether the right box fully contains the 28px glyphs and the left box carries no surplus whitespace.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Declarative foundation (`Node`/`mount`/Store/signals/relink on top of Widget)

- **Only one thing changes**: master's `Node { mount : (View) -> View }` becomes `Node { mount : (Widget) -> Widget }`. The semantics — a constructor only builds the tree, and `mount` instantiates widgets and attaches them to the parent — and the existential-type shape where children are naturally heterogeneous, both unchanged word for word. Foundation pieces: `node_of` wrapping an existing widget as a node; `node_of_new` for create plus a configuration callback, where the callback **returns the widget** so chaining further subtrees stays easy; `mount_children`; and `App::mount(children)` as the content entry, marking dirty once after mounting.
- **Three relink decisions**: ① **In-place replacement** — the new generation mounts at the end of the parent first, then `move_child` puts it back at the old generation's previous index, so sibling order and coordinates are unaffected by the replaced item. To support this, the layout engine gained `Node::insert_child(index)` / `Node::remove_child_at(index)`, with out-of-range clamping on insert and None-with-no-change on removal, and the widget layer gained `Widget::insert_child` / `remove_child` / `index_of` / `move_child`, keeping the widget table and node table in sync and identifying removal by `Widget.id`, since widgets with closure fields cannot compare with `==`. ② **The old chain's two Windows workarounds are unnecessary**: master's `bind_node` used `post_task` to defer one beat plus a whole-window `refresh_layout` after relinking, guarding against yoga not recomputing the root after a native remove+add, which left hit-testing permanently on the old rectangle — verified on real hardware as "one click kills all clicking in the window, irreversibly". This stack re-takes hit rectangles from the layout result every frame, `App::paint_frame` → `relayout` → `collect_abs`, so there is no such hole. Injection evidence: clicking three times on the declarative row and then on the button still increments the count by one. ③ **Each generation's subscriptions go into the disposal bag**: `sub_bag_discard(gen)` before rebuild, `sub_bag_begin/end` collecting the current generation during mount, so dead subscriptions do not accumulate with rebuild count. A side benefit is that **nested `bind_node` is also correct** — an inner `sig.subscribe` registered inside its own `mount` lands in the outer bag and leaves when the outer generation does.
- **Repaint loop**: `set_repaint_hook` / `invalidate()` is a **process-level single slot**; `App::new` installs its own `schedule_paint`, which sets dirty and calls `@win.wake()`. With no hook installed, as in headless tests, `invalidate()` is a no-op, so the component layer may call it unconditionally. Known limit: one host per process, and multi-window waits until the host layer can locate a widget's owning App. There is no multi-window consumer today, so no speculative implementation is written.
- **Port discipline**: the signal kernel and `Store` moved line for line from master's `yue/signals.mbt` / `yue/store.mbt` into `core/signal.mbt` / `store.mbt`; both were already free of platform dependencies and the public names `Signal`/`Store`/`batch`/`sub_bag_*` are unchanged. 19 existing tests came across whole: automatic dependency collection, a conditional branch depending only on the signals it actually read, diamond dependency convergence, batch merging, exact unsubscribe by handle, and whole-generation unsubscribe in a bag with a no-bag fallback.
- **Two writing pitfalls**: ① Multiple `_wbtest.mbt` files in the same package **share top-level helper names**; a duplicate is not reported as `declared twice` but makes **the earlier definition unused** — redefining `sized` in `node_wbtest.mbt` immediately made `widget_wbtest.mbt`'s copy report `Unused function 'sized'`. Grep the package's existing helpers before writing tests instead of making a second one. ② If `node_of_new`'s configuration callback is declared to return `Unit`, using a widget-returning helper such as `sized(w, ..)` in the body is a direct type mismatch; returning `Widget` both drops the `let _ =` and lets the callback build further subtrees.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/core` **53/53** — 28 existing, 19 ported signal/Store, 6 declarative: `mount_children` order and coordinates; `bind_node` replacing in place with sibling coordinates following; the old generation's subscriptions unsubscribed as a whole bag, leaving only 1 subscription on the source after 5 rebuilds; the parent always holding exactly one tree and never half; `swap_node` pre-building two trees and toggling visibility only, with the hidden tree's rectangle zeroed; `invalidate` a no-op with no hook. yoga-mbt **92/92** — new in-place insert/remove: removing a middle item and re-inserting matches the reference tree node by node, and out-of-range leaves the tree unchanged. Eight packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gains a declarative row where a click does `Store.update` and an in-place relink — `decl=3 kids=6/6`, so the root child count stays constant and there is neither a leak nor a duplicate mount — with `clicks=1` in the same round, the button hit still working after three relinks, `t1='hellox' c1=6` for typing plus Tab cycling, exit code 0. **Needs the user's eyes**: the declarative row's background alternating with click parity, which is what proves a new tree really replaced the old one rather than the text merely changing.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Widget interaction foundation (hover/press ownership, pointer capture, callbacks must not capture themselves)

- **State lives in the host; widgets only read**: `Widget` gained `hovered`/`pressed`, maintained by the host on every pointer event from hit and capture — `set_hover(id)` / `set_press(id)`, each traversing the tree only when ownership **changes** — and widgets read them directly in `on_draw`. The old chain's `hover_group` polled, since libyue delivers no move events and had to ask where the mouse was on a timer. This stack has complete routing, so enter and leave are both events: when the hover owner changes, the previous one receives a synthesized `Leave`. A tooltip shape with "enter but no leave" does not hold here.
- **A press enters the capture period**: the dispatch decision is the pure function `route_pointer(root, ev, hover_id, capture) -> (new hover, new capture, consumed, changed)`, and `App` only stores and writes back the two states. Rules: the `Down` hit target is marked pressed and becomes the capture owner, after which every `Move`/`Up` is delivered to the capture owner along its path to the root, with local coordinates folded as usual; `Up` clears the pressed state, releases capture, then re-evaluates hover **from the release position**; during capture hover stays put. Why it is required: without capture, once the pointer leaves the widget it never receives `Up` again. A stuck pressed state is only the mild symptom — measured as the widget staying permanently highlighted — while drag selection and "drag the insertion point" in a text field lose any basis. This is the equivalent of Web's `setPointerCapture`.
- **Callbacks must not capture the widget itself — the reference-cycle discipline**: `on_draw`'s first parameter became `Widget` and `im_cursor` now takes a `Widget`, so a widget reads its own `rect`/`hovered`/`pressed` from the argument and the handle no longer enters the closure. The reason is that widgets in this stack **hold** their own callback tables, so a closure capturing the widget on top of that is a reference cycle, which reference counting cannot break. A throwaway example hides the problem, while with `bind_node` one leaked tree per relink is a steady leak. All draw callbacks in examples and tests were updated with the signature.
- **One expectation corrected by measurement**: a `display:none` sibling **moves up**, since a column container's auto height counts visible items only. The area a hidden item used to occupy is therefore hit by the sibling that moved up, not by the parent container — the first version asserted "hits the parent widget" and `route_pointer` returned the sibling's id directly. The implication for the component layer: no extra hover-state cleanup is needed for hidden items, because live items take the position naturally.
- **One addition to the injection technique**: write a drag sequence as an atomic press, `xdotool mousemove --window <id> X Y mousedown 1`, then move with `xdotool mousemove --window <id> X2 Y2` and release with `xdotool mouseup 1` — no `--window`, so XTEST releases at the current position. Measured: press inside the band, release outside it, and the capture band still receives the release.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/core` **59/59** — 6 new: hover following with `Leave` synthesized; during capture both motion and release delivered to the presser with hover staying put; clicking empty space not entering capture and not crashing; a hidden widget not participating in hover while a sibling moving up takes the hit; `by_id` and `dispatch_pointer_to` delivering by identity with coordinates playing no part in the decision; wheel following the same bubbling rule. Eight packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; yoga-mbt 92/92; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gains a "capture band" whose draw state reads `w.pressed`/`w.hovered` directly — press inside the band, drag to (200,245), drag to (300,100) and release → `band=d1/u1/m3`, so **the release made outside the band was still received** — with the button's `clicks=1` and the declarative row's `decl=2 kids=7/7` unchanged in the same round, exit code 0. **Needs the user's eyes**: the band keeping its pressed color, orange, through the drag and returning to normal after release, with the hover color no longer chasing the pointer.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Component layer, first batch (new package `ui`: text measurement feeding back into layout + container/label/separator/image/icon/button)

- **Why not written into `yue/components`**: that directory is the old chain's component implementation, referencing the `@yue` root package and `@declarative`, and is the main source of the repo's 287 errors. Each new-stack batch rebuilds only the **semantics worth keeping**; placing it in the same package would make the per-package gate `moon check <package> --deny-warn` permanently unexecutable, since the old files' errors would be reported together. The new component layer therefore starts a separate `ui` package, the old package is replaced or deleted batch by batch, and the accounts settle when G7 closes.
- **Text measurement fed back into the layout engine**, the piece G7 owed: `attach_text_measure(w, src)` sets both `set_measure`, taking size from `measure_font`, and `set_baseline`, taking it from `line_ascent_font`, on the node. Text therefore takes part in a real `align-items: baseline` layout for the first time, and a `label`'s width and height are the true sizes Pango reports. Two assertions corrected by measurement: ① **a column container's default `align-items: stretch` pulls the label to the full row width** — to observe the measured width the parent must use `FlexStart` or the label must carry an explicit width; the first attempt asserted the measured width and got 240 instead of 70. ② Under baseline alignment **the top-edge difference equals the difference of the two ascents**, with the larger size sitting higher; the difference was written backwards once. A min-content query, with the requested axis `Some(0.0)`, is currently treated as unconstrained — a documented approximation to be refined once ellipsis self-sizing is wired.
- **Pointer callbacks also take the widget itself**: `on_pointer`'s first parameter became `Widget`, under the same reference-cycle discipline as `on_draw`. A button needs `self.rect` to decide whether the release still lands inside itself — capture guarantees the button receives a release made elsewhere, but only its own rectangle distinguishes inside from outside.
- **Two naming divergences from master, documented with no compatibility layer**: ① `type` in `button(type="text")` is a MoonBit **reserved word** and a syntax error as a parameter name; it becomes `kind : ButtonKind` with `Primary`/`Border`/`Text`. ② The disabled color scheme temporarily uses a `fill_hover` base with `text_secondary` text; a real disabled palette joins `Theme` with the theme batch, since none of its 20 fields covers it today.
- **Theme following is one process-level subscription**: components call `watch_theme()` on mount, idempotently, and a theme change triggers one `invalidate()`. Per-widget subscription is deliberately not done — `invalidate` is global anyway, and per-widget subscriptions would leave one dead subscription per relink while buying no precision. Colors are read fresh inside `on_draw` rather than fixed at tree build, so a theme switch shows in the next frame.
- **The counterpart of text binding**: `label_dyn(sig : Signal[String], ...)` occupies the old chain's `bind_label` position — text changed in place, measure callback re-set, node marked dirty, repaint requested, no subtree rebuild. The subscription is retired into the generation's disposal bag through `@core.sub_bag_register`, which was promoted from package-private to public for that purpose, since all component-layer cleanup goes through it.
- **Verification**: the new package `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` 7/7 — label size coming from measurement and re-measured on signal; the top-edge difference of two sizes under baseline alignment; a button's release inside versus outside; disabled consuming nothing and not calling back; hover changing colors while the text still lands inside the box; container/group/separator geometry with the horizontal line spanning the full width; an icon occupying space by size and really producing pixels, plus a missing image file not crashing. **Nine packages** — core/input/render/text/win/icons/theme/sys/ui — `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; core 59 / input 10 / render 40 / text 28 / icons 4 / theme 7 / sys 7 / yoga-mbt 92 all green; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gains a bottom row built entirely from `@ui` constructors — label, vertical separator, icon, an `加一` button and a `禁用` button — and the window grows to 420×372.
