Injecting `xdotool mousemove --window 135 278 click 1` twice gives `comp=2`; clicking the disabled button next leaves the count unchanged with `decl=0`, so disabled really does not consume events; `kids=8/8` keeps the root child count constant across repeated relinks; exit code 0. The existing evidence in the same round — typing, Tab, click-to-position, capture band — did not regress. **Needs the user's eyes**: the component row's hover/press colors, whether the vertical separator really spans the row height, and the baseline appearance of icon and text on one row.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Form controls, first batch, and two rendering defects only a screenshot reveals

- **Defect 1 — text ignored the widget's origin**: the text layer, `pt_draw*`/`rt_draw`, built its own surface from `Bitmap.data` and drew glyphs onto it, a path that **does not pass through the Painter's CTM and clip**. The host's per-layer `translate + clip_rect` therefore had no effect on text at all, and on the real window every widget's glyphs piled up at the window's top-left — see the before/after screenshots in the "组件首批" entry. The fix hands the Cairo session over: the render stub gains `void *cr_session_context(int64_t id)` returning that session's `cairo_t*`, and the text stub gains `pt_draw_box_cr` and `rt_draw_cr`, which on the **caller's context** do `cairo_save → set_source_rgba → move_to → pango_cairo_show_layout → cairo_restore`. save/restore preserves the caller's source and clip and leaves nothing polluted. The MoonBit counterparts are `Painter::cairo_id()`, `@text.draw_box_at / draw_at / draw_text_at` and `AttributedText::draw_at`. The older `draw_to/draw_in_box/draw(target,…)` stay, since offscreen self-drawing and the chart buffer still need them.
- **Defect 2 — nested drawing accumulated offsets twice**: `Widget::paint` did `p.translate(self.rect.x, self.rect.y)` layer by layer while `rect` is an **absolute** rectangle, so from the second layer up it added the ancestors' offsets again and the second row's text landed outside the window. Changed to `paint_at(p, ox, oy)`: translate only the difference from the already-translated origin, and pass this widget's absolute origin down to its children.
- **Why earlier batches missed them**: in batch 1's drawing case the middle widget happened to sit at `(0,0)`, where absolute equals relative, so the test passed naturally; and the example's status line reports counts and text, never pixels. **Conclusion: for a GUI, "exit code 0 plus correct status" is not "correct picture."** The accumulation page therefore keeps two machine-checkable paths: the `NATIVE-APP-RECTS` geometry line, giving each root child's `x,y,wxh`, from which injection coordinates are taken instead of guessing at a screenshot; and `import -window <id> x.png` whenever the picture itself must be inspected.
- **Linking across static libraries**: the text stub references symbols from the render stub, so `moon test -p .../gui/text` failed at **link time** with `undefined reference to cr_session_context`, invisible at compile time. Per AGENTS rule 1, link flags change only in `scripts/prebuild.py`: text's `link_flags` gained `-lrender_cairo_stub`, consumer first in the order.
- **Disabled state must be a cell, not a boolean**: the test caught a real bug in the stepper — with `disabled` fixed into the closure at tree build, once a value reached the boundary the `-`/`+` buttons' disabled state stayed frozen at the moment of mount. Changed to `Enabled { mut off : Bool }`, read fresh in drawing and events; composite widgets — the checkbox row, the switch, both sides of the stepper — share one cell, and `set_disabled(cell, v)` changes it at any time.
- **Drag state is held by the component itself**: the slider uses `dragging : Ref[Bool]` rather than reading the host's `pressed`, because the host's `pressed` is only set in a real event stream while the component must be able to complete a drag under **any** delivery path — otherwise headless cases could not exercise dragging at all.
- **Two coordinate conventions, found across four cases in this batch**: ① `dispatch_pointer` / `dispatch_pointer_to` take **window coordinates**, converted to local only at delivery; passing local coordinates in a test silently misses, which presents as "the click did nothing". ② The coordinate-based `dispatch_pointer` **cannot deliver a drag that started outside the widget**; out-of-bounds motion must go through `root.dispatch_pointer_to(w.id, ev)`, the equivalent of the host's capture-period delivery.
- **Seven toolchain writings**: a `match` with several subjects must be written as a tuple, `match (a, b) { (Some(x), y) => ... }`; `Double::clamp` takes labelled `min=/max=`; `Int::to_char()` returns `Char?` and needs `unsafe_to_char`, otherwise it silently interpolates `"Some('x')"`; `String.split` yields `Iter[StringView]` and `StringView::to_string` is deprecated in favour of `to_owned`; `Array[Byte]` has no `freeze`/`to_fixed_array`, so when C needs it as `Bytes` start from `FixedArray::make`; a missing closing `]` in `Option[(A, B) -> R]` produces an unrelated `unexpected token infix`; continuation lines cannot start with `+` or `&&`, since MoonBit breaks statements at line ends, and `type` is a reserved word that cannot be a parameter name.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p .../gui/ui` 15/15 — 7 new: checkbox click, toggle-again, out-of-bounds and disabled-not-consuming; radio group writing per item with clicking the selected item changing nothing; switch size fixed and drawing following the Store's current value; slider press taking the value, out-of-bounds drag, step snapping, disabled not consuming; progress bar filling by value; stepper clamping and auto-disabling at the bounds; Store subscriptions retiring with the disposal bag, `sub_count=0` after 5 relinks versus one permanent subscription without a bag. Two rendering regressions also added: text landing with the widget's origin and being clipped, and rich text drawn through the session landing inside the translated box. `text` 29/29; nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; core 59 / render 40 / icons 4 / theme 7 / sys 7 / yoga-mbt 92 all green; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings. Real-window injection with coordinates taken from `NATIVE-APP-RECTS`: `form=true/false/90/1` — checkbox to true, switch to false, slider dragged to 90 snapping to step 5, stepper +1; `decl=3 kids=9/9`, so the declarative in-place relink did not regress; `band=d3/u3/m3`, three releases outside the band all received; `clicks=2 t1='zhelloab' c1=1` for typing, Tab and click-to-position; exit code 0. Screenshot review: title, both input fields, the count button, the mixed line-height boxes, the component row and the form row all correctly placed.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Entry full semantics (`ui/entry.mbt`)

- **Shape**: the single authority for text state remains `@input.Editor`; the component keeps no second copy. `Store[String]` is only its outward projection — after an edit it writes back to the Store, and when something external sets the Store the value flows back into the kernel through a subscription, retired via `subscribe_id` plus the disposal bag so relinks leave no dead subscription. The seam to the host is the five foundation callbacks, and the four input-method conditions are satisfied centrally by `App::pump_ime`; the component only supplies `im_context`, committed text plus byte caret, and `im_cursor`, the candidate window's placement rectangle.
- **Focus highlight is now synced by the host**: added `Widget.focused` and `Widget::set_focused_by_focus(focus_id)`, with `App::paint_frame` syncing once before each frame's drawing. Same reasoning as `hovered`/`pressed`: the focus stack records ids only, while a component needs "is that id me". Having each component ask the focus stack itself would both fail to reach the stack and leak core's focus structure into the component layer.
- **A read-only whitelist must be written by keysym family**: the first version allowed 65288..65300 as navigation, so **Backspace, 65288, passed as navigation** and the read-only field still deleted characters — caught by the test. The real reading: arrows, Home, End and PageUp/PageDown are at **65360..65367**, while Backspace 65288 and Delete 65535 are editing keys. Settled as: allow Ctrl/Shift combinations, 65360..65367 and Tab; Backspace, Delete and printable characters are never swallowed.
- **Double-click detection**: two `Down` events less than 400ms apart and less than 4px apart, using `@core.now_ms()`, which forwards `@win.now_ms()`. **The side effect is on record**: rapid repeated clicks are classified as double-clicks, so a headless case doing "press-release-press" to test dragging takes the word-selection branch on the second press, and the assertions must be written to that semantics.
- **CJK word selection is where the current approximation shows**: `is_word_byte` counts everything `>= 0x80` as in-word, matching the kernel, so a double-click in Chinese selects **the whole contiguous run of Chinese**. Measured on the real window: double-clicking at the end of `组件框ab` selected the entire `组件框ab` and the replacement left `Q`. The ASCII side behaves normally — space-delimited, so in `组件框ab c` a double-click selects only `c`. Whether to converge on Blink's dictionary word segmentation is deferred until the Blink cross-check technique reaches text; recorded, not guessed.
- **Drag selection**: press records the anchor, and during capture each `Move` extends the selection with `select_range(anchor, byte_at_x(x))`, continuous even when the pointer leaves the field — the second consumer of the host's capture period. `Up` ends the drag, and later `Move` events no longer track, asserted by the caret not changing.
- **A shortcut in the observation channel**: the kernel handle is not exposed, since text authority lives in the component; headless cases observe through two public paths instead — `w.im_context()` giving text plus caret, and the behaviour "typing replaces the selection", which is itself the selection check. Cleaner than opening a pile of getters for the sake of testing.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **25/25** — 10 new entry cases: keystrokes writing back to the Store with Backspace and undo; commit landing in the text while preedit only enters drawing; click at the far left/right positioning; double-click word selection; drag to select all with no tracking after release; Shift+arrow extending the selection plus Ctrl+A/C/V on the internal clipboard; read-only allowing navigation and copy; password masking keeping the original text in the Store; placeholder producing pixels while the Store stays empty; external Store changes flowing back into the kernel with `focused` synced by the host. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide back to 287 errors / **68** warnings, having briefly reached 69 from one unused variable in a test. Real-window injection, with `examples/native-app` gaining an `@ui.entry` row at `focus_id=4`: click into the field → type `ab c` → double-click at the end → type `Q` → `Home`+`Shift+End`+`Delete`+`Ctrl+Z` → status line `t3='组件框ab Q'`, `focus=4`, exit code 0. Screenshot review confirms the component field placed and outlined normally. **Needs the user's eyes**: caret blink, driven by the caller's clock through the component's `caret_on?`, preedit underline, and whether the candidate window sits at the end of the composition string.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Display family, first batch (`ui/display.mbt`: label / badge / avatar / separator / alert / card / descriptions / empty / result / polyline progress)

- **One difference from master, on record**: the CSS-style `style=[("marginRight", 8.0)]` channel is not wired yet and comes with the theme batch's style channel, so this batch keeps **typed** parameters only. The semantic color enum `SemanticType` — Primary/Success/Warning/Danger/Info — with `type_color`/`type_light_color` keeps the same names, and colors are read from `theme`'s five main and five light levels, which the theme batch already provides, so no new fields were needed.
- **Two rules for self-drawn components, hit in this batch and written into the code comments**: ① **Draw callbacks must not change layout** — the first version of `statistic` called `set_width` with the measured width inside `on_draw`, making paint a writer of layout: layout and drawing trigger each other within one frame, and the dirty-region incremental relayout's fingerprint check is disturbed by the writer itself. Width must be fixed at mount from measurement. ② **A widget must be tall enough for its own glyphs** — the polyline progress's percentage column first reserved the same 8px as the bar, so 11px text was clipped in half, visible only in a screenshot; text nodes get at least the glyph height and containers stretch to the tallest child.
- **The close hot zone of a dismissible alert**: the whole alert consumes the press so the click does not fall through to what is underneath, but `on_close` fires only in the **top-right 24×24**. The hot-zone test uses local coordinates, `ev.x >= rect.w - 24 && ev.y <= 24`, which still holds under capture since the release returns to this widget.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **33/33** — 8 new display-family cases: five semantic colors pairwise distinct and all valid hex; label and badge sized by content showing `99+` past the cap; avatar's first character producing pixels; a text separator spanning full width with lines on both sides; an alert with a description being taller and close firing only in the hot zone, a click outside not counting; a card with a title taking two extra rows, title plus divider; descriptions row count by entry count; empty/result really producing pixels; polyline progress having two columns with the fill following the Store. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gains a display-family block with a geometry line giving coordinates — clicking the alert outside the hot zone gives `closed=0`, clicking the top-right twice gives `closed=2`, with the component button's `comp=1` and `kids=11/11` in the same round, exit code 0. Screenshot review: three label colors, badges 7/99+/dot, the avatar `刘`, the `或` separator, the alert's left color bar and description, progress bar and percentage all correct.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Display family close-out (timeline + carousel, auto-advance on the host's delay channel)

- **New channel: process-level delay** — `set_timer_hooks`/`set_timeout`/`clear_timeout` in `core/loop.mbt`. A component wants "run once after a while" and must not know which host it belongs to, so it is a process-level single slot like `set_repaint_hook`: `App::new` forwards both functions to its own `Loop`, `timer`/`cancel`, and components only call `@core.set_timeout(ms, f)`. **With no host, `set_timeout` returns 0 and does nothing** — the component keeps working, it just does not advance by itself. Headless tests can therefore install their own channel, take the callback and dispatch it manually, so the carousel's self-scheduling chain becomes deterministically testable instead of waiting on a real clock.
- **Three carousel shape decisions**: ① Panels are **all pre-built** and page switching only flips `Widget::set_visible` — same reasoning as `swap_node`: not destroying a subtree leaves no dangling callback and needs no remount. ② The arrow's hover background reads the **host-maintained** `Widget.hovered` directly, dropping master's `on_mouse_enter/on_mouse_leave` — interaction state is set centrally by the host and components only read it. ③ Hover-pause relies on the `Move`/`Leave` this widget receives **from the parent chain**, since events bubble from the deepest hit widget upward and the first `true` consumes. If the page content consumes both motion and leave, the pause gets no signal — not speculation but a necessary consequence of the routing rule, which is why `carousel_pause(handle, v)` exists for callers to take over directly.
- **Retirement of the self-scheduling chain**: a one-shot delay whose callback schedules the next beat, with the handle stored in `CarouselHandle.timer`; `carousel_stop` both sets `running=false` and calls `clear_timeout` to cancel the pending beat. The test measured the boundary semantics: after stop, **the beat already queued still runs once**, but the `running` guard makes it neither switch pages nor schedule again — so cancelling the handle cannot be the only safeguard and the `running` flag must exist alongside it.
- **Timeline's vertical line convention**, EP as-is: the first row starts at its dot, the last row ends at its dot, middle rows run through. Row height is fixed and drawing writes local coordinates only, since the host translates and clips layer by layer and widgets need no clipping of their own.
- **Two toolchain/test measurements**: ① Constructors of the same name across payload-free enums report `The constructor Primary is ambiguous` — this repository has `Primary` in both `ButtonKind` and `SemanticType` — so annotate the element type on the array literal instead of writing fully qualified names that pollute the assertion. ② The indicator dot is only 8×8, so taking the injection point at "half the row height", `y+12`, lands outside the hot zone; the symptom is "clicking does nothing" with **no error at all**. Before injecting by coordinates, re-read that widget's own `rect` — this example therefore added the `NATIVE-APP-CAR`/`NATIVE-APP-AUTO` geometry lines, giving the arrows, the last indicator dot and the auto-advance panel directly.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **37/37** — 4 new closing display-family cases: timeline rows equal height with no line above the first dot or below the last, and dot and line in different colors; carousel pre-building three pages showing only the current one, with arrows and indicator dots switching and wrapping; auto-advance going through the host channel, paused not advancing but keeping the chain alive, stop cancelling the pending beat; empty entries not crashing. `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/core` **60/60** — 1 new: with no channel installed `set_timeout` returns 0 and does nothing, and once installed `set_timeout`/`clear_timeout` forward as a pair while handle 0 forwards no cancellation. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings, `yoga-mbt` 92/92, repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gains a "display family close-out" block with the window grown to 560×900 — injecting right arrow, then last indicator dot, then left arrow gives `car=2`, a unique index that proves both arrows and the indicator each worked; the baseline auto-advance reads `auto=6`; parking the pointer on the auto-advancing carousel without moving gives `auto=2`, hover-pause measured. Screenshot review: timeline's three-color dots and continuous lines, both carousels' arrows and highlighted indicator dots all correct.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Date family, first batch (value model + self-drawn calendar panel, "today" from platform calendar time)

- **New platform reading `wm_local_date`** — two C stubs in `win` plus an extern in `ffi.mbt` plus the public API in `window.mbt`, forwarded by `core` as `local_ymd()`. A calendar needs **calendar time**, while the stack's existing `now_ms()` is `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, a monotonic clock used as the loop's time base; deriving a date from it gives a stable but wrong number. The C side uses `time()` plus `localtime_r` through the system time zone, packed as `year*10000 + month*100 + day`. **Failure and the portable stub return 0**, which `core` turns into `(0,0,0)`, and only then does the component layer's `today_date()` fall back to 1970-01-01. The layering is "the platform provides the reading, upper layers decide the fallback"; this layer does not guess a date.
- **`today` is an explicit parameter**: `calendar_t(today? : DateYMD = today_date())` defaults to the platform and takes a fixed date in tests. Otherwise an assertion like "which cell does 1 October land in" drifts with the day it runs, which is no assertion at all.
- **The 42-cell grid math extracted as the pure function `month_grid(y, m) -> Array[(DateYMD, Bool)]`**, one more than master: the panel only draws and handles clicks, and the grid rules — the previous month's tail before the first cell, the next month's head after the month end, month cell count equal to the month length — are testable without a widget. The date picker and the range picker then share the same function instead of each re-deriving it.
- **All 42 cells built once; changing month changes data only**: the panel structure is constant, so hit rectangles cannot go out of position through adding or removing child widgets. `Widget::hit_path` takes rectangles from the layout result every frame, but rebuilding a subtree would still break the pairing of a press and a release across generations. `rebuild_grid` writes only each cell's `Ref[DateYMD]`/`Ref[Bool]` and then calls `invalidate()`.
- **Selection read fresh from the Store, no cached copy**: `state_of` reads `value.get()` on every paint, falling back to the widget's own `sel` only when there is no Store, so an external `v.set(...)` replaces the solid square immediately with no "subscribe then refresh manually" step. Master's `refresh()` callback chain is replaced by read-at-draw-time in this stack; subscriptions only request a repaint, `follow_store`.
- **Select on release, cross-month cells not selectable**: a cell's `Down` consumes only when `in_month`, so a cross-month cell does not even take the press and the event keeps bubbling; `Up` additionally requires the release still landing in that cell — capture delivers the release back to the pressed cell, and out of bounds it does not count as a click.
- **Two toolchain measurements hit while writing tests**: ① `(x) -> Bool { ... }` is **not** a closure literal, it is a function type annotation; `Array::filter` needs `fn(x) { x.1 }`. Getting it wrong produces a cascade of unrelated `cannot infer` / `unbound` / `Parse error` messages. ② On this toolchain, `derive(Eq, Show)` on a value type has `Show` deprecated, pointing at `Debug`, while `derive(Eq)` and `derive(Debug)` both raise the `implicit_impl_as_method` deprecation warning — not worth it under a zero-warning gate. Assertions therefore go through string observation, `format()` and cell state names, which adds no derives to components and produces more readable failure output.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **44/44** — 7 new date-family cases: leap years, month lengths and weekdays through three Sakamoto anchors, 2026-10-11 Sunday and 2000-01-01 Saturday; month stepping including ±12 and 15 months; formatting zero-padding, time clamping and range endpoints in either order; the 42-cell grid, October's first cell 2026-09-27, cell 5 being 10-01, last cell 11-07, month count 31, a leap February having 29 cells, and January's cross-year first cell landing in the previous December; local today must be a real year, proving calendar time rather than the monotonic clock; the panel writing to the Store on click with cross-month cells unselectable and release outside not counting; the selected date following after a month switch with the selected cell drawn as a solid square, compared against whether that spot is still the panel background since the panel base is opaque; an external Store change switching the selected cell; range cell mapping for endpoints, middle and half-open ranges. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings, `yoga-mbt` 92/92, repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` rearranged 6b/6c into three columns with the window changed to 900×700 and the geometry line gaining `NATIVE-APP-CAL` — injecting right arrow, last indicator dot, left arrow, then "cell 14 → right arrow to November → the same cell again" gives the status line `car=2 auto=6 date='2026-11-15'`, `kids=12/12`, exit code 0. Screenshot review: three columns side by side, the calendar header `2026 年 10 月`, September's tail greyed out, indicator highlight all correct.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Navigation family, first batch (segmented / breadcrumb / pagination / steps / collapse panel)

- **master's `stateful_item` becomes "read at draw time plus host interaction state"**: the old form kept two Refs per item, `hover`/`focused`, set and repainted inside enter/leave/focus callbacks. In this stack hover and press ownership are maintained centrally by the host from hit results — `Widget.hovered`/`pressed`/`focused` — so background and text color callbacks take only this widget and read as they draw; components no longer handle enter/leave. Two benefits: rebuilding a subtree cannot leave "the pointer has left but hover is still true", and the subscription surface drops from two per item to one per group, since `follow_store` exists only to request a repaint.
- **Selection always through the Store, read at draw time**: `segmented`/`breadcrumb`/`pagination` all "set on click, get on draw", so one Store attached in several places highlights everywhere in step, with no registry for "notify each widget after a change".
- **Pagination arrow clamping lives in the host callback rather than in disabled buttons**: `‹`/`›` stay clickable on the first and last page and the value clamps to `[1, pages]`. Different from Web's disabled form, but one less piece of state — with mutable `pages` there is no recomputing disabled — and a headless test can assert directly that eight consecutive left-arrow clicks still sit at 1.
- **Collapsing sets `set_visible(false)`, display:none, without destroying the content**: content subtrees are pre-built and resident, so opening and closing flip visibility plus `invalidate()` only. The test proves collapsing really stops occupying space by asserting **the whole block's height falls**; asserting visibility alone would miss "hidden but still taking height". Each panel's independent open state is held by its own `Ref[Bool]`, so panels do not interfere.
- **One assertion I wrote wrong, recorded to prevent repeating it**: the steps widget interleaves "connector before the square", so the child order is `方块0 文字0 连线1 方块1 文字1 …`; guessing squares at indices 0/2/4 lands on text nodes, which have no background, so two samples come out the same color and the assertion `l1 != l3` fails as `false`. **Pixel assertions on self-drawn components must re-read the actual child order first**, not guess the structure from the visual order.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **49/49** — 5 new navigation-family cases: segmented setting the Store on click with segment width following the text, and the selected segment's background differing from unselected; breadcrumb separator taking space, clicking a non-last item changing the value and clicking the last item not; pagination clicking a page number landing directly, arrows stepping, and repeated clicks at both ends clamping to 1/5; steps having three mutually distinct background colors with the connector colored by the current step and a pending block changing color after a Store change; collapse panels opening only the first by default, each block toggling independently, and the whole block's height falling after collapse. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings, `yoga-mbt` 92/92, repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` laid this batch into the fourth column with the window at 1240×840 and the geometry line gaining `NATIVE-APP-NAV`, giving the four injection rectangles directly — injecting "segmented second item → breadcrumb second item → page 3 → second block's header row" gives `seg='分段乙' crumb='列表' page=3 step=1 fold='11'`, where `fold='11'` proves the second block opened without dragging the first along; `kids=12/12` in the same round, the earlier `car`/`date` readings unchanged, exit code 0. Screenshot review: segmented highlight, breadcrumb separators, solid page number, steps' three states with connectors, collapse arrow directions all correct.
- **A pitfall in the verification technique, nearly misjudged as "components not working"**: consolidating three batches into one injection round of 10 clicks made the last three ineffective — not because the navigation family was unwired, but because the example's 5-second auto-exit beat the injection. The acceptance check is "the same coordinates work when injected in separate rounds, and only the first few land when merged". The accumulation page's live window therefore moved from 5s to 9s; every future block must check live time against click count × per-click interval, and exit code 0 is not evidence that "all interactions passed".

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Navigation family, second batch (side menu / grouped menu / tree / tabs)

- **Rounded corners implemented in the component layer rather than waiting on the Painter**: the facade has no rounded rectangle, so `fill_round_rect` composes a path inside `ui` from four line segments plus four 90° arcs, with arc angles always increasing — `Painter::arc`'s `ccw` parameter is unavailable on both backends, so a counter-clockwise need is expressed by increasing start and end angles. The menu's 4px corners and the selection accent bar therefore match EP's appearance without adding a new render-layer contract.
- **Tree and collapse panel share one shape: pre-built children toggled by `set_visible`**, with collapse meaning display:none — not measured, not occupying space, not drawn, not hit — and expansion flipping the flag only. Node rows are appended in pairs of "row plus child container", so tests take the row at `children()[2i]` and the container at `children()[2i+1]`. A leaf row does not even consume `Down` when `has_kids` is false, and the event keeps bubbling, so there is no "click did nothing but the parent's hover got eaten".
- **Tab visibility is driven by a Store subscription, and the new page is shown before the old one is hidden**: that order was a Windows-only workaround in master, since the reverse let yoga allocate the outer box at zero content in the intermediate state. This stack relayouts from the root every frame and has no such hole, but "show first, then hide" is harmless to keep and consistent with `swap_node`'s pre-built shape. The tab header row enters the tree **before** the page area, so visual order equals child order, pinned in the test by `head.rect.y < page.rect.y`.
- **Two places where the tests were written wrong, both of the "inject by coordinates" class and worth memorizing**: ① Sample pixels must be taken **at each control's own y**. The three side-menu items share width and x, so using the first row's y to sample the second row still samples the first row, the selected one, and "an unselected item should match the container background" failed as "both are light blue". The symptom looks like a broken component; the assertion sampled the wrong point. ② **A hidden widget's rect is zeroed** — zeroing the whole invisible subtree is G6's convention — so "click an item inside a collapsed group" does not hit that item but another widget near the origin; here it hit group one's header row and expanded it again, presenting as "it changed though I did nothing". To verify "collapsed means unclickable", test `hit_path`/`hit_test` explicitly in window coordinates rather than adding an offset to the widget's own rect.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **53/53** — 4 new second-batch cases: side menu item width following the container, clicking an item setting the Store, and the selected item's background differing from unselected with sampling per row; grouped menu headers affecting only their own group, the whole column moving up after collapse requiring coordinates to be re-taken, and items selectable again after re-expansion; tree children pre-built hence collapsed, clicking the parent row expanding, clicking a leaf doing nothing, clicking again collapsing; tabs pre-building three pages showing only the current one, switching both on tab click and on external Store change, with the header row above the page area. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings, `yoga-mbt` 92/92, repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` adding a fifth column with the window at 1620×840 and the geometry line gaining `NATIVE-APP-NAV2` with the menu's second item, the tree parent row and the second tab page rectangles — a merged 13-click round, three carousel clicks plus three calendar clicks plus four first-batch navigation clicks plus this batch's three, gives `car=2 auto=11 date='2026-11-15' seg='分段乙' crumb='列表' page=3 step=1 fold='11' menu='报表' tab=1 tree=1`, `kids=12/12`, exit code 0. The tab click must precede the tree expansion, since expanding pushes the tabs down. Screenshot review: the menu's light-blue rounded background with the left accent bar and the `报表` icon, tree triangle directions, tab indicator bar and page content all correct.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Transfer box closed out (navigation family 10/10) and two coordinate disciplines for rebuild-style lists

- **Selection moved to two component-owned tables, rows holding no subscriptions**: master's transfer subscribed to the data Store once per row built, retiring the whole bag with `sub_bag_begin/end/discard` before each rebuild so dead subscriptions did not accumulate with moves. In this stack a row reads only its own `Ref[Array[String]]`, with the selection stored by value, so a rebuild is "clear children and re-mount from the Store's current value" and there is no row-level subscription to leak at all; the bag is left for the two column Store subscriptions, one per column. The cost of removing that layer of mechanism is that the selection is not part of a Store; the gain is that rebuild count and subscription count are decoupled.
- **`Store.set` does not check whether the value actually changed**: an empty move, with an empty selection, still calls `from.set(remain)` plus `to.set(merged)`, both Stores notify and both columns rebuild again. That is `Store`'s existing semantics — no deduplication, see `core/store.mbt` — and the component adds no "skip set when equal" check, since that would also block the legitimate "same value, still refresh the view" use. Tests must therefore be written to this semantics: re-take coordinates after any click that may trigger a `set`.
- **Two disciplines for "inject by coordinates plus rebuild-style list", hit in this batch**: ① A freshly rebuilt row **has no rectangle** until the next layout, so in headless tests any operation that may rebuild must be followed by a manual `root.relayout(...)`; the real window is unaffected because the host relayouts every frame. Missing it presents as "clicking does nothing", since a zero rectangle plus an offset hits somewhere else. ② In a merged injection round, **any click that changes layout must come after the widgets below it in the same column**. Here clicking the tree parent row first, expanding it by +64px, then clicking the transfer made both transfer clicks miss, leaving `xfer=3/1` unchanged; moving the tree click last gave `xfer=2/2`. The geometry line reports the **last frame's** rectangles, so the injection order must match it, otherwise it clicks a new position with expired coordinates.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **54/54** — 1 new transfer case: click a row to select, arrow moving items, selection cleared after the move so a second arrow click moves nothing, moving back in reverse, and an external data change rebuilding the column, including both relayout disciplines above. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings, `examples/native-app` zero warnings, `yoga-mbt` 92/92, repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` adding the transfer to the fifth column with the window at 1620×900 and `NATIVE-APP-NAV2` gaining the `xrow`/`xbtn` injection points — after reordering the 15 merged clicks to "click then move", `car=2 auto=11 date='2026-11-15' seg='分段乙' crumb='列表' page=3 step=1 fold='11' menu='报表' tab=1 tree=1 xfer=2/2`, exit code 0. Screenshot review: both columns outlined, squares at the row head, and the `›`/`‹` button directions correct.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Scroll container (yoga gaining relative-position offsets + `ui/scroll.mbt`)

- **Scroll translation lives in the layout layer, not the widget layer**: `position: relative` plus `top: -offset` moves the whole content block up, and a relative offset **changes placement only, not normal-flow occupancy** — the container stretches to the content's natural height and later siblings are unaffected, exactly the semantics scrolling needs. Both hit testing and drawing consume layout results, since the host takes absolute rectangles from `collect_abs` every frame, so the component layer needs no second coordinate conversion. To get here, yoga-mbt gained relative-position offsets: `top`/`left` take priority, the other end of the same axis is ignored when both are given, `auto` does not offset, percentages resolve against the parent's content box; **absolutely positioned items do not take this offset**, since their `top` is an inset measured from the padding box. All three are pinned in `relative_wbtest.mbt`.
- **Content must have `flex-shrink: 0`**: in CSS flex items shrink by default, so when the content is the only child it is compressed to the viewport height and never scrolls. This class of "a scrollable container whose content neither deforms nor scrolls" only shows up when you actually scroll once, which is why the case pins the geometry first with "20 rows × 20 high = content 400 / viewport 100 / max 300".
- **The scrollbar is an absolutely positioned child of the viewport, not a layer of color painted on it**: it sits at the right edge above the content, so on the hit path it is the deepest widget and a button inside a content row cannot steal its press or drag. The form where it is painted in the viewport's `on_draw` gets swallowed by content children's hits, and this "visible but unclickable" only shows when you actually click. The thumb length is the viewport-to-content ratio with a 16px floor so it stays grabbable, and dragging maps thumb center to pointer: `offset = clamp((y - thumb/2) / (bar height - thumb)) * max`. Dragging to the bar's midpoint measured `scr=171/320`, bit-for-bit with the hand calculation.
- **Geometry copied into state at the first frame's draw**: viewport height and content height both come from layout results and can only be read in the draw callback, as `self.rect.h` and the content child's `rect.h`, so `ScrollState.view_h/content_h` is refreshed each frame by the viewport's `on_draw`, and both the bar ratio and out-of-bounds clamping consume them. The cost is that **`max()` is still 0 before the first frame after mounting**, when the wheel does nothing; on the real window every frame draws so it goes unnoticed. Headless tests must `paint` once before asserting scrolling, which is written into the case comment.
- **One diagnostic mnemonic, which cost ten minutes here**: a missing closing bracket in a type, `children : Array[@core.Node>`, reports `Inline wasm syntax error: unknown operator ?STRING` plus `The type alias Array expects 1 argument(s), but is here given 5`, with the error spanning the whole signature and far from the site. When an error is semantically unrelated in that way — "Array argument count wrong", "Inline wasm" — re-read the signature's bracket pairing before speculating about language features. Control experiment: replacing the body with an empty one still reproduces the error, which locates the problem in the signature.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **58/58** — 4 new scroll-container cases: viewport/content geometry coming from layout with the wheel changing offset and clamping at both ends; content moving up as a block with the scrollbar above it, proven on the hit path; clicking the track jumping and dragging the thumb, with no tracking after release; content shorter than a viewport neither scrolling nor drawing a bar, proven per-pixel that the row background shows through. `moon test -p NoahLiu/yoga-mbt` **96/96** — 4 new relative-position cases: top translating without changing siblings or container size; left being negative while auto does not offset; on one axis top/left winning and only bottom/right measuring in reverse; percentages resolving against the parent content box with absolute items not taking the offset. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gaining a sixth column "scroll container" — a 190×120 viewport holding 20 rows of 22, geometry line gaining `NATIVE-APP-SCR` — wheel down three notches giving `scr=90/320` with the geometry line's `row0=1182,437`, that is the content's first row moved up 90 = 527-90; dragging the bar from top to middle giving `scr=171/320`, bit-for-bit with the hand calculation; exit code 0. Screenshot review: rows 7-11 visible after scrolling, rows clipped at the viewport edge, the right-edge thumb moving with the offset.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Overlay base (`core/overlay.mbt`) and the first three pieces (popover / dropdown / tooltip)

- **Three decisions for the host's overlay layer**: ① **An empty layer is invisible** — a `display:none` widget is on no hit path, so with no overlays open clicks fall through to content unchanged. Once the first layer opens it becomes visible and **relayouts immediately**, since the layer was previously invisible with a zeroed rectangle and its own origin cannot be computed without a pass; only then can overlays be placed as "window coordinates minus layer origin". ② **Dismissal on outside click happens on release** — both press and release are consumed by the layer so the click does not leak into content, but dismissal runs only on release: on press, the same click's release would re-hit the trigger and reopen the overlay just closed. Measured: the second click closed and reopened the menu, making the state look unresponsive. ③ **Overlay content is built when opening and detached when closed** — not in the content tree, not occupying space, no hidden state to sync. This is a different road from the pre-built plus visibility-toggled switch components: overlays are transient.
- **`popover_t`/`dropdown_menu` listen for the release outside the trigger**: the trigger's inner widgets run first, since a button consumes the press, and the toggle happens when the release bubbles up, so wrapping a button or a label both work. The normal "click the trigger again while open" path is consumed by the layer, so the component's `overlay_alive` branch is a fallback for programmatic delivery or a removed layer.
- **`tooltip_t` uses host-maintained hover state rather than bubbling motion**: a child may consume motion itself — this repository's button does, `Move => !is_off()` — after which an enclosing component receives no notification at all. Measured on the real window, "no tooltip appeared after 300ms of hovering" had exactly this cause. `Widget::set_hover` was therefore changed to **parent-chain semantics**, with a parent counting as hovered while the pointer is on a child, matching CSS `:hover`, and `on_hover_change` was added, fired by the host only when hover ownership flips. The tooltip component starts and stops its timer on that callback and works around whoever it wraps. The core case pins "three levels on the hit chain all count as hovered, siblings do not, repeated setting does not repeat the callback".
- **One difference from master, on record**: the old chain's `tooltip_t` was a GTK native tooltip via `ffi_view_set_tooltip`. The self-drawn stack has no native tooltip channel, so it became "open a self-drawn bubble after a hover delay" — the appearance stays controllable, following theme and corner radius, at the cost of owning the delay and the dismissal, going through `@core.set_timeout` and doing nothing without a host.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **62/62** — 4 new overlay cases: an empty layer not blocking content, clicking the trigger opening a layer and clicking again dismissing it, the overlay landing 2px below the trigger; clicking outside dismissing without leaking that click to content; the dropdown's 4 items including a 1px separator with the selection callback index and dismissal; the tooltip appearing only when the delay elapses, dismissing on leave, and not appearing if the pointer leaves before the delay. `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/core` **61/61** — 1 new: parent-chain hover semantics plus `on_hover_change` firing on flips, with repeated setting not repeating the callback. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gaining a "first overlay batch" column with the geometry line gaining `NATIVE-APP-OV` — injecting "click dropdown → click item 2 → click popover → click outside → hover on the tooltip target" gives `pick=2 ov=1`, where `ov=1` means the tooltip bubble was still open at exit, with the older readings unchanged, `car=2 auto=14 date='2026-11-15' … xfer=2/2`, exit code 0. Screenshot review: dropdown arrow pointing up, panel of four rows including one separator, overlay painted above content.
- **One environment fact on record**: this machine's monitor turned portrait mid-session, 1440×2560, so the example's seven side-by-side columns, about 1800px, exceeded the screen and the rightmost columns became unclickable. The accumulation page was therefore split into two rows of 4 plus 3 columns, window 1400×1260. **When a requested window size exceeds the screen the WM silently clamps it**, so taking coordinates purely from the geometry line injects into invisible regions, presenting as "some columns not responding at all".

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Overlay family close-out (dialog / toast / context menu) and three measured conventions

- **Dialogs open on the overlay layer**, a difference from master, on record: the old chain made the mask an **absolutely positioned layer inside the page**, one `Node` resident in the page tree, toggled by `set_visible`. This stack opens on the layer instead — a dialog must by nature cover all content and every other overlay, which is exactly the layer's semantics, and no hidden tree stays resident. The mask uses `overlay_show_full`, a wrapper with all insets 0, plus **explicit `width/height: 100%`**: relying on an inner `align-items: center` to fill is unreliable, since when content is wider than the window the mask size follows the content — measured with a 420 panel in a 400 window, where the mask came out 420 wide and could not cover the window.
- **`node_of_new`'s finish runs during construction**, so initialisation that needs the host already installed, such as "open a layer immediately from a Store", must use the explicit `mount` form, `{ mount: fn(parent) { ... } }`. In the test, `dialog_t(visible=true)` constructed before the host was installed made the open call land on an empty slot and fail silently, `overlay_count == 0`. On the real window the App installs the host while building the window, so only tests hit it, but a component treating "construction depending on a process-level single slot" as normal is fragile; this is now done at mount time.
- **Right-click dispatch changed to "ancestors first"**: in `dispatch_on_path`, `button == 3` walks from the root down to the deepest. A context menu is a container-level capability, so a wrapper must get it before the inner widget — otherwise the wrapped button consumes the press, since this repository's buttons consume `Down` regardless of button, and the menu never opens. All other buttons keep "deepest first".
- **Toasts open on the layer and the first one opens it**, a difference from master, on record: the old chain returned "layer node plus push function" and the caller mounted the layer into the page tree. This stack makes the top strip a layer entry, opened on the first push and closed when the last one is withdrawn, so **toasts always sit above dialogs** and the page needs no resident empty tree. The entry point is a single push function, a no-op without a host. Stacking order — later opened on top — is guaranteed by layer entry order, and the case asserts directly on the two entries' handle sequence.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **67/67** — 5 new: dialog opening on press; confirm and cancel both dismissing before calling back, with the Store going false; ✕ dismissing and mask clicks dismissing per `close_on_mask`; toast pushing one entry with width following the text, auto-withdrawing on time and closing the layer once empty; right-click popping at the pointer and calling back with the selected item; toast opening above the dialog. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` adding a "second overlay batch" column to the second row with `NATIVE-APP-OV2` — injecting "click dialog → click confirm → click toast → right-click → click menu item" gives `dlg=1 ctx=1 toast=1`, with `ov=0` at exit since the toast withdrew after 2 seconds, exit code 0. Screenshot review: dialog's translucent mask plus centred panel — title, ✕, body, cancel and confirm — and the top-centred green-check toast strip.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Four date pickers (`ui/datepicker.mbt`, date family 5/5)

- **Popups always open on the overlay layer**, the overlay base being used the moment it landed: both the calendar and the time panels are a single `overlay_show_at` layer, so dismissal on outside click and re-clicking the field are handled by the layer and the field respectively, and the component does not manage "dismissed from outside" itself.
- **The calendar panel and the grid reuse `datetime.mbt` directly**: `build_calendar`, all 42 cells built once with month changes rewriting data, and `range_state_of`, solid endpoints with a light run between, are shared by all four pickers, so `date_range_picker` is only "two-stage click plus write Store", a dozen lines. That is the payoff of extracting the grid math into a pure function.
- **Field interaction settled**: the whole field consumes the press, entering capture, and the release distinguishes three things by **local x** — clicking ✕ clears, offered only when `clearable`, hovered and holding a value, hot zone `width-40..width-20`; if open, dismiss; otherwise open the layer. Clearing does not fire `on_change`, matching master, whose callback signature takes a non-empty value.
- **Two differences from master, on record**: ① the old chain's popup was a native Popover; this stack uses a self-drawn panel on the overlay layer. ② The old chain's time entry was two `input_number` fields for hour and minute; this stack uses **steppers** — hour ±1, minute ±5, wrapping — because a self-drawn stack has no native input semantics and keyboard editing would need its own focus and input-method channel; for keyboard-editable multi-line text use `entry` and the upcoming `textarea_t`.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **71/71** — 4 new: date picker showing the placeholder, opening the calendar on click, filling and dismissing on selection, dismissing when the field is clicked again, clearing via ✕ after hover with clearing not calling back; date range writing the whole span on two-stage clicks and dismissing; time range stepper changing values with confirm writing back and cancel not changing; date-time range with four fields each writing their own, dates through the calendar and times through the stepper. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` adding a "date family pickers" column to the second row, `NATIVE-APP-DP` — injecting "click the date field → click the 1 October cell" gives `dpk='2026-10-01'`; "click the range field → 3 October → 7 October" gives `drg='2026-10-03~2026-10-07'`; "click the time field → click + → click confirm" gives `trg='10:00'`; exit code 0. Screenshot review: the calendar popup landing below the field, the time popup's hour/minute steppers with cancel and confirm.
- **One injection-coordinate discipline, hit again in this batch**: the time popup's two steps, clicking + and clicking confirm, missed entirely on the first pass, because the "container height to centre" calculation was off by one row — it landed on the "minute" row and the confirm click hit blank space right of the button. **Coordinates inside a popup must not be derived; re-read them from a screenshot or print that widget's rect.** Recomputing with "panel padding + row index × row height + half height" hit on the first try.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Table, first batch (`ui/table.mbt`: model + `table_t`)

- **Sort state belongs to the component, sort policy to the user**: on header click the component toggles `Store[TableSort]` and draws the arrow — a new column ascending, the same column flipping, a third click on the same column cancelling with `column = -1` — but **does not sort the caller's data**. Numeric order, lexicographic order or a custom comparison are business decisions, and the component doing it instead would be wrong; master's comment says the same and this batch keeps it. The sort arrow has two forms: a solid triangle for the current sort column, ascending or descending, and a grey ↕ hint on sortable columns while hovered.
- **Column width allocation extracted as the pure function `table_widths`**: fixed columns take their declared width, flexible columns, `<= 0`, share the remaining width, and when total width is short flexible columns take 0, so the table overflows rather than compressing fixed columns. Pinned directly by unit test without drawing a table.
- **Rows are a rebuild-style list**, same shape as `transfer`: a data Store change clears children and re-mounts from the new value, rows holding no subscriptions; selection and sorting affect **drawing only**, read in `on_draw`, so neither clicking to select nor toggling sort triggers a rebuild. Selection stores **source data indices**, not display order, so after reordering the selected row follows the data — steadier than master's display-position Ref.
- **Four cell kinds**: plain text aligned per column; semantic tag with a light base and primary text, same convention as the display family's `tag_of_type`; color swatch with swatch plus text; multi-line, at most two lines within the row height.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **75/75** — 4 new: column width allocation across the three situations; header column count, zebra striping, clicking a row writing the selection Store with the left accent bar appearing, clicking again cancelling, and the row callback carrying the source index; the header sort state machine's four steps with an unsortable column unresponsive to clicks; tag and swatch cells producing pixels plus a whole-table rebuild on data change. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gaining a table block, `NATIVE-APP-TB` — injecting "click the header twice, ascending then descending, then click row 2" gives `tsort=0/false tsel=1`, exit code 0. Screenshot review: header triangle pointing down, zebra striping, selected row with light blue background and left accent bar.
- **One discipline, with three same-class typos in this batch**: a nested generic missing one closing bracket, `@core.Store[Array[TableRow]>` where `]]` is correct, reports `The type constructor Store expects 1 argument(s), but is here given N` plus `Expected upper case identifier for type name`, with the error spanning the signature and unrelated to the real cause, a missing `]`. Adopted as a fixed self-check after this batch: grep for `]>` once nested generics are written. Two of the three were located by the control experiment "replacing the body with an empty one still reproduces the error, so the fault is in the signature".

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Virtual list and virtual table (ten-thousand-row shape)

- **Mount only the visible window**: fixed viewport, fixed row height; whenever the scroll offset changes the window is remounted from "first row = offset/row height − overscan", with one placeholder above and one below stretching the inner total height to rows × row height. Hit and draw depend only on mounted rows; 200 rows measured with only 10-13 row widgets mounted.
- **A placeholder is not a translation; both must be present** — a real-hardware defect: `examples/native-app`'s virtual table scrolled into "a white screen spreading downward from the top". The first version inserted an upper placeholder of `first × row height` when `first > 0` and did no relative positioning on the inner block, on the stated grounds that the placeholder also places the visible rows at the correct scroll position. **That reasoning is wrong**: without translation, row `i` always lands at `i × row height` below the inner origin, that is **exactly one `offset` lower than correct**, and the host clips to the widget's rectangle, `clip_rect` in `widget.mbt`, so the larger the offset the more visible rows are pushed past the viewport's bottom edge while its top empties out — precisely "whitening downward from the top". A placeholder only makes up the difference "first row of the window → content origin"; the actual offset must be carried by the content block's `position: relative` plus `top: -offset`, the same mechanism as `scroll_view`/`sticky_list`. The old form only looked fine when `offset` was a small exact multiple of the row height.
- **Pins must pin geometry, not mount count**: this defect survived a long time because the three existing unit tests asserted only "which rows are mounted and whether the inner total height is right", never that "a row's absolute rectangle lands inside the viewport". The added regression pin scrolls **1.5 rows**, since a non-integer offset exposes it most readily, asserting the content block's upward shift equals the offset and the first row's top equals the viewport top minus half a row, then scrolling deep to the bottom asserting five rows remain visible in the viewport. Acceptance checks for geometry-bearing components are always written as `rect` comparisons.
- **The scrollbar extracted from `scroll_v` for reuse**, `scroll_bar(state)`: track and thumb ratio, track-click jumping, press-drag and stop-on-release are written once and composed by both `scroll_v` and `virt_list`. The extraction hit a "script-style extraction" pitfall: slicing by line numbers duplicated the setup code, since the range from `let bar` to `append` already contained it, and `--deny-warn` immediately reported `unused dragging` — **re-run the gate after extracting**, since duplicated code and unused variables cannot hide.
- **Never rebuild the window inside `on_draw`**: the draw traversal is reading `kids`, so changing child widgets disturbs the iterator. Viewport height is therefore only **copied into state** in `on_draw`, and window rebuilds happen in event callbacks, `ScrollState.apply`, and in data subscriptions. Before the first frame has a real viewport height, the declared `height` is the fallback, since otherwise the first frame mounts only a few rows by overscan and looks empty.
- **When data shortens, clamp the offset before remounting**: the subscription first writes `content_h` from the new row count, pulls an out-of-range offset back to the upper bound, then rebuilds the window; skipping that leaves the view parked on blank space after deleting data.
- **Virtual table = fixed header plus `virt_list`**: the header does not scroll, and row widgets share one constructor with `table_t` — the header and rows were extracted from `table_t` into `table_header`/`table_row_widget`, both using them, after which `table_t` itself is left as "compose the header plus a rebuild-style row list". Header widths subtract the 8px scrollbar and the left and right borders so the columns line up with the data rows.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **78/78** — 3 new: a thousand rows mounting only the visible window, and after scrolling four notches the window's first row equals offset/row height − overscan = 4 with inner total height rows × row height; dragging the scrollbar changing the offset and shortened data clamping the offset back to the bound; the virtual table's header fixed and unscrolling, rows mounting only the visible window, header sorting and row selection on the same conventions as `table_t`. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gaining a virtual table block, `NATIVE-APP-VT` — injecting "wheel down three notches then click the list's middle" gives `vt=1/1` and `NATIVE-APP-VT mounted=13 total=200`, where **mount count far below total** is machine-checkable evidence that virtualization works, exit code 0. Screenshot review: rows 1-6 after scrolling, selected row with light blue background and left accent bar, right-edge thumb moving with the offset.
- **Fix-batch verification**: `moon test ui` **133/133**, including the new pin; `moon test core ui render text theme icons sys input win dbus chart mdview web` **865/865**; `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` zero warnings. Items needing real-hardware confirmation, awaiting user evidence: the process pages of `moon run examples/native-app` and `moon run examples/sysmonitor` — after a dozen-plus wheel notches the row content must keep following the scrollbar with no blank at the top edge; clicking a row to select and dragging the scrollbar must land consistently.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Table column resizing and sticky list (table 2/2, container and scrolling close-out)

- **Column widths are live**: `table_t`/`table_v_t` each hold a `Ref[Array[Double]]` of widths; dragging a header changes it, and both header cells and **the already-mounted row cells** change width on the spot with no tree rebuild. The virtual table relies on a `rev : Store[Int]` that makes `virt_list` remount the whole window, since visible rows are only a dozen or so and rebuilding is cheap. Drag semantics are "the two adjacent columns trade against each other", clamped to `[MIN_COL_W, total − MIN_COL_W]` with a 40px floor; the last column's right edge has no handle.
- **One seam only the real window exposed**: header cells consume the press themselves for sorting, so **edge dragging on a sortable column failed entirely** — the parent widget, the header, never received the press. Fix: a cell does **not consume** when local x is within 3px of either edge, handing the boundary back to the header. The unit test therefore deliberately pins a **sortable** column; written with an unsortable one it passed while the real window could not drag.
- **The sticky list's "current group" is inferred by reading layout results, not computed from the offset**: group height depends on content, since row count and wrapping can both change, so after each frame's layout read the group widgets' rectangles and take the last group whose start is `<= offset` into `StickyList.cur_group`; the sticky bar only draws it. The bar is an absolutely positioned floating strip inside the viewport, using the same relative-position translation as `scroll_v`, and scrolling plus the scrollbar reuse the shared piece.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **80/80** — 2 new: header boundary dragging changing column widths with adjacent columns trading off, out-of-range clamping to the minimum width, in-row cells following, and no tracking after release, using a sortable column; the sticky list changing the sticky title when scrolling past a group boundary, the content block moving up as a whole, and the scroll maximum being content height minus viewport height. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gaining a sticky list block and table dragging — pressing the header's 140px boundary and dragging right 80px gives `head0=24,521,200x40`, total width 240 minus the minimum column width 40, bit-for-bit with the hand calculation; wheel down five notches gives `sticky='组二'` with `NATIVE-APP-STK max=238`; exit code 0.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Split layout and text family, first batch (`hsplit`/`vsplit`, `TextRole`/`label_t`/`measure_text_height`)

- **Split-handle dragging changes styles only**: the old chain, master's `yue/splitter.mbt`, wrote `set_bounds` directly and double-wrote `width/flexbasis` styles — a GTK-era workaround for layout property changes at runtime not taking effect, see its probe-splitter entry. This stack relayouts from the root every frame and a style change takes effect next frame, so styles only. During a drag the host's **pointer capture** applies, since a press enters capture, so motion outside the handle is still delivered to it and displacement is computed in window coordinates.
- **Total length read from the three widgets' actual rectangles, without capturing the parent**: clamping needs "the two sides of the handle summed together", and the parent container must not be captured into a child's callback, since parent and child pointing at each other is a reference cycle. Changed to `first.rect + handle constant + second.rect`, semantically equivalent and cycle-free.
- **The first pane starts in percent and switches to a fixed value after dragging**: the initial `percent(ratio*100)` lets the first pane scale with the container without "measure once then compute", and after any drag it becomes `fixed(px)`, owned by the user from then on; the two ends have `min_first`/`min_second` floors clamped during dragging.
- **`TextRole` and `measure_text_height`**: a role folds size plus color into one — Title/Section/Body/Secondary/Accent — and `role_color` reads the theme at draw time rather than fixing it. `measure_text_height(text, role, width)` supplies an explicit height for labels that grow at runtime: the natural height a container queries need not match the height computed by wrapping at the box width during drawing, so an explicit height is steadiest — a pitfall recorded on the old chain, kept at the same convention here.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **85/85** — 5 new: measuring height by width, a wider box giving visibly more height, and larger role sizes giving taller rows; role sizes and colors, with Accent using the primary color; a themed label wrapping at `max_width` with an explicit color overriding the role color, proven per pixel; horizontal split handle dragging changing the first pane's width with two extreme clamps and no tracking after release; vertical split the same. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gaining a "split layout and text family" block with `NATIVE-APP-SPL` — pressing the handle and dragging right 100px gives `first=24,1236,788x116` / `split=788`, 688 plus 100, matching the hand calculation; exit code 0.
- **One window-size review discipline, hit again in this batch**: the example page has grown to about 1400px while the window was still 1260, so **the lower half of the page was outside the window**; injection points landed in invisible regions and nothing moved. Growing the window to 1500 first made it hit. **Every time a block is added to the accumulation page, check the window height against the last item in `NATIVE-APP-RECTS`** — a geometry line having coordinates is not proof the point is clickable.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Form family, first batch of five (`button_t`/`link`/`form_item`/`form`/`rate_t`)

- **Which pixel column the focus ring lands in**: `stroke_rect(0.5, 0.5, w-1, h-1)` with line width 1 puts the stroke centre at 0.5, covering the **second cell** of the x∈[0,1] column, so sampling at `ox` reads the background and misreports "the focus ring was never drawn" — this batch's first case failed falsely exactly this way. Sample at `ox+1`, or scan a column first to confirm where the ring is.
- **Out-of-bounds clicks do not hit the widget; do not use them as a clamping case**: `dispatch_pointer` performs hit testing first, `rect.contains`, so an event with x beyond the widget's width is never delivered to it and the `clamp` inside the callback cannot be verified. "Clicking the far right still gives the last star" must use the **innermost** right point instead, x=120 for a 126-wide rating; to genuinely exercise the out-of-bounds path use `dispatch_pointer_to(id, ev)`, which is how the host's pointer capture works.
- **`on_change` fires only on interactive input**: master attached the callback to `value.subscribe`, so external writes also called back. This stack standardises on "callback = the user's one action", the same convention as the date pickers, with external writes only repainting. Both semantics are defensible, but mixing them makes a caller think "writing the value myself delivered my own callback", so it is on record.
- **A form item's error row always reserves its height**: the error text row is a fixed 18 high, present even with empty text, so text appearing or disappearing causes no layout jump. Proven on the real window by `NATIVE-APP-FORM item=` rectangles being bit-for-bit identical before and after clicking "danger and report error". The text itself uses `label_dyn(err.signal())`: the Store's signal feeds the label directly, and text changes go through `relabel` for an in-place re-measure with no subtree rebuild.
- **Button width convention differs from master**: master measured text width manually via `get_bounds_for` at mount and added `+32` to set the width, then centred horizontally itself during drawing. Text measurement here already feeds the layout engine, `attach_text_measure` plus 12 left and right padding, so width is a layout result and drawing only centres within the box; that manual measurement is not needed.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **90/90** — 5 new: button color resolution across four variants plus hover, with an explicit override swallowing hover; a themed button's width following the text, release outside the box not counting as a click, the focus ring drawn only while focused, disabled not consuming; link width equal to text width, underline on hover, calling back only on release; form item label fixed width plus the error row's 18 reserved, empty text measuring 0 wide and re-measuring in place after a change; rating star vertex geometry, click writing the value and calling back, hover previewing without changing the value, leave clearing the preview. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gaining a "remaining form family" block with `NATIVE-APP-FORM` — injecting "click solid button → click link → click danger button, writing the error text → click the 4th star" gives `btn=2 lnk=1 rate=4 ferr=1`, with `item=24,1475,245x39` bit-for-bit identical to the unclicked round, exit code 0. Screenshot review: four button variants — solid with white text, light base with primary text, no base with primary text, red base with white text — the link's hover underline, right-aligned labels, five hollow stars.
- **Check window height against the last geometry item**: this batch's block sits at the bottom and the page had grown to 1542, so with a 1500 window the rating row was outside and clicks did nothing; growing to 1660 hit first try. Also watch the race between the auto-exit timer, 12 seconds, and "sleep first, then find the window" — sleeping past the deadline gets a destroyed window and reports `BadWindow`.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Dropdown select and color picker (`select_t`/`color_picker_t`, form family 13/15)

- **Ask an overlay handle for liveness, not for non-zero**: the id returned by `overlay_show_at` increases monotonically and is **never reused**, and dismissal on outside click is done by the layer, so the component's own `open_id` never resets. Testing `open_id.val != 0` therefore treats an **invalidated handle** as still open, and the symptom is "after clicking outside to close it, the field needs two clicks to reopen" — the first only clears the stale handle. Use `overlay_alive(open_id.val)` for the open decision, which internally asks whether `overlay_rect_of(id)` still exists. The `!= 0` guard in `close_pop` stays harmless, since hiding an invalid id is a no-op. `popover_t`/`dropdown_menu` were written this way from the start, while the four date pickers and this batch's two used the weaker check; all are now unified, each with a regression "after outside-click dismissal, one click on the field reopens".
- **Drawing a widget onto a bitmap must cancel its absolute placement**: `w.paint(p)` translates by `rect.x/rect.y`, and a bitmap sized to the widget is only w×h, so a popup row whose absolute y is in the tens to hundreds lands outside the buffer and pixel assertions become constant — the symptom was a false failure of "selected row same color as unselected". Use `w.paint_at(p, w.rect.x, w.rect.y)`, zeroing the translation so bitmap coordinates equal widget-local coordinates.
- **The popup list is wrapped in a `scroll_v`**: panel height follows a formula, `items×28+8` capped at 300, so many options never push the popup outside the window. Scroll geometry is still copied into `ScrollState` at the first frame's draw, see the scroll-container entry, so headless cases must `relayout` once before clicking.
- **`container`'s `padding` applies to left/top only**: it follows `Widget::set_padding(left, top)`, not CSS's four-sided padding. Measured on the swatch container: 176×72 rather than 176×80, with the bottom band covered by the popup panel's own fixed height. Reading it as four-sided writes the geometry assertion one cell off.
- **Three convention differences from master**: ① the popup is a self-drawn panel on the overlay layer, not a native Popover, and "click outside dismisses" is the layer's job, so the component stops tracking it. ② Master dismissed on field blur; here whether the field is focusable depends on the caller supplying `focus_id`, and dismissal goes only through "click outside" and "click the field again". ③ The dropdown's ✕ clearing **also** calls `on_change("")`, matching master, while the date picker's clearing does not, also matching master — both conventions are kept separately and are not an internal inconsistency.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **93/93** — 3 new: dropdown opening with list geometry, the popup landing 2px below the field at the same width with rows 28 high, an option click writing back and dismissing, the selected row's light base and right check producing pixels, ✕ clearing with a callback; dropdown "after outside-click dismissal one click reopens"; color picker swatch grid geometry, two rows of 5 plus 1 and a 176×80 panel, the selected cell having an extra stroke and white check versus an unselected one, differing by more than 20 per pixel, and clicking a swatch writing the value and dismissing. The date picker suite gained the stale-handle regression in step. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app`'s "remaining form family" block gaining a row with the dropdown and color picker, geometry line gaining `NATIVE-APP-FORM sel= col=` and status line `sel= col= ovmax=` — injecting "click dropdown field → click item 2 → click color field → click cell 2 → click dropdown ✕" gives `sel='选项乙/'`, selected then cleared, `col='#2E9E5B'`, and `ovmax=1`, the peak overlay count, recorded once per beat because it had already returned to zero at exit, so it proves a layer really opened; exit code 0. Screenshot review: the 5×3 swatch grid landing below the field and painted above content.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Multi-line input (`ui/textarea.mbt`, form family 15/15)

- **`focus_id` is only a declaration; the focus stack is aligned by the host against the widget tree, convention changed 2026-10-15**: what was recorded back then was "a widget carrying `focus_id` only means focusable, and `App` does not change focus on press if that id **is not in the focus stack**, so the example's new fields 21..24 had to call `app.focus.register(id)` to receive keys" — that discipline never made it into the library, and as a result nothing in showcase could type; see the keyboard-focus entry at the end of this section. The current convention: declaring `focus_id` puts it in the stack, via `Widget::focus_ids` → `FocusStack::sync`, aligned once before Down and once before Tab, and `register` is left for temporary focus targets that are not in the tree.
- **The correct way to inject keys with xdotool**: `xdotool key --window WID ...` uses XSendEvent and GTK does not accept synthetic events, producing the false picture "**every mouse injection lands, every keyboard injection does nothing**". Change to `xdotool windowactivate --sync WID` plus `xdotool windowfocus WID`, then `key`/`type` **without** `--window`, which is XTEST to the currently focused window, and the events arrive.
- **A Chinese input method swallows letters and arrows**: in the real window `type "cd"` did not reach the field, the letters going to fcitx to build preedit, while `Return` passed. The check is to look first at whether preedit appears; to prove ASCII typing, switch the input method to English mode first, reading the state with `fcitx5-remote -n` and **not using `-t`, which toggles**. The multi-line field's keyboard semantics are therefore covered mainly by white-box cases with `dispatch_key` delivered directly, while the real window evidences only click positioning, Enter newline and the wheel.
- **Up/down arrow landing takes "the rightmost code-point boundary not past x"**: written first as "strictly less than", which lost one character when moving between two equal-length lines, measured caret=1 instead of 2. Matching the single-field `byte_at_x` is the correct convention.
- **Advancing byte by byte then backing up a code point must check the end first**: `while at > ln.start && (bs[at] & 0xc0) == 0x80` reads out of bounds when `at == text length`, and the symptom was the test driver reporting only `SIGABRT (core dumped)` with no assertion visible in the stack. Added the `at < n` guard.
- **Do not use `j = hi` as the break inside a segment loop**: `wrap_units`'s inner while exited by pushing the cursor to the end, which swallowed the entire line into one segment — externally, **no width wrapped at all**. Replaced with an explicit exit flag, `let mut go = true`.
- **The appearance of caret following**: when the cursor lands in the last visible half-line the block moves up, measured 16px, so the first row is clipped in half. That is the normal result of `ensure_visible`, not a drawing bug, and should not be reported as one during screenshot review.
