- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **98/98** — 5 new: wrap break units — space, Latin word, CJK per character, with range truncation; display row layout — breaking on newlines, empty text giving one line, greedy wrapping leaving no leading space at a break, rows joined head to tail, Chinese breaking into three rows per character, an over-long word not split but overflowing; typing and Enter, up/down arrows moving by display row while remembering x, Home/End going to row start/end, Shift+Home extending then replacing, Backspace at row start joining rows; click positioning to a given row with Chinese counting the row start in bytes, drag selection across rows deleting whole lines, read-only refusing editing keys; a scrollbar only appearing once content exceeds the viewport, plus thumb and track swapping positions at the bottom and the caret scrolling into view changing the top row's pixels. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app`'s form block gaining a multi-line field, geometry line gaining `ta=` and status line `ta= tacur=`, with the example content changed to 8 lines — injecting "click row 3 inside the field, window y=1644" gives `tacur=12`, that row's start byte, bit-for-bit with the hand calculation; injecting `Return` gives `ta='行 1/行 2//行 3/…'` with `tacur=13`, one extra empty line; scrolling back to the top with the wheel, screenshot review shows three rows fully visible, the right-edge thumb back at the top and the caret-following 16px shift visible in an intermediate frame.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Declarative layer L1 constructors (`ui/declarative.mbt`: vbox/hbox/bind_label/hover_group/mount_window…)

- **`hover_group` needs no polling mechanism in this stack**: the old chain, `yue/declarative/hovergroup.mbt`, ran a global 100ms pointer poll, because GTK pointer events do not bubble and a child's GdkWindow takes events exclusively, leaving the ancestor container without enter. This stack's host hover state is **parent-chain semantics** already — a parent counts as hovered while the pointer is on a child, matching CSS `:hover`, see the tooltip entry — so the component just reads `Widget.hovered`: no timer, no pointer query, and no "do not fire callbacks while the group is stationary" optimisation to make. Recorded as a **mechanism difference**, not "same feature implemented".
- **`bind_label`'s forced relayout is free in this stack**: the old chain's `set_text` only marked dirty without relayout, so a longer label was truncated and had to be followed by `update_layout`. Here a text change goes through `relabel`, re-setting the measure callback and marking the node dirty, so the next frame's layout follows the new text automatically. Real-window evidence: one button click takes the label from 36px to 87px, `lblw=36/87`, with no subtree rebuilt.
- **`mount_window` provides no `center` / `on_close`**: the old chain's window centring and close callback went through the native window channel. Here window position is the WM's decision and closing only makes `App::run()` return, with cleanup after the caller's `run()`. Fewer honest parameters beat two fake ones.
- **Constructors sharing a component's name no longer wrap a second layer**: `label`/`button`/`entry`/`checkbox`/`container`/`group`/`separator`/`image`/`icon`/`radio_group`/`slider`/`progress` are already declarative constructors in `ui` returning `@core.Node`, so another same-named function only adds a signature to maintain. This batch adds three kinds only: renames — `vbox`/`hbox`/`text_edit`/`picker`/`scroll`/`tab`/`date_picker`; foundation entries — `mount_window`, `bind`/`bind_label`; new capability — `hover_group`. `overlay_scroll` is simply `scroll_v` here, since the scrollbar has always been an absolutely positioned child of the viewport; `gif` goes with the icon/animation batch; `cursor_group` needs a window-layer cursor channel, new FFI, so it is its own batch.
- **Three toolchain writings measured in this batch**: ① `test "name"` and the opening brace **must be on the same line**; splitting them makes the parser treat the body as a separate top-level block, throwing the error site dozens of lines away with unrelated meaning, `The value identifier tabs is unbound` plus `Parse error, unexpected token id`. ② `Option::is_none()` is deprecated on this toolchain, pointing at `x is None`; do not write it into new code. ③ A match guard is not `v when cond` but MoonBit's `| cond`; for a simple two-way branch, falling back to `if/else` is less trouble.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **103/103** — 5 new: vbox/hbox direction and spacing coming from parameters; bind_label changing text in place and re-measuring width after a value change, plus producing pixels; bind running a derived signal with subscriptions retiring in the disposal bag; hover_group's child hovering changing the whole group's background, with release outside the group not counting as a click; old-name constructors landing on the new components — picker opening an overlay and filling back, scroll producing a scrollbar with max>0, tab switching pages by Store. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gaining a "declarative L1" block, geometry line gaining `NATIVE-APP-DC` and status line `dcl= lblw=`, with the window grown 1760→1900 because the page lengthened again — injecting "click the `加一` button inside the card" gives `dcl=1 lblw=36/87`, so one Store change moves both label text and width, with `label=34,1377,87x19`; parking the pointer on the card's blank area and screenshotting shows the whole block taking the hover background.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Window-layer cursor channel (`wm_set_cursor` + `Widget.cursor` + `cursor_group`)

- **In a fully self-drawn stack the cursor is one window-level layer**: with no native widgets there is no "each widget carries its own cursor", and a shape can only be set on the drawing area's `GdkWindow`. The chain is therefore: a component declares a **request** on the widget, `Widget.cursor`, numbered `@core.CURSOR_*` — 0 default, 1 hand, 2 text I-beam, 3 horizontal resize, 4 vertical resize; the host takes "the **deepest non-zero request** on the hover path" on `Move`, and only calls FFI, `Window::set_cursor`, when the shape differs from the one already sent. Taking "deepest non-zero" rather than "deepest" lets a `cursor_group` wrapping a whole group fall back naturally: children that make no request use the group's, and a child that does wins.
- **One mechanism difference from master**: the old chain's `cursor_group` had to set the cursor **recursively on the group root and every descendant**, because GTK applies cursors per native event window, so a container setting alone cannot cover children with their own windows. Here one setting on the group itself suffices; the cost is that a child wanting to keep its own shape must state a request of its own, and stating it wins.
- **Two C-side guards**: `gtk_widget_get_window(area)` is NULL before realize, when there is no window to attach to, so it is skipped and the next hover retries; `WmWindow.cursor_kind` records the current shape, so repeated requests for the same shape do not create another `GdkCursor`, since `gdk_cursor_new_from_name` allocates each time and hover jitter would burn it. When the name resolves to nothing, a theme missing the glyph, it falls back to `default`.
- **Two toolchain writings**: ① `pub(all) enum PointerKind` **does not carry `Eq` automatically**, so `pev.kind == Move` does not compile, reported as `Type PointerKind does not implement trait Eq`; write `match pev.kind { Move => true _ => false }`. ② `pub(all) struct Rect`'s fields are likewise public, so tests read `w.rect.x` directly with no extra getter.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/core` **62/62** — 1 new `cursor_at`: inside a group falling back to the group, a child that stated a request winning, and both outside the group and empty space returning default. `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **104/104** — 1 new: hand on button/themed button/hover group, text shape on `entry`/`textarea`, horizontal/vertical on `hsplit`/`vsplit` handles, and `cursor_group` providing an overridable shape while children stay default. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` sampling the shape the host has sent once per beat, status line gaining `cur=手/文本/横向/纵向` — injecting "stop in order on the solid button → the multi-line field → the split handle → empty space" gives `cur=8/8/8/0`, the first three shapes each sampled across 8 beats, with the vertical one at 0 because the example has no `vsplit`; exit code 0. **The actual cursor shapes — whether the hand is the familiar pointer and the text shape is an I-beam — are for the user to re-verify on real hardware**, since injection can only prove the host really sent different numbers per region.
- **A disabled state's cursor request must be computed on hit; fixing it at tree build is guaranteed wrong** — real-hardware feedback: a disabled button still showed the hand. `Widget.cursor` is a one-shot `Int` written at tree build, while disabled state in this stack is a **cell**, `Enabled`, the settled convention in `state.mbt`, since a boolean fixed at build time makes every later `set_disabled` unable to move the frozen field. `button()`/`icon_button_t()` wrote `CURSOR_HAND` unconditionally, so disabled and enabled were indistinguishable on the cursor surface. The fix is not adding a "recompute the cursor" entry to every component but making the request itself computable: `Widget` gained `cursor_fn : Option[(Widget) -> Int]`, which **overrides the static `cursor` when present**, and `cursor_at` now evaluates per node through the new public method `Widget::cursor_request()`. Returning 0 still means "this widget requests nothing", so the query continues up the ancestors and `cursor_group`'s group semantics are unaffected. `ui/state.mbt` gained the private helper `enabled_cursor(cell, on)`, returning `CURSOR_DEFAULT` when disabled and `on` when enabled. Changed: `ui/basic.mbt`'s `button`/`icon_button_t`, `ui/form.mbt`'s `checkbox`/`switch_t`/`slider`/`button_t`; the stepper's two sides go through `button()` and are covered automatically.
- **Lesson: changing a field's semantics requires grepping the whole repository for that field's assertions, not just implementation call sites** — `ui/declarative_wbtest.mbt:151` asserts directly on a button's **static** `cursor` and went red on the spot, `0 != 1`, found by the user running `moon test core ui`. Grepping only the implementation side would miss it, since the assertion reads `.cursor` and is unrelated to the component's construction points. Checklist for this class of change: implementation write points → assertions reading that field → the field's public accessors, where adding `cursor_request()` was exactly to give assertions a semantically correct entry.
- **Verification**: `moon test core ui` **243/243** — new: 1 core case, with `cursor_fn` the computed result wins, overriding the static `cursor`, and a state change in the same tree takes effect on the next query; 1 ui case, the button cursor following the disabled cell, disabled requesting no hand and restoring enabled bringing it back immediately; plus one existing `declarative_wbtest` assertion corrected. Real hardware: a disabled button shows the ordinary arrow on hover and the hand returns immediately once enabled again.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Editable combo box (`combo`, declarative L1 close-out)

- **Composition: all editing semantics live inside that `entry`; this component adds only the candidate layer.** Filtering follows input, since `entry`'s `on_change` reopens the overlay; Enter taking the highlighted item uses `entry`'s `on_enter` hook; ↑/↓/Esc come from **keys bubbling along the ancestor chain**: `entry` does not consume those three function keys — the kernel's `handle_key` reaches `keysym_to_text`, gets None, `handled=false`, and the host keeps asking upward — so the enclosing `combo.on_key` receives them. This is the stack's first real division of labour on "ask the widget first, then its ancestors" for one key press, and it is worth recording: for a component to catch keys its child does not consume, no callback parameter is needed on the child, since the parent's `on_key` is that channel.
- **Open on release, same pattern as popover/dropdown**: `entry` consumes the press, since it must place the caret, and the same click's release bubbles to the wrapping layer, where `combo` opens the layer on `Up`. Clicking anywhere in the field therefore means "position the caret plus open candidates", with no extra arrow hot zone.
- **Highlighting does not rebuild the overlay**: a candidate row's selected state is a closure reading live, `fn() { hi.val == idx }`, so ↑/↓ only change `hi` and call `invalidate()` without remounting the popup content; only a changed filter result reopens it, `close()` plus `overlay_show_at`.
- **Overlay ids increase monotonically, and miscounting in a test crashes**: every `overlay_show_at` issues a new id and closing does not recycle numbers, so an assertion about "the Nth time a layer opens" counts **openings**, not the current layer count. Counting wrong gives `overlay_root_of(nonexistent id)` a None, the test helper falls back to an empty widget, and the next `children()[0]` goes out of bounds — the symptom is the test driver reporting only `SIGABRT (core dumped)` with no assertion in the stack, measured once in this batch.
- **One difference from master**: the old chain's combo was a native editable combobox, GTK `ComboBoxEntry`; this stack is entirely self-drawn, with the overlay on the overlay layer and outside-click dismissal also the layer's job.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` **105/105** — 1 new: click the field opening the layer with the full candidate list → `dispatch_commit` of `甲` filtering to two rows and reopening automatically → the highlighted row's light base and check producing pixels, with the down key moving the highlight to another row → Enter filling the highlighted item, closing the layer and calling back → reopening with only one row left, Esc closing without changing the value → filtering to an empty set not opening. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app`'s form block adding `combo` to the dropdown row, geometry line gaining `cmb=`, status line `cmb='…'`, focus id 25 registered — injecting "click the editable combo field → click item 3" gives `cmb='组件丙'`, exit code 0. A second round of four clicks, "open → item 2 → click the field again → click the old row-3 position", ends at `cmb='组件乙'`: on the second opening the current text is already `组件乙`, filtering leaves one row, and a click at the old third-row position naturally falls outside the popup — exactly the expected behaviour of "filter as you type", not a lost click.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Scaled drawing fix and GIF animation (`cr_blit` rewrite + `Animation` + `gif`/`icon_button_t`)

- **`cairo_pattern_set_matrix`'s scaling path was measurably wrong — the real bug fixed in this batch**: the old form put "source pixel → device pixel" into the pattern matrix, `translate(d0,d1)` plus `scale(k)`, while Cairo's semantics are the opposite of that intuition. With a (20,20)-(99,99) square in a 120×120 source scaled to 72, the pattern-matrix route gave (33,33)-(71,71), pushed to the target rectangle's bottom-right and clipped, while the CTM route — identity → translate → scale → `set_source_surface` → filling with the sub-rectangle size — gave the correct (12,12)-(59,59). **At equal size, target matching source, the two routes coincide**, which is why the error stayed hidden: `draw_image`'s and `draw_canvas`'s scaling branches had no case coverage at all. The diagnostic order is worth copying: first prove, on the MoonBit side with a **fully opaque composite**, that it does draw — all 2304 cells hit; then switch to a **source with a transparent region** to reproduce "drawn wrong"; finally move the whole blit into a standalone C program comparing three formulations, parent surface plus matrix, CTM transform, sub-surface plus matrix, locating it in one pass.
- **Changing the stub library leaves `moon run` artifacts unlinked too**, previously recorded for the test exe only: `build/librender_cairo_stub.a` was 13:50 while `native-app.exe` was still 13:39. MoonBit sources did not change, so moon considered the artifact current — white-box tests all green while GIFs stayed blank in the real window. Delete `_build/native/debug/build/NoahLiu/native-gui/examples/<name>`, noting that `moon run`'s executable lives under `build/`, not `execbin/`. **Acceptance check**: compare the `.a` and `.exe` mtimes; "just ran it" does not mean "is new".
- **GdkPixbuf's animation iterator starts lazily and only knows absolute times**: the first call to `gdk_pixbuf_animation_iter_advance(iter, t)` only anchors the animation start at `t` and necessarily reports "frame unchanged"; afterwards switching is decided entirely by the loader from accumulated time. So this layer's virtual clock **advances only "current frame duration plus 1ms" per beat**, at the same rate as real time, and components ask repeatedly at their `delay_ms` cadence. Written earlier as "push four beats inside one call", the animation ran four times too fast.
- **This machine's gif loader cannot read `tDelay`**, measured as NULL against PIL's reported 400ms, so it falls back to 100ms-per-beat polling; because frame switching is decided jointly by the virtual clock and the loader, it still changes frame every 400ms in practice — 12 seconds of real window giving `gif=30` frames, about 2.5 frames/second, matching the asset's per-frame durations.
- **Both `loop` and `static` are MoonBit reserved words**: the parameter name `loop~` fails to parse, changed to `looping~`, and the struct field `static` triggers a `reserved_keyword` warning, changed to `is_static`.
- **Sampling point for the icon button's hover background**: a `fill_round_rect` with radius 4 clips the corner cell, so the pixel assertion takes the top edge midpoint, `(w/2, 2)`; `(1,1)` reads "no change".
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/render` **42/42** — 1 new scaling regression, with the same source image's opaque bounding box at target sizes 120/72/48 being (20,20)-(99,99)/(12,12)-(59,59)/(8,8)-(39,39), plus `draw_image_from_rect`'s sampling domain not overflowing. `moon test -p .../gui/ui` **107/107** — 3 new: the animation component self-advancing by frame, pause breaking the chain, `play` resuming, a static image not scheduling rotation, and 48×48 scaling really producing ink; icon button sizing, hover changing the base, release outside the box not counting as a click, disabled not consuming. `core` 62/62, `yoga-mbt` 96/96, nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gaining an "icons and animation" block, geometry line `NATIVE-APP-MEDIA`, status line `gif=`/`ib=` — injecting "click the icon button" gives `ib=1` and `gif=30`, the self-advanced frame count, exit code 0. Screenshot review: icons following the theme color, the ✕ icon button, and the 48×48 GIF dots really drawn inside the box, previously blank.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Theme following the system (`theme_from_system` + `App::follow_system_theme`) and the style-channel decision

- **The theme package does not depend on the platform layer; the following logic lives in the window layer**: `theme` takes only two reading functions as parameters, `theme_from_system(sys_color_scheme, sys_accent)`, while the real probes are in `win` and the polling plus `theme_apply` in `core/app.mbt`, as `App::follow_system_theme(interval_ms)` returning a stop function. The theme package therefore stays platform-free, so `core` depending on it forms no cycle, and the follow policy is testable headless with fake readers covering four states. Same reasoning as `local_ymd`: platform probes are forwarded through core, so examples and the integration layer need not import `win`.
- **What is read is the desktop environment's gsettings, not a native widget stylesheet**: `org.gnome.desktop.interface`'s `color-scheme` first, counting only when the value contains dark or light, falling back to the `gtk-theme` name, normalised and searched for dark/light; the accent reads `org.gnome.desktop.wm.preferences button-settings` if it holds a literal `#rrggbb`, or `accent-color`, where GNOME returns **names such as blue/teal** and this layer maps them to hex. **`g_settings_schema_has_key` must come before any read**: this machine's schema has no `accent-color` key at all, and calling `g_settings_get_string` directly prints a GLib critical warning. The GSettings object is created once and kept, since creating and destroying it each beat would re-walk dconf.
- **Measured reading on this machine, Ubuntu 24.04 plus XFCE**: GNOME schemas are installed — `gsettings list-schemas` lists 38 `org.gnome.desktop.*` — with `color-scheme='default'`, neither dark nor light, so it falls to `gtk-theme='Orchis-Teal-Light-Compact'`, which contains light after normalisation, reported as "light"; `accent-color` has no such key so the accent is an empty string. `theme_from_system` therefore takes "light plus built-in accent", matching the base palette, and the real-window status line evidences `sys='light/'`, `fing=#2D68C4/#F5F6F7`. **Acceptance check**: the follow loop calls `theme_apply` only when the **fingerprint**, `primary/bg_page`, changes, so a desktop that yields nothing produces the same value every beat with zero repaints.
- **Style-channel decision: this stack does not do a CSS-style stylesheet.** master's five helpers — `themed_container`/`set_panel_bg`/`bind_bg`/`bind_fg`/`bind_popover_bg` — existed because native widgets' background and text colors were set imperatively as fixed values that did not update with the theme. Components here read the palette in `on_draw`, and a theme change repaints globally through one process-level subscription, `watch_theme`, so **the five helpers are structurally unnecessary**. Callers overriding size, spacing or background have two more direct routes: the components' typed parameters — `width=`/`bg=`/`padding=`… — or `handle=fn(w){ ... }` to reach the underlying widget and set yoga styles directly, which is this stack's style escape hatch and more type-safe than maintaining a string style table. `sub_bag` batch unsubscribe was long since implemented in `core/signal.mbt` and is covered repeatedly by the component batches, whole-generation retirement in rebuild-style lists.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/theme` **8/8** — 1 new: the fingerprint relations across the four states of dark/light and accent — reading nothing and reading light share a fingerprint, dark differs from light, an accent provided goes through the derivation formula and matches `theme_from_accent`, and after `theme_apply_system` both getters and the fingerprint follow the new snapshot. `ui` 107/107, `core` 62/62, `render` 42/42, `yoga-mbt` 96/96, nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` starting `follow_system_theme(interval_ms=1000)` and stopping it at 3 seconds to verify the stop function's ownership — status line gaining `sys='light/'` and `fing=#2D68C4/#F5F6F7`, `frames=118` and other readings unchanged, exit code 0. **Whether the interface recolours immediately when the system theme genuinely switches** is for the user to re-verify on real hardware, observing with `gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme prefer-dark` temporarily; the assistant does not change desktop settings.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Charts, first batch (`chart`: algorithm layer + line/bar/donut/gauge/scatter)

- **A new package rather than editing `yue/charts` in place**: the old directory references the `@yue` root package and the old Painter contract and belongs to the repo's error backlog; the new stack must keep the per-package gate "this package `--deny-warn` zero warnings", which becomes impossible once mixed, for the same reason as `yue/components` → `ui`. Three layers in the new package: `algo.mbt`, pure functions same-source as master — rolling window, coordinate conversion, 1-2-5 ticks, unit stepping, bar slot and hit, sector angles, gauge radians, least squares, range padding, truncation; `draw.mbt`, drawing consuming only pure-function results; `components.mbt`, the `@core.Node` components.
- **The pixel acceptance check changed**: chart components lay a panel base first in `on_draw`, so "count of inked pixels, alpha>0" always equals the whole area — this batch's 5 cases all failed falsely for exactly that reason. New check: **compare two bitmaps pixel by pixel**, `diff_of`, used both for "the picture changed after new data" and for "restored after leaving", the latter asserting the difference is exactly 0. This holds for every "base first, then content" component, not only charts.
- **Dense polyline drawing cost decoupled from window size**, master's decision kept: decimate by pixel column, taking (x, y_min, y_max) per column so extremes survive; area mode fills one rectangle per column down to the anchor line, the fill's top edge being the polyline with no separate stroke, while line mode draws a min..max vertical bar per column. Only sparse data, point count ≤ column count, takes a true polyline plus polygon area. Basis: under software rasterisation each stroked segment costs about 1.8µs, and 1000 points × 4 series fully stroked exceeds the 5ms acceptance line.
- **Donut hit is newly written as `donut_hit`**, sectors tested in polar coordinates with center and radius formulas same-source as `draw_donut`, giving -1 inside the hole and outside the circle. Bar hit still uses master's `bar_hit`, sharing the slot-width formula with drawing so highlight and bar never disagree.
- **Reuse `ui`'s foundation instead of re-copying**: `follow_store`/`watch_theme`/`text_width`/`fill_round_rect`/`default_handle` were made `pub` for the chart package. They were package-private inside `ui`, so the chart package would have had to copy subscription logic, and `watch_theme`'s "subscribe once per process only" is exactly the part that must not be duplicated.
- **Four toolchain writings measured in this batch**: ① `pub const` names **must be uppercase** — `pub const pi` reports "Expected upper case identifier for name of const, found lower case. Did you mean let?"; use `pub let` for a lowercase name. ② `for i = 1..<n { }` is unsupported: a range is legal only in `for x in a..<b`, so the classic for is `for i = 1; i < n; i = i + 1`. ③ `StringBuilder`'s write methods are `write_string`/`write_char`; there is no `add`/`append`. ④ The `Ordering` type cannot be referenced directly on this toolchain — writing a comparator reports "The type Ordering is undefined" — so ordering a few elements fell back to insertion sort.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/chart` **11/11** — 6 pure-function: window dropping the oldest and out-of-range being a no-op, degenerate range and padding ratio, 1-2-5 step with a negative interval start, unit stepping k/M/G, bar slot and both hit forms, sectors accumulating positives only with a single sector keeping 0.0002 radians, gauge segment coloring and polyline segment count, regression degeneration, 8-digit color strings, label truncation. 5 component: line changing output with new data and dense decimation, bar hover changing the base and restoring on leave, donut drawing plus four-state hit, gauge's two smooth paths — jumping straight to the value versus approaching per beat — scatter with a trend line. Nine packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gaining a charts block — line plus bar on one row, donut plus gauge plus scatter plus a push-point button on another, geometry line `NATIVE-APP-CH`, status line `ln=`/`chp=` — injecting "click the push button three times" gives `ln=27/23 chp=3`: window 24→27 points, last value 7→23, bit-for-bit with the hand-calculated `pushes*7%29+2`, exit code 0. Screenshot review: all five charts present — line with area fill and the latest value labelled at the right end, bar with opposite colors for positive and negative plus categories, donut with a centre summary plus a right legend showing percentages, gauge's 68% arc with the centre number, scatter with a least-squares trend line.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · sys batch 3 (hardware family, six pieces: brightness / volume / nightlight / printer / powerprofile / monitor)

- **Dependency injection removes the DBus coupling**: brightness's write path, logind online probe plus SetBrightness, went through `@traybus` in master. In the new stack the two places became **process-level injection slots**: `brightness_set_logind_probe(()->Bool)` and `brightness_set_action((subsystem,name,value)->String)`, an empty string for success and a non-empty error string. Once the DBus line is wired, traybus injects the real implementation. The read path — device enumeration, current value, maximum, pure sysfs — does not use the slots. Same pattern as `ci_tooltip`'s callback inversion: **the semantic layer defines the slot, the platform layer injects it**.
- **monitor moved up ahead of the session family**: nightlight's display enumeration depends on monitor, xrandr, and monitor depends only on platform plus pr_run with no DBus, so by dependency order it belongs to this batch.
- **Three pieces kept on the DBus line**: `sensor`, iio-sensor-proxy, and `bluetooth`, org.bluez, both use `@traybus`'s general D-Bus property reads; `disk` uses `@traybus.gdbus_call_system` in 50 places, UDisks2. Their core is bus calls rather than command lines, so this batch does not force them apart.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/sys` **41/41** — 11 new: monitor's xrandr parsing matrix, plus the pr_run command surface and parsing pure functions ported same-source across six files; brightness's set going Unsupported while no slot is injected, and the read path against real local sysfs. `moon check sys --deny-warn` zero warnings; repo-wide still 287/68. **Real-hardware re-verification**: volume increase and mute, brightness reading the current value, powerprofile listing and switching, printer enumeration, nightlight color temperature taking effect, monitor resolution list.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · sys batch 2 (`sys/dialog.mbt`: file dialogs)

- **The GTK side belongs to the win stub, the semantic layer to the sys package**: the `GtkFileChooserDialog` wrapper lives in `win/gtk_stub.c` under the `wm_file_*` prefix, with a slot table under the same discipline as the window stubs, since a dialog needs a GTK parent window and the file is already compiled into the GTK link unit by prebuild. `sys/dialog.mbt` is a thin semantic wrapper only: filters passed through as strings, option bits, run/read-result/destroy. The sys package **does not import win** — `run_for_window`'s parent is a plain handle id, Int64, so there is no symbolic dependency at the MoonBit level, but linking needs `-lyue_win_stub`, and `scripts/prebuild.py` issues link_configs to the sys package **separately**, with the same GTK library list as win.
- **Querying a chooser that never ran segfaults, measured locally**: `gtk_file_chooser_get_uri` raises SIGSEGV directly while its internal file system model is uninitialised. The stub adds a `wm_dlg_accepted` flag and permits queries only after `gtk_dialog_run` returns ACCEPT, giving an empty string in every other case. Same GTK assertion family: `set_current_name`, and set_filename, is legal only for the SAVE action, so calling it on an OPEN dialog prints Gtk-CRITICAL.
- **The degraded path with no display**: `wm_file_dialog_new` calls `gtk_init_check` first and returns handle 0 on failure, which is the wbtest case with no X connection and CI. Every interface no-ops on handle 0 without crashing; with a display, as locally, objects really are created and the tests assert both paths.
- **The third crime scene of "stub changed without relinking"**: after editing gtk_stub.c, `moon test` reported undefined reference — `build/libyue_win_stub.a`'s mtime was newer than the source, and this batch's test artifacts were not relinked either. The acceptance check is comparing `build/*.a` against the test exe's mtime; delete both `_build/native/debug/test/.../gui/sys` and the stub library to force a rebuild. Same root cause as the G-batch stub lesson — moon's incremental build being unreliable for C source changes is by now the normal state.
- **`get_uri` returns a percent-encoded string and Chinese directories break** (2026-10-16 user feedback on real hardware): `wm_file_dialog_get_result` used to take `gtk_file_chooser_get_uri` and strip the `file://` prefix by hand, so choosing the 下载 directory returned `/home/lkyh/%E4%B8%8B%E8%BD%BD`, and the example handing it to `fsx_list_dir` got `FsError::OpenFailed`. Paths with spaces, `#` or `%` behave the same, and the save dialog's initial directory takes the same fall. Changed to `gtk_file_chooser_get_filename`, the already-decoded local UTF-8 path from GTK; for trash or remote URIs with no local filename it returns an empty string, the same convention as Windows' `SIGDN_FILESYSPATH`. The `wm_dlg_accepted` guard from the previous item stays, since querying without running still segfaults. **Verification**: `moon test ./sys` **187/187**, with mtime checked per the "stub changed without relinking" entry — `gui/build/libyue_win_stub.a` newer than `gui/win/stub.c`, and the sys test exe newer than that `.a`. Real-hardware re-verification: choosing a Chinese directory and a directory with spaces → the playlist shows entries.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/sys` **30/30** — 1 new: dialog create/configure/release on both paths, with a display really creating, configuring and destroying objects, and with no display every interface no-opping; modal run and really selecting a file are left to real hardware. `moon check sys --deny-warn` zero warnings; repo-wide still 287/68. **Real-hardware checklist**: triggering the open dialog from the app → selecting a file → result path correct; the save dialog's initial name taking effect; the filters dropdown grouping correctly.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · sys batch 1 (`sys`: fsx / envx / procrun)

- **The sys stub goes straight through native-stub**: directory enumeration with dirent, environment variables with setenv/unsetenv, text read/write with fopen, and file removal use only standard headers, so they do **not** need the "prebuild compiles a static library plus a portable stub" arrangement used by win/render/text — that exists because those need GTK headers, which native-stub cannot reach through pkg-config. The single file `sys_stub.c` splits by platform with `#if` at the top, the Windows branch being a stub with the FindFirstFileW wide-character routing deferred to M2, and `moonbit_make_bytes` is declared `extern` and links the runtime symbol directly, as in ime_probe_stub.
- **`sys_getenv` reads through the C layer rather than core/env**: after an in-process setenv the value must be **immediately readable**, master's test convention, while core/env's environment table is a start-up snapshot in some implementations. Reads needing live semantics go through the stub; pure reads may still use core/env. The stub also landed `sys_read/write_text_file`, `sys_remove_file`, idempotent, and `sys_platform()`, decided by compile-time `#if`, the equivalent of master's `@yue.platform()`.
- **procrun changed only its dependency surface**: `@yue.read_text_file/ffi_remove_file/platform` → this package's three `sys_*`; `@subproc`, chensuiyi/subproc, is already a main-module dependency, and `pr_run`'s whole chain — spawn, bounded reclaim, capturing through a temp file, C locale — is unchanged.
- **Porting pitfalls**: the old wbtest's root-package helpers `utf8_bytes/from_utf8_bytes` → `@utf8.encode/decode_lossy`; after replacing `ffi_getenv_bytes`'s output `ok` Ref assertion pattern with the `Option`-returning `sys_getenv`, the leftover `inspect(ok.val)` on a neighbouring line had to go too — changing a signature without clearing assertions is a compile-time blow-up.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/sys` **29/29** — fsx: enumerating a real directory including a temp file, `..` excluded, the unopenable branch; flat text decoding; in-process write-read-modify-delete round trip with overwrite=false preserving, idempotent delete and `a=b` rejected. envx: single-key read against core/env, the common set collected only where present plus a full XDG_* sweep, error branches. procrun: `pr_available`/`pr_run` with a real subprocess round trip — `echo`, non-zero exit with stderr captured, timeout kill, the `/bin/sh` script path. `moon check sys --deny-warn` zero warnings; repo-wide still 287/68.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Markdown view (new package `mdview`, component library closed out)

- **A new package rather than reusing the old directory**: master's `yue/markdown` depends on the `@yue` root package, the error backlog; the new stack follows the "one folder one package" convention at `mdview`, with `mizchi/markdown@0.8.3` already a main-module dependency so the new package imports it directly. The pure-function layer — flattening, range metrics, footnote scanning, line splitting — was ported with zero difference from master; the rendering layer switched to the component surface, `@ui.hbox/vbox/label/separator/checkbox/code_view`, `@render.Image`, `@text.AttributedText`.
- **Link opening changed to an `on_link` callback**: master's rich-text row click called `@yue.open_url` directly. In the new stack open_url belongs to the system-capability line, the desktop integration family still to be ported, so `markdown_view` gained an `on_link? : (String) -> Unit` parameter threaded through `MDCtx` into the rich-text row closure — **the first version used a process-level single slot and was changed to ctx threading because multiple instances overwrote each other**. A struct's function field must be applied as `(ctx.on_link)(u)`; writing `ctx.on_link(u)` reports "has no method".
- **Rich-text rows' theme following is cached by fingerprint**: rebuilding an AttributedText cannot happen every frame in on_draw, since animation frames would rebuild repeatedly, nor only at construction, since link and code colors must follow the theme. `on_draw` compares `@theme.theme_fingerprint_of(theme_current())` and rebuilds only when the fingerprint changes.
- **Block spacing strategy changed**: master gave each block its own marginBottom through style strings. `@ui.hbox/vbox` here has only four-sided padding and no padding_bottom parameter, so block spacing is handed uniformly to the outermost `vbox`'s `row_gap`, with individual blocks' bottom space via `node.set_margin_bottom(@yoga.fixed(...))`.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/mdview` **26/26** — 24 pure-function/flattening/range/GFM assertions ported same-source: UTF-16 metrics and emoji, footnote numbering order, reference-style link definitions, strikethrough and superscript ranges, fence info's first word, line splitting, image path stripping `file://`, and the table alignment mapping rewritten as `is` pattern assertions since the yoga enums do not implement Eq. 2 component mounting: a full GFM document — headings, bold/italic/strike, links, task list, ordered list, blockquote, code block, table, rule, definition list, footnote — with a subtree over 5 nodes and height grown by content; a link click callback not crashing. `moon check mdview --deny-warn` zero warnings; repo-wide still 287/68. The real window's geometry line confirms layout, `md=24,2745,420x403`, with appearance left to the user on real hardware. **With this, all ten component families plus Markdown are closed out.**

### MoonBit native GUI stack · code_view syntax highlighting (`ui/codeview.mbt`)

- **Tokenizer ported verbatim, component reshaped**: `Token`/`lang_keywords`, the 8-language keyword tables/`tokenize_lang`/`classify_word` are same-source and unmodified from master's `components_text.mbt`, since the toolchain writings were already the new convention. `code_view` changed from "AttributedText pre-layout plus draw_attributed_text" to "measure each token at construction with `@ui.text_width` → draw each segment in on_draw with `@text.draw_box_at`". The old chain's whole-run coloring, working around Windows' AttributedText range-color defect, is structurally unnecessary here, since self-drawing produces directly; line height comes from `@text.line_height_font`.
- **Counting pixels of a single solid color is a fragile assertion**: 13px small monospace glyphs, such as the keyword "fn", can end up with **no solid-color pixel in the glyph core** after subpixel anti-aliasing — measured `purple=0` in this batch while a 6-character Chinese string gave `green=22`. Component pixel assertions therefore count total ink against the background; per-color assertions are reliable only for large solid areas, chart sectors and color bands.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Specialised charts batch 4 (`chart`: effectscatter / themeriver / geo, chart line closed out)

- **Two clashing meanings of 8-digit color strings, measured in this batch**: the old chain's charts used `#AARRGGBB`, alpha first, see the "yue color values and three drawing pitfalls" entry, while this stack's `@render.Color::parse` reads 8 digits as **RGBA, alpha last**. `eff_alpha_color` feeding 8-digit input straight to `@theme.parse_hex` treated the alpha byte as red — `#ff009688` parsing to r=255, which is the root cause of `"#ffff0096" != "#ff009688"`. Fix: for 8-digit input, **strip the leading two alpha digits and parse the remaining six**, matching the old chain's "RGB is never rewritten" semantics, with the new alpha recomposed from the parameter.
- **Ripple animation moved from "callback returns false to unregister" to a real handle**: the old chain's `set_timer` had no cancel id and stopping relied on the callback returning false. This stack's `@core.set_timeout`/`clear_timeout` return real handles, so `EffAnim` holds `running + timer` and `eff_stop` cancels the pending callback immediately — the same continuation pattern as carousel auto-advance, where the callback schedules the next beat.
- **GeoJSON parsing goes through `@sys`**, with `vsc_json_parse` already ported there, and `RectF` became a local `GeoRect`, shaped like treemap's `TmRect` with each defined on its own. `argb_hex` sat in the old chain's root package among the errors, so the chart package implements it locally with `Int::unsafe_to_char` assembling hex, noting that `Char::from_int` is deprecated.
- **Three test lessons, all hit in this batch**: ① `ink_of` on a "panel base laid first" component always equals the whole area — the charts batch's pitfall — and the headless default theme's bg_panel is **pure white** `#FFFFFF`, so white counts as ink; assert content through **characteristic-color sampling** or `diff_of`. ② themeriver reserves 240px for the legend, so the canvas must exceed 298 to have a drawing area, against the component's default width 560; a narrow canvas test exits early on the whole drawing with no error at all. ③ **Hand-written JSON in tests should be run through an external validator** — this batch's coordinate array had one extra `]`, the parser correctly returned None, and it was briefly misjudged as a parser bug. When all chunked bisections pass but the complete string fails, suspect the string first.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/chart` **189/189** — 43 new: three wbtest files ported same-source, 40, plus 3 component mountings — ripple changing with data with eff_stop leaving is_running=false; river changing with a new series, canvas 560; map parsing plus regional flight lines producing pixels plus clearing changing. Package `--deny-warn` zero warnings; repo-wide still 287/68. The real window's geometry line confirms layout, `eff=24,2542,300x170`, with visuals left to the user on real hardware. **With this, the chart line is closed out: 15 specialised charts plus five general chart types plus the interaction layer.**

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Specialised charts batch 3 (`chart`: sunburst / graph / parallel / pictorialbar)

- **Same routine as batch 2**: a conversion script handles dependency name replacement, and three classes of segments are rewritten by hand — the "no data" block, `draw_text` with conditional alignment, and the component layer's mount blocks. pictorialbar's 4 places omitted the `wrap=` parameter, which the regular expression required, so they were missed; calls that leave out a default parameter also need hand edits. The sunburst's centre summary, 20px SemiBold plus a 「总计」 caption, uses the same `@text.draw_box_at` form as `draw_donut_core`.
- **Same-field structs in one package make a literal ambiguous as "Multiple possible record types"**: `SunItem`/`TreeItem`/`TmItem` all have the shape `{name, value, children}`, so a literal cannot disambiguate — go through `make` plus `children.push`, whose array field contents are mutable. The same applies across packages, a batch-2 pitfall reproduced here and settled as the general convention.
- **Positional passing to optional parameters is restricted**: `GraphNode::make(name, value? : Double)` and `GraphEdge::make(s, t, weight? : Double)` **cannot take optional parameters positionally** — `make("甲", 30.0)` reports requires 1 positional arguments — so always name them: `value=30.0`, `weight=5.0`. `SunItem::make`'s `value? : Double?` is a double Option, so a number must be wrapped as `Some(v)`.
- **graph's layout cache moved onto the disposal bag**: the old chain cleared the cache inside `subscribe` plus `schedule_paint`; here `follow_store` handles repaint only, and cache invalidation has its own `subscribe_id` registered with `sub_bag_register`, the same pattern as gauge_t.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/chart` **146/146** — 48 new: four wbtest files ported same-source, 44, plus 4 component mountings — sunburst changing with data, graph's layout cache invalidating after a data change so the picture changes, parallel coordinates changing rows, pictorialbar producing pixels in both forms. ### MoonBit native GUI stack · Specialised charts batch 1 (`chart`: boxplot / funnel / heatmap / radar)

- **One chart per file, ported same-source**: master's `charts_boxplot.mbt`/`charts_funnel.mbt`/`charts_heatmap.mbt`/`charts_radar.mbt` became `boxplot.mbt`/`funnel.mbt`/`heatmap.mbt`/`radar.mbt` — pure-function layer verbatim, drawing layer switched to `@render.Painter`/`@text.draw_box_at` with colors read live from `@theme`, component layer switched to the `node_of_new` form. The four wbtest files came across correspondingly, each with a **component mounting producing pixels** assertion: `ink_of > N`, plus `diff_of > 50` after new data, plus empty data or insufficient dimensions not crashing. A regression where the pure functions are right but the component is unwired is now caught on the first run. The old chain's `AttributedText` "no data" was uniformly replaced with the fixed-box `@text.draw_box_at` form, same as `draw.mbt`.
- **All dependencies already in the new stack**: `mix_hex`/`lighten_hex`/`parse_hex`/`rgb_to_hsl` are in `@theme.palette`, and `bar_slot`/`draw_hgrid`/`series_color`/`fmt_axis`/`truncate_to` are reused from this package. `mut_view().sort_by(fn(a,b){ -1/0/1 })` works on this toolchain, an Int-returning comparator, unrelated to the `Ordering` unavailability pitfall.

Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gaining a "specialised charts" block, window grown to 1400×2300, geometry line `NATIVE-APP-CHSP` — exit code 0. Characteristic-color sampling from the screenshot shows all four charts: boxplot with a 68px success box plus 28px danger outlier dots, funnel's first layer in primary at 3508px, heatmap's light primary 5773px plus deep primary 1944px, showing the color-band gradient, radar's two series at 169/168px. **Appearance is for the user to re-verify on real hardware.**

Move the target block on screen while **keeping most of the window visible** — around a client origin of -1200 locally with a 2300-tall window — or pixel sampling from the screenshot is meaningless.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Chart interaction layer (`chart`: tooltip + DataZoom/VisualMap/mark/export + clickable legend + `charts_it` three interactive charts)

- **Port surface and file correspondence**: master's `charts_tooltip.mbt`/`charts_interactive.mbt`/`charts_it.mbt` were ported same-source into `tooltip.mbt` — the `CiTip` overlay state with out-of-bounds-safe placement, `CiPlot` drawing area, nearest-point `ci_nearest_idx` and sector `ci_sector_at` hit, the `ci_tooltip` interactive canvas component; `interactive.mbt` — the full `CiZoom` window math, `CiVisualMap` color bands, `ci_mark_line`/`ci_mark_area`, `ci_save` offscreen export, legend hit and visibility bit helpers, the `ci_legend` component; and `charts_it.mbt` — `line_chart_it`/`bar_chart_it`/`donut_chart_it`. The three wbtest files came across correspondingly.
- **Legend color shape changed: no color strings stored, but (name, original index) plus `color_at` read live.** master fixed (name, color string) into a Store, so a theme change left the whole palette stale and required rebuilding items via `on_theme_change`. `ci_legend` here takes `color_at : (Int) -> String` and reads at `on_draw` — series colors, donut colors and bar positive/negative colors all come from the theme live — so a theme switch through the process-level `watch_theme` repaint yields new colors automatically, and **the `on_theme_change` rebuild chain is structurally unnecessary**. The bar's positive/negative split is a closure capturing the data Store's current value.
- **`on_scroll`'s callback signature has no widget first parameter**, `Option[(ScrollEvent) -> Bool]`, unlike `on_draw`/`on_pointer`, whose first parameter is the widget to avoid reference cycles; a scroll callback cannot reach it. Wheel zoom scaling needs the canvas width and height, so the solution is **holding a size Ref inside the constructing closure**, refreshed every frame by `on_draw`, which does have the widget parameter, and read by `on_scroll` as the most recent frame. A visible component has always drawn at least one frame, so there is no window in which (0,0) could be read.
- **`ci_tooltip` gained an `on_leave` callback**: hiding the overlay clears only `CiTip`, but the caller's own hover state — the polyline's guide line and landing point, the sector's outward expansion — is drawing state beyond `hit`, and stays stale if not cleared. The white-box "restored after leaving" assertion failed on the first run, diff=276/1012, exactly because the guide line and expansion were still drawn. All three interactive components pass `on_leave=fn(){ hover.val = -1 }`.
- **Drag capture is no longer managed by the component**: master's `set_capture`/`release_capture` are structurally unnecessary here, since the host's `route_pointer` makes the Down hit target the capture owner automatically, and every later `Move`/`Up` goes to it, so a release is never lost when the pointer leaves.
- **`draw_donut` split to expose `draw_donut_core`**, sectors plus centre summary with colors through a `color_at` parameter: the interactive version's legend is `ci_legend`, clickable and visibility-toggleable, so it cannot reuse the original `draw_donut`'s embedded legend, and `draw_donut` itself became a thin shell, core plus embedded legend. `ci_sector_at`, general sector hit with a thickness parameter, coexists with the simplified `donut_hit` written for fixed thickness in the first batch, since the interactive ring's thickness is configurable and hit geometry must follow it same-source.
- **PNG export really works on Linux in this stack**, `render/png.mbt` being a pure implementation with no platform shim: master's `ci_save` always failed off Windows, its shim not exposing an export API, so the wbtest could only check format without touching disk. Here the wbtest writes to `/tmp` and asserts `Ok`, and `ci_save_chart`'s offscreen `Painter` must call `end()` when done, since Cairo session slots are finite.
- **xdotool's XTest wheel injection does not work on GTK3 — measured in this batch, a limitation of the injection tool rather than the code**: `xdotool click 4/5` produces button4/5 events at the X level, received by `xev` and marked synthetic NO, but GTK3's X11 backend uses XInput2 and **does not translate XTest core button events into scroll events**. Reproduced conclusively with a 20-line GTK probe connecting only scroll-event plus fprintf: not one entry into the stub's `wm_on_scroll`. The wheel-zoom component chain is covered by the white-box `dispatch_scroll` direct call, injecting `dy:1` → narrower window → pixels change, and **real-hardware wheel feel and appearance are left to the user**. Programmatic wheel injection would need uinput; `/dev/uinput` exists while ydotool and evemu are not installed.
- **Triple coordinate alignment for real-hardware screenshots, a pitfall on 10px targets**: ① `xdotool mousemove --window` gives **client-relative coordinates**, the same system as GTK event coordinates, so injection needs no conversion. ② `import -window` on a window taller than the screen captures only the **visible part**, with the screenshot origin at the screen rather than the window — locally a 2080-tall window against a 1080 screen, so after moving the window to negative Y, screenshot y = client y − 866. ③ Frame and client differ by a title bar, 34px on XFCE. Sampling with the wrong offset first produced the false conclusion "the legend swatches were not drawn" — a 10px swatch missed by 34px is entirely absent. **Align first, deriving the client origin from the mouse landing point via `getmouselocation`, before concluding "not drawn".** Likewise, injecting into a window taller than the screen requires `xdotool windowmove` to negative coordinates first, bringing the target block on screen; XTest coordinates are clamped to the screen's bottom edge, so a point off screen means no injection at all.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/chart` **37/37** — 26 new: the three tooltip wbtest files ported, overlay size estimation, out-of-bounds-safe placement, nearest point and map_idx being mutual inverses, sector four quadrants with ring-band tolerance, `CiPlot` fractional and degenerate cases; the full zoom math — normalisation, setting the window, the wheel anchor invariant, pan bounds, visible interval; VisualMap's two-color and three-color bands with invalid colors falling back; legend hit accumulating geometry with a width threshold; visibility bits filling, flipping and filtering with offset addressing; slice narrowing; `ci_save_chart` size and format checks plus PNG really written to disk; the three interactive components mounted with injection — line showing overlay and guide line on hover and restoring on leave, legend click hiding a series changing the picture, bar scaled by `dispatch_scroll` direct call, donut sector expanding on hover and restoring; pure functions — plot margins same-source as drawing, donut geometry clamping the inner radius, items keeping original indices with palette cycling, window scaling taking the longest series. Nine packages' tests all green — core 62/input 10/render 42/text 29/icons 4/theme 8/sys 7/ui 107/chart 37 —, ten packages `--deny-warn` all zero warnings, `yoga-mbt` 96/96, repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings, no increase. Real-window evidence: `examples/native-app` gaining an "interactive charts" block, window grown to 1400×2080, geometry line `NATIVE-APP-CHIT` — exit code 0. After injecting "wheel on the bar canvas, ineffective, see above → click the donut legend's first item → hover the donut sector → hover the line canvas", pixel sampling matched item by item: legend swatches all present including the bar's negative item red `(214,69,80)`, **a hidden item's swatch turning border grey `(216,220,225)`**, the first sector at 12 o'clock, primary blue, gone with the remaining sectors redistributed so that position became success green, the tooltip's dark base `(49,49,51)` to the right of the hover point, and a landing-point color on the hovered line. **Wheel zoom, tooltip following feel and legend click feel are for the user to re-verify on real hardware.**

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Platform input mapping layer (parallel line #19, first batch: `core/input_map.mbt`)

- **Why the tables first and the backends later**: the Windows and macOS backends cannot be validated on this machine, no real hardware, so per the "do not write unverifiable code" discipline the **platform-independent conventions** were landed first as pure functions plus regression: modifier folding for the three platforms, two key-code tables, Win32 virtual keys and macOS `kVK_*`, shift folding, button numbers, and the routing table for "who gets this key first". Backends then fill from the table instead of each deciding the semantics again, which would produce three versions.
- **Three conventions**: ① keysyms use **X11 values**, the Linux backend being GDK keyval already, with the other two platforms aligning to it, and printable ASCII being its character code. ② Letters and digits yield the **unshifted base code**, with shift and caps folded by `win_apply_shift`: X11's keyval already carries shift semantics while Windows' virtual key codes do not, so without this step "Shift+A" would be read as 'a'. ③ Symbol keys, the OEM row, are **not hard-coded into a layout table**: Windows goes through `WM_CHAR`/Unicode, macOS through `charactersIgnoringModifiers`, and a hard-coded table would be wrong often and unmaintainable.
- **One measured semantic correction, written into the decision table**: cursor and selection keys must **count as kernel keys with Ctrl too** — Ctrl+Left/Right jumping by word and Ctrl+Home/End going to start/end are exactly the commonest editor actions — but **not with Alt**, since Alt+Left/Right is a host action such as "back". The order is itself the semantics: chord → cursor key → Tab/Shift+Tab, focus cycling → shortcut chord → printable key, passing the input method first → everything else to the host.
- **Authority ownership must be written in two places' comments**: Linux's modifier folding currently lives in `wm_mods` in `win/stub.c`, which must fold on the C side and cannot call back into MoonBit, and it is **bit-for-bit identical** with `gtk_mods_to_mods`. Both comments name the other, so changing one requires changing the other; the executable definition of the table is on the MoonBit side, pinned by regression.
- **macOS's `kVK_*` covers special keys only**: Return/Tab/Space/Backspace/ForwardDelete/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown/arrows/F1-F12/keypad — letters and digits are **deliberately unmapped**, since mac characters must come from the event's Unicode text and layout resolution is the system's job. Also mac's `kVK_Delete`(51) is **Backspace** and `kVK_ForwardDelete`(117) is Delete; this is the easiest pair to remember backwards, so both are pinned in assertions.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/core` **78/78** — 7 new: three-platform modifier bits including "the GDK lock bit is not a modifier" and "Windows button bits do not leak into modifier bits"; the Win VK table — letters, digits, control, function, keypad, unknown yielding 0; shift folding — letters by shift xor caps, digits and symbols through a table, unlisted keys returned as-is; the mac VK table with Backspace and Delete pinned separately; button numbers folding Win `MK_*` and mac `buttonNumber` into 1 left, 2 middle, 3 right; the routing table's six rules; the trigger conditions for reset and surrounding. `moon check core --deny-warn` zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings. This batch has **no real-hardware evidence**, everything is pure functions, and backend wiring follows the Windows foundation and mac hardware.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · The native tier for overlays (batch E remainder: `core/overlay_native.mbt`)

- **The tier decision looks at one thing only**: whether the containing window has mounted native child surfaces, `Window::has_child_surfaces()`, read from the C-side slot table `wm_window_surface_count`. With a web area present the whole layer switches to real windows; without one it stays on the layer. Putting the check in the C-side slot table rather than MoonBit bookkeeping avoids a counter that can miss decrements. All six overlays — tooltip, dropdown, context menu, dialog, toast, hover card — go through `overlay_show_at`/`overlay_show_full`, so the tier switch takes effect in one place.
- **The native table is not put inside `OverlayHost`**: the host belongs to `App`, and the host holding `App` would be a reference cycle. The popup table is a process-level `Map[handle, App]`, and `overlay_hide`/`overlay_clear` plus exit cleanup all go through it.
- **Two GTK facts behind "open the frame, measure the content, then shrink the frame"**: ① the drawing area's `gtk_widget_set_size_request` is the window's **minimum content size**, set from the initial size at creation, so calling `gtk_window_resize` without changing it cannot shrink below the initial value and a measured overlay would keep a dead margin; ② `set_resizable(FALSE)` makes programmatic `gtk_window_resize` ignored entirely — a borderless window cannot be dragged by the user anyway, so setting TRUE has no side effect. Both are handled together inside `wm_window_set_size`.
- **"Dismiss on blur" misfires during mapping and is off by default**, established by a control experiment: with it enabled the popup closed itself after about two seconds, while the content's own dismiss control had never been clicked, proven by `hides=0`; turning the switch off keeps the same sequence open. Root cause: a transient plus keep-above window receives a run of focus-out during mapping. Until there is a "counts only after having had focus" check, an overlay staying resident and dismissing from its content is preferable — "vanishing right after opening" is worse than "not dismissing on outside click". The switch `overlay_set_dismiss_on_blur(on)` stays and can be enabled once the check exists.
- **A new event constructor hits a "frozen" baseline page**: adding `LostFocus` to `@win.Event` took repo errors from 287 to 288, because `examples/native-window`, the G2–G5 baseline with no further features, matches events exhaustively. The check is to notice the error-count change and find who grew; adding one empty branch returns to baseline. **"Frozen" does not mean exempt from convention changes.**
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/core` **81/81** — 3 new: with no child surface going the layer tier while `overlay_show_at`/`hide`/`count` behave as usual; sizing counting only the visible children's right and bottom edges; with no native-tier overlay, both the blur and shrink-frame paths being no-ops. `moon check core`/`win` and four examples `--deny-warn` zero warnings; ui 110/110, web 11/11, media 18/18 unchanged; repo-wide back to 287 errors / 68 warnings. Real-window evidence, clicking "overlay above web" **in a bridged window that has a web area**: `NATIVE-WEB-OVL opens=1 tier=1 native=1 layer=0`, and the screenshot shows self-drawn content — a title plus a 「收起」 button — above WebKit-rendered body text, exactly what the layer tier cannot do.
- **Not in this batch, not pretending completion**: a usable check for outside-click dismissal, the switch above stays off; Esc dismissal; popup anchor following the owner's scrolling and movement; per-component size hints, currently relying on the three-frame shrink.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Native popup windows (batch E: `win/popup.mbt` + `core/popup.mbt`)

- **Why it must be a real window**: self-drawn pixels always sit **below** a native child surface, such as a webview area, because z-order is decided on the native side and the Painter cannot cover it. So "dropdowns, context menus, tooltips, toasts and dialogs must cover a web page" has exactly one route: the window system, the overlay discipline of plan §4.5. This batch provides that channel, not another self-drawn layer.
- **Five GTK settings must be applied together, and before `show`**: `set_decorated(FALSE)` plus `set_type_hint(GDK_WINDOW_TYPE_HINT_POPUP_MENU)` plus `set_transient_for(owner)` plus `set_skip_taskbar_hint/skip_pager_hint(TRUE)` plus `set_keep_above(TRUE)`, with `set_resizable(FALSE)` as well. The type hint and the transient relation take effect **at mapping**, so setting them after show is too late.
- **One hard measured pitfall: `gtk_window_get_position` always returns (0,0) under the window manager's reparenting.** It reports coordinates relative to the parent window, and a top-level is wrapped into the WM's decoration frame, so relative to that frame it is 0,0. The **screen origin** must be asked of the GdkWindow: `gdk_window_get_origin(gtk_widget_get_window(w), &x, &y)`. The acceptance check is not "an error" but **the popup landing at the requested local coordinates regardless of where the owner is** — in a multi-window shape every window's menu landing at the same screen coordinate looks like "the popup does not follow the button". After the fix, measured `owner_origin=2,34` with a request at local (420,300) landing at (422,334), bit-for-bit with xwininfo.
- **Placement as a pure function**: `popup_place(owner_x, owner_y, x, y, w, h, screen_w, screen_h)` — past the screen's right or bottom edge, flip to the other side of the anchor, so an edge-hugging menu opens in the reverse direction; if flipping still yields a negative, clamp back to 0; a screen size of 0 means "clamp only, no flip". All three boundaries are in assertions, including the easy-to-write-wrong "if the flipped position is still on screen, use it rather than clamping to 0".
- **A popup is just an attached window and needs no second lifecycle**: `App::open_popup` goes through batch A's registry, so it shares the loop and the pump naturally, `close_window()` detaches only itself without affecting the host, and `App::shutdown` tears both down. Example evidence: after picking a menu item, `xdotool search --name '^popup$'` returns 0 while the main window remains, with `NATIVE-WEB-POP opens=1 closed=1 choice='乙' wins=1 owner_origin=2,34 win_size=1100x700`, and the screenshot clearly shows a borderless popup above WebKit-rendered page text.
- **This batch gives the channel plus one self-drawn popup example only**: the six pieces in `core/overlay.mbt` — tooltip, dropdown, context menu, dialog, toast, hover card — still use the self-drawn layer; wiring them to "native tier when a webview exists" is next. The check: switch to a native window only when the containing window has a mounted pane, otherwise stay on the layer, since with no web page there is no reason to open another window.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/core` **71/71** — 1 new placement regression covering seven boundary cases. `moon check win`/`core` and three examples `--deny-warn` zero warnings; ui 110/110, web 11/11, media 18/18 unchanged; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings. Real-window evidence as above: a 240x150 popup landing at (422,334), IsViewable, closing itself on selection, the main window unaffected. **Needs the user's eyes**: the borderless appearance and how keep-above behaves across multi-monitor and window switching.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Media player (batch D: new package `yue/media`, CPU blit + software decoding)

- **Engine ported, not rewritten**: `modules/gui-media`'s `audio_player.mbt`, 416 lines, and `video_player.mbt`, 476 lines, measured to have **zero @yue dependencies**, only the component wrapper layer touching the UI, so the engine and 15 existing regression cases moved wholesale into the new `yue/media` package with only the test asset path and one public entry changed. The old chain's pitfalls — audio and video drifting apart, progress climbing from zero after a seek, crashes when loading a new source, played-to-end needing to differ from the initial state — came across with those tests. **Half the value of this batch is catching what the teacher already got right.**
- **Asset path convention changed**: a native test executable's cwd is the **workspace root**, not the package directory, whereas the old package under `modules/gui-media/src` wrote `../ffmpeg-mbt/src/testdata/`. The new package must write `modules/ffmpeg-mbt/src/testdata/av_1s.mp4`, and the acceptance check is the relative path printed verbatim in the error.
- **Frame blit byte order**: ffmpeg's sws target is `AV_PIX_FMT_RGBA`, R,G,B,A, while `render`'s `Bitmap` is internally Cairo `ARGB32` in little-endian layout, B,G,R,A, premultiplied. Blitting a frame must therefore swap R and B; on opaque pixels premultiplied equals unpremultiplied, so alpha is written as 255. Pinned byte by byte in `rgba_to_bitmap`, with the wbtest asserting `10 20 30 00 → 30 20 10 ff`, and the real-window evidence being testsrc's colour bars showing no swapped colors.
- **This toolchain has no `FixedArray::of_list` / `Array::freeze` / `Bytes::of_list`**: test bytes can only be built with `FixedArray::make(n, b'\x00')` written by index plus `Bytes::from_array`. Also `String::split` yields a **`StringView` iterator**, needing `to_owned()` for a `String`; `replace` takes labelled parameters, `old=`/`new=`; the constructor form is `StringBuilder()`, since `Buffer::new` does not exist; and an unused parameter such as `y` must be written `_y`.
- **Layering between UI and engine**: `video` lives in `yue/media`, importing `@core`/`@render`/`@text`/`@theme` inside the package, and **not in `ui`** — otherwise every button-only application would link ffmpeg and miniaudio. The engine files `audio.mbt`/`video.mbt`/`subtitle.mbt` stay free of UI dependencies, the media layer does not depend on webview, and both depend only on the window, layout and event layers, building-block principle 1.
- **Clock and repaint**: the engine's `tick()`, formerly `vp_tick`, opened as the public `tick` in this batch with `frames_decoded()` added, is driven by a self-continuing `@core.set_timeout(33, ...)`, **not advanced inside drawing**. Each tick calls the observation hook `on_tick(position, frame count, playing)`, which the example uses to prove frames are advancing and the clock is running rather than one static image. The image object is rebuilt only when `frames_decoded()` changes, since rebuilding an Image every frame would repeatedly create cairo surfaces.
- **Seek debouncing made into a partition pure function**: `player_bar_hit` splits the control bar into leftmost 34px play button, right 150px time text and middle progress track; during a drag only the display position updates, with the real **seek happening on release**. The old chain's problem was seeking on every drag step, which stalled the picture for a whole beat given long keyframe distances. Two boundary assertions are worth recording: both ends of the track clamp rather than overflow, at 449px giving >0.99 instead of ==1.0, and a negative coordinate falling into the play-button zone, since partitioning precedes the ratio.
- **A media file that cannot be opened is not silent**: when `video`'s `make` fails it draws an explanation panel and hands the reason out through `on_error`, probing plus degrade with an explicit `Unsupported`, and the example's `err=''` is the evidence that no degradation happened.
- **Not in this batch, recorded in TODO rather than pretending completion**: playback speed — audio needs time stretching, and doing video alone breaks audio-video sync, exactly what this document repeatedly warns about; embedded subtitle tracks, mov_text/ass, this batch taking external SRT/VTT text only; fullscreen; the volume bar UI, the engine has `set_volume` but no control was drawn; frame stepping.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/yue/media` **18/18** — 15 ported: audio play/pump/seek/loop, video decode/clock/duration/frame size/silent advance without an audio track. 3 new: subtitles in four parts, two timestamp spellings, SRT and VTT both handled, inline markup stripped, hit boundaries including start and end with multiple cues joined; frame blit byte order and short-packet tail pixels; control bar partitioning. `moon check yue/media`/`./examples/native-web` `--deny-warn` zero warnings; core 70/70, ui 110/110, web 11/11, render 43/43, text 29/29 unchanged; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings. Real-window evidence — `examples/native-web`'s "open a player window", a third window playing `av_1s.mp4` plus inline SRT — `NATIVE-WEB-MEDIA frames=10 pos_ms=1000 playing=0 err=''`: a 1-second clip decoding all 10 frames, the clock reaching 1000ms, stopping automatically at the end, no degradation. The screenshot shows colour bars with no swapped colors plus the white text 「第二条字幕（0.6~1.0 秒）」 overlaid on the picture plus the control bar's progress full and `0:01 / 0:01`. **Needs the user's eyes**: whether playing with sound really produces audio, this machine having a miniaudio device; the feel of seeking by dragging the progress bar; long-clip speed and frame stepping, not in this batch.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Native fields untypable after clicking into a web page (two root causes: GTK focus not reclaimed + preedit not drawn on an empty field)

- **Symptom, user's real hardware**: after clicking into the webview page, clicking back into a native input field and typing produces nothing.
- Reproduced with xdotool injection plus temporary C-side probes, revealing **two independent defects**:
- **① Our drawing area never reclaimed GTK keyboard focus**: `gtk_widget_grab_focus` ran once when the window showed, after which the WebKit child took focus on click, and a `GtkDrawingArea` does not take focus back because it was clicked — GTK does not do that for it. Probe evidence: after clicking back into the field, not a single `[focus] in` and no `[key]` either; keys all went into the web page, even Ctrl+Z, which is why "some operations still seem to work" is an illusion. Fix: the host calls `request_focus()` **unconditionally** on pointer press. It previously asked only when the focus stack really changed hands, and a change of hands is exactly what does not happen, the field still being in the stack.
- **② On an empty field showing a placeholder, the preedit string was not drawn at all**: `ui/entry.mbt`'s drawing wrote "draw placeholder" and "draw text plus preedit" as one if/else, so with no text an empty field took the placeholder branch and **the preedit branch was skipped entirely**. Pinyin was working normally — probe `[preedit] '爱'` kept arriving — while nothing appeared on screen, presenting as "typing does nothing". Fix: the placeholder is drawn only when there is **neither text nor preedit**, with preedit as its own branch. This defect is unrelated to the web page and reproduces on an empty field alone; the multi-line `textarea` does not have it, since its preedit is drawn outside the placeholder loop.
- **One tightening made along the way**: when keyboard focus is taken away, `Event::LostFocus`, the input-method session is handed back to the system — the in-flight commit goes to the current widget, the preedit display clears, `im_reset` interrupts the engine-side unfinished composition, and the de-duplication cache resets. The focus stack is untouched, so returning to this window restores the widget's focus as before.
- **Probe methodology, hit and recorded**: an application's `println` is **block-buffered** when stdout is redirected to a file, and everything is lost if the process is killed — the first reading led to the false conclusion "the application emitted no log at all", and `stdbuf -oL` was needed to see real data. C-side stderr is unbuffered, so when the two sides' logs look asymmetric, suspect buffering before drawing conclusions.
- **Verification**: `[focus] in` appears after clicking back, with `[key]` following; both absent before the fix. An empty-field typing screenshot shows the preedit `爱` with its underline; the full round trip — clear, click into the page, click back, type — shows the preedit `阿宝`. `core` 82/82, `ui` 110/110, `input` 10/10, `web` 15/15 all green, per-package `--deny-warn` zero warnings, repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings. **Needs the user to re-verify**: whether the originally reported scenario, jumping inside a web page and returning to a native field to type, is now working.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Window-level key fallthrough channel (`App::add_key_fallthrough`)

- Gap: the host delivers keys only to **the focused widget and the ancestors of it that declare `on_key`**, the Key branch of `App::route`, so with empty focus the key is dropped outright. "No keyboard unless something is clicked" is therefore the framework's current behaviour, and window-level shortcuts of the player kind had no entry at the component layer.
- Convention: when the focus chain does not consume a key, or there is no focus at all, fallthrough handlers are asked in registration order and the first returning true truncates. Three boundaries — ① while focus is in an input field the editor consumes the key, so **the channel does not steal characters** and needs no extra check; ② it applies only within this window's event loop, and is not the **system-level** hotkeys of `sys`/`win`, the X11 grab line; ③ the channel has no unregister entry, since this layer has no widget unmount hook yet, so **the handler must do its own liveness check** — asking `Widget::is_painted()`, whether this subtree is still drawn this frame, and returning false when it is not, so a detached component stops eating keys.
- Implementation cost: one more field on `App` required the three hand-built fake-window literals to be updated as well, since record literals cannot omit fields; repo-wide only core's three wbtests and `App::new` were affected.
- Verification: `moon test ./core` **149/149**, with the new `key_fallthrough_wbtest.mbt` adding two cases — no focus receiving a key and release not entering the channel; the focus chain consuming not being stolen, and multiple handlers truncating in registration order. `moon check ./core --deny-warn` zero warnings. Real hardware — whether space and Enter are taken only by the currently focused player — is verified by the user along with the control-surface batch.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Ownership of the present buffer (fix: garbage when opening a second large window / flicker in self-drawn areas)

- **Symptom, user's real hardware**: opening a second window such as the "bridge window" or the "local video window" produced garbage on screen and flicker in self-drawn regions; with only the main window it was invisible.
