- **Root cause**: `wm_present` pointed `w->pending` **straight at the MoonBit-side `Bitmap` buffer**, while the actual blit happens in the **next** draw callback, since GTK can only obtain the GdkWindow's cairo inside the draw callback. Once the callback was queued, that Bitmap had no referring owner on the MoonBit side — in `App::paint_frame` it is a local value, replaced next frame — and when GC collected it depended on allocation pressure. After collection, an expose reading that address read **freed memory**, producing garbage, and each expose re-reading once looked like flicker.
- **Why precisely a second large window**: with a single window and a small picture the buffer is usually blitted again before being collected. One more 1000x620 animated window adds tens of allocations per second, GC pressure rises, and the window falls into the interval "already collected but still to be exposed". Covering it and moving away, forcing an expose of the old region, reproduces it most easily.
- **Fix**: the backend **owns its frame buffer** — `WmWindow` gained `backing/backing_cap`, `wm_present` goes through `wm_store_frame`, reallocating on demand plus one memcpy, with `pending` pointing at its own buffer, and `wm_close` releases it. A slot is reused by the next window, so memset alone would be both a leak and wrong. Both the GTK and Win32 branches were changed in the same shape to avoid two semantics; the Windows side cannot run locally, so it is code-reviewed only, to be verified on hardware with the W line.
- **One convention**: a buffer that must live until the next callback across an FFI boundary must be owned by **the side that will be called back**. Writing a comment — it previously said "ownership is with MoonBit" — does not solve the problem: ownership was documented clearly, but nobody was responsible for keeping it alive to that moment. The same shape was checked in `web`'s JS replies and `yue/media`'s frame blit; both allocate and free on the C side, `malloc`/`g_free`, so the hazard is absent.
- **Verification**: after the change, `moon build ./examples/native-web` relinked, with `build/libyue_win_stub.a` rebuilt. Real window run: "open the local video window → screenshot → cover with the main window and move away to force an expose → screenshot again". A 23-minute real clip kept decoding, `NATIVE-WEB-LOCAL present=1 frames=1369 pos_ms=56397 speed=1.25x err=''` — a 1000x620 animated window allocating tens of times per second, exactly the shape most likely to fall into "collected but still to be exposed" — with zero X errors in the log and both screenshots matching the video with no streaks or dirty regions. **The user has re-verified on real hardware: the bridge window and the local video window no longer show garbage, and self-drawn areas no longer flicker.** Repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Lifetime of handles across FFI (fix: after closing a window the log fills with GTK/WebKit assertions)

- **Symptom, located by a control experiment rather than guessing**: with the same example, **closing only the bridge window** left the log clean, while **closing the main window**, the one with the web area attached, produced a fixed 5 CRITICAL lines at exit — `webkit_web_view_get_title/get_uri` failing the `WEBKIT_IS_WEB_VIEW(webView)` assertion, immediately followed by `gtk_widget_get_parent`/`gtk_widget_destroy` failing `GTK_IS_WIDGET`. The assertions do not crash the process, so they had never been treated as a problem.
- **Root cause**: window teardown goes through the window layer's `wm_close`, which zeroes every native child slot belonging to that window and destroys the GtkWidget tree — WebKitWebView being a grandchild, gone with it — but **nobody told the capability layer**. So `Webview`'s `handle` still held the old slot number and `pumping` stayed true: the scheduled pump and the example's status polling kept calling `wb_get_title/wb_is_loading` with that handle, while the stub's `wb_get(id)` checks only "does the slot have a view" and cannot see "that view was destroyed with the window", so it handed out a dangling pointer. Finally `wb_destroy`, the `close` at exit, used it once more for `gtk_widget_get_parent`/`destroy`, producing those two `GTK_IS_WIDGET` lines.
- **Fix, one choke point, both branches in the same shape**: put the **liveness** check on **the side that knows when teardown happens**. In the stub, `wb_view_alive(v)` means the slot has a view **and** `wm_surface_container(v->surface_id) != NULL` — the container comes from win's slot table, becomes NULL when the window is torn down, and is the only reliable liveness signal. Every `wb_get` passes this gate, so **all** engine queries and actions become no-ops automatically after the view dies, with no per-function check to add; `wb_destroy` uses the same gate — with no container it only `g_free` plus `memset` to return resources and never touches the pointer. MoonBit gained the public `Webview::is_alive()`, and the pump's beat, finding the view gone, sets `pumping=false`, `handle=0L` and drops `eval_waiters`, stopping the scheduling instead of spinning on.
- **One convention, same family as "ownership of the present buffer"**: a handle across FFI and a buffer across FFI are the same class of problem — only the tearing-down side knows when it is gone, so the invalidation check must come from it. `handle != 0L` on the MoonBit side proves only "was created", never "still exists". Putting the liveness check in the stub's single retrieval function, `wb_get`, is far more reliable than writing it in front of twenty methods. Self-check for the same shape, filtered by "did we build another C slot table queried by id": `win`'s `wm_windows[]` is memset cell by cell after teardown, and every slot access was counted — anything touching `w->window`/`w->area` already null-checks and returns, the rest read only counters such as `ev_count`/`commit_len`, which are 0 after memset and naturally safe, so there is no gap. `yue/media`'s FFI surface passes opaque pointers, `MbtAdev`, rather than slot numbers, with the lifecycle owned by MoonBit's own `close`; a different shape, not in scope.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/web` **17/17** — 1 new: with a non-zero handle but no view, `is_alive()` is false, and after `retire_if_dead` closes the gap, `handle=0`/`pumping=false`/`eval_waiters` cleared. `web` and the example `--deny-warn` zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings. Real-window check, the same control experiment rerun: open the bridge window → close the bridge window → close the main window, log with **0 CRITICAL** lines, five before the fix; process exiting itself, `alive=0`, and the exit line readings normal, `last='标题 本地桥接页'`. **The user re-verified on real hardware (2026-10-12)**: closing windows one by one manually, clicking the title bar X, until only the main window remained and then closing it produced zero CRITICAL lines as well. Two regression cases confirm the liveness check did not block live views: the bridge page still loads from the protocol and reads its Chinese title; the main window's protocol line reads `reg=1 loads=1 files=2 unreg=1 fails=1 fail='WebKitNetworkError/399 yuedemo://local/index.html'`, field for field identical to before the fix.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Embedded subtitle track (batch D2c: ffmpeg-mbt exposing the subtitle stream + one duration lie)

- **The subtitle stream simply did not exist**: `modules/ffmpeg-mbt` located only the video and audio streams, two `av_find_best_stream` calls in `vf_open`, and subtitle packets were treated as "not a stream I want" in the decode loop and dropped with `av_packet_unref`. This batch adds a third: `VfFmt.sstream` plus a separate `VfSDec`, `vf_sub_open`/`vf_sub_next`/`vf_sub_pts_s`/`vf_sub_end_s`/`vf_sub_close`, and on the MoonBit side `subtitle_cues(path)` reading the whole track at once into `Array[SubCue]`.
- **A separate container read is required**: if the subtitle decoder shared the `AVFormatContext` with video and audio, both would advance the same `av_read_frame` cursor, so after reading subtitles the video would start from the middle or hit EOF immediately. `subtitle_cues` therefore opens its own context and closes it when done. The cost is one extra container open — subtitles are sparse and read in one pass, cheaper than per-frame queries — and the gain is that **calling mid-playback does not disturb the main timeline**, written as a headless assertion: after reading subtitles, open another instance and keep decoding, frame pts advancing as usual.
- **One duration lie, caught on real data rather than guessed**: mov_text decodes `AVSubtitle.end_display_time` **always as 2000ms**, the default when the decoder leaves the entry duration unset. Taking it literally makes the first subtitle cover the second and linger a second past when it should disappear. The check came from the printed table: `0.2..2.2 / 0.6..2.6` wrong against `0.2..0.6 / 0.6..1.0` as the asset intends. Fix: take **whichever is shorter between the packet duration and end_display_time**, with the packet duration read before `av_packet_unref`, which zeroes it afterwards. The mp4 sample duration is authoritative and the measured result falls back to the asset's intent.
- **The ASS full-line prefix is stripped at the FFI layer**: some text subtitle decoders, mov_text among them, do not fill `rect->text` and give only the whole ASS dialogue line, `ReadOrder,Layer,Style,Name,MarL,MarR,MarV,Effect,text`. That is the decoder output's **shape**, not its content, so normalisation belongs to the transport, `subtitle_ass_text`. The check is conservative: at least eight commas, a non-empty numeric `ReadOrder`, and the three margin fields numeric or empty. Style name, person name and effect are free text and cannot serve as checks, or a subtitle body that happens to contain eight commas would be cut mid-sentence — pinned by a positive and a negative case. Layout markup such as `{\an8}` and `<c.xxx>` still belongs to `yue/media`'s `strip_cue_tags`, the same cleaning road as external subtitles, so the two sources are fully identical on the rendering side.
- **Two sources in the player plus one observation hook**: if `video`'s `subtitle` is provided it is used, an explicit intent taking priority, and only when empty does it try the container's embedded track. `on_subtitle(cue count, embedded?)` is shaped like the existing `on_tick`/`on_speed`, and the example writes both values into the exit line, `NATIVE-WEB-MEDIA ... subs=2 emb=1` and `NATIVE-WEB-LOCAL ... subs=0`, so "this clip has no subtitle track" and "the subtitle track failed to decode" are distinguishable in the evidence — the latter reports its reason through `on_error` instead of silently returning an empty table.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/ffmpeg-mbt/src` **6/6** — 2 new: `subtitle_ass_text` stripping the prefix plus three "should not strip" negatives; the real container `av_1s_subs.mp4` read whole with start and end seconds, Chinese text, no disturbance to the main timeline, and "no track = Ok([])" separated from "cannot open = Err". `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/yue/media` **24/24** — 2 new: embedded track converted to `Cue` with transport and cleaning conventions aligned; end-to-end hit by position. `yue/media`/`web`/`core`/`ui`/`ffmpeg-mbt` and `examples/native-web` `--deny-warn` zero warnings; repo-wide still 287 errors / 68 warnings. The test asset is a 13KB three-stream clip kept in the repository — `av_1s.mp4` stream-copied plus two mov_text tracks, made with `ffmpeg -map 0:v -map 0:a? -map 1:0 -c copy -c:s mov_text`. **The user re-verified on real hardware (2026-10-12)**: the embedded-subtitle window showing two cues appearing and disappearing at 0.2~0.6 / 0.6~1.0, the external-subtitle window unchanged, and the long-asset window reading `subs=0` without error.
- **Not in this batch, not pretending completion**: ASS style rendering — colors, positioning, multi-track selection, currently text overlay only; the subtitle track list and switching, a multi-track container taking only the `av_find_best_stream` choice; audio perception re-verification under speed changes.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Player playback speed (batch D2b: pure MoonBit resampling + clock on the same axis)

- **Speed with zero C**: the audio side needs no new stub — the decoded interleaved s16 PCM is linearly resampled by `1/speed` before being pushed to the device, `media_resample_s16`, pure MoonBit, while the device still consumes at the original sample rate, so half the samples arrive and finish in half the time. The cost is **pitch following**: this is speed change, not speed change keeping pitch, which would need a phase vocoder. The video side changes one place: `vp_target_pts(base, elapsed_ms, speed) = base + elapsed × speed`, both sides on the same axis, so "picture fast, sound slow" cannot happen — exactly the desynchronisation the old chain repeatedly warned about.
- **One pre-existing defect exposed by speed**: the tick used to decode at least one frame per tick, comparing `pts >= target` only after decoding, so low-frame-rate video and **any speed below 1** ran ahead of the clock — the picture advancing at 30 frames/second while the clock ran at 0.5 speed. Fix: move the gate **before** decoding, checking the decoded frames' pts and not decoding when already ahead of the clock. This also delivers what the tick comment had long promised, "on low frame-rate video the picture is held across ticks".
- **Changing speed re-anchors the clock**: `set_speed` reads the current position first, then sets the speed, assigns that position to `base_pts/pos_base` and the current wall time to `wall0/played_base`. Without re-anchoring, the position would jump by the ratio of new to old speed. The audio position convention follows: the queue holds resampled samples, so "consuming N samples = advancing N×speed source samples", and that term in `AudioPlayer::current()` is multiplied by speed.
- **Streams without timestamps are not pretended to be supported**: the fallback path, one frame per tick stepping by the stream's frame rate, has no pts to chase, so speed affects the clock only and not the picture. This is written into `tick`'s comment rather than buried in the code.
- **Speed taken from a table rather than incremented in place**: `bar_speeds = [1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0, 0.75]`, and a click only advances the index, `player_speed_at(i)` handling negatives and wrap-around, so `+= 0.25` can never drift out of the ladder. Clamping lives in the engine, `media_clamp_speed`, [0.25,4.0], with NaN returning 1.0 rather than the fastest or slowest step. The control bar gained a sixth partition, `speed`, so the track's start moved from 114px to 154px and the volume bar's yielding threshold rose from 400 to 440 — the check "drawing and hit testing read the same constants" proved itself for the second time in this batch.
- **An observation hook rather than guessing**: `video` gained `on_speed(v)`, shaped like `on_tick`/`on_error`, and the example writes the step into the exit line `NATIVE-WEB-MEDIA ... speed=1.5x`, so the evidence needs no read of the engine's internals.
- **Not in this batch, not pretending completion**: embedded subtitle tracks, needing `ffmpeg-mbt` to expose the subtitle stream first; real audio output and listening re-verification, whether sync holds at speed and whether pitch following is acceptable.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/yue/media` **22/22** — 3 new: the speed ladder with wrap-around and negative indices plus short labels; `media_clamp_speed` and the three `vp_target_pts` formulas; `media_resample_s16` sample counts at 2x and 0.5x, interpolation midpoints, stereo channels not crossed, and the three pass-through cases. The real-decode case gained a `get_speed` clamping round trip, and the control bar partition test moved to six segments. `moon check yue/media`/`./examples/native-web` `--deny-warn` zero warnings. Real-window evidence — `examples/native-web`'s "open a player window", clicking the speed zone of the control bar twice, 1x→1.25x→1.5x — `NATIVE-WEB-MEDIA frames=10 pos_ms=1000 playing=0 speed=1.5x err=''`: the step reported by the `on_speed` hook rather than read from the engine, with the 1-second clip still decoding all 10 frames and reaching 1000ms at 1.5x before stopping itself, no degradation. The screenshot shows the control bar `▶ |< >| 1.5x` with full progress, the volume bar and `0:01 / 0:01`. **The user re-verified on real hardware (2026-10-12)**: audio and video stayed in sync at speed, pitch following was acceptable, and dragging the volume bar really got louder.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Player control surface completed (batch D2a: frame stepping, volume bar, fullscreen)

- **Frame stepping must decode to the landing frame on the spot**: `seek` clears the current frame to `None` waiting for the next tick, and while **paused `tick()` returns immediately**, so after stepping the picture stayed on a black frame and looked like "the button did nothing". Fix: the segment in tick that decodes forward from the decode point to the target time, capped at 8 frames, was extracted as `vp_settle`, and stepping = pause first → move the position by `1/fps` → `seek` → `settle`. All acceptance checks live in the headless case: after stepping `frames_decoded()` increases, `current()` advances, `current_frame()` is non-empty, and `is_playing()` is still false, since stepping must not start playback.
- **The control bar went from three partitions to five** — play, previous frame, next frame, progress track, volume, time text — with drawing and hit testing reading the **same** `BAR_*` constants, since writing the partitioning in two places eventually desynchronises. A narrow-bar yielding check was added: below `w < 400` the volume bar is neither drawn nor responsive, with the track's right end computed from the time text, otherwise you get "visible but unclickable" or the reverse. Both ends of the track still **clamp** rather than overflow, 114px giving =0.0 and 354px giving >0.99.
- **Volume and seek debounce in opposite directions**: seek is committed only on release, since every real seek must return to a keyframe and that is expensive, while volume **applies at every step** — hearing it while dragging is the expectation, and it does not trigger decoding. The volume bar draws `engine.get_volume()`, the clamped value inside the engine, rather than a local copy, since a local copy disagrees with the display when set clamps. For this, `VideoPlayer` gained `get_volume`; `AudioPlayer` had one long ago and both conventions now match.
- **Fullscreen is a window-level action**: the widget layer cannot reach the window, so the chain is `Window::set_fullscreen` → `App::set_fullscreen`, requested by the host, the example, through a button. The C side is only two lines, `gtk_window_fullscreen`/`unfullscreen`, ABI-only, per the "stubs are on demand and minimal" convention. After toggling, the size change flows through the ordinary allocate event and the host does not compute new rectangles.
- **Not in this batch, not pretending completion**: playback speed — the audio side needs either time stretching or miniaudio pitch, both touching the device thread, so it is another batch with the pitch cost documented; embedded subtitle tracks, needing `ffmpeg-mbt` to expose the subtitle stream first; real audio output re-verification.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/yue/media` **19/19** — 1 new frame-stepping case: `n=0` not moving; after stepping, frame count, position, having a frame and still paused all holding; both ends clamping; `get_volume` returning the clamped value. The control bar partition test moved to five segments plus narrow-bar yielding. `moon check win`/`core`/`yue/media`/`./examples/native-web` `--deny-warn` zero warnings. Real-window evidence — `examples/native-web`'s "open a player window", injecting `>| ×2`, `|< ×1`, the volume bar's middle and the fullscreen button — `NATIVE-WEB-MEDIA frames=21 pos_ms=1000 playing=0 err=''`: a 1-second clip normally finishing at 10 frames then decoded to 21 by stepping, proving stepping really decodes, with `err=''` meaning no degradation. After clicking fullscreen, `xdotool getwindowgeometry` gives `Position: 2560,0 Geometry: 2560x1440`, the attached window really filling the second screen, and the screenshot shows the control bar `▶ |< >|` plus progress track plus the **volume bar**, its fill visible after dragging to the middle, plus `0:00 / 0:01`. **Needs the user's eyes**: the visual jump of frame stepping, the volume bar's drag feel and whether it really gets louder, and the position of subtitles and controls in fullscreen.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Local content channel and fine-grained navigation reasons (batch C remainder: `web/scheme.mbt`)

- **Protocols are registered per context, not per view**: `webkit_web_context_register_uri_scheme`'s callback signature is `(WebKitURISchemeRequest*, gpointer)` — **no view parameter** — so protocol ownership is naturally context-level, and the old chain's process-level static registration loses its meaning once profiles hang at pane level. This batch's slot table dedupes on `(context, scheme)`: within one context a scheme registers with the engine once, and re-registering only changes the root directory.
- **"Unregister" is replacement, not revocation**: WebKit has no unregister-uri-scheme. Unregistering clears the scheme's root directory so every subsequent callback goes to `webkit_uri_scheme_request_finish_error`, and the page gets "protocol present, content unavailable". That is safer than leaving the old directory, which would let a switched profile still read the previous profile's files, and more honest than pretending the registration can be revoked — the return value means only "replacement succeeded".
- **Static files under the root only, with path traversal blocked at the stub**: a request path containing `..` returns an error directly; nothing is absolutised and no symlink escape is followed. MIME is looked up by extension — html/htm/css/js/mjs/json/svg/png/jpg/jpeg/gif/woff2/txt — with everything else `application/octet-stream`.
- **One convention, settled 2026-10-12**: C stubs are **on demand and minimal** — written only where MoonBit cannot reach: GTK3 window layer, Cairo, Pango, WebKitGTK, miniaudio/ffmpeg, dirent/getenv/spawn, socket. In C only ABI translation and slot tables; decisions, parsing and degrade semantics stay in MoonBit. Before adding a function, ask whether existing MoonBit channels can be composed. This batch made one real trade-off: directory creation added no C, and `sys_make_dirs` was composed from the existing subprocess channel, `pr_run("mkdir", ["-p", path])`, with `defaultapps_wbtest` already doing the same in this repository. The cost is that it holds only where `pr_available()` is true, so the function's documentation says "the probe is the convention" rather than letting callers believe it works everywhere.
- **Revisited the same day and corrected — the convention governs capability, not "no C allowed in `sys`"**: compose only when the two routes are **genuinely equivalent**; when they are not, add C. Once directory creation was landed as a composition, the cost materialised in measurement: it held only on POSIX, because Windows' PATH has no `mkdir`, so `fsx_wbtest.mbt:109` had been red on Windows since the day it shipped. It is now a thin FFI, `yue_sys_make_dirs`, `CreateDirectoryW` level by level on Windows and `mkdir(2)` level by level on POSIX, joining the family that was always C — `sys_read_text_file`, `sys_remove_file`, `fsx_list_dir`. That is not a new exception to the convention but the flattening of its only outlier, along with dropping a subprocess dependency: no `pr_available()` requirement, and no fork plus two temp files per call.
- **`CreateDirectoryW` does not return "already exists" for the drive prefix** (measured on real hardware in this batch): creating a directory level by level treats `"C:"` as a segment, which returns **`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED(5)`** rather than `ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS(183)`; accepting only 183 reads the drive root as a failure and the whole call returns 0. The method is **probe first, then create**: `GetFileAttributesW` valid means this level exists and is skipped, with 183 tolerated only for a creation race. POSIX has no such trap — `mkdir` on an existing directory is `EEXIST`.
- **Writing a file does not create parent directories, and the symptom shows up elsewhere** (hit in the real window in this batch): the page area showed only `not found`, looking like the protocol failing, while in fact the root `/tmp/native-web-scheme` did not exist at all and both `sys_write_text_file` calls failed. The fix is `sys_make_dirs`, but **the acceptance check must be split first**: the example's exit line gained a `files=` count — registration succeeded / load issued / files actually present — because without it one is guessing which link broke.
- **Two fine-grained navigation reasons**: ① `WEBKIT_LOAD_REDIRECTED` emits kind 15, since callers must distinguish "address changed" from "reloading". ② The load-failed payload is structured as `uri|domain|code|message`, with `domain` given as a name through `g_quark_to_string`, and MoonBit's `nav_error_parse` splitting it into `NavError`. Error text may contain `|`, so the first three segments are taken positionally and the remainder all belongs to message; too few segments gives `None` rather than guessing fields.
- **One seam defect only the real window could catch**: `WebEvent` **has** `LoadFailed`, but the kind table in `Webview::dispatch` **never listed 14**, so every failure arrived as `Unknown(14, raw)` and the caller could never read the reason. The headless suite claimed a "kind→event case-by-case mapping" and still missed it, because the table being walked had itself skipped 14: **each half had tests, the mapping between them had none**. Now 2/3/4/14/15 are all pinned in that test, plus one end-to-end case — dispatch 14 → `LoadFailed` → `nav_error_parse` splitting four segments.
- **Pages installed with `load_html` do not enter forward/back history** (measured on the real window; do not read this as back being broken): the bridge page was installed with `load_html`, then a click on a nonexistent domain — the example's `a.example`, since `.example` is an RFC 2606 reserved domain and DNS must fail — read `can_back=0 can_fwd=0` with `go_back()` a no-op. **But the root cause is not "a failed navigation cleared history"** — testing the four steps separately makes it clear:
  ```
  after-load_html  url=https://local.test/  can_back=0   ← load_html does not enter history
  after-ok-nav     url=https://example.com/ can_back=1   ← a successful navigation enters history
  after-fail-nav   url=https://a.example/1  can_back=1   ← a failed navigation does not clear history
  after-go_back    url=https://example.com/ can_fwd=1    ← it really went back
  ```
  A failed navigation still leaves a back-stack state; that reading was 0 only because the bridge page's history had nothing besides the `load_html` entry. **Cross-platform consistent**: WebView2's documentation for `NavigateToString` states plainly "the back or forward history will not be modified", the same shape as the Linux measurement; Apple makes no promise for macOS's `loadHTMLString:baseURL:`, to be verified on mac hardware and already recorded in TODO. **Two conventions**: ① a no-op determined by engine semantics must be stated honestly in the UI — the example's button now logs either `后退 → url` or `后退：无处可退（can_go_back=0；load_html 不入历史）` — otherwise it simply looks like a bug. ② To give a local page real history, use the custom protocol above to give it a real URL and `load_url`, not `load_html`.
- **The custom protocol's public surface tightened to "names declared in advance"** (2026-10-12, strictest platform wins): Linux allows registering a new scheme per context at any time, but WebView2's list hangs on the **environment options**, before creating the environment, once per process, and WKWebView's on the configuration **before the view is created**. Treating "add names at runtime" as public semantics means writing code that fails on Windows/mac. Now: `webview_predeclare_schemes([...])`, before the first webview → `register_protocol(scheme, root)` accepting only declared names, with the root directory changeable at any time and `unregister_protocol` still replacing with an error handler. The list is sealed at view creation by `webview_seal_schemes()`; an empty list fills in the default name `app`, so zero configuration works. Linux's dynamic capability stays in the stub, not exposed. **Verification**: `web` 16/16 — new case: creating the view seals the list, an undeclared name's registration is refused, and declaring after sealing returns false leaving the list unchanged; real window `NATIVE-WEB-SCHEME reg=1 loads=1 files=2`, the example calling `webview_predeclare_schemes(["yuedemo"])` before creating the view, with the protocol page working as before.
- **Protocol registration must also accept "before mount"** (2026-10-12, caught while converting the bridge window to a protocol page): a pane's view is built on the frame when it first receives a real rectangle, and `register_protocol` judged on `handle != 0L`, so anything before mount returned false — the caller had to schedule its own wait. `load_html` already had `pending_html`, so one matter had two rules. `pending_protos` was added: `(scheme, root)` queued before mount and applied by `mount_at` right after the view is built; `unregister_protocol` first withdraws a pending registration, returning true when it withdrew something and still false when nothing was registered — "not mounted" is not "arbitrary success". **Acceptance check**: the example's first run fell onto the `load_html` fallback branch and printed `协议未就绪`, which was exactly this seam.
- **The protocol channel returns MIME only, so text types without a pinned charset arrive garbled** (screenshot from real hardware in the same batch): `wb_mime_of` returned bare `text/html` for `.html`, WebKit had no other basis to guess an encoding and decoded as ISO-8859-1, so a Chinese page came out garbled across the screen, `桥接页大标题` becoming mojibake. Fix in two places: the stub returns `charset=utf-8` for text extensions — html/css/js/json/txt — and the page adds `<meta charset="utf-8">`. Each alone suffices, but **only the HTTP header is reliable over a protocol**, since `<meta>` takes effect only after decoding reaches that byte, while the first screen's bytes were already decoded with the wrong table. **Verification**: `web` 16/16, and `web` plus `examples/native-web` `--deny-warn` zero warnings; the real-window screenshot shows the protocol page's Chinese correct, and the event area's `后退 → yuedemo://local/bridge.html` proves the protocol page **is in history** and back really works — control: the same page installed with `load_html` had back as a no-op — with the exit line `navs=5 … dom_ok=1 text_bytes=68 … last='标题 本地桥接页'`.
- **The protocol channel supplies MIME only, so text types must carry `charset=utf-8` themselves** (mojibake caught in the real window): the same bridge page HTML was fine through `load_html` and became whole-page `æ¡¥æŽ¥é¡µ` through `yuedemo://`. Root cause: the two channels differ in encoding basis — `webkit_web_view_load_html` takes UTF-8 text as its input, so the engine decodes as UTF-8, while a protocol reply passes only a content type, and bare `text/html` without an encoding declaration is decoded by WebKit as ISO-8859-1; the page's `<meta charset>` is visible only after tags are parsed, and the tags were already decoded wrongly. Fix closed once at the stub: `wb_mime_of` returns `...; charset=utf-8` for html/css/js/mjs/json/txt, leaving binaries and images alone. **Convention**: over a protocol, MIME is the only encoding basis for text; do not count on the page's `<meta>`, though the in-page declaration is still written, since it is needed when the file is opened in another browser.
- **Registrations made before mount must be accepted, otherwise the natural "register first, then load" order falls on the caller to wait**: the view is built on the frame when it first receives a real rectangle, and `register_protocol` returned false while unmounted. The bridge window in the example took exactly this path: right after `win.mount`, registration returned false, it fell back to `load_html`, and the page's back button was permanently a no-op. Now it shares the shape with `pending_html`: unmounted means recorded in `pending_protos`, applied one by one by `mount_at` after the view is built, and `unregister_protocol` can withdraw a registration not yet applied, returning true when it withdrew something and false when there was nothing to withdraw — "not mounted" is not "arbitrary success". **The example's check changed accordingly**: the bridge page now goes through the protocol, since only a real URL has real history, and on registration failure it no longer degrades silently — the event area states `协议未就绪，退回 load_html（此页不入历史）`.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/web` **16/16** — 4 new headless: `nav_error_parse`'s four segments with `|` inside message and with too few segments; `nav_parse_int`'s minus sign and stopping at a non-digit; unmounted registration accepted, unregister withdrawable, double unregister false; the kind-14 seam above. `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/sys` **164/164** — 1 new `sys_make_dirs`: create level by level, write, read back; idempotent; empty string rejected; writing fails when the parent is missing. `moon check sys`/`web`/`./examples/native-web` `--deny-warn` zero warnings. Real-window evidence — `examples/native-web`'s "batch C remainder" row, with the two checks run separately — ① loading the protocol page: `NATIVE-WEB-SCHEME reg=1 loads=1 files=2 unreg=0 title='本地协议页'` plus `NATIVE-WEB-STAT ... title='本地协议页' url='yuedemo://local/index.html'`, the screenshot giving two hard pieces of evidence: the page title is the protocol page's `<title>` and the body paragraph carries a blue background, so `style.css` also came over `yuedemo://` rather than inline. ② Reloading the same URL after unregistering: `unreg=1 fails=1 raw=0 fail='WebKitNetworkError/399 yuedemo://local/index.html' title=''`, with the page area drawing the text given by `finish_error` verbatim — on screen the single line `scheme unregistered` — proving "unregister = replace with an error handler" really works and that the failure reason is a **structure**, not a string. One enum fact found along the way: `WEBKIT_NETWORK_ERROR_FAILED = 399`, not the intuitive -1. ③ Four pieces of evidence after the bridge page moved to the protocol, injecting clicks and reading the event area from screenshots: `导航开始 yuedemo://local/bridge.html` → clicking link 甲 gives `加载失败 g-resolver-error-quark/0 https://a.example/1` → clicking back gives `后退 → yuedemo://local/bridge.html`, **this time really going back**, whereas the `load_html` version was permanently a no-op → the page area's Chinese title, body and links all correct, with `抓正文 ok=1 title=本地桥接页 链接=0`, DOM capture running against the protocol page and the title read back as UTF-8. **The user re-verified on real hardware (2026-10-12)**: the protocol page's Chinese renders correctly, clicking a reserved-domain link reports a structured reason, and back really returns to the bridge page. One convention left for whoever comes next: when neither window is given its own data directory they share one context, so the main window's "unregister this protocol" clears the bridge window's root directory as well — re-registering restores it, and the example's comment says so.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · JS bridge / DOM capture / navigation surface (batch C: the webkit stub and contract of `web`)

- **Asynchronous events all go "queue in C, drain from MoonBit" - no C-to-MoonBit trampolines**: navigation, title, JS results, page `invoke`, permission, download and process termination are all engine-side async signals; giving each a closure trampoline means managing 12 callback lifetimes and thread affinities by hand. The shape here is one 32-slot ring per view (`wb_next_event` yields the kind, `wb_event_num`/`wb_event_text` read the payload), and a **full queue drops the oldest** - events are hints, not a ledger, and blocking on them would stall the main loop.
- **The pump is not hooked into painting**: a result callback may mount or unmount widgets (e.g. redraw a list after capturing links), and mutating the tree mid-paint is exactly what this stack avoids (`Widget::paint_at` is translating and clipping layer by layer). So mounting starts a self-rescheduling `@core.set_timeout(30, ...)` pump, and `close` stops it.
- **`load_html` must not be dropped before mounting** (hit on the real window in this batch): a pane mounts on the frame where it first gets a real rectangle, so calling `load_html` right after `win.mount(...)` found handle 0 and the page area stayed at `about:blank`. The acceptance check: `navs=1` with only about:blank in the events and every capture empty. Same fix as `load_url`: record `pending_html` and apply it in `mount_at` right after the view is created.
- **Brace balance in the capture scripts must be pinned**: the four variants each appended their own `}})` and one extra closing brace slipped in, so the page replied `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '}'`. Marking that `ok=false` in the parser is correct (no silent success), but the generator needs a lock: a single wrapper `dom_wrap(fields)` (variants only write their own fields) plus assertions that `{`/`}` and `(`/`)` counts match and the script ends with `})`.
- **2.52 has exactly one permission entry point**: the `decide-policy` enum has **no** `WEBKIT_POLICY_DECISION_TYPE_PERMISSION_REQUEST` (only NAVIGATION_ACTION / NEW_WINDOW_ACTION / RESPONSE), so permissions must come from the `"permission-request"` signal; and `webkit_permission_request_allow(request)` **takes one argument** (not the old `(request, gboolean)`). Returning TRUE from the handler means "we dealt with it", so default-deny is "report the event + return TRUE", and allowing is "explicitly allow, then still return TRUE".
- **`g_signal_lookup` before connecting optional signals**, and expose the result as a mask (`wb_signal_mask()`: 1 download / 2 process-terminated / 4 permission / 8 new-window). Whichever bit is missing is a missing piece of evidence - never let "the callback never fired" and "it is not implemented" collapse into the same symptom.
- **Two API shapes that read backwards**: ① under webkit2gtk-4.1 (this build links libsoup-3.0, whose headers and libraries come along with `pkg-config --cflags/--libs webkit2gtk-4.1`) `webkit_cookie_manager_get_cookies_finish` returns a **`GList`, not a `GSList`**, whose elements are `SoupCookie`; ② from 2.40 `webkit_web_view_evaluate_javascript_finish` hands back a **`JSCValue*`** directly (only the old `run_javascript_finish` gave a `WebKitJavascriptResult*`), and `jsc_value_to_string` on a JS string returns the content **without quotes** - so the structured payload is the JSON text itself, with no extra layer to strip.
- **Profile hangs off the pane**: a non-empty `data_dir` in `wb_create` goes through `webkit_website_data_manager_new(base-data-directory, base-cache-directory)` + `webkit_web_context_new_with_website_data_manager` + `webkit_web_view_new_with_context`; empty uses the default context with its own user content manager. `browser_profile_persistence()` is always `Persistent` on Linux - the "macOS 14+ plus a bundle id" API boundary is Apple's - and the probe stays, so callers never branch on platform.
- **Two example-side counting pitfalls**: ① with one shared counter set for four capture variants, the last variant (structure) has no body text or links, so plain assignment erased the earlier evidence - take maxima instead; ② grabbing a top-level window that owns a child X window (WebKit) with `import -window <id>` yields striped garbage; capture the composited screen with `import -window root -crop WxH+X+Y`.
- **Contract names follow the old chain** (`load_url`/`get_url`/`get_title`/`reload`/`stop`/`go_back`/`go_forward`/`can_go_back`/`can_go_forward`/`is_loading`/`load_html`/`set_user_agent`/`execute_javascript`/`execute_javascript_with_result`/`add_user_script`/`add_raw_binding`/`remove_binding`/`has_bindings`/`get_cookies_for_url`), with `current_url` as an alias of `get_url`. `remove_binding`/`remove_all_user_scripts` always return false with the reason written down: WebKit has no unregister entry point, and that must not read as a defect of this stack. `window.open` is intercepted and reported by default, with an opt-in "navigate in this pane" - this stack does not do one-window-many-webviews.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/web` **11/11** (9 new headless: capture-script shape and brace balance; structured parsing of all four JSON variants; parse failure keeps `ok=false` plus the raw text; every call safe while unmounted with `capture_dom`/`add_raw_binding`/result-carrying eval returning false/-1; kind→`WebEvent` mapping item by item; JS results paired by sequence and delivered exactly once; invoke on both paths (`on_invoke` plus the `on_event` side channel); persistence probe consistent with engine availability). `moon check web` and `./examples/native-web` clean under `--deny-warn`; core 70/70 and ui 110/110 unchanged; whole-repo backlog still 287 errors / 68 warnings. Real-window evidence (`examples/native-web`, the "开一扇桥接窗" button = a second window hosting a `load_html` local page, no network needed): `NATIVE-WEB-JS binding=1 evals=1 dom_ok=4 dom_bad=0 links=3 text_bytes=68 meta=1 headings=2 elements=14 invokes=1 navs=2 perms=1 wins=1 crashes=0 cookie_bytes=2 last='invoke {"msg":"来自页面","n":7}'`; the composited screenshot carries three hard facts - the page body reads "已被原生改过" (native→page `execute_javascript` really mutated the DOM), the native event area lists "页面回话 {...} / 权限请求（默认拒绝）WebKitGeolocationPermissionRequest / 新窗请求已拦下 https://b.example/2", and the bridge window count stays 1 (the new window was intercepted rather than spawning a second webview). **Re-verified by the user (2026-10-12)**: in-page scrolling and link clicks work, and our pure-channel IME yields while the webview holds focus and comes back after clicking into a native entry.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · panes and the webview channel (batch B: `win/surface.mbt` + new package `web`)

- **Window content became a `GtkFixed` holding "drawing area + positionable children"**, not a `GtkOverlay`: an overlay needs `pass_through` to let events through the container, and event ownership for a container that itself has children is unreliable there (the container being transparent does not imply its children behave). `GtkFixed` is an ordinary container - a pointer over a child belongs to that child, anywhere else to the drawing area, **with no extra mechanism**. The price is tracking the size ourselves: `set_size_request` on the drawing area from the fixed's `size-allocate`, gated by "only when the size actually changed" - `set_size_request` triggers another allocation round, so unconditionally setting it self-oscillates.
- **The surface table must record its owning window**: `WmSurface{container, window_id, kind, x,y,w,h}`, and `wm_close(window)` clears every surface belonging to that window. Otherwise the window is torn down first and the capability layer (the webkit stub) still calls `gtk_fixed_put` with a dangling `GtkWidget*` - segfault. Surface slots are recycled the same way as the window slots in batch A (scan for `container == NULL`).
- **Pointers travel C-to-C, MoonBit only carries integers**: win exports `wm_surface_container(int64) -> GtkWidget*` and `web/webkit_stub.c` declares it `extern` (same executable, static link). That keeps `web`'s MoonBit layer from importing `win`'s MoonBit layer, so the dependency rule "webview depends only on the window/layout/event layers" holds.
- **A missing webkit SDK is a degradation, not an error**: `scripts/prebuild.py` probes `webkit2gtk-4.1`; found -> compile with `-DWB_HAVE_WEBKIT` and hand `-lwebkit2gtk-4.1` to `web`; not found -> compile the **macro-less** stub implementation (`wb_available()` returns 0). Either way the `wb_*` symbols must exist, otherwise it is a link-time failure rather than a run-time degradation. The stub's branch shape mirrors win: `#if defined(WB_HAVE_WEBKIT)` / `#elif !defined(__linux__)` / otherwise an empty translation unit, so nothing is defined twice against prebuild's `.a`. Link order puts `-lyue_web` before `-lyue_win_stub` (the former references the latter's symbol).
- **Sub-pixel values must be rounded, not truncated**: pane rectangles come from yoga as Doubles and are synced to the surface every frame. With truncation a 0.4 px drift makes "the rectangle changed" permanently true, so every frame pays an extra FFI call plus a native relayout. The rule lives in the pure function `webview_rect_key` (`round()`, same treatment for negative coordinates) and the dedup compares the rounded key.
- **`ChildKind` is a register, not an open set**: only `Webview = 1` today. The child surface keeps exactly the "embed a native control" meaning (plan §4.5); allowing custom values would turn "not a general sub-surface" back into an empty phrase.
- **Verification**: new package `web` headless 2/2 (rounding and dedup key; probe/constructor agreement with zero handles before mounting; `close` safe when never mounted); `moon check win` / `web` / `./examples/native-web` clean under `--deny-warn`; core 70/70 and ui 110/110 unchanged; whole-repo backlog still 287 errors / 68 warnings. Real-window evidence (`examples/native-web`, this host X11/XFCE + WebKitGTK 2.52.6): split layout gives `NATIVE-WEB-STAT supported=1 loading=0 title='Example Domain' url='https://example.com/'` with `NATIVE-WEB-GEO pane=262,71,848x605 sidebar=12,71,240x605` (two non-overlapping panes); injecting "toggle full/split + load + one click inside the page area" yields `loads=1 toggles=1 mode=full pane=12,71,1098x605`, and the screenshots confirm WebKit really renders the page and reflows to the new width after switching to full - **one pane mechanism producing both layouts**. **Left for the user's eyes**: scrolling and link clicks inside the page, and whether our pure-channel IME really yields while the webview holds focus (and comes back after).

### MoonBit native GUI stack · multi-window host (`core/host.mbt`: one host, N windows)

- **Shape**: one window = one `App` (its own platform window + widget tree + `FocusStack` + IME/hover/capture state). Windows share exactly two things - the `Loop` (one process-wide time base, built once by `host_loop()`) and the platform pump (`@win.wait`/`wake` were already process-level). The registry only answers "which windows exist, which is current, does closing one quit the host"; `App::step` now drains events per window, pumps the IME per window and paints the dirty ones, always iterating a `host_windows()` **snapshot** (a window can close mid-drain and mutate the table).
- **The closing verdict**: the first window in the registry is the primary one; only closing the primary - or the last remaining - quits the host (`host_close_action(primary, remaining)` is a pure function, headless-testable). Closing a secondary window just removes it. The teardown order stays "stop dispatch first, then destroy": `running=false` -> deregister -> `window.close()`. `App::shutdown` destroys **every** window still registered (secondaries may be open); handles already recycled to -1 make `wm_close` idempotent.
- **Two process-wide single slots had to be upgraded or multi-window draws/queries wrong**: ① the `invalidate()` repaint hook became a **broadcast** (mark every live window dirty + one wake) - a Store shared by two windows then repaints both, and an over-marked window only wastes one frame; ② the overlay host slot became a **resolver** (`set_overlay_provider(() -> OverlayHost?)`) so popups open on the **current window** (a new window becomes current on creation, whichever window receives input becomes current, and closing the current one falls back to the last registered). `set_overlay_host(h)` survives as the static form for headless tests.
- **A latent design flaw this batch exposed**: overlay handles used to restart at 1 per host, so "handle 1" meant different layers in different windows. Handles are now process-wide increasing (`overlay_cid()`) plus `overlay_ids()`/`overlay_top_id()`. The symptom was not a compile error but a **test crash**: a dozen call sites in `ui` hardcoded `overlay_root_of(1)`, and once ids accumulated the lookup returned `None` and `children()[0]` aborted with `Array::at` out of bounds (SIGABRT). Rule: **handles are allocated at run time - use the return value or `top_id()`, never a literal**.
- **`raise` is a MoonBit keyword**: `pub fn OverlayHost::raise(...)` does not report "reserved word"; the whole function header fails to parse and the errors cascade into `The value identifier self is unbound` plus `unexpected token if, you may expect pub|fn|...`, which looks like a broken body. Renamed to `raise_layer`; the tell is that the first error points at the header line.
- **The GTK stub must recycle window slots**: `wm_window_new` used to only `wm_next_id++`, so opening and closing secondary windows would exhaust the 32 slots (and `App::open_window` would silently return None). It now takes the first slot with `area == NULL` - `area` is always set at creation and `wm_close` memsets the record, so "closed" and "never used" are equally free.
- **Cross-window injection pitfall: clicking raises another window** (XFCE defaults to click-to-raise). In the first round the "close this window" click seemed dead (`closes=0`), looking like a broken button; in fact the earlier click on the main window had raised it over the About window, so that click landed on the main window. Rule: **`xdotool windowactivate --sync <target>` before every cross-window click**, and judge by an observable state (does `xdotool search --name 关于` still list it) rather than by a counter alone.
- **Two example-side rules**: ① each About window owns its **own Store** (sharing one makes "which window got the typing" meaningless and the exit readouts overwrite each other); ② the smoke self-quit timer moved from 12 s to 25 s - the multi-window flow (open -> click and type in the second window -> close -> reopen) does not fit in 12 s.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/core` **70/70** (8 new headless registry tests: `host_loop` returning the same Loop - proved with `pending()` since `started()` cannot prove identity; primary/secondary bookkeeping and active fallback; the three closing verdicts; `close_window` idempotence and a secondary not stopping the primary; `invalidate` broadcasting; overlays landing on the current window with independent stacks and handles per window; `mount` raising only its own layer; `shutdown` destroying all windows and resetting the registry). `ui` 110/110, `chart` 189/189, `mdview` 26/26, `render` 42/42, `text` 29/29, `input` 10/10, `theme` 8/8, `sys` 163/163, `dbus` 64/64, `yoga-mbt` 96/96 all green; `moon check ./examples/native-app` and `./examples/native-sys` clean under `--deny-warn`; whole-repo backlog still 287 errors / 68 warnings. Real-window evidence (`examples/native-app`, the "多窗口（批 A）" panel at the top plus the "关于（第二窗）" window): `NATIVE-APP-MW wins=1 opened=1 closes=1 main_clicks=1 sub_clicks=2 sub_entry_bytes=2 sub_focus=101` and the geometry line `NATIVE-APP-MW-GEO open=688,262,160x32 sub_btn=16,53,464x32 sub_entry=16,85,280x32 sub_close=16,117,464x32`; the injected sequence was "open -> two clicks in the second window -> type and commit in its entry -> the main window's control click -> close the second window -> open another", with `xdotool search --name 关于` going from present to absent while the main window id stayed alive the whole time (**closing one window does not affect the host**), and the About window screenshot showing "本窗点击 2 / 在窗 2" plus the committed text in its entry (**one tree per window, focus stack per window**). **Left for the user's eyes**: repaint while dragging/occluding two windows, and the preedit underline inside the About window.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · single instance and the logind brightness bridge (`dbus`: instance closing + `bridge.mbt`)

- **Single instance = bus-name claiming plus a Wake inbound call**: the first instance takes `RequestName(app_id, DO_NOT_QUEUE)` and gets `PrimaryOwner` (a repeated claim yields the idempotent `AlreadyOwner`); a second instance that gets `AlreadyExists`/`InQueue` instead calls the first instance's `org.moonbitlibyue.Instance.Wake('as' argv)` and exits. The first instance answers the Wake before firing its callback (`is_wake_call` is checked first in `bus.mbt`'s inbound branch - the second instance's `call_sync` has a deadline, so slow work like raising a window must not make it wait). Example evidence: launching a second copy while the first runs prints "已有实例，已唤起并退出" with `exit=0` in the second, and "收到第二实例的唤起" in the first.
- **The brightness write path is wired one way only**: `dbus` depends on `sys` (environment, subprocesses, sysfs reads) and not vice versa, so `bridge.mbt` **injects** the logind capability into sys's two slots at startup (`brightness_set_logind_probe` for the probe, `brightness_set_action` for the `(subsystem, name, value) -> error string` action) and sys never imports D-Bus. Measured here: after injection `@sys.brightness_supported()` flips from the fake default to true (`logind_available=true`), while `brightness_devices()` still reads only sysfs (0 devices on this desktop) - the injection line cleanly separates the read path's and the write path's dependencies.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/dbus` **64/64** (2 new: the brightness gate matching logind's availability after injection, and a repeated same-process name claim yielding `AlreadyOwner`); `moon check ./examples/native-sys --deny-warn` clean; real-window evidence as above (`pool=:1.483`, second instance `exit=0`). **Left for the user on a real machine**: `brightness_set_percent` actually changing the screen needs a machine with a backlight (this host is a desktop with no `/sys/class/backlight` device).

### MoonBit native GUI stack · SNI tray and DBusMenu (`dbus`: sni + icon + instance + filemanager)

- **Migration surface**: the old chain's `traybus` files `sni.mbt` (731 lines, the StatusNotifierItem object side plus a DBusMenu server), `icon.mbt` (75, the program-generated default icon bitmap), `instance.mbt` (221, single-instance name claiming/waking) and `filemanager.mbt` (98, FileManager1 `ShowItems`) ported line by line into `dbus`. **The tray hooks previously stripped from `bus.mbt` came back in the same batch**: the `Conn.items`/`menus` registries, re-registration of every item after a `NameOwnerChanged(arg0=watcher)` watcher restart, carrying tray items along during reconnect migration, and the three-way inbound dispatch (single-instance `Wake` replies first and fires after -> a path hitting `items`/`menus` goes to SNI's `handle_call` -> the `CallReq` fallback last). This is the "foundation strips semantics, capability modules put them back" way of closing out.
- **Tests came along, `inspect` became `assert`**: `sni_wbtest` (212) / `instance_wbtest` (93) / `filemanager_wbtest` (24), with 40-odd old `inspect(x, content=…)` calls replaced this batch.
- **Real-bus evidence (protocol half of rule 5)**: on this host the XFCE panel (`xfce4-panel`) *is* the StatusNotifierWatcher. After clicking "托盘图标" in the example, the watcher's `RegisteredStatusNotifierItems` went from **9 to 10 entries** (the extra one being this process's item), and it is unregistered symmetrically before exit; the `sni_wbtest` live cases create several tray items, verify their paths and menu objects never collide, and confirm both registries are clean after unregistration.
- **A test-environment pitfall (acceptance check first)**: running the create-unregister tray tests repeatedly occasionally yields `托盘注册失败: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NoReply`, or `NameHasOwner` returning something other than true. The cause is not the code: **a test process has no main loop, so the panel's synchronous property queries to our items can only be serviced incidentally inside a `call_sync` pump**; after several rounds a single xfce4-panel query wedges and subsequent registrations time out. The acceptance check is "a re-run is clean, and `dbus-send` still lists `RegisteredStatusNotifierItems`"; the fix is not to leave the test process unpumped for long (the example's host pumps every 200 ms and never sees this). A temporary debug print was used to pin the branch and then removed.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/dbus` **62/62** (12 new: sni 6 / instance 4 / file manager 2), three consecutive runs with zero skips; `moon check ./examples/native-sys --deny-warn` clean, `moon build` passes; real-window evidence `pool=:1.479`, five-button geometry line `tray=747,391,110x32`, exit code 0. **Left for the user's eyes**: after clicking "托盘图标", does an icon appear in the XFCE notification area, does right-clicking it show the "刷新探测 / 退出" menu, and does clicking the icon increment the "托盘点击" counter in the window.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · D-Bus capability modules, first batch (`dbus`: UPower/logind/network/screensaver/inhibit/MPRIS + notifications)

- **Migration surface**: the old chain's `traybus` files `upower` (197 lines) / `logind` (105) / `netmon` (191) / `screensaver` (94) / `inhibit` (146), plus `yue/system/media.mbt` (707 lines, MPRIS), ported line by line into `dbus` (package prefixes swapped only; media's `pr_run`/`pr_available` now point at `@sys`). **Their tests came along in the same batch, and every old `inspect(x, content=…)` became `assert_eq/assert_true`** - those inspects asserted nothing on the native backend (recorded twice before), so porting them unchanged would have meant "all green, zero coverage"; this batch alone contained 54 of them.
- **MPRIS polling moved to an injected schedule channel**: master's `media_watch_status` hooked `@yue.set_timer` directly (its callback returned a Bool to decide whether to keep ticking); the new stack gives it a `schedule : (Int, () -> Unit) -> Unit` parameter (the GUI layer passes `@core.set_timeout`, headless tests pass a fake channel that collects the callbacks) and re-arms internally via `arm()` - the same layering reason as `clipboard_watch` and the theme probe: a capability package does not know about an event loop.
- **Notifications are new work** (master's implementation lives in the C++ libyue with only a thin MoonBit wrapper, so the new stack had to rewrite it): `notify_caps` uses `GetCapabilities` (**no side effects**; the capability list is not translated into an enum, the raw entries stay available), while `notify_send`/`notify_close` use `Notify`/`CloseNotification`. **Progress is not a method of its own** - per the freedesktop spec it means re-sending `Notify` with `replaces_id` set to the same notification and a standard `value` hint (INT32, 0..100; this layer clamps above 100 and treats negatives as "no progress"), which desktop daemons render as a progress bar; `notify_progress` has exactly that shape, and the argument order plus hint shape are pinned by the pure function `nf_notify_args`.
- **Setting-class discipline**: sending a notification really pops a bubble on the desktop, so tests stop at "capability probe + argument construction + error normalisation (unknown method / no service)"; the actual send is left to the button in the example for the user to click (the same rule as open_url/reveal).
- **Example wiring and real-window evidence**: `examples/native-sys` gained a "窗口 / 剪贴板 / D-Bus" panel (session unique name / notification capability count / system bus "not connected (connects on first use)"), a "发通知(带进度)" button, and the host pump (`dbus_set_post_delayed` wrapped around `app.timer`, plus `dbus_pump()` every 200 ms). A full run ends with `pool=:1.434` (the connection is alive the whole time, proving the injected pump really feeds the bus), notification capabilities = 7, exit code 0, and a screenshot confirms all five rows.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/dbus` **50/50** (27 new: UPower 4 / logind 2 / network 3 / screensaver 2 / MPRIS 12 / notifications 4), `moon check ./examples/native-sys --deny-warn` clean. **Left for the user on a real machine**: clicking "发通知(带进度)" should pop a bubble whose progress grows with each click (this host's xfce4-notifyd already reports 7 capabilities over the real bus); and the four monitors (UPower/logind/network/screensaver) need real-world events - plugging/unplugging power, locking the screen, dropping the network - to observe.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · D-Bus foundation (new package `dbus`: wire + dbus + bus + socket stub)

- **Migration surface**: the old chain's `yue/traybus/` `wire.mbt` (833 lines of wire-format codec) and `dbus.mbt` (419 lines, the `GDBusValue` generic call layer) are ported **line by line** (only `sys_f64_to_bits/from_bits` gain new FFI names), while `bus.mbt` (784 lines) is adapted: connect / SASL / Hello / send / receive / dispatch / reconnect all stay, but the **SNI and single-instance semantics embedded in the generic layer are stripped out** (`items`/`menus` fields, the watcher special case, the inbound `Wake` branch) - those come back with their own capability modules.
- **The biggest layering difference: no glib fd watch.** The old chain used `g_unix_fd_add` to hang the bus fd on the GTK main loop and libyue's `PostDelayedTask` for reconnect backoff; this stack bans glib and does not depend on the GUI layer either, so there are two injection points instead: the host calls `dbus_pump()` periodically (default `timeout_ms=0`, a non-blocking poll, fine on every frame/tick), and reconnect backoff goes through `dbus_set_post_delayed(fn(ms, f){...})`. **With neither injected, synchronous calls still work** - `call_sync` and `gdbus_call_*` carry their own `pump_until` pump (handshake, Hello and registration all use it), so a pure CLI scenario needs no event loop at all; the price is that "nobody pumps, no async signals", which the package header states outright.
- **The socket stub uses only standard headers** (`dbus_stub.c`, compiled through native-stub, no link flags written): `socket(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM|SOCK_NONBLOCK|SOCK_CLOEXEC)` + `connect` (tolerating `EINPROGRESS`) / `read` / `write` / single-fd `poll` / `close` / `getuid` / Double bit patterns (`memcpy` reinterpretation guarded by a `static_assert` on 8 bytes). Its error-code conventions are **bit-for-bit identical** to the old shim (read: >0 bytes / 0 peer-closed / -1 EAGAIN·EINTR / -2 otherwise; write: >=0 written / -1 not writable yet / -2 otherwise; poll: revents bits 1=IN 4=OUT 8=ERR 16=HUP), so none of the upper-layer branching changed.
- **SASL EXTERNAL needs no explicit credential passing**: the kernel attaches `SCM_CREDENTIALS` at connect time and the server reads `SO_PEERCRED`; the client only sends `AUTH EXTERNAL <hex(uid)>` (the old shim has no `sendmsg` either - this was verified, not assumed).
- **One place the public surface is cleaner than the old chain**: inbound method calls used to require a handler with same-package access to the priv `Conn`/`Msg` in order to reply; the new package exposes `CallReq{bus, sender, path, iface, action, args, reply, reply_error}`, where `reply` **derives its signature from the argument values** (`gdbus_args_wire`), and signal subscribers receive decoded `GDBusValue` arrays only - wire-format value types never leak, so capability modules and outside callers see the same shape.
- **Three toolchain findings (measured this batch)**: ① struct literal fields use `field: value`; writing `=` gives `Unexpected '=' in struct expression`; ② **a function-typed struct field is not a method** - `req.reply_error(...)` fails with `Type CallReq has no method reply_error`, so bind it first (`let f = req.reply_error`) and call that; ③ `;` is not a comment (nor is `;;`); using it inline triggers a cascade of parse errors.
- **Real-bus evidence (the bus half of rule 5)**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/dbus` **23/23** - session handshake succeeds (local unique name `:1.392`), `ListNames` really returns and contains `org.freedesktop.DBus`, an unknown-method call really yields the D-Bus error name and text, signal `AddMatch` really registers, `dbus_pump` idles without blocking or declaring death, and the system bus `ListNames` returns 96 names. **The panel half (a tray icon actually appearing in the XFCE notification area) and notification popups remain for the user on a real machine**, to be covered by the SNI/notify batches.
- **Later batches**: SNI tray + DBusMenu (with real-panel verification), notifications (`org.freedesktop.Notifications` and `set_progress`), UPower/logind/NetworkManager/screensaver/MPRIS monitors, single instance, and the real logind `SetBrightness` injection for `brightness`.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · cumulative system-capability page (`examples/native-sys`)

- **One page for all of `sys`**: five panels (system & machine / desktop & hardware / apps & file types / windows & clipboard / recent & history) are all **read-only** probes; of the three buttons only "重新探测" (re-probe) is read-only - that is the one injection clicks - while "打开链接" and "打开目录" are setting-class and only act once clicked. Exit prints two lines: `NATIVE-SYS-GEO probe=… open=… reveal=…` (injection points) and `NATIVE-SYS-STAT os=… de=… mon=… wp=… vol=… prof=… mime=… def=… apps=… recent=… hist=… dl=… bm=… ffx=… vsc=… wins=… clip=… probes=… opens=… reveals=… changes=…`, matching the on-screen readings one by one. A run on this host: `os=ubuntu de=XFCE mon=9 wp=ok vol=65 mime=text/plain def=sublime_text.desktop apps=179 recent=156 hist=5 dl=5 bm=166 vsc=1 wins=9 probes=3`, exit code 0.
- **`@core.App`'s root container defaults to Row**: calling only `app.mount([...])` without `app.root.set_column()` lays the panels side by side and pushes them out of the window (the first version of this page had the button's rect at x=1442 in a 1200-wide window, so every injected click missed). `examples/native-app` starts with `root.set_column()`; a new page must do the same, and a panel row that really is horizontal needs an explicit `direction=@yoga.Row`.
- **An injection count lower than the click count is not a lost event**: one re-probe re-reads whole databases (Chrome's `History` is 37 MB here), the UI thread blocks while doing it, and a click arriving too soon is split - press before the block, release during/after it - so it does not count. Acceptance check: three clicks spaced 1.6 s give `probes=3`, clicks inside 1 s give 1 - **injection scripts must leave a beat for heavy work**.
- **How the clipboard watcher is wired**: `@sys.cbw_start_watch(fn(ms, f) { let _ = app.timer(ms, f) }, cb, interval_ms=1000)` - the host supplies the scheduling channel and `sys` never learns about an event loop (headless tests drive it with a fake channel, see the previous entry). This host has no xclip, so the page honestly shows `ClipboardError::Unsupported`; that is not a page defect.
- **Verification**: `moon check ./examples/native-sys --deny-warn` clean, `moon build ./examples/native-sys` passes; `sys` 163/163, `core` 62/62, `ui` 110/110, `chart` 189/189, `mdview` 26/26, `render` 42/42 all green; whole-repo backlog still 287 errors / 68 warnings, unchanged. **Left for the user's eyes**: whether "打开链接" raises the default browser and whether "打开目录" opens `/tmp` in the file manager - injection only proves the button really handed the action to the system call, not the window on the other side.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · system integration, the three bus-free status items (`sys`: sysinfo + windowctl + clipboard_watch)

- **The file-reading stub must not size buffers from `ftell` alone (a real bug fixed this batch; it affected every read that went through this stub)**: pseudo-files under `/proc/meminfo`, `/proc/uptime` and `/sys/class/dmi/id/*` report **0 bytes** for `lseek(END)` - their content only appears when actually read. The old shape (`fseek(END)` → `ftell` → allocate that size → `fread`) hit exactly this: pseudo-files returned `Ok("")` (**not an error**), so callers saw a parse failure and blamed the data format. `yue_sys_read_text_file` now uses ftell only as a hint and loops `fread` to EOF (one path for regular files and for tens-of-megabyte SQLite databases), and the two live assertions (MemTotal/MemAvailable, uptime seconds) flipped from red to green. **Acceptance check**: a pseudo-file read that "succeeds but is empty" points at how the length was taken, not at permissions.
- **Window / clipboard / clock capabilities go through commands**: `windowctl` parses `wmctrl -l -p` (list), `-i -a` (activate by id) and `-c` (close by title); `clipboard_watch` polls `xclip -selection clipboard -o` read-only - a missing xclip surfaces as exit code 127 and is normalised to `Unsupported` (matching "tool absent" rather than "command failed"); `sysinfo` only reads `/etc/os-release`, `/proc/meminfo`, `/proc/uptime` and `/sys/class/dmi/id/`. Activating, closing and watching are setting-class: white-box tests cover command construction and output parsing only, the actions stay with the caller.
- **The clipboard watcher's timer is injected by the caller**: master's `cbw_start_watch` hooked libyue's `set_timer` directly (no cancel id; it stops via a parking flag). `sys` does not import the GUI core layer, so scheduling became a parameter `schedule : (Int, () -> Unit) -> Unit`; the GUI layer passes `fn(ms, f) { let _ = @core.set_timeout(ms, f) }` while a headless test passes a fake channel that collects each tick's callback - which makes re-arming and "stop prevents the next arm" testable tick by tick (same layering rationale as the theme batch's "probe passed in as a function").
- **Six bus-dependent modules stay on the DBus line**: `power` (UPower), `session` (logind/screensaver), `online` (NetworkManager), `keepawake` (logind inhibit), `powerctl` (`gdbus_call_system`) and locale_sys's localed half (the `timedatectl` half is bus-free).
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/sys` **163/163** (36 new: sysinfo 14 including two live `/proc` assertions; windowctl 14 with a real `wmctrl -l -p` list of 8 windows; clipboard_watch 8 covering fake-channel tick dispatch, stop preventing the next arm, and the missing-xclip normalisation). `sys` clean under `--deny-warn`; whole-repo backlog still 287 errors / 68 warnings, unchanged.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · system integration, history family (`sys`: browser history / bookmarks / Firefox / VS Code)

- **The SQLite dependency must be declared at package level**: `prowk/moonsqlitefile` is already in `moon.mod`'s `import`, yet using `@moonsqlitefile.*` from `sys` failed with `Package "moonsqlitefile" not found in the loaded packages` - **a module-level import does not substitute for a package-level one**, so `sys/moon.pkg` needs `"prowk/moonsqlitefile" @moonsqlitefile`. The old-chain `yue/moon.pkg` has no such line (those files sit inside the repo-wide red-dot backlog), so copying the old chain's package config walks off a cliff.
- **Reading SQLite needs a raw-bytes entry**: added `sys_read_bytes_file`, sharing the same stub call as `sys_read_text_file` (`yue_sys_read_text_file` already slurps the file into `Bytes`; the difference is only whether MoonBit decodes it). The text version cannot feed SQLite: decoding with `decode_lossy` and re-encoding is not byte-identical (invalid UTF-8 sequences get eaten by replacement characters), and the database page header fails immediately.
- **The time bases differ per source**: Chrome/Edge/Brave `History` uses **microseconds since 1601-01-01 UTC** (constant `11644473600000`, `<=0` means unknown → 0, sub-microsecond truncated); bookmark `date_added` uses the same base but stored as a **numeric string**; VS Code entries use Unix milliseconds. Mixing them yields dates in 1601 or 50 millennia ahead.
- **Profile probing is "collect only what exists, without reading the database"**: directory enumeration only looks for an entry named `History`/`Bookmarks`, and only the data path reads the matched database in full - listing profiles no longer slurps tens of megabytes just to test existence. Known boundary: this layer has no way to enumerate profile directories, so it probes fixed candidate names (`Default` + `Profile 1..24`) and misses custom-named profiles.
- **Live end-to-end actually runs now** (new strict smoke for `bh_browsers`/`bh_history`/`bh_downloads`): Chrome's 37 MB `History` is really read, two profiles are hit, returned timestamps land in 2026, the ordering invariant (time descending, ties by url ascending) holds, and the `downloads` table reads; VS Code's `state.vscdb` plus recents run end to end; this host has no Firefox (`~/.mozilla/firefox/*/places.sqlite` absent) so it takes the legitimate skip branch. **Same discipline as the previous batch**: a detected database that fails to read must `fail`; `Err(_) => ()` is only allowed when the host genuinely has no such data.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/sys` **127/127** (41 new: browser history 12, Firefox 10, bookmarks 9, VS Code 10, each combining pure-function assertions with a live smoke). `sys` clean under `--deny-warn`; whole-repo backlog still 287 errors / 68 warnings, unchanged.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · desktop integration, second half (`sys`: recent files / recently-used.xbel)

- **Data surface**: the GTK family (Thunar / Nautilus / GIO, xdg-desktop-portal-gtk) all append to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/recently-used.xbel` (default `~/.local/share/`); this layer **only reads, never writes**. The parser is a hand-written thin scanner (it only takes attributes off `bookmark` plus `bookmark:application` / `mime:mime-type`), and everything error-prone lives in three pure functions: XML entity decoding (named entities plus `&#NN;`/`&#xHH;`, with bad codepoints and surrogate values kept literally), URI percent-decoding (consecutive `%XX` groups as UTF-8, while `100%` / `%E` / `%zz` stay literal) and ISO 8601 → Unix milliseconds (first three fractional digits, no timezone means UTC, leap-day validation). This host really yields **156 items**.
- **`inspect(x, content="…")` in the old wbtests asserts nothing on the native backend** (recorded once before; this batch is the second scene): ported as-is the suite goes "all green, zero coverage". Conversion rules: booleans → `assert_true`/`assert_false`; numbers → `assert_eq`, and **Int64 literals need the `L` suffix** (XBEL millisecond timestamps exceed Int's width, `assert_eq(items[0].added, 1776757238510)` does not typecheck); a debug array text like `[1, 2, 3]` becomes an array literal; `content="<should parse ok>"` is not an assertion at all but the caption of an error branch, so it becomes a `println` plus an explicit failing assertion.
- **A smoke case's error branch must not skip silently**: the old `rf_recent` / `rf_by_app` shape was `Err(_) => ()` ("no data on this host, so skip"), which also hides the real regression of "the file exists but cannot be read". It is now `Err(e) => { assert_false(rf_supported()); println(...) }` - the Err branch is only legal when this host genuinely has no such file.
- **Two XBEL tolerance semantics pinned by tests**: a fake `<bookmark>` hidden inside a comment is not collected (`skip_declaration` walks to `-->`); when a bookmark carries two `mime:mime-type` nodes **the first wins**; an XBEL truncated mid-write only collects the already-closed entries.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/sys` **86/86** (13 new: entity decoding, ISO conversion with leap days, calendar day counts, percent decoding, URI restoration, the full XBEL sample's six cases, non-XBEL and truncated input, mapping and tie-ordering, exact per-application filtering, `rf_take` bounds, `rf_data_dir`'s three states, and two live smoke reads). `sys` clean under `--deny-warn`; whole-repo backlog still 287 errors / 68 warnings, unchanged.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · desktop integration, middle half (`sys`: wallpaper + default apps, plus a child-process environment fix)

- **`pr_env_blob` was not passing DISPLAY / DBus, so desktop-side commands could only fail in a child process (this single line is why the previous batch's monitor tests had to skip)**: [pr_run] builds the child environment from a whitelist (previously only `PATH` / `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` / `HOME` plus `LC_ALL=C`); `xrandr --query` exits 1 without `DISPLAY`, and `xfconf-query` / `gsettings` cannot start without `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`. After passing through `DISPLAY` / `XAUTHORITY` / `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` / `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, on **the same host** the monitor cases really read DP-0..5 plus HDMI-0 (primary, 1920x1080) and HDMI-2, and the read-only wallpaper smoke test reads `/usr/share/xfce4/backdrops/Dolomites_by_Felix_Hartlieb.jpg`. **Acceptance check**: if a command works in the shell but exits non-zero through `pr_run`, the whitelist is missing a variable - do not blame the tool version first.
- **Wallpaper property selection is tied to connected outputs**: XFCE's `last-image` is picked in three passes ("workspace0 on a connected output → first workspace0 → first parseable"), the first using [mon_list]'s connected set to discard stale entries left by unplugged monitors; when xrandr is unavailable it degrades to "first workspace0". The write path picks its target property by the same rule (this stack's "drawing and hit-testing share one source" discipline, applied here) and creates the `monitorNone-1` fallback entry when nothing exists. The third pass **no longer considers connection**, it just takes the first parseable entry in list order.
- **The default-app write path really writes and reads back in tests**: `da_set_default`'s landing point is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mimeapps.list`, so the test points `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` at `/tmp/da_wbtest_config` (save / change / assert / restore) and asserts three states (missing file → new section; same mime re-set → the original line is replaced with no second line left; another mime → appended inside the section). The user's real configuration is untouched while the whole read-write chain is exercised.
- **Two toolchain findings (measured this batch)**: ① **same-named constructors across several enums in one package need disambiguation** - `Unsupported`/`CommandFailed`/`ParseFailed` collide between `WallpaperError`/`MonitorError`/`VolumeError`/`FileManagerError`/`AppFindError`; writing them bare in a test gives 4124 (`The constructor ... is ambiguous`), so tests must use `WallpaperError::ParseFailed(...)`. Inside the implementation files `match self { Unsupported => ... }` infers the type and needs no change. ② **A payload-free enum does not get `Show` either**: `println("\{de}")` does not compile (`Type DesktopEnv does not implement trait Show`), so diagnostics go through the dedicated `desktop_name()`.
