- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/sys` **73/73** (14 new: wallpaper 9 - the three-pass selection over this host's real xfconf property list, the `monitorNone-1` fallback, gsettings/KDE output parsing and argument construction, JS single-quote escaping, text helpers, argument guards and `Show` texts, read-only smoke on the live desktop; default apps 5 - mimeapps section parsing with non-deduplicated repeated keys, the four merge cases, association merge/dedup/ordering, a real write/read round trip against a temporary `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, and the live xdg-mime probe). `sys` clean under `--deny-warn`; whole-repo backlog still 287 errors / 68 warnings, unchanged. **`wp_set` is setting-class**: this batch only verifies argument construction and does not change the desktop appearance (same discipline as master); changing the wallpaper is left for the user on a real machine.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · desktop integration, first half (`sys`: desktop detection + app lookup + open-external)

- **Migration surface, file by file**: master's `yue/system.mbt` (`open_url`/`reveal_in_file_manager`) + `yue/system/appfind.mbt` + `yue/traybus/detect.mbt` (desktop environment detection) land as `sys/launcher.mbt` + `sys/appfind.mbt` + `sys/desktop.mbt`. The desktop detection is **carried as its own pure functions inside `sys`** rather than importing `@traybus`: the old-chain traybus package is part of the repo-wide red-dot backlog, and sys feeds it (wallpaper/default apps dispatch on the desktop) so importing it would create a cycle. When the DBus line lands, reuse this one copy instead of writing a second `detect_desktop`.
- **Detached spawn gets its own stub**: master used the shim's `g_spawn_async`, while `sys/sys_stub.c` only uses standard headers, so this is `fork → setsid → fork → execvp` plus a **CLOEXEC pipe** reporting back whether exec succeeded. **Not going through [pr_run] and waiting** is deliberate: `xdg-open` usually stays alive after handing the window off, so waiting would pin the calling thread; the double fork also guarantees no zombie (this function `waitpid`s the intermediate child, the real grandchild is reparented to init).
- **Real bug found and fixed this batch (write end of the pipe closed too early)**: the intermediate child used to `close(fds[1])` **before** forking the grandchild, so the grandchild had no write end to report through when `execvp` failed → the intermediate child read EOF (all write ends closed) and called it a success → "command does not exist" came back as `Ok`. The assertion "a nonexistent command must be Err" is exactly what caught it (red on the first run). Correct order: the intermediate child forks the grandchild first (it inherits the write end), **then** closes its own write end and keeps only the read end; because the write end is CLOEXEC, a successful exec closes it automatically and the intermediate reads EOF, while a failed exec falls through to `write("E")`.
- **`Ok` from `open_url`/`reveal_in_file_manager` means only "handed to the system"**; whether something actually opens is the platform's business. Arguments never go through a shell (argv passed directly), so shell metacharacters in URLs and paths are not an injection surface.
- **The "select" half of `reveal` is an acknowledged gap**: master first asks the FileManager1 bus for `ShowItems` and only falls back to opening the parent directory when the service is absent; this stack has no bus channel yet, so **every call currently takes the fallback path** (parent directory opens, selection lost). `ShowItems` comes with the DBus line.
- **appfind's ordering keeps master's `mut_view().sort_by` shape**: in this toolchain a comparator that returns the `-1/0/1` literals works fine - the earlier "`Ordering` is undefined" note only applies when the type name `Ordering` (or `Ordering::Less`) is written out explicitly, not to a comparator returning Int. Ordering semantics unchanged: compare `name` by codepoint, then `id`; `appfind_str_cmp` compares codepoint by codepoint instead of String's default shortlex order (which would put `"New"` before `"Beta"`).
- **Platform surface**: the Windows start-menu (`.lnk`) and macOS (`.app`) branches did not come with this batch - the Windows side of `sys_stub.c` is still a stub implementation, and `open_url`/`reveal`/`appfind_*` return `Unsupported` off Linux; the platform-dispatch batch can add master's pure functions (`appfind_win_*`/`appfind_mac_*`) directly.
- **Two toolchain findings (measured this batch)**: ① a Uint64 literal suffix like `500u64` **does not parse** (`unexpected token id (lowercase start)`) - convert the monotonic-clock difference with `.to_int()` before comparing; ② **a payload-free `pub(all) enum` does not get `Eq` either** (the earlier note was about `PointerKind` with a closure field; this extends it to plain enums) - `desktop_detect() == before` will not compile, so compare with `match` or via `desktop_name()`.
- **Verification**: `moon test -p NoahLiu/native-gui/sys` **59/59** (18 new: desktop detection 3 - single-value mapping, colon-separated multi-value first-recognised, and a real-environment save/change/assert/restore round trip; app lookup 10 - the INI subset parser, entry filtering with the zh_CN fallback, dedup merge and ordering, directory assembly's three states, real-disk collection with silent skips, `NoScanDir`, a live `appfind_installed` scan of this host, and `appfind_executable` hitting `/usr/bin/sh` plus argument guards; open-external 5 - `parent_dir`/relative-path normalisation, the real cwd, detached spawn's success/failure/non-blocking cases (`sleep 3` returns in under 500 ms), and the two error enums' `Show` plus the platform gate). `core` 62/62, `ui` 110/110, `render` 42/42, `mdview` 26/26, `theme` 8/8; twelve packages clean under `--deny-warn`; whole-repo backlog still 287 errors / 68 warnings, unchanged. **Left for real-machine re-verification** (observable once `examples/native-sys` lands): whether `open_url` really raises the default browser, whether `reveal_in_file_manager` opens the parent directory window, and the app count reported by `appfind_installed`.

## Linux

### Distributions

#### Ubuntu 24.04 ✅ mainline

- System dependencies: `build-essential cmake pkg-config libgtk-3-dev libpango1.0-dev libfontconfig1-dev libx11-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev`.
- AppIndicator runtime is gone, so libyue's built-in tray is unusable → replaced by `yue/traybus/` (pure-MoonBit SNI direct to the panel).
- The webkit2gtk package name varies by distribution (4.0 / 4.1); prepare.py probes with pkg-config and accepts either.

#### Other distributions ❓ untested

- First porting step: check each dependency's pkg-config name, then run prepare.py.

### Desktop environments (tray / menu behavior)

#### XFCE ✅

- Autostart .desktop findings: the Exec path comes from readlink on /proc/self/exe (during development it points into the _build output, so the entry breaks as soon as the artifact moves — only a fixed install path is reliable; AppImage likewise points at its mount point); the full file passes desktop-file-validate with zero warnings; the enabled check honors both system-side disable switches (Hidden=true and X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=false), and disable is idempotent (a missing entry counts as success).

- Context menus are rendered by the panel mirroring DBusMenu; the app is not asked to draw via SNI ContextMenu.
- xfce4-panel 4.18 sends only the batch `EventGroup` / `AboutToShowGroup`, not the singular versions: implementing only the singular forms gets silently rejected by UnknownMethod — the menu opens but clicks do nothing.
- Desktop notifications must go through `Notification::Show()`; `NotificationCenter::AddNotification` never issues the DBus Notify call on Linux and fails silently.
- Global shortcuts are exclusive XGrabKey registrations; a taken key combination makes Register return -1 (no crash, silent failure) — callers must check and offer another key.
- With desktop focus, xfwm4 captures the keyboard and global shortcuts do not fire (they work when an application window has focus).

#### GNOME ✅ (X11 and Wayland sessions)

- The AppIndicator extension reads the Menu property at registration time to build its proxy: an empty menu returning `/` permanently kills the menu client (clicking the icon does nothing). traybus always returns the real `/MenuBar`, exporting it even when empty, filled via LayoutUpdated.
- With `ItemIsMenu=false`, both left and right clicks emit Activate.
- Global shortcuts segfault on Wayland sessions (upstream casts the root window through a GDK X11 macro): a `GDK_IS_X11_DISPLAY` guard is in place; non-X11 sessions get Register = -1.
- Mouse button semantics are yue-unified 1=left 2=right 3=middle (GDK's 2/3 are swapped); components judge by yue semantics.
- Environment variables for launching GUI apps over SSH: X11 session `XAUTHORITY=/run/user/1000/gdm/Xauthority`; Wayland session `XAUTHORITY=/run/user/1000/.mutter-Xwaylandauth.*` and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`; both need `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus`.

#### KDE ✅ (Plasma 5.27)

- The panel consumes SNI directly; new icons go straight into the visible tray area; tray / menu / quit all pass.
- Protocol behavior is the opposite of XFCE: only singular `Event` / `AboutToShow`, no batch versions; traybus implements both.

#### Deepin ✅ (23 / 25, DDE)

- dde-dock implements StatusNotifierWatcher; SNI direct connection works; new icons land in the collapsed tray area by default and can be dragged out.
- libyue's Popover (transparent window + pointer grab) does not render on DDE and slows the pointer: the shim checks `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` (23=DDE, 25=Deepin) and falls back to a borderless plain window.
- Binaries built on the host (Ubuntu 24.04) run directly: the glibc symbol ceiling is 2.38 and deepin ships the webkit2gtk-4.1 runtime; for cross-distribution shipping, check the glibc symbol requirement first (`objdump -T | grep GLIBC_`).
- `TextEdit::Delete()` deletes the selection, it does not clear; use `set_text("")` to clear.
- DDE clipboard-manager interactions produce occasional CHECK / CRITICAL log noise; functionality is unaffected.

#### KDE / MATE / Cinnamon / Budgie / LXQt ❓ untested

- All support SNI at the protocol level and traybus implements the protocol; awaiting per-environment verification.

### DBus wire protocol (traybus)

- The DBus array length prefix excludes alignment padding before the first element; counting it makes dbus-daemon disconnect as a protocol violation.
- The variant signature in the header SIGNATURE field is "g" (u8 length-encoded); encoding it as "s" passes unit tests but real buses reject it.
- The SNI Menu property must always return the real menu object path — never `/`, even when empty.
- Unit-test self-consistency ≠ interop: protocol issues are located with dbus-monitor on the real bus; GNOME panel-side exceptions show up in journalctl.
- Single-instance RequestName must carry flags=4 (DO_NOT_QUEUE): the default 0 queues the request, so the second instance's already-running check hangs until the first instance exits — semantics fully broken. Real-bus findings (Ubuntu 24.04 XFCE): reply 3 = held by another connection (instance exists → wake it and exit); after SIGKILL of the first instance the bus reclaims the name automatically and a new connection gets reply 1 (becomes the primary); reply 4 = this connection already owns it (idempotent). The full chain (RequestName flags=4 → EXISTS → Wake('as') → RETURN) was verified by dbus-monitor capture on the real bus: Wake to RETURN in 39µs; after SIGKILL of the first instance a third instance claims normally.
- The second-instance wake dispatch must hook Conn::handle's kind==1 branch in bus.mbt before sni.mbt's handle_call: all inbound calls funnel into handle_call, and without the interception Wake lands in the UnknownMethod fallback so the first instance never sees it. Wake naming convention: interface org.moonbitlibyue.Instance, object path /org/moonbitlibyue/Instance, member Wake ('as' = the second instance's command line, passed through moonbitlang/core/env args(), including argv[0]; callers decide what to keep).
- FileManager1 (reveal-in-file-manager) findings on XFCE: the NameHasOwner probe works; ShowItems wire format is "ass" (array of file URIs + an empty startup id); file URI percent-hex uses uppercase (RFC 3986 allows either case, uppercase is the convention), unreserved characters (A-Za-z0-9-._~) and '/' stay raw, everything else is %XX-encoded per UTF-8 byte — locked by unit tests. When the service is offline or the call fails, the fallback is xdg-open on the parent directory — selection is lost, a semantic degradation the usage doc must state.
- External-open spawns go through g_spawn_async (G_SPAWN_SEARCH_PATH + stdout/stderr to DEV_NULL); glib reaps the child automatically, no zombies; no shell involved, argv passed directly. xdg-open's behavior for nonexistent paths or unopenable URLs varies by desktop, so the library's Ok only means "handed to the system" — the platform-side outcome does not travel back.
- Screen-saver inhibition (Inhibit/UnInhibit) picks the service by real NameHasOwner presence, not by desktop-name guessing: the candidate list is [org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver, org.xfce.ScreenSaver]; measured on Ubuntu 24.04 XFCE only org.xfce.ScreenSaver is online (held by xfce4-screensaver), org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver is unheld. The two are interface-isomorphic: object path and interface name derive from the service name by dot→slash, Inhibit("ss" = app name + reason) -> u cookie, UnInhibit("u" = the original cookie) must match bit for bit (real-bus capture: Inhibit returned cookie 1516211641, UnInhibit 2 seconds later carried the same value, empty successful reply). GNOME / KDE service holdings pending real-machine notes.
- System bus (measured Ubuntu 24.04): socket is /run/dbus/system_bus_socket — connecting by this default with DBUS_SYSTEM_BUS_ADDRESS unset works; when the variable is explicitly set, take the first unix:path= among the comma-separated entries, and if none matches (e.g. a tcp: address) return an explicit Err carrying the original text — silently falling back to the default socket would reconnect to a bus that really has UPower, turning the degradation acceptance check into a false pass. BecomeMonitor is rejected on the system bus (both dbus-monitor and busctl monitor), so capture is unavailable; verification goes through the probe's own round trips plus busctl call to cross-check reply shapes.
- Multi-bus connections coexisting (B5 infrastructure): the shim's fd watch went from a process-wide single slot (each watch overwriting the previous) to an fd→callback dispatch table plus unwatch; the MoonBit side routes fd→Conn through a registry. Dual connections (session SNI + system UPower) verified to coexist without clobbering. When a glib source callback returns 0, glib destroys the source itself — the shim table entry must be erased in step (otherwise a later unwatch calls g_source_remove on a dead id and warns).
- Wire-level 'd' (DOUBLE) and 't' (UINT64) must land as a set: in a real UPower GetAll reply UpdateTime is 't' and Percentage/Energy are 'd'; missing 't' sent the variant's unknown-signature old defensive branch ("return empty string but leave the read position alone"), misaligning every subsequent element and aborting inside the read_string slice (unit tests stayed green — self-crafted shapes never hit it). The defense is now two layers: unknown variant signatures push pos to the message end (parsing degrades to garbage values instead of misalignment), and read_string/read_sig gained bounds checks. Adding a type is an eight-site whole-chain change: DVal/Sig/sig_align/parse_one_sig/sig_of/sig_char/encode/decode_in.
- Double↔IEEE 754 bit conversion lives in the shim (moonbitlang/core has no Double::to_bits/from_bits — confirmed): yue_mbt_sys_f64_to_bits/from_bits are pure bit reinterpretations (static_assert sizeof(double)==8), and the wire layer's 'd' piggybacks on the Int64 8-byte little-endian read/write. Note: once traybus's whitebox test target references such externs, its link needs -lyue_mbt — but link_configs propagate to "targets depending on the package", and traybus does not depend on yue (it's the reverse), so prebuild.py must carry a separate identical entry for NoahLiu/native-gui/yue/traybus (the single static-lib member references the whole gtk set, so trimmed flags won't link).
- UPower reading path (measured Ubuntu 24.04, desktop machine): DisplayDevice (/org/freedesktop/UPower/devices/DisplayDevice, interface org.freedesktop.UPower.Device) aggregates the main battery — IsPresent=false → Ok(None); mind the interface-name split: devices are …UPower.Device, the toplevel is …UPower, and PropertiesChanged's arg0 filter naturally keeps device-level signals out of toplevel subscriptions. OnBattery lives on the toplevel object; power-source events subscribe to toplevel PropertiesChanged and parse the changed dict directly in the callback (signal dispatch sits on the drain stack — call_sync inside a callback would re-enter the receive path; forbidden).
- Disconnect self-healing (B5, not yet exercised by a real disconnection): mark_dead is idempotent (keyed on the fd registry), reconnects via the shim's post_delayed_task (extern'd directly, bypassing the traybus→yue reverse dependency) after 500ms, at most 3 attempts; on success it replays AddMatch rules, migrates the subscription table and tray items, and re-registers them (during the disconnect the watcher already dropped the old registrations when our unique name vanished). In a pure-CLI context (main loop not running) the reconnect callback never fires and gives up naturally.
- logind event subscriptions (B6): PrepareForSleep(b) lives on the Manager interface; Lock/Unlock live on each session object's Session interface (empty-body signals, one AddMatch per member, path unbounded — all sessions match, so with multiple logged-in users someone else's lock fires too; ownership is the caller's to check via sender). Degradation measured (private bus without logind): suspend_resume_supported()==false and session_lock_watch returns Err(SystemError::Unsupported), never silent. Rapid suspend/resume cycles may deliver two Resuming events in a row (no library-side debouncing); network/DBus may not be ready right after wake — retry logic in callbacks should defer.
- Lock events need a dual signal source (real-machine bugfix): XFCE's xfce4-screensaver does **not** call logind when locking (no Lock/Unlock signals; calling Session.Lock via busctl directly fires them fine, proving the subscription chain is healthy — the locker just never notifies). It emits ActiveChanged(b) on its own org.xfce.ScreenSaver name instead. Fix: session_lock_watch subscribes to both sources — logind Lock/Unlock (system bus, GNOME/KDE path) plus the screensaver service's ActiveChanged (session bus, candidates [org.xfce.ScreenSaver, org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver] picked by real presence) — with a state machine deduping multi-source reports (same-state repeats don't dispatch; only transitions do). The ActiveChanged subscription key carries the service-name prefix, so it cannot clash with the logind subscriptions.
- XFCE "blank-after-1-minute setting has no effect" and the keep-awake verification path (real-machine diagnosis): the power manager GUI's "blank after 1 minute" relies on DPMS or the screensaver's blanking, and on the measured host all three dimming chains were off (xfce4-screensaver /saver/enabled=false, X DPMS Disabled, xfce4-power-manager carrying no dpms/blank keys at all) — the GUI shows a value but nothing executes it, so the keep-awake switch is unobservable. Before verifying keep-awake, enable one executor (the screensaver blank is recommended: same component as the locker, so inhibition and lock events pair up); org.xfce.PowerManagement's inhibit interface is offline here (NameHasOwner=false), so DPMS blanking under XFCE cannot be inhibited via DBus — avoid that path.
- Windows power/session event window (B6, code landed, real-machine verification pending): one message-only window receives both WM_POWERBROADCAST (PBT_APMSUSPEND; both PBT_APMRESUME and PBT_APMRESUMEAUTOMATIC count as resumed) and WM_WTSSESSION_CHANGE (WTS_SESSION_LOCK/UNLOCK, NOTIFY_FOR_THIS_SESSION); the WNDPROC PostTasks back to the main loop (B1 message-window pattern reused). The C side is single-window single-callback shared by sleep and lock — the MoonBit side registers one global dispatcher keyed on the event code, so later registrations must not clobber earlier ones. A WTSRegisterSessionNotification failure only disables lock events and is not treated as overall failure. wtsapi32.lib is the plan's only link-list change; prebuild.py's WINDOWS_LINK_LIBS and shim/CMakeLists.txt must land in the same commit (the two lists carry no consistency-comment backing).
- NetworkManager online status (B7): State and Connectivity are both toplevel properties; a Properties.Get reply body is a single "v" (containing a u32) — a different shape from GetAll's a{sv}. Both change signals are subscribed: the legacy StateChanged(i) carries the new value directly, while PropertiesChanged(a{sv})'s changed dict may carry either property; subscription callbacks sit on the drain stack, so they only update the cache and notify with merged values — never call_sync to re-query (the first cache build happens inside the registration action, legal off the drain stack, worst-case 1.5s block). Normalization: State 70/50 with Connectivity 4/3 is Online; captive portal (Connectivity=2) counts as Offline ("online" = internet-reachable). Measured Ubuntu 24.04: State=70/Connectivity=4 → Online, matching busctl bit for bit; private-bus degradation gives Err(NetworkError::Unsupported). Windows NLM GetConnectivity bitmask: IPV4_INTERNET (0x40) or IPV6_INTERNET (0x400) present means Online, polled every 5s (listener-based later); netlistmgr.h needs no extra link libraries.
- NM StateChanged signal parameter is Int32 (i), not u32 (real-machine pitfall, corrected): the D-Bus spec makes the State *property* u and the StateChanged *signal* parameter i — different types for the same concept; the wire layer decodes i as VI32, and the old implementation matched only VU32, so the signal was silently dropped — signals arrived, callbacks never fired, and after the panel disconnected or "enable networking" was switched off (State 70→20/10) the UI kept showing the initial Online (unit tests alone can't catch this: the hand-crafted signal body happened to use u). Fix: statechanged_of matches both VI32/VU32; bool and other types are still dropped as before. State inside Properties.Get and PropertiesChanged remains u — untouched. The dispatch chain itself was verified alive on a harmless property write (NM 1.46 WwanEnabled toggle, zero network impact on machines without WWAN hardware, PropertiesChanged arriving in real time); the UI flip after a signal was left to real-machine offline/online verification.
- Network callback registration must sit outside the platform branches (located via two-level live observation): on_network_status_change dispatches uniformly through net_dispatch iterating g_net_cbs, but the registration g_net_cbs.push(cb) used to live only in the Windows branch — on Linux every signal arrived and the cache updated value by value (State 70→10→20→40→60→70 matching nmcli monitor line for line) while callbacks never ran, leaving the UI stuck on the initial value; a two-level probe (traybus nm_on_change layer vs the online dispatch layer) pinpointed it. Fix: push moved outside the platform branches so both platforms register uniformly. Other event registrations (on_suspend_resume/on_power_source_change) embed their callback closures directly and don't go through a global array, so they were never affected; net_dispatch dedupes against the network_status() baseline backfilled at registration, so the first same-state signal after registration not dispatching is expected.
- Generic D-Bus call layer (yue/traybus/dbus.mbt, a cross-cutting foundation shared by the media / disk / bluetooth / sensor / time-zone modules): a thin layer over wire.mbt's wire format and bus.mbt's process-wide dual connections, offering "method calls on any service plus property read/write" through six public entries — gdbus_call_session / gdbus_call_system / gdbus_get_property_session / gdbus_get_property_system / gdbus_set_property_session / gdbus_set_property_system (the connection comes from the process-wide singleton, opened on demand; synchronous calls time out at 1.5 seconds, matching the bus's existing convention, and a reply timeout yields gdbus.timeout). **a{sv} support is this layer's reason to exist**: MPRIS Metadata and udisks GetAll property dicts are all a{sv}, and without it every module would decode that dictionary itself - duplicated and error-prone. The value model GDBusValue covers four containers: GVArray (element signature, element table) / GVDict (a{sv}, Map serialized in insertion order) / GVVariant (wrapper preserved) / GVStruct. On the encoding side GVArray's element signature is supplied in full by the caller ("s"/"{sv}"/"(ii)" and any other complete type); when wrapping a GVStruct the field signatures are concatenated and the whole thing pre-checked through parse_signature, **with no timeout cost** - a bad signature is reported locally as gdbus.encode instead of waiting 1.5s for a bus timeout. On the decoding side `VArray("{sv}")` collapses into GVDict with the variant wrapper stripped (downstream code wants values, not categories); Byte and the 16-bit integers fold into GVInt32, and a 'g' signature folds into GVString. The parameter tree forbids GVNone recursively (its signature could not be derived), and every entry runs a whole-tree scan through gdbus_args_ok first. The property-read path already unwraps the variant (a Properties.Get reply body is always a single "v", so the inner value is taken directly); the write path passes a bare value and this layer adds the variant wrapper. The error model is GDBusError{ name, message }: name carries the D-Bus error name verbatim (UnknownMethod / ServiceUnknown and the like), local errors use the gdbus.io (cannot connect / disconnected) / gdbus.timeout / gdbus.encode prefixes, so callers can route "service offline" away from "reply timeout" by prefix alone.
- udisks2 (org.freedesktop.UDisks2, system bus) interface notes: enumerate objects through GetBlocks on `/org/freedesktop/UDisks2/Manager`, which returns a{oa{sv}} (device path → that block object's full property dict), then Properties.GetAll per block for the Filesystem interface as needed; **the MountPoints property is aay (array of byte arrays), not as** - parsing it as strings empties every entry and mount state can never be read, so each byte array must be decoded as UTF-8. Mount/unmount go through the Filesystem interface's Mount(options : a{sv})/Unmount(options : a{sv}), and the first argument may be an empty GVDict; the reply carries mount-point strings (possibly several for a multi-mount device). When udisks2 is offline, lsblk --json serves as an enumeration fallback only (char-typed fields need ansi stripping).
- bluez (org.bluez, system bus) interface notes: enumerate objects with ObjectManager.GetManagedObjects, whose reply shape is a{oa{sa{sv}}} (path → interface name → that interface's property dict), then filter Adapter1 / Device1 out of it; Adapter1's Powered / Discovering and Device1's Name / Alias / Paired / Connected / Trusted all come out of those dicts. Scanning is Adapter1.StartDiscovery (no arguments), pairing Device1.Pair, connecting Device1.Connect - all three are empty-argument methods with empty replies. **No bluetooth adapter is a legitimate state**: when org.bluez is offline or no Adapter1 is enumerated, bt_supported() gives false and the query APIs degrade with an explicit Unsupported rather than an error.
- iio-sensor-proxy (net.hadess.SensorProxy, system bus) interface notes: HasAccelerometer / HasAmbientLight / LightLevel / AccelerometerOrientation are all properties of one interface on one object, `/net/hadess/SensorProxy` (unlike udisks / bluez, which spread across many interfaces and objects). **ClaimLight/ReleaseLight (or ClaimAccelerometer/ReleaseAccelerometer) must wrap any read**: an unclaimed sensor keeps reporting its stale value, and the claim must be released afterwards or other consumers (auto-brightness, for instance) never see new values. AccelerometerOrientation is a **string**, not an enum integer - values like "normal"/"left-up"/"bottom-down".
- Windows NLM GetConnectivity called on the UI thread can freeze for seconds and drag the native layout assert into a crash (measured on a Win10 19045 host; reproduced deterministically with a poor network environment): showcase aborts steadily 3.7–4.7s after launch (0xC0000409 = fast-fail), with yoga's toplevel assert "availableHeight is indefinite so heightMeasureMode must be YGMeasureModeUndefined" on stderr right before; the crash rate drifts 0%–100% with network health (when the network is healthy the query is millisecond-fast, matching the "smoke survived" notes at commit time — easy to misread as a code regression). Locating path: page bisection on the same exe (removing only the System Integration page → 0 crashes) → disabling only the initial network query + callback registration → 10/10 stable → prewarming and delayed queries both still crashed (any in-process query freezes, timing irrelevant). Root cause: the GetConnectivity slow path can take seconds per call; the synchronous initial-value query at registration froze the UI thread for seconds, and the moment it returned yoga processed the backed-up invalidations through ScrollView's content-measurement GetPreferred* path (which calls YGNodeCalculateLayout with a NaN height — fatal for containers with a defined height style). Fix: shim adds yue_mbt_netwin_start/netwin_cached — a background MTA thread owns COM and the polling loop (interval 5s default) and writes a process-level cache; the UI thread only reads the cache (network_status returns QueryFailed until the cache is ready; on_network_status_change no longer backfills the initial value synchronously; g_net_last becomes None = unknown, first value always dispatches). The cross-thread COM apartment problem dissolves because the interface pointer is created and used on the same thread. Verification: moon check zero warnings, 128/128 tests, showcase smoke 12/12 alive (same environment was 7/10 crashes before the fix).
- **Multi-item DBusMenu object paths must be derived from the item path (CORE2, whitebox + real-bus regression)**: the SNI Menu property used to return `/MenuBar` unconditionally, and the menus registry (menu object path → Item) collided on that key — creating a second tray item did `c.menus.set("/MenuBar", item2)`, silently replacing the first item's menu route, so the panel only ever saw the last registered item's menu (the first item's layout queries landed on the second item or hit UnknownObject); unregistering could not clean the stale key either. Fix: `menu_path_of(item_path)` derives the path (`/StatusNotifierItem` → `/MenuBar`, `/StatusNotifierItem_N` → `/MenuBar_N`, the first item keeps the ksni convention), unregister and the create-failure path clear both the items and menus tables symmetrically, and `Conn::next_item_path` now scans for the first free path (the old length()+1 numbering reused an occupied path after a middle item was unregistered, colliding with its menu route too). Real-bus regression (sni_wbtest, auto-skips without a panel watcher): two items get distinct paths/menu paths, `gdbus_call_session(own unique name, each menu path, GetLayout)` returns each item's own labels (never the other's), both tables are empty after unregistering, and a fresh item restarts from `/StatusNotifierItem`; with the pre-fix code stashed in (menu_path_of always `/MenuBar`) the related cases fail precisely. **The panel-side behavior of two icons each opening their own menu still needs on-device visual review** (AGENTS rules 5/6).
- **Disconnect self-healing must not unconditionally open a new connection (CORE2, whitebox + real-bus regression)**: `try_reconnect` used to call connect_session/connect_system and overwrite g_conn/g_sys_conn as soon as it found a saved connection — if an on-demand path (sni_available / Item::create / system_conn) had already rebuilt a live connection after the disconnect, that connection plus its fd and glib fd watch leaked (the g_conns registry routes by fd, and after the overwrite nothing could unwatch/close it), with subscriptions and tray items split across two connections so signals only reached the orphaned one. Fix: the migration logic is consolidated into `Conn::adopt_saved(bus)`, called by connect_session/connect_system whenever any new connection is established (on-demand rebuild and self-healing share the path), and `try_reconnect` first checks whether g_conn/g_sys_conn is already live — if so it only tops up the migration (idempotent) and opens nothing. Two older issues fixed along the way: migrated paths already present on the target connection are not re-registered (avoiding a double icon from a repeated RegisterStatusNotifierItem on the same connection), and `Item::unregister` also clears the item from the saved (disconnected) connection, so it no longer resurrects after a reconnect. Tray-item re-registration is posted back to the main loop via `sys_post_delayed(0, ...)`: register_item_path's internal call_sync pumps the bus, and running it synchronously would let predicates such as sni_available / Tray::is_supported block for up to 1.5s when called from a GUI callback, and would re-entrantly dispatch inbound calls arriving during the pump (the same discipline as never calling call_sync from a netmon/UPower callback). Real-bus regression: mark_dead simulates the disconnect → on-demand rebuild → after try_reconnect g_conn is still the same connection (unique name unchanged) and g_conns gains no entry; with the pre-fix behavior (unconditional new connection) it fails precisely.

- Measured sysmonitor figures (Ubuntu 24.04 XFCE X11, same methodology as the performance baseline at the top of this file: startup median, steady-state RSS, release binary): startup (exec → window map) over 5 runs 77/78/81/82/88ms, median 81ms (the hello baseline of 70ms is an idle system; this run carried 1042 processes); steady state with the process page foregrounded at 1Hz uses 2-3% CPU (sampling + derived data + 1000-row table rebuild + repaint total ≈ 25ms/second), RSS 84.9MB flattening at 85.8MB after 100s; binary 7.72MB (hello counterpart 7.03MB). The 1000-row process page meets acceptance: full sampling of 1053 processes takes 14.94ms/pass (release, ≈14µs per process — two /proc reads each), a 1.5% duty cycle at 1Hz.
- The 1000-row table uses table_v_t virtual scrolling (only visible rows draw): refresh goes "full data sampling → filter/sort derived data → rows Store set → table load + schedule_paint", never rebuilding the view tree; selection is remapped by pid so it doesn't drift as the sort order changes every second. There is no C++ counterpart binary, so the combined "wrapper + data layer" overhead is attributed directly from the figures above; the UI drawing portion is on par with the hello baseline under the same methodology.
- **Panic in the IconPixmap property callback on the empty-pixmap state (2026-10, user's real-machine stack + before/after control)**: after clicking "切主题图标(Linux)" in showcase's tray demo, `set_icon_name` clears the bitmap by design (XFCE's panel prioritizes IconPixmap over IconName; without clearing, the old bitmap keeps drawing after a rename), leaving w=0/h=0/empty buffer. The panel receives NewIcon and re-queries IconPixmap; `Item::property` calls `downscale_pixmap(0, 0, …)` to build the extra 16×16 entry — the old clamp guard `if y*h/nh > h-1 { h-1 }` is true when h=0 (`0 > -1`), clamping **sy to -1**, and `px[src+c]` panics with a negative index inside the DBus callback (exit 134). The user's real-machine stack: `traybus.downscale_pixmap(icon.mbt:63) ← Item::property(sni.mbt:539) ← Conn::handle_call(sni.mbt:660) ← drain ← on_bus_ready`. Fix: `downscale_pixmap` early-returns (0, 0, empty) for degenerate sizes (any of w/h/nw/nh ≤ 0, or a buffer shorter than w*h*4) and the two never-triggered clamps were removed (for valid inputs y*h/nh is always < h); the main `pixmap_value` entry already tolerated the empty state, panels fall back to IconName, and the SNI semantics are unchanged. Before/after control (same probe, same path: create tray → set_icon_name → panel/manual IconPixmap re-query): before the fix, exit 134 with a stack identical to the user's report frame for frame; after the fix, the property returns `[(0,0,[]), (0,0,[])]` and the process stays alive (also re-verified with a manual gdbus Properties.Get). Regression: icon_test gains 3 cases (0×0 empty pixmap, degenerate target size, short buffer — all return empty), `moon test` 659 all green. Lesson: **pure functions on the DBus property-callback stack must also defend against degenerate inputs — a panic there kills the message pump; "clamp to h-1" guards treat -1 as a legal value when the size is 0, so early return beats clamping; the cleared state (0×0) is a legitimate business state that every consumer must tolerate**.

### System monitor data layer (/proc, /sys — sysmonitor example)

- /proc and /sys pseudo-files always report stat size 0 (fseek/ftell cannot learn the length): whole-file reads must loop with incremental `fread` and a doubling buffer (16MB cap); opening a directory succeeds but `fread` fails with EISDIR — detect via `ferror`. Implemented in the app's own native stub `examples/sysmonitor/stub/sysmon.c`; the MoonBit side goes through `read_text_file`.
- An app-owned native stub may live in a subdirectory: `"native-stub": ["stub/sysmon.c"]` resolves relative to the moon.pkg directory; all symbols are within libc's default link set — zero shim / fork / vendored / link-flag changes. The test target links the stub automatically, so wbtests can read real /proc files.
- /proc/stat column order is `user nice system idle iowait irq softirq steal guest guest_nice`: the 9th column (guest) is already folded into user/nice by the kernel — adding it double-counts. Usage = (Δtotal − Δidle − Δiowait) / Δtotal; iowait is not CPU-busy. When the sampling interval is shorter than one tick (USER_HZ, usually 10ms), Δtotal ≤ 0 and the result is 0; a zero first sample makes the first screen show the since-boot average.
- /proc/cpuinfo model field differs by platform: x86 uses `model name`, ARM boards only have `Processor` / `Hardware` — three-level fallback; core count = number of `processor` lines (logical CPUs incl. hyperthreading, matches nproc).
- Windows /proc/cpuinfo core-count correction (>64 cores, final review): `GetSystemInfo`'s dwNumberOfProcessors only covers the calling thread's group (≤64), so multi-group machines must sum ActiveProcessorCount over GetLogicalProcessorInformationEx(RelationGroup). The original guard and offsets were all wrong: the relationship constant was 3 (RelationProcessorPackage; RelationGroup is 4), ActiveGroupCount read at it+8 (really it+10: 8-byte record header + 2-byte MaximumGroupCount), the GroupInfo base/stride assumed 32+64g (really it+32 base with a 48-byte stride per group), and the guard used 32+64g (really 32+48g) — for a single group the API returns Size=8+24+48=80 < 96, so total stayed 0 and the correction never fired, leaving >64-core machines at the current group's count. Authoritative layout (Microsoft Learn winnt.h): GROUP_RELATIONSHIP {WORD MaximumGroupCount; WORD ActiveGroupCount; BYTE Reserved[20]; PROCESSOR_GROUP_INFO GroupInfo[]} (24-byte header, union starts at record+8), PROCESSOR_GROUP_INFO {BYTE MaximumProcessorCount; BYTE ActiveProcessorCount; BYTE Reserved[38]; KAFFINITY ActiveProcessorMask} (48 bytes), and SYSTEM_LOGICAL_PROCESSOR_INFORMATION_EX's Size is the whole record length (including the Relationship+Size header), used as the stride to the next record. Verified: a harness fills a 2-group (64+32) buffer from the real structs and asserts the sum is 96; the single-group and truncated-Size degenerate cases each assert the fallback of 64. **Real multi-group numbers still need Windows on-device confirmation**.
- /proc/meminfo units are always kB; `MemAvailable` only exists on kernels ≥ 3.14 — fall back to `MemFree`; used = total − available (includes reclaimable cache).
- The `moon run` wrapper process does not forward signals to its child: smoke-testing exit behavior requires killing the built exe child process — killing only the wrapper PID leaves an orphan window.
- Measured full-process sampling (release, Ubuntu 24.04): 580 processes × 2 file reads (stat + cmdline) = 9.57ms per pass, ~1% CPU at 1Hz refresh; RSS comes from stat's page count × page size (equal to status's VmRSS), saving a third read per process.
- /proc/[pid]/stat comm can contain spaces and nested parentheses (process name "(foo (bar))") — split at the LAST ')' in the line; comm is truncated to 15 chars, so the full command line is read separately from cmdline (NUL-separated; empty falls back to [comm] for kernel threads).
- getpriority's nice = -1 is a legal value and is ambiguous with the error return: report success/failure via a `Ref[Int]` out-parameter (kill / setpriority still use the errno return).
- Windows has no /proc and no nice semantics: the stub keeps the same ABI at compile time and returns an "unsupported" sentinel (-1000) at runtime, which the MoonBit layer turns into a Chinese notice — the whole process page degrades cleanly; three-platform CI builds are unaffected (macOS takes the POSIX branch naturally).
- GPU utilization / VRAM / temperature on the NVIDIA proprietary driver must not go through in-process NVML: after dlopen'ing `libnvidia-ml.so.1`, `nvmlInit_v2` collides intermittently with the host runtime (measured on this RTX 3070 + Ubuntu 24.04 machine: startup segfaults about 5 out of 6 runs, does not reproduce under gdb, timing-sensitive; dlopen+dlsym without init stays clean). The route is now a popen `nvidia-smi` batch query (`--query-gpu=pci.bus_id,utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total,temperature.gpu,name --format=csv,noheader,nounits`, one line per card), matched against the sysfs enumeration by "take the last colon-separated segment and strip leading zeros" (nvidia-smi reports 00000000:01:00.0 where sysfs has 0000:01:00.0); the price is one subprocess per sampling pass (measured tens of milliseconds, acceptable at 1Hz). When nvidia-smi is absent (no N card / no driver), sysfs generic nodes are the natural fallback (amdgpu / nouveau `gpu_busy_percent`, `mem_info_vram_*`); hwmon temperature serves both. NVIDIA's proprietary driver exposes no hwmon, so its temperature can only come from nvidia-smi.
- diskstats lists both whole disks and partitions (nvme0n1 alongside nvme0n1p1/p2/p3); an LVM mount's device name (/dev/mapper/ubuntu--vg-ubuntu--lv) does not match its diskstats name (dm-N) — resolve via `/sys/block/dm-*/dm/name` to find dm-N, then take the first slaves entry (measured: dm-0 → nvme0n1p3) to attribute IO rates to the mount row.
- hwmon temperature indices skip numbers (coretemp exposes only some cores' tempN_input); labels may be absent (acpitz has none — fall back to the chip name); millidegrees can be negative (battery sensors); NVIDIA dGPUs commonly expose no hwmon temperature (measured: 0x2488 has none), so GPU temperature shows "—" under the hwmon convention.
- statvfs capacity uses f_bavail (available, minus reserved blocks) rather than f_bfree, matching df's Use% convention; the struct is flattened across the ABI into three int64 out-params (total/free/avail).
- /proc/mounts pseudo-filesystems (~20 kinds: proc/sysfs/cgroup2/devtmpfs/efivarfs …) have no meaningful statvfs capacity — the capacity table skips them via an fstype blacklist, keeping only real /dev/ device lines; multiple mounts of one device (btrfs subvolumes / LVM snapshots) are deduplicated by device, first occurrence wins.
- Directory enumeration (/sys/class/hwmon, /sys/class/net, /sys/bus/pci/devices, /sys/block/*/slaves) goes through a generic opendir/readdir stub (newline-separated entry names); together with read_text_file these are the data layer's only two IO primitives.
- The /dev/fuse control mount (appears once the file manager brings up gvfsd-fuse; mount point /tmp/fuse) returns a valid statvfs with f_blocks=0: filtering by the fstype blacklist alone is not enough — also skip total<=0, or the disk page shows a "0 MB / 0 MB" noise row (verified: the S5 whitebox assertion total>0 failed because of it).
- **Windows data layer (SYS1): the Win32 sources are virtualised into Linux-shaped /proc and /sys text at the stub's read entry points, so the MoonBit data layer and its parsing pure functions need zero changes**. Decision: rather than opening platform branches in MoonBit (two implementations per sampler, and pure-function tests could never cover the Win32 path), the C side generates isomorphic text on the fly for `read_text_file`/`list_dir`/`statvfs`/`list_pids` requests against Linux paths — the Linux path is the cross-layer contract, and unit tests keep feeding literals and stay green. The seven routes and their deviation list:
  - CPU: /proc/stat from GetSystemTimes (global; kernel includes idle and must be subtracted) plus ntdll `NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemProcessorPerformanceInformation)` per logical core (an undocumented information class, but the ABI has been stable for decades and Task Manager uses the same source; if the query fails only the aggregate line is emitted and the per-core bars stay empty); units are normalised to 10ms ticks (100ns ÷ 1e5) to line up with clk_tck=100; /proc/cpuinfo model and clock come from the registry `CentralProcessor\0` ProcessorNameString/~MHz (compiler-independent, and it avoids x86 conditional compilation compared to a CPUID intrinsic), core count from GetSystemInfo (≤64) corrected by summing active processors over GetLogicalProcessorInformationEx(RelationGroup) groups (GetSystemInfo caps at 64 on multi-group systems).
  - Memory: GlobalMemoryStatusEx → MemTotal/Free/Available and SwapTotal/Free; ullAvailPhys is Windows' "available" (it serves as both MemAvailable and MemFree), and the commit charge (ullTotalPageFile = commit limit) serves as swap — matching Task Manager's "Commit" rather than the pagefile pool.
  - Disks: /proc/mounts from GetLogicalDrives per drive (GetDriveType accepts only FIXED/REMOVABLE, skipping optical-drive read noise and mapped network drives); the line convention is `dev/C: C:\ ntfs ...` — the device column is forced to carry the /dev/ prefix so parse_mounts accepts it, and the mount point holds the real Windows path (the MoonBit statvfs_info passes it back verbatim, the stub's GetDiskFreeSpaceExW takes it directly, and the UI naturally shows "C:\"); /proc/diskstats from PDH `\PhysicalDisk(*)\Disk {Read,Write} Bytes` (PdhAddEnglishCounterW registers the English names, because localized Windows objects/counter names differ and a hard-coded localized path always fails; **path validity still needs on-device confirmation**), taking raw cumulative counters (not the per-sec variants) so a single Collect is enough, dividing by 512 into sectors for the existing MoonBit sector_rate difference; instance names (e.g. "0 C: D:") are split on spaces and only tokens shaped like "C:" are kept (disk numbers and "_Total" drop out naturally), and every drive letter on a disk emits its own identical line — PDH counts per physical disk while the mounts side emits per drive letter, so each letter must be attributable to its disk (taking the last token only recorded the last letter on a multi-partition disk and left the others at None forever). **The instance-name shape for multi-partition disks needs on-device confirmation**.
  - Network: GetIfTable2 for the full table, InterfaceAlias as the card name, "Software Loopback" normalised to "lo" (main.mbt's rate aggregation then excludes it automatically, as on Windows); InOctets/OutOctets serve as the rx/tx counters. The table carries a 200ms static cache — each card's rx and tx read the path separately, so without a cache 1Hz would pull the whole table 2×N times per second.
  - Processes: K32EnumProcesses (kernel32 exports carry the K32 prefix, so GetProcAddress is required) enumerates pids; pid→ppid/thread count/image name come from a single CreateToolhelp32Snapshot (250ms TTL), then per pid OpenProcess+GetProcessTimes (100ns÷1e5 = 10ms tick, the same unit as clk_tck=100) + K32GetProcessMemoryInfo (WorkingSetSize÷4096 = page count, matching page_size=4096); cmdline = the full path from QueryFullProcessImageNameA, and when OpenProcess is denied on system processes time/memory read 0 and the command line falls back to [comm]. nice is always 0: Windows priority classes do not map onto Linux nice semantics and a mapped value would mislead; normalising priority into tiers is SYS2's scope (SYS2 has landed: the nice field now carries the tier representative value derived back from GetPriorityClass).
  - GPU: DXGI CreateDXGIFactory1 enumerates adapters with virtual pci addresses `0000:00:NN.0` (unique after MoonBit's norm_pci takes the tail segment and strips leading zeros); vendor/device are emitted as "0x%04x" lowercase for the existing vendor_name table; WARP software adapters (Flags bit 0) are skipped; VRAM total = DedicatedVideoMemory (integrated cards reporting 0 get no virtual mem_info_vram_total, so no VRAM curve appears), used = IDXGIAdapter3::QueryVideoMemoryInfo(Local segment).CurrentUsage; the COM headers are not included via dxgi.h — the vtable slots are declared by hand in interface-inheritance order (the COM binary ABI is stable) and the IIDs are custom constants taken from the SDK's published values, avoiding MinGW header version drift and any dxgi.lib link surface. Utilization = PDH `\GPU Engine(*)\Utilization Percentage`, summed over instances whose `pid_*_luid_0xHEX_0xHEX_*` name matches the adapter LUID's low 32 bits (aggregating many engines and processes); **this counter type needs two samples before it yields formatted values, so the query handle is kept process-wide across ticks and the first tick is always 0; the instance-name format and aggregation rule need on-device confirmation**.
  - **Three corrections to the hand-declared COM, from the SDK (SYS1 final review)**: ① all three IIDs were wrong — IDXGIFactory1 was written as 770AAE78-F26F-4DBA-83A9-50BC11D9EE9B (real 770AAE78-F26F-4DBA-A829-253C83D1B387), so CreateDXGIFactory1 refused it and returned E_NOINTERFACE → factory==NULL → no GPU enumerated at all; IDXGIAdapter3 was written as 645967A4-1392-4316-9CEC-9CAF7113F420 (real 645967A4-1392-4310-A798-8053CE3E93FD), so QueryInterface always failed → used VRAM never available; IDXGIAdapter1 (no call site today) was written as 290462F0-AC1E-4212-AA25-4F95B4968B12 (real 29038F61-3839-4626-91FD-086879011A05). ② The IDXGIFactory1 vtable omitted CreateSoftwareAdapter and swapped Make/GetWindowAssociation: the SDK order (the IDXGIFactory block in win32metadata dxgi.h plus the IDXGIFactory1 append block) is EnumAdapters, MakeWindowAssociation, GetWindowAssociation, CreateSwapChain, CreateSoftwareAdapter, then IDXGIFactory1 adds EnumAdapters1 and IsCurrent — so the declared index 11 "EnumAdapters1" was really CreateSoftwareAdapter, which was called with Module=(HMODULE)i (taking a reference count on a module handle) and the 16-iteration loop never found a hardware adapter. ③ The IDXGIAdapter slot names were corrected to the SDK too (EnumOutputs; RegisterHardwareContentProtectionTeardownStatusEvent / UnregisterHardwareContentProtectionTeardownStatus, not RegisterVideoMemoryBudget*). Lesson: **a hand-declared COM's IIDs and slots must each be checked against an authoritative source (win32metadata generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders dxgi.h/dxgi1_4.h, Microsoft Learn struct docs) — "custom constant" does not mean "from memory"**. Verification: with no Windows host here, the check is self-validating (an expected IID/slot table derived from the SDK headers + compile-time `_Static_assert(offsetof(slot)==index)` under gcc + a run-time memcmp; the harness is not committed), and the pre-fix code fails it precisely. The semantics still need Windows real-machine acceptance (GPU page cards / VRAM curves).
  - Temperature: NVIDIA only, via the nvidia-smi subprocess, virtualised into `/sys/class/hwmon/hwmonN/{name,temp1_input,temp1_label}` (one entry per card, millidegrees) so the sensor page parses it unchanged; AMD/Intel temperature is unavailable and not fabricated (no WinRing0-class kernel driver), so the hwmon directory returns NULL on that machine and an empty sensor page is a legitimate state. nvidia-smi's first column is not DXGI's virtual address, so it is matched by the sixth column's model name against desc.Description and rewritten to close the gap (the model name is the only string both share; if the driver renames the product, attribution fails and that card loses utilization/VRAM/temperature, degrading to static DXGI info).
  - Subprocess primitives: CreateProcess + CREATE_NO_WINDOW + an anonymous pipe for output (hStdOutput/hStdError share it) rather than _popen — under a GUI process, _popen's console child flashes a black window; WaitForSingleObject with a 3s timeout and TerminateProcess as backstop. nvidia-smi results carry a 500ms static cache (at 1Hz the hwmon and gpu_list consumers each read once, avoiding two subprocesses per second).
  - Link discipline: pdh/dxgi/iphlpapi/psapi/ntdll all go through LoadLibrary+GetProcAddress, while kernel32/advapi32 are MinGW/MSVC default libraries and are called directly — zero link-flag changes, so prebuild keeps full custody.
  - monotonic must be real (QueryPerformanceCounter): every rate metric divides by wall-clock differences, and the placeholder's constant 0 would make the denominator always 0.
  - Verification: this machine has no mingw/MSVC so the Windows branch cannot really be compiled; syntax and symbol surface are checked with "a minimal Win32 stub header + gcc -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra" at zero warnings (the stub header is not committed), and real correctness is left to the CI Windows runner compiling for real plus Windows real-machine acceptance of the five pages (see the TODO.md SYS1 real-machine list): specifically the PDH PhysicalDisk/GPU Engine counter paths under Chinese Windows, the GPU Engine LUID aggregation numbers, nvidia-smi ↔ DXGI model-name matching, and the empty sensor page on a machine without an N card.
- **Windows process-management semantics unified (SYS2): kill / priority / error codes are normalised to Linux errno semantics inside the stub, so the MoonBit layer's errno_text and Result need zero changes**. Decision: ① the first cut maps kill to TerminateProcess only (SIGTERM/SIGKILL map the same, so the UI collapses to one button; termination is asynchronous after TerminateProcess is issued, so a short WaitForSingleObject(3s) makes "ended N processes" truthful; the gentler WM_CLOSE route was deferred). ② Priority maps the four tiers IDLE/NORMAL/HIGH/REALTIME: set clamps to the nearest tier (≥10 IDLE / -9..9 NORMAL / -16..-10 HIGH / ≤-17 REALTIME), get returns the tier's representative value (19/10/0/-10/-13/-20; BELOW/ABOVE_NORMAL clamp to the neighbouring tier), and the virtual /proc/[pid]/stat nice field changes from constant 0 to the representative looked back from GetPriorityClass (so the process page's nice column and its sorting become real). ③ Win32 error codes are translated to errno numbers inside the stub: ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED→1 (EPERM), ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER→22 (EINVAL), ERROR_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD/ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION→13 (EACCES), ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND/PATH_NOT_FOUND→2 (ENOENT), NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY/OUTOFMEMORY→12 (ENOMEM), INVALID_HANDLE→9 (EBADF), ALREADY_EXISTS→17 (EEXIST), BROKEN_PIPE→32 (EPIPE); anything unlisted becomes EIO=5. ④ **OpenProcess on an exited pid always reports ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (87)**: without a special case, "process does not exist" would be shown as "invalid parameter", so kill/get/set all special-case it into ESRCH (3), matching Linux kill on a missing process. ⑤ REALTIME needs SeIncreaseBasePriorityPrivilege; for a normal user SetPriorityClass reports ERROR_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD→EACCES, aligning with Linux setpriority returning EACCES for negative values on a non-owned process. ⑥ UI copy becomes platform-aware (the pure functions kill_button_labels / priority_ui / priority_result / priority_col_header take `platform` explicitly so unit tests can drive it): Windows shows a single "End task (terminate immediately)" button, the renice message shows the tier name plus the value read back after setting (the real value after discrete clamping), and the priority column header says "Priority"; Linux keeps the two-step kill and continuous nice. ⑦ Unavailable sources such as temperature show "—" per slot: processor cards "12% · —", GPU cards "35% · —" / "— · 55℃" (the old code omitted the slot, so users could not tell "no data" from "not refreshed yet"), and the sensor page gets an explicit "no temperature source available" empty row. ⑧ Platform detection gains yue_sysmon_is_windows (fixed at compile time, one copy per branch) rather than importing @yue.platform(), keeping the data layer self-sufficient.
  - **Pitfall: defining a stub header by the shape of your own code hides real SDK struct-member errors (SYS2 fixing SYS1's leftover)**: SYS1 read the PDH raw value as `RawValue.FirstValue.largeValue`, but the real pdh.h has `PDH_RAW_COUNTER.FirstValue` as a LONGLONG (no `.largeValue` suffix; the anonymous-union shape belongs to `PDH_FMT_COUNTERVALUE`'s FmtValue) — SYS1's minimal stub header had been written to match the code, so `-fsyntax-only` passed and the CI Windows runner would necessarily fail. SYS2 corrected it to `RawValue.FirstValue` and wrote the stub header to the real SDK shape (FirstValue a LONGLONG, FmtValue the anonymous union); conclusion: a stub header only validates the symbol and syntax surface, struct member names and layout must still be checked member by member against the real SDK, and zero `-fsyntax-only` warnings does not mean it will really compile.
  - SYS2 verification: no Windows host here, so the Windows branch passes `gcc -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra` at zero warnings against a minimal Win32 stub header defined to the real SDK shape (not committed); after touching the stub, `moon build examples/sysmonitor` is warning-free (sysmon.o really recompiles); `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test` 608 all green (sysproc_wbtest adds 8: the errno_text translation targets, the four tier boundaries, the kill/priority button and result copy, the column header, the with_temp "—" placeholders, and get/set on a missing pid normalising to ESRCH); **real termination and REALTIME elevation behaviour must be verified on a Windows machine** (list in TODO.md SYS2).
- **macOS data layer (SYS3): the Mach / libproc / getfsstat / getifaddrs / system_profiler sources are virtualised into Linux-shaped /proc and /sys text at the stub's read entry points, so the MoonBit parsing layer and its pure functions need zero changes (the same SYS1 decision: "the Linux path is the cross-layer contract"); GPU goes through a `system_profiler -json` subprocess with the JSON parsed in MoonBit pure functions; disk IO rates and temperature have no source, so the UI shows "—**. The seven routes and their platform splits:
  - Platform split: the stub has three platform structures (`_WIN32` / `__APPLE__` / Linux); kill / priority / statvfs / monotonic / page_size share one POSIX implementation (macOS and Linux agree semantically, so the two-button process-management UI and continuous nice apply unchanged); the CPU / memory / process / network / mount five routes go to virtualised text; the MoonBit layer opens exactly two branches (`on_macos() = @yue.platform() == "macos"`): gpu_list parses system_profiler output, and DiskInfo tolerates a missing /proc/diskstats. Mach / proc_info / statfs / if_data64 are declared from the xnu source layouts (the symbols sit in libSystem's default link range) to sidestep SDK header version drift — the same idea as the hand-written vtable and custom PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS on the Windows branch.
  - CPU: `host_processor_info(PROCESSOR_CPU_LOAD_INFO)` gives per-logical-core cumulative user/system/idle/nice ticks, the aggregate line sums the cores, and the column order matches /proc/stat (iowait/irq/softirq/steal have no counterpart and stay 0); the tick unit is mach's own and only feeds ratios, independent of clk_tck; the returned buffer must be released with `vm_deallocate(mach_task_self_())` (one block per tick at 1Hz, and leaks accumulate). Model from `machdep.cpu.brand_string` (Apple Silicon implements it too) → fallback `hw.model`; clock from `hw.cpufrequency` (Hz→MHz, absent on some machines = 0); core count from `hw.ncpu`.
  - Memory: `hw.memsize` for total; `host_statistics64(HOST_VM_INFO64)` for free / inactive, available = free + inactive (Activity Monitor's rule); swap via sysctl `vm.swapusage` (the `xsw_usage` layout is not published by the SDK, so it is declared from the general definition: total/avail/used as uint64 plus pagesize and encrypted).
  - Disks: `getfsstat(MNT_WAIT)` rewritten into /proc/mounts-shaped text, with all filtering kept on the MoonBit side — `is_pseudo_fs` gains the BSD pseudo filesystems (devfs / fdesc / nullfs / volfs / union / synth; autofs is shared) and `is_system_mount` gains the macOS system volumes (/private is the swap backing volume, plus /System/Volumes/{Preboot,Update,VM,Hardware,iSCPreboot}, while /System/Volumes/Data holds user data and stays); mount points may contain spaces (user volume names), so the stub escapes them as `\040` per kernel convention and the MoonBit side restores them with `unescape_mount` — unrestored, whitespace splitting takes the wrong columns and the row disappears from the capacity table after statvfs fails; capacity reuses the shared POSIX statvfs. **IO rates have no source (IOKit is deferred)**: failing to read `/proc/diskstats` no longer fails the whole tick (the old early return blanked the entire disk page), `DiskInfo.read_bps/write_bps` change from Double to `Double?`, None renders "—" and pushes no point onto the IO curve (no fake 0 line); mounts that cannot be attributed to diskstats (NFS and friends) are also None, which is more honest than the old constant 0 B/s.
  - Network: `getifaddrs` (with a 200ms TTL cache — each card's rx and tx read the path separately, so without a cache every tick pulled the whole table twice), `ifa_data` pointing at `struct if_data64`, using ifi_ibytes/ifi_obytes as the counters; one entry per address family deduplicated by name; loopback "lo0" normalised to "lo" (main.mbt's rate aggregation excludes by "lo", as the Windows branch does for Software Loopback).
  - Processes: `proc_listpids(PROC_ALL_PIDS)` to enumerate (NULL/0 to learn the size plus an 8KB margin for processes born between the two calls), skipping pid 0 (kernel_task, which has no command line or timings); `proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)` for ppid / nice / state / comm and `PROC_PIDTASKINFO` for thread count and nanosecond timings (÷1e7 → 10ms tick, with `yue_sysmon_clk_tck` hard-coded to 100 on the macOS branch so the units agree); RSS bytes ÷ page size; `proc_pidpath`'s full path as cmdline (NULL on permission denial / kernel_task, and the MoonBit layer falls back to [comm]); states mapped from BSD p_stat (SIDL→I / SRUN→R / SZOMB→Z / SSLEEP→S / SSTOP→T). PROC_PIDTASKINFO was chosen over proc_pid_rusage because one call yields thread count / both timings / RSS.
  - GPU: the `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType -json` subprocess — fork + anonymous pipe + poll timeout (8s) then SIGKILL rather than popen (a shell child flashes a window under a GUI process, the same reasoning as Windows' CREATE_NO_WINDOW), execv with the absolute path `/usr/sbin/system_profiler` to avoid a PATH search allocation; the first run takes seconds, then the result is cached process-wide (model / total VRAM are static, like enumerating DXGI once on Windows), and failure retries with a 5s backoff; the raw JSON is handed back and `parse_system_profiler_gpu` parses it in MoonBit (splitting `_items` by brace depth while ignoring braces inside strings, model from `sppci_model` falling back to `_name`, VRAM from `spdisplays_vram`, vendor sniffed from the name). Utilization and temperature have no source (no public GPU-utilization API; SMC / IOReport private keys are deferred), so busy / celsius stay None and the UI shows "—" per slot.
  - Temperature: not shown in the first cut (SMC / IOReport private keys deferred); `/sys/class/hwmon` naturally returns None on macOS, and the sensor page's empty row plus the processor card's "· —" reuse SYS2's existing convention.
  - Link discipline: every new symbol is inside libSystem's default link range, so zero link-flag changes; extern declarations must link on all three platforms — non-Apple uses a same-ABI placeholder returning NULL (the MoonBit `gpu_list` macOS branch only calls when `on_macos()` is true, so the placeholder is never reached at run time), otherwise the Linux / Windows test builds fail at link time (this batch did exactly that and had to add the placeholder).
  - **Pitfall: verify Mach constants and struct layouts against the xnu source before declaring them by hand**: `PROCESSOR_CPU_LOAD_INFO` is 2 not 1, `MNT_WAIT` is 1 not 2, `MAXCOMLEN` is 16, the 64-bit `statfs` has `f_mntonname` before `f_mntfromname`, and `if_data64`'s counters are `ifi_ibytes/ifi_obytes` (there is no `ifi_oobytes`) — writing these wrong from memory never fails to compile (your declaration becomes the truth), and `-fsyntax-only` only checks syntax and symbols while struct offsets must still be checked member by member (the same lesson as SYS2); `host_statistics64`'s count means "below REV0's count → KERN_FAILURE, above → filled as an older version", so pass 40 integers per the current xnu full layout — extra fields are safe.
  - **Pitfall: `String::unsafe_get` returns a UInt16 (a UTF-16 code unit), not a Char**: while scanning JSON / escaped strings character by character, `c == '\\'` does not typecheck — either compare via `to_int()` or copy the untouched runs in blocks (`write_stringview` + slices, surrogate-pair safe); mixing the two invites "has type UInt16, wanted Char".
  - Pitfall: a host clock that jumped backwards makes moon treat `.o` files with future mtimes as current, so `touch`-ing sources does not trigger a rebuild — when `moon build` reports "up to date" after a stub change, delete the corresponding `.o` under `_build` first.
  - SYS3 verification: no macOS machine in this environment. On the Linux host `moon check` is warning-free and `moon test` 614 all green (syshw_wbtest adds 6: unescape_mount's restore and invalid sequences, parse_mounts against the macOS getfsstat shape (spaced volume names / BSD pseudo filesystems), is_system_mount's system volumes, parse_vram, json_string_value / json_items_objects splitting and nesting, parse_system_profiler_gpu's dual-card parse and tolerance; after DiskInfo's rate fields became Option, the S5 / S6 live-sampling assertions were relaxed to both shapes accordingly); the macOS branch passes `gcc -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -D__APPLE__` at zero warnings (syntax and symbol surface only — the struct layouts were checked field by field against xnu, semantics left to real hardware); after touching the stub, `moon build examples/sysmonitor` is warning-free; the non-mac placeholder symbols were confirmed exported in the Linux build artefacts. **The seven data routes and process management must be verified on a real mac** (list in TODO.md SYS3): specifically the per-core numbers from host_processor_info (a wrong order reads idle as user), system_profiler -json's key names and attribution (sppci_model / spdisplays_vram / spdisplays_vendor — test on Apple Silicon and on Intel/AMD cards), the getfsstat mount table against df (including spaced volume names and /System/Volumes/Data), proc_listpids' process count against ps, and kill / setpriority taking effect for real.
- **Linux GPU utilization completed (SYS4: DRM fdinfo aggregation gives whole-card utilization without root, for i915 / xe / amdgpu). The earlier framing "ask for administrator privileges to read the GPU" is replaced, on this machine's evidence, with "complete the data source without root + make the elevation boundary explicit"**. Decision: ① **permission evidence** (measured here as uid 1000 on Ubuntu 24.04): `/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/temp*_input` and amdgpu's `gpu_busy_percent` are both 0444, and DRM fdinfo comes through the standard /proc interface (this user's own fdinfo files are r--r--r--), so nothing the panel normally needs requires root; the only restricted path, `/sys/kernel/debug/dri` (debugfs, drwx------ root), is the i915 debug view (per-engine / per-client detail) and carries no metric the panel wants — so "request elevation to read the GPU" had no data behind it and polkit / pkexec integration is not planned (a separate batch if the user insists on the elevation route). ② Utilization source priority: nvidia-smi (N cards) > sysfs `gpu_busy_percent` (amdgpu, a driver-side whole-card average covering all clients) > DRM fdinfo aggregation (i915 / xe / amdgpu fallback); the VRAM / temperature conventions are unchanged. ③ fdinfo aggregation rule: enumerate `/proc/<pid>/fdinfo`, parse `drm-driver` / `drm-pdev` / `drm-client-id` / `drm-engine-*` (all engines summed), merge by (device key, client-id) (dup'd fds and fds passed over a unix socket are the same drm_file with identical counters, so take the maximum once), and convert the difference between two samples against wall clock into whole-card utilization (clamped 0..100) — the same source as intel_gpu_top / nvtop. ④ Attribution: `drm-pdev` (kernel ≥6.5, a PCI slot address shaped like the sysfs device directory name) wins; older kernels lack it, so the fallback matches `/sys/bus/pci/devices/<addr>/uevent`'s `DRIVER=` name (two cards on the same driver merge into one value — a known boundary). ⑤ The scan only runs when a card has neither a sysfs utilization source nor nvidia-smi coverage: AMD / NVIDIA machines skip the whole tick, Intel machines scan every tick (the same cost as nvtop / intel_gpu_top). ⑥ No number before the first sample (from the next frame), and a client first seen in a tick is not counted; the data-layer entry moved from `gpu_list()` to `GpuMonitor::tick()` (previous samples live with the App; the macOS branch is unchanged).
  - **Version boundaries (checked against the torvalds/linux source version by version)**: `drm-engine-*` / `drm-driver` / `drm-client-id` since v5.19 (amdgpu / i915 "Convert to common fdinfo format v5", 2022-05-26; absent in v5.18, present in v5.19); `drm-pdev` since v6.5 (the `dev_is_pci` branch of `drm_show_fdinfo` in `drm_file.c`; absent in v6.4, format `%04x:%02x:%02x.%d`); the cycles / maxfreq keys since 6.2 (not consumed here). Ubuntu 22.04's 5.15 kernel has no engine keys → busy is None and shows "—"; 24.04's 6.8 has all three.
  - **Known boundaries (honest rule: show "—" when a source is unavailable)**: ① fdinfo only covers this user's processes — other users' (root services / other logged-in users) `/proc/<pid>/fdinfo/<fd>` reads return EACCES (measured: `/proc/1/fdinfo/1` permission denied), so whole-card utilization is "as far as this user can see" and will under-report; full accounting needs root (no polkit for now). ② Scan cost measured: the full /proc fdinfo walk touches 9123 files / 4.2MB, about 56ms per tick (measured by a C program with the same read loop as the stub, on a 554-process desktop; Python at the same rule took 78ms). ③ A short-lived client that opens and closes between two scans loses its busy time along with the client (the fdinfo counters live on the client). ④ Parallel engines (gfx + compute at once) can sum above wall clock, clamped to 100. ⑤ Non-monotonic counter updates are allowed by the kernel spec and are treated as a zero delta.
  - **Pitfall: parsing must exclude `drm-engine-capacity-<name>`**: with several video engines, i915 prints the parallel engine count (e.g. `drm-engine-capacity-video: 2`), and collecting by `has_prefix("drm-engine-")` would add that engine count (2) as nanoseconds into busy time; the value side likewise takes the first whitespace-separated field before parse_u64 — engine values carry an ` ns` suffix, side keys carry units (`drm-memory-vram: 1024 KiB`), and amdgpu prints an extra space after the colon in `drm-memory-gtt: `; parsing without taking the first field always fails.
  - Pitfall: /proc directory enumeration includes non-process entries such as `cpuinfo` / `self` / `irq`, so filter to pure numbers before walking fdinfo; amdgpu omits idle engines entirely (source has `if (!usage[hw_ip]) continue;`), so entries list only nonzero engines and the sum is unaffected; i915 gen<8 returns early without engine keys → parses as None and busy shows "—".
  - SYS4 verification: zero stub changes (pure MoonBit side, reusing the read_text_file / list_dir primitives). On the Linux host `moon check` is warning-free and `moon test` 623 all green (syshw_wbtest adds 9: parse_drm_fdinfo's amdgpu / i915 / None shapes, is_drm_engine_key and drm_device_key, drm_clients_total merging (dup fd / cross-process / two devices / missing client-id), drm_busy_percent (first frame / fallback / clamp 100), is_pid_entry, parse_uevent_driver, and a two-tick live fdinfo sample); after deleting the sysmonitor `.o` under `_build`, `moon build examples/sysmonitor` is warning-free. **Real-machine verification on i915 / xe / amdgpu is performed by the user** (this machine runs the NVIDIA proprietary driver, has no fdinfo usage counters, and cannot exercise this path): ① Intel iGPU utilization compared against `intel_gpu_top` in the same window ② AMD dGPU sysfs `gpu_busy_percent` versus fdinfo (sysfs must win) ③ attribution correctness on a dual-card machine (drm-pdev first) ④ driver-name fallback attribution on an older kernel (<6.5) ⑤ whether short-lived GPU clients (benchmarking loops repeatedly starting and stopping) under-report utilization ⑥ the magnitude of the gap against `sudo intel_gpu_top` ⑦ the scan's effect on the 1Hz duty cycle.
- **Linux GPU model names (SYS5): AMD / Intel cards get their commercial model name from pci.ids — sysfs carries only numeric ids (vendor / device nodes) and the driver binding name, so the commercial name lives in no /sys node and a plain-text database without root is the only source; when it misses, fall back to the device id verbatim**. Decision: ① source priority: nvidia-smi hit (N cards, where its name is more specific than pci.ids — smi's "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070" vs pci.ids' "GA104 [GeForce RTX 3070 Lite Hash Rate]") > pci.ids lookup by vendor:device > device id text ("0x7480", which at least separates cards); the "(未知)" placeholder from a failed sysfs read becomes empty so the UI omits the model slot. ② Path differences: the hwdata package at `/usr/share/hwdata/pci.ids` (on many distributions a symlink into misc) and the pciutils package at `/usr/share/misc/pci.ids`, tried in order; when neither is reachable (database not installed / Flatpak sandbox / non-Linux) the "not found" fallback applies. ③ Caching: the whole pci.ids text is read once when first needed and kept (about 1.4MB, inside the native-stub's 16MB single-file cap), and parse results are cached per PCI address — measured, one full-file search costs about 14ms (`moon test` debug build; Intel's vendor sits at line 27868 of 38108, so early exit still walks 70% of the file), which cannot be repeated per card per tick at 1Hz; vendor:device is static hardware info so one lookup at the first tick is enough, and when the database is unreachable the cached value is the fallback and the next start retries. ④ UI: the model name is folded into the sensor page's section title (the existing gpu_label path, page_sensors.mbt unchanged); overview cards show compact numbers only and leave the model to the detail page.
  - **pci.ids format measured (2024.03.31, 38108 lines)**: unindented lines are vendors (4 hex id + two spaces + name), one Tab = a device of that vendor, two Tabs = a subsystem (not consumed here), '#' starts a comment; 2378 vendors, 18685 devices, 16258 subsystems; the file has no CRLF, no trailing whitespace, and every id is exactly 4 lowercase hex digits; the 7 blank lines all sit in the header comment area and inside the class section (modern versions do not blank between vendor blocks); the trailing class section ("C 00" onwards) is shaped like vendor lines but its ids are not 4 hex digits, so it cannot match naturally; "ffff Illegal Vendor ID" is the last vendor, has no device lines, and is followed immediately by the class section — looking it up exercises exactly the "left the section, return early" path.
  - **Pitfall: empty-id normalisation must not zero-pad**: `norm_pci_id("")` padding "left-pad with zeros to 4 digits" would yield the fake valid id "0000" (caught by the unit test's first run), so an empty string must stay empty; a failed sysfs read leaves vendor / device as the "(未知)" placeholder, and is_hex4 must reject it before the fallback applies.
  - Pitfall: keep the model name verbatim, including internal spaces and brackets (e.g. "Navi 33 [Radeon RX 7700S/7600/7600S/7600M XT/PRO W7600]") — never split on whitespace and rejoin (this version has 0 names with double spaces, but slicing the whole run is the correct approach); slicing indexes by UTF-16 code unit (`StringView::exact_view`'s basis), not by `iter2`'s codepoint index — every structural character is ASCII, so surrogate pairs can only appear inside names; a device entry with an id but no name (never in a real database) is not a hit — keep scanning and fall back to the id.
  - SYS5 verification: zero stub changes (pure MoonBit side, reusing the read_text_file primitive). On the Linux host `moon check` is warning-free and `moon test` 628 all green (syshw_wbtest adds 5: norm_pci_id / is_hex4, pci_ids_device_name's indent-level parsing (subsystems skipped / no cross-vendor leak / vendors with no devices / class section / early exit leaving the section / invalid ids), gpu_model_name's four shapes (smi first / database hit / miss and absent entry fall back to id / placeholder id blank), GpuMonitor::gpu_model's persistent cache and smi priority, and a live pci.ids sample (take the first vendor/device pair positively, plus a dead vendor with no device lines negatively)); after deleting the sysmonitor `.o` under `_build`, `moon build examples/sysmonitor` is warning-free; on this machine (Ubuntu 24.04, NVIDIA proprietary driver) three real entries parse correctly (1002:7480 → Navi 33, 8086:3ea0 → WhiskeyLake-U GT2, 10de:2488 → GA104). **Real-machine verification on AMD / Intel is performed by the user**: ① the sensor page's section title shows the commercial model name for an AMD dGPU (compare with `lspci -nn`) ② same for an Intel iGPU ③ on a dual-card machine each card shows its own model ④ when not found (a very new card / missing entry) the device id is displayed rather than blank ⑤ the fallback shape on a minimal install (no hwdata / pciutils) and inside a Flatpak sandbox ⑥ path differences on other distributions (Fedora / Arch hwdata, openSUSE, etc.) ⑦ how a long model name wraps or overflows in the section title.
