- sysmonitor UI copy discipline (from the full UI-polish pass): interface text states only "what it is / how to use it" — never data conventions or implementation paths (e.g. /proc paths, "two-sample difference", "milli-degree conversion", or a "nvidia-smi planned later" note); rates, capacities and axis values always switch units dynamically (B→K→M→G) so numbers stay short; the large 24px statistic cards especially must never wrap and overflow.
- sysmonitor overview card pattern, modeled on Mission Center: icon + title, a spec subtitle (hardware specs such as CPU model / total capacity / mount point live in the card subtitle — not in a window-level subtitle row), a current-value line (usage % · temperature, used / total · swap), and an in-card sparkline (series window + end dot; fixed 0-100 range or peak-adaptive, dual series overlaid for network rx/tx). Cards share width via flex and equal height per row via stretch, following window resizes; each card is self-contained and readable without the rest of the window.
- xrandr's output format changes across versions (measured while enumerating displays): since 1.5.2 the refresh-rate markers ('*' current / '+' preferred / 'i' interlaced) print '+' as a standalone token placed **after** the rate it marks (`59.95 +  75.00`, and xrandr --verbose confirms 59.95 is that +preferred mode), while older versions append it to the rate (`59.95+`). mon_fold_marker_tokens re-attaches standalone marker tokens to the preceding token, normalising to the attached shape before parsing.
- **Two correctness defects in the process data (EX2, high severity: all negative nice values display 0, and a newly appearing pid pegs CPU% at full scale)**. ① the nice field of `/proc/[pid]/stat` is **signed** (-20..19), but the parser used `parse_u64`, which returns None for a leading minus → `unwrap_or(0)` silently turned every negative nice into 0: the process page's nice column reads wrong and ByNice sorting reads wrong too (this host has 142 negative-nice processes, all kworker threads at -20 — an everyday population, not an edge case). Fix: choose the parser by field sign inside the same parse — unsigned fields (utime/stime/starttime/rss_pages) use `parse_u64`, signed fields (nice/ppid/threads) use the existing `parse_i64`, with field indices and reading rules unchanged. ② `ProcMonitor::tick`'s previous sample used `self.prev.get(pid).unwrap_or(0)`: for a **pid that appeared between samples** (a new process, or a child spawned by `moon test` itself) there is no previous sample, yet treating "previous tick = 0" made the delta cover the process's whole since-boot accumulated ticks, so CPU% jumped straight to the cores×100 clamp (white-box control measured `400 != 0`, a single-tick full-scale reading) and only fell back to the truth on the next tick. Fix: the previous sample became optional behind the pure function `proc_tick_cpu_pct(prev : Int64?, cur, clk_tck, wall_s, cores)`, which returns 0 for the tick when prev is missing (the same rule as "no sample before the first frame"); `tick` now passes `self.prev.get(pid)`. With a previous sample present it dispatches to the existing `proc_cpu_pct` and behavior is unchanged.
  - Pitfall: both `parse_u64` and `parse_i64` collapse failures into `unwrap_or(0)`, so `None` and "genuinely 0" are indistinguishable at the call site — using the wrong parser on a signed field raises nothing and only yields a wrong value, which is why this class of defect survives so long; picking the parser explicitly by field sign beats one generic `num()`.
  - Pitfall: for a delta-based CPU% metric, "no previous sample" must be distinguished from "previous sample is 0". The first is "unknown", the second is "really started at 0"; `unwrap_or(0)` merges the two, and for a **monotonically accumulating counter** (ticks / bytes / sectors) that necessarily produces a since-boot full delta, which the clamping then disguises as "full scale" instead of an obvious outlier — hard to attribute by eye.
  - Verification: zero stub changes (pure MoonBit side). `moon check --deny-warn` warning-free and `moon test` 644 all green (sysproc_wbtest adds 3: parse_proc_pid_stat with a real negative-nice sample (this host's /proc/4/stat kworker/R-rcu_gp, nice=-20 asserted field by field, plus nice=-1 / 19 / a bare minus fallback), sort_procs' ByNice ordering with negatives (three tiers -20/0/19 no longer mixed), and proc_tick_cpu_pct giving 0 on the tick with no previous sample, compared against with-sample full load / half load / clamp / invalid wall clock / negative delta); after deleting the sysmonitor `.o` under `_build`, `moon build examples/sysmonitor` is warning-free; white-box control — stashing the pre-fix code and running `moon test -p sysmonitor` makes the negative-nice case fail precisely (`0 != -20`) and restoring the old `proc_tick_cpu_pct` semantics makes the tick case fail precisely (`400 != 0`); with the fix back, 24/24 pass; the real-/proc end-to-end case (forcing short-lived processes to fill the 2s window) measures the new pid's tick CPU% at 0.

### System capability data layer (volume / brightness / browser history / VS Code history / app lookup)

This batch adds five modules (yue/volume, brightness, browser_history, vscode_history, appfind), measured on Ubuntu 24.04 + XFCE + X11, PipeWire audio stack, Chrome with multiple profiles, and VS Code (the official OSS distribution). What follows is what real-machine testing produced:

- Volume verified on both backends (wpctl first, pactl as fallback): wpctl `get-volume @DEFAULT_SINK@` prints `Volume: 0.42 [MUTED]`, and the sink display name comes from `wpctl status` (hierarchical text, the first entry under Audio → Sinks); the pactl path needs three queries (get-default-sink + get-sink-volume + get-sink-mute). **pactl's human-readable output is localized per locale** — in a Chinese locale it prints 「音量:」 rather than "Volume:" — so parsing written against English text fails on a localized machine; the child environment must pin `LC_ALL=C` (vol_env_blob also passes PATH, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and HOME: PipeWire/Pulse socket discovery depends on XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, and without it the tool cannot reach the service and exits non-zero). Sample assertions use text captured from the real machine (volume_wbtest; the pactl sample is LC_ALL=C output — localized text in it counts as a parse failure).
- Browser history reads the Chrome-family SQLite files directly (moonsqlitefile pure parsing: no SQLite FFI, no locking, no copying the source database): ① the time base is microseconds since 1601-01-01 UTC (same origin as a Windows FILETIME), Unix ms = µs/1000 − 11644473600000, and the measured sample 13435769563030519 → 2026-10-06T14:12:43.030Z; ② although urls.id is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, on disk the column stores **Null** (a rowid alias is not written out), so reading by column position must not assume a type; ③ rows with a nonzero hidden column are redirects and other hidden entries and must be filtered; ④ while Chrome runs, new writes land in the -wal file, and the current implementation passes only the main database to open_database (no WAL merge — moonsqlitefile also offers open_wal_database); ⑤ the bytes read during probing are handed straight to the open call, so one database is never read twice (History databases commonly reach tens of MB).
- VS Code local history: ① the `<hash>` directory name in `User/History/<hash>/entries.json` is a base-31 rolling hash over the resource URI (seed 149417, wrapping into Int32), printed as a **signed** lowercase hex value — negative directory names really exist (measured `-10b5e510`), and recomputing three cases (positive / negative / vscode-userdata scheme) all hit; ② some entries.json records carry **no source field** (measured), so parsing must not assume it; ③ storage.json's windowsState has lastActiveWindow first plus an openedWindows array, whose window objects come in two shapes — folder (a plain directory) or workspaceUri (a .code-workspace) — and the URIs are percent-encoded (space `%20`, Chinese `%E4%B8%AD`) and must be decoded; ④ the end-to-end case only runs where VS Code user data exists (gated by vsc_supported), and all pure logic is asserted white-box against in-memory samples.
- Brightness: setting goes to logind's SetBrightness (system bus, session/auto objects, through @traybus), enumeration and the current value read /sys/class/backlight sysfs read-only — when logind is offline set reports Unsupported while devices/get keep working; keyboard backlight lives in the leds subsystem (device names shaped like `inputN::kbd_backlight`). sysfs value parsing tolerates surrounding whitespace and a trailing newline.
- App lookup (appfind): desktop entries have no directory-enumeration primitive, so `appfind_installed_with` takes the listing function from the caller, and the default convenience entry point was dropped because it always returned nothing and its name promised otherwise; `appfind_executable` decides "hit" by whole-file readability (read_binary_file) — slurping a large executable just to test existence is an accepted trade-off (fixing it needs a new native stat primitive, so the shim stays untouched for now).
- Default-application lookup (defaultapps, closing an omission in the checklist): ① queries go through `xdg-mime query filetype/default`, and association enumeration reads the three mimeapps.list layers directly (`~/.config` → `~/.local/share/applications` → `/usr/share/applications`, i.e. the XDG mimeapps precedence), with a thin read_text_file parser for every path that does not depend on a command; ② **repeated same-name keys in mimeapps.list are a candidate list, the opposite of the "first key wins" rule for .desktop INI** — several lines for one MIME under `[Default Applications]` register candidates in last-wins order, so da_parse_mimeapps does not dedup same keys and da_default_for's fallback path takes the section's first value of that MIME's last candidate; ③ `xdg-mime query default` for an unregistered type **returns an empty string with exit code 0** (not a nonzero exit), so "no default" can only be judged from empty output, never from the exit code; ④ setting is a read-modify-write of the `[Default Applications]` section in ~/.config/mimeapps.list: replace the line if present, append inside the section if not, add the section at the end if that is missing, writing through write_text_file (same-package FFI, as in autostart); ⑤ libyue's native Notification has no progress interface (the vendored notification.h exposes only title/body/info/silent/image/actions, and the shim has no matching FFI), and the Linux standard for notification progress is the freedesktop hints `value` field (reachable over the traybus D-Bus) — this batch confirmed the native notification surface is sufficient and built no progress bar; if it becomes necessary it goes through D-Bus Notify + a{sv} hints.
- Real-machine entry point for browser history / VS Code history: the NoahLiu/gui-examples/systemprobe example (charts and system capabilities on one board) — `moon run NoahLiu/gui-examples/systemprobe` and press "读取系统能力" to see all five modules' live results.

#### Media and desktop-control command routes (pr_run as the single wrapper, with an MPRIS bus fallback)

Every command-class module added in this batch goes through `pr_run` in `yue/procrun.mbt` (spawn → timed reclaim → stdout/stderr captured through a temp file) rather than spawning on its own; the environment pins the C locale, exit code 0 normalises to Ok and nonzero to Err carrying stderr, so callers never inspect codes themselves. **Meaning of a missing command**: on Unix the shell surfaces it as exit code 127 and each module's own `*_supported()` probe normalises it into Unsupported (pp_profiles / prt_default / nl_supported / win_list each probe their own command), so callers classify by the error value instead of guessing from text. The command routes and their degradation chains:

| Capability | Primary route | Fallback route | Probe (read-only, no side effects) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Night colour temperature nightlight | `redshift -P -O <K>` (2500K..6500K, one-shot set) | `xrandr --output <output> --gamma R:G:B` (red nudged 0.85..1.00, blue decayed 1.00..2.20, green fixed at 1.00) | `redshift -V` exits 0; otherwise `xrandr --query` works (no connected output → Unsupported, headless) |
| Display configuration monitor | `xrandr --query`, fully parsed (refresh rates as integer centihertz) | none (Unavailable → Unsupported) | same single read-only `--query` probe |
| Wallpaper | XFCE `xfconf-query -c xfce4-desktop -p /backdrop/.../last-image` (read / write) | GNOME `gsettings get/set org.gnome.desktop.background picture-uri`; KDE `qdbus6/qdbus org.kde.plasmashell evaluateScript` (not verified on real hardware) | desktop detection reuses @traybus.detect_desktop (XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP); an unknown desktop → UnknownDesktop carrying the original text |
| Window management windowctl | `wmctrl -l` list / `-i -a <id>` / `-ic <id>` | none (non-Linux or missing wmctrl → Unsupported) | a missing command surfaces as 127 → Unsupported |
| Clipboard watch clipboard_watch | `xclip -selection clipboard -o` (read-only polling) | none | same; a read failure (not installed / no text in the selection) silently skips that tick |
| Power profile powerprofile | `powerprofilesctl list / get / set` | none | missing command → PpUnsupported; list output keeps the backend order (a recommended profile listed first stays first) |
| Printer printer | `lpstat -p / -d / -o <printer>` + `lp [-d printer] -n copies file` | none | lpstat missing (CUPS not installed) → PrtUnsupported |
| Disk volumes disk | udisks2 D-Bus (system bus) | `lsblk --json` (enumeration only; mount/unmount unavailable) | NameHasOwner or a reachable Manager call |

MPRIS (media control) is the only member of this family with an inverted route — bus first, command as backstop. Interface notes: player instances are filtered out of the session bus `org.freedesktop.DBus.ListNames` reply by the `org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.` prefix (proxy instances such as playerctld included), the object path is always `/org/mpris/MediaPlayer2`, the interface `org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.Player`; Play/Pause/PlayPause/Next/Previous/Stop are all no-argument methods with empty replies, and state is read from `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.PlaybackStatus` plus the Metadata string fields title/artist/album. **playerctl is only consulted when the bus call fails** (available when `playerctl --version` exits 0); the fallback names the instance with `-p <player>` and reads with `metadata --format <US>title<US>artist<US>album<US>` (delimited by US; a title containing the separator is split on the first segment — an accepted trade-off). Probe rule: media_supported trusts ListNames, and playerctl is only consulted when the bus is unreachable. Playback control is setting-class and is never triggered inside a probe.

#### Audio and video (FRAME → draw_image render route)

- Audio: integrates `CorvusCinereus/miniaudio@0.4.0` (a MoonBit wrapper of miniaudio; small artefacts, ABI surface = engine + clip). Link verification: inside the same prebuild.py custody scheme, after moon add the whole-repo moon build passes and coexists with the subproc/moonsqlitefile native stubs without conflict; the package itself declares no supported_targets in its moonbuild (a third-party package warning, not a problem of this project). Headless real-machine smoke (this XFCE + PipeWire host): the engine builds, `/usr/share/sounds/alsa/Front_Center.wav` loads, and volume reads/writes hold around 0.5; play/stop are setting-class and were not executed in tests.
- Video frame render route: **libyue's Image has no raw-pixel constructor** (checked against vendor/libyue/include/nativeui/gfx/image.h: the constructors are Image(NativeImage, scale_factor) / Image(FilePath) / Image(Buffer, scale_factor), and Buffer only accepts PNG/JPEG), and Canvas/Painter expose no pixel-write interface. So frames travel "frame-source callback → pngr_encode_rgba into an in-memory PNG → Image::new_from_png decode → draw_image scaled to fill". The PNG encoder is pure MoonBit (signature/IHDR/IDAT/IEND + CRC32 + Adler32 + zlib stored blocks, with the CR table and running sums in Int64 — MoonBit's `>>` on Int is an arithmetic shift while the reflection table needs a logical shift, and `>>` on a non-negative Int64 is exactly the 32-bit logical shift).
- **PTREF**: in the headless test environment (moon test), Image::new_from_png / new_from_file always return an empty image — without a GUI context (GTK not initialized) libyue's decode never succeeds; measured on this machine against real PNGs (`/usr/share/icons/hicolor/48x48/apps/*.png`), is_empty=true as well. The PNG encoder's wbtests are therefore all byte-level self-checks (magic / IHDR fields / IDAT stored block count / total length consistent / adler tail), and real-machine decode verification of Image moved to the systemprobe example.
- Video component and decoder stay decoupled: a VideoFrameSource callback (frame number → RGBA) is injected, and moonav1 (a pure-MoonBit AV1 decoder on mooncakes) is the next frame-source implementation to wire; H.264 needs ffmpeg, for which no MoonBit binding exists yet, so it waits.
- Frame advance uses @yue.set_timer (no cancel handle: the handle holds a Ref switch, and after stop the callback returns false to unregister — the same EffAnim pattern as charts_effectscatter); set_progress and the media poller follow the same shape.

#### Media status watch (MPRIS polling deltas) and notification progress (a body text bar)

- Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 + XFCE + PipeWire (pipewire-pulse). MPRIS's org.freedesktop.DBus.PropertiesChanged signal is subscribable, but subscribing needs a permanent read loop, which does not fit this library's model of "synchronous request-reply socket transactions + set_timer" (the generic D-Bus layer gdbus_call is a round trip with no async reader thread). So media_watch_status polls deltas: it reads PlaybackStatus + Metadata every 1000ms by default and fires on_change when play state / title / artist / album changes; the first round only establishes a baseline; rounds that fail to query (bus error / playerctld gone) are silently skipped without affecting later rounds.
- Target resolution: with an empty player argument, each round retries resolving the first player instance (skipping the round when media_players fails) and locks on once an instance appears; switching players while playing does not follow automatically, which the usage doc states.
- Stop semantics: set_timer has no cancel handle (a callback can only return false), so the handle holds a Ref[Bool] and media_watch_stop sets false, unregistering on the next frame with no recovery — the same EffAnim pattern as charts_effectscatter. Accepted trade-off: an exception thrown by on_change kills that timer (no try/catch, which is MoonBit's unused_try trade-off) — documented.
- Real-machine smoke: this host has no MPRIS player, so the watch was started and stopped immediately: on_change fired 0 times and nothing raised (the smoke case in media_wbtest.mbt; 12/12 pass).
- Notification progress: the freedesktop notification protocol has no progress field (Windows / macOS present progress differently again), so the cross-platform-consistent answer is a character bar in the body plus a percentage. notification_progress_text clamps percent to [0,100], treats NaN as 0 via `percent != percent`, prints only the percentage when width<=0, and rounds the cell count (add 0.5 then to_int); Notification::set_progress composes body = original text + newline + progress line.

#### Firefox places.sqlite (read-only, no WAL merge)

- places.sqlite is usually in WAL mode: the newest visits are still in places.sqlite-wal / -shm while the main file is an older snapshot. The current implementation hands only the main database bytes to moonsqlitefile's `open_database`, **so there is no WAL merge and records checkpointed into the main file are unreadable** — a known boundary the doc must state: "readings are a snapshot of the main file as of the moment it was read". The missing piece (not done): moonsqlitefile also offers `open_wal_database`, which needs the -wal file handed to the same Database.
- Tables and columns: `moz_places` is the only table needed, taking `url` (TEXT; keyed by id but row parsing does not depend on it), `title` (TEXT, may be NULL), `last_visit_date` (INTEGER, **Unix-epoch microseconds** — not the same base as Chrome's 1601 microseconds, so ffx_time_to_unix_us converts to ms as us/1000) and `hidden` (INTEGER; nonzero rows are bookmarks/starred entries and must be filtered, same rule as Chrome).
- Row parsing reads by column position but **makes no type assumptions**: url may be a Blob (SQLite's dynamic typing means title/url can both be stored as BLOB), so every BhValue branch needs a fallback (ffx_parse_places_row returns None for a non-text value and skips the row).
- Profile location: `~/.mozilla/firefox/profiles.ini` supplies the `Path=` directory names (both [Install*] and [Profile*] sections can carry Path, so collect all of them), falling back to fixed candidate names when it is missing (default / default-release / default-esr / default-nightly / dev-edition-default) — **profile directories with a random prefix (e.g. `a1b2c3d4.default-release`) are only reachable through profiles.ini**, a hard boundary while this package has no directory enumeration (fsx_list_dir landing would close it by scanning).
- The entry type reuses browser_history's `HistoryItem` (its fields match Chrome history exactly), and ordering / truncation / column extraction reuse bh_sort_history / bh_take / bh_value_text / bh_value_int rather than duplicating a second set.
- Multi-profile aggregation follows the Chrome rule: the same url in different profiles appears once per profile, undeduplicated — deduplication would hide the fact that two accounts sit in two profiles.

### System information (si_machine / memory / uptime) and system-level security boundaries

- /sys/class/dmi/id/product_serial is root-readable on most distributions; when it cannot be read return `Err` with the path rather than papering over with an empty string; /proc/meminfo units are always kB, MemAvailable exists only on kernels ≥3.14 and falls back to MemFree; uptime is a float of seconds and is returned directly.
- Sensor reads (iio-sensor-proxy) must be wrapped in ClaimLight/ReleaseLight, because an unclaimed sensor keeps reporting stale values; AccelerometerOrientation is a string, not an enum integer.

### Display protocols

- X11 ✅ mainline; Wayland unsupported — verify GUI behavior in an X11 session (tray / shortcuts are session-guarded).
- User idle seconds come from the X Screen Saver Extension (XSS) XScreenSaverQueryInfo, dlopen'd at runtime ("libXss.so.1"/"libXss.so") instead of build-time linking: keeps libxss-dev out of the distribution chain (prebuilt static libs ship via mooncakes; an extra dynamic dependency may be absent on consumer machines). XScreenSaverInfo is minimal — the shim hand-mirrors the struct (idle-milliseconds field at offset 24); a failed load takes the same path as "no X" and returns Unsupported.
- In an XWayland session input events never reach the X server, so the XSS idle reads absurdly high (hours right after user activity): an explicit WAYLAND_DISPLAY probe returns Unsupported — better no number than a wrong one; env -u DISPLAY (no X session) is likewise Unsupported; neither crashes. Measured cross-check (Ubuntu 24.04 XFCE X11): idle_seconds vs xprintidle same-instant double read differs by 17ms (acceptance check ±2s); after an xdotool-simulated mouse move, 0.317s vs xprintidle 320ms.
- Screen locking does not count as input: the XSS idle keeps growing while the screen is locked (lockers report no input). "User idle" and "screen locked" are orthogonal dimensions — do not approximate lock detection with an idle threshold (lock events come from logind, landing in a later batch).
- Idle-reading demo interaction: a click is itself an input event and resets the XSS idle counter — a "click the button to read the current idle" demo contradicts itself (it always reads 0.x seconds; command-line probes and xdotool-based external reads never exposed this). The correct shape is a switch that starts a periodic refresh (one read per second), with the timer stopping itself on the next tick once the switch turns off (libyue timers have no cancel id — the callback checks the switch state and suicides).

### GTK specifics

- A Table inside a Notebook tab segfaults during size measurement (negative allocation): keep it in a plain container or a standalone window.
- Content widgets (Group / Scroll) extend View, not Container: attach content via `SetContentView`; `AddChild` is rejected by the type check.
- Upstream NUContainer defects (patch `patch_linux_container_events`): ① the event window raises on map, stealing hits from native child widgets (tabs unclickable, wheel dead) → `gdk_window_show_unraised`; ② container preferred sizes hardcode 0 and Scroll's size_request is 0×0 → width follows the viewport, height resolves to the content's natural yoga height. Do not report yoga's dynamic natural size to GTK: allocation pollutes yoga state and requisition negotiation oscillates without converging.
- The visibility guard at the top of `UpdateChildBounds` misses GTK's first size-allocate (it happens before map): layout must run unconditionally.
- `Slider::SetValue` sets the ignore flag even for identical values, swallowing the user's first callback: set it only when the value actually changes.
- `ProgressBar::SetValue` means 0..100 on both Linux and Windows; the yue layer is unified on 0..1, so the conversion branch must cover both platforms.
- `View::GetBoundsInScreen` stacks coordinates wrongly under Scroll / nested containers (patch `patch_linux_view_bounds_in_screen`): GTK screen coordinates must be "client-area origin (`gdk_window_get_origin`) + offset within the client area (`gtk_widget_translate_coordinates`)"; `gtk_window_get_position` includes the title-bar decoration — mixing it with translate is off by exactly one decoration size.
- Table checkbox-column indicators scale with row height (XFCE theme): set `indicator-size=16` explicitly on checkbox columns and cap the renderer height at 20.
- Drag-out data must use the `Data(std::vector<base::FilePath>)` constructor (the string constructor silently degrades to Text); absolutize relative paths first (`g_filename_to_uri` rejects relative paths).
- The drag preview hotspot is hardcoded to (0,0) upstream; the patch centers the image on the cursor (`patch_linux_drag_icon_hotspot`).
- Whether a drop is accepted is decided by drag-motion (`handle_drag_update`); `handle_drag_enter` is only an entry notice. Register the Image data type too — dragging in from image viewers / browsers yields image content, not file paths.
- libyue's `Entry::SetText` swallows `on_text_change`: the GTK side guards with an `is-editing` object-data flag that filters the `changed` signal during programmatic sets (loop prevention), so the visible text changes but consumers get no callback — `input_t`'s clear ✕ therefore "cleared the text but never refreshed the filtered list". Fix: the clear handler explicitly invokes `on_input("")` once. Any path that programmatically changes Entry / TextEdit text and then relies on the callback must invoke it manually.
- Drag-out initiation: calling `gtk_drag_begin` synchronously desyncs GTK's drag state machine (nested gtk_main never exits, drag works once), so it must be deferred until the event queue drains, initiated with the press event, and the drag_context backfilled; drag-failed needs a defensive cleanup (fork mbt.12).
- Creating a Browser page (WebKitGTK) aborts the process immediately: `Could not create GBM EGL display: EGL_NOT_INITIALIZED. Aborting...` — WebKitGTK 2.5x's DRMDeviceManager initializes the main DRM device when a WebView is created and RELEASE_ASSERTs to death when the GBM EGL display cannot be obtained. On the NVIDIA proprietary driver without `libnvidia-egl-gbm`, GLVND only has the X11 backend (`10_nvidia.json` has no GBM), so neither card1 nor renderD128 yields a display (measured: `eglGetPlatformDisplay(GBM)` returns NULL; note that in-process probe results don't match WebKit's actual path — an in-process probe on renderD128 initialized successfully while WebKit still aborted, so don't gate on probe results). showcase mounts a Browser page on its first screen, so it always crashed. Library-side fix: the shim's app_init (Linux) sets `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1` (overwrite=0, an explicit user setting wins), pushing WebKit onto the legacy rendering path — no more crash, full Browser functionality (only web content loses one layer of GPU acceleration; the cairo self-drawn UI is untouched). Verified: bare `moon run examples/showcase` opens its window, stays alive, zero aborts. Root fix at the system level: install `libnvidia-egl-gbm` (NVIDIA's GBM EGL backend), after which `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=0` restores hardware rendering. Engineering note: after changing the shim, moon does not necessarily relink (the exe isn't in its dependency graph) — run `moon clean` or delete the exe to force a relink and confirm with `nm exe | grep <new symbol>`.
- **Follow-up (measured 2026-10-14, answering "is the Linux webview integrated at all?")**: ① it is — this machine has `pkg-config --modversion webkit2gtk-4.1 = 2.52.6`, prebuild compiles the **real** branch (`nm gui/build/libyue_web.a` shows 46 undefined `webkit_*` references, impossible for the stub branch), and 2026-10-12 left a set of real-hardware readings (Chinese text correct on protocol pages, back-navigation genuinely returns, in-page scrolling and link clicks work, the IME yields while the webview has focus and comes back afterwards). ② The protection above, however, **did not make it into the new stack**: `grep WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER` across the repo returns nothing (it lived in the deleted shim's `app_init`). ③ It does **not** reproduce on the current machine: the driver now ships a GBM backend (`/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gbm/nvidia-drm_gbm.so` present, RTX 3070), and a C probe that creates no window — with the variable unset — survived `webkit_web_view_new()` plus `load_uri("about:blank")` plus about two seconds of main-loop iterations (`PROBE ALIVE`, exit 0), so the `setenv` was deliberately **not** re-added (it would only cost web content its GPU compositing). ④ Acceptance check left for whoever comes next: after a machine or driver-stack change, if the browser page dies "at creation" again, this lost protection is the first suspect, and reproducing it **needs no GUI** — construct a WebView in a console process without mapping a window. The system-level fix remains installing `libnvidia-egl-gbm`.
- The overlay-scrollbar default needs a process-environment guard: the `GTK_OVERLAY_SCROLLING` environment variable outranks gsettings inside GtkSettings (distro scripts / users exporting `=0` to force classic scrollbars is a common practice), and GTK re-reads the process environment every time a ScrolledWindow is created — writing the `gtk-overlay-scrolling` GtkSettings property during theme init alone cannot beat the env-var path. app_init (Linux) calls `setenv("GTK_OVERLAY_SCROLLING","1",1)` before gtk_init (overwrite=1: the library default and `set_overlay_scrollbar(true)` win over the global preference; a caller turning a single scroll area off explicitly still goes through the per-widget API), so machines running such scripts are immune; the later GtkSettings write stays as a fallback.
- **Scroll range stays at the skeleton height after lazy mounting (the second root cause of unscrollable pages, proven by a probe bisection matrix)**: on GTK the ScrolledWindow's scroll range does not come from content measurement — nativeui's nu_container always reports GTK preferred 0 (it never uses the GTK layout system), so the viewport's adjustment upper depends entirely on a one-time snapshot of the content's natural height taken **at set_content time** by the fork's `Scroll::PlatformSetContentView` (written as a size request); worse, re-setting the same content makes that function read the old snapshot (not -1) and skip the recompute, and remove-then-add writes the stale value back. Whenever content arrives after set_content (lazy mounting) or grows noticeably, the scroll range stays frozen at the skeleton height — "the content is clearly taller yet nothing scrolls and the wheel is silent". All 111 showcase sections are lazily mounted, and the long icon-wall section (9 rows) exposed it first, though the defect is page-wide. Four-column probe bisection settled it: always-mounted text/icon walls max=428/518 (scrollable), lazily attached walls max=0 (the holder measured 1120/1210 and GetPreferredSize 1164/1254, both correct) — independent of content type, purely mount timing; re-running set_content does nothing (the old snapshot short-circuits) while an explicit set_content_size with a large value takes effect immediately (the adjustment chain is sound; the frozen size-request snapshot is what fails). Fix: the shim gains `yue_mbt_scroll_refresh_content_size` (on Linux it writes `gtk_widget_set_size_request(width unchanged, height = Container::GetPreferredSize(), i.e. yoga run on the spot)`; a no-op on win/mac — Windows' ScrollImpl::Layout already re-queries the content's natural size each round and macOS derives the range from the documentView frame, so neither has a snapshot problem), plus `Scroll::refresh_content_size()` in the yue layer; mount sites call it once mounting completes (showcase's section_body is wired). End-to-end probe: after page switch / section switch / a second show-hide round / switching back, max_y recovers exactly to content height − viewport (598=1290−692) and stays correct when the viewport changes. This complements the "cross-axis scroll-range bug" (a read-side defect): this one is the write side, and both fixes live in the shim. Regression tool: `moon run examples/probe-iconscroll` (four-timing end-to-end sampling; a long section's max_y must stay >0). The same snapshot mechanism also bites **non-lazy** cases: `set_text` growing content after mount (systemprobe's system-capability report, dozens of text lines) and `mount_into` attaching a new subtree after mount (the video player mounted into a placeholder container) leave the scroll range unupdated as well — "after the result loads the bottom is clipped and nothing scrolls, after the player mounts you cannot scroll to the end". The mounting side calling `refresh_content_size()` after the change restores it; systemprobe's multi-page refactor injects the refresh closure into the page-body builder and wires report set_text, player mounting and command-preview text (measured 2026-10).
- **A report label does not grow after set_text (clipping — the second half beyond the scroll-range snapshot, 2026-10 user real-machine report + probe control proven)**: on systemprobe's system-capabilities page, clicking "读取系统能力" showed only the first 1-2 lines of a dozens-of-lines report (user screenshot: the volume section kept only its sink line; "音量: 45% 静音: 否" and everything after was invisible). Root cause: a GTK label's (nu_label) yoga height is measured once at mount (from the placeholder text); `Label::SetText` only changes the pango text and does not mark yoga dirty — the new text is clipped to the old height. `refresh_content_size()` only writes the container's **existing** preferred height to the GTK viewport, so it cannot save the label's own height (it fixes the scroll range, the first half above). Probe control (same page-shell structure: scroll → vbox → long-placeholder label): set_text + refresh alone rendered only line 1 of a 16-line report; adding `set_visible(false)` → `set_visible(true)` before refresh rendered all 16 lines. The toggle works because the shim's `yue_mbt_view_set_visible` performs a root-level `Layout()` recalculation (same code on all three platforms, no platform branches), forcing yoga to re-measure the label; both calls happen within one tick, so there is no visible flicker. Fix: systemprobe's shared layer gains `report_set(label, text, refresh)` (set_text + visibility toggle + refresh), and every report write site on the system-capabilities / command-preview / video pages routes through it. Verification: real-machine click on "读取系统能力" rendered the full report (volume 45% / brightness / browser history / downloads / VS Code / binary lookup — six sections), 62979 differing pixels before and after the click; `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test` 657 all green. Lesson: **a GTK label's "growing" and its "scroll range" are two separate things — the former needs a visibility toggle (or an equivalent relayout) to force a yoga re-measure, the latter is what refresh_content_size is for**; the toggle cures half, and the other half once content exceeds the viewport is the next entry.
- **All three paths to a GTK label's natural height are untrustworthy (deepening the "visibility toggle fixes it" entry above; only exposed when dynamic content exceeds the viewport, 2026-10 user feedback + probe + D-Bus double corroboration)**: the earlier fix (visibility toggle forcing a yoga re-measure) cured only half — while the content fits the viewport (a 16-line report < viewport) everything looks fine, but once it exceeds the viewport nothing scrolls and the label is still clipped (40 lines rendered 19), which the user reported as "the report updated and refresh ran, yet there is no scrollbar". Three layers of root cause: ① a GTK label's natural height is measured by yoga's `MeasureLabel` → `AttributedText::GetBoundsFor`, whose `pango_layout_set_height(text_, size.height() * PANGO_SCALE)` **does not guard NaN** — when yoga passes an undefined height (GetPreferredSize's NaN measurement), NaN→int yields garbage and pango measures the whole layout as **one line** (a temporary shim print measured preferred_h=92, i.e. button plus one placeholder line); ② the viewport's definite height (382) flows down holder→vbox and MeasureLabel's AT_MOST mode truncates the text to 341 (40 lines allocated 19) — the content can never exceed the viewport; ③ `refresh_content_size` writes ①'s wrong value (92) into the viewport, the adjustment upper never moves and `get_max_scroll_position_y` stays 0. Mechanism corroboration: in the same probe, `set_content_size(600,1000)` gave `max=618` (=1000−382) on the next tick, proving the adjustment chain itself works and the value refresh writes is the culprit. Fix (pure MoonBit side, no shim/fork changes): yue gains `measure_text_height(text, role?, width?)` (an AttributedText probe in the role's font measured at a large width and height, avoiding both the NaN and AT_MOST traps); `report_set` becomes set_text → measure natural height → `set_style(label, "height", h+2)` **explicit height** → visibility toggle (root relayout) → refresh. With an explicit height yoga never calls the measure function, so both traps are avoided at once. Verification: probe (same page-shell structure, 40-line report) before the fix label_h=341/max=0; after, label_h=699 (full text height), body_h=773, **max=391 (=773−382)**, five wheel clicks give pos=263, and a screenshot confirms all 40 lines render and scroll correctly. Boundary: the explicit height is not recomputed on window resize (width changes → wrapping changes → stale height); acceptable for a demo page, and a later on_size_changed hook could re-set it. Lesson: **all three paths to a GTK label's natural height are untrustworthy — a yoga re-measure gives one line for an undefined height and a truncated value for the viewport's definite height, and mounting measures the placeholder text; dynamically growing text must always go "measure with an AttributedText in the same font + set an explicit height", never leaving the natural height to any automatic path**.
- **Cross-axis scroll-range bug (the root cause of unscrollable pages, verified bit-for-bit with probes)**: the fork's Linux ScrollImpl::GetMaximumScrollPosition uses the **viewport width** as the vertical page_size — measured `max_y = content natural height − viewport width` (window 900×600: pure drawn-rows content 1064 → maxy 164, charts+rows 1088 → 188, pure labels 1160 → 260, all exact hits), with the horizontal axis wrong symmetrically. Consequences: programmatic scroll range collapses to a fraction of the real one, and the floating thumb never appears (the library hides it at maxy ≤ 0.5). **Initially-visible and shown-after-hidden are equally wrong** (briefly misdiagnosed as a hidden-mount measurement issue, disproved by an always-visible control group reading the same value; the queue_resize/update_layout remeasure attempts had no effect — GTK's measurement was correct all along, nativeui's reading is what is wrong). Fix: on Linux the shim's `yue_mbt_scroll_get_max_position_x/y` now reads `upper − page_size` straight from `gtk_scrolled_window_get_h/vadjustment` (other platforms still pass through to nativeui); after the fix 1160−600=560 is exact, and sysmonitor's right pane scrolls by wheel (5871 differing pixels before and after).
- A hover group's (hover_group) verdict cannot rely on container enter/leave: GTK pointer events do not bubble — they are delivered to the deepest hit GdkWindow and end there — and child containers' (NUContainer) / native widgets' (Entry etc.) event windows **monopolize** pointer events, so ancestor containers never see enter (sysmonitor's cards receive enter only because their children are window-less labels; once a child is a container or a native widget the stream breaks). True "event pass-through" would need either upstream fork changes (each view broadcasting events up the ancestor chain) or platform-wide hooks (XI2/WH_MOUSE) — both invasive and costly to maintain, so not taken. The workable mechanism is pointer-position polling: **all groups share one global 100ms timer (a set_timeout chain that stops entirely when no groups exist), one pointer query plus one screen-rectangle compare per group per tick, all microsecond-level**; cursor_screen_x/y and get_bounds_in_screen share screen-root coordinates and agree under multi-monitor tiling including negatives (verified bit-for-bit with a probe). enter serves only as a hit accelerator; leaving is entirely the poll's job. A visible background must be self-drawn in on_draw (set_background_color and the backgroundColor style are both unreliable for draw-less containers — theme CSS and child widget windows suppress them; paint the hover/idle backgrounds directly in the group container's draw, and transparent child regions show through naturally). Measured: hovering a child widget (an input) turns the whole card to fill_hover (239,241,243) exactly, and leaving restores it.
- The self-drawn floating scrollbar (overlay_scroll) was first demoted to an explicitly opted-in component because of the cross-axis bug, then picked back up for Windows after real-machine acceptance: it was once the declarative `scroll()` default form (to unify the look across platforms against Windows' classic bars), but the thumb depends on the maxy/on_size_changed chain and turned unstable once the cross-axis bug stacked on top, so it fell back to the platform's native scrollbars; after the cross-axis fix the Windows form was restored on its own after real-machine acceptance — on Windows `scroll()` with overlay=true and no explicit policy wraps a host container and routes through attach_overlay_thumb, while non-Windows and explicit-policy paths keep the native bar (overlay=true requests the overlay style: guaranteed by the environment variable on Linux, with no overlay counterpart on Windows); the overlay_scroll component and Windows page-level scrolling share this path.
- Reading the system accent color (GTK3 has no accent API; `yue_mbt_system_accent` steps through three): ① GNOME 47+'s GSettings `org.gnome.desktop.interface`/`accent-color` — when the schema exists but the key does not (e.g. Ubuntu 24.04's gsettings-desktop-schemas), `g_settings_get_string` aborts instead of returning empty, so probe with `g_settings_schema_has_key` first (abort reproduced with a probe on this machine); ② `@define-color theme_selected_bg_color` in the current theme's CSS: GTK themes express their primary colour as the selection background, searched in `~/.themes` → `$XDG_DATA_HOME/themes` → `$XDG_DATA_DIRS/themes` → `/usr/share/themes` under `gtk-3.0/{gtk,gtk-contained,gtk-dark}.css`, with the dark preference deciding which file is parsed first (Orchis themes define the light accent in gtk.css and the dark variant in gtk-dark.css); ③ empty when neither hits. Verified with a probe (Ubuntu 24.04 + XFCE + Orchis-Teal-Light-Compact): returns `#009688`, matching the theme CSS bit for bit; XFCE has no accent setting, so step ② is what captures the theme's primary colour.
- Container-level hover highlighting (switching the background in on_mouse_enter/leave) must flicker whenever a child widget is involved: GTK dispatches enter/leave by **native window boundary**, so entering a child window counts as leaving the parent window; libyue compensates (responder_gtk.cc `OnMouseEvent`: leave is deferred one tick and a child's enter cancels the pending one, GTK only) but has two holes — ① when a child widget has no mouse handler attached at all, `PlatformInstallMouseMoveEvents` never runs, so there is no enter mask and no enter can ever be emitted to cancel the pending leave, which then fires as scheduled (label and icon bands inside a card); ② an empty container (a self-drawn sparkline canvas, for instance) does not satisfy "defer leave only for Containers with children", so the parent leave triggers immediately. Measured on sysmonitor's left resource cards: every time the pointer crosses a child widget inside a card, the hover background goes out once. Workaround: a self-drawn container's hover feedback should use cursor (hand pointer) plus a persistent selected state (outline / light background) and not depend on enter/leave; if a hover-style effect is genuinely required, draw the whole card as a single self-drawn canvas (as table rows do) or change the library's event dispatch. Related: hover cursors also apply per native window, so setting one on a container does not cover children with their own windows (hbox rows / self-drawn canvases) — set it on each child (NUSetCursor is a safe no-op for window-less widgets; one nu::Cursor can be shared by many views through scoped_refptr, so reuse a single instance). Pass-through generalised: the `cursor_group` component shares hover_group's global poll tick — while the pointer is inside the group bounds, the shim's `yue_mbt_view_set_cursor_deep` recursively SetCursors the group root and all its descendants, and leaving restores Default; what gets restored is the default cursor, not each child's original one (the library offers no read-back, so do not wrap a group whose children must keep their own cursors).
- Changing layout styles at run time triggers no relayout (the root cause of an unmovable splitter, characterised across 8 probe scenarios): on GTK, after mounting, changing **any** layout property through `SetStyleProperty` (`width` / `flexbasis` measured) never lands — a root `update_layout` call, a leaf call, a bare set_style and natural layout cycles (bounds read 600ms later) are all ineffective; style values present at initial mount do apply (the first full size-allocate chain reads them). On Windows, run-time flexbasis does work (verified with the 5f272b4 synthetic drag), so this is a platform difference and cross-platform components must not assume styles are writable at run time. Found along the way: inside a Scroll even the initial flexbasis does not land (the first pane drops to minwidth) while width is fine. Fix: the shim adds `yue_mbt_view_set_bounds` (a straight pass-through to `View::SetBounds`) plus a generic `set_view_bounds` on the MoonBit side; splitter dragging and the initial ratio now "write the three geometries directly with set_bounds + write the first pane's width/height styles as well" — the direct write takes effect immediately and the style values let a later full-chain relayout on window resize take over from the last width. Verification: the examples/probe-splitter probe (kept in the repo) compares two phases — the style path fails in all 8 scenarios, set_bounds succeeds in all 6 exactly (direct / inside a Scroll × two sizes); 131 tests pass, showcase smoke survives, and drag feel was re-verified on the real machine. Method: a mechanism probe that changes parameters step by step from a timer and dumps bounds on alternating ticks characterises the layout chain with no simulated mouse needed.
- **On Linux, Label is the self-drawn widget NULabel, so no GtkLabel `selectable` channel exists**: libyue's Label is a custom GtkWidget on GTK (nativeui/gtk/nu_label.cc — cairo self-drawn text, preferred size hardcoded to 0, no built-in text selection/copy), so `gtk_label_set_selectable(GTK_LABEL(GetNative()))` hits the wrong object and is silently ignored (gtk_label_get_selectable always reads back 0, proven with a runtime probe). Selectable text must come from a self-drawn component (hit calculation + selection highlight + Ctrl+C into the clipboard), not from a native channel. A set_selectable API was once added on the assumption that GetNative returns a GtkWidget; after verification failed the whole change was withdrawn, and experiment/input_probe stays in the repo as the chain probe.
- **Two defects in the Linux on_wheel hookup (fixed in 0.5.10): a bad downcast between the sibling classes Window/View, and GtkWidget's missing wheel mask by default**: yue_mbt_view_on_wheel used CastToView(view) — Window derives from Responder, not View, so the static_cast misaligned the object and View::GetNative() read a member at the wrong offset; g_signal_connect then received a garbage instance, GLib reported "instance of invalid non-instantiatable type" and the signal was never attached (two visible CRITICAL lines at run time are exactly this). Separately, GtkWidget/GtkWindow do not include GDK_SCROLL_MASK by default, so without an explicit gtk_widget_add_events the scroll-event is never delivered. Fix: dispatch by GetClassName (Window uses Window::GetNative, everything else takes `dynamic_cast<View*>`'s GetNative) and always add GDK_SCROLL_MASK|GDK_SMOOTH_SCROLL_MASK (NUContainer's event-window mask goes through nu_container_add_event_mask, which unions). Related lesson: **in the shim, any view-level interface that needs GetNative() must not route a Window argument through CastToView** (Responder-level Signal Connect happens to be safe because both Responder classes share a header layout, but that must not be relied on).
- **NUContainer (a self-drawn container) receives no mouse events when it hosts wgpu rendering; Window-level signals are reliable (settled by a staged probe)**: after presenting a wgpu surface into a Container's GdkWindow (even merely creating the surface without rendering), that container's on_mouse_down/move/wheel all go silent; staged experiments (render/surface/one-frame modes) cross-located against no-wgpu and Window-level controls — X-layer events are intact (Window's on_mouse_down still fires), the break sits in NUContainer's input-only event-window hit/forward layer, and the same symptom appears on an empty container without wgpu for synthesized clicks (reproduced with XTEST; native-widget clicks in real-hardware hello-themed are unaffected, because a native Button owns its own GdkWindow). **Workaround: in render-host scenarios, attach all mouse interaction to Window-level signals** (the client-area coordinate system is the same, so coordinates are equivalent when the container fills the window); for the wheel, attach both window and host (window-level wheel was not observed for XTEST-synthesized events and real-machine behavior is unverified — attaching both lets whichever works count, and they never both fire). Diagnostic tool: three-native examples/input_diag (staged modes via INPUT_DIAG_MODE=render/surface/frame). The root cause (NUContainer's event window interacting with the wgpu surface) is still to be dug out and sits on the fork's investigation list.
- **Segmentation fault on an explicit quit() (root-cause chain nailed with gdb; fixed by disconnecting all signals before quit)**: when the program calls quit() itself (menu exit / a callback path, with no delete-event), the windows and widgets are held by the shim's handle registry ViewStore and only die during the exit static-destruction phase; ~Window then makes GTK dispatch focus-out synchronously, which travels OnFocusOut → MoonBit trampoline → schedule_paint → `Store<Responder>::get` and hits the unordered_map mid-destruction → SIGSEGV (about 1 in 20 runs when a focusable button_t is in the window; pure labels never trigger it, and it does not reproduce under gdb because it is timing-sensitive). Fix: shim `yue_mbt_quit` walks ViewStore before MessageLoop::Quit and disconnects every application-layer signal on every view (7 Responder-level + 4 View-level + the Window's on_focus/on_blur; on_close is deliberately left alone because quit usually runs inside its callback chain and Emit already holds a slot copy, so leaving it is safe); during exit, signal Emits do nothing. Implementation note: Window derives from Responder rather than View (sibling classes), so branch on GetClassName and static_cast each on its own — converting View* straight to Window* is refused at compile time. Verification: explicit-quit probe ×50 with zero faults (before: 1 in 20 segfaults), no-focus probe ×30 clean, window-close path (wmctrl -ic) ×12 all rc=0, 135 tests pass; the reproducer and probes stay in experiment/exit_crash/. The root fix (an is_quitting flag short-circuiting OnFocusOut in the fork) is listed as an optional follow-up vendor batch.
- **Growth after a run-time set_text is truncated (label width never follows the text, settled by probe bounds measurements)**: bind / bind_label and any "subscribe to a signal then `Label::set_text`" path clip as soon as the text gets longer than at mount — the length exceeds the allocation width captured at mount, and GTK clips drawing to the widget's allocation; only a later real window resize recovers it. Three layers of root cause: ① libyue's `Label::SetText` only does `YGNodeMarkDirty` + `queue_draw` (a pure repaint, no layout); ② even when someone calls `Layout()` (a full yoga recompute whose new deep-node values are computed), **delivery** of the bounds depends on each container's `UpdateChildBounds`, and the root only SetBounds its direct children; ③ GTK short-circuits a `size_allocate` for an unchanged allocation — intermediate containers whose own size did not change (an hbox, say) do not propagate, so a label deeper in that subtree whose measure changed never receives a new width. libyue's `Container::Layout()` non-root branch already has a "if the parent did not deliver, do it yourself" self-heal (walking the dirty chain calling UpdateChildBounds level by level), but its upward propagation stops at a non-Container parent (a Scroll), and the shim's `yue_mbt_view_layout` walked to the root and called `root->Layout()` itself, which bypassed exactly that self-heal. Fix (shim): extract `layout_root_down` — after `Layout()` on the root, force `UpdateChildBounds()` on every Container along the **root → start-point** path (idempotent delivery; the visibility guard on non-Linux platforms stays as is), and `yue_mbt_view_refresh` switches to it too. **The order must be outside → in**: a Scroll's content container is an independent yoga root (not hung on the big tree; `IsRootYGNode` decides by "no YG parent"), and only its `UpdateChildBounds` triggers the local recompute; delivering inside → out means the inner level runs first with pre-recompute values and the new measured width still never reaches the target — under showcase's in-section scroll architecture (every page lives inside a Scroll), the first fix (inside → out) still lagged one round in the probe, and flipping the order made it synchronous. Fix (MoonBit): the three `set_text` sites in `bind_label`'s subscription callback, stat_card's number (num) and form_item's validation text (err) now call `update_layout`. Verification: the examples/probe-bind probe (kept in the repo, including the Scroll-wrapped shape) alternates short/long text on a timer and dumps bounds each round — before the fix the long text stayed at 25px (always clipped) and lagged one round; after, both inside and outside a Scroll give 243 long / 25 short immediately; 65 tests pass and showcase smoke survives. Observation lessons: ① GTK's size_allocate is asynchronous to the current callback, so a synchronous print always reads the previous frame's allocation — never conclude from same-frame values; ② after a shim change moon does not necessarily relink an existing exe (the `.a` is not in its dependency graph), so delete the exe to force a relink; the first day's fix therefore "looked ineffective" on showcase when it was simply the old exe.

## Windows 10 / 11 ✅

First full local-chain verification environment: Windows 10 19045 + VS BuildTools 2022 (v17.14) + SDK 10.0.26100 — prepare.py build → moon check / test / build → hello launch smoke all pass (previously Windows had CI-only verification; some branches had never been compiled against a real Windows SDK).

### Toolchain

- Requires VS Build Tools (VCTools workload + the ATL component for `base/win/atl_throw.h`); run moon / cmake from an x64 Native Tools Command Prompt or after vcvars64. Installer quiet / passive mode requires elevation, else Exit 5007.
- Release asset names are `libyue_{v}_win.zip` / `_mac.zip` (not windows / darwin).
- On case-sensitive volumes compilation fails with C1083 on `webview2.h`: the SDK ships only `WebView2.h` (capital W); prepare.py adds a lowercase alias after extraction. On the same volume `shutil.copyfile`'s samefile check is unreliable — delete the destination before copying.
- Platform-specific code must guard its includes and implementations in the same batch: a bare `gtk/gtk.h`, or a function guarded at the call site but not at the definition, explodes on the other platform's compiler with C1083 / C2065.
- The power/session message code (B6) hit three SDK facts on its first real-machine compile: the `PBT_APMRESUME` macro does not exist (resume only ever sends the unconditional `PBT_APMRESUMEAUTOMATIC`, plus `PBT_APMRESUMESUSPEND` afterwards only for user-input resumes — the latter is a subset of the former, and matching both fires the callback twice per wake); SDK 10.0.26100 has folded the `PBT_*` constants into winuser.h and there is no standalone `pbt.h` at all — explicitly including it fails with C1083; `WTSRegisterSessionNotification` / `NOTIFY_FOR_THIS_SESSION` are declared in `wtsapi32.h` while the `WTS_SESSION_LOCK` message codes live in winuser.h — a missing include therefore reports only the functions as undeclared while the message codes compile fine, which misleads you into thinking the headers are okay.
- shim platform differences: guard `dlfcn.h` with `__linux__`; MSVC needs `_USE_MATH_DEFINES` for `M_PI`; `base::FilePath` is `std::wstring` under UNICODE builds — go through `FromUTF8Unsafe / AsUTF8Unsafe`; Windows has no Popover and no `SetOverlayScrollbar` / `Clipboard::Selection` / `Tray::SetTitle` etc., all degraded to no-ops in the shim; `operator new/delete` redirect to `malloc/free` (moon builds its runtime with MOONBIT_ALLOCATOR=SYSTEM); a widget's HWND comes from `dynamic_cast<nu::SubwinView*>(GetNative())->hwnd()` — `GetNative()` itself is not an HWND.
- Native child HWNDs do not follow the container after scrolling (they float over scrolled content): force `View::Layout()`, and the scroll wrapper registers on_scroll with the callback deferred via a 0ms timer until layout completes; an input's inner shadow is `WS_EX_CLIENTEDGE`, so borderless must clear STATICEDGE / CLIENTEDGE / WS_BORDER; DatePicker shows only the year unless given an explicit width; glyph-based small icons are inconsistent across platforms — draw them with Painter vectors inside components.

### Link flags (moon → cl / link)

- `cc-link-flags` is spliced verbatim into the cl command line; GNU-style `-L/-l` triggers D9002. The correct form is link inputs (`build/yue_mbt.lib setupapi.lib …`): cl forwards .lib position arguments to link, and system libraries resolve via the LIB environment variable.
- Path separators must be forward slashes: backslashes are eaten by moon's argument parsing and link fails with LNK1104.
- The official CMakeLists system-library list is incomplete; copying it verbatim yields 144+ LNK2019. The prepare.py list is complete.
- The CRT must match moon's static /MT: CMake multi-config generators ignore `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE`, so `cmake --build` must pass `--config Release` (prepare.py automates this), else LNK4098 plus unresolved `__imp__*`.
- **The console window on exes is gone via an in-library link mechanism (current stack, measured 2026-10-12 on Windows)**: `gui/win/win_gui.c` carries `#pragma comment(linker, "/SUBSYSTEM:WINDOWS")` plus `/ENTRY:mainCRTStartup` under `#if defined(_WIN32) && defined(_MSC_VER)`, and sits in `gui/win/moon.pkg`'s `native-stub` list next to `stub.c`. The pragma lands in the object's `.drectve` section; moon compiles native-stub C sources straight into the exe build (the cl command line lists `win_gui.c`), but the linker only honours `.drectve` of archive members it actually extracts — so the file also exports `wm_win_gui_marker`, referenced by `win/window.mbt`'s `init_backend()` as `ignore(wm_win_gui_marker())`. That reference is the extraction anchor, and `core/app.mbt`'s app path calls `init_backend()`, so consumers get GUI(2) with zero configuration. `/ENTRY:mainCRTStartup` is not optional: switching the subsystem makes `WinMainCRTStartup` the default entry point while moon emits a console-style `main()`, so without it the link fails on an unresolved `WinMain`. Appending the flags instead cannot work — user `link_flags` are spliced before `/link`, so cl discards `/SUBSYSTEM`-class link options outright (D9002). `release-bin.yml` therefore **verifies** rather than rewrites: the step fails the build unless every release exe's OptionalHeader.Subsystem is 2. Evidence: `moon build examples/{hello,hello-themed,showcase} --target native --release --strip` produces three files whose Subsystem reads back as 2 with no post-processing; test exes are largely unaffected because only those whose code reaches `init_backend()` become GUI(2) (measured: `core.whitebox_test.exe`, `ui.whitebox_test.exe`, the rest CONSOLE(3)), and the library gate stays 830 tests / 825 passed (the 5 reds are the pre-existing dbus session-bus and `fsx_wbtest.mbt:109` cases). Under the GUI subsystem stdout is visible only through pipes / redirection — which is exactly how the test harness captures it.
- After swapping `yue_mbt.lib`, `moon build` reports "no work to do": delete the produced exe under `_build` to force relinking.
- prepare.py mode-switch pitfall (prebuilt↔source): `cmake -D` only overrides the CMakeCache when explicitly passed — a stale ON from a previous prebuilt configure survives into source mode, so none of the globbed sources get compiled, `yue_mbt.lib` ends up with just the single shim obj, and the final link fails with 360 library-wide unresolved symbols. Fix: always pass the flag explicitly as ON/OFF for both modes. Quick check: `lib /list build\yue_mbt.lib` and count the objs — a full Windows source build has 27.
- prebuild's link_configs Windows branch once omitted the separate entry for `yue/traybus`: traybus does not depend on yue (it is the reverse), so propagation "to targets that depend on the package" never reaches it, and `moon test` linking the traybus test exe failed with 12 LNK2019 `yue_mbt_sys_*` symbols; the Linux/macOS branches already carried the separate entry, and Windows was brought in line.

### Manifest

- moon's link-flag splicing behavior (measured on Windows): for each main package it splices the flags of every package carrying link_configs in the dependency closure once, and for blackbox test targets it splices the tested package's own flags one extra time (tested package's entry ×2). Listing a `.lib` twice is harmless; listing `manifest.res` twice puts two same-name MANIFEST resources into the exe → CVT1100 link failure. The earlier conclusion that "newer moon embeds its own MANIFEST that conflicts with our res" was wrong: mt verified that moon-linked exes contain no manifest resource at all — the "other copy" of the conflict was always our own duplicated res (it started firing for any target that splices both flag sets once the Windows link config for traybus was added).
- Channel exploration conclusions: link options like `/MANIFEST:EMBED` `/MANIFESTINPUT:` placed into link_flags are discarded by cl as compile options (D9002 — options before `/link` do not reach the linker); `#pragma comment(linker,"/manifestdependency")` requires the linker to run with /MANIFEST, which moon's link does not (no external .manifest file appears next to moon-linked exes either); prebuild's stdin carries only an environment snapshot and module_root, with no target/package info, so per-target differentiated configs are impossible.
- Final scheme: manifest.res stays out of the default link_flags — dev / test / moon run need zero configuration. The cost of running without a manifest is more than visual: on a real Win10 19045 machine, clicking a button in a message box killed the process — `TaskDialogIndirect` is only exported by ordinal 345 of comctl32 v6; without a manifest the v5.82 comctl32 is loaded, whose export table also has an ordinal 345 pointing to an unrelated function, so libyue's by-ordinal lookup resolves a non-null garbage pointer and calling it is plain UB (a python ctypes probe confirmed the resolved non-null address; a MoonBit probe replicating the exact same usage ran clean three times in a row — UB is nondeterministic, a single non-repro does not disprove it). Fork fix (mbt.13): MessageBox checks comctl32's DllGetVersion before resolving the ordinal and only calls it on major version ≥ 6; below v6 it falls back to the classic `MessageBoxW` (icons mapped from the TD_*_ICON values to MB_ICON*, MB_OKCANCEL with OK returning the first custom button's response when two or more buttons are registered, MB_OK otherwise with cancel semantics), so a dialog always shows regardless of the manifest; OnClose is uniformly posted back to the UI thread (the old empty-resolution path calling it straight from the background thread was also a cross-thread hazard). The first degradation build closed silently on a null resolution, which real-machine feedback reported as "clicking the message box does nothing", hence the MessageBoxW fallback; a second round of feedback reported "icons and buttons but no text" — TaskDialog keeps the main text in `pszMainInstruction` and only the informative text in `pszContent`, while `SetText` writes only the former, so the fallback must concatenate both fields into MessageBoxW's single text line. Distribution-style builds set `YUE_MBT_KEEP_MANIFEST=1`: the res rides the yue entry, and moon build's main packages splice each entry exactly once, embedding exactly one manifest (Common-Controls v6 + supportedOS, verified by reading it back with mt) — with v6 a real TaskDialog shows; do NOT set this switch for a full `moon test` (the blackbox tested-package duplication guarantees CVT1100). release-bin.yml is configured accordingly.
- After an environment variable changes link_flags, moon occasionally keeps relinking with the stale config: if setting/unsetting the variable seems to change nothing, fall back to `moon clean` (or delete the produced exes under `_build`).

### Runtime differences

- **2026-09-25: the whole tree rolled back to the 09-23 evening state f3ba8bf (the user's call)**: the entire fix chain made from 09-24 onward for "form-page native children following the scroll / page-switch streaks / tooltips never showing" (first-generation 0ms resync → fork recursion into UpdateChildBounds → dropping WS_CLIPCHILDREN → allocation translation → pixel blit → band repaint ordering → page-switch relayout coalescing, 30+ commits, including fork ba479418/e373e60a/f4528cb8/cf308737, the browser package split, and three tooltip generations) proved a **net burden** across rounds of real-machine review — every round introduced new diseases (jank / blue ghosts / streak recurrence / ghosting / floating inputs / tearing) without curing the old ones, so the tree was rolled back wholesale per the user's decision; native pinned back to v0.15.6-mbt.12. Core lesson: **sync-layer fixes for mixing native HWNDs into a self-drawn world failed on the real machine repeatedly — each such fix must pass a single-point real-machine verification before the next one is layered on; bundling several fixes per round is forbidden**. Full root-cause narratives of the rolled-back approaches live in the git history of 09-24~09-25 (both repos). Accepted known state after the rollback: native tooltips never show on Windows (the native path needs a comctl32 v6 manifest), native inputs follow scrolling via the update_layout fallback, and page-switch/scroll streaks remain (inherent to WS_CLIPCHILDREN). **After the rollback the user hand-picked items to restore** (same day): the browser package split (with the lib-form-differentiated linking fix), vector self-drawn result symbols, the cursor_group component, the network-status label() fix plus the Linux initial-dispatch fix, the Windows live-resize bitmap placeholder (pure shim subclass), and the single-line Entry wheel forwarding (fork 7f57e87f, delivered via the v0.15.6-mbt.18 prebuilt; the unselected fork ba479418 was removed in 3f8e8935 before cutting that release). Not restored: the self-drawn tooltip bubble, the prepare backport machinery, and every scroll/page-switch family fix. **The Windows overlay-scrollbar form was restored later** (its own batch after real-machine acceptance): only the form itself was ported (host wrapper + self-drawn thumb + flex/basis 0 inside the host branch); the 09-23 baseline's update_layout follow fallback stays untouched and the non-Windows branch is unchanged. The original commit's bundled "remove the fallback + unconditional basis 0" (the collapse root that aab1a74 had to cure) did not come along.
- MoonBit concrete-type misuse in FFI handle parameters: `MessageBox::run_for_window` once passed the `Window` struct straight into an extern expecting a `View` handle (the C side received a MoonBit heap address instead of the registry id), so `CastTo<nu::Window>` failed silently — the message box ended up parentless and the synchronous path deadlocked. Detection: the MoonBit-generated C prototype shows `struct ...Window*` for the parameter instead of `void*`. Rule: any extern declaration taking a handle must use `View` (the external type) and let MoonBit call sites unwrap the concrete struct via `.view()`; the async `show_for_window` and the sync `run_for_window` must follow the same convention. Also note: moon's incremental check is unreliable — after changing the shim/library, `moon build` may report "up to date" and not relink, so delete the produced exe under `_build` to force it (otherwise you probe stale-library behavior).
- Visibility-toggled pages disappear after switching (set_visible-driven tabs like tabs_t, verified on a real machine): libyue win's `View::Layout()` propagates only to an `IsContainer()` parent (`if (GetParent() && GetParent()->IsContainer())`), and Scroll is not a Container — after a subtree mounted under a Scroll's content toggles visibility (set_visible → yoga display switch), the propagation chain breaks at the Scroll, the yoga root never recalculates, and the page being shown gets a 0-height allocation; when the page content has no explicit height it is squeezed to the sum of its paddings (measured: page height 50→16, the whole content block vanishes). GTK hides this behind full size-allocate relayout; it is Windows-only. Fix: the shim's `yue_mbt_view_layout` (update_layout) now walks the parent chain to the root container and calls `Layout()` there, and tabs_t's `sel.subscribe` adds one `update_layout(outer)` after the visibility flips. A probe (page-content on_draw self-report + bounds dump) confirms every switch paints correctly with a stable page height. Note: only trees routed through a Scroll's content break the chain — a direct flex child of the root always recalculates.
- Visibility-toggle vanishing, residual three-layer case (the showcase structure: page-container set_visible switching + scroll + section + tabs_t, still reproduces on a real machine): on tab switch, the dirty self-heal branch of `Container::Layout` (the one carrying a TODO comment in view.cc) allocates outer containers from the yoga mid-state of the display switch — sibling flex:1 page containers get a compressed height from the scroll content's mid-state measurement (measured: 210→56), and it cannot self-correct afterwards: the self-heal propagation breaks at Scroll (not a Container), and the root-level recalc's SetBounds chain breaks at intermediate containers whose size did not change (identical size → ViewImpl::SizeAllocate early-returns → children's UpdateChildBounds never fires). Consequence: the WM_PAINT dirty rect is clipped by the compressed page container into a 24-high sliver that does not intersect the page area (74,278,512,50), so `DrawChild` skips the whole block on `child_dirty.IsEmpty()` — on_draw never fires while bounds look fine. Tried and measured ineffective: root recalc ×N, reversed visibility order (true before false), root recalc inlined into set_visible (shim side), leaf-level visibility (only page content toggles), page_c flexbasis 0 (CSS flex:1 1 0 semantics). Conclusion: the root cause lives in libyue win's yoga integration itself (dirty self-heal using stale layout + the Scroll chain break), which external shim/yue-layer patches cannot penetrate; a fork-side fix is needed (candidate directions: force YGNodeCalculateLayout before allocating in UpdateChildBounds, or keep Scroll content measurement out of the mid-state). The 20babb5 fix fully covers the case where tabs_t sits directly in a scroll's content (no page-container layer); the showcase case awaits the fork-side approach.
- Scrollbar form: libyue's Windows scrollbar is a self-drawn classic style (the Scrollbar class: track + arrow buttons + permanent layout space), and `Scroll::SetOverlayScrollbar` is a no-op on Windows (the API is excluded by `#if !defined(OS_WIN)` in the header) — GTK's floating form has no counterpart here. The unifying answer is the yue-level `attach_overlay_thumb`: set policy to Never to hide the platform bar, and a self-drawn thumb positioned via yoga absolute (static right/top/bottom) spanning the right edge's full height, with the visible segment painted in on_draw from Ref state — scroll updates only schedule_paint with zero yoga relayout; appear/fade uses two clear_timeout-cancellable timer steps (d9→73→hidden), dragging relies on the implicit mouse capture acquired on press (moves keep arriving outside the thumb — see the WM_CAPTURECHANGED note under the splitter entry), and wheel events on the slim thumb are forwarded to the Scroll manually via on_wheel. Landing point: the declarative `scroll()` default form (Windows, overlay=true with no explicit policy) wraps a host container and routes through it (the style parameters move to the host with the Scroll filling it — the thumb's absolute positioning is anchored to the host; attaching the thumb to the page container directly would be skewed by padding/margins); the overlay_scroll component and Windows-side page-level scrolling share this path. The Windows on_scroll→0ms-timer forced relayout of native HWNDs is kept.
- System accent color: `DwmGetColorizationColor` returns the "window colorization color" — a blend of the accent color with the system base color, visibly off from the Settings accent color under default configuration (reference machine Win10 19045 returned yellow-green 0xFFB7AC00 while the Settings accent color is teal 0xFF00B7C3); read the registry `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\DWM\AccentColor` first (0xAABBGGRR, written since Win10 1803+), falling back to the colorization color only when missing / 0 / 0xFFFFFFFF — after the fix the probe returned 0xFF00B7C3, bit-for-bit equal to the Settings page. The fallback value's alpha bits encode "intensity", not opacity; take RGB only.
- GetSystemPowerStatus semantic losses (battery query): ACLineStatus 255 (unknown) counts as not-online; BatteryFlag 128 (no battery) / 255 (unknown) both count as no battery; BatteryLifeTime drifts with AC/battery mode and is often -1, so remaining time is never reported (the Linux UPower side folds State 1/4/5 all into "on power", aligning the two platforms). Also: at full charge on AC the BatteryFlag is High without the Charging bit (measured: percent=100 charging=false), so "full but still on power" shows as non-charging on Windows; there is no change event for the charge level itself (only plug/unplug), so slow drain/charge needs polling to stay fresh (the showcase system page uses a 30s set_timer plus instant refresh on plug events, both through the same query path).
- `AttributedText` ranged font / color: upstream Windows supports only whole-text (ranged calls CHECK-crash; GDI+ has no rich text). Fork mbt.9 builds a segmented layout engine (run storage / flowing line breaking / measure-draw from one source) and the MoonBit-side degradation guards are removed — three platforms now agree. Gotcha: `Gdiplus::Font::GetHeight`'s overload takes `(const Graphics*)`; passing a reference does not compile.
- `Color::Get(Border)` hits NOTREACHED and returns a garbage color: the shim maps Border to `GetSysColor(COLOR_WINDOWFRAME)`.
- Blurry self-drawn text: libyue's GDI+ brush hardcodes grayscale antialiasing; an idempotent prepare.py patch switches it to `TextRenderingHintClearTypeGridFit`.
- System notifications: WinRT toast looks up the notifier by AUMID and silently fails without an AppUserModelID; the shim sets the AUMID automatically before the first notification and writes the registry DisplayName.
- Browser prefers WebView2 (falls back to IE when the loader / runtime is missing); WebView2 follows the system proxy — on machines with a broken proxy set `LIBYUE_WEBVIEW2_ARGS=--no-proxy-server` (a prepare.py patch injects AdditionalBrowserArguments from the variable); the demo:// custom protocol does nothing under WebView2 (the IE path works).
- win32 Group / Scroll do not grow with content: give them explicit heights; ScrollImpl's scroll range only honors SetContentSize, so a prepare.py patch queries the content yoga tree for natural size when none was set explicitly.
- Key codes and modifiers: the Windows KeyboardCode uses Win32 VK values, normalized to the constant table at the events.mbt entry; Windows' native modifier bits are Shift=2 / Ctrl=4 / Alt=8, and the shim's `NormalizeModifiers` gained an OS_WIN branch mapping to the unified 1/2/4/8.
- Ghost tray icons: abnormal exits skip the CRT static-destruction chain and leave the icon behind; the shim installs four process-level hooks (atexit / SetConsoleCtrlHandler / SetUnhandledExceptionFilter / SIGABRT) that re-issue NIM_DELETE by "owner window + icon ID range"; a taskkill /F hard kill cannot be rooted out in-process.
