A blank tray icon means check the asset first (it was once a 1×1 placeholder).
- The Popover substitute (borderless / non-activating / topmost window): the popup needs `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE` (else clicking the popup steals focus); under nested scrolling `GetBoundsInScreen` yields garbage offsets, so anchor coordinates come from the native child HWND's `GetWindowRect`; close is destructive on Windows — a reusable popup switches to `SetVisible(false)`; outside-click dismissal installs a `WH_MOUSE_LL` hook that PostTasks a close when the press lands outside the popup rectangle; the popup background ignores themes, so `Popover::set_background_color` was added end to end. libyue's SetVisible / IsVisible are unreliable on a non-activating topmost window — use Win32 `SetWindowPos` + `SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE` directly.
- autocomplete keyboard navigation: the Windows branch attaches on_key_down on the Entry (↑↓ highlight / Enter select / Esc dismiss); single-line EDIT has no vertical-centering style, so `entry_vcenter` narrows the control by font line height and splits the leftover into margins; RichEdit text stays black regardless of theme — `Entry::set_colors` (EM_SETBKCOLOR + CHARFORMAT2) hooks it into the theme chain.
- Dark mode for native controls: real Win32 common controls (RICHEDIT50W / SysListView32 / SysDateTimePick32 etc.) all ignore the system dark theme; RichEdit can be darkened via the message channel; Table cannot (its custom draw repaints a white base over external messages); the official answer is the self-drawn component library, with native dark mode as a known boundary.
- Hit testing runs opposite to painting: upstream `FindChildFromPoint` iterates children in insertion order, so a late-attached full-screen mask paints on top but its events fall through to the earlier container (dialog uncloseable, clicks pass through) — fork mbt.6 reversed the traversal to match paint order. Any "visually-topmost view receives no events" — check the hit-test direction first.
- The wheel is consumed outright by the outermost Scroll and never dispatched, so nested scroll areas and self-drawn canvases never scroll: a prepare.py patch (`patch_win_wheel_dispatch`) dispatches to the child under the cursor via FindChildFromPoint, and shim `yue_mbt_view_on_wheel` gained a Windows branch converting WM_MOUSEWHEEL deltas.
- Text measuring and drawing disagree: `GetBoundsFor` uses GenericDefault (with overhang) while `DrawString` uses GenericTypographic, so manual `x=(width−measured)/2` centering always sits left; positioning must use `align=Center/End` and leave it to the platform — measuring is only for computing container widths.
- Two splitter traps: an explicit `SetCapture` on Windows triggers `WM_CAPTURECHANGED`, which tears down the implicit capture (skip if capture is already held); the `flexbasis:"50%"` percentage string parses only on GTK — use pixel values everywhere.
- The Entry infinite-recursion case: two mutually recursive functions in the non-Linux branch overflowed the stack, and MSVC C4717 had already warned — treat "logically doomed" warnings as errors. For "no window" GUIs use `Get-Process <name> | Select MainWindowHandle`; MoonBit println is fully buffered through pipes and lost if the process dies — instrument via stderr.
- mount_window activates the window automatically after the handle callback; consumers no longer call activate manually.
- Platform info / locale / scaling / clipboard / timers / global shortcuts / global mouse polling / canvas (GDI+) all verified working.
- An offscreen Canvas cannot be created before initialize on Windows: a single `Canvas::new` crashes with 0xc0000005 (minimal repro involves no drawing at all). Root cause: Canvas / DoubleBuffer / Painter construction depends on `nu::State` — GDI+ (`GdiplusHolder`), the default font, and NativeTheme are all established with State, which initialize() creates; a bare `GdiplusStartup` fallback inside canvas_new still crashed (State has more null dereferences), and the correct fix is running the same `yue_mbt_app_init()` as initialize when `g_state` is null. Contrast with Linux: the cairo image surface has no State dependency, so offscreen geometry runs without initialize (only the text path needs the GTK stack — see "Self-drawn canvas and chart rendering"); Windows could not even start geometry, and after the shim fallback the "offscreen Canvas usable anywhere" semantics now agree across all three platforms. charts_wbtest's offscreen geometry benchmark passes on Windows accordingly (17/17).
- A platform-independent function mistakenly stubbed in a platform branch: wire's `'d'` codec goes through `yue_mbt_sys_f64_to_bits/from_bits` (a pure bit reinterpretation implemented with memcpy), but the implementation sat inside the OS_LINUX branch with a non-Linux stub returning 0 — on Windows three pure in-memory wire tests failed with everything decoding to 0 (wire codec tests need no bus and run on non-Linux too). Fixed by moving them outside the platform branches. The rule: go through the stub list asking "is this really platform-specific" — pure computation / pure in-memory logic never gets stubbed (same family as the macOS note on the `#else` fallback swallowing macOS).
- The single-instance message window is the first self-owned WNDPROC/window-class code in this repo (grep found no prior usage): the class name derives from the app_id (`moonbit_libyue_instance_<app_id with dots replaced>`), and the window must be created on the main thread that runs the libyue loop. WM_COPYDATA is dispatched synchronously by SendMessage into the WNDPROC (it does not traverse the message queue); the receiver posts back to the main loop via MessageLoop::PostTask before invoking the MoonBit callback, so no application code runs inside the peer process's SendMessage stack. The mutex uses the Local\ session namespace (no elevation needed); a second same-name CreateMutexW within one process hits ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS, guarded idempotent via a static handle. [Pending real-machine verification] actual dispatch of the message window under the libyue loop, SetForegroundWindow success rate under foreground-lock, and the title-based fallback when mixed with older builds.
- The UI thread's COM apartment must be STA or file dialogs hang/crash: the common file dialog `IFileDialog::Show` requires STA — with COM never initialized on the UI thread, `CoCreateInstance(CLSID_FileOpenDialog)` fails outright (null dereference inside the lib), and when an application call path initializes the thread as MTA first (typically an old in-UI-thread `CoInitializeEx(MTA)` network query), `Show` hangs forever — observed as "app freezes the moment you open/save a file". Fix: shim `yue_mbt_app_init` calls `State::InitializeCOM()` right after creating State (ScopedCOMInitializer STA + OleInitialize, idempotent); afterwards `CoInitializeEx(MTA)` on the UI thread only yields `RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE` and local COM objects keep working. Complementary to "move NLM queries to a background MTA thread": the background thread's COM init is thread-local and does not replace the UI thread's own STA. Verify: file dialogs open and return paths on a real machine.
- No global repaint on theme switch on Windows leaves stale pixels ("ghosts"): the GTK side of `theme_apply` rebuilds CSS and repaints every window synchronously as a fallback; the Windows side used to only notify theme-subscribed custom views, so unsubscribed regions (and the area behind hidden/moved native child windows) kept old pixels until a mouse-over invalidated them locally. Fix: shim `yue_mbt_repaint_all` gains a Windows branch — `EnumWindows` filtered to this process's visible ownerless top-level windows, `RedrawWindow(RDW_INVALIDATE|RDW_ERASE|RDW_ALLCHILDREN)` to invalidate everything including native children, invalidation only (WM_PAINT goes back to the message loop); `theme_apply`'s windows branch calls it. Verify: toggling dark/light repeatedly leaves no residue on headers/pages.
- Zero-height custom-drawn views silently render nothing (table_t text column invisible): `ViewImpl::Invalidate` returns early on empty sizes, and a childless on_draw container with no height style measures to 0 in yoga and never paints — table_t's CellText cell is exactly that (text drawn via on_draw, no children), so the whole text column vanished while header/zebra/checkboxes stayed fine; GTK's clipping behaves differently which is why it never showed there (the mirror-image of the earlier "GTK small-cell path fills don't render" trap). Fix: `cell_view` sets `minHeight=row_height` on the CellText container. Lesson: an on_draw container needs a non-zero size source (explicit height or children); "no children + auto height" equals "not painted" on Windows; an offscreen canvas pixel probe rules out the paint pipeline first (colored AttributedText is bit-exact fine on a Windows canvas).
- GDI+ blend modes: only Normal/Copy take effect: `PainterWin::SetBlendMode` maps only Copy to `CompositingModeSourceCopy`, everything else falls to `SourceOver` — GDI+ `Graphics` has exactly these two compositing modes, so Multiply/Screen/Difference/Xor are silent no-ops. Offscreen pixel probe: the Multiply overlap (128,128,255) is bit-identical to SourceOver (mathematically expected #8028FF). This is a platform capability gap; the lib stays untouched (a full blend set needs D2D); the showcase canvas demo reports "only Normal takes effect on this platform" on Windows, and the platform wording of `Image::write_to_file` in docs is corrected accordingly (Windows GDI+ encoder handles png/jpeg; the mac release package never compiled it and always fails).
- The native Tab emits `on_selected_page_change` when the first page is added (internal initial selection, not a user switch): registering the callback before adding pages makes it fire spuriously during mount (declarative `tab()` used to let switch-counter demos start at nonzero); registering after the add loop avoids it.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Windows build baseline (W0/W1, first batch of Windows enablement)

- **Environment**: Windows 10 19045 + VS BuildTools 2022 (MSVC 14.44) + SDK 10.0.26100, moon 0.1.20260920; new-stack branch `feature/yoga-mbt`. Goal: verify every completed new-stack item (all `[x]` in TODO.md) on Windows, with the Windows foundation (Win32 backend) first.
- **moon native works out of the box on Windows, no vcvars needed**: run `moon test` from a plain shell (Git Bash / CMD) — moon locates the MSVC toolchain itself and compiles/links (evidence: cl/link error codes C2059/C1083 and lib.exe's Chinese output). This differs from the old-stack note "run moon from a Native Tools Command Prompt" — that applied to the old prepare.py/cmake chain, not the new stack's build.
- **A hard failure in any workspace member's prebuild blocks every moon command**: `modules/ffmpeg-mbt/prebuild.py` exits non-zero when pkg-config is missing, and every check/test across the five `moon.work` members runs it first; the main `scripts/prebuild.py` already degrades gracefully off Linux (empty link_configs). Fix: ffmpeg's prebuild gains a "non-Linux → empty link_configs, exit 0" branch (Linux behavior unchanged), matching the main script; its consumer (gui-media) is a transition-period red dot anyway and not on the new-stack verification path.
- **GLib types in non-Linux placeholder stubs are syntax errors under MSVC**: `win/gtk_stub_portable.c` used `gint32` as placeholder return types — the whole file sits inside `#if !defined(__linux__)` so it never compiled on Linux and the issue never surfaced; MSVC reports 6× C2059 (no glib.h, `gint32` undefined). Changed to `int32_t` (same 32-bit ABI, extern prototypes unchanged). Lesson: placeholder stubs must be written to the standard "compiles for real on Windows" — MSVC is the first real reader a placeholder stub gets.
- **`chensuiyi/subproc`'s C stub uses POSIX `poll.h` and cannot compile on Windows**: `sys`'s `procrun.mbt` builds on @subproc (its own comment says "Linux only"), so sys and chart (which depends on sys) all fail to compile. The Windows subprocess layer (spawn→timed reclaim→output capture) belongs to W14 and will be redone with CreateProcess, replacing the MoonBit-side @subproc dependency; until then sys/chart are unverifiable on Windows.
- **Per-package test scoping behaves the same on Windows as Linux**: running bare `moon test` inside a workspace member directory drags the main package's red dots into the build; scope with `-p` (already recorded in HANDOFF.md, confirmed identical on Windows).
- **Verification** (2026-10-11, this machine): `moon check` 287 errors / 68 warnings — **verbatim identical** to the Linux baseline; pure-MoonBit packages all green — yoga-mbt 96/96, core 62/62, input 10/10, mdview 26/26, theme 7/8 (the failing "control-height baseline" case depends on Pango font measurement, which the placeholder text backend cannot satisfy — deferred to the text-backend batch), icons 2/4 (the two failures are "actually paints pixels" assertions, deferred to the render-backend batch); ui panics on `TextMetrics::unwrap` null (same text batch), sys/chart fail to compile on subproc (W14).

### MoonBit native GUI stack · Windows window foundation (W2, unified stub + Win32 backend)

- **Architecture decision: the platform stub is merged into a single three-branch `win/stub.c`** — `_WIN32` real Win32 implementation, `WM_STUB_GTK` real GTK implementation (prebuild compiles it on Linux with `-DWM_STUB_GTK` + pkg-config header paths into `libyue_win_stub.a`), and placeholders for the rest; the old `gtk_stub.c`/`gtk_stub_portable.c` pair is gone. The physical constraint behind the merge: moon's native-stub compiles every .c listed in moon.pkg **on all platforms**, while GTK header paths are only reachable via prebuild — so the GTK branch must hang off a "prebuild-only macro"; the Linux native-stub compile (no macro) falls into no branch and produces an empty TU, avoiding double definitions against the .a. This is the equivalent of the old two-file structure, converged into one file. An empty TU is proven fine in this chain (the old portable file already compiled empty on Linux).
- **moon's native-stub sees `windows.h` directly on Windows** (probe package actually compiled and linked): moon locates the MSVC toolchain itself and sets up the SDK include paths, so the Win32 stub goes through native-stub with no prebuild help; prebuild's Windows branch only emits system-library link flags (`user32.lib gdi32.lib imm32.lib advapi32.lib`, MSVC positional-input style).
- **MSVC's `IDC_*` cursor macros default to the ANSI variants**: without UNICODE, `IDC_ARROW` is the `MAKEINTRESOURCEA` form (LPSTR), and passing it to `LoadCursorW`'s `LPCWSTR` parameter trips C4133; force `#define UNICODE`/`_UNICODE` at the top of the stub file to go all-W.
- **Key mapping aligned with GDK**: the character face is taken in `WM_KEYDOWN` via `ToUnicode` (ASCII/Latin-1 verbatim, otherwise `0x01000000|unicode`, matching `gdk_unicode_to_keyval`, so both of `keysym_to_text`'s Latin-1/UCS paths accept it); **for Ctrl combos the `VK_CONTROL` bit must be removed from the `GetKeyboardState` snapshot before conversion** — with the control bit present ToUnicode yields control characters (`\x01`) and the kernel's Ctrl+A check (`keysym=='a'`) breaks; cleared, it matches GDK's "keyval is the base character, modifiers ride in mods" semantics. AltGr (Ctrl+Alt) therefore cannot reach special characters — deferred to the IME/later batches. Dead keys (`ToUnicode` returning negative) push no event; composition happens naturally on the next key via layout state. Alt+F4 is handed back to `DefWindowProc` to produce `WM_CLOSE` (same semantics as "the window manager requests close"); other system keys (F10 menu, Alt+Space) are swallowed.
- **Blitting needs no byte swap**: `render`'s Bitmap is cairo ARGB32 (little-endian bytes B,G,R,A premultiplied), which is byte-compatible with GDI's 32bpp `BI_RGB` top-down DIB (negative biHeight) — `StretchDIBits` blits directly; present only records the pointer + `InvalidateRect`, the actual blit happens in `WM_PAINT` (same shape as the GTK stub's "blit only in the draw callback", avoiding the dead-window window). `WM_ERASEBKGND` returns 1 to prevent flicker.
- **Loop recipe**: wait with `MsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx(0,NULL,timeout,QS_ALLINPUT,MWMO_INPUTAVAILABLE)` (returns immediately when undispatched messages exist, negative timeout = INFINITE); cross-thread wakeup is an `HWND_MESSAGE` message-only window + `PostMessageW(WM_APP+1)`; the pump drains with `PeekMessageW` + `DispatchMessageW` and deliberately does **no TranslateMessage** (WM_CHAR is not consumed; the character face is taken in WM_KEYDOWN).
- **Slot and creation ordering**: `WM_SIZE` arrives during `CreateWindowW`, so the slot id must land in `WM_CREATE` via `CREATESTRUCT.lpCreateParams` (setting `GWLP_USERDATA` only after the call drops the first WM_SIZE); client-area semantics via `AdjustWindowRect` (frame stretched so the client area is exactly width×height). DPI via `SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext` per-monitor v2 (through GetProcAddress so old systems missing the export don't fail to load), whole stack in physical pixels, `WM_DPICHANGED` repositions by the suggested rect with WM_SIZE doing the bookkeeping.
- **Verification** (2026-10-11, this machine): `moon build examples/native-window` links the full chain; smoke `NATIVE-WINDOW-OK frames=45` (5s timer exit, exit 0, 45 presented frames ⇒ present→WM_PAINT→StretchDIBits works); the core.App host shape verified by a delete-after-run probe printing `WIN-SMOKE-OK` (App::new + declarative mount + timer + clean exit); core 62/62 still green (tests never call App::new, so no real windows pop up), whole-repo check 287/68 unchanged. band_h=0/0/0/0 is the placeholder text backend (W5).

### WebView2 webview stub and ffmpeg real linking on Windows (platform batch, 2026-10-13)

- **WebView2 custom schemes must be pre-registered at Environment creation**: navigating to a custom scheme not registered via `ICoreWebView2EnvironmentOptions4::SetCustomSchemeRegistrations` fails outright (failure code 9 on a real machine, later 8). The MoonBit-side `webview_predeclare_schemes` list flows through a new extern into a global list in the C stub; `wb_create` passes a hand-written `WbOptions` (four nested sub-interface COM object) and the engine collects the list while creating the Environment.
- **A hand-written COM propget/propput missing the `self` parameter silently corrupts the vtable on x64**: declaring `get_bool(BOOL *value)` with one parameter — the engine calls it with `(self, &value)` per the COM contract; on x64 RCX (=self) is read as value, so `*value = FALSE` actually zeroes the first 8 bytes of the object (lpVtbl!), and every later call on that interface jumps a NULL vtable = segfault. put_str/put_bool share the disease (missing this read, harmless on x64). **C does no signature checking on vtable slots (only a C4113 warning)** — count the parameter list of every hand-written COM method against the header.
- **The array returned from `GetCustomSchemeRegistrations` must be `CoTaskMemAlloc`-allocated**: the contract is that the caller (loader) frees it with `CoTaskMemFree` — handing over a static array pointer means the loader frees it and the heap manager raises `0xC0000374` (heap corruption), crashing inside the engine right after get_regs returns with nothing on the stack pointing at registrations. Debugging used AddVectoredExceptionHandler (exception code/address/module) plus HeapWalk full-heap validation (stderr is unbuffered; stdout buffers are lost on segfault).
- **MSVC reads BOM-less UTF-8 sources using the system code page (GBK) by default** (C4819): UTF-8 bytes of Chinese comments and ffmpeg headers get misread — when the last byte of a comment line pairs with the newline into one GBK double-byte char, the next line is swallowed into the comment, cascading into hundreds of "illegal storage class / undefined identifier" errors. Fix: add `/utf-8` to `stub-cc-flags` (the vendored ffmpeg headers hit this too — rational.h reported C4819).
- **moon prebuild `vars` + moon.pkg `${build.VAR}` substitution works** (verified on 0.1.20260920): prebuild emits `{"vars": {"FFMPEG_INC": "..."}, "link_configs": [...]}` and moon.pkg declares `link: { "native": { "stub-cc-flags": "/utf-8 -I${build.FFMPEG_INC}" } }` — vendor header paths get injected into stub compilation without static hard-coding; `stub-cc-flags` only affects native-stub compilation. Platforms that do not emit the variable must still provide a placeholder value (`/usr/include` or `.`) so `${...}` never resolves to nothing.
- **ffmpeg dev-content vendor policy**: from BtbN `ffmpeg-n9.0-latest-win64-lgpl-shared-9.0`, the include headers + 7 import libraries + LGPLv3 LICENSE total 2.5MB committed under `modules/ffmpeg-mbt/vendor/` (**choose lgpl-shared over gpl-shared** — LGPL obligations are minimal for dynamic linking); runtime DLLs (150MB) stay out of the repo — place next to the exe or on PATH. `ffmpeg_stub.c` drops the `_WIN32` all-failure stub branch; all three platforms share one implementation (the ffmpeg API is cross-platform and the original Linux branch had no POSIX-specific calls).
- **miniaudio needs zero extra link libraries on Windows**: WASAPI/COM/dsound/winmm are all runtime LoadLibrary'd — `gui-media/prebuild.py` emitting empty link_configs is the correct shape (not a fallback). gui-media passes 24/24 including the AudioPlayer smoke (pump 33 ticks playing a 1-second asset — the WASAPI device chain actually produced sound); ffmpeg-mbt passes 6/6 (real ogg/m4a/wav + video decoding).
- **Unattended shutdown for GUI-subsystem examples**: `native-web` has no self-exit timer (manual acceptance walks through every section), so automation must use `taskkill /IM` (sends WM_CLOSE; statistics print after app.run() returns and get flushed) — `kill -9` loses the stdout buffer too.

### WebView2 cross-HWND focus and wheel forwarding (focus batch, 2026-10-13)

- **GotFocus/LostFocus live on the Controller, not on ICoreWebView2**: `add_GotFocus/add_LostFocus` are methods of `ICoreWebView2Controller`; and for this event pair the `Invoke` sender parameter is `ICoreWebView2Controller*` (the event-handler macro hard-codes sender as `ICoreWebView2*`, which on x64 means real crashes beyond C4113) — these two handlers are hand-written, not macro-expanded.
- **Wheel messages are delivered to the focused window regardless of mouse position**, so once WebView2 takes focus the host's scroll areas go dead. Fix: two halves. ① The stub subclasses the engine input window (`Chrome_WidgetWin_1`, found by class name under the panel HWND via FindWindowEx right after the controller create completes; not finding it only loses half the forwarding and is not an error) — when focus is in the page but the mouse is elsewhere, wheel messages are SendMessage'd back to the host root window; ② the host's `WM_MOUSEWHEEL` branch first asks via a wheel probe (registered by the web stub at create time through the `wm_set_wheel_probe` function-pointer slot, avoiding a reverse win→web symbol dependency) whether the screen coordinate lands on a web page, and forwards the message verbatim to the Chrome window if so. Together the two halves reproduce the GTK "hover scrolls" behavior. Subclassing stores the original proc and self HWND via SetProp; destroy restores and RemoveProps.
- **Host-driven focus handover**: `MoveFocus(COREWEBVIEW2_MOVE_FOCUS_REASON_PROGRAMMATIC)` (WebKit branch: `gtk_widget_grab_focus`); the GotFocus event fires afterwards, so the host can react with UI state.
- **Focus events are exposed as kinds 16/17 (WebView2-only)**: WebKitGTK is same-tree widgets where the host perceives focus natively, so it does not emit them.
- **Debugging incident (lesson)**: a one-line `python -c` script passing a bad `newline` value to `io.open(p,'w')` on an existing large file raises ValueError during TextIOWrapper init — but the file is already truncated empty by the 'w' open, losing hundreds of lines (recovered via git checkout and redone with the Edit tool). Never rewrite large files with inline python one-liners; use the Edit tool or write the script to a file first.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · image decode backend (W9: WIC on Windows)

- **Why this is the single exception to the platform matrix**: Windows rendering is a **pure MoonBit rasterizer** (zero third-party deps, per the plan matrix), but a rasterizer does not decode — image decoding has to borrow a system capability, **WIC** (`windowscodecs.lib`, an OS component, not a third-party package). The non-Linux branch previously stubbed the whole `img_*` set as no-ops, so on Windows `Image::new_from_file` always returned an empty image and the animated-GIF widget collapsed to zero size; the test layer skipped those cases behind `decode_available()` / `ui_decode_guard()` probes (so they were never red). This batch implements the `_WIN32` branch of `gui/render/stub.c`.
- **Three measured WIC facts** (proven by the pure-C probe `experiment/img_probe`, no MoonBit runtime involved):
  1. **WIC's GIF decoder hands back raw sub-rectangle frames and does not composite for you** — `IWICBitmapFrameDecode::GetSize` reports the **frame rect** (12x12 in the probe), with the offset in `/imgdesc/Left|Top` (14/14 measured). GdkPixbuf's `GdkPixbufAnimationIter` on Linux does that compositing for us, which is why this difference is new here: full-canvas compositing is our job — the canvas is the logical screen from `/logscrdesc/Width|Height`, and each frame is closed out by its disposal method (0/1 keep, 2 clear the frame rect, 3 restore the snapshot taken *before* that frame was drawn).
  2. **The transparent index is already applied by WIC** (frame alphas measured at only 0 and 255). GIF transparency means "keep the previous frame here" rather than blending, so the compositing rule is simply "skip alpha==0, otherwise overwrite the whole pixel" — no alpha blending involved.
  3. **`/grctlext/Delay` is in centiseconds** (per the GIF spec), so multiply by 10 for milliseconds; missing/zero falls back to 100 ms, same rule as the Linux branch.
- **Premultiplication matches the Linux branch word for word**: after converting to `GUID_WICPixelFormat32bppBGRA` (straight), this layer premultiplies with `(c*a+127)/255` before handing pixels to MoonBit — the same formula as the Linux branch, which keeps "encode -> decode -> re-encode" byte-stable (the semi-transparent round-trip assertion in `image_wbtest` depends on it). The static first-frame size rule also follows Linux: **a GIF is composited at logical-screen size**, so a sub-rect first frame is not cropped down to the frame rect.
- **Memory strategy for animation**: pixels are decoded **on demand** (N frames are not all cached) and the composited result is cached in a canvas, so repeatedly fetching the same frame (once per repaint tick) does not re-decode; advancing one frame is incremental (only the previous frame's disposal is closed out), while wrapping or jumping replays from frame 0. The 4096-frame cap only guards against pathological files (memory is independent of frame count, but the wrap tick is O(n)).
- **Frame numbering keeps Linux's monotonic rule**: `img_anim_frame()` only ever increases (the displayed frame is `frame % count`). As a result the widget-side `gif(looping=false)` stop condition ("frame number back to 0") **never fires on either platform** — that is pre-existing behavior and `image_wbtest`'s "frame number equals number of successful advances" assertion depends on it, so this batch does not change it. One asset fact worth noting: the four frames of `examples/showcase/assets/dot.gif` (used by showcase) have **byte-identical** compressed data and differ only in their local color tables (so it reads as "the same dot changing color" rather than moving).
- **Link surface**: the Windows branch of `gui/scripts/prebuild.py` gains a **RENDER_PACKAGE** entry (`windowscodecs.lib ole32.lib user32.lib`) — previously the render package had no link_configs at all on Windows (every stub was a no-op needing no external symbols), so `render.whitebox_test.exe` would hit unresolved symbols the moment it calls WIC. The GUID constants (`CLSID_WICImagingFactory1` / `IID_IWICImagingFactory` / `GUID_WICPixelFormat32bppBGRA`) come from the same place as the W20f icon loading; C mode cannot use `__uuidof`, so they are resolved at link time.
- **No `/utf-8` needed**: under MSVC's GBK misreading of the Chinese comments, the render stub emits only 2 C4819 warnings (byte-for-byte the same as before the change; `win/stub.c` emits 6), with no swallowed lines and no syntax errors — so no `stub-cc-flags` is introduced (the ffmpeg-mbt one exists because its vendored headers genuinely trip).
- **Verification**: the pure-C probe `experiment/img_probe/img_backend_probe.c` (independent of the moon toolchain, compiled directly with `cl /W4 /utf-8`, including `render/stub.c` so it can call the `img_*` entry points) ends with **`IMG-BACKEND-OK`** across 60 assertions: PNG file/memory entry points agree on size and premultiplication never overflows, garbage/NULL/zero-length/out-of-range handle/missing file all return 0, `dot.gif` static first frame is 120x120, the animation reports 4 frames with a 400 ms delay, advancing is monotonic, different frames really do differ, and after wrapping the displayed frame is byte-identical to frame 0; free is idempotent and everything is a no-op afterwards; a PNG opened through the animation entry reports `is_static=1` and never advances; and **sub-rectangle compositing** (`experiment/img_probe/assets/subrect.gif`, frame 1 is 12x12 at (14,14)) keeps the canvas at 40x40 with (0,0) still holding frame 0's black and the box tinted red. To run it: compile the exe with `cl`, then execute `experiment/img_probe/img_backend_probe.exe .` from the repo root (the asset rebuild script `make_asset.py` regenerates subrect.gif with ffmpeg). `moon check` on the library module is warning-free.
- **Not done in this batch, and not pretended otherwise**: the macOS backend (still a stub implementation); the "frame number wraps to 0" semantics for `looping=false` (pre-existing cross-platform behavior; changing it would require touching both `ui/gif.mbt` and the `image_wbtest` assertion); JPEG/BMP/TIFF were not verified format by format (they go through the same `CreateDecoderFromFilename` sniffing path, with PNG/GIF proven); real-machine appearance (the image areas of showcase's card/media pages, whether the GIF animates) belongs to `_人工测试清单.md`.

### C-side text layout object cache (Pango / DirectWrite, 2026-10-14, data-driven)

- **Background and evidence**: the frame-stage ledger (`gui/core/prof.mbt`) read on the native-app real machine `frames=190 layout=220ms paint=34487ms present=78ms total=34785ms` — **paint is 99.1% of the frame cost while layout is only 0.6%** (yoga's internal cache works; "full-tree relayout every frame" is not the bottleneck). The cost is that every full-window repaint re-creates a layout object per visible text widget on the C side (Pango `PangoLayout` / DirectWrite `IDWriteTextLayout`: itemize + shaping + font resolution, all redone).
- **Fix (same shape on both branches)**: cache layout objects keyed by path marker (`"m"` = measure / unconstrained draw, `"b"` = box-aligned draw) + full text bytes + font quadruple (family/size/weight/style) + width constraint/wrap/ellipsize/alignment — same key means identical layout configuration, so reuse is read-only. Cap 1024 entries (Pango) / 1024 (DWrite), whole-table clear on overflow (same contract as the MoonBit-side metrics cache). Measure and unconstrained draw share the `"m"` key (identical config path); box draws use `"b"` (width normalized by wrapped_axis, alignment only participates when width-constrained).
- **Read-only-reuse preconditions (hold on each platform)**: Pango — color is set via `cairo_set_source_rgba` and geometry offsets are computed per call, neither touches the layout; DWrite — `ptw_render` does not mutate the layout when there are no ranges (range fonts/colors belong to the rich-text rt_* path only, which still builds layouts per call and skips the cache), text color goes through `SetColor` on the shared brush.
- **Windows-side free precondition**: `img_anim_advance` (WIC) is one frame per call and the component asks once per `delay_ms` beat, so layout objects naturally reuse across beats; the canvas resources (WIC bitmap + D2D render target) were already process-cached — this batch covers the remaining big chunk, `CreateTextLayout` (with full shaping).
- **Measured (platform correction 2026-10-14)**: `experiment/anim_cost_bench` (a 30-row typical page of "button + input + text", 1400×900) — full-window repaint **21ms/frame**, a 90×32 dirty rect **0.8ms**, relayout 0ms. **These readings come from this host's Linux/X11 (cairo backend), not the Windows pure rasterizer** — see the "animation go/no-go" section below for the measured backend selection on the same machine; the per-frame cost of the `PureBackend(Raster)` path still has no real-machine number (every real-machine check by the user so far has been on this Ubuntu + X11 host; Windows/mac must re-run the same probe once hardware is available). P5's go/no-go was passed on this host's readings, and the Windows-side risk is recorded here. The after number for the full native-app page awaits a re-run of `NATIVE-APP-PROF` (the ledger now lands in `native-app-prof.txt`).
- **Not done, not pretending**: rich text rt_* (AttributedText) still builds layouts per call (small share on the demo pages; benefits to be estimated separately); when the MoonBit-side measure cache hits, the C side is never reached — this C cache mainly serves the draw path and cold starts after the MoonBit cache clears.

### Raster fill fast paths: direct-write fill_rect + analytic rounded-rect fill (2026-10-14, probe-located)

- **How it was located**: the NATIVE-APP-RENDER three-stage stats proved text accounts for only ~15ms of a ~232ms full frame — the culprit is non-text drawing. `experiment/paint_probe` (component-level isolated timing) broke it down: 60 cards of 400×120 rounded rect = **432ms/frame (7.2ms each)**, straight rects 110ms, three charts 56ms, virtual table 22ms — **rounded rects going through generic path scan (flattening + polygon AA) is the single largest item, 20ms per card**.
- **Fix (pure-raster backend, render package)**: ① `composite_solid_span` — whole-span direct write for **opaque solid** source + Normal op (no per-pixel source/premul/blend calls; premultiplied BGRA, opaque source = raw color); ② `Raster::fill_device_rect` tries the fast path before the generic cov composite; ③ `Raster::fill_round_rect` **analytic fill** — no path scanning: per-row ink (middle rows via the fast path), corner-strip pixels get coverage from "pixel-center distance to the corner circle center" (0 outside / AA at the rim / 256 inside). Applies only when axis-aligned and uniformly scaled (corners stay circular); oblique matrices or non-uniform scale fall back (`fill_round_rect` returns Bool and the Painter side takes `trace_round_rect+fill`).
- **Trap (hit in practice)**: the fast-path entry **must call `apply_fill()` first** — calling `raster.fill_round_rect` directly skips Painter::fill's source setup, so the shape gets painted with the previous source color (the table color-box and overlay-panel pixel asserts went red instantly for exactly this reason).
- **Measured (same probe, re-run)**: single rounded card 20ms→**1ms (20×)**, 60 cards 432→**23ms (19×)**, 60 straight rects 110→**10ms (11×)**, virtual table 22→**5ms (4×)**; chart row 56→36ms (vector paths/strokes are the next big chunk). Package-by-package suite 866+ green (only the virtlist style-slot red remains — a pre-existing failure from the frontend session).
- **Follow-up batch · frame-level text batching (DWrite submission merge)** (2026-10-14): NATIVE-APP-RENDER shows the d2d stage at 132us/segment (62 segments/frame = 8.2ms) — the fixed per-segment BeginDraw→EndDraw submission overhead dominates. `dwrite_text.cpp` gains a batch queue: consecutive pt_draw/pt_draw_box calls on the same target bitmap accumulate (cap 128); flushing does one BeginDraw → Clear(**union**) → per-segment DrawTextLayout → EndDraw → one read-back of the union + one per-pixel blend (overlapping segments composite inside D2D in queue order). **Triple z-order safety**: ① flush on target/dimension change (multi-window alternation); ② render gains a process-level "raster gate" — each of the 11 pixel-writing entries (fill/stroke/rounded/box_shadow/draw_image/draw_canvas) calls `pt_flush_if_overlap` with the current clip rect first, flushing only when the op's clip intersects the pending batch union (non-intersecting ops keep the batch alive, so fill-text interleaves on card walls still form long batches); ③ core `paint_frame` calls `flush_pending` before present. Layout-cache eviction can happen between enqueue and flush, so queued layouts are AddRef'd and Released after flush (no dangling). **Switch isolation**: batching is enabled only on the production path (core `text_batch_init`); tests/probes keep the old path bit-for-bit — zero suite disturbance. Measured (paint_probe): 200 segments/frame, immediate **21ms → batched 2ms (10×)**; the immediate path (rt_* rich text) flushes the batch at entry to preserve order. Pango/mac branches have no batch (stub no-ops); stub.c's common tail uses `#ifndef _WIN32` to avoid double definitions with dwrite_text.cpp.
- **Follow-up · the batched target is a raw pointer, so Windows text corrupted the heap (2026-10-15, reproduced and closed on Windows 10.0.19044)**: **Symptom** — showcase and hello-themed die right after startup (frame and native menu appear, client area stays black, exit within a second), while `hello` (one bare text line) survives; Git Bash only reports 139, the real evidence comes from WER (`Get-WinEvent` Application, Id 1000/1001): exception **0xc0000374 = STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION**, faulting module ntdll, P4 a StackHash. **Root cause** — the batch queue stores the **raw pointer** of the target pixel buffer, but the Windows text channel `draw_box_raster` (taken whenever `cairo_id()==None`, i.e. by every `draw_at`/`draw_box_at` call site) draws each segment into a **fresh offscreen `Bitmap` allocated inside the call** and frees it as soon as `blit` returns; the frame-end `flush_pending` then writes ink into a block the allocator already owns. **Neither safeguard helps**: ① the raster gate tests overlap against the batch's ink rect, but inside the batch those rects are **offscreen-local** while the gate passes **window coordinates** — different spaces, so the intersection test is luck; ② the "flush when the target changes" rule is in fact the main detonator — the next segment's new buffer flushes the *previous, already-freed* one. **Why it appeared to work before**: same-size blocks get recycled at the same address, so the pointer comparison passes and the ink lands in whatever object currently occupies that address — intermittent crashes coupled to segment count and allocation cadence (rerunning one probe level 5 times gave 139/124/127 alternately). **Fix** — `draw_box_raster` calls `flush_pending()` **before** `blit` (ink lands while the offscreen bitmap is alive); the contract now stands in `enable_batching`'s doc and comment: **a batch target must outlive the next flush, and channels drawing into temporary bitmaps must flush before dropping them**. **Attribution method** (recorded because it beats reading code): patch `pt_set_batching` to force batching off, rebuild — all seven probe levels survive; restore — crash returns. One A/B settled attribution, no debugger needed. **Cost, not hidden**: the Windows offscreen+blit text channel therefore no longer benefits from batching and is back to per-segment BeginDraw/EndDraw (the pre-10× shape); capturing that 10× for real means drawing text straight into the window canvas, i.e. handing the Painter's origin and clip rect to the C side for clamping (`rx*/ry*` already clamp against the buffer, one more clamp against the clip is enough) — a separate performance batch; this one only restores correctness. Linux/mac are unaffected (their stubs never batched).
- **Follow-up batch · incremental active edge table (AET)** (second fill_polys rewrite, pixman-isomorphic): the GET (global edge table) is sorted by y_lo once; scanline advancement only does "deactivation compaction / edge activation (monotone pointer) / exact-precision x recompute + nearly-sorted insertion sort" per subsample — no more full edge rescan per subsample. **Two measured iron rules**: ① x must be **bit-identical** to the old crossing formula `ax + (bx-ax)×t` (store the original traversal-direction endpoints ax/ay/bx2/by2; incremental stepping drift, and mistakenly using bx2 as by2 in the t denominator, both flip boundary-pixel coverage quantization — caught by box_shadow/star/icon asserts in practice); ② a sub-1px span straddling two pixels (e.g., [10.6,11.4)) covers `[floor(xa), ceil(xb))`, not one pixel (star tips / thin rings caught it). **Diff-harness methodology**: extract the old algorithm from git into a temp wbtest, render identical shapes through both, pixel-diff (this round caught a whole triangle rendering zero ink = activation pointer indexing the unsorted array). Measured (paint_probe): 80-segment polyline 11→**4ms**, arcs 15→**2ms**, chart row 28→**17ms**; the icon full-scan crash was a debug print's cov OOB (not the AET). Known rendering change: under-coverage artifacts at self-intersecting-polygon (pentagram) inner-boundary pixels (old 239/207/159 dim seams) corrected to full coverage 255 — nonzero winding has nonzero on both sides of a wind 1↔2 boundary, so full coverage is correct. **Addendum (2026-10-14 evening)**: the AET batch carried the actual crash culprit — the y1 clamp mistakenly wrote `cx1` (clip right bound) instead of `cy1` (bottom bound); when a bitmap is wider than tall and geometry extends past the bottom edge, the row loop runs past the bitmap height and composite_span writes out of bounds (0xc0000409, caught by graph_wbtest, fixed 494fa72→728d0d5); the batch had initially mis-attributed this to the frontend session, and a git-worktree bisect (3be0d9b 189 green → e2c7c14 crash) corrected the record.
- **Follow-up batch · scanline engine, pixman-style** (fill_polys rewrite, 2026-10-14): ported four proven pixman/Cairo scanline patterns — ① **full-coverage runs set directly**: pixels whose four samples all fall inside a crossing span are set to 256 in one go (the old code evaluated all 16 samples per pixel inside polygons); ② **sampling only at span boundary pixels** (at most one per end, `add_pixel_samples`, capped at 256); ③ **composite only the inked range** (per-row ink_l/ink_r — usually ~90% of the bbox width is empty coverage); ④ `composite_span` gained a **direct-write fast path for fully-covered runs** under opaque solid + Normal (partial-coverage pixels expand to the identical formulas, bit-for-bit); ⑤ crossing sort switched to `sort_by` index sort (old insertion sort was O(n²): 160+ crossings × 4 subsamples × resort per row) plus **zero-allocation scratch arrays** (tuple push boxed once per crossing — measured 57k allocations/frame of GC pressure; scratch area + index sort bring it to zero). Measured (paint_probe): 80-segment polyline 18→**11ms**, arcs 15→**12ms**, chart row 39→**28ms**. The remaining structural item = incremental active edge table (edges walked once per row, x stepped incrementally, no per-subsample full edge rescan + sort) — a larger rewrite.
- **Follow-up batch · analytic stroke**: after adding stroke benchmarks to `paint_probe` — 60 card borders of 400×120 **stroke = 49ms/frame** (0.82ms each, the largest remaining item on card-heavy pages). `Raster::stroke_round_rect` analytic stroke: ring pixels partitioned uniquely by center (straight bands via row/column overlap with `[edge-hw, edge+hw]`, corner quadrants per-pixel `|dist-rr|≤hw` SDF, inner hole vanishes naturally when line width ≥ 2×radius), measured **49→6ms (8×)**; also adds a public `Painter::stroke_round_rect` API. Polylines (80 segments, 18ms) and arcs (3 14px rings, 15ms) remain generic — chart-primitive analytics queued as the next candidate batch.
- **Final measurement (native-app real machine, all five batches in)**: `frames=4421 paint=144299ms` — **full-frame paint 232ms→32.6ms (7.1×)**, max_frame 344→188ms; text is ~28% of paint (d2d 9.3ms/frame), the rest is chart vector paths and strokes. Layout 0.23ms/frame and present 0.5ms/frame are negligible.
- **Not done**: stroke_round_rect / chart vector paths (stroke_polys) still generic — chart pages and card borders are the remaining chunk; rounded corners under rotation or non-uniform scale (elliptical corners) still take the generic path; per-frame batching of DWrite's per-segment BeginDraw/EndDraw (next step for the 9.3ms/frame of text).

### Self-sustaining repaint loop: present and expose igniting each other (2026-10-13, real-machine feedback)

- **Symptom**: on real hardware, `examples/native-app` felt "laggy overall - scrolling, clicking and hovering all have 300-500 ms of latency", together with "the chart's push-point button does nothing, clicking a table header does not sort, and the virtual table will not scroll". In the code these look like three unrelated bugs; in fact it is **one root cause plus one example-side wiring gap**.
- **Root cause (identical shape in both branches)**: `wm_present` asked the system to redraw on every frame (`InvalidateRect(NULL,FALSE)` on `_WIN32`, `gtk_widget_queue_draw` on GTK), while the system's repaint callback (`WM_PAINT` / `wm_on_draw`) set `need_draw = 1` again - so MoonBit's `poll_event` returned `NeedsDraw`, `dirty` became true, a full frame was painted, `present` ran, and the cycle repeated: an **endless loop**. Two consequences: ① the app was **never idle** - `wm_wait` always returned immediately because a paint message was always queued, every tick repainted 1400x3520 ~ 4.9M pixels, and input could only be serviced after a whole frame, which is exactly the 300-500 ms latency; ② the mouse-move events accumulated during one frame (easily 100+ with a high-polling-rate mouse) filled the 64-slot event queue, and `wm_push`'s "drop when full" rule then **threw away the button-up and wheel events that followed** - that is the "button does nothing / header does not sort / wheel does not scroll". Note that all three symptoms hold **simultaneously within one frame**: the `Down` made it into the queue, the `Up` was dropped, the widget stayed in its pressed state, and the button simply looks broken.
- **Fix (both branches, kept symmetric)**: the repaint callback now only **blits the cached frame** and no longer requests a repaint (`WM_PAINT` sets `need_draw` only when there is no frame to blit yet; `wm_on_draw` likewise). The sole source of repaint requests is back to the MoonBit side's `schedule_paint` (`@core.invalidate` / `App::schedule_paint`), which is the stack's documented contract anyway: **paint only when content changed**. The first frame is unaffected - `wm_show` already sets `need_draw = 1` (`wm_mark_draw`).
- **The other half: coalescing consecutive moves in the queue.** In `wm_push`, if the last entry in the queue is also an **unconsumed** move, it is replaced by the new one (a pointer position is state, not a stream). Replacement only happens when the last entry is a move, so a Down/Up in between is never disturbed and FIFO semantics survive. This one must stay even with the loop fixed: any single frame (still on the order of a hundred milliseconds) can accumulate dozens of moves.
- **Window height 3520 -> 900 (example side)**: viewport culling (`widget_cull_skip`) paints only the part inside the clip, so **the window height directly determines the per-frame pixel count**; now that `enable_root_scroll` exists, the tall column whose only purpose was "show the whole page in one screen" is pure cost. It is now the `APP_WIN_H` constant - set it back to 3520 for a full-page view.
- **"Sorting does not work" is an example wiring gap, not a component bug**: a header click only flips the `TableSort` store (the component deliberately **does not sort for the caller** — that rule is documented on `TableSort`), and the example never subscribed to it to write the reordered rows back. A `@ui.sort_rows` reference implementation was added (**leading digits compared numerically first** — the demo data is mixed "12 处/6 处" style, where plain lexicographic order puts 12 before 6 and looks like nothing happened; plus a **stable** sort so blocks of equal keys do not shuffle), and the example wires it up in two or three lines.
- **Lesson**: "never idle" bugs show up on real hardware as **a pile of unrelated broken features**, not as a performance problem. Next time "clicking does nothing + lag + cannot scroll" appear together, check the **enqueue rate versus consume rate of the event queue** first, then look for a self-sustaining repaint loop — both silently drop events, and dropping leaves no log at all.
- **Verification**: `moon check --deny-warn` is clean for both the library module and the `examples` module (two injected-error probes confirmed the gate really covers those modules); `gui/win/stub.c` compiles standalone under MSVC (`cl /c /W4 /utf-8`) with a warning count byte-for-byte identical to before the change (only the 2 pre-existing C4996); `table_wbtest.mbt` gains 2 tests (sort rule + stability). **The real-machine behavior (whether latency really drops to "one frame", whether clicks stop being dropped) belongs to `_Windows真机测试清单.md` for re-verification.**

### Three long-red library tests on Windows closed out (2026-10-13, W9 / table-sort follow-up)

After the W9 and table-sort batches landed, the Windows local library suite carried 3 permanent reds (`moon test` as one combined run also sporadically times out on this machine; **run it package-by-package** to stay stable). Root causes and fixes:

- **`moon test` runs test processes with cwd = module root (`gui/`), regardless of the invocation directory** (probed via `yue_sys_getcwd`: `moon test gui/sys` from the repo root and `moon test sys` from `gui/` both report cwd `gui/`). So the repo-root-relative path `examples/showcase/assets/dot.gif` used by wbtests **never exists in tests**; the GIF decode case hit `None => assert_true(false)` permanently, and `ui_decode_guard()` could never find the image, so the ui GIF component assertions were silently skipping. Fix: tests now probe two candidates (`examples/...` and `../examples/...`, whichever decodes wins — `test_asset` in `image_wbtest`, `gif_asset` in `basic_wbtest`); the guard and the component tests now really run on Windows.
- **`Image::resize` only opened a Cairo session; Windows has no Cairo backend, so the whole frame came back empty** — upscaled pixels read `(0,0,0,0)`. `Cairo::over` returns `None` on backend-less platforms and the old implementation just gave up. Fix: route through `Painter::draw_image` (stretching blit implemented on both the Cairo and pure-raster backends), platform-free.
- **`compare_cells` only read a leading integer — not natural sort** — `"虚拟行 3"` starts with a non-digit and fell back to lexical order, putting `"虚拟行 12"` before it (a platform-independent real bug; Linux should have failed too — the case simply never met a green CI run since landing). Fix: rewritten as **natural order** (char-by-char; when both sides sit on a digit run, compare the whole run numerically; equal runs are treated as equal and continue; the string that runs out first sorts first); `leading_int` removed.
- **Per-tick animation cadence differs by platform (test contract)**: Windows (WIC) `img_anim_advance` is **one frame per call** (the component asks once per `delay_ms` beat; no internal clock); Linux (io-gif) anchors on a virtual clock, so frames advanced per beat differ. The `basic_wbtest` window "12 beats → 2..6 frames" was calibrated on Linux; replaced with the platform-neutral invariant "12 beats advance at least 2 frames and at most 12 (a guard against multi-frames-per-beat runaway)".
- **Verification**: all green on Windows, package-by-package — core 132, ui 125, render 43, text/theme/icons 41, sys/input/win/dbus 280, chart/mdview/web 233, **854/854**; `moon check` zero warnings. The combined run's sporadic SIGTERM timeout is a local-machine phenomenon; CI (Linux) and the per-package gate are unaffected.

## macOS (CI build chain verified, GUI pending real-machine)

- The libyue v0.15.6 release ships ARC / no-ARC dual libraries: Darwin link flags = main library + `-lyue_mbt_noarc` (no-ARC symbols are referenced by the main library, so it goes after) + frameworks AppKit / Carbon / IOKit / Security / WebKit / OpenDirectory + `-lobjc -lc++ -lpthread -lbsm -Wl,-dead_strip`; the prebuild Darwin branch is pre-configured accordingly.
- CI (macos runner) covers build + tests; headless runners have no WindowServer, so no GUI smoke.
- `#else` fallbacks in shim platform branches swallow macOS: borderless needs `#elif defined(OS_WIN)`; CurrentDirForDrag splits into three branches (mac uses `getcwd`); `Window::SetSkipTaskbar` / `SetIcon` / `App::SetID` have no macOS declarations — guard the calls as no-ops.
- **AppleClang 17 (after the macos-15 image update) parses the return of `getRed:green:blue:alpha:` as void**, making `![...]` a compile error; the value is guaranteed after the nil check and sRGB conversion, so discarding the return compiles under both BOOL/void parses (69136b7 — once lost to a full-tree rollback and picked back up; when a rollback baseline contains a sick file, later fixes vanish with it, so cross-check that file's history before re-pushing vendor).
- **Three root causes of the CI red streak before the 0.5.0 release (since 9-22; Linux/macOS red, Windows green)**: ① the AppleClang compile error above blocking prepare; ② the missing extern "C" (see the ABI section) blocking the link; ③ sysmonitor's S4 hardware-sampling test asserting "coretemp always has a Package sensor" — virtual-machine runners lack the hardware, so environmental gaps (no sensors / no DISPLAY) must skip, not assert. Also: the CI native-layer cache key must include the shim source hash (with only prepare.py in the key, a shim change keeps the old key and the restored build/ cache holds a stale shim archive); and with no Actions log access, slicing the failing output into `::error` annotations (the check-runs annotations API is anonymously readable) is the only forensics channel.

### ffmpeg CLI video decode route (whole frame-set read + offset slicing)

- Environment: Ubuntu 24.04, ffmpeg 6.1.1 + ffprobe (apt). Decision: mooncakes has no ffmpeg binding (an ABI surface +100 is not accepted), so video decoding goes through the ffmpeg CLI: `vidf_probe` uses ffprobe CSV (`-show_entries stream=... -of csv=p=0`), `vidf_extract` decodes into a single continuous frame file with `-f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgba` (the rawvideo muxer writes frames in order, so no image2 sequence is needed), then `read_binary_file` slurps it and slices by frame-number offset — frame data never travels through stdout (pr_run's stdout capture has text semantics, binary would corrupt it), so ffmpeg writes the file directly.
- Memory clamp: frame-set size = frames × width × height × 4; the defaults are fps=8 / max_frames=240; 480p at 12fps for 60 seconds would reach ~630MB, so long videos must be downsampled — stated in the doc.
- ffprobe CSV parsing traps: r_frame_rate is a fraction ("30000/1001"), and the format duration is a bare decimal line ("2.000000") with no label prefix — dispatch on the "video,/audio, prefixes and treat the remaining numeric lines as the duration"; the delimiter is a comma and fields carry no quotes (probe output contains no commas inside fields, so no escaping is handled).
- Full-chain real-machine verification: lavfi `testsrc` generated a 2-second 160x120@5 AVI (AVI chosen to match the requesting scenario's container), probe returned the right width/height/fps, extracting at 8fps gave 9 frames, and the first frame sliced to 76800 bytes; on the systemprobe board, clicking "载入演示视频" really rendered the testsrc colour bars (confirmed by an xdotool screenshot), and the status bar read "已载入 160x120 × 16 帧(@8fps,循环播放)".
- A/V sync: the audio track is extracted to WAV and handed to AudioEngine, each starting from 0 — approximate sync; exact sync needs a shared playback clock, deferred to a later batch.

### Media split into three layers (yue zero-ffmpeg / gui-media optional layer / ffmpeg-mbt FFI)

- Background: VideoPlayer once lived directly in yue and pulled in ffmpeg FFI — moon dependencies are declared at **module** level, so as soon as yue imports ffmpeg, every GUI-library user's build runs ffmpeg's prebuild (and fails without the dev package), infecting users who never touch video. Audio had gone through `CorvusCinereus/miniaudio` (a MoonBit dependency); after the user's 2026-10 decision "audio goes to ffmpeg too", audio was unified as well: yue core dropped AudioEngine/audio.mbt, and both audio and video now live in the optional layer.
- Three layers: ① yue core (zero ffmpeg, zero miniaudio, pure GUI); ② modules/ffmpeg-mbt (FFI bindings, zero yue, moon name `NoahLiu/ffmpeg-mbt` — the user's chosen name, ffmpeg training-data pollution is heavy enough that the bare name ffmpeg was not claimed); ③ modules/gui-media (VideoPlayer/AudioPlayer plus the player components, depending on the first two) — anyone who wants media playback imports this layer, and skipping it costs zero extra dependencies. Workspace members reference each other: the referenced module appears in the main moon.mod import list with a version number, and moon resolves the workspace member locally (no registry); **renaming inside the workspace** (ffmpeg → ffmpeg-mbt) needs three places in sync: moon.work members, the main and dependent moon.mod imports, and the `package` field of prebuild.py's link_configs (the package name is hard-coded there, and a missed rename reports "Link config package name ... does not start with module name").
- **"Video shows only the first frame" root cause**: the old playback clock only advanced a position Ref and nobody called the picture container's schedule_paint — GTK never repainted, so it stayed on frame 1. Fix: the component's 50ms clock calls vp_tick() (frame-by-frame decode over FFI) and ViewLike::schedule_paint(cv) as a pair.
- FFI streaming semantics: the playback clock decodes one frame per tick at the fps (decode_rgba is a sequential stream), and seek is timestamp-level (Demuxer::seek → avformat_seek_file + decoder flush); when the container has no duration metadata (lavfi AVI reports N/A) duration is 0 and the progress bar treats it as 0 (frames still play).
- Cross-package component infrastructure: yue's attach/themed_container/set_panel_bg/theme_border/theme_bg_panel were package-private; the yue-video component layer needs them, so these five were minimally made pub (the component-extension API).
- yue-side interface alignment: after VideoPlayer moved to yue-video, vpc_frame_image (RGBA→PNG→Image) replaced calling vid_frame_image directly; audio slicing/extraction kept the CLI single commands (audiof_extract_wav/audiof_supported), with FFI audio PCM direct output left for later.
- Real-machine verification: sustained synthetic X11 clicks (xdotool mousedown/up) kept being intercepted by XFCE's click-to-focus (motion events arrived, button events did not), so playback visual checks were left to real hardware; the logic layer is fully asserted in wbtest (make→play→vp_tick advances frames→seek clears and re-decodes→pause/stop→free). The demo board's video page auto-plays on load.

### Declarative root container height collapse (mount_window default flex)

- Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 + X11 + XFCE, the systemprobe example. Symptom: `mount_window([scroll(vbox(...))])` opened a blank window (background colour only, no content, process healthy).
- Root cause: mount_window's root container carried no styles, so the window's content area performed no flexible allocation; a Scroll's viewport height comes from flex allocation and collapses to 0 without a height constraint. showcase missed this because its outer layer happened to have an `hbox(style=[("flex", 1.0), ("alignItems", "stretch")])` wrapper.
- Fix: mount_window's root container defaults to `style=[("flex", 1.0)]` (a window root means "fill the window", so defaulting is safe; `mount()` targets a subtree under any parent container and is not defaulted, to avoid breaking existing layouts); scroll's doc comment gained a flexible-height warning; systemprobe's scroll also passes `("flex", 1.0)` explicitly (belt and braces, and scroll children that supply their own flex keep working).
- Verification: xdotool + import cropped the window region and measured pixel variance — pure background colour before, fully rendered after (title / button / radar chart visible); no regression in showcase/hello.

### Toolchain version upgrade (fork route dropped)

- Environment: this machine's toolchain had been switched to moonc v0.10.12+1634b282e (core 0.10.12) while moonsqlitefile 0.7/0.8 across the board and moonbitlang/async both require the v0.10.14 API (`Bytes::exact_view`, `eprintln`); CI pinned no version (install.sh installs the latest), so the drift broke the whole-repo build after a clean, hidden by stale `_build` caches.
- Decision evolution: moonsqlitefile 0.8.0 was vendored into `third_party/` as an emergency patch (exact_view rewritten as a byte slice); once the right answer was confirmed to be **upgrading the toolchain rather than forking around it** (forking an ecosystem package is a long-term maintenance debt taken only for an emergency), the official install.sh upgraded moon to v0.10.14, the third_party fork was withdrawn, prowk/moonsqlitefile@0.8.0 came back as the official dependency, and sysmonitor's four `String::exact_view` sites returned to the upstream form.
- Conclusion: a version gap is always solved by upgrading the toolchain (aligning with CI), never by forking an ecosystem package; third_party/ keeps only vendored code with genuinely no alternative.
- Verification: after moon clean, a full rebuild is warning-free at `moon check`, `moon test` 575 all green, `moon build` passes.

### ffmpeg dynamic-link FFI (workspace submodule modules/ffmpeg-mbt)

- Shape: `modules/ffmpeg-mbt` is a moon.work workspace member (module `NoahLiu/ffmpeg-mbt`), sitting beside the main module (yue does not import it, so the GUI library is never saddled with a system-library dependency; the main module declares it because examples use @ffmbt directly, and GUI library users are not infected). Dynamic linking, zero vendoring: pkg-config probes libav* (including libswresample for audio) at compile time and the system .so files load at run time.
- **Link propagation**: a library package's moon.pkg `link` section never reaches the final link (the old trap in AGENTS rule 2) — so, following the main repo's architecture, the submodule gets its own `prebuild.py` (moon.mod options --moonbit-unstable-prebuild) emitting `{"link_configs":[{"package":"NoahLiu/ffmpeg/src","link_flags":"-lavformat ..."}]}`, which propagates automatically to dependents' main packages; the `link` section was removed from moon.pkg. How to test: run `moon test src` inside the module directory (a full test from the workspace root also builds examples, where other people's unfinished code interferes).
- **Three FFI traps (located with gdb on the real machine)**: ① extern type declarations must be `#external` — without it the GC treats a raw pointer returned over FFI as a GC heap object and drop calls mi_free, segfaulting (crash stack moonbit_drop_object→mi_free); ② the C side never returns NULL on failure — a uniform dumb handle plus a vf_ok probe instead (NULL↔Option conversion semantics are not well defined); ③ intermediate raw values on the MoonBit side are wrapped into a struct field immediately before being passed (miniaudio's retention pattern). FFI pointer arguments each carry a `#borrow` annotation per the new toolchain's requirement.
- Demuxer shape (after audio merged in, 2026-10): open only opens the container and probes the streams (vstream/astream); the video and audio decoders are **opened explicitly on demand** (open_video_decoder RGBA/sws, open_audio_decoder s16 interleaved/swr) — audio-only files are no longer rejected (the old NoVideoStream straight-to-Err trap). On one Demuxer instance the video and audio decoders **share the AVFormatContext read cursor and eat each other's packets**, so video-with-audio scenarios require two Demuxers (one per open on the same file — exactly the VideoPlayer shape).
- Audio decode traps: ① vf_decode_pcm's EOF drain — after av_read_frame returns AVERROR_EOF you still call `avcodec_send_packet(NULL)` and keep receiving frames to drain the decoder's residue (an AAC tail ≈ 1 frame of samples), otherwise the tail is lost (measured: m4a 45056 frames vs wav 44100 — the difference is the encoder delay); ② after a seek, swr must be re-inited to drop the old position's resampling cache, otherwise you get leftover audio.
- Test assets are committed: src/testdata/ holds mp3/ogg/m4a/wav sine tones of 1 second each + a testsrc AVI + av_1s.mp4 with an audio track, generated with ffmpeg lavfi, under 120KB total — removing the "本机 trae 素材路径" dependency and making CI reproducible. **`moon test`'s cwd is each module directory** (in a workspace-wide test the path `src/testdata/...` resolves inside the ffmpeg-mbt package and fails inside gui-media), so cross-module asset references use `../ffmpeg-mbt/src/testdata/...`.
- Real-machine verification: PCM direct output for all four audio formats (cumulative frame count asserted within ±10% plus decoding continues after a seek) and video RGBA frame-by-frame / seek, all on committed assets, runnable in CI; the error path (missing file → OpenFailed) and version probing are self-contained.
- Runtime library versions: Ubuntu 24.04 = libavcodec60 (avformat 60.16); CI matching this host needs the dev packages installed via apt (see modules/ffmpeg-mbt/README).

### Audio across the full ffmpeg chain (miniaudio demoted to an embedded device layer)

- Trigger: the user's machine failed to load an MP3 with "音频加载失败: Invalid file" while the browser played it. A standalone C program linking the same miniaudio 0.11.25 directly decoded standard libmp3lame MP3s and system MP3s fine — miniaudio upstream is not broken; the `CorvusCinereus/miniaudio` MoonBit wrapper had dirty error semantics (load_sound reused engine->result to carry error codes, so after one load failure the engine's result stayed poisoned and every later load reported Invalid file), and its decoder set was only WAV/MP3/FLAC (OGG needs stb_vorbis, m4a/aac have none built in). The user decided: audio also goes to ffmpeg (every format, same stack as video, one source for both).
- Architecture: **ffmpeg decodes, miniaudio only owns the output device**. miniaudio.h (upstream single header 0.11.25) is vendored into `modules/gui-media/src/` and compiled as a native-stub alongside audio_stub.c — miniaudio drops from "a MoonBit dependency (mooncakes)" to "an internal implementation detail of the player", appearing in no moon.mod import, invisible to anyone not pulling in gui-media.
- Device-layer design (audio_stub.c): ma_device (playback, s16, channels/sample rate matching ffmpeg's decode output so there is no resampling) + a PCM chunk linked list under a mutex; the MoonBit layer's pump (50ms) pushes decode_pcm bytes into the queue (high-water 40KB ≈ 0.3s), the device callback thread drains and mixes, and volume is applied per sample inside the callback. Position = bytes consumed by the device (played_bytes) minus the base recorded at seek; natural end = demuxer EOF && queue empty. Seek = clear the queue + reposition both Demuxers + refill.
- **Degradation with no output device**: in headless/CI environments where ma_device_init fails, a dumb device handle is returned (has_device=0), pushes are silently dropped and the state machine proceeds as usual (the pump advances position by tick × 25ms) — so AudioPlayer's smoke run passes every assertion even with no device, with no environment-specific skip branches.
- AudioPlayer and VideoPlayer share this device layer; the components (audio_player_t/video_player_t) pump + refresh on a 50ms clock and stop after free via the closed flag.
- Traps: ① in the C data_callback, queued_bytes must be recounted after consuming a chunk (mixing half-consumed and whole-block decrements leaks); ② ma_device_init takes three arguments (context, cfg, device) — omitting context is a compile error; ③ `guard` is a MoonBit reserved word (the loop sentinel name collided: Parse error); ④ a custom Node's mount closure returns a View, not a Node (so the tail is `(row.mount)(parent)`); ⑤ after reloading, the old player was freed while its component's 50ms clock kept pumping a freed FFI handle (dangling) — free() sets closed and the clock checks is_closed and returns false to stop; for the same reason VideoPlayer::duration now uses a field cached at make (after free, the old clock's refresh once called demuxer.duration_s() and dereferenced a freed fmt).
- Real-machine verification: the AudioPlayer smoke ran a 1-second MP3 from play to natural end in 17 ticks (a real device consuming the queue, not the degraded path) plus seek / loop replay / error paths; VideoPlayer ran both routes (video frames + audio PCM queue) and the silent path with no audio track; the whole repo's 575 tests pass; systemprobe's smoke process stayed alive.

### Player component reload crash and the seek-debounce storm (2026-10, real machine)

- Symptom (user's machine): the video page crashed (segfault) after "选择本地视频", and the audio page froze after "选择本地音频". Reproduced locally (a GUI reproducer scripting the user's timing: reload a real 960x720 mp4 while the demo video plays): a deterministic segfault with the gdb stack frozen at `vf_seek_s → d->fmt->streams[...]`, a dangling pointer.
- Root cause (two layers stacked): ① slider_t's on_change fires for **programmatic Store.set** as well (subscriptions do not distinguish origin) — during playback the 50ms clock refreshes the progress bar every tick, each of which arms an 180ms seek-debounce timer (a seek storm: one redundant seek every ~230ms); ② on reload, vid_mount_player made the new player first (including a new device) and freed the old, while the old component's last debounce timer was still in flight and, 180ms later, called vf_seek_s on a freed demuxer — use-after-free. The trigger window is "the timer armed by the last programmatic refresh lands after the free", which reloading during demo playback always hits. The "freeze" is the other face of the same cause: running make() synchronously inside the FileDialog callback (a large file's dual-Demuxer find_stream_info plus device handshake, seconds) freezes the GTK main loop, which reads as a hang.
- Fix (three layers): ① the component's refresh wraps pos_store.set in a syncing suppression flag (programmatic refresh no longer triggers on_change or arms seek timers); ② a user_seeking flag — while the user drags plus during the debounce, refresh skips the progress bar (also fixing the bar bouncing back to the playhead mid-drag); ③ closed guards added at the head of the debounce closure and of every public mutating method on both players (play/pause/stop/seek/set_volume/set_looping) — after free they are all no-ops and stray closures never touch FFI; ④ the audio page's FileDialog now sets "载入中" and defers make by set_timeout(50) (the dialog closes first, the UI renders first, so the synchronous cost no longer stacks on the modal loop).
- Verification: the reproducer (100% segfault before) survived 3 rounds × 20 seconds after the fix; 575 tests pass; systemprobe smoke alive. Visual/interaction verification on real hardware belongs to the user.
- Click-free GUI reproduction method (the key technique this round): xdotool synthetic clicks are intercepted by XFCE's click-to-focus (see earlier), so for "it crashes only when the user clicks" problems, **script the user's timing with set_timeout** — arm timers in the real operation sequence (0.3s autostart the demo video → 4s reload a large local file mid-playback → 12s reload again), hitting the crash window deterministically with zero interaction; pair it with `import -window root` differential screenshots to confirm the picture is updating. For gdb stacks use `gdb -batch -ex "set environment DISPLAY :0.0" -ex "handle SIGSEGV stop nopass" -ex run -ex bt` against `_build/.../xxx.exe` directly (gdb may lose DISPLAY, so set it inside gdb; moon run is a wrapper process, so gdb must target the exe).
- Two dead ends worth recording: ① a yue application must call `@yue.initialize()` before creating any widget or window (Window::make inside mount_window depends on it too); omitting it in the reproducer segfaulted in `nu::View::View()` or printed `Gtk-ERROR: Can't create a GtkStyleContext without a display connection` — easily misread as an audio/video problem; ② `pgrep -f` matching `moon run` hits the moon parent process and fakes "process alive" — check the real exe process name or exit-code semantics; before gdb debugging, `touch` the source to force a rebuild so old artefacts cannot mislead.

### Video playback clock and duration on different axes (frame counting / hard-coded fps, 2026-10, real machine)

- Symptom (user's machine): "the video duration does not match" — the time text and progress bar drifted from the real length: videos above 12fps hit full scale long before the end (a 30fps video finished at pos = 2.5 × duration), those below never filled the bar; and the picture rate drifted with the real frame rate (decoding fixed at 20fps made a 30fps video play at 0.67×), while the audio device streamed in real time, so A/V error diverged as playback went on.
- Root cause: `vp_tick`'s playback clock was `frame_no / fps`, where fps is a make parameter (8 for the demo video, 12 for local files — all hard-coded by the caller) while duration is the container header's real seconds — **two time axes with different scales**, so dividing pos by duration is meaningless. The demo video was itself wrong: generated at `rate=5` but passed `fps=8`, so its 2-second clip stopped at 1.25s (62% of the bar). The built-in test asset happens to be 12fps and the test happens to pass 12, so green unit tests masked the problem entirely — **clock regressions must deliberately pass a wrong fps and assert that the time axis is unaffected**.
- Fix (wall clock + frame timestamps, on the same axis as duration): ffmpeg-mbt exposes frame-level information — `vf_decode_next` records the frame pts on success (`best_effort_timestamp` preferred, converted to seconds through the stream time base, read via `vf_frame_pts_s`; reset to -1 after a seek) and the stream's real rate `vf_stream_fps` (avg_frame_rate preferred, r_frame_rate as fallback); gui-media adds a monotonic wall clock `mbt_now_ms` (in audio_stub.c, CLOCK_MONOTONIC). VideoPlayer's clock is rewritten: play/seek record a base (position + wall clock), each tick computes `target = base + real elapsed`, decoding forward to the frame at that time (high-frame-rate videos skip frames to catch the clock, low-frame-rate pictures hold across ticks, catch-up capped at 8 frames/tick so a seek landing far from a keyframe never blocks the UI for a whole tick), and `pos = clamp(target, duration)` — always 1× speed, and at EOF the position is pinned to the duration (bar full). The fps parameter is demoted to **the fallback rate for streams without pts** (the stream's real rate wins). Bonus: the audio device consumes at sample rate and video advances on the wall clock, so the two rates are in the same scale by construction and the A/V gap drops from "diverging with the frame-rate ratio" to a constant.
- Verification: the regression test deliberately passes fps=5 (the asset is really 12fps) and asserts position still follows timestamps (wall clock wound back 500ms → pos=0.5; wound past the duration → EOF pins duration=1.0 and it stops); ffmpeg-side pts is non-negative and monotonic, the last frame sits near the container duration, and seek resets it to -1. 576 tests pass; systemprobe smoke alive. Real-machine interaction (progress / time display) is re-verified by the user.

### The audio progress bar "cannot be dragged" (current climbs from zero after a seek, 2026-10, real machine)

- Symptom (user's machine): dragging the audio progress bar halfway and releasing snapped it straight back to the start — which reads as "it cannot be dragged". The video page's bar behaved normally (the two components share the same syncing/user_seeking structure, so the difference sits in the player layer).
- Root cause: AudioPlayer's `current()` = seconds consumed by the device since played_base — **its semantics are "amount consumed", not "position on the media timeline"**. Seek only reset played_base (the consumption base) and pos still accumulated from 0, so after seek(0.3) current climbed from ~0 and the component's 50ms refresh set the bar back to vp_pct(current≈0) = the start. VideoPlayer's seek sets pos = target directly, which is why video was fine. The component-level user_seeking drag lock only covers "dragging + 180ms debounce"; once the debounce fires the seek, the lock releases and the next refresh yanks the bar back.
- Fix: AudioPlayer gained a position base `pos_base` (set to the target on seek, zeroed on stop / loop restart), and `current() = pos_base + seconds consumed since the base` (the dumb-device branch adds pos_base too, and the dumb-device EOF test in pump now uses current()) — back to media-timeline semantics, on the same axis as duration and the progress bar.
- Verification: the regression asserts current ≥ 0.29 after seek(0.3) and does not fall back over one pump tick (covering both branches: real device = 0.3 + consumption, dumb device = 0.3 + 0.025); 576 tests pass; systemprobe smoke alive. Drag feel on real hardware is re-verified by the user.
- Lesson: **a "position" field's semantics must be self-consistent across the whole seek/play/pause lifecycle** — when a consumption-counting clock (device bytes / frame counts) is converted into a position, seek must carry a position base, or the progress UI gets yanked back. Same family as the video-clock bug above: both are playback clocks detached from the media timeline, one off in rate, one off in origin.

### Video aspect distortion and失效 transparent colour (HEX byte order + decoder single-side size, 2026-10, real machine + probe evidence)

- Symptom (user's machine): "there is still no control-bar background — is transparency not supported?"; "the ratio is still wrong". The fullscreen/page letterbox maths had been fixed earlier and the user's re-test still failed.
- Root cause 1 (**transparency**): nu::Color's 8-digit HEX is **AARRGGBB order (alpha first)** — the library's own `argb_hex()` emits `#ffd46a6a`. Every component value was written with RRGGBBAA semantics (`#00000080` intended as 50% black), so AA=00 meant fully transparent and the control bar's translucent black plate, the slider's translucent track and the button hover overlays were all invisible; values like `#ffffffe6` were only visible because their first three digits happened to be read as AA=ff. **The dialog_t mask `#00000059` had the same wrong order (AA=00), so the dialog's dark scrim had always been transparent** (a pre-existing bug, fixed together).
