Probe evidence: `#80000000` 50% black, `#ff000000` opaque black, `#000000ff` fully invisible (leading 00 = transparent).
- Root cause 2 (**aspect**): the page called `VideoPlayer::make(width=480, height=0)`, and the C layer's `vf_open_video_decoder` used the source value directly for a 0 size, so a 16:9 video decoded to 480×1080 via sws (a tall frame squashed horizontally) — no letterbox maths could rescue it. Fix: when only one side is given, complete the other from the source aspect ratio (ffmpeg's `-1` semantics, both directions, minimum 1). Probe evidence: a 320x180 video passed width=480 decodes to `480x270` (480x180 before the fix).
- Locating method: a GUI probe × screenshot pixel sampling (`import -window` plus ImageMagick `pixel:p{x,y}`) × temporary DBG prints of the frame size inside the component; a 2×2/combined matrix probe isolating each factor (absolute positioning, the drawing method and the height source were all ruled out, and "even opaque black does not show" finally pinned it on colour parsing). Note that probe-window screenshot coordinates include the title-bar offset, and eyeballing cropped images is faster than point sampling.
- Dead ends: "absolute-positioned child containers do not render" was a false lead — the sample point simply fell outside the window; "the host's on_draw swallows child drawing" was suspected — the matrix proved absolute+on_draw renders normally, and everything reduced to the colour byte order.
- Verification: 576 tests pass; probe numbers prove it (frame 480x270 + the bar background measured at 50% black); systemprobe smoke alive. Final appearance on real hardware is re-verified by the user.
- Lesson: **the library convention for colour values is ARGB (AARRGGBB) — put alpha first when writing an 8-digit HEX**; any semi-transparent colour must be verified by real-machine/probe sampling, because fully transparent and semi-transparent are hard to tell apart on a dark background. Rewriting a decoder's output size (scaling) must preserve the aspect ratio — specifying one side implicitly means "complete the other proportionally".

### The dialog mask came out pure black (background-colour alpha clamped opaque by GTK, 2026-10, user real-machine report + local proof)

- Symptom (user's machine): dialog_t's scrim turned pure black and covered the content beneath — the expectation was 35% translucent black (`#59000000`).
- Root cause: the scrim colour goes through `ViewLike::set_background_color` → the shim passing `nu::Color(std::string)` straight → the GTK backend's `View::SetBackgroundColor`, which builds CSS from `Color::ToString()`. libyue's (upstream and fork alike) `ToString()` emits `rgba(r, g, b, a)` with **a as a 0-255 integer**, while GTK CSS rgba alpha accepts only 0..1 and clamps out-of-range to 1.0 — measured here with `gdk_rgba_parse`: `rgba(0,0,0,89)`→alpha=1.000, `rgba(0,0,0,128)`→1.000, `rgba(0,0,0,0.35)`→0.350. So every 8-digit hex carrying alpha renders opaque through the background-colour path on Linux. `6af827c` only fixed the byte order, and its "#80000000 = 50% black" probe conclusion came from the Painter fill path and does not hold for the background-colour path (on a dark background opaque black and 50% black are hard to tell apart — the source of the misjudgement).
- Fix: the scrim became an on_draw + Painter `set_fill_color("#59000000")` + `fill_rect` (the same Cairo path as the control bar, alpha working; consistent with hover_group's existing "visible backgrounds must be self-drawn" conclusion); the absolute container gained an explicit `height:"100%"`; the `set_background_color` call was deleted; `set_background_color`'s doc comment now says "#AARRGGBB, alpha not guaranteed to take effect — semi-transparent plates go through Painter". Whole-repo scan: the scrim was the only 8-digit alpha hex on the background-colour path; `with_alpha` outputs all flow through Painter and are fine.
- Verification: the probe example (white content + a permanent visible dialog_t) screenshotted on the real machine — three sample points inside the scrim all read `srgb(166,166,166)` = `#a6a6a6`, bit-for-bit the theoretical value of `#59000000` over `#ffffff` (255×(1−0x59/255)=166); `moon check` zero warnings + `moon test` 657 all green.
- Lesson: **semi-transparent plates always go through on_draw + Painter fills, never set_background_color** (libyue's Color→CSS rgba clamps a 0-255 alpha to opaque); a probe conclusion must name its render path — the Painter fill and the background-colour CSS path behave differently for the same value.

### Audio plays silent and only sounds while dragging the progress bar (has_device state test written backwards, 2026-10, real machine)

- Symptom (user's machine): audio output was silent throughout, with a brief sound (~0.4s) only at the moment the progress bar was dragged. The video page's audio track was normal.
- Root cause: the C layer's `mbt_adev_has_device` was written `started == 0 ? 1 : 0` — `started` is a three-valued state (-1 = init failed / dumb device, 0 = initialized stopped, 1 = playing), so **`play()` starting the device (started=1) immediately flipped "device present" to 0**, sending pump down the dumb-device degradation branch: decoded bytes dropped, the queue never fed, the device consumed nothing (silent while the state machine carried on). The sound while dragging came from `seek()`'s `ap_fill` — it never checks has_device and pushes straight to the real device (whose callback thread is alive once started), and the queue (~0.43s) drained with nobody refilling it: exactly "a brief sound". Video was unaffected because VideoPlayer's `vp_fill_audio` never consults has_device and always pushes directly.
- Locating method: **a real-cadence probe** — in wbtest, busy-wait on `mbt_now_ms` and print `started/has_device/queued/consumed/current` on every 50ms beat: the single line "after play started=1 has_device=0" settled it; with the fix the same probe shows queued ≈ high-water from t0 and consumed rising per tick (at 44100Hz exactly 0.05s per beat).
- Fix: `has_device` became `started >= 0` (stopped or playing both count as a real device; only init failure is a dumb one); the wbtest smoke moved to real cadence (25ms per beat, busy-waiting) and added a regression assertion "a playing real device must have PCM in flight" (auto-skipped in a device-less environment).
- Two deeper lessons: ① **a three-valued state flag's test must cover the whole range** (`==0` vs `>=0` differ by one character and read "playing" as "no device"); ② **a degradation branch that "works" masks the upstream test bug** — the dumb-device design turned the wrong verdict into silence rather than an error, and the old wbtest hammered pump calls, borrowing the misjudged dumb branch to fast-forward 0.025/tick and "finish playing" (the illusion of completing 1 second in 17 ticks), so the test depended on the bug; device-consumption timing must be tested at real cadence (waiting per beat), never hammered.
- Verification: the before/after probe comparison reproduces it; 576 tests pass (3 pre-existing environment failures); systemprobe smoke alive. Listening on real hardware is re-verified by the user.

### Floating control-bar alignment unified, and the final cause of the background not rendering (absolute content-grown height × host on_draw, 2026-10, probe-proven)

- Symptom (user's machine): on the control bar the play/pause, aspect/native and fullscreen buttons had different heights and did not line up; the progress slider and the loop checkbox were not vertically centred with the buttons; and after the earlier semi-transparent-black fix (6af827c changing to ARGB order) the background was **still** invisible.
- Alignment unified: all three buttons fixed at height 28 (the play button's built-in intrinsic height is larger, so it is pinned with `Button::make(style=[("height",28)])`; aspect 44x28, fullscreen 28x28); **slider_t carries a built-in marginBottom 10 and checkbox_t a 6, which push the controls above the row's midline** — callers pass `("marginBottom", 0)` in style to override (the base pushes first and the caller after, so it can be overridden), returning control to alignItems=center for true centring; the buttons' private marginLeft was dropped in favour of gap; the aspect label is measured with `get_bounds_for` and centred horizontally.
- **Final cause of the background not rendering**: the component's control bar is `absolute` + bottom/left/right **with no explicit height (grown by its content)**, and the host (the picture container) has its own on_draw (drawing video) — under this combination the bar's own on_draw fill is not rendered at all (child widgets still draw). An isolation matrix proved each factor: absolute positioning ✓, the drawing method ✓, the host on_draw ✓, content-grown height × host bg ✓ — only the "content-grown height × host on_draw" combination failed; giving the bar an explicit `height: 40` (28 controls + 12 padding) restored it immediately, and pixel sampling showed the bar area = video colour × 50% black exactly. The deeper mechanism (the GTK draw chain against yoga content-measurement timing) awaits source-level confirmation, so the empirical rule stands first: **an absolute child container with no explicit size must be given explicit width and height whenever its host installs a custom on_draw**.
- Dead ends: ① stdout pipe buffering — `timeout` killing the probe loses all println (a missing READY does not mean the program hung; only a natural exit flushes), and whether a window is mapped must be checked with `xwininfo -root -tree` against the real title; ② probe-window screenshot coordinates include the title-bar offset, so scan for the border before point sampling; ③ a change to get_bounds_for/alignment was once blamed for a hang — it was only the buffering illusion.
- Verification: probe pixel sampling showed the bar's translucent black darkening by exactly 50%; a close-up screenshot showed the whole row vertically centred; 576 tests pass; systemprobe smoke alive. Appearance on real hardware is re-verified by the user.

### Video player (FFI dual Demuxer: video frames + audio-track PCM direct)

- Components: VideoPlayer + video_player_t (play/pause/progress drag/volume/loop/time text). After the 2026-10 audio merge: the audio track is a second independent Demuxer over the same file (its read cursor does not interfere with video), vp_tick decodes to the wall-clock target and refills the audio queue to the high-water mark (clock semantics: see "Video playback clock and duration on different axes"); sound and picture each start from the play/seek point, giving a tens-of-milliseconds offset (exact sync needs the audio cursor read back, deferred).
- Floating control bar + fullscreen (2026-10, component layer only, zero platform code): the bar is `position:absolute` pinned to the picture's bottom (bottom/left/right 0, semi-transparent black via on_draw), the same absolute precedent as dialog_t/toast_layer; the controls are white-on-dark (label_t/checkbox_t/slider_t each gained optional color/bar_color/track_color parameters — empty means the theme colour, because white text on a dark scrim is a general need and was promoted into the component library). Show/hide is a **motion-wake state machine** — enter/mouse_move shows and arms a stillness timer, hiding after 1s of stillness or after leaving (a 250ms short delay, so the picture's leave arriving first while the pointer slides across the bar cannot flicker), **independent of playback state** (the first cut's "always shown when paused/not started" was rejected by real-machine testing: the demo video ends in the stopped state and the bar would never hide, which reads as "moving in and out does nothing"); dragging progress (user_seeking) postpones it; when the pointer is over the bar, GTK sends the picture a leave first, and the bar's own enter/move cover it. The picture draws a black plate plus two display modes (**aspect-fit letterbox / native 1:1 centred with overflow cropped**, toggled by the bar's "等比/原始" text button). Fullscreen is **a separate fullscreen window that self-draws the picture**: its root container (flex:1, geometry from the window's layout) attaches the same picture-drawing function and events (enter/move/leave/double-click/Esc), and the bar is re-parented there (absolute follows the fullscreen width); **re-parenting the picture container plus writing geometry with set_view_bounds is deliberately not done** — a direct write is overwritten by any later layout event (e.g. the relayout triggered by the bar showing/hiding), which is the root cause of the user's real-machine report "after going fullscreen the video did not enlarge and the ratio changed"; leaving geometry to the window's layout is what stays stable. Four exit paths: the bar's button / Esc (the root container set_focusable + focus + on_key_down VKEY_ESCAPE) / double-clicking the picture (a ClickTracker counting consecutive clicks, since libyue's MouseEvent has no click_count) / WM close (on_close returns the bar as a fallback); on reload, the tick's is_closed branch also closes the fullscreen window. Mutual recursion between event wiring and the fullscreen definition is bound through a `Ref[() -> Unit]` indirection (MoonBit local functions have no forward reference, and calling a Ref field needs `(x.val)()`). Show/hide, fullscreen and the two modes are re-verified by the user on real hardware.
- seek implementation: timestamp-level via avformat_seek_file (video/audio Demuxers seek separately + decoder flush + swr re-init), drag debounced at 180ms; the ffmpeg CLI slicing route is gone (the leftover CLI audio extraction file audio_extract.mbt was deleted — the media chain is CLI-free).
- When the audio track fails (no track / decoder unavailable / no device) playback continues silently rather than blocking video.
- Reload order must be "old player stop → free (closed set, the old refresh timers stop) → old root view `remove_child_view` → attach the new node"; any other order leaves leftover audio or timers, and correct order alone is not enough — after freeing the old player its in-flight timers (the seek debounce and others) still fire, so components must defend themselves with closed guards (see "Player component reload crash and the seek-debounce storm"). systemprobe's video page auto-loads 300ms after the first mount (make's synchronous cost); after the audio page moved to AudioPlayer: load plays immediately, the control bar audio_player_t attaches to a holder, a 200ms poll refreshes the is_playing label, and the demo asset became an MP3 (lavfi + libmp3lame).

### VideoPlayer replay state machine: play after end does nothing / replay after stop is silent (2026-10, whitebox regression)

- Symptom: after a video ends (EOF, non-looping), clicking play changed nothing — position pinned at the duration, picture on the last frame, audio queue empty; after stop, play did restart the picture but produced no sound at all.
- Root cause 1 (**play after end does nothing**): `vp_tick`'s EOF non-loop branch set state back to `VpIdle`, indistinguishable from the initial idle — `play()` treats VpIdle as "resume from the current position", and since pos=duration at the end, the target time always exceeds the duration while the demuxer already sits at EOF, so the first tick hit EOF again and stopped: the click did nothing.
- Root cause 2 (**replay after stop is silent**): `stop()` only seeked the video demuxer; **the audio demuxer is a separate container instance over the same file** (its read cursor is independent of video, see the section above) and stayed at EOF — so on replay, `vp_fill_audio`'s `decode_pcm` returned None at once, the queue stayed empty and output was silent. Every "back to the start" operation must seek both demuxers; missing one gives picture without sound.
- Fix: ① an explicit `VpEnded` state added (mirroring AudioPlayer's `ApEnded`), with EOF non-loop transitioning to VpEnded; `play()` on VpEnded first runs `vp_restart` (both demuxers seek(0) + pos/base_pts/frame_no zeroed + audio queue refilled) before starting; ② `stop()` now also seek(0)s the audio demuxer; ③ `seek()` moves VpEnded to VpPaused — dragging the bar after the end and pressing play resumes from the drop point rather than being misjudged as a replay (replay semantics belong only to "press play again while parked at the end").
- Design trade-off: **an explicit state rather than a `pos>=duration` heuristic** — during playback the target can exceed the duration before EOF, where pos is clamped to duration (a false positive for the heuristic, turning "paused at the end then play" into a replay back to 0), and with no duration header (duration=0) the heuristic fails outright; the explicit state is right in both cases.
- Verification: whitebox control — stashing video_player.mbt back to the pre-fix state and running `moon test -p gui-media` makes the two new cases fail precisely (is_playing after end→play; the audio track's decode_pcm after stop→play), and with the fix restored 11/11 pass; whole repo `moon check --deny-warn` warning-free and `moon test` 641 all green (5 new over the previous 636: loop EOF→vp_restart, end→play, seek at end→play, stop→play, volume clamping). Real-machine interaction (clicking play after the end, replay after stop) is re-verified by the user.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · pure-audio files rejected at the component layer, and the `_t` tail dropped (2026-10-16, user real-machine report)

- Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 + X11 + XFCE, `modules/gui-examples/audio` loading `assets/1.mp3`.
- Symptom: the right-hand red text read "打不开媒体：视频解码器打开失败：解码失败：无视频流" — not a single file would play in the audio example.
- Root cause (two layers; only the lower one had ever been fixed): the Demuxer layer stopped rejecting audio-only files back in the 2026-10 audio merge (`ffmpeg_wbtest.mbt` asserts it), but the **component** layer's player called `VideoPlayer::make` unconditionally, and that engine's clock is wall clock plus frame pts, so `open_video_decoder` returns `Err(DecodeFailed("无视频流"))` with no video stream. `AudioPlayer` (device-consumed-bytes clock) existed as an engine all along and was complete, with **no UI anywhere using it** — the example's header comment claiming "audio-only files go through it too, the engine detects the missing video track" described code that was never written.
- Why not fold audio-only into `VideoPlayer`: with no video stream, `vp_tick` gets `decode_rgba() -> None` on the first tick and reads that as EOF, flipping to `VpEnded`; making it audible means rebuilding a device clock inside the video engine — i.e. copying `AudioPlayer`. The two clocks are not on the same axis, so keeping them apart is right.
- Fix: ① new component `media/audio_player.mbt`; its control bar shares the same zone constants and hit judgements as the video one (`BAR_*` / `bar_hit` / `bar_speed_at`), and the per-frame keys become ±5 second jumps on the audio side (`ap_skip`: with an unknown duration clamp only the lower bound, otherwise `vp_clamp_t` sends any target back to 0); when an outer layout grows the component, the extra height goes to the stage area — the no-output-device degradation note is written there and the spectrum animation lands there too. ② `VideoPlayer::make` now returns an actionable message when it probes no video stream ("纯音频文件请用 audio") instead of letting the decoder report "no video stream". ③ The tick period became one constant, `ap_tick_ms` — the component comment said 50ms while the muted position approximation assumed 25ms, and one number must serve both or progress drifts where there is no output device.
- Naming: per the rename batch in `docs/zh/design.md` §2 the historical `_t` (themed-variant) tail is dropped and component names follow the Web elements — the player became `video`, the new one is `audio` (gui-media 0.1.0 was never published, so this breaks nobody); the shared `player_bar_hit`/`player_speed_at` became `bar_hit`/`bar_speed_at`. **Note that `audio_player_t`/`video_player_t` are names of the deleted old chain** (`modules/gui-media/src`) taking an engine instance, unrelated to this round; the historical entries in this file and in `system-capabilities.md` keep those names as they were.
- Verification: `moon test ./media` **25/25** (new `ap_skip` case), `modules/gui-media` and `modules/gui-examples` warning-free under `moon check --deny-warn`, both examples build for native; whole-repo `moon test` **1179/1179**. Does it sound, where -5s/+5s lands, how non-1x speed reads, and track switching are re-verified by the user.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · audio spectrum animation (pure MoonBit FFT, no C, no libavfilter, 2026-10-16)

- Shape: the tap sits in `ap_fill` **after resampling and before the push** — the engine exposes a `pcm_tap` callback that runs on the main thread in MoonBit and never in the device callback thread (rule 3, "no C-to-MoonBit callbacks", holds inside the component too). The sample ring keeps a 1024-point window plus 16384 frames of look-back, and painting looks back by `queued_frames` before computing — that pays back the ~0.23s the tap runs ahead of the ear (high-water 40000 bytes over 176400 B/s at 44.1kHz stereo s16). At non-1x speed the tapped stream is the resampled one, i.e. the same stream the ear gets.
- Why not ffmpeg: `showspectrum`/`ebur128` would first require a filter-graph surface in the bindings, costing far more C than it returns; a 1024-point radix-2 is about a hundred lines of MoonBit and negligible at 30fps — "if MoonBit can solve it, it does not go into C".
- Acceptance checks (all headless): the FFT itself is pinned with a DC input (only bin 0 carries energy, the rest below 1e-6); band mapping with 440Hz and 1000Hz sines (24 log bands over 40Hz..16kHz put 440Hz near band 9); stereo downmix equals the mono shape; feeding two windows and looking back one window still lights the same band.
- Toolchain pitfalls: ① **a record field holding a closure must be applied as `(self.tap)(...)`** — `self.tap(...)` parses as a method call and fails with `Type AudioPlayer has no method tap`; ② `String.trim()` yields a `StringView`, so anything wanting a `String` needs `.to_owned()` (same for `s[0:n]`); ③ when only the array contents change and the field is never reassigned, do not mark it `mut` — `unused_mut` is an error under `--deny-warn`.
- Verification: `moon test ./media` **33/33** (4 new spectrum cases), whole-repo `moon test` **1187/1187**, gui-media and gui-examples warning-free under `--deny-warn`, the audio example builds for native. Whether the bars keep up with the beat, whether it flickers after a seek, and the empty state in a device-less environment are re-verified by the user.

### MoonBit native GUI stack · player control surface: icon buttons, three zoom modes, fullscreen, window-level keys (2026-10-16, user real-machine report)

- Reported (by the user): the control bar was **drawn text glyphs** (`▶ ❚❚ |< >|`) — no hover, no focus ring, not in the Tab chain; the video component had **no zoom and no fullscreen** (the capability exists as `App::set_fullscreen`, but a widget cannot reach the window and nobody had wired it); neither player took keyboard input.
- The icon library is enough: `IconKind` in `gui/icons` has `video-play`/`video-pause`/`pause`, `d-arrow-left/right`, `full-screen`/`fullscreen-exit`, `zoom-in/zoom-out`, `sound`/`sound-fill`, `folder-open`/`file`; the self-drawn side paints them with `draw_icon(painter, kind, cx, cy, size, color)`.
- Shape: the bar splits into **real buttons on the left plus a self-drawn display region on the right** (`media/control_bar.mbt`, one implementation shared by both components). Play/pause and fullscreen are `ui.icon_button` (hover shade, pressed shade, focus ring, Tab reach all come from ui); speed and zoom are `ui.button(variant=Text)` showing the current gear — an icon cannot say "1.25x" or "fill". Gear readouts go through `Store` + `bind_node` remount (`Store::set` does not re-emit equal values, so refreshing per tick costs no rebuild).
- The old acceptance check was retired and rewritten: `bar_hit` used to split one drawn strip into six zones (play / frame step / speed / track / volume / time); it now covers only the display region's three zones (seek / volume / time text), and its coordinate becomes the display region's local x instead of the whole control's. The zone constants still live in exactly one place, read by both drawing and hit-testing.
- Zoom: `vp_fit_rect(vw, vh, rw, rh, mode)` is pure — fit takes the smaller ratio, fill the larger (the widget rectangle clips the overflow), 1:1 uses native pixels, all centred; headless assertions pin the three placements and the zero rectangle for illegal sizes.
- Fullscreen: the component reaches the window through `@core.host_active()` then `App::set_fullscreen` — that is the documented facade exit in `core/app.mbt` ("a widget cannot reach the window"), not a new back door. With no host (headless) it returns false and the local gear state stays put.
- Keys: the window-level fallthrough channel of the previous section — space play/pause, Enter fullscreen, `←`/`→` (audio ±5s, video frame step), `↑`/`↓` volume, `Esc` exits fullscreen (and is only taken while actually fullscreen). Liveness is judged by `watch.is_painted()`: the channel has no unregistration, so a removed player stops being drawn from the next frame and therefore stops eating keys.
- Dependency: `gui-media/media` therefore newly depends on `NoahLiu/native-gui/ui` (icon buttons need real widgets; redrawing a button set inside the media layer would be copying ui). The edge still points media → ui, ui knows nothing about media, so there is no cycle.
- Verification: `moon test ./media` **35/35** (three new `control_bar_wbtest.mbt` cases: display zones, the three zoom placements, gear labels; the old six-zone check retired with the shape), `moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, both examples build for native. Real-machine checklist: do the icon buttons show hover and a focus ring, does Tab reach the play key, does space pause without clicking the window first, do Enter/Esc enter and leave fullscreen, is the fill mode's left/right overflow clipped, is 1:1 centred.

### Store built-in dedup and `T : Eq` bounded impls (2026-10-13, frontend P3 step 0)

- Policy: `Store::set` / `Store::update` get `pub fn[T : Eq]` bounded implementations (same value: store without notify, via `Signal::set_eq`); `Signal::set` and the notifier are untouched, and `Store::signal()` still reaches `Signal::set` for forced delivery. Use `set_always` / `update_always` for unconditional re-notify.
- Pit ①: **a same-name bounded impl shadows the generic one** — calling `self.set(...)` from inside the unconstrained `Store::update` fails with `Type T does not implement Eq`, because the name resolves only to the bounded impl. Cross-constraint logic must call the low level directly (`sig.set_eq` / `sig.update`), not the public name.
- Pit ②: dedup requires **element Eq**: `Array[T]`'s Eq derives from `T : Eq`. Composite value types need `pub impl Eq for X with fn equal` plus `pub extend X with Eq::{not_equal, equal}` (without extend you get the `implicit_impl_as_method` deprecation warning, same precedent as W21c); Eq for 2-tuples already exists in core and redefining it reports "already defined".
- Pit ③: chart data windows (`Array[LineSeries]`, `TreeItem`, `GeoRect` and friends) have no Eq on their elements and comparing the whole window costs more than it saves — chart and examples use `set_always` throughout; 33 call sites were pinned one by one by the compiler.
- Verification: core 121/121 (new dedup regression: same value silent, changed value fires once, `set_always` forces, `update` follows the same policy); repo-wide `moon check --deny-warn` error- and warning-free; library tests 859/861 (the 2 reds are the pre-existing W9/sort baseline).

### Animation go/no-go: under pure software raster a transition is a full-window repaint per frame (2026-10-14, sets P5's schedule)

- Question: should P5 (`transition` = state-bucket property interpolation + frame driver) follow P4 immediately? The judgement cannot rest on feel, so a version was measured: `experiment/anim_cost_bench` (a typical page of 30 rows of "button + input + text", 1400×900, `page.paint` × 20 frames) reads on this machine `full=16ms/20 frames`, `relayout=0ms/20 frames`, a local 90×32 rounded fill `<1ms/frame`.
- **But this box is Linux, and the `Painter::new` probe picks the cairo backend** (see the backend selection in `render/painter.mbt`, `Cairo::over` preferred), so 0.8ms/frame is the **host-side submit cost handed to system cairo/X**, not the CPU raster cost. The real pure-raster price sits on the Windows/mac `PureBackend(Raster)` path (§6.6's performance-batch real-machine reading: a full-window frame takes 300–500ms, and per-tier timing is still pending; `text_bench` on Windows measures ~0.35ms per boxed text draw, and one full-window repaint pays layout + ink for **every on-screen text node**).
- Conclusion / policy: **animation is continuous dirty-repaint**. Before damage rects exist, a 150ms hover transition on Windows is about 9 full-window repaints — visibly stuttery, and it would undo the granularity promise that "typing repaints only that box". So **P5 moves behind §6.6's "damage-rect repaint + text layout cache"**, with the go gate stated as: a local change (hovering one button) must cost < 16ms per frame. P4's `opacity` / `box_shadow` are **static properties** (one frame suffices) and are not held by this gate — they shipped first.
- A toolchain pit found along the way: `local` is a **reserved word** (measured: `[0035] The word 'local' is reserved`), so `let local = ...` collides immediately; the probe variable was renamed `part`. When writing new code, treat words like `alias` / `abbrev` / `local` as reserved until probed (same source as §1.6's table).
- The real-machine number still needed (run by the user, one command): start `moon run examples/native-app` on this machine, quit, and read the `NATIVE-APP-PROF` line (layout / paint / present accumulated plus the longest frame, always-on via `core/prof.mbt`) — that decides "how much damage rects buy" and serves as P5's go gate.

### Declarative frontend P4: Painter global alpha and hard shadow (2026-10-13)

- Global alpha lives in the **facade state machine** (`PainterState.global_alpha`, save/restore with the stack): fills/strokes (gradient stops included) scale colour alpha in `apply_fill/apply_stroke`; text goes through `Painter::paint_color` (parse the string → multiply the factor → re-emit hex at draw time); images/canvases run `dim_bitmap` (per-pixel alpha scale) before the blit when `global_alpha < 1`. Both backends (cairo / pure raster) get full-path coverage with zero backend changes, because the facade is the only entry.
- Pit ①: **asserting on the wrong channel** — layering 50% red over an opaque target keeps the pixel alpha at 255 (alpha compositing changes colour, not coverage); `alpha == 0` style checks must run on a **transparent** target, and gradients must be compared `full.a` vs `0.25.a` on a blank bitmap.
- Pit ②: when `round_rect_path` called `begin_path` internally, the shadow's "outer ring + inner ring" two subpaths were wiped by the second call — the tracer split into `trace_round_rect` / `round_rect_path_ccw` (no new path), so a ring = one outer loop plus one reversed inner loop, and nonzero winding strokes only the annulus without overlap darkening.
- The `Style.opacity` channel: `apply` writes `Widget.alpha_paint`; the paint traversal sets `p.set_global_alpha(inherited × own)` on entering a widget and restores after its subtree (CSS-like box-tree accumulation). `box_shadow` currently ships the **hard** tier (offset rounded-rect rings, `layers` stroked at equal steps); the blur tier is re-evaluated once a blur capability exists.
- Verification: 3 new render tests (full-path factor / rounded rect / shadow ring), render 45/46 (1 red is the pre-existing W9 baseline); ui's `fill_round_rect` moved into the facade with zero behaviour change for ui/nav; repo-wide `moon check --deny-warn` error- and warning-free; library tests 880/882 (same 2 reds). Real-machine look (the opacity demo page / shadowed cards) belongs to `_人工测试清单.md`.

## Declarative frontend P2-e: frame-cost A/B and the idle-repaint gate for self-driving widgets (2026-10-14)

Real-hardware report: "page switching in showcase lags, section widgets render late". A controlled experiment came first (probe `experiment/showcase_cost_bench`: 14 pages × 120 text lines, 1835 drawn widgets, 20 full-page repaints, same machine and same tree, only the revision changes):

- **Readings**: `380610a` without the C-side text-layout cache = 9.9 / 11.95 ms per frame (warm/cold); `323b537` with it = 3.35 / 3.25; `HEAD` after the four P2-e batches = 3.4 / 3.35. So **the text cache made full-page repaint roughly 3× faster**, and **per-frame style-slot reads (P2-e) sit inside the noise** — they are not the lag. The cold variant (1680 distinct strings, above the cache's 1024 cap) did not regress to the no-cache level on the local Pango path, but the **"clear the whole table on overflow" policy has never been measured on Windows/DWrite** — the A/B harness is in place and the on-device ledger comes from `SHOWCASE-PROF` / `showcase-prof.txt`.
- **The gate reads "was I painted this frame"**: carousel rotation and gif advance ride the process-level `@core.set_timeout`, and previously they only checked `rotation.paused` — so a carousel whose **page is hidden still switched panels and called `invalidate()`, repainting the whole window for nothing**. The widget layer has **no reference to its parent** (parent↔child is a reference cycle the counting collector cannot break — see the split-layout batch), so "is some ancestor visible?" cannot be asked. Instead core keeps a process-level paint epoch: `bump_paint_epoch()` once per frame before the host's traversal (`App::paint_frame`), `paint_at` records it into `Widget.paint_epoch` only after the `visible` test and the viewport cull pass, and `Widget::is_painted()` answers "painted this frame". The self-driving callback becomes `if !w.is_painted() { re-arm only — no page switch, no dirty }`: hidden pages skip every wasted frame and resume on their own once visible again.
- **Related pit (order-sensitive tests)**: the epoch is **process-level** and shared by every test in the package. The pre-existing "fire a tick without painting" self-rotation tests passed by accident on `0 == 0`; once a new test bumps the epoch they turn falsely red. Rule: **a test that drives self-animation must paint one frame first** (same shape as the real host), otherwise the assertion measures an initial zero rather than "was painted".
- **Verification**: 1 new whitebox test (hide the block → fire a tick: no panel switch, the `invalidate` counter does not move; show it again → rotation continues), `moon test ui` 140/140, library-wide 872/872, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free; showcase prints `SHOWCASE-PROF` (frames / layout / paint / present / worst frame) at exit. If `frames` is still abnormally high, something else is spinning and that is the next check.

## Damage-rect narrowing: section/page switches did not repaint (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Environment**: `examples/showcase` walked on device after damage-rect repaint landed (frame bitmap reuse + painting clipped to the dirty region); the ledger is the `SHOWCASE-PROF` line printed at exit.
- **Symptom**: switching a section or a page left the screen unchanged — the new content only appeared once the pointer hovered some widget. `SHOWCASE-PROF` (615 frames / 1323 ms, 2.2 ms average, 134 ms worst) showed nothing wrong: frames were being produced, just a tiny patch.
- **Root cause**: `App.dirty_rect : Rect?` used `None` for **two different meanings** — "whole window is dirty" and "nothing is dirty yet". Within one batch, a whole-window request (`invalidate()` / `schedule_paint` / `host_repaint_all` all only write `dirty_rect = None`) could be followed by the pointer router marking the hover change through `mark_widget_rect`, whose shape is `Some(rect_union(dirty_rect, w.rect))`, and `rect_union(None, r) = r`. **The whole-window request was therefore narrowed to the small rectangle under the mouse**, so the frame repainted only that cell and kept the previous pixels everywhere else. "It refreshes when I hover" is exactly that narrowed rectangle covering the cell beneath the pointer.
- **Fix**: `App` gains `mut dirty_full : Bool`, set by every whole-window request (`schedule_paint`, `host_repaint_all`). Local marking now goes through the pure function `accept_widget_rect(full, cur, r)` — with `full` set it **holds the whole-window state instead of narrowing**; `paint_frame` takes the frame's clip through `dirty_clip(full, rect)` (whole-window → `None`, i.e. no clip) and resets the flag and the region together. The two decisions are pure functions so they can be pinned: the host `App` needs a real window, these judgements do not.
- **General policy**: an `Option` carrying "two different kinds of nothing" invites exactly this accident — when one `None` means "the whole window" and another means "empty set", any "union one more entry in" operation writes the strong meaning as the weak one. Either add a flag bit (this batch) or switch to an explicit sum (`Whole | Region(Rect)`).
- **Verification**: 1 new core regression on the pure helpers (without a whole-window request the rectangles still union; with one, a local mark must not become a small rectangle; the clip prefers whole-window), `moon test core` 133/133, all packages individually 882/882 (13 packages each green), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free. Device re-check (user): switch sections/pages in showcase **without moving the mouse** and the new page should appear immediately; re-run `moon run examples/showcase` and paste the exit `SHOWCASE-PROF` line (`frames` must not grow because of this change — whole-window semantics are only preserved within a batch that already asked for it).

## Windows-only `GUID` helpers sat outside the guard, so the library would not compile on non-Windows (2026-10-14)

- **Symptom**: `moon run examples/showcase` / `moon test ui` would not start, reporting `sys/sys_stub.c:2023:45: error: unknown type name 'GUID'` (the power-scheme code).
- **Root cause**: the two exported functions (`yue_sys_pp_current_guid`, `yue_sys_pp_set`) do have `#if defined(_WIN32)` branches ✓ in their bodies, but the two `static` helpers they share (`sys_pp_guid_string` / `sys_pp_parse_guid`) take `GUID` in their signatures and sit **outside every guard** — a `static` function still has to type-check even when never called, and on Linux/mac `windows.h` is not included.
- **Fix**: both helpers wrapped in `#if defined(_WIN32) ... #endif` (they are only called from the Windows branch, so Windows behaviour changes by nothing).
- **General rule**: in platform stubs, **as soon as a type comes from a platform header** (GUID / HINSTANCE / PangoLayout, …) the function must go wholesale into the guard — guarding only the body while leaving the signature outside does not count, and `static` helpers count the same. After adding C, run at least one compile on a *non-target* platform (`cd gui && moon check`) — that shows in one look whether the guard was missed.
- **Verification**: `moon check sys ui --deny-warn` passes, `moon build showcase --target native` links, library-wide 924/924.
- **Same trap, second time (2026-10-14 windowctl batch)**: the same rule hit a second time — `sys_win_find_ctx_t` / `sys_win_find` / `sys_win_find_cb` / `sys_mon_find_t` / `sys_mon_find_cb` / `sys_monitor_index` / `sys_win_enum_cb` / `sys_wcs_icontains`, a set of `static` helpers whose signatures carry `HWND` / `HMONITOR` / `BOOL CALLBACK`, again sat outside every guard, and `moon test sys` on Linux died with `sys_stub.c:2338: error: expected ‘=’, … before ‘sys_win_find_cb’`. The fix is the same: both blocks (the enum helpers, and find + title matching) wrapped in `#if defined(_WIN32)`; `sys_win_blob_t` / `sys_win_blob_append` / `sys_win_enum_ctx_t` only use stdlib and stay outside the guard.
- **Closing action (the precondition for it not recurring)**: whenever C is added for one platform, that same batch must run `cd gui && moon test <that package> --target native` **on the opposite platform** — exported functions never break, because their bodies carry an `#else` branch; only helpers outside the guard break, and only the opposite compiler sees them. Windows-only `sys` batches are therefore run on Linux, and `win` / `dbus` the other way round. Readings for this batch on Linux: `moon test sys` 182/182, library-wide 928/928, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and `cd examples && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links.
- **A third way of stepping on it (2026-10-14, platform batch 4, volume)**: the guard was drawn **too wide** — the whole section, including the two exported functions `yue_sys_vol_get` / `yue_sys_vol_write`, was wrapped in `#if defined(_WIN32)`, even though each of their bodies already carries its own `#else` route. On Linux this surfaces not as a type error but as a **link error** (`sys.whitebox_test.o: undefined reference to yue_sys_vol_write`), because the MoonBit-side declaration is still written while the C symbol is gone. One more rule: **exported function bodies always stay outside the guard** (they carry both branches); the guard wraps only platform-specific helpers, constants and GUID tables, and its `#endif` must close at the end of the helper block, never over an exported function. Readings for this batch on Linux: sys 185/185, library-wide 932/932, `moon build showcase --target native` links.

## Table hover lit only one cell, and "add a row" did nothing: damage covered only the deepest widget, and a dedup Store held the array it mutates (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom ①**: hovering a single-selection table lit only the cell under the pointer instead of the whole row (the user confirmed every table variant behaves this way).
- **Root cause ①**: not a painting problem — a headless probe showed that after `set_hover(cell.id)` the whole 440 px row is `fill_hover` from x=10 to x=400 ✓. What was wrong is the **damage region**: hover is parent-chain semantics (the same meaning as CSS `:hover`; `set_hover` flags the whole ancestor chain `hovered`), but after pointer routing the host marked only the "old/new hovered widget's" rect. The row paints a row-wide background while the repaint window was one cell, so it read as "only one cell lights up".
- **Fix ①**: `App::mark_state_chain(id)` marks dirty along the hit chain — the deepest widget is always marked, an ancestor only when **its own drawing changes with state**. "Changes with state" is recorded by `@style.apply` as `Widget.paints_state` (true when the style carries any of the `hover`/`active`/`focus` buckets); core does not know the style layer and only reads the boolean. With no state-changing ancestor on the chain the cost stays one cell rect — switching to chain marking never degrades back to whole-window.
- **Symptom ②**: showcase's "添加一行" button grew no rows.
- **Root cause ②**: Store's built-in dedup compares **by value** (`set_eq` when `T : Eq`), and the example stored the `lang_base` **array object itself** in the Store, then "add a row" did `lang_base.push(...)` in place and `table_rows.set(lang_base)` — old and new are the same object (whose content changed along with it), so they are necessarily equal ⇒ the notification is swallowed and the whole-table rebuild in the subscription never runs. Switching to `set(rows.copy())` is swallowed the same way, because the stored object already holds the new content.
- **Fix ②**: seed the store with a snapshot (`Store::new(lang_base.copy())`) so the stored value is not the object being mutated in place ⇒ after push, the new and old values really are comparable and the notification fires (the sort path benefits too: notify only when the order changes, skip when it does not — exactly what dedup is for).
- **General rules**: ① any parent-chain state (hover / press / focus) must extend the damage region to **ancestors that paint that state**, otherwise local repaints produce a half-updated frame; ② "mutate an array in place, then set the same array" is a dead end on a deduplicating Store — hand it a fresh snapshot each time, or call `set_always` deliberately.
- **Verification**: `moon test core` 136/136 with 1 new pin (a state-bucket ancestor merged into the dirty region → width ≥200; no state ancestor on the chain → dirty width ≤50.5), library-wide 922/922, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free (also deleting `App::mark_id_rect`, now unreferenced). Device check: hovering lights the whole row; "添加一行" appends a row and the read-along echo follows.

## The timeline connector came out broken: row gaps were left to `row_gap`, so no widget owned them (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: on showcase "数据展示 → 时间线" the vertical line between the three nodes was broken — a 12 px gap at every join.
- **Root cause**: each row's marker cell drew its line only inside its own box (`fill_rect(9, top, 2, bottom - top)`, with top/bottom clamped to the dot centre on the first/last rows), while the 12 px between rows came from the container's `row_gap` — **that band belongs to no widget**, so nobody painted it and the line broke at every gap.
- **Fix**: the row spacing is painted **inside the row** (a non-last marker and row box grow to `height + gap`; the last row carries no extra), and `timeline` no longer passes `row_gap`. The dot centre still comes from the content band (`cy = height / 2`), so dot positions and the first/last start-end are unchanged — each row just owns one more segment of line. Measured row heights after the fix: 68 / 68 / 56 at y = 0 / 68 / 136 (total height unchanged).
- **General rule**: anything that must run continuously across rows (connector lines, timeline spines, table separators, scrollbar tracks) cannot depend on container gaps — the gap is not a paintable unit. Either fold the spacing into the row (this batch) or have the container draw the continuous line itself.
- **Verification**: `moon test ui` 156/156 — the timeline case now asserts the broken-line row heights `(68, 68, 56)` and adds two **pixel checks that a line must exist inside the gaps** (`pixel(10,60)`, `pixel(10,130)`); control experiment: putting `row_gap` back with no in-row spacing turns it red on the spot at `(56,56,56) != (68,68,56)`. Library-wide 921/921, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free. Device check: the spine runs unbroken from the first dot to the last.

## Breadcrumb clicks did not navigate: "current item" was decided by position, not by the bound store (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: on showcase "导航组件 → 面包屑", clicking the last crumb ("基础组件") did nothing.
- **Root cause**: the component's own comment says "**the current item** is dark and not clickable", but the code decided it by position — `is_last` served both as "current" for the dark colour and as "not clickable" for the `on_click` guard. The demo passes a static three-item list `["数据展示", "导航组件", "基础组件"]` while the current page is the middle one ⇒ the last crumb was neither the current page nor clickable. The component logic was fine (non-last crumbs really write the Store); what was wrong is the **definition of "current"** — the navigation state is the only authority.
- **Fix**: clickability and colour both key off `selected.get() == mine`: the crumb equal to the navigation state is dark and does not change the value, every other crumb navigates directly (including the last one). The `/` separators stay non-clickable.
- **Test side**: the nav_wbtest case asserted "the last item does not change the value" — written against the wrong rule — and now asserts "the last item navigates too + the current item does not + separators do not"; the comment states that the title occupies a slot. Control experiment: putting the positional predicate back (`i < n - 1`) turns it red at `"列表" != "详情"`, reverting makes it green. The showcase section description was corrected too (it promised "no special highlight for the current item, clicking navigates directly", matching neither the old nor the new code).
- **General rule**: "which item is current" has exactly one source — the bound Store. Any positional stand-in (last/first) used in place of state shows up as a "looks clickable but never fires" dead corner as soon as the demo hierarchy differs from the real one.
- **Verification**: `moon test ui` 156/156, library-wide 921/921, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free. Device check: each of the three crumbs switches page, and only the one matching the current page stays inert.

## The time popup drew its title over the panel instead of occupying a slot (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: in the time picker popup the top "00:00" overlapped the first `[−] 时 [+]` row.
- **Root cause**: that time line is not a child widget — the panel's own `on_draw` painted it onto `(0, 0, w, 28)` as floating ink, while the steppers and buttons are real children laid out from the `top=10` padding ⇒ the first row landed at y=10..42, pressed under the 0..28 title. **Painting something "as a header" does not reserve a layout slot** — the same trap was already recorded for `md_marker` (a marker cell with no registered measure got height 0 and the number dropped onto the baseline).
- **Fix**: the title became a **child that occupies space** (height 28, width 100%), and the panel's `on_draw` keeps only the background and border; padding was completed on all four sides (it had only `top`/`left`, so the button row sat flush against the bottom edge). Measured after the fix, the popup children run `y=10 h=28` (title) → `38/32` → `70/32` → `102/28`, the panel is 140 tall, and neighbours never overlap.
- **Test side**: three existing cases indexed the popup as `panel.children()[0]` / `[2]` for the stepper row and button row; with the title now child 0 they shift by one and the comment states "the title is a space-occupying child". A new layout pin asserts: 4 children, the first is the 28-high title, consecutive children do not overlap, and the panel height contains the content.
- **Verification**: `moon test ui` 156/156, library-wide 921/921, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free. Device check: the popup's time sits on its own row, the two stepper rows and cancel/confirm follow in order with even padding all round.

## `stroke_rect` strokes inward while callers passed centered coordinates: the ring sat 1 px off to the bottom-right (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: in the colour picker each swatch's border looked displaced — a 1 px strip of fill survived on the left/top while the right/bottom edge was flush.
- **Root cause (measured pixel by pixel)**: the facade contract fixes `stroke_rect` as drawing **inside** the rectangle (both backends implement it that way: the cairo stub `cr_stroke_rect` and the pure raster `Raster::stroke_rect` both draw inward by `lw` and snap to pixels), yet **28 call sites used the Canvas/CSS centered-stroke habit** and passed `stroke_rect(0.5, 0.5, w - 1.0, h - 1.0)`. Under inner semantics that call puts the ring in `[0.5, 1.5]` — snapped to column 1 — while the right/bottom edges land on the last column ⇒ the whole ring shifts 1 px down-right. Probe reading (a 26×26 swatch, middle row): before `F B F…F B` (column 0 is fill), after `B F…F B` (columns 0 and 25 are border).
- **Conversion (centered → inner)**: `(x, y, w, h)` at line width `lw` becomes `(x - lw/2, y - lw/2, w + lw, h + lw)`. A 1 px outer ring is therefore `stroke_rect(0.0, 0.0, r.w, r.h)`; the focus ring inset by one pixel, `stroke_rect(1.5, 1.5, w - 3.0, h - 3.0)`, becomes `stroke_rect(1.0, 1.0, w - 2.0, h - 2.0)`.
- **Scope**: the ui family (overlay / datepicker / form / virtlist / table / nav / datetime / scroll / message_box / declarative) and the chart family (tooltip / boxplot / draw / treemap), plus two example sites (sysmonitor, showcase's events/canvas) — 28 sites in total. `fill_rect` / `clip_rect` are unaffected (they were always integer-box semantics).
- **One test followed the geometry**: the button focus-ring case in form_wbtest sampled column 1 — written against the offset geometry — and now samples column 0, with the comment stating "inner stroke, ring flush with the box edge". A new swatch symmetry pin (left column equals right column, top equals bottom, border differs from fill) turns any offset regression red.
- **Verification**: `moon test ui` 155/155, library-wide 920/920, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free. Device check (this machine, Linux/X11): every swatch border is equal on all four sides with no exposed fill, and the 1 px borders of buttons / inputs / panels / overlays line up on all edges.

## Text inputs could not take keyboard focus by default: the `focus_id=0` trap (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: on the showcase "表单组件" page an input could not be clicked into or typed in; that page was missing the EP-style clear ✕; the "数据输入" stepper's three cells looked uneven in height and did not join into one control.
- **Root cause ① (cannot click in)**: the host decides focusability as "the first non-zero `focus_id` on the hit path" (`Widget::focusable_at`), while `input` / `textarea` default `focus_id?` to **0** — without an explicit number the box is **permanently unfocusable**. Examples and users both had to remember to assign one, which plants "cannot type in an input" into every call site (probe: with no focus_id, `focus_id=0` and `focusable_at` returns `None`).
- **Fix ①**: text components now **auto-allocate** a focus number (`auto_focus_id`: when none was passed, count up from 1000000 so it never collides with hand-written small ids like 21/101; an explicit value still wins). Tab cycling follows registration order = mount order. `select` / `button` keep the original rule (their focusability is deliberately opt-in and involves overlay and activation-key semantics, out of scope for this batch). **Note**: a number alone was not enough — it still had to enter the host's focus stack, and at the time "whoever builds a widget registers its number" was a discipline that only held inside examples, so the form page still could not type; the hole is closed by 《Keyboard focus was dead everywhere》 at the end of this section.
- **Root cause ② (focus ring / caret never repaints)**: `App::mark_focus_rect` fed the **focus-stack id** straight into `mark_id_rect`, which looks widgets up by **instance id** (`root.by_id`) — two different id spaces: a miss falls back to a whole-window repaint (wasted), and an accidental hit marks **some other widget's** rect, so the newly focused box's ring and caret never repaint that frame.
- **Fix ②**: new `App::mark_focus_id_rect` looks the widget up through `find_by_focus_id` (whole-window fallback only when it truly is not in the tree); the one `mark_id_rect(id)` in the Down path switched over too.
- **`clearable` (the ✕)**: `input` gained the same-named parameter (off by default, like EP): with content and (hovered or focused) it paints a 14×14 ✕ at the right edge — a small background patch laid first so long text cannot collide with it; clicking it clears the whole box, writes back to the Store, and that press no longer positions the caret. Disabled and read-only boxes never paint it. Password fields get none (EP parity).
- **Stepper shares one frame**: the old `[-] value [+]` drew three independent borders (rounded ends, square middle), which read as three unjoined boxes — **measured, the three cells were already the same height** (both equal `control_height`); what looked uneven was the borders. Now the row container draws the frame once (background / border / radius / 1px from the style slot) and each cell paints only its own hover fill (inset 1px so the shared frame survives), its content glyph, and the separator on its inner edge. The group width is fixed at 108 and no longer stretches with its parent.
- **Verification**: `moon test ui` 154/154 with 3 new cases — an input with no focus_id is still hit by `focusable_at` and typing writes back to the Store (plus explicit ids winning and two auto ids differing); `clearable` changes pixels in the hot region on hover and clicking empties the Store; the stepper's three cells are equal-height, share edges head to tail, tapping +/- changes the value and a bound side stops changing it. Library-wide 918/918, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free. Device check: the form page accepts clicks and keystrokes, hovering shows the ✕ and clicking clears, and the stepper reads as one control.

## The frame-batching stubs got defined twice: Linux link failure (2026-10-14, reported by `moon run examples/showcase`)

- **Symptom**: `/usr/bin/ld: ... multiple definition of pt_flush` (plus `pt_flush_if_overlap` / `pt_set_batching`), the two definitions coming from `gui/build/libyue_text_pango.a(stub.o)` and `_build/native/debug/build/NoahLiu/native-gui/text/libtext-*.a(stub.o)` — two compilations of the same `stub.c`.
- **Root cause**: on Linux `gui/text/stub.c` is compiled **twice**: prebuild compiles it with `-DWM_STUB_PANGO` into `build/libyue_text_pango.a` (the real implementation), and moon's native-stub pass compiles it again without the macro because it cannot reach the pango headers — that second pass **must come out empty** (the comment at the end of the file states exactly that discipline: fall into no branch, become an empty translation unit, let the archive provide the real code). The three functions added by the frame-level text batch sat in an `#ifndef _WIN32` block **after** the outermost `#endif`, i.e. outside every branch ⇒ both compilations emitted a copy. Windows escaped via the `_WIN32` exclusion; Linux did not.
- **Fix**: the three functions moved into branches — one copy in the `WM_STUB_PANGO` branch (Pango paints and blends per run and never batches, so flushing is a no-op) and one in the `#elif !defined(__linux__)` branch (macOS placeholder); the real Windows implementation stays only in `dwrite_text.cpp`, and the Linux native-stub pass compiles to an empty TU again.
- **General rule**: when adding a cross-platform function to `gui/text/stub.c` (and to the same shape of platform stubs — `render`, `win`, anything organised as "one stub.c with branches + prebuild macros"), it must go **inside an existing branch** or open a new `#elif`; anything written after the outermost `#endif` double-defines against the prebuild archive. One-command judge: `nm --defined-only _build/native/debug/build/NoahLiu/native-gui/text/libtext-*.a | grep -c <symbol>` must print **0**.
- **Verification**: `moon build examples/showcase --target native` passes from both the workspace root and the `examples` module and produces `showcase.exe`; `nm` confirms 0 `pt_flush` definitions in the moon-side archive; `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, text+core+ui+render 360/360.

## Timers armed during page construction never fire: the charts page sat at "no data" (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: on showcase "图表 → 折线" both canvases stayed at "暂无数据" with the y axis pinned at 0..1, and the gauge did not move; ticking "暂停推点" made no difference either (this is the leftover half of the earlier "the push-point button does nothing" report).
- **Root cause**: `@core.set_timeout` uses a **process-level** delay channel installed by `App::new` (via `install_host_hooks`); with no host it is a **no-op returning 0** (the contract in `core/loop.mbt`). In the example `page_charts(app)` is an **argument** to `@ui.mount_window([...])`, so it is evaluated before the window exists — and "arm the first tick on the last line of the page function" therefore armed into the empty channel: the callback never ran and the self-rearming loop never started. The data path is fine: `series_push` uses `set_always` (bypassing Store dedup) and the canvas invalidates inside its subscription.
- **Fix (example-side rule)**: **arm the first tick from the mount callback** — `@ui.row([...charts...], handle=fn(_) { line_pump() })`. The two build-time `let _ = @core.set_timeout(...)` lines are deleted, and the on-page code snippet was rewritten too (otherwise the demo text keeps teaching the broken pattern). **[Correction 2026-10-15: this entry treated `view`'s `handle` as a mount callback — that is wrong; `handle` also runs at construction time, so this fix never took effect. See the next entry.]**
- **General rule**: anything that arms a timer inside a page/component constructor — and anything that stores `set_timeout`'s return value in order to cancel later — belongs after mount (or after the host App exists); a returned 0 is the signal "no host", so never keep 0 as a handle.
- **Same batch (visible in the same screenshot)**: the section description `@ui.text(s.desc, max_width=900.0)` had no `wrap=true`, so a long description was **one unwrapped 900 px line** whose tail was cut off wholesale (the broken word at the end of the line-chart description). It now wraps, so the section container is no longer stretched by a single long line.
- **Verification**: `cd examples && moon check showcase --deny-warn` warning-free, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, library-wide 915/915 with no regression. Device check (user): open the charts page — both line canvases should climb one point every 0.5 s with an adaptive y axis and the latest value annotated at the right end, 暂停推点 should freeze the curve and unchecking should resume it, and the left gauge should sweep at 2 Hz. **[Correction 2026-10-15: this re-check never actually passed — the pump chain was still dead and the fix was wrongly declared verified.]**

## `view`'s handle is not a mount callback: the charts pump chain was still dead after the "fix" (2026-10-15, Windows real-hardware report + local probe evidence)

- **Symptom**: after the previous entry's "arm the first tick from `handle`" fix and its write-up, the charts page still pushed no points; the real-hardware exit capture `showcase-prof.txt` contained not a single `CHART-DIAG` line (one per tick — a live chain must print), i.e. the self-rearming loop never started. The earlier "device check passed" claim was a misjudgement.
- **Root cause**: `node_of_new(finish)`'s `finish` is **eagerly executed at construction** (`gui/core/node.mbt`, equivalent to "new first, then configure"), and `view` (`ui/basic.mbt`) writes `handle(w)` inside `finish` ⇒ `handle` runs **while the tree is being built** — it is not a mount callback. Since `page_charts(app)` is an argument to `@ui.mount_window([...])` evaluated before the window exists, the `set_timeout` armed inside `handle` landed in the **empty channel** — the same trap as arming in the constructor, moved to a different place without changing the timing.
- **Evidence** (`experiment/timer_probe`, Windows dev machine, `moon run experiment/timer_probe`, readings written to `C:/tmp/timerprobe.log`): the probe arms its first tick from `@ui.col(..., handle=...)`; the log shows `ARMED pending=0` (the timer armed inside the "mount callback" never entered the queue), while a timer armed **after** `mount_window` returns shows `POST-ARM pending=1` and fires on time 400 ms later — the hook itself is fine, only the timing was broken.
- **Fix**: `core` gains `Node::on_mount(f)` — it wraps a Node and defers `f` to the **real mount moment** (after `mount_into` has attached the widget to its parent); the charts page's two first ticks moved from `handle=` to `@ui.row([...]).on_mount(fn() { pump() })`. The section body's lazy mount only calls `mount_into` when the section is first selected, by which time the host has long been ready. The on-page code snippet and the charts.mbt header comment were rewritten to the on_mount form; the CHART-DIAG diagnostic line was removed once it had produced readings.
- **General rule**: `view`/`row`/`col`'s `handle` is a **construction-time** callback (fine for layout tweaks and Store subscriptions that do not need a host); anything that needs the host (arming timers, reading a host handle) belongs in `Node::on_mount` or `mount_window`'s `handle(app)` (that one is genuinely after mount). `on_mount` runs on every mount — a one-shot startup callback relies on the caller mounting once (the lazy section mount is guarded by a `mounted` flag, so it holds).
- **Verification**: core gains 1 on_mount regression (not run at construction; on `mount_into` it runs after the widget is in its parent), `moon test core` 144/144; `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, `cd examples && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, showcase builds and links; library-wide regression per this round's readings. Device re-check goes to P42: line canvases climb a triangle wave one point every 0.5 s, "暂停推点" freezes and resumes it, the left gauge sweeps at 2 Hz.

## yoga-mbt left the line gaps out of free space, so a grow item ate them and pushed the row out of its container (2026-10-14, real-hardware report: the copy button is still clipped)

- **Symptom**: in a showcase section body the code row (left "代码" label + a growing spacer + the "复制" button on the right) had its button's right half clipped outside the window. That shape is used everywhere (`@ui.row([..., spacer, button], column_gap=...)`); elsewhere it only overflowed by a little margin, which nobody noticed.
- **Root cause**: in this port's §9.7 distribution, `initial_free`, the loop's `remaining`, the auto-margin `free` and justify-content's `free2` subtract only the sum of the children's outer frames — **never the line's total gap** `gap x (n-1)` — while the positioning pass adds `main_gap` per item ⇒ whenever an item grows, it over-grows by exactly `gap x (n-1)`.
- **Minimal acceptance check** (pinned in `modules/yoga-mbt/src/layout_wbtest.mbt`): row width 100, `column_gap=10`, children [fixed 30, grow 1] ⇒ the grow item must be 60; before the fix it came out 70 (whole row 110).
- **Fix**: compute `gap_total = main_gap x (line.length()-1)` before distributing the line and subtract it in all four free-space computations (spec: gaps occupy space and do not participate in grow/shrink).
- **Measured** (headless probe over the real page tree; window 1010, sidebar 180 → viewport 830): before, spacer=728 and the button at `x=962 w=50` → right edge 1012, past both the window (1010) and the scrollbar (1002); after, spacer=712 and the button at `x=946..996`, exactly on the row's right edge (content 802 + 14 padding per side).
- **Verification**: `moon test src` (yoga-mbt) 102/102 (including the new pin), library-wide 916/916, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free, `moon build examples/showcase --target native` passes. This is a third, independent problem — stacked with "the strip never wraps" and "viewport min 0" it produced the collapsed body plus half-clipped button seen on device.

## The section strip never wrapped: `Style` gains `flex_wrap` (2026-10-14)

- **Symptom**: in showcase the top section strip (segmented) overflows horizontally and gets clipped once a page has many sections, even though `shared/section.mbt` documents "wraps automatically when too wide".
- **Root cause**: this stack's `ui` never writes `flex_wrap`, and the style layer **had no such property** either (CSS has `flex-wrap`; our `Style` was missing it), so every container is `NoWrap` — the comment described a capability that does not exist.
- **Fix (added into the style layer per "property name = CSS property name", not as a component parameter)**: `Style` gets `flex_wrap : FlexWrap?` (the short type name imported in `types.mbt` via `pub using @yoga {type FlexWrap}`), the factory takes `flex_wrap=`, `merge` / `empty_style` / the setter follow, and `apply` routes it to `Node::set_flex_wrap`.
- **Two companions wrapping needs (the first device build shipped only `flex_wrap` and it squashed the body)**:
  1. **Put the strip in a column, not a row**: a row does not stretch its cross axis, so the wrapping container sized to its content (measured: given 450 of 1000 available) and the segments folded into six or seven lines. A column stretches children across by default ⇒ the strip gets the full width and folds only when it truly needs to.
  2. **Give the wrapping container — and every level of its parent chain — an explicit `min_height=0` (and `min_width=0` horizontally)**: per spec §4.5 a column child's `min-height:auto` resolves to its **min-content height**, and the min-content height of a wrapping row container is *all children stacked* (6 segments ×30 + 5 gaps = 200). That floor propagates up the chain — measured: strip 224 px, body down from 646 to 476. The engine is spec-correct, not buggy; explicit zeros are how a strip like this is meant to be written.
- **Final shape**: `strip = @ui.col([@ui.segmented(names, selected, class=[style(flex_wrap=Wrap, row_gap=4.0), style(min_height=0.0, min_width=0.0)])], padding=10.0, class=[style(min_height=0.0, min_width=0.0)])`.
- **Verification**: `moon test style` 26/26 with 1 new layout pin (a 100-wide row container with two 60-wide children: `NoWrap` keeps the second at `top=0`, `flex_wrap=Wrap` moves it to `top>=20`), plus 1 new yoga-mbt pin freezing the §4.5 floor and its escape (same tree: `min:auto` gives the strip height 200, explicit `min_height=0` gives 30). After the fix a headless probe over the real page tree (1200×700) measures: strip 54, body container 646, and on the code page viewport 652 vs content 808 (155 px scrollable) — the strip no longer eats height, and a definite viewport with taller content scrolls. `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, library-wide 915/915, yoga-mbt green.

## Scroll viewport was stretched by its own content, so nothing could scroll (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: in showcase a section body taller than the window had nothing to scroll with the wheel or the bar — the content was simply cut off at the bottom.
- **Root cause**: `scroll_view`'s viewport node never set `min-height`. Yoga flex children default to **min-size = auto** (as large as the content, never smaller than a screen's worth), so the viewport was pushed out to its own content's natural height — `view_h == content_h` and `max() = content_h - view_h` is always 0, so the wheel and the bar both conclude there is nothing to scroll. A call site writing `handle=fn(v){ v.node.set_flex_grow(1.0) }` only sets grow, which cannot override that default.
- **Controlled measurement** (headless probe: 20 rows × 20 px of content inside a 240×140 parent): before `viewport=676 content=676` (viewport equals content height); after `viewport=200 content=676` (viewport stays at the size the parent gives, content keeps its natural height).
- **Fix**: `scroll_view` writes `min_height=0` and `min_width=0` on its viewport (closed at the library level, so every call site benefits together: showcase's section bodies and sidebar, native-app, `virt_list` hosts). Call sites that pass an explicit `height=` are unaffected (an explicit size beats min).
- **Verification**: `moon test ui` 151/151 with 1 new pin — given only `flex_grow` and no height: viewport height ≤ parent height, `content_h=400`, `view_h=140`, `max()>200`, and after `scroll_by(60)` the content node really moves up; library-wide 914/914, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, examples module warning-free. Device check: showcase's section bodies and the long sidebar list should scroll with the wheel and drag with the bar.

## Markdown page, two defects: wrong range unit + rich lines that never wrap (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptoms** (showcase "代码文档 → Markdown" section): ① in mixed CJK/Latin paragraphs the bold / italic / inline-code / link runs came out as tofu boxes pressed on top of each other; ② the right edge was cut off wholesale; ③ the "复制" button on the code row was half outside the visible area; ④ the content area would not scroll vertically (a separate root cause found in the same batch — see the next entry).
- **Root cause ① (unit contract)**: `md_span_ranges` accumulated range endpoints in **UTF-16 code units**, while the `AttributedText` contract is **UTF-8 byte indices** (both the header note in `text/attributed.mbt` and the `tlen` handed to C by `rt()` are bytes; the Pango side uses `start_index/end_index` as byte indices directly, and the Windows/DWrite side converts through `ptw_widx`). One CJK character is 3 bytes but counts as 1 code unit ⇒ every range shifted forward and endpoints even cut inside characters (on device: tofu plus overlapping glyphs). Pure-ASCII paragraphs agree in both units, which is why these code paths always "looked right" in English samples.
- **Root cause ② (never wraps)**: `md_rich_label` used `wrap=false` and sized the node to the **natural width of the whole paragraph** (measured: one paragraph came out 656 px inside a `width=480` document). Consequence: the right edge is cut, and the section container is stretched past the viewport by that over-wide row — the 复制 button sits at the row's end, so half of it is clipped.
- **Fix ①**: `md_byte_len` (UTF-8 sequence length per code point) now produces the ranges; `md_span_ranges`'s doc comment and the file header both say "UTF-8 bytes".
- **Fix ②**: greedy wrapping at construction time — CJK and full-width punctuation break **per character** (Chinese has no spaces, so a break can only fall between characters), a Latin word plus its trailing space is one unit (never break inside a word), `\n` is a hard break, and a **single unit wider than the line** (long URLs) is hard-cut per character. One `AttributedText` per line; strike-through rules use that line's pixel ranges, and link hit-testing first picks the line by `y`, then the segment by the in-line pixel range. Wrap width derives from the container: `md_narrow(ctx, by)` shrinks it for list items (marker column / checkbox), blockquotes (the bar), footnote definitions and definition lists, while table cells get `max_w=ctx.width/columns`.
- **Toolchain reading**: MoonBit's `String.length()` returns the **UTF-16 code unit count** (`"甲乙"=2`, `"👍"=2`, `"abc"=3`) — neither bytes nor code points — and `String.sub(start=,end=)` is not byte-based either. So neither may serve as a length oracle for a byte-contracted API; byte length has to be computed per code point or via `@utf8.encode`.
- **Verification**: `moon test mdview` 31/31 with 4 new cases — byte readings (in `前👍中` the following bold run must land at `[10,16)`), every endpoint must fall on a character boundary, no descendant may be wider than the document width while the paragraph is clearly taller than one line, and a long URL must be hard-cut. **The judges were proven to bite**: restoring the old UTF-16 accumulation turns exactly those new checks red on the spot (`4 != 10`, "区间终点切进字符内部: 4"), and reverting makes them green. Library-wide 913/913, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, `cd examples && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free.
- **Still needs the device** (user): do the tofu / overlap disappear, does the right edge stop being cut, is the copy button whole? The "content area does not scroll" half was diagnosed separately (viewport stretched by its own content) — see the next entry.

## Visual fix: `badge_dot` now paints a real circle (2026-10-14)

- **Symptom / root cause**: `badge_dot` is documented and named as a round-dot badge but drew with `fill_rect` — the result is an 8×8 square. It was a boundary item recorded during frontend P2-e (that batch only moved the style channel, it did not change how anything is painted).
- **Fix**: it now calls `Painter::fill_round_rect` with a default radius of half the short side (an inscribed circle). A `border_radius` from `class` wins, clamped to no more than half the short side — so a square is still reachable with `border_radius=0.0`. The fill colour is still taken from the style slot (`color_of(s.background_color, "")`), so theme switches keep following.
- **Verification**: `moon test ui` 150/150 with 1 new pixel regression — at the 16×16 size the top-left cell has no ink while the centre does (the inscribed-circle criterion), and the `class=[style(border_radius=0.0)]` variant puts ink in that corner. On-device look (showcase's data-display page / native-app's dots) belongs to `_人工测试清单.md`.

## The GTK backend left the window-enhancement calls empty: "set title" and "borderless" did nothing (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: on the window page only "全屏切换" works; "改标题" and "无边框切换" do nothing at all, and "还原尺寸" shows no effect either.
- **Root cause (three, each different)**: ① set title / borderless — the **GTK branch of `gui/win/stub.c` still held the empty implementations left by W20e** (`wm_set_title` / `wm_set_borderless` were whole `(void)id;` blocks); the section comment at the time ruled them "internal business of the Linux backend, not on the roadmap", while the Win32 branch implemented both: the MoonBit facade call is harmless and nothing appears on screen. ② Restore size — `wm_window_set_size` **is a real implementation** on the GTK branch (`gtk_window_resize`), but the demo button hardcoded `set_size_pixels(1280, 720)`, which is exactly showcase's launch size: unless you drag-resize first there is nothing to observe — a missing acceptance check in the demo, not a backend gap. ③ Fullscreen — implemented on both branches, which is why it was the only one that "worked".
- **Fix**: ① the GTK branch gained `gtk_window_set_title` (with three guards: id out of range, `win->window == NULL`, `title == NULL`) and `gtk_window_set_decorated(on ? FALSE : TRUE)`; the remaining calls in that block — **icon / minimum size / self-drawn-titlebar drag region — stay empty on purpose**, with the reasons written into the section comment (a GdkPixbuf source is not of a HICON's kind; `geometry_hints` is not wired; `begin_move_drag` needs the pointer and button number at press, which this stack never sends down to the window layer), leaving nothing that merely "looks not obviously broken". ② The demo button became a two-step toggle 1280×720 ↔ 960×540 (renamed "尺寸切换", section copy updated) so every click has a visible result. ③ The MoonBit docs for `set_title` / `set_borderless` now **name each backend** (Win32 rewrites the style bits and recomputes the frame / GTK uses `set_decorated` / macOS still empty) instead of "empty implementation on non-Windows backends".
- **Verification**: window-level actions cannot be judged headlessly (they need a real window plus a window manager), so per rule 6 they go to real hardware. Gate readings for this batch: `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, library-wide 937/937, `cd examples && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links (gtk-3 is already on the link line).
- **Rule**: when a backend lacks a capability, **the demo must not ship the button** (this repo's precedent: "maximize/restore" and "always on top" are absent because the Win32 section never wrote them). An empty implementation may stay in the facade — the cross-platform shape is the same — but the demo and the docs must name which backend does not carry it.
