- **Pending real-hardware re-check** (user): "改标题" → the title bar becomes 组件库演示板 · 标题已改 (also proving the UTF-8 title path); "无边框切换" → the title bar and frame disappear, and a second click brings them back; "尺寸切换" → the two sizes visibly alternate; fullscreen behaves as before.

## Dragging the splitter handle did not follow the mouse: the delta was taken in the handle's own local coordinates, so each frame subtracted the previous frame's move (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: on the nested-layout page, dragging the `split` handle does not track the pointer — it snaps backwards mid-drag.
- **Root cause**: the drag delta in `splitter_impl` used the **handle's local coordinates** (`ev.x` is delivered by the host as `ev.x - w.rect.x`), while the handle itself slides as the first pane widens. Every frame's delta therefore lost the previous frame's handle displacement: `nw = first0 + (local pointer - local start)`, where the local pointer has already had the *new* handle origin subtracted. Measured (400 wide, ratio 0.5, starting at the handle centre): the first move (pointer +50) lands the handle at 250 and **looks right**; the second move (pointer +60 cumulative) sends it back to **210** — the correct value is 260. The further you drag, the more it snaps back, which is exactly the "won't follow / bounces back" feel.
- **Fix**: both the start and the move now use **window coordinates** (`ev.x + s.rect.x`), decoupling the delta from the handle's own slide. This stays exact even when a batch of events is drained before relayout: the local value is by construction "window minus that same rect.x", so adding the same rect back restores it. Clamping is unchanged (`min_first` / `min_second` still apply).
- **Verification**: new `gui/ui/split_wbtest.mbt` with two tests (this component had **no tests at all** before) — ① the initial `hit_test` must land on the handle, drag +50 → x0+50, drag a further +10 → x0+60 (the old code snaps back to 210 here), and after Up further moves change nothing; ② both minimum widths still clamp (the handle stops at `total - 8 - min_second` = 312). The tests drive the same path the host uses: `dispatch_pointer_to(handle_id, ...)` emulating the pointer-capture window — calling `dispatch_pointer` on the root carries no capture, so the second event hits a different pane instead (that is how the first draft of the test false-failed). **The judge's bite was proven by a control experiment**: replacing `win = at + origin` with `win = at` turns the second-move assertion red on the spot (measured 210). `moon test ui` 160/160.
- **The remaining half**: `@core.invalidate()` broadcasts to the whole window (`host_repaint_all` sets `dirty_full`), so one drag step costs one full-viewport repaint per tick — measured around a hundred milliseconds per frame in debug builds. That is the frame-cost item already listed under "known differences" (TODO §6.6), not a coordinate problem; re-check the feel after this fix before deciding whether it needs its own work.
- **Pending real-hardware re-check** (user): does the handle track the pointer now (fast back-and-forth drags without snap-back), do both minimum-width clamps still hold, and does it stop following after release.

## `alert(closable=true)` had a hit zone but no mark: an invisible hit zone is not a button (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom / root cause**: the `alert(..., closable=true)` `on_draw` painted only a light plate + a 3 px accent bar on the left + title/description; the `closable` branch **installed only a 24×24 hot zone at the top-right in `on_pointer` and not a single pixel of a mark**. The demo copy says "点我右侧的 ✕ 试试" while there is nothing on the right ⇒ reported on device as "the icon renders wrong". It has nothing to do with the icon-size batch (that one was glyphs drawn to 176% of the box and clipped); this one is a missing mark outright.
- **Fix**: mark and hot zone share one source and are both painted in `on_draw` — `@icons.draw_icon(p, @icons.IconKind::Close2, r.w - 12.0, 12.0, 6.0, main)`: the centre sits dead in the middle of the 24×24 hot zone with a glyph radius of 6 (ink ≈ 10.6 px, under the "s is the content radius" convention), coloured with the banner's main colour `main` (semantic colour tokens read live, so it follows theme switches). Naming note: the bare ✕ is `Close2` (its font_class is literally `close`); `CircleClose` / `CloseCircleFill` are the ringed variants — do not mix them.
- **Verification**: `moon test ui` 158/158 — the old "the close hot zone is only at the top-right" case grew into "both hot zone and mark are only at the top-right", adding two acceptance checks: inside the closable banner's top-right 24×24 there must be >8 pixels "different from the light plate", and a non-closable banner's same region must be ==0 (nothing extra may be drawn). Ink is filtered by "sum of the three-channel difference from the light plate > 30", the range avoids the left 3 px accent bar, and no concrete colour value is locked (so a theme switch cannot false-red). **The judge's bite was proven**: removing the `draw_icon` line turns the mark assertion red on the spot (`false` is not true), restoring it turns green. Library-wide 932/932, `cd examples && moon build showcase --target native` links. Whole-repo `--deny-warn` is still blocked by the 5 sys warnings from the parallel batch 60e094e (4 in `appfind.mbt`, 1 in `recent_files.mbt`) — files outside this batch.
- **Ruled out along the way**: the two "✕" in the demo copy are **U+2715 characters in the body text**, covered by both DejaVu Sans and WenQuanYi Micro Hei on this machine (`fc-list :charset=2715` lists them), not missing-glyph tofu; the three red boxes in the screenshot are the user's own annotations.
- **Pending real-hardware re-check** (user): on the feedback-component page, a closable banner should show a ✕ mark on its right, and clicking it collapses the whole row; the other, non-closable banners must show no mark.

## The hard shadow piled up into dark blobs at the four corners: neither backend has reverse arcs, so the "outer ring minus inner ring" trick never cut a hole (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: on the "过渡与效果" page, the `box_shadow=8` card shows a dark blob at each of its four corners while the four straight sides look like an even ring.
- **Root cause**: `Painter::box_shadow` built each band as "outer ring + reversed inner ring + fill with nonzero winding", with the inner ring traced by `round_rect_path_ccw`, which expressed the counter-clockwise direction by feeding **decreasing angles** to `arc`. But `arc`'s `ccw` parameter **does nothing on either backend** (`painter.mbt`'s own doc says so: `cairo_arc` normalises `ea < sa` into the long clockwise sweep, and the pure raster replicates that normalisation) — so every inner segment actually swept 270°, the inner boundary never landed where it should, the hole was never cut at the corners, and the stacked rings overlapped there into blobs. Offscreen image comparison (PNG read directly): a single layer already shows corner blobs, and more layers make the corners darker (16 layers gives solid black circles).
- **Fix**: draw **one stroke** instead — line width = `spread`, centreline pushed out by `spread/2`, which tiles exactly `[0, spread]`; each backend takes its own stroke path (a wide stroke is an existing `stroke_polys` capability in the raster backend, the same route every border uses). The `layers` parameter was dropped along the way: all layers share the same alpha and never overlap, so it only chopped one uniform band into N segments with no visual effect. The reverse-inner-ring helper `round_rect_path_ccw` was deleted with it (no references outside the package).
- **The other report on that page (font size never changes)**: not the transition's fault — the demo wrote `font_size` on the **container**'s `class`, while state buckets are computed per widget, so a parent block's hover never swaps a child's font size. It now lives on the text widget's own slot, and the text spans the whole block so a pointer anywhere inside hits the text itself.
- **Verification**: render's `box_shadow` regression now samples the **four corners at 45°** (one point per corner midway between the inner and outer boundaries — the old drawing either missed a patch there or piled it into a blob) plus "inside the body and far outside must be 0"; `moon test render ui` 206/206, library-wide 939/939, `--deny-warn` error- and warning-free under both `cd gui` and `cd examples`, `moon build showcase --target native` links, and the rendered comparison confirms the blobs are gone with an even density all round.
- **Rule**: **fills that need a reversed subpath (cutting a hole) do not hold on either backend of this stack** — `arc` only sweeps forward. Cutting a hole means polyline approximation (the chart donut is the precedent) or switching to a stroke; new drawing should prefer shapes that are independent of winding.
- **Pending real-hardware re-check** (user): the shadow card should show an even ring with no dark corners; hovering the 字号+底色 block should jump the font from 13 to 17 in **one step** (font size not interpolated) while the background still eases over 300 ms. **(The rule has since changed: after the 2026-10-15 user re-check, font size was asked to gradient too, so it joined the interpolation set and measurement now reads the same value — see "Font-size animation was not an animation"; the shadow item was re-checked in this same batch.)**

## The code "copy" button claimed success but nothing reached the clipboard: the message threw away the return value, and a cross-process judge was missing (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: clicking 复制 on a code block showed "代码已复制 ✓", yet Ctrl+V elsewhere produced nothing.
- **Root cause 1 (the reporting)**: `examples/showcase/shared/section.mbt` did `let _ = @sys.clipboard_set_text(...)` — **the Bool return value was discarded**, so success and failure printed the same line and the toast had nothing to do with reality. (The write path itself had already moved to GtkClipboard in the previous batch.)
- **Root cause 2 (missing acceptance check)**: the existing clipboard regression is an **in-process** write-then-read, which cannot prove "another program can read it" — on X11 the CLIPBOARD selection is answered by the owning process, so once that process exits and no clipboard manager lives in the session, outside readers get nothing. **A green in-process test can coexist with a broken cross-process path**, so this class of capability needs a second process as a witness.
- **New acceptance check**: `experiment/clipboard_probe` — it calls `@win.init_backend()` first (the same shape as a real graphical app: the GTK branch runs `gtk_init_check`), writes, then **stays alive for six seconds** while an external process reads back. Measured here (external reader: a separate python-gi process): `backend=true / available=true / set_ok=true`, the outside read returned all 100 characters including Chinese, curly quotes, a double backslash, a tab and the trailing marker, and `PROBE-AFTER-HOLD` matched the write exactly → **the Linux GtkClipboard write path holds across processes**, so what broke here was the reporting, not the write.
- **One correct behaviour not to chase as a bug**: in a plain command-line process (window backend never initialised) `clipboard_available()` is permanently false and the code falls back to the xclip command line; **xclip is not installed on this machine**, so such a process genuinely fails to write — that is degrade with an explicit `Unsupported`, not a defect. Reproducing in-app behaviour requires `init_backend` first, otherwise probe readings mislead (my first probe run read `available=false` and nearly sent me down the wrong path).
- **Fix**: the copy button now branches on the real result — success prints "代码已复制 ✓", failure prints "复制失败：剪贴板不可用" (Danger tier). The repo's other `let _ = clipboard_set_text` sits in `gui/ui/clipboard.mbt`'s kernel slot: the kernel's `copy()` has no reporting channel and the internal clipboard still backstops a failure, so it stays by design.
- **Verification**: `moon check clipboard_probe --deny-warn` warning-free, `cd examples && moon check --deny-warn` error- and warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links, no library changes (core+ui+sys re-run 486/486). The visible outcome (pasting in a browser) goes to real-hardware re-check per rule 6 (checklist S15).
- **Pending real-hardware re-check** (user): click 复制 on a code block, then Ctrl+V in a browser/editor — the same code should appear. If it now says "复制失败：剪贴板不可用", paste that sentence back to me: it would mean the in-app probe is not reaching GtkClipboard, a different root cause — but at least the two are now distinguishable.

## "Reveal in file manager" opened the folder but selected nothing: the two channels have to meet in core (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: on XFCE, pressing "在文件管理器显示 TODO.md" opened the folder in Thunar, but `TODO.md` was not selected.
- **Root cause**: the Linux branch of `@sys.reveal_in_file_manager` is simply `xdg-open <parent dir>`, and its own doc comment states "the bus channel's open-and-select arrives with the DBus line; for now everything falls back to opening the parent directory (selection lost)" — yet that half **already lives in `@dbus`** (`filemanager_available` / `show_items` / `file_uri`, all three present, with test coverage for the percent-encoding); **nobody had connected the two**. The layering is why they could not meet on their own: `@dbus` depends on `@sys`, so sys cannot import dbus back — the meeting point can only be core.
- **External measurement (this machine)**: `gdbus` answers `(true,)` for `NameHasOwner org.freedesktop.FileManager1` (Thunar registers it), and `thunar --help` has **no** `--select`-style switch — the bus is the only channel that can carry a selection, so falling back to `xdg-open` necessarily loses it.
- **Fix**: new `gui/core/reveal.mbt` with `@core.reveal_in_file_manager(path)`: on Linux, when FileManager1 is online it calls `show_items([reveal_uri(path, cwd)])`, and only when the name is absent or this call fails does it fall back to the `@sys` command-line path; Windows still goes through sys's direct `explorer /select`. The pure helper `reveal_uri(path, cwd)` is exposed separately so tests can pin it (the selection hinges on exactly this string: it must be absolutized plus percent-encoded). The sys doc now names itself as the fallback ("to get selection, use `@core`"), and both demo call sites (showcase's external section and systemprobe's reveal) call the core version.
- **Verification**: one new core URI regression (relative path absolutized, a space, Chinese — three segments) → `moon test core` 138/138, library-wide 939/939, `--deny-warn` error- and warning-free under both `cd gui` and `cd examples`, and `moon build showcase` / `moon build systemprobe` link. The visible outcome (the highlighted row in Thunar) goes to real-hardware re-check per rule 6 (checklist S14).
- **Rule**: **when two channels live in two layers, the meeting point must be the layer that sees both**, and the docs must name what the fallback loses (here: the selection). Otherwise the capability is fully present while the behaviour stays on the fallback path and simply looks "not implemented".
- **Pending real-hardware re-check** (user): from showcase's external section, revealing TODO.md should open the repository root with **TODO.md selected**; systemprobe's reveal (`/tmp`) should select `/tmp` itself.

## The Linux tray "never started": the demos gated tray creation on an icon handle (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: on Linux the tray icon never appeared in showcase / native-app; the in-page echo stayed at "建图标失败".
- **Root cause**: `wm_icon_from_bgra` is **a W20f failure stub on the GTK branch** (HICON is a Win32 concept; it always returns handle 0), so `@win.icon_from_bgra` yields `None` — and both demos wrapped the whole tray creation in `match icon_from_bgra(...) { Some(ic) => Tray::new(...)  None => note a failure }`, meaning **`Tray::new` was never reached on Linux**. The library is not the gap: the SNI backend never reads that handle (its icon comes from a panel theme-icon name or the library's built-in bitmap — see `Tray::set_icon_name` and `default_icon_pixmap` inside `Item::create`).
- **Evidence chain** (three independent legs): ① on the session bus, `gdbus` reports `NameHasOwner org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` as `(true,)` (the XFCE panel's notification area is up); ② the four pre-existing "real bus" SNI tests in `moon test dbus` (multi-item paths / menu routing, symmetric cleanup on unregister, disconnect self-heal) all pass on this machine, so the registration chain works; ③ reading `Tray::new`: whenever `sni_watcher_present()` is true it goes through `@dbus.Item::create`, independent of the `icon` argument.
- **Fix (demos only)**: the handle is now **passed through instead of used as a gate** — `let ic = icon_from_bgra(...)` then `Tray::new(id, icon=ic)` directly; on success the handle stays in the holder (a Win32 HICON must not be released while the tray lives), and it is freed only on failure (on Linux `ic` is `None` anyway, so both paths go through Option).
- **Rule**: **an optional, platform-specific input must not double as a capability switch** — handle-style resources may be permanently empty on another backend, and making them a precondition blocks that platform's entire path. This is the mirror image of "don't ship a button for a capability no backend has": here a button that should have been shown was hidden.
- **Verification**: `cd examples && moon check --deny-warn` error- and warning-free, `moon build showcase` and `moon build native-app` both link; no library changes (library-wide 938/938 re-tested, see the commit). The **visible outcome** on Linux (icon in the panel, left-click counter, right-click menu) goes to real-hardware re-check per rule 6 (checklist S13).
- **Pending real-hardware re-check** (user): open the "托盘" section of the system-integration page — the echo should read "已建（sni）" and an icon should appear in the XFCE notification area; left click should increment the counter, "挂菜单" should give a right-click menu, "改提示" should show the new tooltip on hover. If the icon still does not appear, paste the echo text — that would already be a different root cause.

## The periodic timer could not be stopped: the self-rearm dropped the new handle, so cancel hit an already-fired id (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: in the timer block of the system-integration page, the "1.5 秒后提示" one-shot worked and "起周期表(1s)" ticked, but pressing "停表" left the counter climbing.
- **Root cause**: the demo's periodic timer is **self-rearmed at the tail of the callback** (this stack's `timer` hands out one-shot handles), and the re-arm line read `let _ = a.timer(1000, tick.val)` — **the new handle was discarded**, while `tick_id` still held the very first one. That id had already been removed from the queue on the previous tick, so `cancel_timer(stale)` found nothing and cancelled nothing; the timer kept ringing. `Loop::cancel` is not at fault: it looks the id up and returns false when absent, which is the correct semantics.
- **Fix**: record the handle back on every re-arm (`tick_id.val = a.timer(1000, tick.val)`), and do the same for the tick that starts the table; the demo page's code sample now says "each re-arm must store the new handle, otherwise it cannot be stopped".
- **Rule**: one-shot handle + self-rearm means **the handle must be refreshed every tick**. Like the Store dedup rule, this is a constraint the shape itself carries, so it belongs in design.md §6 and in the component samples, not only in a commit message.
- **Verification**: `gui/core/loop_wbtest.mbt` gains a test pinning the semantics — after several ticks, ① cancelling the first (already-fired) id leaves the timer ringing and ② only cancelling the newest handle stops it (`hits` stops growing). `moon test core` 137/137, library-wide 938/938, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and `cd examples && moon check --deny-warn` error- and warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links.
- **Pending real-hardware re-check** (user): start the periodic timer → press stop → the counter should freeze immediately; pressing stop again should report "the table is not running"; restarting it should still be stoppable.

## Linux clipboard now goes through GtkClipboard — and that exposed a missing `moonbit_make_bytes` declaration truncating pointers in the win stub (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: on this machine (Ubuntu 24.04 / X11 / XFCE) the clipboard was reported unavailable — the read/write buttons on the system-integration page did nothing, and Ctrl+C/X/V in inputs never reached the system.
- **Root cause 1 (capability gap)**: the only Linux backend was the command line `xclip`, and **xclip is not installed here** (`which xclip` empty), so `clipboard_available()` was permanently false, `ui`'s `attach_system_clipboard` never installed a slot, and every facade read/write degraded to failure.
- **Fix 1**: the GTK branch of `win/stub.c` gains `wm_clipboard_available / get_text / set_text` (GtkClipboard), and the sys side externs straight into the win stub — **the same precedent as the file dialog's `wm_file_*`** (the MoonBit layer does not import the win package; prebuild ships the link line). Probe order is GTK then xclip; after `gtk_clipboard_set_text` the code also calls **`gtk_clipboard_store`** (registering ownership alone is not enough — without the store, other applications lose the content once we exit); the watcher's `cbw_get_text` follows the same route and thereby drops one subprocess per poll tick. Win32 and the placeholder branch provide identically named symbols (Windows' real path stays in `sys_stub.c`'s own CF_UNICODETEXT, untouched). The demo adds `@ui.use_system_clipboard(true)` (previously only native-app opted in).
- **Root cause 2 (ABI, shaken out by the first)**: **`win/stub.c` used `moonbit_make_bytes` without declaring it** — this file's GTK branch is compiled directly by prebuild, which never gets moon's `moonbit.h` include path (`compile_stub` only adds pkg-config cflags). An implicit declaration assumes an `int` return, so on x86-64 the returned pointer is cut to its low 32 bits. **Proven by disassembly**: with the declaration removed, `wm_clipboard_get_text` contains `mov %eax,%edi` (passing a 32-bit return value on as a 64-bit pointer argument), while this machine's heap addresses are of the magnitude `0x61bc76xxxxx` — truncated, i.e. garbage. Adding `extern void *moonbit_make_bytes(int size, int value);` (the same line `sys_stub.c:57` already has; matching `~/.moon/include/moonbit.h`'s `moonbit_bytes_t moonbit_make_bytes(int32_t, int)` bit for bit) leaves the TU with zero implicit-declaration warnings.
- **A pre-existing hazard fixed on the way**: `wm_file_dialog_get_result` (the Linux file-dialog result path) had been returning a truncated pointer all along — headless tests simply never reached it, because it takes a real file selection to trigger.
- **Control experiment**: declaration removed + forced relink → `moon test sys` dies with SIGSEGV; restored → 188/188. **Trap recorded**: changing only the C in a stub does **not** make moon relink the test executable (dirtiness is tracked per .mbt package), which is why the first control run falsely passed; `touch` some .mbt source (or delete the archive and dirty the package) for the comparison to count.
- **Readings and rule**: the GTK path really read this user's clipboard here (the watcher test printed `cbw_get_text: Ok (13 字符) …`). Note that `gdk_display_get_default()` returns non-NULL even in a test process that never ran gtk_init (GDK opens lazily from `$DISPLAY`), so the Linux probe is also true under headless tests — clipboard regressions must therefore be written as "if available, do a save → set → get → restore round trip and never pin the user's content" (`clipboard_wbtest.mbt` already is that shape, so swapping backends cannot false-red it).
- **Verification**: `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and `cd examples && moon check --deny-warn` error- and warning-free, library-wide 937/937, `moon build showcase --target native` links. The real-hardware checklist gains S11 (the system page's read/write buttons, and Ctrl+C/V in inputs interoperating with external apps).
- **Pending real-hardware re-check** (user): write from the system page → Ctrl+V in a browser/terminal should show the same Chinese text; the page's read button should pick up text copied elsewhere; Ctrl+C/X/V inside inputs should interoperate with the system; and after quitting the app the clipboard content should still be there (that is the `store` call).

## The section strip was squeezed flat by its own body: a fixed-height header needs flex_shrink=0 while the stretchable body needs min=0 (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom**: on the "代码文档" page, switching to the Markdown section made the segmented strip at the top collapse in height and its labels poke out of the band; the "代码高亮" section looked fine.
- **Root cause**: the page assembly is a column holding "strip + body column (`grow=1.0`)", and both sides were given `min=0` (the strip got it in the previous batch, for "wrap when too wide": the CSS §4.5 main-axis `min:auto` of a wrapping container equals its min-content height, which otherwise eats the whole body height). **Zeroing the minimum without locking the shrink** leaves the reverse channel open: the body column was *not* given `min=0`, so its min-content height is the entire body (the Markdown section is the full document, on the order of 2000 px), the window is only 720, and once the parent column overflows yoga puts **all of the shrink onto the only freely-shrinkable layer — the strip** (it has min=0, while yoga-mbt defaults `flex_shrink` to **1.0**, `modules/yoga-mbt/src/style.mbt:53`). Sections with short bodies never trigger it, which is why it looked like switching tabs caused it.
- **Headless repro readings** (temporary probe in `gui/ui`, structure identical to the assembly: root 300 tall, strip 24 + 10 padding, body 2000): the strip measured **23.32** (natural height 44, so the 24 label sticks straight out); after "strip `set_flex_shrink(0.0)` + body column `min=0`" it measured **44**. The probe was deleted once run; the fix landed in `examples/showcase/shared/section.mbt`.
- **Rule**: in a column with "fixed header + stretchable body" the two things must be locked separately — **header: shrink off** (`flex_shrink=0`), **body: shrink allowed** (`min_height=0` + `grow`), and let the `scroll_view` inside the body absorb the overflow. `min=0` alone is a necessary condition, not a sufficient one: it lets a container wrap and, at the same time, makes it the only layer that can absorb shrink.
- **This stack's boundary**: the `Style` field set has `flex` (=grow) but no `flex_shrink`, so locking the header's shrink goes through `handle=` with `w.node.set_flex_shrink(0.0)` (the same route as `scroll_view`'s content column). Whether to add `flex_shrink` to the style factory is tracked separately (see design.md §6).
- **Verification**: `cd examples && moon build showcase --target native` passes; this batch touches only the demo assembly, no library changes. The repo-wide `--deny-warn` gate is still blocked by 5 sys warnings from the parallel batch 60e094e (4 in `gui/sys/appfind.mbt`, 1 in `recent_files.mbt`), files outside this batch.
- **Pending real-hardware re-check** (user): after switching to the Markdown section the strip should keep its fixed height (labels no longer poking out), the strip should still wrap in a narrow window, in-section scrolling should be unchanged; also click through the other 14 pages and see whether any other fixed-height band gets squeezed.

## A thousand scatter points merged into a solid band: dot diameter must respect "dot area × point count ≤ plot area" (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom / root cause**: `scatter_t` defaulted to `dot=6.0` and painted opaque `fill_rect` squares. The demo page pushes 2000 points into a 320×260 chart (plot area 260×224), so the dots' total area, 2000×36 = 72000 px², was already 1.24× the plot area — **the default dot diameter and the point-count magnitude simply did not match**. Neighbouring points bit into each other and the whole correlation band was daubed into one solid mass with no readable distribution shape. Squares also eat the π/4 of visual whitespace, leaving not even a seam in dense regions.
- **Fix**: ① the default `dot` drops to **3.0**, and the rule is written into the component docs (dot area × point count ≤ plot area; pass a larger diameter explicitly); ② the drawing becomes `Painter::fill_round_rect` (radius = half the short side) = **a dot**, which leaves gaps between points by construction; ③ the point layer is wrapped in `set_global_alpha(0.7)` (inside `save()`/`restore()`, restoring as usual), so overlaps darken by accumulation instead of plastering solid, and sparse areas still show the grid. The trend line and grid are unaffected (drawn before the alpha change).
- **Measured readings** (offscreen `Painter::new(Bitmap)` session; the point mask filters on "closer to the dot colour than to the panel colour", which excludes grid lines and ticks by construction): a single `dot=15` point inks a 14×14 bounding box whose four corners stay clean and whose centre is inked (old code: 15×15 with **all four corners inked** = a square); at 2000 points on the default, pixels at the pure dot colour number 201 (old code: 20189 = 35% of the 58240-px plot area, i.e. solid). Both checks are now regression tests in `moon test chart`.
- **Toolchain readings** (moon 0.1.20260920): ① the demo's LCG cannot use `% 2147483647` to get a positive remainder — **MoonBit's `%` takes the sign of the dividend**, and once `seed * 1103515245` overflows int64 and wraps negative the remainder is negative, so the scatter spread onto the negative half-axis (real-machine reading: the axes became -100..100 while the comment said 0..100). Masking the low bits with `& 0x7fff_ffff` removes overflow and sign in one step. ② In a multi-line expression **an operator may not start a new line**: `a + b
< c` fails outright with `[3002]`/`[4139]`; the comparison has to move into an intermediate `let`.
- **Verification**: `moon test chart` 190/190 (one new two-judge regression). **The judges' bite was proven by a control experiment**: restoring the old painting path and default dot size (`fill_rect` + `dot=6.0`) makes the corner judge true and the pure-colour count 20189, above the bound; reverting turns green. Library-wide 931/931, `cd examples && moon build showcase --target native` links. The repo-wide `--deny-warn` gate is currently blocked by 5 warnings from the parallel batch (60e094e, sys platform batch 3: a duplicated `#borrow` in `gui/sys/appfind.mbt`, an unused `ffi_file_mtime`, two deprecated string-slice spellings); those files are not touched here.
- **Pending real-hardware re-check** (user): both scatter panels should read as "a cloud of points" rather than a solid band, the trend line should stay legible, and the small panel in `native-app` (250×130) should not regress.

## Icon glyphs were drawn at 176% of their box and then clipped: the content-radius contract belongs in the component layer (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Symptom / root cause**: parameter 5 of `@icons.draw_icon` has always been a **content radius** (ink ≈ 1.76×s, since the path data is normalized to ±1000 and scaled by `s*0.88/1000`), but `@ui.icon` and `@ui.icon_button` passed the **box edge length** as that radius (`size` / `icon_size`), so glyphs were drawn at 176% of the box's short side — and the host clips each widget to its rect, cutting a large piece off all four edges. Offscreen pixel probe (ink bounding box measured directly on a `Painter::new(Bitmap)` session): `icon(size=24)` reported a 24×24 box that the glyph **filled exactly** (unclipped it would be 44×44 — calling `draw_icon(...,24.0,...)` directly reads `10,10-53,53`), and `icon_button(box_size=28, icon_size=16)` likewise filled its 28 box. That is the reported "glyphs burst out of their container, edges sliced, content and container out of agreement". The library's three other direct call sites already used the radius convention and are unaffected: `message_box` (24 box passing 11), the `overlay` snackbar (passing 7), `nav` sidebar items (passing 6.72).
- **Fix**: `@ui.icon` now derives the radius from the **live rect** (`r.w.min(r.h) / 2.0`), so the glyph keeps following the box even when `class` overrides width/height and never overflows; `icon_button` passes `icon_size / 2.0`, keeping the button box (`box_size`) and the glyph box (`icon_size`) as separate concerns — the default 28/16 pair inks ≈16 px with more than 6 px of margin inside. The doc comments on `draw_icon` and `icon` state the contract at the entry point ("s is the content radius = half the box edge", "the glyph is centred with 88% optical margin of the short side"). Nothing was needed on the data side: all 803 paths were scanned, every one fills the ±1000 space and its geometric centre is off by at most 60 fixed-point units (≈3% of the box), so no entry is lopsided or under-sized.
- **Toolchain readings** (moon 0.1.20260920): `println` takes exactly one `String` (more arguments give `[4015]`); `debug_printline` has no matching overload for mixed "4 Int + 2 Double" payloads (`%g` is not accepted either, `[4021]`) — multi-value diagnostics go through string concatenation.
- **Verification**: `moon test ui` 158/158 with one new pixel regression — `icon(size=24)` must ink inside `[1,1]-[22,22]` with equal horizontal/vertical centres (measured `1,1-22,22`), and `icon_button(box_size=28, icon_size=16)` inside `[5,5]-[22,22]` with a width of 10..17 (measured `6,6-21,21`). **The judge's bite was proven by a control experiment**: restoring the old arguments (passing `size` / `icon_size` directly) turned it red on the spot (`a.0=0`, `b.0=0`, i.e. ink pinned to the clipped box edge); reverting to the fix turns it green. Library 13 packages 926/926, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and `cd examples && moon check --deny-warn` error- and warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links.
- **Pending real-hardware re-check** (user): the large icons on the empty/result pages, the sidebar deep/light toggle (moon glyph), the icon-wall page (`size=30`), and the small prefix/suffix and table-sort icons — none should break out of its container, none should have sliced edges, all should sit centred.

## Declarative frontend P5: `transition` property animation (state-bucket interpolation + frame driver, 2026-10-14)

- **The interpolation set is drawn along the "read from the style slot every frame" line**: only `color` / `background_color` / `border_color` / `border_width` / `border_radius` animate. The reason is not convenience — any property that feeds layout (font size, line height, sizes, margins) forces a full relayout of the tree every frame once it interpolates, while `opacity` / `box_shadow` take effect where `apply` writes `Widget.alpha_paint` / `shadow_paint`, and the paint traversal follows host fields rather than slots, so interpolating them would have no effect. Properties outside the set **switch immediately**: `step` compares a projection of the interpolated fields and settles directly when the projection matches.
- **State-machine rules**: ① the first time a widget is seen, only the target is recorded — no animation (otherwise building or remounting a tree would fade the whole page in); ② when the target changes mid-flight, the animation continues from the **currently displayed value** (`from = shown`), so reversing an interrupted hover does not jump; ③ the same target continues on the original clock while non-interpolated fields follow the new target; ④ `transition_ms` absent or 0 settles at once and **leaves no account behind** (`style_for` goes through `forget_anim`). Easing is smoothstep (`t·t·(3-2t)`).
- **One timer drives all animations**: a process-level `@core.set_timeout(16)` starts the table, each tick calls `@core.invalidate_id(id)` only for widgets that are animating (whichever window contains it gets its dirty region; only when no window can find it does it fall back to a whole-window broadcast), and the table stops as soon as everything converged — no per-widget timer and no idle spinning. Values are computed from **elapsed real time** rather than counting ticks, so dropped frames or a busy host cost frames, never speed. An account whose block was hidden pays over the endpoint value on the expiry tick and marks dirty once, leaving no long tail.
- **How the two colour endpoints are taken**: `Var` tokens resolve against the current theme before mixing (`@theme.mix_hex`), so switching themes mid-animation leaves that run's endpoints on the pre-switch colours and the next switch follows the new theme — theme switches dirty the whole window anyway, so this is not a visible defect. When either endpoint is missing or is not written as hex (named colours), `mix_hex` degrades to an endpoint value: middle frames stay on the start colour and the final frame is still the target, so **the wrong colour is never painted**.
- Toolchain readings (moon 0.1.20260920, judged by `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn`):
  - **`pub(all) enum Color` carries no `==`**: a tuple comparison containing `Option[Color]` fails with `[4018] Type Color does not implement trait Eq`. Same family as the existing note (`derive(Eq)` on a value type promotes impl methods into plain methods and warns), so **state comparison always goes through a string projection** (distinguishing Hex/Named/Var by the `#`/`n`/`@` prefix) rather than deriving.
  - **Package-private structs must be declared `priv struct`**: a bare `struct Anim` emits the `missing_priv` warning, which fails under `--deny-warn`.
  - **`}` and the next condition's `{` cannot be split across lines**: writing `} else if cond` then `{` on the following line gives `[3002] Unexpected line break here, missing {` — the brace must sit at the end of the condition line (the same discipline as `test "name" {`).
  - **`moon fmt` rewrites unrelated files**: the committed tree is **not** in this toolchain's fmt shape (`moon fmt style core` touched 42 files in one go, e.g. inserting a blank line before every `pub const` in `keys.mbt`). Format only the files of **the current batch** and read the diff line by line afterwards; this batch closed out with "only change the lines I wrote".
- **Verification**: 6 new style tests (interpolation endpoints / midpoint / one-sided default, the state machine's first frame does not animate, the 150 ms three-point reading `#000000→#808080→#d7d7d7→#ffffff`, mid-flight reversal continuing from `#282828`, out-of-set properties settling at once, and no account left when no transition is configured) plus 1 new core test (`invalidate_id` marks only the owning window, leaves the other alone, and an unknown id falls back to whole-window); `moon test style core` 159/159, all 13 library packages green at 908/908, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, `cd examples && moon check showcase --deny-warn` warning-free. Demo page: showcase gains a "过渡与效果" page (0/150/600 ms in three blocks + reversal + the text and effect fields); the on-device look (comparing the three blocks' speed on hover, and whether moving away mid-way jumps) is the user's check.

## Declarative frontend P1: gui/style package and yoga-mbt z_index (2026-10-13)

Toolchain boundaries (moon 0.1.20260920 / moonc v0.10.14; readings must be re-measured after upgrades, mirrored in design.md §1.6):
- **`alias` / `abbrev` are both reserved keywords — there is no function or type-alias syntax.** Short names for external types come only from `using @pkg {type X}`, and that declaration is **package-scoped**: writing it in two files hits `[4051] declared twice`; the correct form is one `pub using` in one file, serving the whole package and outside callers with the short name.
- **Labelled arguments have no forwarding channel at all**: `f(width=width)` fails typing (the in-body optional parameter is `T?`), `f(width?)` / `f(width!)` / `f(...)` are all `[3002]` parse errors, and binding `pub let g = f` then calling `g(width=1.0)` gives `[4117]` ("labelled functions can only be applied directly"); `moon.pkg` imports do not accept key-value form (`unexpected token :`), so package short names cannot be configured either. Conclusion: the style-factory call site is fixed as `@style.style(...)`, and the draw-period builder inside the `.hover/.active/.focus` state methods is written out in all three places.
- `priv` only修饰 declaration forms other than `let`/`fn`; a top-level `priv named_x = ...` fails to parse — package-private values are plain `let`.
- `Array::contains` requires `T: Eq`; testing an option that holds a value uses `is Some(_)` (`is_some()` is a deprecation warning); `Map::new()` is deprecated — write the `Map([])` literal.
- `for i in 0..n` (half-open) and `0..=n` are unavailable outside `for`; a range loop requires the `for i in (0..<n)` form or an outright `while`. This package falls back to `while` throughout.

Architecture decisions:
- **core must not depend on style** (style depends on core's Widget/yoga landing points; the reverse edge would form a cycle). The Widget's resolved-Style slot is implemented as a **process-level side table** `Map[widget id, Style]` inside the `@style` package (the same precedent as overlay_native's process-level handle table): `apply` writes, and drawing reads `resolved(w)` / `style_for(w)` (choosing the bucket by `hovered/pressed/focused`); a widget that was never applied reads back an empty style. **Stale-row cleanup has landed (the P2-e wrap-up)**: core gained a process-level "widget discarded hook" `set_widget_discard_hook`; `clear_children` and `remove_child` report every id of the detached subtree, and `@style` installs the hook itself on its first `apply` to clear those entries — dynamic tree swaps (`bind_node` remounts, `for_list` row removal, virtual-list window remounts, overlay teardown) no longer accumulate across generations. **Rule: detaching means discarding; moving must go through `move_child`** (core does not know the difference between move and drop — the hook only sees those two APIs). The acceptance check is `@style.resolved_count()` (for diagnostics), and a regression pins "remove a widget that has a subtree ⇒ the count falls back".
- **cursor is a draw-period property and may be carried by state buckets**; a widget's **static** `cursor` field is written directly by `apply`, and a bucket's cursor is handed down by P2's hover path reading `style_for`.
- yoga-mbt's `z_index` is paint-only: the setter does not `mark_changed` (geometry is unaffected) and the engine **never physically reorders children** (incremental layout caches by index), so it exposes an index projection `Node::paint_order`; on the gui side `Widget.z_index_paint` is written by `apply` and `widget_paint_order` stable-insertion-sorts the kids (identity order when all are zero, so existing examples stay frame-for-frame unchanged).

Verification: style 18/18, yoga-mbt 100/100 (baseline 95 + 5 new), core 120/120, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and repo-wide `moon check` error- and warning-free; the set_margin labelling conversion covered all 14 call sites in one batch; library tests 856/858 (the 2 reds are the pre-existing W9/sort gaps, same reds on a stashed clean tree).

## Toasts carried a whole-window background plate: overlays now open content-sized (2026-10-14, real-hardware report)

- **Environment**: Ubuntu 24.04 + X11 + XFCE, `examples/showcase` (the browser page hangs in the same `bind_node` tree as the rest, so the webview area is permanently mounted).
- **Symptom**: when a message toast popped, everything above the top strip looked as though **the whole window had been covered by an opaque background plate** (the user's words: "message 不应该有遮罩背景").
- **Root cause**: `toast_layer` opened through `overlay_show_full`. When the owning window carries native children (the webview area), overlays take the **native tier** (`overlay_native_tier()` = `Window::has_child_surfaces()`), and the full-window tier opens **a real window** sized to the owner's content area — while every `App` root widget paints `theme_bg_page()` by default (`core/app.mbt`). So a window-sized plate of page background was hung over the main window, with the toast strip just a rounded band on top of it. The tier also made its carrier a full-window `absolute` wrapper with all four sides 0 (it paints no background, but every hit in the window belongs to it).
- **Fix**: toasts now open **content-sized** (`overlay_show_at`, `y=0`, `x` centred on the window width; the centring formula is extracted into the pure function `toast_left` so it can be pinned), and the carrier is no longer absolute — a column plus `align-items: center` lets its width equal the widest strip naturally. Two companions:
  - core gained `overlay_set_pos(id, x, y)` (moves a **layer-tier** overlay in window coordinates; a native-tier window's position belongs to the window system after it opens, so it returns false and does not move) — needed when a wider toast arrived later and the whole group had to re-centre.
  - The native tier's resize pass gained a rule: after `overlay_fit_pass` exhausts its three-frame budget, **growth is still allowed** — if the content gets longer or wider and the box does not follow, the extra part is cut off; shrinking stays under the three-frame limit (so a width loop never flips the size back and forth).
- **One thing left untouched, recorded here**: the layer is a full-window absolute child of the root widget, so while any overlay is open, presses outside it are still consumed by the layer (the "click outside to dismiss" in `core/overlay.mbt`) — during the two seconds a toast is on screen, clicking a page control does not receive that press. This is the shared input model of the overlay family; this batch only closed out the visual size, not dispatch. Whether overlays that have no outside-click-dismiss semantics (toasts) should let clicks through is decided in another batch.
- **Verification**: `moon test core ui` 299/299 (core adds 1: after `overlay_set_pos` moves a layer, `overlay_rect_of` lands at the new window coordinates and an unknown handle yields false; the ui toast case gained assertions: the overlay rect is smaller than the window in both dimensions, and `toast_left`'s centring plus clamping-to-0 across three points), library-wide 914/914, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and `cd examples && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links. Real-machine appearance (no whole-window plate outside the strip, still centred as strips of differing widths arrive) belongs to `_人工测试清单.md` S18.

## Keyboard focus was dead everywhere: the focus stack only knew manually registered ids, and production code registered none (2026-10-15, real-hardware report on Linux *and* Windows at once)

- **Symptoms**: on both platforms an input box could not be clicked into or typed in, Latin and CJK alike; the Chinese IME preview (composition string) appeared at an **uncertain position** instead of following the input box; buttons / menus / the section strip showed no focus ring at all. `examples/showcase` hit it everywhere, while `examples/native-app` looked healthy.
- **Root cause**: `App::route`'s Down only does `if self.focus.focus(id)` — **if that number is not already in the focus stack, focus does not move** — and the only thing that fills the stack, `FocusStack::register`, had exactly **two** call sites in the whole repo: `ui/message_box.mbt` (a transient overlay focus) and **the examples themselves** (`native-app` hand-registered 1..25; showcase registered only the events-page one). The discipline "whoever builds a widget hands its focus number to the host" never entered the library, so examples remembered to补 and the demo board did not → in showcase every `input`/`textarea` got an automatic focus number (`auto_focus_id`) yet that number was nowhere in the stack: clicks travel the pointer path (the caret still paints, the border still lights), so it *looked* like the box had been entered, while keys are delivered only to the widget named by the focus stack — hence zero typing. The Chinese symptom lines up exactly: with no focused widget `im_cursor` cannot supply a caret rectangle, so the candidate window stays at the system default = "an uncertain position".
- **Fix (the contract becomes "declaring is registering")**: the focus stack's content is decided by the **widget tree**; callers only declare `focus_id`.
  - `Widget::focus_ids()`: collects the focus numbers that are "in the tree and not hidden" in tree order (depth-first, children in mount order), duplicates folded away, `focus_id<=0` ignored. A hidden block (an unselected page, a dismissed popup) drops out of the Tab order by itself.
  - `FocusStack::sync(ids)`: realigns the whole registry. **Current focus is preserved by number** (still in the list — still focused; removed — focus cleared); when the list is non-empty but nothing was focused it **does not grab focus** — after `drop_current` hands the keyboard to a webview child, the next realignment must not take it back to a self-drawn widget.
  - `App::route`'s Down and `App::move_focus` (Tab) each realign once beforehand. Those are the only two consumers: painting only reads `focus.current()` (`set_focused_by_focus`) and needs no ordering, so **there is no per-frame tree walk**.
  - `register`/`unregister` stay, with their use narrowed to **transient focuses that are not in the widget tree** (a message box's overlay ids). The cost: such a number is dropped by the next realignment, so a long-lived one must be re-`focus`ed after each realignment.
- **Why not "components register themselves on mount"**: a widget can be mounted into a different window (one stack per window), `bind_node`/`for_list` remounts and virtual-list row swaps would all need paired deregistration, and `focus_id` is a public mutable field (`w.focus_id = 910`) that nothing can intercept — bookkeeping hung on widgets will leak. One pass in tree order solves all of it and uses the same predicate as `focusable_at` (first non-zero number along the hit chain).
- **Buttons / the section strip / menus stay deliberately opt-in** (they enter the Tab order only when given a `focus_id`): this stack does not yet have the "focus + Enter/Space activates" semantics (the focus ring has long existed), so making them focused by default would ship the half-feature "Tab stops there, Enter does nothing" — another batch decides.
- **Verification**: `moon test core` 143/143 with 4 new tests (`gui/core/focus_route_wbtest.mbt`): `focus_ids` tree order / hidden-block skip / duplicate folding; `sync` preserving focus and never inventing one; the end-to-end case that **never calls register** — click into the widget with focus number 7, keys reach it, Tab moves to 9, hide 9 and Tab then only circles 7; and pressing empty space does not move focus. Library-wide 906/912 (the 6 red are this machine's Windows environment baseline: sys's `/tmp` and `.desktop` path assertions plus render's PNG read-back, unrelated to this batch), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free. The showcase events page's "register on mount" demo was deleted in step (it now only declares `focus_id`). On-device re-check is item S19 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## The pure raster backend never cleared the path: one widget's arcs were redrawn at another widget's origin (2026-10-15, real-hardware report on Windows)

- **Symptoms**: in `examples/showcase`, form component "开关" section — a checked and an unchecked checkbox looked **indistinguishable**, both become a solid plate; a selected radio painted as a filled disc (the gap between ring and core was gone) and even the *unselected* one carried a core dot. The same code was fine on Linux (cairo backend).
- **Root cause**: `Raster::fill` / `Raster::stroke` do not clear the current path after putting pixels down, while `cairo_fill` / `cairo_stroke` always do — a violation of the "the two backends are method-for-method identical" rule stated in `Painter`'s header (item 3). One page shares a single Painter session and each widget paints at **its own origin** (`paint_at` does `save()+translate()` per level), so a subpath left by the previous widget is re-traced in the *next* widget's coordinate system: after the radio's ring + core, the checkbox's tick `stroke()` re-drew those two arcs as a 2 px accent shape at the checkbox's origin — a plate that appears out of nowhere — and an unselected radio got carried along with somebody else's core. **Unit tests could not see it**: painting one widget alone into a clean bitmap leaves only its own part in the path, and the contamination needs "the previous widget drew arcs" to show (in the probe, the third radio's red core came from the second).
- **Fix**:
  - `Raster::fill` / `Raster::stroke` clear the path as soon as the ink is down, matching cairo (the zero-line-width branch paints no pixels but clears all the same).
  - Fixed the **one call site that relied on the old behaviour**: `chart/geo.mbt` built a region ring, `fill()`ed it and then `stroke()`d it directly — that stroke was already a no-op on Linux (the path had been cleared, so map regions never had an outline); extracted `geo_ring_path` and lay the path out twice, a fresh one per draw op.
  - Added explicit `begin_path` on the component side (the checkbox tick, the radio ring and core): that is the house style (`paint_seq_aa` in `cairo_wbtest.mbt` begins every op) and the discipline of "each stroke carries its own path".
  - The tick being too thin is a separate complaint, fixed in the same batch: line width 1.0 → **2.0**, geometry tightened to `(3.2,7.3)→(5.8,10.0)→(10.9,3.9)` (a 1 px polyline inside a 14×14 box leaves a dozen pixels — it does not read as a tick).
- **Verification**: 1 new render test on the shared backend contract (after the first triangle is filled red, neither the second green fill nor the blue stroke may redraw it) and 2 new ui pixel tests (the tick's solid coverage >20 pixels; an unchecked box contains 0 accent pixels; an unselected radio contains 0 accent pixels inside its ring — all three red under the old code). Library-wide 909/915 (the 6 red are this machine's Windows environment baseline: sys's `/tmp` and `.desktop` path assertions plus render's PNG read-back, unrelated to this batch), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free. On-device look (unchecked = grey frame, checked = accent frame + thick tick; selected radio = ring + core, unselected = clean grey ring) is item S20 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## Widget shapes: the switch painted as two right-angled rectangles, the radio's ring and core merged into one plate (2026-10-15, real-hardware report on Windows)

- **Symptoms**: with the path contamination gone, the same "开关" screenshot still reads wrong — the switch is a **right-angled bar** with a **square knob** (no capsule arc, no round ball); a selected radio has no seam between ring and core, so it reads as one solid plate; the checkbox's tick upper arm jams into the frame corner. Linux (cairo) renders the same code the same way, so this batch is the component's own drawing, not a backend split.
- **Root cause**:
  - `ui/form.mbt`'s `switch` was earlier two `fill_rect` calls (a 40×20 rectangle plus a 16×16 square), with a comment parked saying "the capsule is approximated by a rounded rectangle, square corners noted for later" — the note never landed, so a bar-with-square is what shipped.
  - The radio ring was stroked at line width 1.0 (radius 6 → inner edge 5.5) around a core of radius 3.5: only 1 px of seam left on each side, which antialiasing smears into nothing.
  - After the previous batch thickened the tick to 2 px, its upper arm ended at `x=10.9`, 3 px from the 14 px frame's right edge; the thicker end cap pushed it into the corner.
  - Trying a *rounded* checkbox frame surfaced one backend fact: at **line width 1.0** `Raster::stroke_round_rect` drops **all four straight segments** — `rect_device` snaps the rectangle to integer edges while coverage is measured from **pixel centres**, so with `hw=0.5` the overlap against an integer edge is exactly 0; only the corner SDF ring still paints. This batch's checkbox frame therefore went back to `stroke_rect` (an inner stroke — 1 px lands on a full cell), and a 1 px **rounded** frame waits for the backend to compute edges in exact device coordinates — another batch.
- **Fix**:
  - `switch` → `fill_round_rect(0, 0, r.w, r.h, r.h / 2)` for a real capsule plus `arc(cx, r.h / 2, 8)` for a round ball; the ball's centre sits half the height from each end so its rim meets the capsule wall.
  - Radio ring line width 1.0 → **1.2**, core radius 3.5 → **2.8**. The centre row now measures `##..######..##` (ring 2 cells, gap 2, core 6, gap 2, ring 2).
  - The checkbox tick tightened one more notch: `(3.2,7.3)→(5.8,10.0)→(10.9,3.9)` → `(3.4,7.4)→(5.9,9.9)→(10.5,4.3)`, keeping both ends ≥2 px from the frame edges.
- **Verification**: 2 new ui shape regressions (the radio centre row asserted cell by cell as "ring — gap — core — gap — ring"; the switch's four corners free of ink with the knob 16 cells wide at mid seam and only 6 at the top/bottom edge rows, i.e. round) — `moon test ui` 164/164, library-wide 912/917 (the 5 red are this machine's Windows environment baseline: sys's `.desktop` and directory-enumeration assertions, unrelated to this batch), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free. On-device look is item S20 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## A 1px rounded-rect stroke lost all four straight edges: the rasterizer snapped the edges but measured coverage from pixel centres (2026-10-15, development machine on Windows)

- **Symptoms**: giving the checkbox a 1 px **rounded** frame (`stroke_round_rect(0.5, 0.5, 13, 13, 3)`, line width 1.0) left only the four corner arcs on Windows — not one lit pixel along the straight sides; the same line paints a full ring on Linux (cairo backend). `stroke_round_rect` is public API (no call site inside the library), which means "a centred 1 px rounded border" had never actually painted on this analytic fast path.
- **Root cause**: the edges came from `rect_device`'s **snapped** result while coverage is computed at **pixel centres**: with `hw = line_width / 2 = 0.5` and an edge on an integer, the nearest pixel centre is exactly 0.5 away → `d = hw - 0.5 = 0` → coverage 0 and the whole straight segment vanishes. The corners survived because their branch runs the "distance to the arc centre" SDF, and an arc centre need not be an integer. Not isomorphic with cairo (the method-surface rule is stated in `Painter`'s header).
- **Fix**: edges now always come from **exact device coordinates** (`m.apply` on the two diagonal corners, min/max for negative scales), and rounding is only used to bound the loop; coverage became the analytic cell overlap `cov = hw + 0.5 − |distance from centre to the ring|` — the standard SDF antialiasing form, where `+0.5` is the "a pixel is a whole cell" area correction — one formula for straight segments and corners alike.
- **Recorded along the way, deliberately not changed**: a centred stroke landing on a **half-pixel origin** necessarily spreads into two adjacent cells at half ink. The checkbox mark is vertically centred in its row — a 14-high mark in a 17-high row gives `rect.y = 1.5` — so after switching to a rounded centred stroke the frame line would read at roughly 50% strength, a step paler than the inner stroke it replaced; the frame therefore stays on `stroke_rect` (integer-snapped, crisp at any origin). Putting rounded frames on mark-class widgets first requires aligning them to integer device cells (or adding a "snap-to-cell centred stroke" to `Painter`) — another batch.
- **Another pit (unrelated to this change, noted in passing)**: running `moon fmt` once inside the batch — the toolchain's reflow conventions disagree with this repo's existing style, and one command rewrote 287 files (splitting `if … { x }` across lines, wrapping short parameter lists, etc.), forcing a whole-tree revert before re-applying this batch's four edits. **Do not run `moon fmt` inside a feature batch**; a repo-wide reformat is its own batch, and only after confirming the toolchain's fmt conventions match the repo style.
- **Verification**: 1 new render test on the shared backend contract (edges on the cell centre 0.5 → all four side mid-points read full ink 255, outside the arc corner and inside the frame read 0; edges on an integer boundary → the straight segment still carries half ink, >60) and 1 new ui test that the frame stays sharp (all four sides and corners above 200). `moon test render ui chart` 403/403, library-wide 914/919 (the 5 red are this machine's Windows environment baseline: sys's `.desktop` and directory-enumeration assertions, unrelated to this batch), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free.

## Why arcs and rounded corners looked like pixel art: a sign-flipped miter, a closed stroke stitched into one contour, and a rounded fill snapped to the cell grid (2026-10-15, real-hardware report on Windows)

- **Environment**: development machine, Windows 10 22H2, pure-MoonBit raster backend (`PureBackend`; Linux runs the cairo backend against the same component code).
- **Symptoms**: the radio outer ring had breaks along its line (per-cell readings such as `...-####.###-...` at the apex), the checkbox tick read as a row of steps, and **every** rounded corner / arc / chamfer felt mosaic-y. The user guessed "the canvas resolution is too low".
- **Root causes** — three, all inside the rasterizer, none of them canvas resolution:
  - **Canvas resolution is not the cause**: the process declares per-monitor-v2 DPI awareness (`gui/win/stub.c`), but nothing in the repository ever *reads* a DPI value (no `wm_dpi`/`wm_scale` export, and Linux never looks at `Xft.dpi`/`GDK_SCALE`); the frame canvas is allocated 1:1 in physical pixels (`paint_frame` in `gui/core/app.mbt`) and `StretchDIBits` gets identical source and target sizes. This machine reports `AppliedDPI = 96` (100%), so there is neither DWM stretching nor scaled down-sampling. **Open item**: on a 125%/150% display this convention makes the whole UI small, and laying out by a scale factor needs its own batch.
  - **`stroke_polys` solved the miter intersection with the wrong sign**: joining the two offset lines means `s·prev − t·cur = n − pn`, and crossing with `cur` gives `s = cross(r, cur) / det`; the code wrote `cross(cur, r) / det` — the **opposite sign** — so the outer-angle miter point landed on the inner angle and vice versa, the outline self-crossed at every joint, and each turn of a polyline / arc / chamfer bit out a notch. The "the tick's upper arm jams into the frame corner" noted last batch is a symptom of it.
  - **A closed polyline was stroked as one stitched contour** (side A forward plus side B reversed): the two windings cancel at the stitch, leaving holes along the ring. A full `arc(0..2π)` never calls `close_path`, yet its coincident first/last points were handled as an open path — which also added two butt caps.
  - **`Raster::fill_round_rect` snapped the rectangle to integer cells**: the straight edges got no antialiasing at all (a panel at a fractional origin is shifted by up to half a cell) while only the corners were measured against the arc centre — the main source of the "rounded corners look like pixel art" impression; the same fast path also snapped concentric marks (ring / core / knob) to different cells, so they read off-centre.
  - The flattening tolerance `RASTER_FLAT_TOLERANCE` was 0.25 (cairo defaults to 0.1), so a small radius was cut into only twelve chords, which amplified the two above into visible gaps.
- **Fix**:
  - The miter solution became `s = (rx·uy − ry·ux) / det` (`gui/render/raster_fill.mbt`).
  - Closed subpaths (including those whose endpoints coincide) now form **two separate rings per side**: outer forward plus inner reversed, and nonzero winding punches the hole automatically; the wrap-around vertex gets a real joint instead of end caps.
  - `Raster::fill_round_rect` was rewritten on **exact device coordinates** with per-pixel signed-distance coverage (256 levels); each row still resolves its fully covered column span and writes it as a solid run (the opaque-solid-source fast path unchanged), and only the few pixels at either end go through the distance form. Zero radius still takes the crisp cell-aligned rectangle.
  - `RASTER_FLAT_TOLERANCE` 0.25 → **0.1** (same as cairo).
  - Components: the radio ring became `stroke_round_rect(1,1,12,12,6)` and the core `fill_round_rect(4,4,6,6,3)`, and the `switch` knob became a `fill_round_rect` circle — a 14 px-scale circle should not be flattened into chords at all; ring line width 1.2 → 1.3 (with 1.2 only one cell of the ring stays solid within 12 cells, which reads fuzzy); the tick 2.0 → 2.4.
- **Verification**: 3 new render tests on the shared backend contract — a full circle stroked (`r=6`, line width 1.3) swept cell by cell along the band with no 1-cell break allowed; a right-angle joint whose miter must reach the outer corner (`(17,17)` must read full ink 255, the cell outside the corner 0); `fill_round_rect` at a fractional edge must antialias the straight side (that cell lands in the 60..200 half-ink range). All three are **red under the old implementation** (verified one by one by stashing each backend file: the miter read 128, the ring case had a 1-cell break, the fractional edge read 0). The two ui shape tests were re-calibrated to the new readings (radio centre row still `##..######..##` plus the core's 6 solid cells; the switch knob's rows 4/15 now 10 solid cells). `moon test render ui chart` 406/406, library-wide 917/922 (the 5 red are this machine's Windows environment baseline: sys's `.desktop`/directory-enumeration assertions, unrelated to this batch), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free. On-device look is item S20 in `_人工测试清单.md`.
- **Still open (separate batch)**: generic path fills are still 4×4 supersampled (16 coverage levels), so long diagonals show mild steps; `stroke_round_rect` at a half-pixel origin still splits across two cells; every rounded background in the library is still bordered with `stroke_rect` inner strokes (square corners over rounded ones), and unifying those into rounded borders first needs the mark widgets aligned to integer device cells.

## Typing a space in an input gave no feedback: both text engines trim trailing whitespace out of the measured width (2026-10-15, real-hardware report on Windows)

- **Symptoms**: typing a space in an input moved neither the caret nor anything else; the space only "appeared" together with the next non-space character typed after it.
- **Root cause**: a space carries no ink, so the only visible signal for a typed space is the **caret moving right** — and the input's caret offsets come entirely from `@text.measure_font` prefix widths (`prefix_width` in `gui/ui/entry.mbt`). Both layout engines define "text width" with alignment semantics that **exclude trailing whitespace**: DWrite's `DWRITE_TEXT_METRICS.width` excludes it by definition (the inclusive field is `widthIncludingTrailingWhitespace`, and the C-side `pt_measure_font` took the former), and Pango has trimmed trailing whitespace from the layout width since 1.44 (`pango_layout_get_pixel_size` likewise). So measuring `"abc "` equals `"abc"`, and the caret never moved. The drawing paths (`ptw_render` / the batch queue's ink rect) use `widthIncludingTrailingWhitespace`, which is why a space **mid-line** always worked — only the trailing one was affected, and tests measuring whole words never caught it.
- **Fix**:
  - DWrite (`gui/text/dwrite_text.cpp`): `pt_measure_font` and `rt_measure` now take `tm.widthIncludingTrailingWhitespace`; the alignment helper `ptw_box_offsets` keeps `tm.width` (centring / right alignment should not count trailing whitespace) — two concerns, two fields.
  - Pango (`gui/text/stub.c`): new helper `pt_width_with_trailing_ws` — when the text ends in whitespace (`g_unichar_isspace` on the last character) and the layout is a single line, the width is recovered from `pango_layout_index_to_pos(len)`, the **cursor endpoint** (Pango cursor positions do cover trailing whitespace), taking the larger against the pixel width; multi-line layouts are left alone (the last line's endpoint is not the total width).
- **Verification**: 1 new cross-backend regression in `text` (`measure("ab ")` must be wider than `measure("ab")`, and a lone space must measure > 0). `moon test text` 30/30, library-wide 918/923 (the 5 red are this machine's Windows environment baseline: sys's readings loop and directory-enumeration assertions, unrelated to this batch), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free. On-device re-check is item S19 ⑧ in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## A closable alert did nothing when clicked: the component never implemented "collapse by default" — the default callback was an empty function (2026-10-15, real-hardware report on Windows)

- **Symptoms**: on the feedback page's "可关闭" section, clicking the ✕ at the banner's top right left it exactly where it was.
- **Root cause**: the ✕'s hot zone and callback chain were fine all along (the white-box test shows `on_close` firing when the hot zone is clicked). What was broken is the semantic layering — `on_close`'s default value is an empty function, showcase happened to pass no callback, and the component itself never implemented the *collapse* behaviour that ✕ denotes: clicking it amounts to calling an empty function, so nothing happens. The component page's copy "这里留默认(只收起)" promised exactly this unimplemented behaviour.
- **Fix** (`gui/ui/display.mbt`): ✕'s own behaviour moved into the component — a hot-zone click always `set_visible(false)` (synced with yoga `Display::None`, so layout reflows) plus `@core.invalidate()` (whole-window dirty: the collapse reflows the whole column below, which a local dirty rect cannot cover); `on_close` is demoted to an **optional notification** on top of the collapse, and the banner collapses whether or not a callback was passed. The `native-app` call site that passes a counting callback gains the consistent behaviour for free (banner collapses and the counter ticks).
- **Verification**: ui's existing alert regression was rewritten — paint the open state and assert the ✕ mark exists, click the hot zone and assert the callback fired + `visible == false` + after relayout/repaint the whole frame is ink-free; a click outside the hot zone collapses nothing. Library-wide 918/923 (same baseline), `cd examples && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free. On-device re-check is item S8 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## Form controls could not be reached by Tab and had no keyboard interaction: the opt-in focus contract kept the whole family out of the Tab order (2026-10-15, user report)

- **Symptoms**: stepper, slider, rate, select (plain / colour / date / time), switch, checkbox and radio options could not be Tab-reached and did not respond to space/arrows/Enter; buttons, menus and the segmented control were the same.
- **Root cause**: the focus infrastructure (focus stack, Tab wrap-around, `dispatch_key` delivering along the focused widget's ancestor chain, tree-order `focus_ids` alignment) was all in place; the 2026-10-14 batch only auto-assigned numbers to text inputs, and `select`/`button` etc. stayed under the then-rule "focusability is deliberate opt-in" (the note at the end of the 《Keyboard focus was dead everywhere》 entry) — because back then the "focus + activation key" semantics did not exist, so default-focusing would have shipped the half-feature "Tab stops there, Enter does nothing". This batch completes the activation semantics and flips the contract: the form / navigation / menu families **auto-assign a focus number and enter the Tab chain by default** (`auto_focus_id`; an explicit number still wins), so call sites no longer hand out numbers one by one.
- **Fix** (key semantics per control):
  - `button` / `checkbox` / `switch` / radio option / segment item: space/Enter activates (toggles or selects);
  - `radio_group` / `segmented`: arrows re-select by the **focused item's index** (not relative to the current value), wrapping at the ends; Enter/Space activates the focused item;
  - `slider`: ←/↓ decreases, →/↑ increases (one percent of the range when no `step`), Home/End to the two ends;
  - `stepper`: ←/↓ decreases, →/↑ increases; the out-of-range side consumes the key without changing the value;
  - `rate`: arrows add or remove a star, Home/End to the extremes, writing the value fires the same callback as a click;
  - `select` (non-editable) / `color_picker` / `dropdown`: space/Enter/↓ opens the layer, ↑/↓ (the swatch grid: ←→ move one cell, ↑↓ move one row) moves the highlight, Enter/Space takes the highlight, Esc closes; `dropdown`'s `-` separators take no highlight slot;
  - `date_picker` / `date_range_picker` / time fields: space/Enter/↓ opens, Enter/Esc closes (`attach_field_toggle_key`; arrow navigation inside the calendar is not done — the popup stays click-only);
  - focus ring: entry/picker field outlines turn to the theme colour when focused (painted over the resting outline), marker-class controls (checkbox outline, radio ring, switch pill, stepper frame, rate/segment/slider) draw a theme-coloured outline ring, buttons keep their existing ring. Painting is clipped to the widget rect, so every ring is drawn **inside** the widget rect.
- **Verification**: 8 new headless ui regressions (marker controls space/Enter/disabled-ignores-keys + `focus_ids` coverage, radio wrap-around re-select, slider/stepper/rate key adjustment, button space/Enter, the full select keyboard flow, colour-picker grid navigation, dropdown skipping separators, date-field open/close). `moon test ui` 176/176, library-wide 934/935 (1 red = this machine's Windows environment baseline), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free. On-device re-check is item S22 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## Fullscreen and window resizing did nothing on Windows: the win branch ships two symbol-bearing stubs while GTK has had the real thing all along (2026-10-15, real-hardware report on Windows)

- **Symptoms**: on showcase's window page, the "全屏切换" and "尺寸切换" buttons (and every call going through `App::set_fullscreen` / `Window::set_size_pixels`) did nothing on Windows — clicking raised no error, the window stayed put.
- **Root cause**: in `gui/win/stub.c`'s Windows branch, `wm_window_set_size` / `wm_window_set_fullscreen` were symbol-bearing empty stubs (every parameter discarded with `(void)`), while the GTK branch had long wired `gtk_window_resize` / `gtk_window_fullscreen`. Because the symbols exist the link never breaks and the calls are silently inert — the "same method surface on both backends, the real implementation landed on only one" pitfall struck the win stub too (the same shape as the Raster path-not-cleared and rounded-stroke-straight-segments bugs before it).
- **Fix** (`gui/win/stub.c` Windows branch):
  - `wm_window_set_size`: the parameters are client-area physical pixels (the stack-wide physical-pixel convention); expand to the outer window size with `AdjustWindowRectEx` on the current style and `SetWindowPos(SWP_NOMOVE|SWP_NOZORDER|SWP_NOACTIVATE)`; width/height < 1 clamp to 1 (the MoonBit side `set_size_pixels` already rejects <1, so this is the C-side backstop; measured: a window with a title bar gets held up by the system minimum width, so the width clamp is only observable on the borderless form). The existing WM_SIZE bookkeeping sets `resized`, so the MoonBit side keeps receiving the `Resized` event and the host never computes the new rectangle itself.
  - `wm_window_set_fullscreen`: entering records the scene (style + `WINDOWPLACEMENT`), strips `WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW` for `WS_POPUP`, and `SetWindowPos` onto the nearest monitor (`MonitorFromWindow` + `GetMonitorInfoW`) at full screen; exiting restores the style and placement verbatim. Repeated calls with the same value return immediately (idempotent).
- **Verification**: two new sections in `experiment/window_probe/window_enhance_probe.c` — after `set_size`, `GetClientRect` reads back the target size, `wm_windows[].resized` is set, and `wm_size` agrees; fullscreen entering gives a window rectangle equal to the monitor rectangle with the client-area bookkeeping in sync, exiting restores position and style value by value, repeated enter/exit is idempotent, and an out-of-range id does not crash. The full run prints `WIN-ENHANCE-OK` (this machine, Windows 1920×1080). Compiling the probe also required two missing pieces: `shell32.lib` (the tray's `Shell_NotifyIconW` is now in the symbol surface) and a malloc backstop for `moonbit_make_bytes` (the clipboard stub references a runtime allocation symbol); the build recipe is updated in the probe header comment and `build.bat`. `moon test win` 28/28, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, `cd examples && moon build hello --target native` links. On-device re-check is item S23 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## Global hotkeys never fired: the poll loop sat in a construction-time hook and died on its first tick before the host existed (2026-10-15, real-hardware report on Windows)

- **Symptoms**: on showcase's window page, clicking "注册 Ctrl+Alt+C" reported registration success, but after switching to another program and pressing the combo, "命中 N 次" never moved.
- **Root cause**: the library-side chain (register → pump intercepts WM_HOTKEY → poll extracts) is fine — `experiment/window_probe` drives the exact same path with `PostThreadMessageW` delivering real WM_HOTKEY messages and is all green. What broke was where showcase parked its poll table: the "zero-size mount hook" was written inside `node_of_new`'s finish, which runs at **construction time** (documented in `core/node.mbt`), and page functions are `mount_window` arguments evaluated before the window exists — so the first tick's `hotkey_poll()` ran on the empty timer channel with `app.host.val` still None, and the **loop never re-armed: dead on the spot**. Every WM_HOTKEY intercepted by the pump afterwards had no reader. This is occurrence #2 of the same pitfall the charts push-point fix (52119a4) closed; the "零尺寸挂载钩子" comment in the page promised mount time while using a construction-time API.
- **Fix** (`examples/showcase/pages/window.mbt`): the hook moved to `Node::on_mount` — the section body mounts lazily, so it runs only when this section is first selected, by which time the host is ready; the 200ms self-rearming table is unchanged. The fragile shape of the poll table ("dies permanently if the host is not ready before the first tick": the tail tick reads `app.host` and stops re-arming when None) is the example side's current state and is an open hardening item (another batch).
