- **Verification**: `experiment/window_probe` gained a hotkey section — register → `PostThreadMessageW` posts WM_HOTKEY → `wm_pump` intercepts → `wm_hotkey_poll` extracts, repeated posts within one batch count once, re-registering the same combo is refused by the system, and after unregistration the same id no longer sets; the full run prints `WIN-ENHANCE-OK`. `cd examples && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links. On-device re-check is item S24 in `_人工测试清单.md` (a real key press can only be done by a person).

## The tray menu would not pop and neither mouse button did anything: occurrence #3 of the same construction-time pitfall — the dispatch table is started inside finish too (2026-10-15, real-hardware report on Windows)

- **Symptoms**: on showcase's "系统集成" page the tray icon is created (the icon shows, the tooltip hovers out), but left clicks do nothing (the counter stays 0 and no hint pops), and after "挂菜单" a right click pops no menu either.
- **Root cause**: exactly the same shape as the hotkey section above. The library chain is intact — `experiment/tray_probe/tray_backend_probe.c` feeds `wm_tray_*` directly, and left/right-click callback messages queueing and extraction by `wm_tray_poll`, menu attachment through `wm_menu_popup_new` + `wm_menu_add_item`, and invalid slots / no menu never blocking are all green. What broke is the example side: `tray_poll_loop()`'s **start** was written in `node_of_new`'s finish (running at construction time), so on its first tick `@core.host_active()` was still None ⇒ the 200ms table never re-armed and died on the spot. From then on nobody ever called `dispatch_tray_event()`: left-click callbacks were never extracted, and on Win32 the rule "a right click with no `on_context` callback pops the attached menu automatically" also lives inside `dispatch_tray_event` ⇒ what the user saw was "menu won't attach + clicks do nothing". The menu-item dispatch on the same page (`dispatch_menu_command`) was unaffected because its table starts in the host `handle` (the genuine mount phase).
- **Fix** (`examples/showcase/pages/system.mbt`): the table start moved to `Node::on_mount` (the section body mounts lazily and only runs when the section is first selected, when the host is ready); creating the tray itself stays in construction (the existing shape where the icon appears at startup is unchanged). The page comments were rewritten to match reality — the old line "段首次选中时建托盘 + 起派发表" promised mount time while using a construction-time API, which is why this pit was hit three times in a row.
- **Verification**: `moon check --deny-warn` (examples) warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links. The library changed nothing this batch; its tray semantics were re-established on this machine with `experiment/tray_probe/tray_backend_probe.c` (pure C, `#include`s stub.c directly): left/right-click callback messages queue and are extracted one by one by `wm_tray_poll`, `kind` 0/1 correct, non-click messages do not queue, `wm_menu_popup_new`'s popup root is a real HMENU and after attaching, `wm_menu_add_item` yields command ids, `wm_tray_popup` with no menu / an invalid slot returns 0 immediately without blocking, and removal is idempotent — the last line reads `TRAY-BACKEND-OK`. The probe builds like window_probe with a `build.bat` added; compiling the whole stub.c brings in the `moonbit_make_bytes` referenced by the clipboard stub, and the probe backstops it with malloc (recorded in the header comment). On-device re-check is item S25 in `_人工测试清单.md`: enter the "系统集成" page → left click increments the counter and pops a hint → click "挂菜单" → right click pops three items → clicking an item goes through `dispatch_menu_command` into the callback.
- **Open hardening item (another batch)**: the "the host drains once per tick" contract currently depends entirely on caller discipline and has now been hit three times in a row (chart push-point / global hotkeys / tray); the way to end this pit is folding `dispatch_menu_command` + `dispatch_tray_event` + `hotkey_poll` into the host's per-tick step (`App::step`). A consume-style queue tolerates several extractors coexisting (native-app's explicit calls will not steal events from it).

## Windows system-level drag-in: OLE callbacks live inside message dispatch, so the drop effect has to be written back in two stages (2026-10-15, feature request from the user)

- **Environment**: Windows 10 19044 dev machine, MSVC `/W4`, pure-C probe that `#include`s `../../gui/win/stub.c` directly (no moon runtime linked).
- **Symptoms/motivation**: the user asked "drag-and-drop should also interact with the outside world — drag in, drag out — and internally it should support repeated drags too". W21c only shipped in-app drag and drop, with the system level (dragging files in from Explorer) explicitly recorded for a platform batch. Repeated internal drags turned out to be an **existing capability** (`route_pointer` releases the capture on button-up and the session resets in `drag_drop`/`drag_cancel`, so it was never one-shot) — this batch just pins it with a regression. System-level **drag-in** lands here; **drag-out** (`DoDragDrop` + `IDropSource` + `IDataObject`) is a separate batch.
- **Root cause / design rationale** (why it looks like this):
  - OLE calls `IDropTarget` **on this thread, inside message dispatch**, the same constraint as tray/menu/hotkeys (rule 3: no C-to-MoonBit callbacks) ⇒ the C side pushes `DragEnter`/`DragOver`/`DragLeave`/`Drop` into a process-wide ring (64 slots) and the host drains it per tick with `wm_dragdnd_poll`. The payload does not go through the queue - it lives in a separate 64 KB buffer, read back with `wm_dragdnd_payload` as the most recent "enter/drop" payload.
  - **Two-stage effect**: at `DragEnter`, MoonBit has had no chance yet to decide whether this drop target accepts, yet the callback must return `pdweffect` immediately — so C gives a provisional value from "do I recognise this format at all" (CF_HDROP/CF_UNICODETEXT → COPY, unrecognised → NONE). Every later `DragOver`/`Drop` reads the per-window flag MoonBit wrote back with `wm_dragdnd_set_effect` on the previous tick. The app-side `accept` judgement therefore reaches the system cursor without a synchronous question into MoonBit.
  - **`accept` needs its own hook**: calling `on_drop` performs a real drop (side effects), so it cannot double as the hover-time "would you take this?" query ⇒ `Widget::drag_accept` + `drag_wants` (defaults to accept when no hook is installed), and `@ui.drop_target(accept=)` wires both `on_drop` and `drag_accept`.
  - **One session, not two**: `core/drag.mbt`'s process-wide singleton `drag_current` is the one in-app drag and drop already uses; external events are fed into it as ENTER→`drag_begin(data,0,x,y)`, OVER→`drag_move`, LEAVE→`drag_cancel`, DROP→`drag_drop`, so drop-target hit-testing (`drop_target_at`) and hover highlight (`drag_hover`) are all reused. The drop tree is picked from the **event's own window** (`drag_window_root_of` scans `host_windows()` comparing `a.window.id`), and `drag_root()` prefers that tree while an external session is live.
  - **Neither direction hijacks the other**: `drag_ext_window` records which window owns the current external session, LEAVE/DROP only act on same-window events, and an external ENTER is ignored outright while an internal drag is in flight (it does not steal the running drag).
- **Payload wire shape**: CF_HDROP **wins** (that is what Explorer sends), enumerated with `DragQueryFileW` one wide string at a time and joined with `\n` → `Paths` (kind 4); only when HDROP is absent does CF_UNICODETEXT → `Text` (kind 1); neither recognised → empty payload and effect NONE. All text goes through `WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8)` and is encoded as `[kind:i32 LE][payload]`, the same shape as `drag_encode`, so MoonBit's `drag_decode` consumes it as-is. Coordinates are converted with `ScreenToClient` into client-area pixels (the stack-wide physical-pixel convention).
- **Pitfalls (C side, each hit for real)**:
  1. `IDataObjectVtbl::QueryGetData` takes **exactly one `FORMATETC *`** — copying `GetData`'s shape and adding an extra `NULL` is C2197 "too many actual arguments" (confirmed against the SDK's `objidl.h`).
  2. In C mode `GetCanonicalFormatEtc`'s second parameter is `FORMATETC *`, not the C++ alias `DFORMATETC` (which only exists under `#ifdef __cplusplus`) — writing it does not compile (C2143/C2081).
  3. `DROPFILES` is defined in `um/ShlObj_core.h`, **not `shellapi.h`** — you need `#include <shlobj.h>`; `pFiles = sizeof(DROPFILES)` + `fWide = TRUE` + a double-NUL-terminated wide table are what make `DragQueryFileW` accept the blob.
  4. COM interfaces are implemented the C way (iface as first member + a static vtable); the vtable definition **must not be `const`** (the `lpVtbl` field is a non-const pointer). IID_*/CLSID_* come from `uuid.lib`, the drag functions from `shell32.lib`, `OleInitialize` from `ole32.lib` — all three were already on prebuild's Windows link line from the earlier icon/tray/taskbar batches, so nothing was added here.
  5. Whether OLE is up must be probed **once and cached**: `OleInitialize` returning `S_OK`/`S_FALSE` or `RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE` (someone already called `CoInitialize`) all count as ready. When `dragdnd_supported()` is permanently false the layer above skips attaching silently and in-app drag and drop keeps working.
- **Pitfall (probe side)**: OLE hands `DragEnter`/`DragOver` **screen** coordinates, so to test a point at client (20,30) the probe must derive the screen point with `ClientToScreen` **in reverse**; offsetting from screen origin (0,0) folds in the window's own position and shifts the whole hit test by a window distance (measured -48/-84) — it looks like a library bug but is a probe misuse.
- **Verification**: `experiment/drag_probe/dragdnd_probe.c` ends with **`DRAGDND-OK`** (40 assertions: attach/detach/idempotence/out-of-range id/live count/initial effect; HDROP → Paths(4) with both paths matching character for character; `set_effect` observed by the next `DragOver`/`Drop`; payload cleared after a drop; HDROP preferred over text; plain text → Text(1); an unrecognised format answers NONE with an empty payload; `DragLeave` clears the payload and queues LEAVE; after `disable` the count is 0 and the effect -1). `core/drag_wbtest.mbt` adds 1 test (fed events drive the session, COPY/NONE answered per drop target from `drag_wants`, a `data = None` event leaves an existing session alone, DROP delivers and resets, LEAVE cancels without delivering, cross-window events do not steal, an internal session is not hijacked); `ui/drag_wbtest.mbt` adds 2 (the same drag source can be dragged twice in a row with the payload rebuilt each time; `accept` is wired as the hover query too). `moon test core ui win` **351/351**, full library **937/938** (the one red is `si_machine` failing to read `SystemManufacturer` from the registry — this machine's environment baseline, unrelated), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links, and a local window exits normally after the smoke run. A real cross-process drag (Explorer → window) can only be done by a person: item S26 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## Windows system-level drag-out: a read-only IDataObject plus `SHDoDragDrop` saves an entire IDropSource — and `GetFullPathNameW` must not write back in place (2026-10-15, feature request from the user)

- **Environment**: Windows 10 19044 dev machine, MSVC `/W4`. The library build goes through moon's native-stub (the toolchain assembles the `cl` command); the probe goes through `experiment/drag_probe/build.bat` (vcvars64 + explicit `cl` flags) — **two different macro and include-path sets**, which is what makes pitfall 2 below bite.
- **Symptoms/motivation**: the "drag out" half of the user's sentence "drag-and-drop should also interact with the outside world — drag in, drag out". The goal: dragging out of this window must give the receiving program (desktop, Explorer, an editor) standard copy/move/link semantics, not just play inside our own window.
- **Root cause / design rationale** (why it looks like this):
  - **No `IDropSource`**: build a read-only `IDataObject` (12 slots) and hand it to `SHDoDragDrop(hwnd, pdata, NULL, dwEffect, &effect)`. With the third argument NULL the system uses its **default IDropSource**, which polls the real mouse button and Esc for us — that removes the whole `QueryContinueDrag`/`GiveFeedback` vtable, and Explorer's "Copy to X" drop-description bubble comes along for free. `SHDoDragDrop` is declared in `um/ShlObj_core.h` and lives in `shell32.lib` (already on prebuild's Windows link line from the earlier batches).
  - **Both data-fetching paths of the read-only object have to be implemented**: our own drag-in side (`wm_dnd_fetch`) calls `GetDataHere` (write in place into a caller-supplied HGLOBAL) while foreign targets often call `GetData`; both are real. `EnumFormatEtc` yields only the single current format for `DATADIR_GET`, `SetData`/`DAdvise`/`EnumDAdvise` answer `E_NOTIMPL` explicitly, and `QueryGetData` accepts only the entry whose `cfFormat` matches.
  - **Blocking semantics**: this call **blocks** until button release or cancel (OLE runs a message loop inside it). Drag-in callbacks for this window still land in the C queue and the host drains them on the next tick after it returns ⇒ "drag out and back into our own window" works, but there is **no live in-app hover highlight while the drag runs** (that is the in-app session's treatment, and only one session can run at a time). It also **must be called while the mouse button is still down** (the moment the threshold is crossed); calling it after release is not accepted by the system — `@ui.drag_source` fires exactly in the `Move` branch.
  - **Fallback contract (important)**: `@ui.drag_source(external=true)` tries the system run first and falls back to the **in-app session** only on `Err` (backend not wired / this kind has no system-level form / the run cannot start); `Ok` (delivered or user-cancelled) **never falls back** — by then the button is already released, so starting a session would drag out a phantom segment. The same example code therefore runs on all three platforms: the Linux/mac stub implementations always answer `Unsupported` and land back in-app.
  - **Effect numbering**: `DragEffect` (Rejected/Copy/Move/Link) matches Win32 `DROPEFFECT_*` value for value (0/1/2/4). `drag_effect_of_flag` accepts only those four; combined bits (3, 7) and out-of-range values are treated as "no deal" rather than guessed as copy. The `dwEffect` handed to the system at start is COPY|MOVE|LINK fully open, and Ctrl/Shift/Alt decide the actual one.
  - **Kind filter runs before the drag starts**: `Text` → `CF_UNICODETEXT` and `Paths` → `CF_HDROP` have system-level forms; `Html` (needs CF_HTML's `StartFragment`/`EndFragment` source-markup format) and `Img` (needs a bitmap / `METAFILEPICT`) are not offered in this batch, so `drag_data_has_system_form` stops them outright and OLE is never touched.
- **Pitfalls (C side, each hit for real)**:
  1. **`GetFullPathNameW` must not write back into its own input buffer.** CF_HDROP wants absolute paths; the first version called `GetFullPathNameW(buf, size, buf, NULL)` and a relative segment such as `rel\乙.txt` came out as `<cwd>\<truncated string>` junk — writing in place overwrites input that has not been consumed yet, and that is exactly what the receiving program gets. Fixed with **separate in/out buffers** (`wm_dsrc_one` for the wide conversion, `wm_dsrc_abs` for the full path); if resolution fails or overflows, the value is passed through as-is rather than swallowing the whole path.
  2. Worse: **the probe computed its expected value with the same in-place call**, so "each path parses back to the original path" stayed green against the broken implementation. The probe now uses separate buffers (`srcw`/`want`), assembles the expected string itself, and **writes the `\n` separator into the table before the conversion** (this was initially done the other way round). Rule of thumb: in a synthetic probe, deriving the expectation with the function under test is not a test.
  3. **`DROPFILES` and `SHDoDragDrop` are not visible to the library build**: `gui/win/stub.c` only included `<shobjidl.h>`, while the probe additionally included `<shlobj.h>`, so the probe was always green — but moon's `cl` invocation fails with 17 `C2065: "DROPFILES" undeclared` (and `SHDoDragDrop` only shows up as an implicit declaration, not a hard error — the easiest thing to miss). Adding `#include <shlobj.h>` makes both builds pass. The same "SDK headers are trimmed by include order and version macros, so a green probe does not mean a green library" pitfall, this time caused by **two different compile commands**.
- **Verification**: `experiment/drag_probe/dragdnd_probe.c` ends with **`DRAGDND-OK`** (**84 assertions**: the 40 drag-in ones plus 44 drag-out): after `wm_dsrc_fill`, `QueryGetData` positive/negative; the CF_HDROP blob from `GetData` is parsed by `DragQueryFileW` back into **independently computed** expected strings, all three entries present, relative paths absolutised (asserting characters 2 and 3 are `L':'`/`L'\\'`); `GetDataHere` matches `GetData` character for character on the first entry; the enumerator's `Next`/`Reset`/`Skip` behave, `Clone` answers `E_NOTIMPL`, `SetData` fails; feeding the same object back into this window's `IDropTarget` yields a payload identical to the original encoding (the round trip closes). Text case: wide characters match one by one, `GlobalSize == (wlen+1)*2`, round trip gives `Text`(1). Negative cases: kinds 2/3 have no system form, empty body, no buffer left behind after failure, and `wm_dragdnd_send` returns 0 without writing an effect for out-of-range ids, NULL payload, `len < 4` or a NULL `out_effect`. The probe source is `/W4`-clean (a C4389 signed/unsigned comparison and two C4456 shadowings fixed) and `stub.c` keeps only its two pre-existing C4996 warnings. MoonBit side: `core/drag_wbtest.mbt` +2 (effect numbering round-trips with `DragEffect::flag`, unknown flags mean Rejected; only Text/Paths have a system form, and a headless send always `Err`s leaving no half-open session), `ui/drag_wbtest.mbt` +2 (`external=true` falls back to the in-app session when the system run cannot start and still completes the drop, with `on_external` reporting it; `Html` data is judged `Unsupported` and falls back). `moon test core ui win` **355/355**, full library **941/942** (the single red is `si_machine` failing to read `HARDWARE\DESCRIPTION\System\BIOS:SystemManufacturer` — this virtualised machine's baseline red, unrelated to this batch), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links, and the local smoke run stays alive 4 seconds and terminates normally. Dragging onto the desktop or into Notepad can only be done by a person: item S27 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## Re-checking S26 on a real machine: dragging files in from Explorer showed the "no drop" cursor — `GetDataHere` alone cannot read the shell's payload (2026-10-15, real-hardware report from the user)

- **Environment**: Windows 10 19044 real machine, showcase's "窗口" page drag-and-drop section, source = **Explorer** (a genuine cross-process COM data object).
- **Symptoms**: dragging files onto the window showed the **prohibition cursor** and released nothing (S26 item ① failing), while the same code was fully green in the probe.
- **Root cause**: `wm_dnd_fetch` only used the `GetDataHere` leg (the comment at the time justified it as "spares the IMalloc release leg"). **The shell's data object usually implements only `GetData` for CF_HDROP** and answers `GetDataHere` with `E_NOTIMPL`/`MK_E_UNAVAILABLE` ⇒ `QueryGetData` recognises the format but nothing can be read back ⇒ `wm_dnd_extract` concludes "I don't recognise this payload" ⇒ `DragEnter` promises NONE, so the cursor is **prohibited from the very first moment** and no later write-back from MoonBit can rescue it (the initial value is already NONE).
- **Fix**: fetching now has **two legs** — try `GetDataHere` first (we hand over an empty `GMEM_MOVEABLE` and the block stays ours to `GlobalFree`), and on failure fall back to **`GetData`** (the callee allocates the medium, ownership lives in the medium, so it must be released with `ReleaseStgMedium` and never `GlobalFree`d). Because the release path now depends on the fetch path, the return changed from a bare `HGLOBAL` to `WmDndBlob{h, via_medium, medium}` plus `wm_dnd_blob_free`, and both branches of `wm_dnd_extract` use it.
- **Why the probe stayed green**: the probe's synthetic data object **implements both legs**, so "only one leg is tried" is invisible against it — exactly the class rule 5 warns about ("self-consistent unit tests ≠ interoperability passing"). `ProbeDo` gained `no_get_data_here`/`no_get_data` switches, and 9 new assertions pin that an object implementing only `GetData` must still be recognised as Paths(4)/Text(1) with a COPY promise, and that only an object refusing both legs may honestly answer NONE with an empty payload.
- **Diagnostic logging added along the way** (a real cross-process drag can only be run by a person, so failures need readings): with the environment variable `NATIVEGUI_DND_LOG=<absolute path>` set, `gui/win/stub.c` appends the key nodes of the drag chain to that file — `ole_init ready=…`, `enable slot=… hwnd=… ok/FAILED hr=…`, `enter slot=… recognized=… payload=… promised=… pt=…`, `over slot=… answered=…` (only when the answered effect changes, so it never floods), `set_effect slot=… effect=…`, `drop slot=… recognized=… eff=…`. With the variable unset it writes not a byte. That separates "OLE never came up" / "never registered" / "payload unreadable" / "MoonBit answered NONE" at a glance.
- **Verification**: the probe `experiment/drag_probe/dragdnd_probe.c` ends with **`DRAGDND-OK`**, **93 assertions** (84 → 93); `moon test core ui win` **355/355**, full library **941/942** (the one red is still `si_machine`'s BIOS registry reading — this machine's environment baseline), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links. Real-machine re-verification stays under item S26 in `_人工测试清单.md` (recommended: run once with `NATIVEGUI_DND_LOG` and paste the log back).

## "Reveal TODO.md in the file manager" did nothing: the absolute check only recognised a leading `/`, so Windows paths got glued into `<cwd>/C:\…` (2026-10-15, real-hardware report)

- **Environment**: Windows 10 19044 real machine, showcase's "系统集成" page "外部打开" section (the button passes the relative path `TODO.md`).
- **Symptoms**: clicking "在文件管理器显示 TODO.md" located nothing (it opened somewhere else, or nothing at all); the user also pointed out two missing entry points — **open a given file with the default software**, and **open a given file with a specified software**.
- **Root cause** (three things stacked):
  1. `launcher_abs_path` decided "absolute" only by a leading `/`, so `C:\…` and UNC `\\srv\…` were treated as relative and appended to the cwd, producing junk like `<cwd>/C:\a\b.txt`.
  2. Joining always used `/`, and `explorer /select,"…"` **does not select** a path with mixed separators (it usually just opens a folder, sometimes "Documents") — separators must be unified to `\` before handing over.
  3. `ShellExecuteW` returning >32 only proves "explorer started", so `Ok` was a false promise: when the path does not exist the system side succeeds silently. Added `yue_sys_path_exists` (`GetFileAttributesW` on Windows, `stat(2)` elsewhere) and one check before handing over, with a new `NotFound` variant (in both `FileManagerError` and the new `OpenFileError`).
- **A toolchain pit blown open on the way**: in this toolchain indexing a `String` yields a **UTF-16 code unit (UInt16)**, so rebuilding the string character by character as `Char` **corrupts non-ASCII paths** (one 3-byte UTF-8 sequence becomes three Chars). `launcher_win_path` therefore encodes to `Bytes` with `@utf8.encode`, replaces byte by byte, and decodes back.
- **Why it was never caught**: every normalisation assertion in `sys/launcher_wbtest.mbt` used POSIX shapes (`/a/b`, `/cwd`) — not one Windows shape — and `reveal`'s real action was only ever proven by the example. Rule of thumb: **path-normalisation white-box checks need a set per platform shape**, otherwise "only `/` counts as absolute" is invisible in tests.
- **Two new entry points**: `@sys.open_file(path)` (default program: Windows `ShellExecuteW "open"`, Linux `xdg-open`, macOS `open`) and `@sys.open_file_with(app, path)` (specified program: Windows goes through the new entry `yue_sys_shell_open_with`, with `lpFile` = program and `lpParameters` = the **quoted** path — otherwise a path containing spaces arrives as several `argv[1]` pieces; Linux/macOS use the detached spawn with argv passed directly, where spaces are inherently safe). Both put the **platform gate first** (unsupported platforms answer `Unsupported` before any path check); `app` may be a command name resolvable on PATH (`notepad.exe`) or a full executable path. The macOS "by application name" form (`open -a TextEdit`) is not wired — pass the executable path — and follows the mac platform batch.
- **Verification**: 4 new assertion groups in `sys/launcher_wbtest.mbt` — the three absolute shapes (`/`, drive + colon, `\\` and leading `\`) with `C:` drive-relative explicitly *not* absolute, Windows absolute paths never appended to the cwd, `launcher_win_path` leaving Chinese and already-correct strings unchanged in shape (including mixed input fed through `launcher_abs_path` and the normaliser together), live `sys_path_exists` readings (the working directory exists, an appended made-up name does not, empty is false), and the three **side-effect-free** negative cases of the open entry points (empty path / nonexistent path / empty program name). `moon test sys core` **333/334** (the single red is still `si_machine` reading `HARDWARE\DESCRIPTION\System\BIOS:SystemManufacturer` — this machine's environment baseline), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links, and the local smoke run stayed alive 4 seconds and was terminated by its Windows pid. Real-machine re-verification: item S28 in `_人工测试清单.md`.
- **Same-batch self-check gap closed on Linux (2026-10-15)**: the assertion above "win_path round-trip still exists" (`sys_path_exists(launcher_win_path(cwd))`) was hard-coded to Windows filesystem behaviour — Windows' stat accepts both separators, while on Linux a POSIX path turned into a backslash string never stats as existing, so CI Linux would necessarily go red. It now dispatches at run time on `sys_platform()`: Windows keeps the win_path round-trip, other platforms assert the `launcher_abs_path` normalisation round-trip instead (a path that exists is not broken by normalisation). The first landing of this section's "one assertion group per platform shape" lesson.

## Circles/arcs/rounded corners still look pixelated (second root cause): 4×4 sample counting gives only 17 coverage levels, and shallow edges measured 2 (2026-10-15, real-hardware report)

- **Environment**: Windows 10 19044 real machine; the backend is the pure-MoonBit rasterizer (`gui/render/raster*.mbt` — Windows/mac take this path, Linux uses cairo). An earlier round had already fixed miter sign, closed-stroke seams and rounded-fill snapping (see "Why arcs and rounded corners looked like pixel art"), yet the user's re-check still said "circles, arcs and rounded corners still look pixelated".
- **Symptoms**: brightness along curve edges **jumps** instead of fading — worst on small circles (switch knob, radio core, r≈6).
- **Readings first** (measure before changing; the throwaway probe was deleted afterwards): count the **distinct alpha levels** among partially covered pixels. Under the old implementation a r=25 filled circle had only **8** levels across the whole ring, a lw=2 ring **9**, an r=6 small circle **2** (values only 16 and 96), and a fractionally-centred circle 12.
- **Root cause**: coverage in `fill_polys` was **sample-point counting**: 4 sub-rows × 4 x-samples, each sample worth a fixed 16 ⇒ coverage could only be a multiple of 16 (17 levels). Horizontally four samples still yield 0/16/32/48/64, but **a sub-row was counted whole or not at all** ⇒ near-horizontal edges stepped by 64 (four levels per cell), so circle tops/bottoms and shallow diagonals smeared into stairs. Rounded-rectangle straight edges did not have this problem (`fill_round_rect`/`stroke_round_rect` use analytic SDF coverage, continuous) — which is why "the corners are a bit hard but the circles are worse".
- **Fix** (`gui/render/raster_fill.mbt`): ① vertical sub-rows 4 → `RASTER_AA_SUB = 8` (each worth 32); ② the horizontal side moved from "count samples" to the **exact intersection width** — a boundary pixel contributes `min(xb, px+1) − max(xa, px)` × sub-row weight, making coverage continuous in x. Fully covered interior pixels still take 256 directly, and the `s0 = ceil(xa)` / `s1 = floor(xb) − 1` test also moved from "sample centres" to "the whole column really is enclosed", which removes the old over-estimate for pixels that were only almost covered. Cost: the sub-rows doubled while x dropped its 4-way inner test — the render package's 53 cases run in 1.5s and the whole library in 20.8s, with no perceptible regression.
- **Readings after**: r=25 filled circle **22** levels (right-edge profile 28/94/146/185/220/235/248, a smooth ramp), lw=2 ring **37**, r=6 small circle **5**, fractionally-centred circle **45**, a 32° line **7**.
- **One trap recorded so nobody else steps on it**: an **exactly 45°** straight stroke legitimately has only about 2 levels (the half-plane `x+y = c` cuts every pixel at the same relative position; measured 2 for both lw=1 and lw=3) — that is geometry, not an AA defect. The first version of this check asserted "45° must have many levels" and turned the corrected code red. Level assertions must use **shallow-angle** segments and circles.
- **Verification**: `gui/render/painter_wbtest.mbt` gains the `aa_levels` helper and 2 assertions ("circle and ring edge grey levels": r=25 ≥16 levels and ≥60 partial cells, ring ≥20 levels, r=6 small circle ≥4; "shallow diagonal continuity": 32° lw=1.5 ≥5 levels) — all red under the old implementation. Same contract on both backends (cairo's analytic coverage sits far above the thresholds). `moon test render` **53/53**, full library **947/948** (the single red is still `si_machine`'s BIOS registry reading — this machine's environment baseline), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free. Real-machine look: item S29 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## The radio dot "solid core" assertion always went red on Linux: cairo area sampling and the pure rasterizer read edge cells of small circles differently (2026-10-15, Linux CI + local)

- **Environment**: Ubuntu 24.04 (X11/XFCE, cairo available so `Painter::new` picks a cairo session) against the Windows dev machine (cairo cannot start, falling back to the pure rasterizer); the same pixel assertion in `ui/form_wbtest` runs on **different backends**.
- **Symptoms**: after the 0213284 batch the CI Linux job went red in a row (`ui/form_wbtest.mbt` "单选标记的环与心之间留得出一条空白" failing with "圆心不是实心的") while the Windows job stayed green; reproduced locally on Linux at 941/942.
- **Root cause**: the assertion required all six diameter cells (indices 4..10) of the radio core to exceed 200, written against **pure-rasterizer readings** — 0213284's fill coverage treats "a pixel is a cell" (signed distance + 0.5-cell compensation), so the two diameter-end cells (centres 2.5 from the circle centre, radius 3) come out fully 255. cairo uses standard anti-aliased **area sampling**, where the same geometry leaves those end cells at ~196/197 (0.76 coverage), 3-4 short of the 200 threshold. The shape itself is correct on both backends (the alpha-60 shape assertions "ring-gap-core-gap-ring" are all green) — this is a **same method surface, different reading on small-size edge cells** gap, not an implementation error. The lesson is the same family as 6dff6c1's "assertions hard-coded to one machine's measurements": pixel-level assertions must either take the intersection of both backends' readings or avoid edge cells.
- **Fix**: the assertion now uses one contract for both backends — the "solid" assertion tightened from six diameter cells to the **four middle cells (5..9) all above 200** (full 255 ink under cairo, also full under the rasterizer), while "the diameter ends have ink" is already covered by the existing alpha-60 shape assertion; a comment spells out both readings and why the ends stay out of the check.
- **Verification**: local Linux `moon test ui` **180/180**, full library 14 packages **968/968** with zero red, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free; the tightened end (the rasterizer) stays covered by Windows CI (5..9 ⊆ the all-full 4..10 readings).

## Linux system-level drag-and-drop wired up (W23 platform batch): four signals feed the same session, press-event stash for starting drags, blocking semantics via a nested main loop (2026-10-15, requested by the user)

- **Environment**: Ubuntu 24.04 (X11/XFCE, GTK3). W23a/b had only landed the Windows half so far and the GTK branch was a failing stub (`supported` always 0); this batch adds the Linux side with zero changes to the facade, the event pump, the fallback semantics or showcase.
- **Design (the same wiring as the Windows branch)**: drag-in uses `gtk_drag_dest_set` on the GtkWindow (its coordinates are already client-area coordinates), with four signals — `drag-motion` (a two-phase `gdk_drag_status` answer + the first **asynchronous** payload fetch), `drag-leave` (close the session), `drag-drop` (only arm "drop awaiting payload", letting the `GTK_DEST_DEFAULT_DROP` default handler request the data), `drag-data-received` (cache the payload during motion and emit the late ENTER; on drop emit DROP + `gtk_drag_finish`). Events go into the process-wide queue and the host pumps `wm_dragdnd_poll` every tick; `core/drag.mbt`'s `drag_external_pump` is not changed by a line.
- **Pitfall ① (the motion-time payload is asynchronous)**: under X11/XDND a destination **cannot read selection data** mid-drag; it must call `gtk_drag_get_data`, and the data arrives via `data-received` (GTK then emits another motion). The ENTER event is emitted from `data-received` — if the pointer stops there will be no further motion, so ENTER cannot wait. A failed fetch (the source offers nothing at all) sets the `asked` flag and answers "deny" without retrying. The payload lives in one process-wide buffer (only one session at a time, the same rule as core's `drag_current` singleton).
- **Pitfall ② (starting a drag needs a GdkEvent, and the handling chain is outside the GTK dispatch stack)**: `gtk_drag_begin_with_coordinates` requires a button event, yet this stack starts drags on the tick where MoonBit handles the pointer Move — long after leaving GTK signal dispatch, so `gtk_get_current_event()` returns NULL. The press stashes a `gdk_event_copy` and releases it on up; with no stash (tests / keyboard-initiated) the call simply fails — `Err(Failed)` falls back to the in-app session, which is exactly the one-code-three-platforms contract.
- **Pitfall ③ (blocking semantics)**: Windows' `SHDoDragDrop` runs its own message loop and blocks until release; GTK's `gtk_drag_begin` returns immediately, so this batch nests `gtk_main_iteration()` in C until the `drag-end` signal (a 60-second `g_timeout` backstop, so a lost `drag-end` cannot hang the caller forever), and the effect is read back from `gdk_drag_context_get_selected_action` at `drag-end`.
- **Pitfall ④ (two sets of effect bit values)**: `GDK_ACTION_COPY/MOVE/LINK` are 2/4/8, unlike the Win32-derived `DROPEFFECT_*` (1/2/4) the facade follows — converted explicitly; several bits lit resolve to "no deal" (0) rather than a guess, matching core's `drag_effect_of_flag` accepting only 1/2/4.
- **Why there is no synthetic probe**: the Windows `drag_probe` can synthesize the whole chain in pure C because OLE's COM interfaces accept directly-fed objects; XDND motion is **pointer-driven**, so a cross-process drag cannot be synthesized. The Linux verification ladder is "compile + real-environment reading tests (`win/dragdnd_wbtest`: attach/idempotence/count/effect write-back; printed skips when headless) + smoke run + checklist items S26/S27".

- **Two small C-level snags along the way**: `GPOINTER_TO_ATOM` does not exist (GDK spells it `GDK_POINTER_TO_ATOM`), and `gtk_target_list_add_text_targets`/`add_uri_targets` require the `info` argument (a C compile-time error, easy to catch).
- **Verification**: `moon test win` **29/29** (1 new environment-reading test), full library 14 packages **975/975** with zero red, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, showcase links plus a local 8-second smoke run alive; real cross-process drags (Thunar/gedit ↔ the window) belong to the Linux items of S26/S27 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## Font-size "animation" was not an animation: the interpolation set excluded font size back then because "it means relaying out every frame" — while this stack already relayouts every frame (2026-10-15, real-hardware report)

- **Environment**: Windows 10 19044 real machine, showcase's "过渡与效果" page, the section formerly labelled "集合外属性" (`@ui.text(class=[style(font_size=13.0, transition_ms=300.0).hover(font_size=17.0)])`).
- **Symptoms**: hovering jumped font size 13 → 17 **in one step**, with no gradual change (the background colour beside it did transition).
- **Root cause** (two layers, both written into the design contract):
  1. `gui/style/transition.mbt`'s `lerp_style` covered only the three colours + border width + radius; every field outside the set took the target value;
  2. harder: `animatable_key`'s projection contained no `font_size` ⇒ a state switch that changed only the size was judged `at_shown == true` → `settle` → **the timer never even started**. §1.1's justification at the time was "a property that feeds layout must not interpolate — that equals relaying out the whole tree every frame".
- **Why that justification does not hold in this stack**: a paint frame is already `App::step` → `root.relayout(...)` → `paint` (the whole tree relaid out every frame — see the known difference "one frame is still a full-viewport redraw"), so interpolating font size costs no extra layout pass. What was really missing is the other half: **measurement read the base block** — the measure and baseline callbacks in `gui/ui/base.mbt` took the font size from `@style.resolved_by_id(id)`, while drawing read the interpolated `style_for(w)`. With the two disagreeing, glyphs were drawn large inside a box measured small, so it still read as "a jump plus clipping".
- **Checked against CSS first** (the user's rule: "implement what CSS implements, skip what it does not"): in CSS Transitions both `font-size` and `line-height` are animatable `<length>` values, and browsers indeed relayout each frame — so both join the set. `font-family`/`display` are discrete, and `opacity`/`box_shadow` take effect off the style-slot read path, so they stay out.
- **Fix**: `lerp_style` interpolates `font_size` and `line_height`; `animatable_key`'s projection carries both (otherwise a size-only switch is judged "state unchanged" → `settle` → **the timer never starts**, which is the main reason no gradient was visible); added `anim_shown_font_size(id)` / `anim_shown_line_height(id)` and `resolved_for_measure(id)` (the base block plus those two), and both measurement callbacks in `ui/base.mbt` switched to it. `resolved_for_measure` builds a **copy** through `merge(st, empty_style())` before overriding — `resolved_table` holds the same object, so writing the fields in place would corrupt the base block. Once an account settles, `shown` *is* the target (state buckets included), so after the hover ends the box still matches the drawing instead of snapping back.
- **Wiring found along the way** (without it the growth is simply cut off mid-way): when font size or line height changes the widget rect **grows**, while the local dirty rect was merged from the *previous* frame's rect, so the newly exposed ring never gets painted. `transition.mbt`'s `grows_layout(a)` detects exactly those two and `mark_dirty` dispatches between "whole-window dirty / local dirty" on it — colour/border-width/radius-only transitions keep the local path (P5's optimisation is not surrendered for them). `anim_needs_full_paint(id)` exposes that decision to tests.
- **Still outside the set**: `opacity` / `box_shadow` (they take effect where `apply` writes `Widget` fields; the paint walk does not read their slots per frame) and the sizing layout properties. Whether `box_shadow` deserves animation depends on whether the shadow can become a real drop shadow at all (CSS does animate shadow lists) — see the next section.
- **Contract kept in sync**: the showcase section renamed from "集合外属性 / 不参与插值的属性" to "插值范围 / 哪些属性会渐变" with the body rewritten; `docs/zh/design.md` §1.1's 过渡 row rewritten (font size and line height in the set, measurement reads the same value, those two repaint the whole window, reason changed from "would relayout every frame" to "we relayout every frame anyway"); P5's pending-recheck line gained a pointer to the changed contract so nobody files the old wording as a bug.
- **Verification**: `gui/style/transition_wbtest.mbt` — 1 case updated and 2 added: `lerp_style` gives 14 at the midpoint for 12→16 and 18 for line height 16→20 (under the old rule both took the target) while out-of-set `opacity` still takes the target directly; `step` starts the timer for a font-size-only change with readings 12.625 / 14.0 / 16.0 at 25/50/100 ms (smoothstep), reversing to the original value continues the reverse segment from the current 14.0 instead of an endpoint, and `anim_needs_full_paint` reports true (false for the colour-only account); a line-height-only change also starts an animation and reports 18.0; `resolved_for_measure` equals the same frame's `style_for` for **both** font size and line height, stays within [13,17] and [20,28], and leaves `resolved_by_id`'s base block unwritten. All of these are red under the old implementation. `moon test style ui core` **354/354**; real-machine look: item S30 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## The library test popped "You'll need a new app to open this …" on every run: ShellExecuteW does not fail on an unregistered protocol (2026-10-15, reported by the user)

- **Environment**: Windows 10 19044 dev machine; running `cd gui && moon test sys` (or the full library suite) repeatedly raised a system dialog.
- **Symptoms**: the user reported "when you run the tests it keeps saying 需要使用新应用以打开 libyue-invalid-probe 链接".
- **Root cause**: `sys/launcher_wbtest.mbt` carried a Windows probe `open_url("libyue-invalid-probe://no-such-scheme")` whose comment claimed it probed via the SpawnFailed semantics of an invalid target "**without popping a dialog**" — that sentence is wrong. `ShellExecuteW` goes through the shell's association/protocol dispatch: an **unregistered protocol does not return `SE_ERR_*`**, it hands the "which app should open this" picker to the user (equivalent to success), so the test neither got the expected `SpawnFailed` nor stayed off the desktop — it had a real system side effect on every run, and it also broke the division of labour in rule 6 (real-machine actions belong to the user).
- **Fix**: added the pure predicate `open_supported()` (true on Windows/Linux/macOS, runtime detection, touches no system), and the test now asserts only that plus cases that return **before anything is handed to the system** (`open_file("")` → `NotFound`, `open_file_with("", …)` → `SpawnFailed`, `reveal_in_file_manager("")` → `NotFound`, or `Unsupported` on macOS). Real opening stays in the example's buttons (S28, user-verified). `open_url`' macOS branch was filled in along the way (one `open`, the same shape as `open_file`), so `open_supported` and the dispatch tables of the three entry points now agree.
- **Rule going forward**: library tests must **not** call `ShellExecute*` / `xdg-open` / `open` against a real target. To prove a backend is wired, use a pure predicate; to prove what actually opens, write it into `_人工测试清单.md` and let a human run it. Before reaching for "invalid target → error variant" again, confirm that the invalidity really surfaces as an error **without launching system UI** — an unregistered protocol is precisely the case that does not.
- **Verification**: `moon test sys` **186/187** (the single red is still `si_machine` reading the BIOS registry — this machine's environment baseline), and no dialog appeared on the desktop while running the suite; `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module warning-free.

## The shadow looks harsh because it is a uniform-width ring, not a shadow — rebuilt as layered feathering, then removed outright after the real-machine review (2026-10-15, real-hardware report)

- **Environment**: Windows 10 19044 real machine, the shadow card on showcase's "过渡与效果" page.
- **Symptoms**: the user said the shadow effect is jarring — "it is now **a limited patch inside one region**, not really floating beneath the element", and offered the way out: if a real float cannot be done, cut it.
- **Root cause** (three layers):
  1. `Painter::box_shadow` drew **one stroke** (line width = spread, centreline pushed out by spread/2), so the whole ring had a single density with hard edges inside and out ⇒ it looked like a grey frame around the box, not a cast shadow;
  2. the call site in `ui/basic.mbt` passed `dx=dy=0`, and `Style` had only one `box_shadow : Double?` with **nowhere to put an offset, blur or colour** ⇒ always a symmetric halo, with no sense of being cast downward;
  3. why multi-layer had been avoided: `docs/zh/adaptation.md` recorded "hard shadows stacked into dark blobs at the four corners: neither backend has reverse arcs, so the inner/outer ring hole cannot be punched". That version filled an outer ring and punched a reversed inner one; the hole was never clean, so ink piled up at the corners. Layered fills **need no hole at all** — the body paints on top afterwards and hides the inner over-accumulation, which makes the route viable again (and matches CSS: a body with a transparent background does show its own shadow).
- **Fix**: `Painter::drop_shadow(x, y, w, h, radius, blur, dx, dy, color)` — the Minkowski sum of a rounded rectangle with a disc of radius e is again a rounded rectangle (width and height +2e, radius +e), so the same shape is filled N times from outside to in (roughly a 1 px transition band per layer, capped at 2..8 layers), each with `global_alpha = total density / N` (source-over accumulation is near-linear): densest against the body's edge, faded to zero at `blur`, and **corner and edge share the same density at equal distance**. `Painter::box_shadow` was deleted outright, with no compatibility shell left.
- **API aligned with CSS**: `Style` gains `shadow_x` / `shadow_y` / `shadow_color` and `box_shadow` now means the blur radius — the four together are CSS `box-shadow: blur x y color` (the colour's own alpha is the density; when it is not written, the built-in baseline `#00000040` applies). All reads go through `@style.shadow_of(s)`. `apply` writes **expansion = blur + |dx| + |dy|** into `Widget.shadow_paint`, computed from the **merged** base block (it used to look only at the `s` passed in this call, so a later apply that only added an offset left the expansion stale and the bottom edge got cut by the clip window).
- **Two corners fixed along the way** (a real shadow amplifies both): ① the viewport-culling test in `core/widget.mbt` used only the bare rect, so the soft ring disappeared the moment the body slid out of view — that test now inflates by `shadow_paint` too; ② the clip window was expanded by the old "spread" value, which is not enough once an offset exists — same root as ①, both now use blur+|dx|+|dy|.
- **Still to be assessed**: the layering is an **approximation** (N steps; at blur ≥ 8 the staircase is essentially invisible) and will be replaced once the render layer gains a real gaussian blur; `box_shadow` also stays outside the interpolation set (it takes effect where `apply` writes `Widget` fields and the paint walk does not read those slots per frame), so a "hover shadow grows" transition first needs those three moved into the slot-read path — a later batch.
- **Measured readings** (200×160 canvas, body 40,40,120×80, radius 8, blur 8, dy 6, `#00000040`): left edge from inside out `57 57 57 51 44 37 30 23 16 8 0` (monotone, ten levels); below at y=124/128/132/136 = `57/44/16/0` versus above at y=48/40/36 = `57/23/0` ⇒ the bottom casts the extra 6 px of offset; at equal distance the corner reads `34` against the edge's `37` (the old version either missed a patch there or piled into a dark blob); the body centre reads `57` (inner accumulation, covered by the body afterwards).
- **Verification**: `render/painter_wbtest.mbt` replaces the old `box_shadow` case and adds 2 (direction + gradient + corner/edge equality; and four "no shadow" inputs that must leave no ink); `ui/basic_wbtest.mbt` adds a sixth assertion (a 24-high spacer pushes the card down to y=24, then ink cells are counted in the bands **above** and **below** the box — with `shadow_y` the lower band grows and the upper shrinks). `moon test render` **54/54**, `moon test ui` **180/180**, full library **976/977** (the single red is still `si_machine`'s BIOS registry reading), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` and the examples module error- and warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links, local smoke alive 4 s then terminated by its Windows pid. Real-machine look: item S31 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## Four real-hardware findings (click-to-screen latency / keyboard stuck at 65507 / space not activating / radio circle clipped): GTK frame dispatch must run on the spot, the IM needs a focus gate, click ripples need a whole-window fallback, and marker row height must not collapse with the font (2026-10-15, Linux real-hardware report)

- **Environment**: Ubuntu 24.04 (X11/XFCE, an ibus input-method session), showcase on the user's machine. Four reports: ① in the form section's stepper, the number did not move while clicking and jumped ~1s after the hand left; ② the keyboard-test section's echo stayed at 65507 (= X11's Control_L) no matter which key was pressed; ③ space did not toggle radio/checkbox; ④ the radio circle rendered high and was clipped. Toasts showing only the first one shares root ①.
- **Root cause ① (GTK's draw signal needs a main-loop iteration to dispatch)**: `wm_present` only called `gtk_widget_queue_draw` after storing the frame, and this stack's pump `wm_wait` runs `wm_pump()` only when an **fd is ready** — on ticks where a timer expires or the poll times out, `ready=0` means no iteration, so the frame lay in GDK's queue waiting for the next X event. With no follow-up event after a click, the blit stalled until the next event source (measured ~1s). **Fix**: `wm_present` now **dispatches one non-blocking round on the spot** after queue_draw (`while gtk_events_pending() gtk_main_iteration_do(FALSE)`, capped at 8 against accidental re-entrancy; button/key events re-entered during the iteration still enqueue into this window's queue as usual and are drained next tick). The second toast not appearing has the same root: the frame painted by push's invalidate also lay in the queue.
- **Root causes ②③ (ibus eats character keys into the commit channel)**: `wm_on_key` called `gtk_im_context_filter_keypress` unconditionally — in a session with ibus the IM consumes every character key (reported through the commit channel, and commits whose focus is not an input box are dropped), so the key-event channel kept only the **modifier keys** the IM does not eat (65507 = Control_L). Space is a character key, so radio/checkbox `KS_SPACE` activation naturally never received it. **Fix**: an IM focus gate — C-side `wm_im_set_active(id, on)` plus `WmWindow.im_active`, filtering only when the MoonBit-side focused control is an input box (`im_context_of` has a value); `App::pump_ime` syncs it at focus changes. The Windows branch's IMM does not filter ordinary keys, so it gets a link-only stub.
- **Root cause ④ (marker row height collapses with font metrics)**: the radio/checkbox row height is decided by the text line box; the test host (Noto) has a 19 line height, which fits a 14 px marker, but the real-machine XFCE default font's line box can be shorter than 14 px — the marker then breaks out of the row and the circle's top gets covered by what is above it (diagnostic reading: on the test host both dot groups are perfectly symmetric at y=2.5/h=14, ruling out a layout-structure problem). **Fix**: the radio/checkbox rows `set_min_height(fixed(20.0))`, so marker height no longer depends on font metrics (the switch's pill is a fixed 20 px and never collapsed — unchanged).
- **Along the way (a core-layer click-ripple defect, all platforms)**: after pointer events the host only marked the hover/capture chain **locally** dirty, yet the Store changed by `on_click` usually affects siblings outside that chain (the stepper's number: the display control does not subscribe and reads live at paint time), so the dirty region does not cover it and the blit keeps stale pixels. **Fix**: pointer **Up (a settled click) always falls back to whole-window dirty** — clicks are low-frequency interaction, a full frame is acceptable; Move/Down keep their local dirtying.
- **Verification**: full library 14 packages **975/975** with zero red, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, examples `--deny-warn` warning-free, showcase links plus a local 8-second smoke run alive; real-hardware re-check belongs to S30 in `_人工测试清单.md`.
- **One item waiting for a real-hardware reading (untouched this batch)**: "the sidebar menu can receive focus through Tab" — headless diagnostics show the sidebar `menu_sections` tree's `focus_ids()` is **empty** (menu items carry no focus_id and were never in the Tab chain), so there is no component-layer defect to fix; when re-verifying, please screenshot which element the focus ring lands on after pressing Tab, and the next pass locates from that reading.

- **Follow-up (same day, removed on the user's call)**: the layered version measured correctly on its own (ten monotone steps, corner equal to edge, cast downward by the offset), yet **the real-machine look still did not satisfy** — after re-checking, the user said "阴影悬浮还是去掉吧". So the whole thing was removed: the four `Style` fields (`box_shadow`/`shadow_x`/`shadow_y`/`shadow_color`) with their setters, `shadow_of`, `Painter::drop_shadow`, and `Widget.shadow_paint` (including the clip-window and viewport-culling inflation) were all deleted, and showcase's two shadow cards plus the `docs/zh/design.md` §1.1 "效果" row and the P4 row were re-worded in step; no "accepted but does nothing" field was left behind — that would amount to pretending the capability exists. Two lessons: ① **self-consistent numbers are not a pass on looks** — for visual work in this project the real-machine review is the only signature, and readings can only help localize; ② if a drop shadow returns, solve **a real gaussian blur** first (a layered approximation carries a staircase naturally at 1× physical pixels with no HiDPI upscaling) rather than stacking more API on the approximation.

## Browser DOM capture came back all ok=false on both platforms: JS evaluation replies truncated to half a JSON by the 768-byte event text slot (2026-10-15, Linux + Windows real machines at once)

- **Environment**: examples/browser on both platforms; all four buttons ("抓正文/抓链接/抓 meta/抓结构") echoed `ok=false`.
- **Root cause**: `capture_dom`'s reply carries `JSON.stringify({title,url,…})` (body text up to 4000 characters, 200 links, 100 metas), while JS evaluation replies went through the **event channel** — the event text slot is `WB_EV_TEXT=768` and `wb_push` hard-truncates with `strncpy`, so any reply past 768 bytes becomes **half a JSON**; MoonBit's `vsc_json_parse` then necessarily returns None ⇒ `ok=false` with the leftover fragment as raw. The two platform stubs are mirror implementations sharing one constant, so Linux (WebKitGTK) and Windows (WebView2) died together — the "replies ride the event slot" design could never hold the DOM tier's volume from the day it was written, and it stayed hidden in the showcase era because those demo replies happened to be short.
- **Fix**: JS evaluation replies now go through a **per-view dedicated buffer** (cap `WB_EVAL_TEXT_MAX=64KB`, the same scheme as the drag payload buffer) — the C-side completion callbacks (GTK `evaluate_javascript_finish` / WebView2 `ExecuteScriptCompleted`) store the full text in `WbView.eval_text`, the kind=7 event carries only the sequence number with empty text; a new extern `wb_eval_text(id,out,cap)` fetches the full text (returning the total length; >cap means you read the truncated prefix); MoonBit's pump reads the big buffer for kind=7 (`WB_EVAL_CAP=65536`) while the other events keep the 768 slot (short text like titles/URLs fits there). The mac stub gained an empty implementation in step.
- **Verification**: `moon test web` **18/18** (1 new long-reply regression: a complete JSON with 4000 characters of body text and 200 links parses whole, and it is red under any truncating path), full library 14 packages **978/978** zero red, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, examples `--deny-warn` warning-free, browser links plus a local 8-second smoke run alive; both platforms' real-machine re-verification belongs to S32 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## A third layer on curve pixelation: the fully-covered run was written as `cov[px] = 256` inside the band loop, so the vertical direction never accumulated (2026-10-15, real-hardware report)

- **Environment**: Windows 10 19044 real machine. After the previous batch replaced "count 4×4 samples" with "8 sub-rows + exact horizontal width", the user re-checked and still found the curves less smooth than on Linux.
- **Why that batch did not cure it**: it only verified the **right-edge profile** (a vertical boundary, where exact horizontal width pays off immediately). But inside the band loop the fully-covered run was written `cov[px] = 256` — an **assignment**: as soon as one band enclosed the column, that row was recorded as full coverage, so **the vertical direction never really accumulated**. Near-horizontal boundaries (a circle's top and bottom) and the corner regions around vertices therefore stayed all-or-nothing, producing profiles like `0 → 249 → 255`.
- **Fix** (`gui/render/raster_fill.mbt`): ① coverage now accumulates `+= area`, first into a Double-side buffer (`cov_f`) advanced slice by slice and quantized once at row end (rounding per segment would accumulate ±2); ② "band-centre sampling" became **analytic integration per slice**: each row gathers the edges crossing it into a row-local active table, then cuts the row at "band boundaries ∪ every active edge's endpoints clipped to the row". A slice contains no vertex, so both span boundaries are linear in y and their overlap with a pixel column has a closed form (`span_slice_cover`: the integrand is piecewise linear, with breakpoints only where a left or right boundary hits `px`/`px+1` or where the two meet, so the trapezoid formula is exact). The band count is thereby demoted from "source of the quantization staircase" to "bounds the intra-slice reordering error of two edges", and 8 sub-rows went back to 4 bands with no cost increase.
- **A real bug fixed on the way**: a degenerate span where the left and right ends coincide at the slice's top or bottom was skipped wholesale by `if ra0 <= la0 || ra1 <= la1 { continue }`, yet that slice really is a triangle — so ink disappeared around triangle apices, measured 33-44 levels off against an independent reference. Removing the skip and letting the integrator handle it (it already carries the `la=ra` breakpoint) is correct. **That judgement is worth writing down: measure it against an independent reference — using your own implementation's output as the expectation is exactly how the previous batch stayed "self-consistently wrong".**
- **How accuracy is proven**: a reference that shares no code with the implementation (32×32 grid sampling + ray casting for polygons inside/outside / a per-point radius test for circles) measures the maximum deviation — 1-2 levels for polygons (old: 33-44), 7-9 for circles, of which about 8 levels come from the **bezier flattening tolerance of 0.1 device pixels** itself (the same as cairo's default), not from the coverage algorithm. Both became permanent regressions: `worst_cover_gap` (4 shapes ≤4 levels, including a flat triangle with a long near-horizontal edge) and `ref_circle_cover` (r=25 circle ≤12 levels). All red under the old implementation.
- **Readings before/after**: r=25 circle partial cells 100→180, grey levels 22 (integer centre) / 77 (fractional centre); r=6 small circle 24→44 cells; r=3.5 (radio core) 28 partial cells. The render package went 1.5s→2.0s (including the two new reference comparisons) while the whole library stayed 20.4s (from 20.8s).
- **Verification**: `moon test render` **54/54**, full library **976/977** (the single red is still `si_machine`'s BIOS registry reading — this machine's environment baseline), `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, `moon build showcase --target native` links, local smoke alive 4 s. Real-machine re-check still belongs to item S29 in `_人工测试清单.md` (look especially at circle tops/bottoms and shallow diagonals).


## Toasts eaten by the second click + the sidebar keyboard gap: the layer's outside-click policy must be declared per overlay, and pass-through belongs at the hit-test layer (2026-10-15, Linux real-hardware report)

- **Environment**: showcase on device. Reports: ① with a toast on screen, clicking the trigger button a second time "ate" the first toast; waiting for the toast to close made the next trigger work, and so did opening and closing a dialog in between. ② The sidebar menu was unreachable by Tab and had no focus ring.
- **Root cause ① (exactly the "separate batch" 505f3ba left open)**: the overlay layer is full-window and hit-testing runs back to front — **every click hits the layer first**; the layer's `on_pointer` consumed any "outside all overlays" press unconditionally and ran `overlay_hide_top()` on release. Toasts have no "dismiss on outside click" semantics yet followed the same rule: clicking a button during the two seconds a toast is up delivered nothing to the button (no second toast) while that same click wrongly dismissed the first — read together, exactly "the second click eats the first". Once the toast expires (or a dialog round trip gives the expiry callback time to reset `open_id`) the layer hides and clicks reach content again, hence "fine after a while / after a dialog".
- **Fix ① (click policy + hit-level pass-through)**: `OverlayHost.items` grew from `(id, w)` to `OverlayItem{id, w, dismiss}` — `overlay_show_at` takes `dismiss_on_outside` (default true, so menu/dialog modality is unchanged) and `toast_layer` passes false. **Merely returning false from the layer's `on_pointer` is not enough**: the hit chain excludes page controls before the layer is ever asked (full-window, appended last), so pass-through is done at the **hit level** — when the hit lands on the layer itself (inside no child overlay) and the topmost item declares pass-through, `route_pointer` temporarily sets the layer `visible=false`, re-hit-tests once and restores it, so the click/hover go back to the page control (layout untouched, rects kept). Recorded trade-off: stacked overlays consult the **topmost one only** — a toast sitting over a dialog lets outside clicks fall through to the page without closing the dialog.
- **Root cause ②**: the a1b2c89 batch wired the form family into the Tab chain but left `menu_sections`' items out — `focus_ids()` was empty (proved by the previous batch's headless diagnostic), so Tab had nowhere to land and no focus ring could be drawn.
- **Fix ②**: `menu_item` gained `focusable`/`step` parameters (the same keyboard contract as segmented): a declared `focus_id` enters the Tab chain, space/Enter selects the item, ↑/←/↓/→ cycle the selection inside the group, and `on_draw` traces a theme-coloured ring at the end when focused; `menu_sections` wires all its items.
- **Verification**: `moon test ui` **182/182** (2 new: outside clicks pass through a toast layer without dismissing it + the control layer still consumes and dismisses, and the menu keyboard chain is reachable with space/arrows effective — wrapping from the first UP to the last item is the correct shape of wrap semantics), full library 14 packages **978/978** zero red, `cd gui && moon check --deny-warn` warning-free, showcase links plus an 8-second smoke run alive; real-machine re-check belongs to S33 in `_人工测试清单.md`.

## Renderer coverage-precision assertions went permanently red on CI Linux: single-backend readings hard-coded, again (2026-10-15, Linux CI)

- **Environment**: the "deviation against an independent analytic reference" assertions added by 610bf7f (the third-layer rasterizer coverage fix) measured 1-2 levels for polygons and 7-9 for the circle on Windows (pure rasterizer), and the thresholds were written as ≤4/≤12 from those readings; the CI Linux job runs the cairo backend — the triangle measured 18, the flat triangle 16, the circle 21, **all over threshold**, red in a row.
- **Root cause**: cairo's own AA algorithm differs from the "32×32 grid sampling + ray casting" reference more than the rasterizer does on diagonal edges (16-21 levels) by nature; the thresholds left headroom only for raster readings, so cairo cannot pass — the same family as the radio-core assertion (cairo area sampling vs raster pixel-cell readings), the fourth time this repo steps on the same shape.
- **Fix**: the thresholds now take the **intersection of both backends** — polygons ≤20 (cairo's 16-18 passes, the old implementation's 33-44 stays red), circle ≤24 (cairo's 21 passes, old 33-44 stays red), keeping the regression's teeth; the assertion messages carry the measured level count so the next red shows the magnitude at a glance, and the comments record where each side's readings come from.
- **Verification**: local Linux `moon test render` **54/54**; the Windows side is re-verified by CI (the raster readings 1-2/7-9 sit far below the new thresholds).
- **Rule (recorded once more)**: pixel- or number-level assertions must first ask "what is the other backend's reading" and take the intersection. This repo's assertion failures now run four-of-a-kind: the radio dot core, the launcher round trip, the dragdnd initial effect value, and this coverage precision — all the same shape.

## macOS backend, first batch (mac platform batches 1-8, 2026-10-15; compile/link proven by the CI macOS job, on-device items still pending)

- **Environment**: GitHub Actions `macos-latest` (Apple Silicon; clang and the SDK frameworks come with Xcode CLT). **The development machine here is Ubuntu/X11 and cannot touch the macOS window server**, so "compiles and links" is proven by CI, while "runs and looks right" is on-device work per AGENTS rule 6 (checklist: section T of `_人工测试清单.md`).
- **Branch shape (same "one stub.c, several branches, prebuild macro" rule as Linux/Windows)**: `WM_STUB_MAC` in `gui/win/stub.c` (Cocoa, Objective-C), `WM_STUB_MAC` in `gui/render/stub.c` (ImageIO, plain C), `WM_STUB_MAC` in `gui/text/stub.c` (CoreText, plain C), `WB_HAVE_WKWEBVIEW` in `gui/web/webkit_stub.c` (WebKit, Objective-C). **Every placeholder branch gains a `&& !defined(__APPLE__)` guard**: on macOS the macro-less native-stub pass must compile to an empty translation unit, otherwise it double-defines the prebuild archive. The Darwin branch of prebuild compiles the archives with `cc -x objective-c -fobjc-arc` (`link_configs` has no compile-time fields - `c_flags` is silently ignored, same finding as GTK/Pango) and hands out `-framework` flags per package.
- **Pitfalls CI threw at us on the first round** (worth writing down so they don't recur):
  1. CoreText puts **the text object first** - `CTLineDraw(line, ctx)` - opposite to the `CGContext` family intuition;
  2. `CFAttributedStringReplaceString` / `CFAttributedStringSetAttribute` take a **`CFRange`**, not location + length, and the length comes from `CFAttributedStringGetLength` (`CFStringGetLength` does not compile: different type name);
  3. non-mac one: `kill` in the POSIX arm of `sys_stub.c` was reached through some other header on Linux, while macOS clang treats an implicit function declaration as an error - explicit `#include <signal.h>`;
  4. Cocoa detail: ARC-managed **properties can only be read with `.`** (`s.win`), while the `@public` plain fields of the same struct use `->` - two notations in one function is a real trap; `setAllowsMultipleSelection:` / `setCanChooseDirectories:` are declared on `NSOpenPanel`, not `NSSavePanel` (a save panel is single-choice by nature);
  5. two "warning level but genuinely broken" ones: `NSTextInputClient`'s marked-text method is the **three-part** `setMarkedText:selectedRange:replacementRange:` (writing it with two parts earns only a `-Wprotocol` warning, and the input-method composition channel never connects at runtime), and `resignFirstResponder` returns **`BOOL`** (declaring it `void` is `-Wmismatched-return-types`). The macOS stub gate therefore reads warnings too, not just errors.
- **Pitfalls, rounds two and three - "no longer declared in the current SDK" and "wrong name"**:
  1. `setCanShowHiddenFiles:` (NSOpenPanel), `setSendActionOn:` (the status-item button) and `setApplicationNameForUserAgent:` (WKPreferences) are **not publicly declared on the macOS 26 SDK** (clang reports `no visible @interface` / `no known instance method`), while they do exist on older SDKs. One shape covers all three: an **informal declaration** on `NSObject` keeps the selector visible to the compiler, and every call site asks `respondsToSelector:` first - if the runtime has no such method we fall back to the default behaviour (the show-hidden-files switch, tray right-clicks and the UA suffix stop working) and **we do not guess at replacement names**.
  2. `WKWebsiteDataStore` has no `dataStoreWithURLStoragePath:error:` (that name was inferred from the Linux `WEBKIT_DATA_DIR` semantics and does not compile). The public one is **`+[WKWebsiteDataStore dataStoreForIdentifier:]`** - macOS 14+, takes an `NSUUID`, and needs a bundle identifier (libyue uses exactly this at `nativeui/mac/browser_mac.mm:86`). A directory path cannot be fed to it, so data_dir is hashed into a stable UUID (two FNV-1a 64-bit chains, then RFC 4122 version/variant bits - `NSUUID` only accepts well-formed strings): the same directory keeps one session across runs. Where that cannot be honoured we still fall back to `nonPersistentDataStore` and say so through `wb_persistence()`.
  3. The cookie-store property of `WKWebsiteDataStore` is named **`httpCookieStore`** (`.cookieStore` does not compile; clang's fix-it supplies the right name).
  4. **An Objective-C parameter must not be named `id`**: `wb_evaluate(int64_t id, ...)` shadows the type name, so the block signature `^(id result, NSError *error)` parses as a variable declaration and one parameter name produces a cascade of `type-id cannot have a name` plus a dozen `undeclared identifier` errors.
- **Display enumeration (mac platform batch 8, `sys/monitor.mbt` plus the `__APPLE__` arm of `sys_stub.c`)**: CoreGraphics covers it in one family - `CGGetOnlineDisplayList` ("online" only, i.e. attached and powered; macOS has no public list of attached-but-off displays, so the mac side never yields `connected=false` entries), `CGDisplayBounds` for the origin in points, the scale derived as "current mode pixel width / logical width" to turn origins and sizes into **physical pixels**, `CGDisplayCopyAllDisplayModes` for the mode table (deduplicated by pixel width x height x refresh - CG lists several timing configurations for the same pixel size and duplicates mean nothing to layout; when the table is unavailable the current mode is emitted alone), `CGDisplayScreenSize` for millimetres. **The two mode predicates are no longer declared in the current SDK** (`CGDisplayModeIsCurrentMode` / `CGDisplayModeIsPreferred` - clang says `call to undeclared function`; only these two were pulled from this family, `CGDisplayCopyAllDisplayModes` / `GetPixelWidth` / `GetRefreshRate` are still there): "current" is now decided by "same pixel size and same refresh rate as `CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode`", which appears exactly once in the deduplicated list and is equivalent at reading level; `preferred` has no public signal, so it is reported as 0 rather than faked with the current mode. Three things it cannot give, stated plainly: a name (`NSScreen.localizedName` is out of reach for a plain-C stub and CG has no public name - built-in panels are `Built-in`, others `Display-<CGDirectDisplayID>`, machine-specific strings like the other platforms' output names), millimetres (0 when the engine withholds them), and built-in refresh rates (`CGDisplayModeGetRefreshRate` reports 0 = unknown for some built-in modes; 0 is passed through rather than a faked 60 Hz). `MonitorInfo` needs no scale field: every number in the list is already physical pixels, the same basis as xrandr.
- **Deliberate differences from the other two platforms, now part of the contract**:
  - **Event loop**: no `[NSApp run]`. `wm_wait` uses `nextEventMatchingMask:untilDate:` (AppKit's own blocking fetch), `wm_wakeup` posts one `NSApplicationDefined` marker event to wake it - the macOS equivalent of "the loop belongs to MoonBit" + "no C-to-MoonBit callbacks". Known limit: during window drag / live resize AppKit enters tracking mode and our pump does not see those events (T6b).
  - **Pixel scale**: the stack speaks physical pixels, Cocoa speaks points; one conversion per boundary using the window's screen `backingScaleFactor`. The drawing view deliberately **does not override `isFlipped`** - in a non-flipped view `CGContextDrawImage`/`CTLineDraw` land memory row 0 at the top, which matches this stack's Bitmap; flipping the CTM would render text upside down.
  - **Premultiplication rounding belongs to ImageIO/Quartz**: Quartz composites only in premultiplied space, so an RGB bitmap context cannot give us a non-premultiplied form and the `(c*a+127)/255` step other platforms take is skipped here. Byte order and semantics are unchanged; the difference is +/-1 rounding, and the "encode -> decode -> re-encode is byte-stable" criterion must be read as "stable against ImageIO itself" on macOS.
  - **GIF animation falls back to a still frame on macOS**: per-frame compositing needs the frame rectangle plus disposal method, and disposal is not on Apple's public GIF property list - without on-device proof we do not guess. `img_anim_decode_file` returns 0 and the component shows frame 1.
  - **Menu / tray / notification are app-level**: `wm_menu_apply` becomes `setMainMenu:` (the menu bar belongs to the application, last apply wins), tray is `NSStatusItem`, notification is `NSUserNotification` - **whether a non-bundle binary can actually present a notification is an on-device question** (T4e).
  - **Taskbar progress: unsupported on macOS** - the dock badge is a text counter; it cannot express progress, and we do not fake it.
  - **webview**: `wb_signal_mask()` returns 10 on mac - downloads (need macOS 15 `WKDownload`) and permission requests have no public hook, so we report exactly which proofs are missing; `wb_persistence()` probes "macOS 14+ **and** a bundle identifier", a bare binary returns 0 and falls back to a non-persistent store.
- **Backend choices across `sys`**: public CLI whenever it suffices - `open` / `open -R` (reveal with selection), `sw_vers` / `ioreg` / `sysctl` (system info), `osascript` for `volume settings` and the System Events desktop picture, LaunchAgents plist + `launchctl load/unload` (autostart), `lpstat` / `lp` (macOS ships CUPS - same line as Linux, **a declared choice, not a fall-through to the Linux branch**). Only kernel-ish readings go into the stub: `hw.memsize` + `host_statistics64`, `kern.boottime`, `CGEventSourceSecondsSinceLastEventType` for idle. Four families stay explicitly unsupported behind a platform gate: windowctl (Accessibility requires user consent), nightlight (CoreBrightness is private), powerprofile (`pmset` does not match the three-scheme semantics), media (no MPRIS counterpart).
- **The first real `moon test` run on the macOS job: 4 red out of 851, all "declared contract not followed through in code", not broken plumbing**:
  1. **The animation fallback kept the picture but lost the size**: when `Animation::new_from_file` returns None, `ui/gif.mbt` set no width/height, so the node occupied 0x0 - the image itself decodes fine (`ui_decode_guard()` passes on mac; ImageIO gives the 120x120 first GIF frame), it just could not be laid out. The None branch now follows the still image's size, and both animation tests (`render/image_wbtest`, `ui/basic_wbtest`) became **probe-branching**: no animation support means we assert "the still path yields the first frame + the component queues no self-advance + it paints ink", while platforms that do decode animation keep the full frame-advance assertions (no coverage lost on Linux/Windows).
  2. **The underline assertion counted rows**: `text_decoration` was checked as "one more inked row", but on macOS the 1px line falls inside the last glyph row's line box, so the row count stays equal and the test goes red. It now compares **inked pixel counts**, which is what "was an underline drawn" actually means - one criterion for all three platforms.
  3. **The launcher platform gate had gone stale**: the test still asserted "anything that is not Linux gives `Unsupported`", while batch 5 gave macOS a real `open`-based implementation. Mac now shares the Windows shape: probe with an invalid target and only require "no longer `Unsupported`" (`Ok` or `SpawnFailed`), which opens neither a browser nor a Finder window.
- **App discovery (batch 13): two things the public surface cannot give**. An `.app` bundle's `Contents/Info.plist` may be a **binary plist** (common for third-party apps), which plain-text reading gets no keys from - the entry then falls back to the bundle directory name rather than the application vanishing from the list. Localized names live in `.lproj/<lang>.lproj/InfoPlist.strings`, while the public plist keys only give `CFBundleDisplayName` / `CFBundleName`, so `locale_name` equals `name` and `categories` stays empty (macOS has no counterpart to desktop Categories). One difference for the executable lookup: a process started from the Dock/Finder **has no shell PATH**, so `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/opt/homebrew/sbin` must be appended from the fixed list, otherwise every Homebrew tool on Apple Silicon is reported missing.
- **`ld: warning: ignoring duplicate libraries: '-lyue_win_stub_mac'` is expected noise - do not "fix" it**: the macOS link log prints one to three such lines per test executable, because the same archive appears twice in one link line.
