Packages reach each other through **direct extern links** (web needs `wm_surface_container` from the win stub, sys needs `wm_file_*`), which are not MoonBit import edges, so the win archive has to be in the link_flags of win, sys and web each; a final exe that links those packages together duplicates it. ld64 simply ignores the later copy - the link result and its meaning are unchanged - and GNU ld tolerates the same thing on Linux without saying so. Removing the warning would mean turning those externs into package-level imports (wrapping the native artifact behind a facade layer), which costs far more than one warning line.
- **Media line on macOS (batch 17)**: neither stub needed changes - `ffmpeg_stub.c` has always been platform-free (ffmpeg's API is cross-platform) and `audio_stub.c` embeds miniaudio, a vendored single-header implementation library that picks CoreAudio under `__APPLE__` on its own. Only the **two prebuild scripts** needed a Darwin branch: `ffmpeg-mbt` probes with pkg-config, the same route as Linux (missing → non-zero exit with a `brew install ffmpeg` hint; the difference is that brew's `.pc` files and headers are not on the default search path, so `/opt/homebrew/lib/pkgconfig` and `/usr/local/lib/pkgconfig` are spliced into `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`, and includedir/libdir are asked from pkg-config rather than hardcoded, so one script covers Apple Silicon and Intel); `gui-media` hands out `-framework CoreAudio -framework AudioToolbox -framework Foundation` and **must not copy the Linux library list**: `-ldl` lives inside libSystem on macOS and `-latomic` has no counterpart at all, so copying that list fails the link with "library not found". From this batch the macOS job runs `brew install ffmpeg` and puts the two example mains that depend on the media packages (systemprobe / native-web) back into the build step - which compiles the ffmpeg and miniaudio stubs on a real macOS machine and actually links that framework set.
- **How this is verified**: the CI macOS job starts with a **native stub compile gate** - the same clang flags prebuild uses (`-fsyntax-only -O2 -x objective-c -fobjc-arc -D<macro>`) over the four mac stubs plus the plain-C `sys_stub.c`. That step is not optional: `moon check` never compiles those stubs, so an API-shape error only surfaces at `moon test` link time, and there it shows up as a pile of `Undefined symbols` (the archive failed to build, so its link entry is never handed out) with no trace of the real cause. Then: `moon check` + 12-package `moon test` + the library build by explicit package names + examples/hello link, and a final `moon run examples/hello` that must survive to the timeout (the human checklist in section T covers what CI cannot).
- **What CI has now proven (2026-10-15, run 38616056855 green on all three platforms)**: all five mac stubs compile against the current SDK; `moon check` is warning-free; 12-package `moon test` passes - including the readout loops that only run on a real macOS machine (`appfind` scanning `/Applications` and getting applications, `appfind_executable("sh")` hitting one; the `sys` family's `host_statistics64` / `kern.boottime` / idle readings; `render`'s ImageIO decode and `text`'s CoreText measurement), plus `hello` **creating a window and pumping its loop** on the runner's logged-in session until the 20s timeout.
- **Still needs eyes on real hardware** (what CI cannot give): the T1-T6 look-and-feel items (Retina appearance, inline input-method composition, loop behaviour while dragging a window, whether a notification presents from a non-bundle process), display enumeration across several external monitors, whether launchd actually picks up a freshly written plist, and osascript automation consent.

## macOS alignment batch (2026-10-18, closing the 17-function gap recorded by merge 717d246 on a real Mac; first full-workspace `moon test` 1236/1236 on macOS hardware)

- **Window surface filled in (hide/is_hidden/opacity/layer/transparent_bg/im_set_active/hotkey_\*)**:
  1. **`wm_show` must clear the `hidden` flag** - Cocoa's `orderOut:` does not lose the frame, so no position restore is needed (deliberately unlike the GTK rule "restore saved geometry before show"), but the W23 "hidden-resident windows stay out of `wm_wait`'s enumeration" semantics rest on our own `hidden` bookkeeping, and `orderFront:` without clearing it turns `hide_wbtest`'s "is_hidden==0 after recall" red.
  2. The IM focus gate `im_active` shares GTK's semantics and default (first window defaults to 1; after `im_set_active(0)` keys no longer pass through `NSTextInputContext`).
- **System drag & drop on mac (the dragdnd eight)**:
  1. **The assertions encoded one side's semantics again**: `dragdnd_wbtest` checks **Win32 semantics** (count = number of registered windows; `effect` of an unregistered window returns -1), while the GTK branch gives a constant 1. Mac implements the Win32 line (`wm_dnd_registered[]` bookkeeping), and the comment records "GTK differs" - when two semantics coexist across three platforms, a new platform follows **the one the tests check**.
  2. **Drag-out needs the live mouse-down event**: `beginDraggingSessionWithItems:event:source:` requires the actual `NSEvent` from this `mouseDown:` and will not accept a fabricated one - `mouseDown:` archives `down_ev`, `send` consumes and clears it (same contract as GTK's "press archived for drag start").
  3. **Blocking via a nested pump**: after starting the session, a small loop of `nextEventMatchingMask:NSEventMaskAny untilDate:+4ms inMode:NSDefaultRunLoopMode` + `sendEvent:` runs until `draggingSession:endedAtPoint:operation:` marks done or the 60s timeout hits - `cancelDragOperation:` is deprecated and no longer honored, so a timeout simply returns 3.
  4. **NSDragOperation must be mapped explicitly to the facade's effect bits**: Copy=1, Move=16, Link=512, and a multi-bit result counts as "no deal" returning 0 - the native enum values share no numbering with the wire flags (0/1/2/4), so nothing can be passed through.
  5. The payload wire is one contract across three platforms: `[kind:i32 LE][body]`, kind 1 = text, kind 4 = '\n'-joined absolute paths; on drop, file URLs come from `readObjectsForClasses:` with `NSPasteboardURLReadingFileURLsOnlyKey`, falling back to `stringForType:NSPasteboardTypeString`.
- **webview module mac link filled in**: `webkit_stub.c`'s placeholder branch is gated with `!defined(__APPLE__)`, so on mac the native-stub compile yields an **empty translation unit** - `modules/gui-webview/prebuild.py` therefore needs its own Darwin branch (archive built with `-DWB_HAVE_WKWEBVIEW -x objective-c -fobjc-arc`, linked against WebKit/Cocoa plus **the main repo's `libyue_win_stub_mac.a`**: webview needs `wm_surface_container` from the win stub via a direct extern link with no MoonBit import edge, so a missing archive shows up as a pile of `_wb_*` Undefined symbols). The failure shape of a module prebuild is link-time symbol explosions, not one compile-time error - when debugging, first confirm the archive was actually produced. One more finding from the same batch: **a branch frozen at an older wire shape**. Master moved kind=7 JS-eval results into a dedicated 65536-byte buffer (`wb_eval_text`) leaving the event text empty; the mac arm predated that and `_wb_eval_text` link errors exposed it. An alignment batch must re-check **changed wire shapes of existing functions per branch**, not just add new functions.
- **sysmonitor mac stub fixes**:
  1. **`mach_task_self_` is a data symbol; `_mach_task_self` is the function**. Declaring the underscore-trailing one as an `extern function` compiles and links, and calling it **jumps into a data page - SIGBUS** (signal 10). Located by resolving frames in the crash report `.ips`; a fifty-second repro that only calls `vm_deallocate` beat attaching lldb to the full suite.
  2. **`proc_pidinfo(pid 1)` returning 0 is not an error under SIP**: BSDINFO/TASKINFO give 0 bytes for launchd (denied without root) while `proc_pidpath(1)` works - so launchd vanished from the process list. Fix shape: when stat is unreadable, synthesize the comm from the path's basename and report it running, keeping pid 1 in the list ("0 bytes" and "failure" must be handled apart).
- **mac clipboard switched to the NSPasteboard main path (pbcopy silently no-ops on non-ASCII)**: `printf ... | pbcopy` round-trips **pure ASCII** fine, but writing text with **Chinese/newlines** leaves the pasteboard cleared-or-unwritten while rc stays 0 (`clipboard info` even looks healthy - a pure no-op). The probe string "yue-clip ... first line\nsecond line" turned the roundtrip test into exactly that None; the same string through `NSPasteboard setString:forType:` is intact. The fix mirrors Linux's GtkClipboard route: `clipboard.mbt`'s macOS branch prefers the `yue_sys_clipboard_gtk_*` forwarding layer (sys_stub.c's non-`_WIN32` arm -> the win stub's mac-arm NSPasteboard implementation, `available` always 1), with pbcopy/pbpaste as fallback only. The stale "Windows/macOS get a dumb implementation" comment in `sys_stub.c` was corrected in the same batch - the dumb branch is `_WIN32`-only and mac has always gone through the real forwarding.
- **render mac arm: three W35 empty stubs**: `cr_set_line_cap/join/dash` exist to keep the link - mac always paints through the pure raster path (`cr_begin` returns 0, the Painter never enters a cairo session), so line-cap semantics live in the pure-MoonBit rasterizer: deliberately different in shape from the cairo-backed GTK/Win32 branches, same facade contract.
- **What backs this batch**: everything above was run on real macOS hardware (`moon test --target native`, full workspace 1236/1236) - the first time the library suite ran in full on a Mac after the merge; the CI macOS job keeps its coverage, and eyes-on items still follow section T of `_人工测试清单.md`.

- **Windows CI link missing `wm_hotkey_supported` (2026-10-18)**: after the merge the Windows job died with LNK2019 on the shell whitebox exe - when the three-arm stub was rebuilt, **the WIN32 arm dropped exactly the supported entry of the hotkey family** (register/unregister/poll were all there), while the GTK/mac/placeholder arms each kept it. Fix shape: `return 1` in the WIN32 arm (RegisterHotKey is always present). Rule: after changing the arm structure of the single stub.c, cross-check the extern name list from `ffi.mbt` against the target arm's definitions one by one - `grep -oE '= "wm_[a-z_]+"' | sort -u` piped through `comm -23` with the arm's definitions finds everything in one step, instead of letting CI explode one symbol at a time. (`wm_win_gui_marker` is a legitimate exception such a scan should skip: it lives in the package's other native-stub file, `win_gui.c`.)

- **Three merge wounds that only the CI could surface (2026-10-18)**: the mac branch had forked from a baseline **before** webview was extracted into a module (4602886), so merging it into master reintroduced three stale shapes that a green local suite cannot catch - only the three CI platforms running once each expose them one by one:
  1. **A dead Windows call in the main prebuild**: the mac arm brought `if system=="Windows": ensure_release_files()` back into `link_configs()`, but that function (download the WebView2 headers/Loader) was already moved into the module's own prebuild at extraction time - the Windows job died on `NameError` before ever reaching the link. How to find it: the CI traceback points at the call line, and `git show <merge>^2:<file> | grep def` confirms the definition only lives on the mac parent side. **After a divergent merge, re-check every moved file for "all call sites resolve across the repo"** (on the Python side, `ast` plus one dry run of the output is enough).
  2. **A stale path in the macOS stub gate**: the ci.yml mac gate still read `web/webkit_stub.c` (its pre-modularization home), so clang reported "no such file" and the five-stub gate went red. Repointed at `../modules/gui-webview/webview/webkit_stub.c` (working-directory is gui) - **when a batch moves a package, gate scripts that reference its source path must be updated in the same batch**; unlike the duplicate-library warning, this is a hard reference.
  3. **A stale package list in the macOS job**: the test/build steps still named `core` (since split into base/shell/widget) and `web` (now a module); when those were fixed for Linux/Windows the macOS job didn't exist yet, so nobody back-filled it. Aligned to the Linux 15-package list minus dbus (macOS has no session bus) = 13 packages, and gave macOS the "unit tests (gui-webview module)" step it was missing (Linux/Windows both had it) - which brings the module's Darwin link branch into CI coverage.
- One cross-job rule that came out of it: from now on the **Linux job is the baseline** for the library package list (it is the full set); Windows drops sys/dbus by platform gate and macOS drops dbus. A new package must be added to all three - missing one is the next merge's wound.

- **Once the link gates went green, the readout loops ran for real in CI - three "CI runner ≠ real machine" test shapes fixed (2026-10-18)**: after the Windows link fix, the module step's bare `moon test` (whole workspace) exposed the sys readouts for the first time -
  1. **`/tmp` is a Linux/mac landing spot, not a Windows one**: appfind's disk-scan fixture hardcoded `af_tmp()` to `/tmp`, so `sys_write_text_file` returned false on Windows and four tests went red. Now dispatched at runtime to `TEMP` (falling back to `.` when unset) - test fixtures need the platform gate too, same as "a Dock-started process has no shell PATH".
  2. **`vol_supported()` does not mean "readable"**: on Windows the supported probe only proves COM starts; **the missing default audio endpoint only surfaces at `vol_get`**, and CI runners have no audio device. The readout loop became probe-then-branch: a first-read Err skips out loud, and the round-trip assertions only run when a device is present (real hardware) - the same philosophy as the GIF first-frame fallback.
  3. **The first-tick upper bound now scales with the frame period**: the video smoke's 0.09-0.15 window was broken by decode backlog on a slow runner (CI macOS measured 0.204), so the bound widened to one-and-a-half frames (0.25 at fps=12) while the "it advanced without skipping the segment" round-trip meaning stays.
- One CI-structure fact worth recording: the "unit tests (gui-webview module)" step in all three jobs **bare-runs the whole workspace** (`moon test` normalizes upward from the module directory), so that step is really the final full-suite gate per platform - the package lists only constrain the earlier steps, and new tests surface there first.

## Maintenance

1. New conclusions go into the matching section and record only the pit and the fix; protocol-interop conclusions must come from the real bus and real panels — unit-test self-consistency does not count.
2. Keep both language versions (this file and docs/zh/adaptation.md) in sync in the same batch.
3. Landing points for the media and desktop-control batches: "Media and desktop-control command routes" (under the Linux system-capability data layer), "System information and system-level security boundaries", "Directory enumeration and in-process environment variables" (under Cross-platform general), "Generic D-Bus call layer" (under DBus wire protocol), "Map and flight-line projection" (under Self-drawn canvas and chart rendering); browser-side conclusions go into the `Firefox places.sqlite` section.
4. Do not run `moon fmt` inside a feature batch: the current toolchain's reflow conventions disagree with this repo's existing style (one round touched 287 files); a repo-wide format pass is its own batch, opened only after confirming the conventions match.

### Frontend-batch real-hardware feedback fix set (2026-10-14, migrated in from TODO on 2026-10-16)

> This batch is a one-item-one-cause record of "user reports from a real machine → locate → fix", previously held only in TODO.md; under the split "the full picture lives in the roadmap, unfinished work in TODO, process in adaptation" it moved here in one piece, and the TODO side deleted it.

- [x] **Stroke convention unified (2026-10-14, real-hardware report "the colour-picker borders sit off")**: the facade contract is "`stroke_rect` lands **inside** the rectangle" (both backends implement it that way), yet 28 call sites passed `(0.5, 0.5, w-1, h-1)` out of centered-stroke habit ⇒ the whole ring shifted 1 px down-right (a strip of fill exposed on the left/top). Converted with `(x-lw/2, y-lw/2, w+lw, h+lw)` and switched across the repo (ui + chart + examples); the button focus-ring test sampled column 1 because it was written against the offset geometry and now samples column 0, plus a new four-side swatch symmetry pin.
- [x] **The library would not compile off Windows** (2026-10-14): sys's power-scheme batch put two `static` helpers taking `GUID` parameters outside every guard (`static` still type-checks when uncalled), so `unknown type name 'GUID'` on Linux killed the whole build; both helpers were wrapped in `#if defined(_WIN32)`. Rule: any function whose types come from a platform header goes into the guard wholesale, and after changing C, compile at least once on a non-target platform.
- [x] **The transfer panels were too small** (2026-10-14, real-hardware report): the default 160×min 60 was far too small to read as an operable list ⇒ default 200×160, plus a `height?` parameter (a long list still grows on its own and never clips rows).
- [x] **Table hover lit only one cell, and "add a row" did nothing** (2026-10-14, real-hardware report): ① hover is parent-chain semantics, but the host marked only the "old/new hovered" widget's rect ⇒ the row painted a row-wide background while the repaint window was one cell. New `App::mark_state_chain` marks dirty along the hit chain, an ancestor only when it paints that state itself (`@style.apply` sets `Widget.paints_state`; core does not know the style layer and only reads the boolean); with no state ancestor the cost stays one cell. ② Store's built-in dedup compares by value, and the example stored the array it pushes into ⇒ old and new are the same object and the notification is swallowed; the initial value became a snapshot. Full wording in this file's entry from the same batch.
- [x] **The timeline connector came out broken** (2026-10-14): the row gap was carried by the container's `row_gap` and belongs to no widget ⇒ the line broke at every gap. The spacing is now painted into the row (a non-last marker and row box grow to `height+gap`) with pixel assertions that the gaps must carry line. Continuous cross-row decoration (connector / spine / separator / track) can never live in container gaps.
- [x] **Breadcrumb clicks did not navigate** (2026-10-14): "current item" was decided by position (the last item) rather than by the navigation state ⇒ the last crumb stops working whenever it is not the current page. Clickability and colour now key off `selected.get() == mine`.
- [x] **Three form-page items** (2026-10-14, real-hardware report): ① inputs could not take keyboard focus by default (`focus_id?` defaulting to 0 means the host judges "not focusable") ⇒ `input`/`textarea` auto-allocate when no number is given (from 1000000, explicit numbers still win); ② marking focus changes fed the **focus id** into a lookup by **instance id** (`mark_focus_rect`→`mark_id_rect`) ⇒ new `mark_focus_id_rect` going through `find_by_focus_id`; ③ `input` gained `clearable` (EP's name, off by default, ✕ on hover/focus, clicking clears and writes back); ④ the stepper's `[-] value [+]` now shares one frame (the row container draws the frame once, the cells draw only hover fill and the separator; the old three rings read as unjoined boxes, and measurement showed the three cells were already equal height).
- [x] **Form-family keyboard accessibility** (2026-10-15, user report: "nothing but inputs can be Tab-reached and there is no keyboard interaction"): button/checkbox/radio/switch/stepper/slider/rate/select/color_picker/date_picker/date_range/time_field/dropdown/segmented all auto-allocate a focus number by default (`auto_focus_id`, retiring the 2026-10-14 "deliberate opt-in" rule); space/Enter activates, radio/segmented arrows re-select by focused index, slider/stepper/rate arrows adjust the value (slider adds Home/End), select/color_picker/dropdown popups take ↑↓ highlight + Enter pick + Esc close, date/time fields open and close the layer (arrow navigation inside the calendar is not done); focus rings go through "outline turns theme colour" and the inner-ring form. `moon test ui` 176/176, library 934/935 (1 red = the Windows baseline), real-machine re-check under S22.
- [x] **Fullscreen and size switching did nothing on Windows** (2026-10-15, real-hardware report): `wm_window_set_size`/`wm_window_set_fullscreen` in `gui/win/stub.c`'s Windows branch were symbol-bearing empty stubs (GTK had long had real implementations), so links held and calls were silently inert. Win32 implementations added: set_size expands client-area physical pixels to the outer window per the current style and calls `SetWindowPos`; fullscreen records the style + `WINDOWPLACEMENT` scene, strips decorations for `WS_POPUP` and moves onto the nearest monitor, restoring verbatim on exit; the existing `WM_SIZE` bookkeeping keeps delivering `Resized` to MoonBit. `experiment/window_probe`'s C probe gained two sections (size read-back + fullscreen enter/exit scene restore, full `WIN-ENHANCE-OK`), real-machine re-check under S23.
- [x] **Global hotkeys never fired** (2026-10-15, real-hardware report): the library chain (RegisterHotKey → pump intercepts WM_HOTKEY → poll) was fine; showcase's poll table was armed at the wrong moment — the "zero-size mount hook" sat in `node_of_new`'s finish (construction time) and page functions are evaluated before the window exists, so the first tick ran on the empty timer channel with `app.host` still None and the loop never re-armed (occurrence #2 of the charts push-point pit). Moved to `Node::on_mount`; window_probe gained a hotkey section (WM_HOTKEY injected via PostThreadMessageW, checking interception/extraction/dedup/exclusivity/unregistration) printing `WIN-ENHANCE-OK`, real-machine re-check under S24.
- [x] **The charts page sat at "no data"** (2026-10-14, real-hardware report): `set_timeout`'s process-level channel is installed by `App::new` and is a no-op returning 0 without a host, while `page_charts(app)` is an argument to `mount_window` evaluated before the window exists ⇒ the first tick armed during construction never fired. Changed to hang on `handle` (running after `mount_children`), with the on-page code sample re-worded. Same batch: section descriptions gained `wrap=true` (they were single 900 px unwrapped lines whose tails were cut).
- [x] **yoga-mbt left the line gaps out of free space** (2026-10-14, real-hardware report "the copy button is still wrong"): in §9.7 the distribution, `initial_free` / `remaining` / auto-margin `free` / justify `free2` subtracted only the sum of child frames and never `gap x (n-1)`, while positioning added gap per item ⇒ grow items over-ate the gaps and the whole row overflowed its container (acceptance check: row 100 + gap 10 + [fixed 30, grow 1] should be 60, computed 70 before the fix). All four places now subtract `gap_total` first.
- [x] **"The strip wraps when too wide" was a fake claim** (2026-10-14): `ui` never wrote `flex_wrap` and the style layer had no such property ⇒ every container was NoWrap and long strips overflowed and got clipped. `Style` gained `flex_wrap` per "property name = CSS property name" (factory/merge/apply all wired). Real wrapping still needs two companions: the strip belongs in a **column** (a row does not stretch its cross axis ⇒ the wrapping container sizes to content and folds into six or seven lines), and **the wrapping container plus every parent level needs explicit `min_height/min_width=0`** (spec §4.5 makes a column child's min:auto equal the min-content height = everything stacked; measured strip 224 px with the body dropping from 646 to 476; the engine is spec-conformant). Post-fix numbers: strip 54, body 646, and the code-document page viewport 652 / content 808 scrollable.
- [x] **The scroll container would not scroll** (2026-10-14, real-hardware report): `scroll_view`'s viewport never set `min-height`, and Yoga flex children default to min-size=auto ⇒ the viewport was pushed up to its content's natural height and `max()` stayed 0 (measured: inside a 240×140 parent, viewport=676=content). `min_height/min_width=0` added at the library level, so all call sites (showcase section bodies and sidebar, native-app, virt_list hosts) benefit together; explicit `height=` is unaffected. The acceptance check and control readings are in this file's entry from the same batch.
- [x] **Two Markdown-page defects** (2026-10-14, real-hardware report): ① rich-text ranges were produced in UTF-16 code units while the `AttributedText` contract is UTF-8 byte indices ⇒ in mixed CJK/Latin text every style shifted forward and endpoints cut inside characters (tofu plus overlapping glyphs); ② `md_rich_label` never wrapped and the node width equalled the whole paragraph's natural width (a 656 px line pushed into a 480 document) ⇒ the right edge was clipped and the code area's "copy" button was pushed out of the visible region. Fixed with `md_byte_len` producing the ranges plus greedy wrapping at construction (CJK per character / Latin per word / `\n` hard breaks / over-long units cut per character), one AttributedText per line, strike-through and link hits computed per line, and list/quote/footnote/table cells narrowed to their available width (`md_narrow`). The acceptance checks and the "switch back to the old unit and it goes red on the spot" control experiment are in `docs/zh/adaptation.md`'s entry from the same batch. **Pending real hardware**: do the tofu / clipped right edge / copy button disappear, and does vertical scrolling of the content area come back?
